on behalf of the s&d group. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, today, if a member state prohibits the cultivation of a gmo on its territory, it is systematically condemned by the court of justice of the european union following a complaint by monsanto. the agreement reached on 3 december in the trilogue is a game changer. it is important to remember this in this debate. without this agreement, we would have maintained the current situation, where the european commission authorises the cultivation of a gmo because of the absence of a common position in the council. this situation could not continue. it systematically put the member states who want to say no to gmos, like france, in the wrong. in this long and difficult negotiation in the face of a council that is not very flexible, we have succeeded, together with frédérique ries - our rapporteur, whom i would like to congratulate - in strengthening the protection of consumers, farmers and the member states. this directive means more safety for member states opposed to gmos. from spring 2015, member states will be able to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of gmos on their territories on environmental, agricultural and socioeconomic grounds. this means more security for farmers who favour conventional or organic crops. within two years, member states will take measures to prevent contamination of traditional crops by gm crops in cross-border areas. this means greater security for european consumers. the european commission has committed to review and strengthen the rules for risk assessment by the european food safety authority within two years. in another victory for european consumers, we have convinced the commission not to grant any new authorizations for the cultivation of gmos before the entry into force of this directive. it was a hard fight that was fought and we got there. i think we have won, but this directive is only the beginning. it is a good start, but we must continue the fight against gmos.
madam president, gmos as they are imposed on us by the agrochemical multinationals, the united states and the european union are unacceptable and dangerous. on the one hand, the investment required to set up a new gmo plant is high. therefore, this technology may lead to a decrease in the number of plant varieties grown. and diversity is agriculture's best asset against the problems of disease and pests. on the other hand, the vast majority of gmos are roundup ready varieties. crops can be sprayed with roundup, a highly toxic weed killer for wildlife and plants as well as humans. other gm plants secrete pesticides themselves. some of these pesticides are therefore likely to be ingested by consumers. it should be noted that the amount of roundup residues tolerated in soybeans was increased fourfold in the united states in 1997 to allow the sale of gm soybeans. roundup is a potentially very dangerous carcinogen. consumer health appears to be an adjustment variable here. finally, farmers must replenish their stocks of gm seeds each year; they are enslaved, not liberated by this technology. the new directive you want us to vote on is a trap. you're going to give states a little bit of sovereignty back by allowing them to allow or ban a gmo on their territory. however, as a result of the principle of free movement, french supermarkets will increasingly welcome gmo products from other eu countries on their shelves. french consumers will therefore be increasingly exposed to gmos despite their strong opposition to this technique. the compulsory labelling of food containing gmos - unfortunately not visible on the packaging - will be the last line of defence against those who intend to impose them without limitation, in particular through the eu/us free trade agreement. as usual, you are therefore legislating against the will of the people on a crucial issue, thus favouring the interests of the multinational agrochemical companies at the expense of the health of consumers and farmers, of the diversity of crops and by denying a fundamental principle: we must feed without making people sick.
madam president, i would like to congratulate the rapporteur, mrs frédérique ries, and our fictitious rapporteur, mrs elisabeth köstinger, and to thank mr la via for the important role he has played in these negotiations. until now we have had a system without a head or tail, which by its complexity discouraged research and innovation in the biotechnology sector and, on the other hand, brought member states - such as france - which are hostile to the cultivation of gmos to justice. we have a compromise - after five years - which offers freedom of choice and, at the same time, greater legal certainty. what is important to me is that the evaluation of gm seeds and their safety for human health should be based on a scientific approach and not be subject to purely ideological debates. secondly, member states are obliged to adopt coexistence measures in cross-border areas to avoid contamination of traditional crops by gm crops. i have fought for this because i believe that farmers should be able to remain free to choose their crops. this compromise is certainly not the outcome we could have dreamed of for the gmo issue. i would have preferred a genuinely european solution to the impasse, but since the best is often the enemy of the good, i am calling on everyone to take responsibility for establishing a stable legal framework for gm crops in europe.
in writing. for several years we have been debating how to deal with the introduction or rejection of gmos in the european union. until recently, our differences prevented any possibility of agreement. we cannot be satisfied with fragmented and uncoordinated procedures. we now have the opportunity to provide a clear framework for the private, public and associative actors in this sector. i think this opportunity should be seized. however, in the absence of agreement on the content, we have had to restrict ourselves to the content: no decision on the advisability of gmos is left to the member states, this european text will ultimately be purely procedural. it would be wrong to make this agreement a precedent in other areas which in the longer term would risk draining the law and policies of the european union of its substance.
in writing. the health of the people of europe is not negotiable. we cannot cause a disruption of our food and environment. behind this text of technical reforms is an attempt to develop genetically modified organisms in europe. in addition to the health risks, gmos are a means of controlling agriculture by agro-food groups via patented seeds. will the european parliament be the relay for the international economic oligarchies? the hypocrisy of this text is striking. while the member states are to have new tools in the authorisation of gm crops, the text does not call into question the restrictions on the most basic freedoms of the states. what would it mean to ban the cultivation of gmos in one country if it is impossible to ban the circulation of gmos grown in another member state? one of the first forms of sovereignty of a state is control of all flows that pass through it. this text maintains supranational oversight of the states, whereas the standards and evaluation procedures are not satisfactory. i am aware that security has a price, but we cannot sell our peoples' food security and the independence of their agriculture.
in writing. the production of genetically modified organisms (gmos) is a sensitive and controversial issue within the european union (eu). the negotiations to provide the eu with a suitable and modern legislative framework have been under way for five years but have been hampered by significant differences of opinion. the compromise reached by the union will allow member states who wish to grow gmos and those who do not wish to do so to ban them legally. in practice, the authorisation application procedure is clearer and more transparent: a company applying for authorisation to grow genetically modified crops must nevertheless, after the authorisation of the european food safety authority, obtain that of the member state which will host the crops on its soil. i would also like to stress that, as regards crossborder areas, the agreement reached obliges the member states to adopt coexistence measures to avoid contamination of traditional crops by gm crops. in the end, this system is not perfect, but it does allow us to get out of a deadlock. it will be important to ensure that a european solution is found in the medium term.

in writing. i voted in favour of this recommendation because this support meets the objectives of the national fisheries policy, and in particular the needs of the democratic republic of são tomé and príncipe with regard to support for small-scale fisheries and the fight against illegal fishing.
in writing. this protocol sets out the fishing opportunities and financial contribution provided for in the fisheries partnership agreement between the eu and the democratic republic of são tomé and príncipe. the protocol, which entered into force in may 2014 for a period of four years, is intended to allow 34 eu vessels to fish there. in return, são tomé and príncipe will receive eur 2 805 000 over the entire four-year period (this may be increased if the annual catch exceeds the annual reference tonnage). i therefore voted in favour of this text, which seems fair and balanced.
in writing. the fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and the democratic republic of são tomé and príncipe is part of the network of agreements on tuna fishing in west africa. in particular, it allows 28 tuna seiners and 6 longliners to fish in the são toméan eez. while we approve the agreement in principle, we are deeply concerned about the many illegal fishing activities in the gulf of guinea. the european union should immediately step up the traceability of its imports of fishery resources from countries suspected of covering up illegal fishing activities, given the democratic republic of são tomé's weak capacity to monitor its territorial waters. i therefore voted with reservations in favour of the european parliament's recommendations to the commission, which aim at transparency in all stages of the procedures relating to the protocol and its renewal.
in writing. the fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and the democratic republic of são tomé and príncipe is one of the union's tuna agreements in west africa. it allows eu vessels to fish in the waters of that country. this agreement is beneficial to both parties as it allows the development of the european market for fishery products and the sectoral development of fisheries in são tomé and príncipe. the rapporteur stresses that the european commission must do more to monitor the principles necessary for the proper absorption of aid, while respecting the sovereignty and legitimate choices and priorities of são tomé and príncipe. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which opens up new prospects for our fishermen. it will allow 34 eu vessels to access são toméan waters (28 tuna vessels and 6 surface longliners). it also supports small-scale fishing, which i am very fond of because it values traditional know-how, which guarantees quality fishing. the text also provides for the fight against illegal fishing, which is a necessary measure for the preservation of our ecosystem.
in writing. this report proposes the ratification of the fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and the democratic republic of são tomé and príncipe. this important agreement, which will run for four years, is part of the network of agreements on tuna fishing in west africa. it allows for the development of support for the local fishing sector in exchange for access for european union vessels to fish part of the fisheries surplus in são toméan waters. it is a balanced agreement and that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. thanks to its network of tuna fisheries agreements in west africa, eu vessels can fish in the waters of a number of countries in the region, including the democratic republic of são tomé and príncipe. with the adoption of the new protocol between the european union and são tomé and príncipe, the european union is rightly maintaining its vessels' access to tuna-rich waters, while ensuring that this access is remunerated at fair value. the purpose of this remuneration is, inter alia, to support the sectoral policy of são tomé and príncipe.
in writing. this agreement between the union and the democratic republic of são tomé and príncipe will improve access control to the exclusive economic zone (eez) concerned by increasing the presence of observers. this will eventually facilitate the monitoring of tuna catches and fisheries in this area, an activity with a high environmental stake. the preservation of natural and animal resources is a prerequisite for sustainable development in the field of local economic activities. for these reasons i voted in favour of this recommendation.
in writing. i will vote in favour of this proposal because this agreement is in the well-understood interests of both parties. on the one hand, it will allow 34 european union vessels access to são toméan waters. among these vessels are 12 french tuna vessels. the european union also provides equal compensation to são tomé: eur 710 000 for the first three years and eur 675 000 for the fourth year. this includes eur 325 000 per year for supporting sectoral policy, which will support small-scale fishing and combat illegal fishing. finally, shipowners will pay 35 euros per tonne for the first two years, 60 euros for the third year and 70 euros for the fourth year. it seems that none of the parties is therefore harmed, even if the rapporteur stresses that the results achieved so far in sectoral policy are insufficient. in particular, we should improve our knowledge of fish stocks, but above all we should support the development of são tomé's own monitoring capabilities. it is only then that this agreement could really be part of a sustainable fisheries policy.

in writing. the island of mayotte has recently become a french department and as such there is a need to regularize relations with france's neighbours in this region, in this case the republic of seychelles, through clearer suspension and surveillance procedures. the aim is also to maintain fishing activities which are essential to the economies of the two territories. for these reasons, i voted in favour of this recommendation.

in writing. this agreement between the european union and the republic of seychelles is intended to allow fishing vessels flying the flag of seychelles access to the waters and marine biological resources of mayotte, which fall within the jurisdiction of the eu. since mayotte became an outermost region of the eu in 2014, its exclusive economic zone (eez) has been part of eu waters, indicating a loss of sovereignty for france in the use of this zone. this agreement nevertheless allows a limited number of vessels flying the flag of the seychelles, which have a historical tradition of fishing in mayotte's waters, to continue their activities and i therefore voted in favour of the text.
in writing. traditionally, vessels flying the flag of seychelles have fished in mayotte's waters. this french territory became an outermost region of the eu at the beginning of the year and the exclusive economic zone of mayotte has since been made community under the common fisheries policy. following the change of status, an agreement was negotiated to allow a limited number of seychelles vessels to fish in the exclusive economic zone. an agreement provides for the payment of a financial counterpart by each vessel. these fees will be collected by france and redistributed to mayotte. these are to be devoted in particular to port infrastructure and to the control and marketing of products, in the framework of the sustainable tuna fisheries partnership agreement, which entered into force on 10 may 2003 between the european union and the republic of seychelles. i therefore voted in favour of the report by alain cadec, which proposes to approve the agreement.
in writing. a sustainable fisheries partnership agreement (sfpa) governs relations between the european union and the republic of seychelles in the field of fisheries. it should be recalled that, according to article 3 tfeu, the conservation of fisheries resources is an exclusive competence of the union, a competence whose legitimacy we formally contest, since it constitutes an essential element of the territorial maritime sovereignty of france. however, in the best interests of the economic development of mayotte and in particular of the fishing sector, i support this agreement because the fees paid by the seychelles shipowners will be directly redistributed to mayotte. the fishing industry in the mahora is still very small-scale and employs some 5 000 people. rather than opening up fishing grounds to large industrial tuna vessels, it is better to encourage cooperation in the archipelago and to use the fees wisely to enable the mahora fishermen to improve their fishing equipment while preserving their artisanal know-how. that is why i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution approving the conclusion of the agreement.
in writing. my report on the agreement allowing seychelles vessels access to part of the exclusive economic zone of mayotte was adopted by a large majority in the european parliament. this agreement is a strong signal for mayotte, which has become the 101st french department. the fees paid by the shipowners will be redistributed for the development of fisheries and aquaculture in mayotte, particularly as regards port infrastructure. i have received assurances from the french government that this money will be redistributed entirely to the mahora fisheries sector. the other part of the economic zone is reserved for local fisheries in order to preserve the small-scale mahora fishery, which is therefore french. this agreement allows sustainable fishing because it respects the rules on the good management and conservation of tuna resources as well as the rules of the common fisheries policy. in the context of the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, this agreement strengthens the credibility of the european union.
in writing. i voted in favour of this agreement which should allow seychelles fishing vessels access to mayotte's waters and biological resources. the aim is to give a legal framework to a historical practice of seychelles vessels, all in accordance with the cfp. the main task of the legislator should always be to promote the customs and traditions of the people, where they are respectful of the common good.
in writing. this report proposes ratification of the agreement between the european union and the republic of seychelles granting access to eight seychelles fishing vessels and two seychelles supply vessels to part of the exclusive economic zone of mayotte under the jurisdiction of the european union. this is a balanced ratio, since in exchange for access to the mahour waters, seychelles vessels pay fees which will be reimbursed in full for the development of fisheries and aquaculture in mayotte, including port infrastructure. in addition, the remainder of the economic zone is preserved as it is reserved for small-scale mahora fisheries and the development of mahora fishing infrastructure. for these reasons i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. since 31 march 2011, the department of mayotte has officially become the 101st department of france and its fifth overseas department. as the european union has also become an outermost region, it is now important, through this balanced text, to conclude an agreement between the european union and the seychelles on access for seychelles fishing vessels to the waters and marine biological resources of mayotte. in return, shipowners will have to pay fees, which are a particularly necessary source of revenue to enable this department, which is in a difficult economic and social situation, to comply with the rules of the common fisheries policy.
in writing. since 1 january 2014, mayotte, the 101st french department, is an ultra-peripheral region (urr) that is an integral part of the european union. as such, its exclusive economic zone, i.e. the maritime space over which a coastal state exercises sovereign rights in the exploration and use of resources, is now community-wide under the common fisheries policy. with the change of status, an agreement between the republic of seychelles and the european union was to be negotiated to allow a limited number of vessels flying the flag of seychelles and having a long history of fishing in mayotte waters to continue fishing activities in the mahoura eez in accordance with the rules of the common fisheries policy. this agreement will preserve the special relations which the european union has with the republic of seychelles.
in writing. mayotte has recently become a french department and, as such, it is necessary to regularize relations with france's neighbours in this region, in this case the republic of seychelles, through clearer suspension and surveillance procedures. it is also a question of maintaining fishing activities which are essential to the economies of the two territories, which is why i voted in favour of this recommendation.
in writing. i will vote in favour of seychelles fishing vessels having access to mayotte's waters and biological resources. in reality, this agreement formalises a historical practice of seychelles vessels, even though it is an exceptional one in that it allows a third country to fish in french waters. however, it concerns only a limited number of vessels flying the flag of seychelles, namely 8 tuna vessels and 2 supply vessels. in addition, shipowners pay redistributed fees to mayotte which will increase from eur 110 to eur 125 per tonne caught in 6 years. these charges will be used to develop the port infrastructure of mayotte, which needs them to develop. however, as the rapporteur has also pointed out, it is regrettable that local mahora fishermen are only allowed to fish from 0 to 24 miles off the coast, whereas seychelles vessels are only allowed to fish from 24 to 100 miles. it is to be hoped that the development of mayotte's port infrastructure will eventually allow the mahora fishery to replace the seychelles fishery. this is the basis on which we will judge the system at the mid-term review in three years' time.

in writing. this agreement between the european union and the republic of seychelles authorises fishing vessels flying the flag of seychelles to access the waters, and thus the marine biological resources, of mayotte, which fall directly under the jurisdiction of the eu. since mayotte became an outermost region of the european union in 2014, its exclusive economic zone (eez) has been part of eu waters. it is worth noting that france's national sovereignty is once again being violated. however, in form this agreement concerns only a very limited number of vessels flying the flag of the seychelles, which have always been used to fishing in mayotte's waters. this is the continuation of a historical tradition. so in order not to penalize these activities, i voted in favour of this text.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the trilogue reached on the night of 3 to 4 december is a minimum agreement which allows the member states to prohibit the cultivation of gmos on their soil. i am not going to go into the details of the text, but i would like to make a few comments on the text. this is not the first phase of a sovereign political response to the gmo question but the last very symbolic concession to the states as a handout. the problem of gmos is a food safety problem. nothing is said about the ability of states to impose traceability and labelling of gm food wherever it is produced. the problem of gmos is a problem of contamination of other crops. there is no mention of the risk of cross-border contamination from a state which refuses to allow gmos to be grown on its soil. finally, the problem of gmos is even a civilization problem in that it is a tool in the hands of very powerful firms to manipulate the living for immediate profit. we have no debate beyond the prosaic aspect when this debate is taking place elsewhere, notably in russia.
madam president, the text proposed to us is a trojan horse, because under the guise of restoring freedom to the states, it is handing over our people, consumers and farmers to the agrochemical multinationals. the effects of gmos on the health of our fellow citizens and on the flora and fauna are already known and unacceptable. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for approval, and the council will then be able to take a decision on the matter. to serve who? not the people, but the shareholders of a few publicly traded companies, when we already know that it is possible to feed humanity without gmos. the key is to make the right political choices. the gmos imposed on us by this text are incompatible with any food sovereignty. that sovereignty is to the people what freedom is to the individual. we need to be able to choose and grow what we want to eat at home and have our children eat what is safe for our health. that is why i voted against this text.
in writing. despite the fact that this directive will allow france to ban the planting of gmos on national soil, i did not vote in favour of this text, as it will not protect the french from the consumption of gm food. in the european free trade area it will be impossible to assure our fellow citizens that genetically modified food will not end up on their plates. neighbouring exporting countries within the eu may have chosen to use gmos themselves and resell them in all eu countries, including those that have chosen to boycott them.
in writing. the agreement we are voting on today allows member states who wish to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of gmos on their own territory to do so. their decision to restrict or prohibit such crops will benefit from greater legal certainty and will avoid the systematic use of moratoriums which can be challenged at any time by litigation. thanks to the action of the european parliament, the text also provides for several other improvements. as requested since 2008, the commission will have to update the legislation on environmental risk assessment of gmos within 2 years. coexistence measures at the border between two states, one of which would allow the cultivation of gmos and the other not, are mandatory. member states authorising the cultivation of gmos are allowed to establish liability schemes for damage caused by gm crops to neighbouring conventional and organic crops. i would like to thank the rapporteur for his report, which is a very good report, and i would like to thank the rapporteur for his report.
in writing. the proposed text is misleading. it is presented as a guarantee of freedom given to the states, and will facilitate the cultivation of gmos. even if a state refuses to allow the cultivation of a gmo, the internal market rules prevent it from prohibiting the movement of that gmo and products derived from it for consumption. the health, environmental and food requirements are also not sufficient in the authorisation procedures and monitoring of gmo crops. i voted against this text which threatens the health of the citizens of the member states of the european union and the independence of farmers who will be dependent on patented seeds.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution because the socioeconomic impacts of gmo cultivation are not currently taken into account in eu regulations. it was therefore necessary to evolve the system to ensure that each member state had the possibility to choose whether or not to grow gmos on its territory.
in writing. i voted against this text, which i consider to be a trojan horse of the agrochemical multinationals: under the false pretext of giving the states the freedom to authorise or not to authorise gmos, it will de facto impose them on the french people's plates, despite the ban currently in force on our territory. in fact, if free movement is still an untouchable dogma within the european union, how can we ban the import of gmos? how can we limit consumption when we cannot guarantee the traceability and labelling of consumer products? the gmo technology would only be acceptable if we were able to control its design, production and marketing, which is far from the case.
in writing. this recommendation concerns the council's position at first reading with a view to the adoption of a directive of the european parliament and of the council amending directive 2001/18/ec as regards the possibility for member states to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of gmos on their territory. even if it restores a certain degree of sovereignty to the states, which seems positive at first sight, the reality is quite different and is distorted by the free movement in europe, which will in no way prevent the import of products from countries which allow gmos to countries which prohibit them. unfortunately, member states no longer have control over borders, legislation or budgets and this recommendation is just another trick. the european union, by refusing to listen to the opinion of the citizens who in the majority condemn gmos, is thus subject to multinational companies and the future free trade agreement with the united states. health becomes a variable of adjustment which endangers both man and nature and that is why i voted against.
in writing. this text is the result of a painful compromise. i am thinking of that long night of 3 december when the concessions made by the council and the commission were minor. parliamentary representation and therefore the peoples of europe are being mocked. the choice left to the member states, the so-called opt-out clause, not to grow gmos is a real decoy. on the one hand, under the principles of free movement, these gmos, legally produced and marketed in a member state, will be able to find their way onto the plate of a french consumer. the second is the false precaution put forward by the rapporteur of the text, according to which 'the minority of member states which cultivate gmos will now have to take compulsory measures in border areas to avoid possible contamination'. a bit like that radioactive chernobyl cloud that miraculously blocked the franco-german border... i am voting against this text, which goes against the will of the people, against the health of consumers and farmers and against the diversity of crops. once again, this parliament is serving the interests of the agrochemical multinationals. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives to combat the use of gmos, such as those imposed by certain multinational companies, the united states and the european union.
in writing. the proposed amendments to amend directive 2001/18/ec, which allow member states to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of gmos on their territory, are not satisfactory. this gmo directive is a real trap because, under the guise of a supposed respect for the sovereignty of the member states, it offers a gateway to gmo cultivation on the european market. it is no secret that some member states of the union are in favour of gmo cultivation. however, in view of the respect for the free movement of goods and services, if a member state can prohibit the cultivation of gmos on its territory, it will be unable to refuse the import of agricultural products derived from the cultivation of gmos. in practical terms, this directive is likely to have the opposite effect and thus facilitate the sale of foodstuffs in the french supermarket shelves. for all these reasons, i voted against the motion for a resolution and will oppose in the strongest possible terms anything which facilitates the marketing of products containing gmos.
in writing. i voted in favour of the directive on the prohibition or authorisation of the cultivation of gmos in the european union. the text will allow member states which, like france, prohibit the cultivation of gmos on their territory to continue to do so legally. it was necessary to create a legal basis for settling disputes concerning the use of gmos in europe. the situation had been deadlocked for far too long. however, this text is a major setback because the union has preferred not to legislate on a fundamental subject of european dimension and has referred the matter to the member states. i regret the choice of not being in europe.
in writing. because i am committed to the principle of sovereignty, i voted against this text: on the surface, the directive seems to proclaim the freedom for states to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of gmos on their territory; this declaration of good faith is a deception. the principle of free movement of goods enshrined in the lisbon treaty prevents france from really protecting itself against the consumption of transgenic plants: many eu member states have adopted legislation that is very favourable to gmos. as a result, french consumers will, against the wishes of the majority of them, be forced to consume more and more food products containing transgenic plants. the real freedom of the states therefore requires mandatory labelling of products containing gmos. i could not vote for a text which, like the european union, gives people a substitute for freedom.
in writing. this report concludes several years of negotiations on the management of the introduction or disposal of genetically modified organisms (gmos) in the european union. until recently, differences between member states and the european parliament prevented any possibility of agreement, leaving private, public and associative actors with fragmented and uncoordinated procedures within the internal market. this is therefore a welcome compromise, even if the text remains mainly procedural and does not take a position on the very appropriateness of gmos, which is left to the member states. i will therefore be careful that this necessary compromise does not set a precedent in other areas, which in the longer term could lead to the european legislation being deprived of its substance. the text is nevertheless an opportunity which must be seized and that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the text amending directive 2001/18/ec as regards the possibility for member states to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of genetically modified organisms (gmos) on their territory is a compromise. like all compromises, it is not perfect, but it has the merit of providing a solid legal basis that has not existed until now. this legal stability will thus protect france from legal action if it takes measures to ban gmos. the text also guarantees the member states the final say on the use of gmos in their territory. it is for these two reasons in particular that i have decided to vote in favour of this text. i will, however, be very attentive to this matter, particularly in the context of the free trade agreement negotiations currently under way with the united states.
in writing. currently, genetically modified organisms (gmos) can be grown in the european union after the gmo seed growers have obtained a marketing authorisation in accordance with european regulations. however, there are many differences between member states as to whether or not gmos should be grown. the adoption of the directive on the possibility for the latter to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of gmos on their territory is therefore a step in the right direction. it provides a reasoned legal framework for member states, like france, which wish to ban the cultivation of gmos on their territory. the european parliament also obtained an obligation for member states where gmos are grown to take coexistence measures at the borders to avoid contamination in neighbouring member states where gmos are not grown.
in writing. i voted in favour because although this agreement is proof of the impossibility of finding a european answer to this question at the moment (irreconcilable differences of opinion between pro- and anti-gmo), it finally establishes legal stability for all the parties concerned, and in particular the member states. the system will allow member states who wish to cultivate gmos and those who do not wish to legally prohibit them. it is a two-speed system which is not perfect, which did not fully satisfy the pro- and anti-gmo groups, but which does get us out of the current deadlock. this agreement must be a first step towards a european solution in the medium term. we need a common response to the question of gmos to avoid distortions of competition between european farmers.

in writing. meps agreed on tuesday at noon on the principle of a compromise on the thorny issue of gmos. for years, negotiations have been blocked by the irreconcilable positions of pro- and anti-gmo groups. the answer which has been endorsed by the european parliament is imperfect. you have to admit it. the system allows member states that wish to cultivate gmos and those that are opposed to it to legally ban them. so it's a never-before-seen response that perpetuates a two-speed system. however, this compromise provides legal guarantees which are essential to curb the actions brought against member states such as france which are against the cultivation of gmos. that is why i have decided to support this approach.
in writing. i voted in favour of the agreement on the possibility for member states to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of genetically modified organisms. the agreement provides that member states wishing to grow gmos may do so and that those wishing to ban them are free to do so legally. the agreement also provides for the adoption by the member states of coexistence measures in crossborder areas to avoid contamination of traditional crops. the two-speed system is not perfect, but it does put an end to a long period of confusion and stalemate which could not satisfy anyone and which i felt it was urgent to end. it also has the merit of finally bringing legal stability to this sensitive issue. the agreement means that countries such as france which take measures to ban gmos will no longer have to justify their actions before the court of justice of the european union. i welcome the adoption of this agreement.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this text, which puts an end to a deadlock after five years of debate between the european institutions. the new legislation gives member states more freedom to decide whether to grow or ban gmos on their territory, and provides greater legal stability for all parties concerned. it is true that it has not yet been possible to find a single european response to the problem, which would have avoided distortions of competition between european farmers. however, the progress made by the new text is to be welcomed, namely the extended list of grounds for legally prohibiting the cultivation of gmos and the creation of coexistence measures in cross-border areas to avoid contamination of traditional crops by gm crops.
in writing. i voted in favour of this very important european directive on genetically modified organisms (gmos). the aim was to fill the legal vacuum which had previously existed in this field at european level by providing a common legal basis for the member states. they will now have a legislative framework to practice, restrict or prohibit the cultivation of gmos in their territory. this directive is a compromise which does not fully satisfy either the pro- or the anti-gmo groups, but which does have the merit of regulating the cultivation of gmos and their marketing within the internal market, including in cross-border areas.
in writing. the proposal for an 'à la carte' authorisation will certainly facilitate national refusals of genetically modified organisms, but it will also favour european authorisations, since the member states will no longer fear being forced by the commission to authorise the cultivation of gmos on their territory. the logic of authorization is further reinforced by the fact that the very basis of future national bans is fragile, since the articles concerned the internal market, while parliament asked that the legal basis of the text be the environment. i therefore refused to be associated with this pyrrhic victory and voted against this text. it has just broken the common european front against gmos, at the very moment when the commission is negotiating a major trade agreement with the united states. with this national approach he is scaring away european opposition to american genetically modified products. how can we continue this ban if we allow the same gmos to be grown in some european countries? this is at best a tactical error, at worst a deliberate calculation by the commission's negotiators, which i reject as a whole.
in writing. with this directive, member states will have the possibility to prohibit or allow the cultivation of gmos on their territory. the number of gm products in retail trade is likely to increase sharply in all countries as a result of free movement. this directive is therefore unacceptable.
in writing. i voted against this because it is a decoy designed to deceive the citizens. it ostensibly respects the sovereignty of states, since it allows them to prohibit the cultivation of gmos on their territory. but in reality, it does not change anything for consumers. because with the free movement of goods, gmos will come to french supermarkets from the european states that allow them. and french consumers will eat gmos without knowing it. it is therefore a text that satisfies multinational companies at the expense of the sovereignty of states and also of human health, because it must be remembered that gmos are generally designed to withstand massive doses of roundup, which is then found in food.
in writing. i am voting against this because parliament wants us to believe that a state can prevent the consumption of gmos on its territory. this is absolutely impossible in a globalised economy in the hands of multinationals, where borders no longer exist. a genuine sovereignty must allow a state to prohibit the consumption of gmos or, if necessary, to support national research independent of lobbies.
in writing. despite a misleading title, the text on gmos put to the vote is not satisfactory in several respects. it is tantamount to prohibiting the import and free movement of gmos in territories which have banned their cultivation. such a prohibition must be validated by the commission. if the plant is banned, farmers cannot exploit the technology, but consumers would still find these gmos on their plates, without any traceability. the text should therefore be voted against. the gmos imposed on us by the agrochemical multinationals and the european union are unacceptable and dangerous: increased pesticides, enslavement of farmers, ecological disasters on fauna and flora. in the interests of food sovereignty, gmo technology is acceptable in france only under three conditions: the state can decide on the improvements and properties to be made, be able to produce them on our territory according to our own uses, and control their marketing. the fn is not opposed to further reflection on this, particularly to avoid a technological gap between europe and the united states.
in writing. i voted against this recommendation which would amend directive 2001/18/ec and give member states the possibility to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of gmos on their territory. even if this text appears to restore a certain degree of sovereignty to the member states, in reality it will not do so, since the very principle of free movement within the european union distorts the situation from the outset. the ultra-liberal economic model advocated by brussels will in any case allow the import of products from third countries that allow gmos, to eu countries that prohibit them. the member states no longer have any control over their national borders, so the legislation or budgets allocated to this recommendation are just another trick. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives to improve the quality of foodstuffs and to improve the quality of life of the population. the eu, by remaining deaf to the demands of european citizens, who in the majority condemn gmos, remains subject to the agro-food lobbies. the next free trade agreement with the united states will of course only make this situation worse by introducing total deregulation.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which clarifies the possibilities for member states to allow or not to allow the cultivation of genetically modified organisms (gmos) on their territory. this text increases legal certainty and gives member states the final say on whether or not to allow the cultivation of gmos. it also provides for the adoption by member states of coexistence measures in crossborder areas to avoid contamination of traditional crops by gm crops.
in writing. on tuesday 13 january i voted in favour of the report providing for the possibility for member states to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of gmos on their territory. after five years of debate between the european parliament and the council, this text does not offer an ideal answer, but it does help to unblock the current situation. the member states will thus be able to prohibit or allow the cultivation of gmos on their soil if they so wish, without fear of legal action. until now, the lack of clear legislation has left vulnerable those states which, like france, have initiated proceedings to ban these crops. the text also provides for coexistence measures around cross-border areas to avoid contamination of traditional crops by gm crops. i support this compromise, which should eventually lead to a european response.
in writing. this new framework for the prohibition of gmo cultivation by member states may at first appear to be a positive development for ending gmo cultivation in the european union. but it is the opposite. by nationalising the decision to authorise or prohibit the cultivation of gmos, we run the risk of a great disparity in the use of gmos in europe, and thus of possible cross-border contamination, but also of a distorted competitiveness between european farmers. the pressure exerted by the large international gmo producers is well known and will now be exerted on each member state. there is therefore a strong fear that contrary to what was argued in favour of this proposal, the cultivation of gmos will be widespread in europe and will pose even more difficulties than before. for these reasons i voted against this proposal.
in writing. it is pointless to ban the cultivation of gmos when we cannot control and ban the import of gm products. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. this text is a travesty that claims to give sovereignty to the peoples while depriving them of the possibility to know what they consume. in addition, farmers in countries that ban gmos will face unfair competition from those that allow them. i therefore vote against.
in writing. the legal instability surrounding the control of gmos in the european union could have challenged the will of states not wishing to see gmos establish themselves on their territory. the text before the european parliament reflects the antagonistic positions of the member states, but nevertheless has the merit of clarifying this situation. from this point of departure, member states will now be able to establish, under the control of efsa, or not to establish, gmo crops on their territory. in addition, very strict legal criteria are now being applied to the authorisation of gmos. it should be stressed that these restrictions are accompanied by measures placing expertise on an equal footing, ensuring that consumers are prevented from finding traces of gmos in their food and creating buffer zones between member states. france will therefore be able to continue to refuse gmos on its territory, without fear of any challenge from any company or state. on the contrary, if the french population were to accept gmos one day, it could do so on the basis of scientific studies validated by the health authorities.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text and amendment no 52, which takes up the terms of the agreement concluded with the council on the sensitive issue of the cultivation of gmos. it is good that we have got out of the current impasse and have been able to overcome the 'pro' and 'anti-gmo' deadlock on this text. i supported this compromise because it takes up several key points in this dossier: firstly, the safeguarding of the european character of the system, while opening up the possibility for member states who wish to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of gmos on their own territory. secondly, on the technical level, the rebalancing of the role of undertakings and that of the member states in the two phases, and more flexibility as to the types of grounds that may be invoked to justify the ban. i also welcome the obligation to provide for an update of the directive on environmental risk assessment of gmos. finally, the obligation to avoid contamination in the event of coexistence between gm and non-gm crops. for these reasons, i supported the text, which we have reached after four years of work.
in writing. i welcome the adoption by parliament of the gmo directive (480 votes in favour, 159 against and 58 abstentions). in the past, the commission could authorise genetically modified crops in the absence of a qualified majority. however, states such as france which wished to defend their consumers and their agriculture could be condemned by the court of justice of the european union. the directive will now allow member states to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of gmos on their territory on environmental, agricultural and socioeconomic grounds. member states have two years to take measures to prevent contamination of traditional crops by gm crops in cross-border areas. in addition, the european commission has committed to review and strengthen the rules for risk assessment carried out by the european food safety authority (efsa). in voting in favour of this directive, i have chosen to strengthen the safety of member states opposed to gmos, the safety of farmers and the safety of european consumers.

in writing. with this report, the european parliament opens a loophole in the protection against genetically modified organisms. it is intended to extend the rights of member states to justify a national or regional ban on the cultivation of a gmo, but will ultimately lead to the legal weakening of such bans. first, its lack of clarity opens the door to regulatory attacks by multinational seed companies like monsanto against countries that have banned the cultivation of one of their gmos. this breach is particularly problematic at a time when the creation of private international tribunals is being negotiated in the context of ttip. moreover, the legal basis for this report is not article 192 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, which is devoted to the environment, but article 114 on the internal market. as a result, member states will not be able to invoke the precautionary principle or go beyond the minimum environmental requirements. i therefore voted against this report, in line with the demands of many european citizens who oppose gmos because of the risks they pose to their health, to biodiversity, to the diversity of cropping methods and to conventional and organic farming.

in writing. this annual report on the activities of the european ombudsman in 2013 tells us that 23 245 citizens sought the services of the ombudsman for assistance in 2013 and that 2 420 requests were registered as complaints (compared to 2 442 in 2012). the complaints concerned mainly access to documents, institutional or political issues, staff and competitions and selection procedures. this report thus shows the progress to be made in the area of transparency, both within the eu and in the member states. eu agencies are directly affected by this lack of transparency, as the share of complaints concerning them has almost doubled from 12,5% in 2012 to 24% in 2013. the european personnel selection office (epso) has seen a sharp decline, as has the european parliament, but this is a clear indication that the eu, which is so quick to give lessons in good conduct and transparency, should first learn to sweep in front of its own door. i therefore abstained on this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the ombudsman's activity in 2015. it was an opportunity to pay tribute to the work of the previous ombudsman, nikiforos diamandouros, and to reiterate my support for mrs o'reilly. the european ombudsman's task is of the utmost importance. it is a link between the european institutions and the citizens. it ensures the protection of the rights of european citizens and strengthens the democratic character of the european union. i appreciate the fact that the ombudsman is implementing new strategies to address the many transparency questions that our citizens have, particularly with regard to the negotiations for the transatlantic trade and investment partnership.
in writing. since taking up her post in october 2013, ms o'reilly has been reflecting on the role of the european ombudsman and its role in serving european citizens. as a key element of the democratisation of the european political and administrative system, the ombudsman opened 341 inquiries at the request of european citizens and nine own-initiative inquiries in 2013 and closed 441 inquiries and 20 own-initiative inquiries. it also published a new version of the european code of good administrative behaviour, while calling on the new commission to adopt binding rules and principles on the administrative procedure of the european institutions and to present a draft regulation in this regard. this work was welcomed and mrs o'reilly was confirmed in her post at the plenary session last december. for these reasons i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. accusing russia of aggravating the situation, the european parliament proposes to send arms to the government in kiev. the european union has once again failed to act as a mediator in the peace process and is leading a country towards civil war without even seeming to realize it. such a vague resolution, which is the sole responsibility of russia and does not call into question the attitude of the government in kiev, is unacceptable. i therefore vote against.
in writing. repeated violations of ceasefires by pro-russian forces are a fact. i therefore commend the courage of the members of the european parliament in reporting on the situation in ukraine. it is a matter of great indignation that the violations of the minsk agreements are undermining relations between russia and ukraine, but above all are damaging the well-being of the people.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution which condemns russia's actions in ukraine and expresses its full solidarity with it. we call on the european council in particular to put the matter on the table at the summit in march and to adopt a strict framework for determining whether or not sanctions can be lifted. in addition, ukraine needs external support to cope with the current situation: we call on the european union to act urgently in the face of the humanitarian crisis currently affecting it, and to provide more substantial technical assistance, including the secondment of advisers to help implement reforms.
in writing. in view of the difficult situation in ukraine, the european union must reiterate its support for its neighbour, who has embarked on a major reform process. we must encourage ukraine to continue its efforts to implement the eu-ukraine association agreement, including the completion of a comprehensive and deep free trade agreement. it is also imperative that russia abide by the ceasefire, withdraw russian troops and illegal armed groups from ukrainian territory and respect the territorial integrity of ukraine. finally, it should be noted that in this resolution the european parliament asks the commission to present a communication strategy in the near future to counter the various communication campaigns launched by russia and directed in particular at the eu.
in writing. with this resolution, the european parliament has once again lost an opportunity to live up to the european values of peace and dialogue between peoples. unlike the gue/ngl resolution which rejects any manichean vision, this resolution defends a unilateral pro-ukrainian stance without any nuance. by demonizing russian diplomacy and the ukrainian opposition forces, without ever mentioning other interference in the country, or even the participation of far-right ministers in the government of petro poroshenko, this text clearly takes sides in this conflict, when there is more need than ever for mediation. the european union is backsliding on its so-called values, and above all on the right of self-determination of peoples. ukraine must not become the centre of a new conflict between cold war-style imperialisms, both in the interests of its people and for the european and global geopolitical balance. likewise, more than ever, we must beware of self-fulfilling prophecies about a so-called war of civilizations. so i again opposed the resolution.
in writing. in this resolution, parliament expresses its deep concern at the widespread violation of democratic rights in egypt, condemns once again the military coup and the brutal repression by the egyptian army, deplores the loss of life and more. if everyone agrees unanimously with these beautiful phrases, it is not enough to lament, condemn and worry about solving problems, but to give our real support to those who are fighting to defend a democratic model for egypt. i voted against this text, which rejects any outside interference in order to promote democratic values and to combat persecution of all kinds (especially against women and christians).
in writing. following the overthrow of marshal mubarak in 2011, egypt experienced a period of social and religious unrest that culminated in the coming to power of mohammed morsi, a member of the muslim brotherhood, an organization affiliated with the emirate of qatar. the muslim brotherhood government has been relentless in its efforts to transform egypt into an islamist society, to demote sharia as the sole source of law and to discriminate against christians, who make up 10% of the population, while turning a blind eye to the violence against them. since the coming to power of marshal al-sissi, the egyptian government has been fighting against the attempts of the muslim brotherhood to radicalize egyptian society in order to return to power. the new egyptian constitution is the most favorable to religious minorities that egypt has ever had. president al-sissi, a devout muslim himself, attended the christmas mass celebrated by the coptic orthodox pope in solidarity with egyptian christians. for all these reasons, i think that the european parliament should support the reformist intentions of the egyptian government rather than try to impose sanctions on it to prevent it from fighting the muslim brotherhood.
in writing. three years after the egyptian people's uprising and the resignation of hosni mubarak, and since the fall of the muslim brotherhood-led morsi government, egypt is ruled by general al-sissi. the situation is catastrophic, with a near-permanent civil war, and repressive measures have been taken. the new constitution, however, was approved by 98% of egyptians and president al-sissi was elected with 96% of the vote (doubling the number of votes of former president morsi). in the face of the rise of radical islamism and muslim fundamentalism in the arab world, which have tried to surf the post-arab spring and the vacuum left, the situation is still not serene and it is clear that only stability will allow these countries like egypt to find the path of progress and democratization in order to avoid the grip of the sharia. i therefore voted against this text, which does not solve the situation in any way.

mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, in the last few days, it seems to me that the debate has made some progress on one point: the fight against terrorism involves seeking a balance between the need to ensure the security of the union and its citizens on the one hand, and to guarantee respect for fundamental freedoms and rights on the other. i believe we have also made progress in the idea that the fight against terrorism is far from being a purely technical matter within the purely security logic. radicalisation is a multifaceted, evolving and multidimensional phenomenon, developing both within the union and beyond its borders. the european response must therefore favour a transversal, global, long-term approach and involve a multiplicity of actors. among the areas of action to be developed, i would like to support the avenues already mentioned, such as improving the exchange of information between member states and with the union agencies europol, eurojust , improving the implementation of the schengen information system, combating the financing of terrorism and the illegal trade in firearms, or optimising the full potential of the internet in terms of awareness-raising while effectively combating its misuse. in this set of actions, the social and cultural dimension of the fight against terrorism must not be cosmetic or declarative, but must generate concrete actions on the ground. let us not forget that radicalisation often arises from disarray and lack of prospects. finally, do not fall into the trap that is set before us. the debate today should not be treated with emotion and haste, with the emergency services on the one hand and the homeopaths on the other. if no one is defending the status quo, we must act thoughtfully, based in particular on a precise assessment of existing european tools and their implementation.

mr president, the internet must be a space of freedom, respecting the right to information and freedom of expression, but it must also respect the right to be forgotten, which is a fundamental aspect of the right to privacy and the protection of personal data. the right to be forgotten was enshrined on 13 may 2014 by a judgment of the court of justice of the european union. it allows anyone who has been harmed by information published on the internet to oblige the operator of the search engine concerned to withdraw it when a reasonable period of exposure, of the order of several years, has been exceeded. this is an important judgment, but it is not enough. google is trying to resist this: on february 6, 2015, it published a report that calls into question the right to be forgotten. this is why the internet governance forum must take over from the court. three points in particular need to be clarified urgently. first, the period of time after which information may be subject to the right to be forgotten; secondly, the balance to be struck between this right to be forgotten and the public's right to information. and thirdly, the possibility of giving the right to be forgotten a non-european dimension, which is particularly necessary in the face of the american version of google.

in writing. the purpose of this report is to propose a regulation to lay down specific provisions to enable the union, where it deems it appropriate, to bring a measure taken under regulation (ec) no 1225/2009 (anti-dumping measures) or (ec) no 597/2009 (anti-subsidy measures) into conformity. in practice, this means that the contested measure is repealed or amended or that another implementing measure is adopted. it is not normal that the member states cannot retain a full margin of manoeuvre in external relations, especially trade, since the disparities and demands are too different from one country to another in the union. moreover, this regulation subjects us to the european commission, which imposes compliance, which is in fact the aim of the dispute settlement body, which is an offshoot of the wto. i therefore voted against this report.

in writing. the european parliament proposes to adopt the commission's proposal for a regulation which would allow it to repeal or amend a measure challenged by a report of the dispute settlement body (dsb). in addition, the commission would be competent to adopt any other implementing measures necessary to bring union law into line with the recommendations of the dsb. because i formally challenge the primacy of eu law over national law, especially when its implementation involves complying with the highly questionable injunctions of the wto, i am opposed to the european commission being able to arbitrarily amend a law which particularly affects the commercial practice of the member states. the proposal for a regulation is part of a strategy to strengthen the european commission's prerogatives in international law. i am committed to preserving france's room for manoeuvre on the international economic scene and therefore voted against this text.
in writing. codification of legislative texts is a kind of compilation of different european regulations dealing with the same subject. the aim of codification is to simplify european legislation and make it more accessible. in this particular case, we are talking about the codification of legislation on anti-dumping or anti-subsidy measures. it is essential to have maximum clarity and precision on these matters. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. i voted against this text, which represents an attempt to erase our sovereignty by a supranational structure. the ability to conduct trade negotiations is an indispensable lever for ensuring the prosperity and freedom of any nation state. the dispute settlement body, which is the wto's replacement, is therefore presented as a mechanism for global or even globalised management, that is to say, to the detriment of dialogue between sovereign states. moreover, it is not the european commission's job to represent the interests different, or even divergent, in some cases of each member state of the union.
in writing. this report proposes to codify into eu law council regulation (ec) no 1515/2001 on the measures that the community may take following a report adopted by the wto dispute settlement body concerning anti-dumping or anti-subsidy measures, as substantially amended in 2014. this text allows the union, when it deems it appropriate, to take trade defence measures, namely anti-dumping or anti-subsidy measures, in accordance with the recommendations and decisions contained in a report adopted by the dispute settlement body (dsb) of the world trade organisation concerning these measures. i support this text, which is merely a codification of positive law without any change in substance. for these reasons i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. with this vote, the european parliament is demonstrating its desire to encourage greater transparency in european law. the consolidation of the regulation on the measures that the union may take following a report adopted by the wto dispute settlement body on anti-dumping or anti-subsidy measures is indeed in the right direction. this brings clarity to a text that has undergone many changes.
in writing. the dispute settlement body is a new tool created by the world trade organisation to bring national laws into line with the requirements of the wto and multinational companies. the european union facilitates the interference of organisations which are totally foreign to the interests of the member states. reasons why i voted against this text. it believes that the only way to return to a realistic and effective economic policy is to pursue national policies. the member states have interests so divergent that it is obviously impossible to accord them all, so much so that only germany today benefits from the policies of a union which is subject to it. the freedom of each country to protect itself and to develop economic patriotism is one of the alternative solutions to this perishing economic system.

in writing. i voted against this proposal on the possibilities for the union to take anti-dumping or anti-subsidy measures for two reasons: firstly, the introduction of these measures is conditional on the adoption of a report adopted by the wto dispute settlement body, which already leads to a loss of reactivity that leaves the field open to the dumping states. on the other hand, experience shows that the european commission has never been quick to defend the interests of europeans in the face of distortions of competition imposed by third countries. in view of this failure, it is essential that the member states should be able to react to these anti-competitive practices without waiting for a hypothetical action by the european union.

in writing. the aim of anti-dumping and countervailing measures is to remedy market distortions created by unfair trade practices, whereas the aim of safeguard tariff measures is to protect against a sharp increase in imports. the european commission considers that the combination of the two against a single product may have a greater impact than expected in the light of the union's trade defence policy and objectives. the commission considered that such a combination could impose an unjustified burden on certain exporting producers seeking to export to the union and deny them access to the union market. the commission submits that it is not always possible to determine in advance the precise moment when such overlap will occur, and therefore it seizes the opportunity to be able to modify, suspend or repeal anti-dumping and/or countervailing measures at its discretion or to provide for total or partial exemption from anti-dumping or countervailing duties. this decision seems to be an aberration, since this regulation will allow the european commission to deprive itself of the few protectionist tools at its disposal. i therefore naturally spoke out against this text, which is based on a logic which goes against the expectations of my fellow citizens.
in writing. i voted against this ideological text which favours free trade to the detriment of our manufacturing industries. our productive forces are being competed with by countries where labour and production costs are very low and the european union is preventing member states from protecting themselves in the name of the principle of free movement of capital and goods. the timid measures taken against unfair competition are proving ineffective in the face of an entire system which is destroying our productive apparatus. these small steps were however quickly reversed by political forces fiercely committed to defending globalisation and assuming their refusal to accept that countries wishing to export to the union bear "unjustified financial burdens", thus sweeping away the outline of european protectionism.
in writing. in this text, the parliament and the council question what they consider to be a danger of protectionism which, in respect of certain imported goods only, would result from the simultaneous application of anti-dumping and countervailing measures on the one hand and safeguard tariff measures on the other. the purpose of the proposed regulation is to enable the commission in cases where it considers that exporters seeking to export to the union are being overly penalized by financial burdens or by prohibitions on access to the union market to amend, suspend or repeal existing anti-dumping and/or countervailing measures or even to exempt imports from anti-dumping/countervailing duties which would otherwise have to be paid. this appalling sacrifice of the national interests of the member states in favour of the free trade dogma, which rejects any idea of protectionism, national or continental, once again demonstrates the absurdity of the union's economic and trade policy. i voted against this text, of course.
in writing. this report proposes a regulation which lays down specific provisions to allow the commission to act at its discretion, so as to avoid that a combination of anti-dumping or countervailing measures and safeguard tariff measures against the same product imposes an unjustified burden on certain exporting producers seeking to export to the union, and thereby denies them access to the union market. even if the regulations provide for anti-dumping clauses through collective action measures or a national safeguard clause (which is now heavily reduced), the text is based on the principle that the union must allow exporters seeking to export to the union not to be penalised by financial burdens or by prohibitions on access to the union market. the commission is not thereby derogating from the rule of the sacred dogma of free and undistorted competition and is no longer hesitating to promote the interests of the member states by prohibiting all protectionism even as the number of barriers to trade in many countries of the world continues to grow, directly affecting european-based industries and services. i therefore voted against this regulation.
in writing. even when it comes under the union's competence, trade policy is not entirely common. member states have the possibility of taking measures against third states, and even against member states. but the freedom to take action within the community is being reduced more and more. the former ec treaty (article 134) provided for a national safeguard clause, the scope of which is now considerably reduced. collective defence measures are also provided for, in particular against dumping. the text deals with the combined effects of these two types of measures. i voted against this text, in particular the adaptation of recitals 7 and 8 which state that 'it should therefore be ensured that exporting producers seeking to export to the union do not bear unjustified financial burdens and can continue to have access to the union market. it is therefore desirable that the objectives of the safeguard measures and of the anti-dumping and/or countervailing measures can be achieved without the exporting producers concerned being denied access to the union market.'
in writing. the proposal for a regulation of the council and of the european parliament codifies council regulation (ec) no 452/2003 of 6 march 2003 on the measures which the european community may take in respect of anti-dumping measures. in concrete terms, this new regulation will allow the commission to take discretionary action against a member state in the field of anti-dumping legislation. if the commission considers that a combination of anti-dumping measures against an imported product creates an unjustified burden for certain exporters, it will be entitled to amend, suspend or repeal any legal or regulatory provisions, and even to provide for total or partial exemption from anti-dumping duties. the granting of this power is a scandal and must be strongly condemned. it is for the member states, not the commission, to decide in a sovereign manner whether an anti-dumping measure is proportionate to the risk posed by the importation of a product. that is why i voted against this text.

in writing. the purpose of the proposal for a regulation of the council and the european parliament is to codify council regulation (ec) no 260/2009 of 19 october 2009 establishing common rules for imports. i am, in essence, hostile to this type of text which facilitates free trade and puts member states and their economies in the grip of unbridled globalisation. as regards the form, i note that it allows certain surveillance and safeguard measures to be taken in the interests of producers, particularly in the event of massive imports likely to cause them serious damage. however, member states must be able to take back control of tariff and non-tariff quota competence when vital economic and agricultural sectors are directly threatened by unfair competition. the current state of the legislation is still more than vague, so i voted against.

in writing. the hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction was established in 1980. all the member states of the european union are signatories to this convention. this private international law legislation imposes a uniform legal basis for the abduction of a child by one of the parents in the event of a bi-national separation. sometimes a parent abducts a child and is given legal custody in their home state. the other parent is then obliged to comply with this decision because of a lack of legal uniformity between the two states of which the parents are nationals. such situations must not happen again. we must ensure that children's rights are applied in the same way all over the world. i voted in favour of gabon's accession to the hague convention.

in writing. this report proposes to support the accession of the gabonese republic to the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction. this international agreement, ratified by all eu member states, aims to establish a system of cooperation in the field of international child abduction, most often in cases of separation or divorce of binational couples. if the courts of both states concerned are seised, they may declare that they have jurisdiction and each of them may award custody of the child to the parent who is a national of the state in which he or she is domiciled. the convention thus specifies the jurisdiction of national courts and guarantees a system for the immediate return of the child who has been abducted. it is necessary that this international regime be as broad as possible, especially in view of the fact that the european union has many citizens of gabonese origin on its soil. this will protect children linked to this community from illegal abductions. that is why i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. i voted in favour of this text which approves the accession of andorra to the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction. the convention is a major instrument in the fight against the illegal detention and removal of children as a result of family conflict. in concrete terms, it provides for cooperation mechanisms to resolve conflicts of jurisdiction between courts in the event of a bi-national couple's separation. it also guarantees a system of return in the event of abduction. the more states that sign the convention, the more children's rights will be effectively guaranteed at international level.
