in writing. i voted in favour of this text which allows andorra to accede to the hague convention on international child abduction. this multilateral treaty protects children who are abducted outside their place of usual residence. since the opinion of the court of justice of 14 october 2014, the european union has exclusive competence for the acceptance of a new state to the convention. these kidnappings, which are becoming more frequent in cases of divorce between couples of two nationalities, give rise to dramatic situations which require a rapid response from the public authorities. accession to the convention will facilitate cooperation between the european and andorran judicial authorities in organising the speedy return of abducted children, so that the competent local judge can make a decision on the person responsible for the child's custody.

in writing. the hague convention was established in 1980. this convention deals with the civil aspects of international child abduction. the member states of the european union are all signatories. it was important to create such an institution. indeed, far too often we hear of parents who kidnap a child and obtain custody of the child in their home countries without first consulting the parent who was the victim of the kidnapping. this situation cannot last. the legal systems of the countries must cooperate on this important issue for the protection of children. i voted in favour of seychelles joining the hague convention.
in writing. i refused to sign in favour of this report for a simple reason: an international convention is a legal norm that must be signed by sovereign states. the european union does not have this legal status and its legitimacy is therefore questionable as regards its legal capacity to become a party to the hague convention. it is clear, however, that child abduction is a very serious problem and that it is therefore important that states continue to cooperate actively to prevent these tragedies and to deal with the civilian aspects of them.
in writing. this report proposes to support the accession of the republic of seychelles to the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction. this international agreement, ratified by all eu member states, aims to establish a system of cooperation in the field of international child abduction, most often in cases of separation or divorce of binational couples. if the courts of both states concerned are seised, they may declare that they have jurisdiction and each of them may award custody of the child to the parent who is a national of the state in which he or she is domiciled. the convention thus specifies the jurisdiction of national courts and guarantees a system for the immediate return of the child who has been abducted. it is necessary that this international regime be as broad as possible. this will protect children linked to this community from illegal abductions. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the hague convention of 25 october 1980, which has been ratified by all the member states of the european union, aims to protect children from international kidnapping by providing a procedure for their speedy return. the vote on this text is an invitation to the council of the european union to ask the member states to accept the accession of the seychelles. the extension of the territorial scope of the convention to the islands and islets of the seychelles is in line with a fundamental objective of the european union to strengthen the protection of children at international level. i therefore supported the text.

in writing. the convention establishes a system for contracting states to cooperate in finding a solution to cases of international child abduction. this situation usually arises when a couple divorce or separate. the explanatory memorandum to the report states that 'the major problem is the nationalist conception underlying the legal system of the states'. that is why, like my frontist colleagues in the legal affairs committee of the european parliament, i question the legal capacity of the european union to become a party to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of child abduction. this approval for albania must not be a matter for europe and i therefore voted against it. moreover, when we know that albania is a hub for child trafficking at european level, we can only disapprove of this request until these internal problems are resolved.
in writing. the hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction was established on 25 october 1980. the member states of the european union have all ratified it. all too often we hear of cases of child abduction by a parent who obtains custody of the child in his/her home country when a binational couple separates. a uniform legal basis for determining the court with jurisdiction in such matters is essential. we must ensure the protection of children who are victims of abduction. i voted in favour of this resolution approving albania's accession to the hague convention.
in writing. i refused to sign in favour of this report for a simple reason: an international convention is a legal norm that must be signed by sovereign states. the european union does not have this legal status and its legitimacy is therefore questionable as regards its legal capacity to become a party to the hague convention. it is clear, however, that child abduction is a very serious problem and that it is therefore important that states continue to cooperate actively to prevent these tragedies and to deal with the civilian aspects of them.
in writing. this report proposes to support the accession of the republic of albania to the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction. this international agreement, ratified by all eu member states, aims to establish a system of cooperation in the field of international child abduction, most often in cases of separation or divorce of binational couples. if the courts of both states concerned are seised, they may declare that they have jurisdiction and each of them may award custody of the child to the parent who is a national of the state in which he or she is domiciled. the convention thus specifies the jurisdiction of national courts and guarantees a system for the immediate return of the child who has been abducted. it is necessary that this international regime be as broad as possible, especially in view of the fact that the european union has many citizens of albanian origin on its soil. this will protect children linked to this community from illegal abductions. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the hague convention of 25 october 1980, which has been ratified by all the member states of the european union, aims to protect children from international kidnapping by providing a procedure for their speedy return. the vote on this text is an invitation to the council of the european union to ask the member states to accept the accession of the republic of albania. the extension of the convention's territorial scope to albania is in the right direction to ensure the best possible protection of the child in situations of international abduction.

in writing. this report proposes to support the accession of the republic of armenia to the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction. this international agreement, ratified by all eu member states, aims to establish a system of cooperation in the field of international child abduction, most often in cases of separation or divorce of binational couples. if the courts of both states concerned are seised, they may declare that they have jurisdiction and each of them may award custody of the child to the parent who is a national of the state in which he or she is domiciled. the convention thus specifies the jurisdiction of national courts and guarantees a system for the immediate return of the child who has been abducted. it is necessary that this international regime be as broad as possible, especially in view of the fact that the european union has many citizens of armenian origin on its soil. this will protect children linked to this community from illegal abductions. that is why i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. this report is identical to directive 2011/82/eu which was annulled by the court of justice. the text before us here therefore alters the legal basis. the proposal for a directive aims to facilitate the cross-border exchange of information on road safety offences committed in a member state other than that in which the vehicle in question was registered. it should be noted that three countries will have permission to delay the implementation of this proposal: the united kingdom, denmark and ireland. in principle, while it is necessary that foreign drivers who take advantage of the current system without exchanging data can be prosecuted when they commit offences, the question of data protection at european level must nevertheless be raised. the road safety policy must also be reviewed. the commission is only moving towards a policy of systematic repression of motorists (it is true that radar and other fines bring considerable revenues to the states) while the question of road infrastructure or the development of public transport - especially in rural areas to provide an alternative to motorists - is avoided. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which promotes the crossborder exchange of information on the most serious road safety offences: drunk driving, driving under the influence of drugs, failure to wear a seatbelt, etc. the text will make it possible, while respecting fundamental freedoms and the protection of personal data, to make the sanction more systematic for drivers who commit serious offences in a member state other than that in which their vehicle is registered. the aim is to improve the protection of all european road users.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on facilitating the crossborder exchange of information on road safety offences. this proposal for a directive is a step forward for the protection of road users in the european union, as it promotes exchanges between the member states' traffic and road safety authorities. for example, when an individual commits an offence outside the state in which his vehicle is registered, his data is communicated to the responsible authorities. the directive, which will ensure equal treatment for european drivers, will also be applied in the united kingdom, ireland and denmark. harmonisation of information exchange is necessary to ensure the safety of users of european road networks.
in writing. i voted for this report because it allows the member states' traffic and road safety authorities to request the transmission of the data of the owner of a vehicle registered outside the member state in which it is used, if the owner has committed an offence considered to be very dangerous, in order to be able to notify the individual of the offence committed.

in writing. i am a driver myself and i understand that some may not like the approval of cross-border exchange of information on traffic offences, but we must remember that this is also a matter of life and health. statistics clearly show that the current 'impunity' of drivers for offenses abroad has led to more safety violations outside the country where the vehicle is registered than in the home country. however, those who break the rules, including traffic rules, are to be held accountable according to the standards of the place where they are. for this reason, this standard deserves support.
in writing. the increase in border crossings in the european union has revealed the inability of police authorities to enforce traffic sanctions, as they are unable to locate european motorists. the road safety requirement requires a greater capacity for cooperation by the national authorities and i therefore welcome an effective mechanism to finally deal with this issue.
in writing. the european exchange of information on the most serious traffic offences is an essential element in the fight against road crime in europe. that is why i support this directive, which prevents us from going back to the time when these offences committed by motorists from other member states went unpunished. we had already adopted a directive to this effect in 2011, but under pressure from the council, police cooperation was chosen as the legal basis instead of road safety. the united kingdom, ireland and denmark had thus taken advantage of an opt-out clause to exempt themselves. in may 2014, the court of justice of the european union logically invalidated the directive while giving us a one-year deadline to adopt a new legal basis. that is what we are doing today, despite the irresponsibility of some members who are following an ideology when it comes to saving lives. in europe, nearly 30 000 people, including over 3 000 in france, die on the roads every year. at a time when road violence is on the rise again in our country, it is abnormal not to support this measure.
in writing. in this new directive, cooperation between member states is strengthened with a stricter enforcement obligation for recalcitrant countries such as the united kingdom, ireland and denmark. in addition, this new version takes into account the issue of the protection of personal data by building on directive 95/46/ec. this text is a breakthrough which marks a return to the issue of road safety at european level. it is worth noting that 73 europeans die every day on european roads and 250,000 are seriously injured every year. in france, the number of road deaths increased in 2014, the first time in 12 years. europe has a key role to play in addressing this scourge. cooperation on sanctions against all drivers who commit offences with impunity, provided they are committed in another country, is a first step. this demonstrates a desire to apply sanctions consistently. we regret that the commission does not go further by proposing harmonisation of legislation, particularly in the field of speed limits and alcohol consumption, which remain the main causes of accidents.
in writing. i supported the resolution on the directive facilitating the exchange of information on road traffic offences. the aim of the vote is to extend to the uk, ireland and denmark a major 2011 directive ending the anonymity of drivers who commit road traffic offences outside their member state of residence. following the court's judgment, a revised legal basis and clearer data protection provisions, we will avoid, through the sharing of vehicle registration data, that offences go unpunished on the grounds that they were committed 'abroad': within two years, offenders will be able to receive their fines at home, regardless of the eu country where the offence occurred. in my country, the stakes of this text are high: more than 20% of the road traffic offences detected by speed and red light radar are committed by drivers of vehicles registered outside france. i don't know anybody who likes to get a "p.o". but this is about road safety, equal treatment of road users and serious offences for which national exceptions or impunity were certainly not a good signal.
in writing. i supported this text which concerns an important aspect of the freedom of movement of european citizens and their safety on the road. a road traffic offence committed in a member state other than the one in which the offending vehicle is registered is subject to penalties. the transport policy of the european union must maintain a high level of protection for all road users and must also be harmonised in its application. this requires a consistent and uniform application of penalties for infringements committed on european roads.
in writing. i voted in favour of this directive, which makes it possible to ensure that drivers in the european union do not go unpunished for traffic offences. in france, 21 per cent of all traffic offences involving speeding or crossing red lights are committed by foreign-registered drivers. the text allows the exchange of registration files between european countries in order to locate the owner of the car in infringement. the european police are involved in such cases as speeding, crossing red lights, driving under the influence of drugs, failure to wear a motorcycle helmet, the illicit use of a mobile phone and driving on a prohibited road. this directive had already entered into force at the end of 2013, but due to legal problems, its form had to be revised. the adoption of the new text today puts an end to legal uncertainty and will promote a safer road, particularly in border areas.
in writing. the purpose of the report is to facilitate the cross-border exchange of information on road safety offences by requiring member states to transmit road traffic offences committed on their territory to the member state of origin of the driver. because of the impossibility of integrating motorists' associations into the process and of limiting the application of the directive to the most serious offences, thus resulting in excessive penalties for the most minor offences, i shall vote against this report.

in writing. i voted in favour of this recommendation, which aims to allow eu vessels to fish in senegalese waters. the commission has already proposed that the fishing fleet be increased to 38 french and spanish vessels, which will be able to catch 14 000 tonnes of tuna and 2 000 tonnes of hake per year. in return, we will invest €750,000 a year in the development of senegal's port infrastructure. it is therefore an agreement that will benefit both the eu and senegal, while respecting the principle of 'sustainable fisheries'. the rapporteur of the draft resolution of 21 november 2014, norica nicolai, said that the cod stocks in senegalese waters were not being exploited optimally, so that 'the demersal species could be increased ... in the framework of a future agreement between the european union and the republic of senegal, without affecting the state of the resources too much'.

in writing. the protocol to the fisheries agreement between the european union and senegal has been renegotiated by the european commission for a period of five years. under the agreement, three categories of vessels will be allowed to fish in senegalese waters: 28 tuna seiners, 8 longliners and 2 spanish trawlers. the protocol contains clauses on the suspension and denunciation of fishing activities in the event of violations of human rights or commitments to combat illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. i voted in favour of this report approving the conclusion of this agreement.
in writing. i wanted to vote in favour of this text, which offers great prospects for our fishermen. the agreement gives 28 tuna vessels, 8 reels and 2 trawlers the possibility of fishing up to 14 000 tonnes of tuna and 2000 tonnes of black hake. this agreement is therefore in favour of the french fishing industry, and moreover with senegal, a country with which france continues to have close relations because of their common history. senegal will also benefit from this agreement, as it will receive eur 1 808 000 for these fishing authorizations for the first year, including eur 750 000 per year for the development of senegal's sectoral policy. a text that therefore enshrines a win-win agreement that every french patriot, concerned about france's industrial and commercial interests, had to vote for.

in writing. a report released by the us senate on 9 december 2014 shed light on the secret program used by the cia to interrogate suspected al-qaeda militants after 9/11. the report accuses the agency of subjecting several detainees to brutal techniques for several years. it was concluded that the cia's torture methods were ineffective. the joint resolution of the epp and ecr groups stresses that the fight against terrorism and respect for human rights are not contradictory but complementary. transatlantic cooperation based on these common values and respect for fundamental rights is a priority in the european union's external relations. our resolution here welcomes the report of the special committee of the us senate, which is a positive step forward in the public opposition and criticism of the cia detention and interrogation programme and which demonstrates the willingness of the american political circles, with the support of members of both parties represented in congress, to hold the public accountable for the cia programme.
in writing. i voted against this text and supported the resolution put forward by the epp and the ecr, because the text was more balanced and respected the national prerogatives of the member states. it recalled the importance of human rights, condemned advanced interrogation techniques and called on the member states concerned to conduct their investigations seriously. the resolution adopted calls on the libe committee to conduct an inquiry, although it has neither the legitimacy nor the means to do so. the result cannot be serious.
in writing. this resolution concerns the recent us senate report on the use of torture by the cia. some countries of the european union have been involved and blamed, more or less directly, for these practices. the report confirms the allegations of the cia's transporting and illegally holding prisoners in secret prisons located in certain member states of the european union. equally serious, the report mentions probable corruption, once again demonstrating the submission of some eu countries to the us. this proposal in fact hinders and complicates the fight against terrorism. i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. i would first like to welcome the us senate report on the use of torture by the cia and the measures taken by the us president to close guantanamo. the resolution on which the european parliament was to deal first was mainly led by a socialist alliance, thus excluding the ppe group. i therefore voted against the first resolution, because the resolution proposed by the epp group was more balanced and more practical. while transparency requirements are crucial, they must not be detrimental to the primary objective of combating terrorism. as the epp group proposed in its resolution, while maintaining a firm stance against torture, it is necessary to emphasize cooperation between states and the establishment of mutual trust.
in writing. by instructing the civil liberties committee to resume its investigation into allegations of the cia's transportation and illegal detention of prisoners in european countries, the european parliament allows the work begun in 2006 by its temporary committee to continue. the european parliament is all the more concerned about shedding light on these operations and establishing the responsibilities of each individual, since the us senate report clearly establishes the complicity of a number of member states in the cia programme. it does not merely confirm the existence of secret prisons on european soil or the practice of torture in its most abominable forms. it also reveals - and this is new - probable facts of corruption. some member states have reportedly accepted money in exchange for their cooperation with the cia. these are all matters which the european parliament will have to investigate. making complicity transparent, revealing the truth and bringing justice will not make terrorism a reality, quite the contrary. it is a fight for our values and a fight for a strengthened democracy. that is what the european parliament has voted for today.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution which condemns the use of illegal interrogation practices. respect for fundamental rights and the rule of law is essential, including in counter-terrorism policies. i welcome the decision of the us senate intelligence committee to release the report on the cia's detention and interrogation program. it is now the duty of the united states to investigate and prosecute the practices of your agency and we invite you to do so. beyond the conviction, we urge member states to shed light on the allegations against them: people detained in the framework of the cia programme, torture or illicit transport of prisoners. to this end, our committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs has been instructed to carry out an inquiry and to publish the results within a year.
in writing. i voted against this joint resolution by the s&d, alde, greens, gue and efdd groups because, in my opinion, the resolution by the epp and the ecr was more balanced and measured. our resolution strongly condemned the cia's interrogation practices and welcomed the publication of the report of the u.s. senate select committee on the agency's deviant program. we called on president obama to continue his efforts to close the detention centre at the us military base in guantanamo and to release the detainees who have not been charged. however, i am not convinced that the establishment of a special european parliament committee of inquiry into the participation of european countries in the cia programme, as proposed in the joint resolution, is effective or appropriate. the commission of inquiry would have neither the means, the competence nor the legitimacy to carry out such a mission.
in writing. nearly 15 years after the beginning of the cia's abduction, internment in third countries and torture programs, when the facts were known and exploited even by the cinema since at least 2005, we are lucky to see today an act of repentance by america and european states that participated in them. america has used methods that are dishonorable to its values and those who have followed in europe have dishonored the values of europe. it is the following and the forgetting of values that have given rise to torture. as in ukraine today, the same forgetfulness, the same pro-american following and the same dishonor. will it take 15 years for you to say, "we didn't know, we're sorry"? the european parliament will also have to make its mea culpa.
mr president, there are good things in the resolution that has just been voted, but there is also, i think, a certain angelicality. one essential factor, for example, is not mentioned: it is the breeding ground for terrorism and, in particular, the fact that it is the product of a massive immigration from mainly muslim countries, a part of whose population - not all of them, of course - is sensitive to the literal and bellicose interpretation of the qur'anic texts. where did the kouachi brothers, who are responsible for the murders at the charlie hebdo editorial office in paris, come from? where did the coulibalys come from, responsible for murders in a hidden grocery store and an assassination attempt against police officers in nice? how did they become french? what had they done to justify their presence on national territory? what was the status of these men? who had provided for them? these are questions which the french government does not ask, because they would lead to a review of the questions of substance. this is also the major shortcoming of the resolution which has just been adopted.
in writing. in the face of the growing danger of terrorism in europe, whether imported, financed from outside or developing more or less autonomously on the territory of the member states, i share the european parliament's desire to deal with the problem. the proposed measures are unfortunately not up to the task, such as data exchanges, which are too timid a solution. the real measures to combat terrorism are not even mentioned, in particular the recovery of sovereignty by states over the control of their borders in order to control the flows that cross them and the assessment of the financial participation of certain extra-european powers in the development of international terrorism in europe. so i decided to abstain.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution because the measures adopted make it possible to strengthen the security of citizens who reside in the territory of the european union.
in writing. while the european union is continuing its negotiations with turkey, which lets jihadists come and go, while the libyan authorities what remains of them are warning us of the risk of jihadist infiltration among illegal immigrants, the only concrete measure proposed by the eurobieats is to follow the anglo-saxon model and to check airline passengers. but all the intelligence experts tell us that our security services do not have the means to monitor the thousands of suspects already on our soil. i could not therefore support the irresponsible blindness of these measurements.
in writing. your proposals to fight terrorism at european level seem to be just another trick with "measures" to make a good impression after the tragic events that have hit france. after the debates we had in the last plenary, i can only make a sad observation about the impotence in the face of terrorism, which is the result of years of laxity on the part of the union and the governments of most member states. that is why i have drafted and tabled with colleagues a european motion for a resolution on the immediate suspension of the schengen agreements, in accordance with article 2 (2), with the aim of re-establishing border controls and preventing the terrorist threat. in addition, we ask the commission to draw up a list of passenger name records (pnr) and to add a list of passengers who are not allowed to fly. finally, it is high time to stop indulging in illusions and the union must also and above all stop all negotiations for the accession of new countries to the union, such as turkey or the balkan countries. i still abstained on that report.
in writing. threats to our continent are increasing. our people and our values are in danger from terrorism. some european citizens are beheaded in conflict zones and then brought to europe. these events are one of the consequences of the lack of awareness of our governments in managing migration flows. we have left the doors of europe wide open. we are paying the price today. the asylum system can therefore present many problems. this means that jihadists can infiltrate via lampedusa, among other places. the restoration of the internal borders of the union would make it possible to strengthen controls in order to effectively protect the population against this terror. i abstained on this resolution which hardly raises the problems and does not propose the solutions which are necessary in the light of these events.
in writing. the paris attacks have re-ignited the debate on the appropriate european measures to combat terrorism. the resolution adopted by the european parliament proposes certain measures for prevention and cooperation between member states. it was important that parliament should speak with one voice on a subject so important and unfortunate that the greens and the far left did not understand it. however, it does not offer a real and immediate solution, which is what the situation requires. the measures proposed by the epp were, however, concrete: judicial and police cooperation, reinforced controls at external borders and the rapid adoption of a european pnr. we must find european solutions to combat terrorism. the establishment of a european pnr is one of these solutions. i find it regrettable that the socialists and liberals are still dogmatically opposed to a european nrp, which is necessary. i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. i voted for this motion for a resolution because the preventive measures it proposes to stem the wave of radicalisation we are experiencing and especially the european responses it gives to fill the gaps in the legislation in force in our member states are appropriate. the schengen rules need to be optimized, because only improved police and judicial cooperation between member states will make it possible to guarantee freedom of movement at european level. we must take action: the fight against crossborder crime requires a stricter use of border controls. in this context, the european pnr should no longer be an option but a matter of course. we have to make sacrifices and find a balance between civil liberties and security. there is no doubt that enhancing the exchange of intelligence is enhancing the security of our countries. however, one thing is missing from this resolution, and i regret it, and that is the creation of a european prosecutor's office, which is necessary of its own accord. europol cannot take over everything. today the alleged perpetrators are arrested, but it is very difficult to try them, for reasons of the jurisdiction of the national courts. i therefore welcome the establishment of this european prosecutor.
in writing. the urgent need was indeed to adopt a text on measures to be taken to combat terrorism. i would like to stress the imperfection of this text, however: it is a case of 'social terrorism', where we worry about the rise of fundamentalism on the one hand, but reaffirm the validity of schengen on the other. the european parliament's resolution on the schengen agreement is a welcome step towards the conclusion of the schengen agreement. the measures proposed are more a matter of evangelicalism than a pragmatic analysis of reality: if potential jihadists are becoming radicalised, it is because society stigmatises them. yet despite these imperfections, we must support everything that goes in the direction of the war on terrorism; that is why i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. this resolution calls on the european union to respond without delay to the terrorist threats it faces. the european union should promote cooperation between member states by allowing the adoption of a harmonised definition of the phenomenon of 'foreign fighters', by stepping up the prevention of and the fight against radicalisation, particularly in prisons, and by supporting deradicalisation programmes. it should also strengthen the tools available by making more efficient use of the schengen information system, the possibilities for control at the union's external borders and the capacities of europol and eurojust. finally, the union must have a legislative arsenal which respects the freedoms and rights of european citizens, but which is effective, with a rapid agreement on the pnr directive and the creation of a european system for monitoring the financing of terrorism. i believe that this resolution strikes a balance between the necessary objective of data protection and the imperative of the security of european citizens, and i therefore voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. while this joint resolution contains some interesting proposals, i regret that we have not reached a satisfactory agreement on the issue of the european pnr. i therefore reject the strict link between the progress of the negotiations on the european pnr and the negotiations on the data protection package. while it is essential for the european union to have a clear legislative framework to guarantee the fundamental right to the protection of personal data, the slowness of its negotiation should not be used as an argument to hold back the urgent adoption of a tool essential to the fight against terrorism in europe. strengthening security and protecting fundamental rights are not incompatible. we must stop taking the security of european citizens hostage.
in writing. the european parliament has demonstrated europe's capacity to act by adopting by a very large majority its resolution on counter-terrorism measures. the answer must be a firm one within the natural framework of our rule of law. the aim is to put in place a comprehensive strategy to combat radicalisation and terrorism by optimising the existing legal frameworks, including the fight against money laundering, the european arrest warrant, the introduction of systematic checks at the schengen external borders, but also to go further by setting up a european pnr, strengthening the powers of europol and eurojust, creating a european prosecutor and monitoring exchanges and networks on the internet.

in writing. improving existing tools, strengthening the exchange of information between states, internal security, financing of terrorist organisations, europol powers, police cooperation, judicial cooperation, coordination, relations with third countries, etc.: the resolution we adopted lists the measures to be taken in the fight against terrorism in the wake of the horrific attacks on charlie hebdo. in the fight against terrorism, at the level of the european union, there are two urgent issues. firstly, to improve the functioning of the arsenal of tools which the european union already has in the fight against terrorism and, above all, to improve the exchange of information between member states, which was so lacking during the attacks europol, eurojust, sis, etc. secondly, we must have new tools to respond fully to the threat: genuine strategies for radicalisation, prevention of radicalisation and de-radicalisation, a european national identity number which respects the criteria of legality, necessity and proportionality and, above all, a genuine european prosecutor's office with competence in the fight against organised crime and terrorism, which we have been calling for for several years. i am sorry that some groups in this house have refused to include this last point in the resolution.

in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on counter-terrorism measures. indeed, since the attacks in january 2015, france has been more than ever at war with an enemy that knows no face and no borders, terrorism. a spirit of unity and solidarity has therefore swept across the european union to defend our values and our freedom. i am convinced that we can only deal effectively with terrorism at european level. to this end, measures such as better police and judicial cooperation between member states, reinforced external border controls and increased internet surveillance must be implemented as soon as possible to ensure effective protection of european citizens. it is our responsibility. i regret, however, that the establishment of the european pnr, which seems to me to be both essential and urgent, is not unanimously supported by all the political groups.
in writing. the national front meps decided to abstain on the joint resolution on counter-terrorism measures, as the text unfortunately shows a disabling angelicism. while the authors of the resolution state that they want to "address the roots of terrorism" and call on the commission to "propose a clear and common definition of 'eu foreign fighters'", they lack the political courage to name islamist fundamentalism as the essential and main source of current terrorism. in addition, the text is cynical in stating that it is 'fundamentally opposed to proposals to suspend the schengen system', whereas the schengen system is a major problem. the lack of internal border controls facilitates the movement of terrorists within the european union. the fight against terrorism is therefore an additional argument for giving member states the right and the possibility to control their own borders.

in writing. contrary to rumours, the european parliament has adopted an ambitious resolution on the fight against terrorism. it was more necessary than ever to strike a balance between security and respect for fundamental freedoms and rights. although this resolution addresses security issues more than socio-economic aspects (prevention and deradicalisation strategies, inclusion, education, anti-discrimination, etc.), it clearly stresses the need to assess existing systems, to fully implement them and to analyse their weaknesses. finally, a measured amendment was tabled on the subject of air passenger data, known as pnr. a european pnr will help to combat terrorism and transnational organised crime provided that the data collected is regulated by a strong legal framework that protects the privacy of everyone. the commissioner also stressed that the eu should be able to take action to ensure that the eu's citizens are not left behind in the process of the eu's reform.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted against the renewal of the mandate of the internet governance forum. whether it's climate, human rights or the internet, we can see the ineffectiveness of these global projects. all of them are empty incantations and prove useless in addressing the real challenges facing our countries and our fellow citizens. at least, can we agree here that the internet is not under the control of some us government agency, endangering our freedoms. but when the commission deplores this, it is because it regrets not exercising general supervision over europeans itself. it is therefore only the states that - as russia does - can demand the repatriation of data to their territory and defend their citizens by exercising their royal functions.
in writing. i support this resolution which promotes an inclusive and multi-stakeholder model of internet governance and the improvement of its international governance in the future. i am particularly pleased that the united states will abandon its supervision of the iana (ip address range management) function, which is provided by icann, the us-based body responsible for the allocation and management of domain names on the internet, as of september 2015. the aim is now to internationalize icann and all its contracts with the us administration. a few months ago, together with the wine industry, governments and the commission, we denounced the poor functioning of icann and called for a fundamental reform of the organisation. indeed, its programme for the creation and assignment of new generic internet domain names in the wine sector (.vin/.wine) was in complete disregard of european and international legislation on the protection of geographical indications. we will therefore remain committed in the weeks and months ahead to global internet governance which, while taking into account the interests of all, also acts in accordance with international law on the protection of quality agricultural and food products.
in writing. i voted against the renewal of the mandate of the internet governance forum. whether it's climate, human rights or the internet, we can see the ineffectiveness of these global projects. all of them have become empty incantations and have proved incapable of meeting the challenges facing the peoples. the very ambition to make the internet a transparent, neutral, safe, reliable and endlessly growing global space is utopian. but it is possible to find a compromise around a refusal to see this international network as being dominated by a particular interest that endangers our freedoms, namely the interest of a foreign power that deploys means of surveillance worldwide. but when the commission deplores this, it is because it regrets that it does not itself exercise general supervision over the peoples of europe. only states can demand the repatriation of data to their territory and defend their citizens by exercising their royal functions.
in writing. i voted against because i believe that 'internet governance' the term used to describe 'the global arrangements that ensure the smooth functioning, accessibility and technological standards of the internet in all countries' is detrimental to the interests of member states. the threats to their security and independence have been sufficiently highlighted by the recent revelations of the existence of large-scale us surveillance programmes. it is not so much that europeans are being spied on that bothers the commission, but rather that it is incapable of doing so itself. european nations must be able to protect the personal data of their citizens, as well as retain control over the governance of their strategic data. i therefore oppose all forms of internet surveillance, whether it comes from the united states or the commission. russia is a good example to follow in this respect: it has called for data storage to be carried out within its territory in this forum on internet governance. we can and must also demand it in order to defend the sovereignty and independence of our nations.
in writing. the internet is today one of the few areas in the world to allow freedom of expression, but it is also an indispensable tool for present and future development, even if it remains essential to monitor its deviations such as terrorist or mafia networks which are also present in large numbers. even if, like the commission, we can only deplore the american influence on internet governance (and patriotic colleagues have tabled a motion for a resolution calling for the creation of a european search engine), the commission should not itself want to apply to europeans a surveillance that it denounces elsewhere. regretting the ineffectiveness of such governance projects, i therefore voted against the renewal of the mandate of the internet governance forum.
in writing. the internet governance forum (igf) is an institution that promotes dialogue between the various public and private actors involved in internet governance. the forum is implementing a multilateral approach to the management of various internet-related challenges, such as net neutrality and the protection of fundamental freedoms. i voted in favour of this resolution which calls on the un general assembly to renew the mandate of the forum in 2015.
in writing. i voted against this text, which is another attempt to undermine the sovereignty of nations, especially in the area of data protection. after the recent scandals over us surveillance programmes, the commission seems to be offended that it was not the commission which had the idea of spying on the citizens of the member states. the european union is therefore negotiating its independence with the united states in this forum. only russia has dared to raise the question of its independence by asking, in the context of this forum, that its data be stored within its territory. the patriotic members, because they have at heart the defence of france's interests, but also, and above all, the protection of the freedom of their fellow citizens, will strive to ensure that france recovers the management of our country's strategic data.

in writing. the european parliament voted by a large majority in favour of a renewal of the mandate of the internet governance forum by the united nations general assembly. the forum's mission is to discuss a wide range of issues related to internet governance and to make recommendations to the international community. it was particularly necessary to reiterate our commitment to the multi-stakeholder model of internet governance through a strengthening of openness, transparency, and above all the accountability of the actors in the digital world.
in writing. since 2005, the main issues of internet governance, such as equal access for all or security, have been discussed annually under the auspices of the united nations general assembly in the internet governance forum. this inclusive and multi-stakeholder model of internet governance, which allows governments, the private sector and civil society, in their respective roles, to develop principles, standards, rules and decision-making procedures, must of course be maintained and strengthened. in its resolution, the european parliament therefore calls for the mandate of the forum to be extended beyond 2015. at the next internet governance forum, to be held in brazil from 10 to 13 november 2015, the european union will have to ensure that it expresses an ambitious and coherent position, in the service of its values and political and economic interests.

in writing. internet governance aims to ensure that the internet works properly and that any website is accessible from anywhere. this is done by strengthening the defence of democracy, individual freedoms and human rights. but recently, the scandal that erupted following snowden's revelations has challenged the u.s. management of this issue. the document before us is too conciliatory of american surveillance practices. so he asks himself the following questions. is this an admission of impotence on the part of the european union and a lack of independence vis-à-vis the united states? can this project challenge us surveillance of the internet? or is it a new powerful geopolitical lever to coerce certain "reluctant" states to us interests? in view of these questions and the lack of clarity in the draft, i am voting against the principle of centralised 'governance' of the internet. in a multipolar world, each nation must be able to store and protect its own strategic information. it's the defense of sovereignty.

in writing. in this resolution, the european parliament calls on the commission to submit legislative proposals to make it compulsory to indicate the origin of meat used in processed foods. following the mad cow crisis, the indication of the country of origin was made compulsory for beef. this obligation should now be extended to other food categories and cover all ingredients in processed products. the european union must require all operators, producers and intermediaries, to provide clear and intelligible labelling. this labelling could also enhance local production and short-distance services. consumers know that it is better to trust a well-identified chain to have quality products, rather than sacrificing a whole culinary culture for a cheap and tasteless product. in the background it is clear that the food trading system is the source of unacceptable deviations; it is no longer about producing to sell, but about buying cheaper to sell at the highest profit. it is therefore essential to return to a more transparent, clearer and more ethical system with fewer intermediaries.

in writing. following the 'horse lasagna' scandal, this resolution recalls the importance of food labelling and traceability and proposes to strengthen certain aspects of it. it welcomes the obligation, effective from april 2015, to indicate the country of origin for unprocessed pigmeat, sheepmeat, goatmeat and poultrymeat. it also stresses the importance of taking into account horse meat as meat used in processed foods, as well as beef, pork, sheep, goat and poultry meat, as it constitutes a significant proportion of meat used in processed foods. this lucid text admits that the labelling of the country or place of origin of meat and meat products does not prevent fraud. however, considering that a rigorous traceability system does indeed help to detect and combat possible infringements, it calls on the commission to make legislative proposals to make the indication of the origin of meat in processed foods compulsory, in order to ensure greater transparency throughout the food chain and to better inform european consumers. i vote in favour of the proposal, but i would like to remind you that neither lasagna nor horse lasagna are harmful to health.

in writing. after the horse meat scandal in 2013, we need to respond to citizens' aspirations for traceability and transparency. that is why i supported this resolution calling on the commission to submit a legislative proposal making it compulsory to indicate the country of origin of meat used in processed foods. as with unprocessed beef and soon pork, sheep, goat and poultry meat, the compulsory indication of the origin of prepared meat will help to increase the non-price competitiveness of european agricultural production at the lowest cost. european farmers, who are subject to demanding production conditions, deserve recognition for their quality work. we will nevertheless be careful that the commission's proposal does not lead to an excessive increase in production costs for smes and artisans, many of whom are in the agri-food sector.
in writing. the european commission, faced with the horse meat scandals and the anger of consumers who rightly claim the right to know what they are eating and not to be deceived, has only come halfway. it has limited itself to labelling the origin of fresh beef without taking into account the meat used for processed products such as lasagna, pizza, chicken nuggets, etc. 90% of eu consumers want to know where the meat they eat comes from. the country of origin labelling of meat, whether processed or not, will meet consumer demands and enable consumers to make informed choices, ultimately leading to a more transparent supply chain and promoting short circuits instead of long food transport. labelling the origin of meat used as an ingredient will ensure better traceability along the food chain and will help avoid fraud when agri-food businesses choose their suppliers and products.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the indication of the country of origin of meat used in processed foods, in which we call on the european commission to come forward with legislative proposals to make this indication compulsory. of course we ask the commission to take account of the practical aspects of introducing such labelling, but we set a clear objective for it: consumers want to know what they are eating and they say so very strongly. i have been supporting this for a long time and i hope that things will now move forward. we can see that voluntary labelling in this area, which some advocate, is not enough. it is time to solve the mystery of the origin of meat in prepared dishes sold throughout the union, such as lasagna. this will increase transparency throughout the food chain and provide better information to the consumer. in concrete terms, this means extending the system we have already planned for fresh beef, which will be extended to all fresh meat from april 2015.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution to call for more transparency and information on the origin of meat in processed foods. the text comes as a commission report states that more than 90% of consumers surveyed believe it is important that the origin of meat used in processed foods is mentioned on the label. this vote will allow further reflection on the issue of meat labelling and it will be important to take account of the increase in costs and administrative burdens in the forthcoming debate in order to strike a fair balance between the interests of our consumers and the competitiveness of our businesses.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution, which calls for legislation to make the indication of the origin of meat compulsory for processed products, as is already the case for fresh meat. the horse meat scandal in lasagna in 2013 has undermined consumer confidence, even though in this case the problem was fraud and not lack of indication. we must regain that trust and reconcile europeans with the content of their plates, through more transparency and information. more than 90% of consumers believe it is important that the origin of the meat is mentioned on the label of processed food products. however, i am very cautious about the way in which this indication is to be implemented and the additional costs it may entail for the 13 000 smes in the european sausage and meat sector. we will have to answer many questions: how can we avoid too much bureaucracy when a traditional pastry requires more than 20 different types of meat? how can the supply of meat from one country to another be guaranteed when prices and production fluctuate? a thorough impact assessment will be essential before any binding proposal is adopted.
in writing. although the horse meat scandal erupted a year and a half ago, the european commission has not yet made any regulatory proposal to close the legal loopholes. i supported the resolution making it compulsory to label the country of origin of meat used as an ingredient in processed products. this resolution was adopted by a majority of the votes cast by parliament at its meeting in strasbourg on 10 february. i regret that the epp has given in to the lobbying against the marking of the origin of meat. allowing europeans to choose processed meat products according to the territories is, however, a value-add generator. european farmers will be recognised, even though 89% of consumers in france consider it essential to be able to know the origin of the ingredients that go into the composition of a food product. while it is proven that the cost of a frozen parmentier hash would rise from only 3.14 euros to 3.16 euros, increased confidence could even make some consumers return to this type of products!
in writing. vote in favour of the resolution which aims to make it compulsory to indicate the origin of meat in processed food following the food scandal involving the company spanghero and its lasagna made from horse meat. this has alarmed consumers, who are increasingly demanding quality and information about the products they buy. this traceability is essential for several reasons: it will enable the consumer to make an informed choice about the food they consume, and it will support our french farmers who suffer from unfair competition and have long been asking for this traceability. the argument of the additional cost of labelling is not significant, since a study has shown that this additional cost would not exceed one euro cent.

boundaries are the only way to ensure the separation and respect for the integrity of two different spaces. most eu member states are part of the schengen area, which has extremely porous common external borders and which makes migration flows across the territories uncontrollable. frontex is equally as ineffective in controlling migration flows in europe; the european agency is accompanying illegal migrants across the union, leaving thousands of people to roam free in the various countries that are trying to enforce their sovereign rights. this management of migration flows has also encouraged mafia networks to maintain clandestine channels, particularly in the mediterranean, where too many people have already died. asylum policy is a matter for the member states and it is unacceptable that they should suffer the political errors of the european union, which, living outside reality, is unaware of the human disasters it is in fact sponsoring, nor of the need for sovereign borders that protect the peoples of europe. the only realistic future for asylum policy and border management is respect for the legal and territorial sovereignty of the member states.
in writing. i have decided, together with all the members of the national front, to call for the abolition of the european external border agency, frontex. there are two main reasons for this. firstly, frontex no longer guards our external borders, it no longer prevents anyone from entering the union illegally. it is a substitute for the "smugglers": they fill up trash boats with illegal immigrants and then let them sink off the italian or greek coasts, knowing full well that frontex agents have a moral obligation - and it is quite normal - to come to their rescue and bring them back to the mainland. frontex therefore facilitates the entry of illegal immigrants into the union. the second reason is the hypocrisy of the union. it has made it easier for people to move, and it has encouraged millions of unfortunate people to attempt the often deadly crossing. without the union, without schengen, we would not have the migration problems we have today. and we certainly do not think that those who are causing these disasters will be able to solve them. uncontrolled immigration is a consequence of the union, and only nation states have the capacity to respond to these problems.

mr president, i would like to mention two major problems relating to access to medicines. firstly, we are faced with a veritable medical-industrial complex with considerable economic and political weight. the fact is that health care today is as lucrative a business as clothing or war. the patient often takes a back seat the mediator or vioxx scandals are only symptoms of a profit system applied to health. the major consequences of this system are the exorbitant costs of health care. the second problem is the drift away from an egalitarianism which tends to impose a right that can be challenged in all areas: the right to housing, education and medicine. it puts a huge amount of medicines - not always suitable - on the backs of the community for the benefit of a pharmaceutical industry that practices omerta to the extreme. you have spoken about this - is paramount and the european union provides 53% of the energy it consumes. the recent events in ukraine therefore require us to be vigilant and to promote greater energy independence. to do this, we must make complementary use of all the different energy sources available, with a market-based approach. this energy security also and above all requires the creation of a more integrated internal energy market with better interconnections, and i welcome the european commission's intention in this regard. the european commission should also strongly encourage member states to apply the existing rules before adding new ones. energy efficiency must be our main concern if we are to avoid waste. it's the most important thing. we must not abandon the millions of european citizens who live in energy poverty. research and innovation must also be supported in this area. the energy transition offers us the opportunity to use different energy sources. i would like to conclude by saying that we are really working on a project here and that you can count on us, commissioner, to help you with this project. but for that we absolutely need the support and political will of the member states.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, your energy union project suffers from three design flaws. firstly, it is a violation of subsidiarity. only states can build their own energy security. they are the essential links in the european energy security chain. it is the states, with their rules and policies, that build and solidify this chain. you're breaking this chain. secondly, your project neglects the security of supply of our states by promoting spot markets at the expense of long-term and very long-term bilateral and multilateral contracts. while the market is only thinking six months or a year ahead, this long-term vision is absolutely necessary for the financing of energy infrastructure. and you're destroying it! thirdly, your project creates a major geopolitical risk, by the willingness to attack a safe, reliable supplier. in the past, by imposing your rules on russia - as you impose your rules on our states - you have broken south stream and the security of our energy supply. your european energy security policy is a european policy of energy insecurity.

in writing. the strategy for a 'resilient' energy union, which can withstand supply difficulties or significant price fluctuations, hides some very dubious intentions. for example, there is a fear that the european union's intervention in the interconnection of networks will result in a decline in energy production, with each state relying on its neighbour to produce for it. this is what germany has been doing since it abandoned nuclear energy in favour of renewable energy. as renewable energy sources, germany imports nuclear energy produced in its neighbours, thanks to the interconnection of electricity grids. similarly, the european union's commitment to combating climate change is hampering our growth by placing heavy financial constraints on our own industries while our international competitors are scrambling to get their hands on it. finally, by preventing russia from building new gas pipelines, as was the case recently with south stream, the european union is preventing the diversification of europe's gas supply routes. in the end, this is the crux of the problem: the energy union, a seemingly virtuous project, has no other purpose than to prolong an absurd conflict with russia, to the sole benefit of the united states.

president of ecb. - madam president, honourable members, it is not going to be easy to respond to all these – more than questions, statements really. so i will only say a few words about the interaction between our monetary policy and what is called economic policy: namely structural reforms. we have two issues here: one of substance, that concerns the interaction between supply and demand, and one of legitimacy. as far as the substance is concerned, we have to see that the present economic situation of low output, big economic slack in the euro area and great cross-country differences, with a decline in potential output as well, is mostly due to declining investment and increased structural employment. but first and foremost, the crisis that started in 2010-2011 was a combined effect of several things that went wrong in the financial markets, but also a total loss of confidence. when we stabilise financial markets, confidence in the financial markets returns first, but confidence in real investment takes much longer, and now we see the first signs. so, all in all, the outlook is more positive than it was a few months ago. it is pretty natural: to make a financial investment, confidence can be, in a sense, easier to get back than making a real investment that is going to last for many years. but is monetary policy by itself going to create growth, employment? you seem to give a lot of responsibilities to the ecb; it has far fewer, in fact, than what you seem to be willing to give it. can monetary policy produce growth by itself? the answer is no. we know that monetary policy can still determine the basic, necessary conditions for growth, but then you have to have an environment that is growth friendly. you have to make the necessary structural reforms. i often give an example: we have taken unprecedented monetary policy expansion measures which certainly made it easier for the banks to give credit. but if someone, for example a youth, was to open a shop and before opening the shop had to wait nine, ten months for the permit, and having got the permit, had to pay immediately a heavy tax on it, what incentive do you think this person has in borrowing money from the banks? that is what i mean by structural reforms; that is what i advocate, and i do not think i am infringing on other fields of legitimacy when i advocate the need for structural policies, because these policies will make our monetary policy infinitely more effective than it is. so that is why, as a central banker, i feel perfectly right in urging governments to undertake these monetary policies. they are essential and a good complement for our pursuit of the primary objective of price stability. certainly, many of you said that we need to reconsider the transmission channels. one lesson from the crisis is certainly that the banking channel upon which this continent has relied for all its history is not enough and has proved to be much more fragile than capital-market-based economies. to some extent this is already happening, and capital markets in fact have expanded; bond issuance on capital markets has expanded greatly in the last two years. but capital markets are not yet shaped for smes. most of the credit to smes still comes from the banks. that is why the ecb, through the creation of the single supervisory mechanism (ssm) – and, frankly, even before, by national supervisors – has pursued the objective of strengthening, making the financial intermediaries, the banks, more and more resilient so as to make them able to give credit. but we certainly should work more and make sure that this capital market union that we talk a lot about also has as one of its potential beneficiaries the smes: those entities that are not large enough to issue bonds on the capital markets. some of you touched on the conflict of interests, and there are different potential conflicts of interest one can touch upon. the first is that we do monetary policy, and we also do supervision. the european parliament has been heavily involved by many of you in making sure that this proper separation would be designed exactly to avoid these conflicts of interest, and frankly i must say that, since the ssm became operative a few months ago, i do not see much of it now. but that, i should say, is really thanks to most of you, or to those of you who have worked on this. someone said that we are subject to the banks and we do the will of the banks. the only answer there is: just ask them; ask them what they feel. then there is another conflict of interest: the presence of the ecb in the troika and how would this square with outright monetary transactions (omt) and quantitative easing (qe). with the omt, the opinion that the european court of justice (ecj) has issued says that we should look. it did not say that there is a conflict of interest; it says that we should look further, and we are doing so. for omt countries we are doing so precisely to see whether our role in the troika could be in conflict with our role as provider of omt. so at this stage i can simply say: rest assured, it is not something that we ignore; we are seriously thinking about this. this conflict of interests does not arrive at all with qe. qe is a broad-based monetary policy expansion that has nothing to do with programme countries or not. it so happens that in certain countries which do not have a programme or do have a programme there are certain restrictions on the amount of bonds that we can purchase. but that is nothing to do with having a programme or not having a programme. let me respond to two what i might call popular mistakes. the smp profits: you still believe that the smp profits are owned by the ecb and are kept there? that is not so. the smp profits, like any other profit, have been distributed to all the central banks – members of the ecb – and the central bank members of the ecb have transferred their profits to their national budgets. and the national budgets have transferred their profits to greece. so they are there, available for financing. (interjection from mr marias) no, no, no: agreed to transfer the equivalent of income made by the euro system on the smp portfolio to greece as grants out of their own budgets as long as greece complies with the programme. (objections from mr marias)
president of ecb. - madam president, as i said, this is a fairly popular mistake, but it is not true. the ecb transferred these profits to the member banks. the member banks transferred these profits to the national budgets, and these profits are now available as grants out of their own budgets as long as greece complies with the programme. therefore this operation reflects a commitment by member states, not by the ecb. there is no euro system involvement in this operation. someone touched on the waiver. let me make it clear that the issue of the waiver is an issue of rules. the ecb accepts from the banks of all countries bonds, government bonds, as collateral only if these bonds are rated above a certain threshold. in the case of greece, these bonds were below this threshold, and years ago, when greece accepted the programme and was complying with the programme, we said that maybe we can waive this threshold and accept these bonds as collateral anyway. the thinking behind this was that maybe with the programme, the economic situation will improve to the point where these bonds become better rated, so we can accept that. but when the waiver decision was taken, the governing council clearly stated that if it did not assess the presence of a programme, the waiver would be lifted. you say no; we say yes; we do this. we are the ones who actually wrote the minutes of that decision. at some point we decided that there were no other conditions for a successful completion of the review of the programme. so the ecb had no choice other than to lift the waiver. having said that, we are ready to reinstate the waiver as soon as the governing council decides that the conditions for a successful completion of the programme are in place. my final comment is about the future genuine monetary union. it is not true actually; i never said anything about that. i said what i thought i could say in a speech given in helsinki two or three months ago, if i am not mistaken. but here is exactly a field where a central banker can only point out the fragility of the present construction – which, i fully agree, is a fragile construction – and possibly in general terms what the next steps could be. it is pretty clear that an institution-based integration is much stronger than a rules-based integration. the first type of integration is exactly supplied by the example of monetary policy. there we have successfully, in a sense, integrated our monetary policies. if we go back to the time before the euro, we had a rules-based monetary policy in a sense – you remember that, before the euro? in the budgetary policy we have an integration that is rules-based – and which is the more successful of the two? that is what i basically explored very briefly in the speech given in helsinki some time ago. finally, on fragmentation, i think the ones who said that it has taken time for our monetary policy to go and find its way through the economy are absolutely right. it has taken a long time. we started with monetary expansion – monetary policy – almost three years ago, at the end of 2011, and we have started seeing the first positive signs – i would not say now; we have been seeing this in the last two or three or four months. having said that, we have got to be aware that not all countries are the same. in some countries monetary policy – our monetary policy expansion – was fully transmitted through the economy and immediately produced good effects, and in other countries it did not. and so we should also ask ourselves: why is this so? what were the initial conditions that made monetary policy effective in one part of the union and not effective in other parts?
madam president, we are discussing the annual report on the ecb, and this is not against the commissioner – i perfectly understand that mr draghi has to leave – but we need some forward guidance, madam president, on the way the debate is organised. we had time-slots distributed. if we had known before, we would have given the floor only to one of us; but to say now that we have to discuss with an empty chair – even coming from france, i do not like la politique de la chaise vide. if you allow me, i ask you please to tell the president that either we have the time to discuss and to use our slots, or we close the debate.

member of the commission.– mr president, thank you for this really lovely debate. it clearly shows that the proposal is important and that the compromise text strikes a good balance. this is why i would encourage you to adopt the report today. citizens, road hauliers and european truck manufacturers are all waiting for it. let me also briefly refer to the longer trucks, or modular concepts as they are referred to in the directive. the commission is particularly satisfied that a compromise could be found on this political point. we all recognise that a particular type of service needs to be adjusted based on the available infrastructure and local characteristics. the compromise maintains the status quo of the current directive, meaning that its member states have competence to decide either to introduce longer trucks on a trial basis or not to do so. member states can also decide which roads longer trucks are allowed to drive on, in order to minimise safety risks and impact on infrastructure. these are concrete examples of implementation of the subsidiarity principle. so member states already allowing longer trucks can continue to use them and those member states which do not wish to have longer trucks can decide against them. let me be very clear on the clarification issue. at the request of the legislators, the commission clarified during the interinstitutional negotiations its interpretation of this existing text through a statement. the statement says that longer vehicles may cross only one border between two countries, both of which allow longer trucks. i am looking forward to your support and a positive outcome of the vote.
