the rapporteur. mr president, the creation of the european long-term investment funds (eltif) is the first concrete step in the reorientation of financial resources towards the real economy and, in particular, towards long-term investment. in the last few weeks we have seen all the engines of growth return to europe. we have benefited from the collapse in the price of the barrel, from a significant fall in the euro, from the particularly accommodating policy recently launched by the european central bank and, finally, from the launch of the juncker plan. we must consolidate these fundamental elements of growth, first by retaining the global liquidity that is now spontaneously returning to europe. of course, by strengthening financial stability across all dimensions of the banking union and by removing remaining barriers to investment between member states, with our partners. this is the whole point of the banking union and the capital markets union. eltifs are a highly anticipated first investment for this purpose. we started with a worrying observation with the commission. there are huge masses of money available in the world, but very little of it is directed towards long-term financing and very little of it is directed towards europe for that financing. governments themselves are held back by high debt and the need for fiscal reforms. large companies adopt conservative investment strategies or invest outside europe and banks weakened are still too often dependent on state aid. in addition, insurance companies and pension funds wishing to invest in long-term assets do not always have the resources to mobilise sufficient funds on their own, and there is no european pooling mechanism, such as investment funds, to facilitate this type of action. so there was a market need to be met. the creation of the new investment vehicle is intended to encourage them to invest in assets such as unlisted companies seeking long-term capital, certain listed smes, as well as the european venture capital funds and the european social entrepreneurship funds we created some time ago. these types of funds require investors to agree to lock their investments for a period of time in exchange for a premium, unlike other funds that allow investors to recover their investment at any time but for a lower return. to qualify as an eltif, funds will have to invest at least 70% of their capital in certain types of assets, be marketed only by managers the alternative investment fund managers directive sets strict rules and stringent requirements for fund managers and finally, be managed for a specified period during which investors are not entitled to recoup their investment, except in certain circumstances to be clearly specified from the outset. we have tried to create a statute as flexible as possible to appeal to sovereign wealth funds, hedge funds, pension funds, but also to wealthy individuals. eltifs target mainly professional investors such as local or corporate pension funds, municipalities, insurance companies. they will also be available to certain retail investors. that, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, is how we propose to consolidate the investment toolbox in europe. its entry into force will coincide with the effective start of the juncker plan and will have the same objective: to boost growth and competitiveness throughout the union.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the european longterm investment funds have a priori provisions which are common sense. they are intended to support small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) in projects that are of structural importance for our territories. however, the relevance of the european level for the implementation of these funds is not demonstrated. the commission will be able to take account of the need to ensure that the banking union is fully integrated and that the common rules on regulation are brought closer together. the additional report states that 'eltifs are a first step towards the creation of an integrated internal market for raising capital that can be channelled to long-term investments in the european economy'. however, on what basis will we converge at european level? as you know, our models of financial market regulation and our tax and social legislation differ greatly between the many states. finally, by placing this fund under the control of the european financial markets authority and the commission, you are making yet another affront to the sovereignty of the states, which will not have a say in the management of these funds, however strategic they may be for them.
mr president, commissioner, we are dealing here with a report which should have been published much earlier, when the crisis broke out on a european scale in 2007 and everyone was aware that it was a crisis of speculation and a diversion of long-term financing from the real economy. since then, we have taken a long time to stabilise the financial markets and to save the banks, but basically very little is being done to ensure the essential thing, namely the long-term financing of the economy so that the european union can face its own challenges: climate change, the demographic challenge and what have you. so here is the good news and perhaps tomorrow the european longterm investment funds, the eltifs, will become that new label, much as the ucits were the demonstration that europe knew how to invent financial markets or financial products useful for financing the economy. this will be true if these funds allow investment outside speculation, outside tax havens and in particular in compliance with the oecd conventions. this will be true if it does indeed help to create jobs here in europe through these strategic investments or if it also allows individuals to contribute to these funds. we must also learn from the lessons: the trilogue on this issue was concluded on the day of the launch of the juncker plan. there's a signal. we need to encourage these long-term investments again and again, and i would like to see this as a guiding principle when we look at commissioner hill's proposal for a european capital market, which should not simply be a return to securitisation but a financing of the real economy.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the 2008 capital market crash was the cause of the crisis which is now weighing heavily on our economies, even if mr kyrtsos of the epp thinks that everything is going very well. since then, the private banking system, which is too fragile, has almost ceased to finance the traditional economy, especially small and medium-sized enterprises. after toxic products, it is therefore necessary to converge financial savings towards this traditional economy with a stable investment horizon and disconnected from speculation on world markets. the creation of these eltifs to channel long-term savings to smes should therefore be welcomed. nevertheless, the investment rules for these products would have benefited from stricter and more controlled rules. for example, the 70% share of investment in longterm projects seems to us to be very inadequate. where will the remaining 30% of these funds, which are supposed to finance the economy, go? the other handicap is the contractual possibility of exiting the fund before the end of the economic projects, which can distort these long-term investment funds. but most importantly, there are no rules against the rampant takeovers of rapacious investors. eltifs will allow an investor to enter the capital of an sme, even if it is listed, without going through the threshold declarations. we will therefore be very attentive to the details of the second stage and will refrain from doing so in the meantime.
the rapporteur. mr president, i would like to endorse the excellent conclusions of the commissioner and thank all the colleagues who have supported us, in particular the fictitious rapporteurs, the european commission and the italian presidency, which has been very effective in concluding the dialogues. if mr lamberts were still present, i would have reassured him that the solution of a 60% quota of compulsory investments in europe was not adopted. but it is all the better because we now have a drafting system in which not 60%, but 100% of the investments will be devoted to european projects. if our colleague, mrs matias, were still here, i would have reassured her by saying that with these long-term investment funds we are going to encourage the opposite of the casino economy, because she was afraid of the casino economy. the idea is to take the money where it is and to invest it in jobs and competitiveness through longterm investment. if mr monot were still here, i would also reassure him that, contrary to what he has said and what he fears, the banks have continued, particularly in our country, france, to finance small and mediumsized enterprises at the rate of previous years, but this is not enough to revive investment throughout the union. finally, i would like to end with a recommendation to the member states. of course, these funds will only be attractive if we make them a little bit more attractive - if i may say so - by making them benefit from the most tax-friendly savings clause in each of our countries. we need these kinds of incentives to make these funds successful, and today's discussion has amply demonstrated how much we need them.

written explanations of vote
in writing. ‒ poland has applied for assistance from the european globalisation adjustment fund following the dismissal of 615 employees at zaklady chemiczne zachem between 31 march and 31 july 2013. the redundancies were the result of the cessation of activities and the restructuring of the zachem company, located in the cuyávia-pomeranian voivodeship. they are concerned with the decline in the european union's market shares in the chemical industry. from 1992 to 2012, the union's share of the global chemicals market increased from 35,2% to 17,8% in 2012. during the same period, china's share of the chemicals market increased from 8.7% to 30.5%. the collapse of the european chemical industry is therefore due to the ill-considered liberalisation of trade which has allowed asian competitors to oust europeans from the chemical industry. i voted in favour of this eur 115 205 aid to poland because it will help victims of the globalist and ultra-liberal policies of the european union by supporting the reintegration of dismissed workers into the labour market.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this debate because, although i have some reservations about the timing of the introduction of this tool, i support its primary purpose. i believe that the adjustment to globalisation should be made upstream or at the beginning of the company's financial problems rather than at the time of the number of redundancies.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, knowing full well that this 'adjustment fund' is only a setback: if the european union really wants to combat the harmful effects of globalisation, it must renounce the dogma of the free movement of goods and people and no longer stand in the way of the introduction of protectionist measures.
in writing. poland submitted an application for a financial contribution from the egf following 615 redundancies at zaklady chemiczne zachem and two of its suppliers due to the cessation of production and restructuring of zachem, a chemical industry company located in the cuyávia-pomeranian voivodeship. the requested aid is eur 115 205 and i therefore voted in favour of this mobilisation of the egf.
in writing. ‒ poland submitted application egf/2013/009 to obtain a contribution from the european globalisation adjustment fund following 615 redundancies at zaklady chemiczne zachem. the european parliament acknowledges that redundancies are directly linked to a decline in the eu market share in the chemical industry from 35.2% in 1992 to 17.8% in 2012. at the same time, asia and particularly china are experiencing a considerable increase in their production due largely to their wage costs, much more flexible regulations, and subsidies from public administrations to support the sector. these redundancies are therefore the result of a free trade policy open to all the winds of unbridled globalisation which are now affecting the eastern member states of the union, which are supposed to be better able to withstand international competition. rather than releasing funds to put out the social fire, we should implement an economic policy which protects our industries from unfair competition upstream. i have voted for the granting of this fund to help those workers who are victims of the excesses of globalisation.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament voted to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund to help the dismissed employees of zachem in poland. the amount of the aid shall be eur 115 205. the dismissed workers will receive training aimed at reintegrating them into the labour market and finding a job. the request from poland justifies intervention by the european globalisation adjustment fund in view of the decline of the european chemical industry in the face of asian and in particular chinese competition. i voted in favour of this report, which shows the union's solidarity in the face of certain negative consequences of globalisation on employment.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is right that workers in the member states of the european union who are suffering the most from the crisis and the austerity policy imposed by the european union should receive compensation. in the present case, the 615 redundancies at zachem and two of its suppliers have seriously affected polish workers. the commission also found that the polish request was justified in that companies in the european union have suffered particularly in recent years from chinese competition, in particular in the chemical industry: from 1992 to 2012, the union's share of the global chemicals market fell sharply, from 35,2% in 1992 to 30,5% in 2002 and 17,8% in 2012. 2012.in view of these facts, it seemed important to me that zachem's employees receive compensation, as light as it was, for their work. he did.
in writing. ‒ following the dismissal of 615 employees of zaklady chemiczne zachem and two of its chemical suppliers, poland has asked the european union to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) to support those who have lost their jobs and to help them find work or set up their own business. the grant is eur 115 205 and covers 50% of the cost of the projects to be proposed to these employees. since the request of the republic of poland meets the criteria for mobilising the egf, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. to support workers suffering from the consequences of globalisation, poland requested the activation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) for the redundancies of 615 employees of the company 'zachem' and its two suppliers active in the chemical industry. as a major employer in a region, these job losses caused by the migration of the chemical industry to asia have contributed to the worsening of the economic and social situation of a region already marked by the highest unemployment rate in the country. the egf will provide financing for a package of personalised services to help workers reintegrate into the labour market. in this respect, it is to be welcomed that, according to provisional data, 36 people have so far been re-employed through their participation in the services offered.
in writing. ‒ poland has applied for assistance from the european globalisation adjustment fund following the dismissal of 615 employees at zaklady chemiczne zachem between 31 march 2013 and 31 july 2013. the company had ceased its activities and then started restructuring due to the decline in the european union's market shares in the chemical industry. between 1992 and 2012, the union's share of the global chemicals market increased from 35,2% to 17,8%. china's share went from 8.7% to 30.5%. trade liberalization, the absence of protectionism, has led to the downfall of our chemical industry. i voted in favour of this eur 115 205 aid to poland to help, for example by facilitating the reclassification of these polish employees, victims of the ultra-liberal policy of the european union.

written explanations of vote
in writing. ‒ germany has applied for assistance from the european globalisation adjustment fund following the redundancies of 657 employees at aleo solar. the commission also found that the union industry had a significant market share in the union market. the decrease is largely due to unfair competition from china in the solar module sector. between 2005 and 2011, china's share of the revenue increased from 11% to 45%, while germany's share fell from 64% to 21%. germany itself has refused to allow brussels to impose sanctions on photovoltaic, betting that unfair chinese competition would weaken its other european competitors. the germans lost that bet because the chinese industrialists ended up ruining the entire european solar sector, including the german solar sector. i therefore abstained on this report because i cannot support the german authorities' attitude on this matter.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this debate because, although i have some reservations about the timing of the introduction of this tool, i support its primary purpose. i believe that the adjustment to globalisation should be made upstream or at the beginning of the company's financial problems rather than at the time of the number of redundancies.
in writing. ‒ i generally vote in favour of mobilising this fund, although i condemn its perverse logic of giving tranquilizers rather than treating the ill. exceptionally, i chose to abstain because germany strongly opposed the imposition of anti-dumping measures on chinese solar panels. in the country of angela merkel, the photovoltaic sector has no less than 10 000 companies, 350 of which produce solar panels. the remainder is involved in resale and installation and therefore benefits from the low chinese costs. germany has clearly chosen "services" over industrial production... but now proposes to the european union to pay the price of this policy. it is therefore up to germany to bear the consequences of its irresponsible policy which is harming european producers.
in writing. germany has applied for a financial contribution from the egf following 657 redundancies, 390 of which occurred at aleo solar ag, a company in the computer, electronic and optical products manufacturing sector, and 267 in two of its subsidiaries, of which 476 are expected to participate in the measures. we are being asked for eur 1 094 760 in aid from the egf. i abstained on this report because i felt that the measures taken were insufficient and that the european union had not taken effective action against the unfair international competition which we denounce in this sector.
in writing. ‒ germany submitted the application egf/2014/014de/aleo solar for a contribution from the european globalisation adjustment fund due to 657 redundancies, 390 of which occurred at aleo solar, a company specialising in the manufacture of photovoltaic panels. the european parliament considers that these redundancies are directly linked 'to changes in the structure of world trade', i.e. to the sharp decline in the share of revenues of german companies in the sector, from 64% to 21% between 2005 and 2011. despite multiple attempts at restructuring, aleo solar has never managed to regain competitiveness against the chinese. these redundancies demonstrate first that the crisis affects all the member states of the union, including those considered to be unaffected by chinese competition. the commission also found that the chinese exporting producers had not been able to demonstrate that the measures were in line with the union interest. while this is a sovereign choice, it is not up to the european taxpayers to pay the price. that is why i abstained on this vote.
in writing. ‒ parliament decided to accept the request from germany for assistance from the european globalisation adjustment fund to help the employees of aleo solar in germany who have been severely affected by the employment consequences of globalisation. the dismissed employees will receive training aimed at reintegration into the labour market and job search. the amount of the aid is eur 1 094 760. the request is justified given the very strong global competition in the solar module sector, with china being one of the main competitors. i voted in favour of this report, which shows the union's solidarity in the face of certain negative consequences of globalisation on employment.

in writing. the solar module industry is facing serious difficulties in europe, in particular due to competition from china. the subsidy to the chinese solar module industry created significant overcapacity which led to a sharp drop in prices. today, more than 90% of chinese production is exported, 80% of which is to the european union. in this context, the german company aleo solar and two of its subsidiaries have laid off 657 employees in a region of germany with a deteriorating social climate. per capita income is well below the national average and the unemployment rate is 15.5%, one of the highest in germany. the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) is therefore an additional factor in supporting the actions already undertaken to help redundant workers to return to work as quickly as possible. to this end, the egf will provide eur 1 094 760, or 60% of the total cost of the proposed actions, to provide vocational training, facilitate interregional mobility and provide individual support.

written explanations of vote
in writing. ‒ belgium has applied for assistance from the european globalisation adjustment fund following the redundancies of 708 employees at the steel companies duferco and nlmk, located in la louvière. duferco closed down and nmlk cut back on staff. the commission notes that the restructuring plan was submitted by the french authorities in the context of the restructuring plan. the reason for this is the decline in the market shares of european steel industries. the opening up of frontiers, particularly in the automotive sector, has weakened the european steel industry. the commission established the profitability of the sampled union producers by expressing the pre-tax net profit of the sales of the like product to unrelated customers in the union as a percentage of the turnover of those sales. during the same period, world production rose from 1 249 million tonnes to 1 548.3 million tonnes. european production therefore fell from 16.5% to 11.4% of world production. the globalisation of trade has benefited china most, with its market share in steel production rising from 33.7% to 45%. that is why i voted in favour of this aid of eur 981 956 to belgium, to enable it to help the victims of the deindustrialisation wanted by the european union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this debate because, although i have some reservations about the timing of the introduction of this tool, i support its primary purpose. i believe that the adjustment to globalisation should be made upstream or at the beginning of the company's financial problems rather than at the time of the number of redundancies.
in writing. ‒ i am opposed to the hypocritical system of the 'globalization adjustment fund', but i voted in favour of this report which proposes to release aid for belgian ex-employees of the steel companies duferco and nlmk: if this fund exists, it might as well be used to help european workers in distress. but again, instead of trying to mitigate the effects, the causes should be tackled by protecting european workers from the ravages of globalisation.

in writing. ‒ i do not share some of the aims of this text and regret that the protection of companies and employees is not included in the motivations, in favour of a strictly ideological vision that absolutizes competition. i also think that this text is contrary to the principle of subsidiarity. whether it is the improvement of the aerodynamic performance of vehicles, their energy efficiency or the performance and safety requirements, i do not see any area in which the member states would not be able to act effectively. under the pretext of combating global warming, the commission is allowing itself to intervene in all areas, in defiance of the treaties. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ under the pretext of combating global warming, the commission believes it is entitled to intervene in all areas, in defiance of the principle of subsidiarity supposedly guaranteed by the eu treaties. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the road network is open to international competition. i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. this text should improve the aerodynamic performance of vehicles and their energy efficiency in order to reduce co2 emissions, while ensuring that they meet performance and safety requirements. this also includes facilitating intermodal transport. unfortunately, this text opens up the road network to competition rather than protecting companies and employees. in addition, infringements should be subject to appropriate measures at member state level and drivers should be able to access the information recorded by the on-board devices. i therefore voted against.
in writing. heavy goods vehicles and buses travelling within the european union must comply with a number of rules on their dimensions, according to a directive. the revision aims to improve road safety and energy savings, while improving the environmental footprint. indeed, these vehicles account for about a quarter of greenhouse gas emissions. in april 2014, the european parliament adopted a position at first reading. last december, after interinstitutional negotiations, an agreement was reached and adopted in the committee on transport and tourism. i voted against this text because it is a matter for the individual member states and therefore not for the european union to intervene. moreover, the text opens up the road network to competition instead of protecting transport companies and their employees.
in writing. ‒ the draft directive before us provides for a revision of the standards for certain road vehicles in the european union. it may enable manufacturers to launch new truck models whose weight and length would be likely to exceed the limits in force. however, by failing to demonstrate the value of entrusting the european commission with the task of legislating on these relatively technical matters, and by not specifying anything strictly concerning road transport undertakings and employees, this text once again tramples on the sovereignty of the member states and prepares the way for the full opening up of the union's road infrastructure to competition. in this text, neither the principle of subsidiarity nor the protection of road hauliers is respected. that is why i voted against this draft directive.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the dimensions and weights of road vehicles in the community. this directive will improve road safety, protect the environment and encourage technological innovation. these are very important for the european union and for the citizens.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this text which not only violates the freedom of member states in transport policy but also puts road transport companies and their employees in a precarious situation. the proposal for a directive as envisaged by the council thus calls on the member states to take surveillance measures against road vehicles by making it compulsory to monitor the weight of vehicles by means of automatic monitoring systems. furthermore, member states have no control over weighing systems since they are prohibited from requiring the installation of such systems on vehicles registered in another member state. it is therefore impossible for the member states to protect national undertakings, especially since they will now be obliged to provide the commission with information on the number of checks carried out in the previous two years and the number of overloaded vehicles detected. the text thus deprives the member states of their ability to influence the daily lives of citizens, since brussels now decides the content of national public policies.
in writing. ‒ the aim of this report is to ensure better control of the weight of certain road vehicles in order to combat the many frauds concerning the maximum volume that a heavy vehicle can carry on our roads. the text also aims to encourage investment in heavier vehicles that are safer and consume less co2 while strengthening european rules on the control of maximum authorised dimensions. this balanced agreement was the subject of difficult negotiations during the last mandate and i am particularly pleased that there is no longer any question of opening up the movement of 'mega trucks', those giant heavy goods vehicles which are currently only used locally in some countries of the union and which in my view have no place in a europe geared towards a sustainable economy, and therefore logically towards modal shift, to free movement on european roads. the original proposals of the european commission on this subject have been withdrawn, so i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. the revision of directive 96/53/ec on the maximum dimensions and weights of lorries in international traffic was adopted at this european parliament plenary session. proposed in april 2013 by the european commission, this revision of the directive as amended by the parliament and the council proposes a number of innovations. thus, the size of trucks is increased and the weight of trucks is increased in the context of intermodal transport operations, i.e. combining road with rail or waterways. in addition, the revised directive will make improvements to aerodynamic design of both the cabin and the rear of the vehicles.
in writing. ‒ this text will make it possible in the future to have safer and cleaner lorries on european roads, and to improve their comfort for their drivers. another very important point is that the text prohibits the circulation of "mega trucks" weighing more than 60 tonnes. the infrastructure of the member states of the union is not all adapted to support such heavy vehicles. it was therefore essential that a limit could be set on size and weight. these new rules are a step in the right direction. member states will have a two-year period to implement them. they will also need to ensure that manufacturers and users have the time and resources to adapt to the new changes.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament adopted on 10 march 2015 a revision of the 1996 'weight and dimensions' directive for heavy goods vehicles. although this new text does not put an end to the mega-trucks, these giant lorries which pose risks to road safety, road maintenance and the environment, i voted in favour of this revision which includes several major positive points such as the reaffirmation of the ban on lorries over 40 tonnes crossing from one country to another, as well as the generalization of the control box system to allow better monitoring of heavy goods vehicles. another key point of the revision is the enhancement of the safety and well-being of road workers through a change in the design of the cabs. finally, improving the aerodynamics of trucks and developing low-carbon engines are equally crucial issues in the objective of reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this balanced text on the maximum size and weight allowed for certain road vehicles which encourages road hauliers to invest in trucks that are safer for users, safer and less polluting, because they consume less co2. these vehicles will therefore have to meet higher safety and environmental standards, and i welcome this. in particular, i am pleased that, despite the pressure, this text does not address or authorize the use in europe of 'mega trucks', those oversized 60-tonne, 25-metre long trucks. the 'mega trucks' are too dangerous and unsuitable for our infrastructure and european roads. i will continue to oppose it.

in writing. ‒ technological developments offer the possibility of adding retractable or folding aerodynamic devices to the rear of vehicles, allowing for significant energy savings. however, these devices would result in exceeding the maximum lengths allowed under council directive 96/53/ec. a derogation from the maximum lengths is therefore necessary, and that is the subject of this text. the proposal therefore aims to limit pollution from buses and lorries. of course, these measures will remain a long shot until real ecological planning will make it possible to reduce road transport to rail. i am abstaining in this context in order not to prevent these meagre advances while denouncing the commission's lack of ambition in reducing greenhouse gases.

in writing. ‒ following negotiations with the council of the european union and the vote of meps in the committee on transport and tourism, the european parliament voted no to mega-trucks in a plenary vote on the directive on the weights and dimensions of heavy vehicles. it is a victory for the protection of the quality of life of europeans. thanks to the vote of the european parliament, our towns and villages will no longer be crossed by lorries 25 metres long and weighing more than 60 tonnes! the vote is also the culmination of a long struggle by socialist members against the commission's proposal to allow the cross-border movement of mega-trucks. this vote is a positive signal for the reduction of co2 emissions and the promotion of the modal shift from road freight to rail. the text also takes account of user safety and environmental protection by incorporating provisions to promote alternative fuels and vehicle aerodynamics.
in writing. ‒ the aim of the proposal is to make our trucks safer and more comfortable, more environmentally friendly and suitable for multimodal transport. i therefore welcome its adoption, which brings european legislation into line with recent technological developments. the adjustment of vehicle dimensions standards will allow the addition of aerodynamic features, improved cabin profiles and better energy absorption in the event of an accident. the increase in the average weight of passengers and their luggage and the equipment with alternative propulsion systems (hydrogen, electricity, etc.) involving the addition of batteries or dual engines were also taken into account. finally, i am pleased to see that on the question of the international movement of mega-trucks originally considered by the commission, it has been decided to maintain the status quo. we're not ready for such a change. it is regrettable, however, that the new standards set may not come into force until 2020 as a result of the action of some member states, under pressure from their manufacturers. that's how long the public will be unable to benefit from the advances in heavy-duty innovation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the revision of the 1996 heavy goods vehicle weight and dimensions directive. the new text brings about considerable improvements in road transport. the aim is to change the design of the cabs in order to improve the safety of road users in the event of an accident and to ensure greater driver comfort. it also improves aerodynamics with the aim of reducing greenhouse gas emissions and their impact on the environment. i regret, however, that this new text does not mark the end of the mega-trucks or "gigaliners". these vehicles, which can weigh up to 60 tonnes, raise major concerns for road safety and the environment. one reason is that they divert freight from rail to road, whereas rail should be preferred. it also encourages the adoption of new standards favouring commercial trucks or buses with low-carbon engines. the directive should also ensure better control of heavy goods vehicles by extending the control box system, which is still too little used in europe.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the maximum dimensions and weights of certain road vehicles. the text aims in particular to adapt the dimensions provided for to take account of technological developments. for example, new aerodynamic features generate many gains, but add to the rear and thus can lengthen vehicles. in approving this amendment, our assembly is stressing the imperative of reducing greenhouse gas emissions, and in particular co2, but also of improving safety on our roads. with new cab design, blind spots for drivers can be reduced. this will save the lives of both drivers and vulnerable road users such as pedestrians and cyclists.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which allows the introduction of new types of trucks with higher performance and with the integration of technologies that emit less co2, devices that will increase visibility for drivers and therefore the safety of other users. a delay was obtained to allow manufacturers time to prepare for these changes and the integration of these new standards. the aim is also to combat fraud in relation to the maximum volume that a heavy goods vehicle can carry on european roads. with this vote we have increased road safety and defended industrial jobs.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this directive, which will allow manufacturers to design safer and greener trucks. the new directive amends a 1996 text on the weight and dimensions of trucks to allow exemptions from the current limits and to improve their environmental performance and safety. parliament has fought to introduce a sufficient time limit for all manufacturers to adapt to the new standards, thus preserving fair competition between manufacturers for the benefit of employment.
in writing. ‒ at first reading (april 2014), the three fn meps voted contra this text which was finally adopted by parliament. the text amended the commission proposal, in particular as regards controls and infringements. the amended text proposed a classification of offences according to their gravity and the penalties for each. the council partially incorporated the european parliament's proposal. the council also does not follow the commission in classifying offences into categories. it replaces it by an obligation on member states to determine the system of penalties applicable to infringements of the directive. they are required to provide the commission with information on the number of checks carried out in the previous two calendar years and the number of overloaded vehicles detected. the commission has also proposed that the commission should be given the task of drawing up a report on the implementation of the directive on the protection of workers from harmful exposure to asbestos. infringements shall be subject to appropriate measures at member state level.

in writing. ‒ this report does not bring the expected transformations on this subject which is essential for european economies. the stimulus of longterm investment is one of the main channels of industrial recovery and job creation. the european long-term investment funds are a welcome proposal and meet the financing needs of the real economy. however, the eligible investments are not clearly defined by their sectoral impact and weight which would, in the context of a realistic and committed economic and industrial policy, respond to the definition of national priorities and strategies. although i approve of the proposal to leave, i abstained because of the lack of clarity and visibility in the management of a recovery at national level.
in writing. ‒ i do not exclude the possibility that smes may benefit from the establishment of these european long-term investment funds (feilt or eltif in english), a new category of financial instruments that is to be created. but in view of the organized vagueness of mr lamassoure's report on the rules supposed to govern investment, the risk does not seem to me to be negligible and i preferred to abstain on this report.
in writing. this supplementary report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on european long-term investment funds lacks clarity since the investment forecasts put forward by brussels appear to be overestimated. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the future of the european union. however, i abstained on that text.
in writing. the purpose of this regulation is to create a new financial instrument, the eltif. the instruments that exist are ill-suited to long-term saving. they are subject to prudential standards, the prospectus directive and retail investors are subject to a strengthened advisory obligation. making europe a financial hub can be beneficial for france. the mediation would allow investors to diversify their portfolios and companies to access more sources of financing. i abstained on that text. indeed, caution is required with any new financial instrument. in addition, there is some confusion about certain investment rules. however, i welcome the fact that these instruments are intended for the long-term financing of smes, which are the engine of our economy. but i criticise the fact that while the aim of eltifs is to finance long-term projects, they are only obliged to invest 70% in such projects. for the same reason, i have reservations about the possibility of an early release. in addition, the fund may waive diversification obligations according to rather complex rules.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the european long-term investment funds. this will undoubtedly encourage investors to invest in long-term projects. we need it badly in europe. this, together with the investment plan of the commission of jean-claude juncker, will help to bring the rate of investment within the union back on track and thus stimulate growth and employment in europe. i congratulate my colleague alain lamassoure on this report.
in writing. - i preferred to abstain on this report. this is a new financial instrument, and we have no objections to it at the moment. it is true that these funds are mainly geared to financing smes, which is a very good thing. in addition, they favour long-term investments over speculative products, which is also very positive. however, some investment rules remain unclear: while the aim of eltifs is to finance long-term projects, investors are only required to invest up to 70%; the remaining 30% can therefore be related to cash, other shorter-term projects or alternative investments. i also remain skeptical about the possibility of an early exit with derogations, even though the principle of the fund is that the investor is committed until the project is completed.
in writing. ‒ the aim of this legislative proposal is to increase the pool of capital available for long-term investment in the real economy of the european union. to this end, the text creates a regulatory framework for a new form of financing vehicle, the european long-term investment funds, in order to subject these funds to consistent rules across the european union and to enable investors to identify them throughout the union. considering that this proposal will facilitate the flow of capital into the real economy, in line with the european objectives for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. contrary to current belief, the investment deficit in europe is not new. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's macro-financial assistance to the countries of central and eastern europe, including the countries of the former soviet union, and will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's macro-financial assistance to the countries of central and eastern europe. the european union is now providing a common regulatory framework that is easily identifiable to investors, in order to ensure that the level of investment returns to its pre-crisis level.
in writing. ‒ the european union needs structural and innovative investment to get back on the path to sustainable growth. the adoption of this report on the creation of the european long-term investment fund is a step in the right direction and will increase the options for long-term financing of projects in research, innovation, infrastructure or energy. the fund will be one of the tools of the commission's investment plan and a further step towards the market and capital union, which is intended, among other things, to facilitate the financing of european smes.
in writing. ‒ the rapporteur's text does not bring the expected changes to a subject which is essential to european economies. the stimulus of longterm investment is one of the main channels of industrial recovery and job creation. the european long-term investment funds are therefore a welcome proposal and meet the financing needs of the real economy. however, it appears that eligible investments are not clearly defined by their sectoral impact and weight which would, in the context of a realistic and committed economic and industrial policy, respond to the definition of national priorities and strategies. despite the good proposal at the outset, i abstained because of the lack of clarity and visibility in the management of a recovery at national level.
in writing. ‒ i abstained on this draft european long-term investment fund (eltif). these funds may be useful, since they are intended to finance the real economy through long-term infrastructure. nevertheless, the exclusion of the member states from the management of these funds is harmful because it gives the european union full power to choose the beneficiaries of these funds. it is therefore illusory to think that the eurocrats will stimulate the real economy. the big multinationals will get the lion's share and the small businesses will be left behind once again. finally, eltifs risk allowing unsuspecting investors to take control of smes, in particular by allowing them to circumvent the thresholds.
in writing. ‒ the rapporteur's text does not bring the expected changes to a subject which is essential to european economies. long-term investment is sorely lacking in our economy, even though it is enabling economic recovery and industrial recovery. the provision of funds for this purpose responds to a real need for financing in the real economy. but the text does not give any details of the investments that will be made, nor what the overall economic strategy at national level will be. despite the good starting point, the lack of vision and clarity of this text led me to abstain.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by my colleague alain lamassoure establishing a regulation to increase the capital available for long-term investment in the european economy. these investments must be beneficial to the european economy and growth and not fuel speculation, while ensuring full protection and information for investors. this report was adopted by a large majority, which i welcome.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on european long-term investment funds. long-term financing is essential to enable the european economy to move towards smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. european long-term investment funds (eltifs) provide long-term financing for a variety of projects. eltifs thus contribute to the financing of the real economy and the implementation of union policies.

in writing. ‒ long-term financing is essential to support the european real economy. in june 2013, the commission published a legislative proposal for the introduction of a framework for collective investment that would allow investors to put money into companies and projects that require long-term capital. these european long-term investment funds (eltifs) provide financing to various long-term infrastructure projects, unlisted companies and smes, which issue equity or debt instruments for which there is no readily identifiable buyer. but attempts to shift these investments towards social and environmental sustainability have not been taken into account. in addition, investment priority is given to public-private partnerships and privatisations. the regulation thus fails completely to achieve the necessary objectives. i vote against it.
in writing. ‒ financial instruments that redirect savings to the real economy and long-term projects, rather than speculation, should be encouraged. eltifs have a stake in this. these funds are based on long-term investments in smes, with no possibility of early exit. so the principle is good. the proposed regulation allows up to 30% of other investments and gives managers the possibility of anticipating the early exit of the fund. secondly, these funds can serve as a screen for creeping equity take-overs, without threshold declarations. finally, there is no provision for investment to be targeted at european countries. for all these reasons, we must remain vigilant as to what will become of these instruments and abstain on the report.
in writing. i abstained on this supplementary report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on european long-term investment funds on the grounds that the forecasts put forward by brussels seem to me to be overestimated. the european union is not clear on this point either.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report, of course, because it proposes to boost long-term investment in the real economy through the european long-term investment funds. the return of jobs in europe requires these strategic investments and smart, sustainable and inclusive growth.
in writing. ‒ i support the rules adopted for european long-term investment funds, because i consider investment to be a key element for the healthy development of our economies. that is why i voted for the report on the european long-term investment funds.
in writing. ‒ at a time when the new juncker commission is focusing on competitiveness and growth, it is necessary to regulate and control the different types of investment. the european parliament gave its opinion on the european long-term investment funds. i voted in favour of this text. this funding is crucial to achieve the europe 2020 objectives for smart, sustainable and inclusive european growth. these funds are essential to enable the actors concerned, and in particular the regional and local authorities, to undertake projects for the future.
in writing. ‒ many projects, which are essential for europe's economic recovery, require a long-term financial commitment: transport, energy and telecommunications infrastructure are examples. i therefore voted in favour of the commission's proposal to create european longterm investment funds (eltifs). by targeting actors such as pension funds and insurance companies, this new tool should encourage non-bank investment in certain projects. in addition, this new collective investment framework should allow for economies of scale and critical mass, while reducing market fragmentation and thus regulatory uncertainty. the next step is to align eltifs with the proposal for a european fund for strategic investments as presented in the juncker plan published last november.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report by alain lamassoure which launched a new and effective tool which will not only promote long-term investment financing but also help build the capital markets union. given the current crisis and investment deficit, we need to find a solution to boost economic growth, allow financial stability and remove barriers to cross-border investment while ensuring consumer protection. the aim of these instruments is to boost the activities of smes by granting loans to encourage their development and growth. these european long-term investment funds will help professionals, insurance companies, pension funds and retail investors who want to invest at least eur 10 000 in the long term to invest in projects that serve the european economy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report by my colleague alain lamassoure, which allows the creation of european long-term investment funds (eltif) to redirect financial resources towards the real economy. indeed, there is a lot of liquidity available, but investments have fallen by 15% since 2008. very little of this capital is mobilised for long-term financing of infrastructure, equipment, educational or research centres. eltifs will support the creation of new 'investment vehicles' that will stabilise assets in exchange for attractive premiums. the aim is to attract investment funds, pension funds and insurance companies through a flexible and attractive framework, in order to boost the growth and competitiveness of our economies.
in writing. ‒ the new financial products which are supposed to promote the long term and which are presented in this report, although they may be based on a correct intuition, do not seem to us to offer the necessary guarantees as regards their possible misuse and the power of control which the states should exercise over them. in addition, there is a high risk of having profitable investments which are only made in the nordic countries which do not need them, in the absence of an investment agency promoting long-term profitable investments in the context of sectors, such as energy saving or new energy (financing companies, craft industries, companies selling equipment). therefore, i abstained.
in writing. ‒ we can be against borderless markets for goods and services while being in favour of deeper and more unified capital markets. for investors, this allows for diversification of the projects and companies in which they invest; the commission has already taken a number of measures to improve the quality of the information provided by the member states. there are two arguments in favour of these funds. firstly, they are geared to financing smes. secondly, they are an instrument which favours the long term, unlike speculative products. we are against qatar buying our national assets, without prohibiting anyone from investing in our country, let alone in our smes. what we must combat are toxic, speculative products, developed for immediate profit and which are a source of instability and diversion of savings from the needs of the real economy. the french delegation of the fn therefore takes a cautious position by abstaining from voting on this new financial instrument, particularly in view of the vagueness surrounding certain investment rules.

in writing. ‒ charges for credit card payments reveal the lack of interoperability between terminals and are an obstacle to better competition. the caps on fees for debit or credit card payments proposed in this report are a welcome step forward, which i welcome. i voted in favour of this text, which improves the conditions of competition, economic activity and transparency in the management of means of payment.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text because it is in the interests of both consumers and merchants: too often, some cards are still refused, especially abroad, and some small merchants continue to refuse cards below a certain amount. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the european parliament is able to make a full contribution to the work of the european parliament. the regulation will probably not solve these various problems, but it is a step in the right direction.
in writing. this supplementary report on interchange fees for card-based payment transactions is a positive development as it is moving towards increasing security. it also reduces the costs borne by consumers by introducing caps (0.2% for crossborder transactions, 0.2% or eur 0.05 for domestic transactions or 0.3% for credit card transactions). i therefore voted in favour of this text.
in writing. i voted for this because its aim is to limit bank charges and to force networks to be more competitive by accepting different cards by terminals. although the regulation could go further, particularly on the interoperability of payment terminals, it is a step forward. interchange fees are fees charged by card issuers to merchants offering card payments. these are in practice reflected in the selling prices. this constitutes a restriction of competition within the meaning of the treaties and the case law of the court of justice. the report proposes a cap on bank fees at 0.3% of the transaction amount for credit card payments and 0.2% for debit cards, with the possibility for member states to set lower caps. the challenge to the exclusivity clauses in licensing agreements required by card providers and the various technical mechanisms that limit the possibility of using different cards from the same payment terminal is to be welcomed.
in writing. ‒ interchange fees are fees charged by card issuers to companies offering card payment services. the cost of these commissions is directly passed on to the consumer price. these interchange fees encourage companies to refuse card payments below a certain amount and for products with very low added value (e.g. tobacco). hence the cap on commissions at 0,3% of the transaction amount. the proposal also aims to tackle the exclusivity clauses in licensing agreements required by card providers and the various technical mechanisms which limit the possibility of using different cards from the same payment terminal. the draft regulation is therefore a real step forward for the consumer, since it will allow him to control the fall in sales prices in the transactions concerned. moreover, it seems that the adoption of such a regulation at european level is rather appropriate in view of the interoperability of payment terminals. that is why i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on interchange fees for card-based payment transactions. this measure will ensure fair and transparent competition in card payments. consumers will then be better informed about the cost of card transactions and can make their choices on the basis of this information. this type of measure is a first step towards greater transparency in the banking sector.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which is about a proposal for a regulation which will be beneficial for the consumer, both in terms of purchasing power and in terms of transparency of information. the regulation provides that, in the case of crossborder transactions carried out by bank card, the bank's commission would be capped at 0.3% of the transaction amount; for transactions made by debit card, the ceiling would be 0.2% of the transaction amount. the framework of this regulation also allows member states to retain their competence in this area, since they have the possibility of setting lower ceilings. this regulation also helps to deal with the fact that too often certain cards are refused abroad; the consumer's cards will now be accepted more easily, making it easier to pay for purchases. good news for the purchasing power of the french.
in writing. the aim of the text is to regulate interchange fees for card-related payment transactions. because these interchange fees represent a significant proportion of the fees charged to traders by the companies providing this service, their level affects the purchasing power of europeans. the costs imposed on traders are passed on to consumers. by placing a ceiling on the fees charged to payment service providers, the text is moving in the right direction, that of protecting the purchasing power of european citizens.
in writing. ‒ the aim of this legislative proposal is to establish common rules on interchange fees in the european union by placing a cap on such fees for transactions carried out using payment cards. as these payment cards are widely used by consumers and as the legislative proposal provides, in addition to capping fees, for increased transparency measures for retailers and consumers, i voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. ‒ the fees charged by banks for payments to retailers differ from one member state to another and there is a lack of transparency in these transactions. the capping of these payments, whether transnational or national, will allow a certain uniformity of european rules and thus more transparency. this is in the interests of the european consumer and his right to information.
in writing. ‒ the costs of card payments reveal the lack of interoperability between terminals and are an obstacle to better competition. the proposed caps on fees for debit and credit card payments are also a welcome step forward, which i support. i voted in favour of the whole of this text, which improves the conditions of competition, economic activity and transparency in the management of means of payment.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal on interchange fees for card-related payment transactions. the aim of the project is to limit these fees to a maximum of 0.2% of the value of the transaction for any credit card transaction. this cap will reduce the costs of traders, which should also benefit consumers, since traders pass on their costs to the price of their goods and services. a decrease in the costs of interchange fees is therefore likely to lower the prices paid by consumers.
in writing. ‒ this text facilitates fair competition and transparency in the area of payment methods. it breaks down some barriers to interoperability between terminals, while raising commission ceilings which i consider to be valuable. i therefore voted in favour of this text.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague pablo zalba bidegain on interchange fees for card-based payment transactions. the text aims to reduce interchange fees (fees paid by financial institutions for credit and debit transactions), and aims at greater transparency (obligation for banks to inform on the rates applied, maximum 0.3%) and mechanically to competition, and thus a reduction in costs borne by consumers. i welcome the adoption by a large majority of this report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of legislation to cap the fees charged by banks to merchants for processing credit card payments made by their customers. this will lead to a real reduction in costs for consumers as well as for traders.
in writing. ‒ the costs of card payments reveal the lack of interoperability between terminals and are an obstacle to better competition. the proposed caps on fees for debit and credit card payments are also a welcome step forward, which i support. i voted in favour of the whole of this text, which improves the conditions of competition, economic activity and transparency in the management of means of payment.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this because it caps the cost of each crossborder transaction by credit card at 0.2% of the value of the transaction. in five years' time, the same ceiling will apply to domestic transactions. this text thus doubly protects the interests of consumers.
in writing. the issuers of credit cards charge merchants a fee, the interchange fee, which is passed on to the selling price. the aim of the regulation is to cap these fees, to make them more transparent, to address exclusivity clauses and the various technical mechanisms that limit the possibility of using different cards from the same payment terminal. this is in the interests of consumers and merchants, as it will result in lower commissions and easier acceptance of all types of cards for payment of purchases. some cards are still often rejected, particularly abroad, and some small shops continue to refuse cards below a certain amount. the settlement improves the situation.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this proposal because it is a step in the right direction to limit bank charges and force the networks to compete more. the text also leaves the member states free to intervene with further reductions in national transactions, and the fees for card transactions are officially increased: interchange fees for debit cards cannot exceed 0.2% and 0.3% for credit cards.
in writing. ‒ the proposed regulation aims to improve the functioning of the internal market for card payments. one of the main obstacles to card payments is the widespread existence of interchange fees. interchange fees are interbank fees charged between acquiring banks and card issuers. each year, 9 billion euros of interchange fees are levied in the european union. merchants, in turn, pass these card-related costs on to the price of their goods and services. in practice, competition between card schemes aims to convince the largest number of payment service providers to choose their cards, which generally leads to higher costs (advertising, ancillary benefits, etc.). in fact, it is a private consumption tax. the regulation provides that 'payment service providers shall not offer or request a transaction fee of more than 0,2% of the transaction value for any debit card transaction [and] 0,3% for credit cards'. the aim is therefore to tackle (somewhat) the profits of the banks in order to reduce the cost to consumers. i vote for it.
in writing. ‒ the proposed text brings two improvements that will benefit consumers and traders. reducing and capping interchange fees on bank cards, even for small amounts, contributes to a fall in consumer prices. by promoting the interoperability of payment terminals and by breaking down certain restrictions on the use of competing network cards, a step is also being taken towards wider acceptance of all bank cards. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial instruments are used effectively.
in writing. i voted in favour of this supplementary report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on interchange fees for card-based payment transactions. this text is in fact in the direction of greater security, which seems to be a positive element.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which introduces more transparency in the area of interchange fees for transactions carried out with a payment card. these fees, which are paid by the merchant's bank to the bank which issued the customer's card, vary from one member state to another. the text i voted for requires banks to report transparently on these fees and caps them at 0.3% of the transaction. since traders pass on interchange fees to their prices, this text will therefore restore purchasing power to consumers.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this supplementary report because it sets out rules on interchange fees for card-based payment transactions with a view to contributing to the establishment of a european union-wide payments market. i am therefore in favour of greater harmonization of these practices in order to simplify and promote the trading system on our continent.

in writing. ‒ giving half of humanity its rightful place in social and political representation is a universal struggle that socialists have always carried. i welcome the fact that, on the day after international women's day, our parliament is voting on a report which highlights the persistent discrimination in the field of equality and proposes concrete measures to reduce it. it is part of this collective will to work for the freedom and emancipation of women. there are many things to be done: increase the employment rate and its quality, reduce the pay and pension gap, reduce the risk of poverty, combat stereotypes, promote reconciliation between private and professional life, promote the participation of fathers and mothers in family life, unblock the directive on maternity leave, combat violence against women, promote sexual and reproductive rights, that is, the fundamental right of women to dispose of their bodies, which the reactionary conservatives are constantly trying to challenge. equality is a daily struggle that must be fought relentlessly. advancing women's rights is about wanting a more just society and a more effective democracy. the mentality still needs to improve!
