oral explanations of vote
written explanations of vote
in writing. ‒ the annual report on eu competition policy fails to conclude that the objectives of pure and perfect competition in the single market have not been achieved in the goods and services sector. the abuses of dominant positions and cartels, against which the text suggests some laudable measures, are evidence of a risk of abuse of market power in certain sectors characterized by the presence of oligopolies. this report clearly calls for further projects to open up the network and energy industries to competition, in line with the objectives of the juncker plan. i voted against this text, refusing to approve a failed single market project and plans for large-scale liberalization.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because it advocates many measures that would help to solve the problems that are hindering the internal market. i support the conclusions of this report which call on the commission to implement rules on infringements of competition law, state aid and merger control in order to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market and to enable social progress.
in writing. ‒ i voted against mr messerschmidt's report because it refuses to recognise the bitter failure of european competition policy, which has only increased the constraints on smes without preventing the dominance of a few monopolistic players. worse still, this policy makes most of the targeted state aid illegal and therefore does not allow for a strategic state policy, which is more necessary than ever. i also believe that taxation cannot be a matter for the union, contrary to what is stated four times in this report.
in writing. this annual report on competition policy highlights the key role it plays in strengthening the european single market and thus increasing federalism and the race to the top. the european union, under the guise of promoting growth, innovation and social progress, is thus seeking to further regulate the granting of state aid, to further harmonise tax rules and to complete the digital single market. the report also seeks to identify imbalances which are likely to create distortions of competition, but never mentions the so-called posted workers directive which creates unfair competition vis-à-vis our companies and smes or the union's refusal to introduce intelligent protectionism at the frontiers. the report also stresses the need to 'effectively respect the needs of citizens ... by placing their concerns at the centre of the decision-making process', something we could welcome if this technocratic and sprawling union did not do the exact opposite of what it advocates. the union in its present form is a machine for crushing peoples on the altar of ultra-liberalism and free and undistorted competition; i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ the union's competition policy is one of the pillars of the policies pursued by the european commission. however, far from supporting the emergence of a free market that would promote 'pure and perfect competition', the union's competition policy has in fact increased the regulatory pressure on smes/tses and local public services. it also supported the replacement of public monopolies by private monopolies run by rapacious multinationals. the commission has, through its state aid legislation, blocked any attempt by states to implement a policy of economic patriotism towards these strategic sectors. finally, the report advocates giving the union fiscal competence, which is tantamount to endorsing a further leap forward in euro-federalism. for all these reasons, i voted against the messerschmidt report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on european competition policy for 2013. i am all for competition, provided it is fair. competition is a driver of economic growth and job creation, but it must be done in an environment where all actors have the same chances of success. i have reaffirmed my position in this report in favour of fiscal and social convergence within the european union. we must fight against social dumping which only widen the disparities between our countries. if we are to open our borders and promote the mobility of workers, it is essential that we bring our social policies closer together. the same applies to the convergence of tax policies in the member states. it is time to act and to harmonize our tax policies in order to avoid these problems. i would like to reiterate my intention to fight for this cause as an alternate member of the special committee on taxe.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report, which once again shows that within the european union, dogmatism is stronger than reality. competition policy is one of the european union's greatest failures: were we promised the end of monopolies? they have been replaced by oligopolies which are twice as dangerous for smes: just look at the union's incompetence in the face of google. we were assured of equal competition for access to public contracts? however, the regulations continue to favour the large groups. this policy is equally disastrous for the protection of our strategic sectors. what is the solution of the commission and its accomplices in parliament to this? more european integration, more of the single market! the commission is calling for a new wave of liberalisation in the gas and electricity sectors and is seeking to bring tax competition under european regulation. the margin of manoeuvre for the states is therefore being reduced a little more and, in the name of the ideology of the removal of frontiers, the peoples of europe are being promised an ever more austere future.
in writing. ‒ this report is based on the 2013 annual report on the european union's competition policy, which was established by the european commission to combat cartels and anti-competitive practices. the report notes in particular the modernisation work carried out in state aid in many areas, such as the environment, energy, regional funds and research and innovation. in the agricultural sector, the report calls on the commission, in particular, to examine the potential effect of large supermarkets on competition in the food supply sector, both in europe and in the developing world, when it is next to review the reform of the cap. for these reasons i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the european union's competition policy is at the heart of the european construction. it helps to boost the competitiveness of firms, to promote the single market and to ensure that consumers benefit from the fairest prices. this is why this european parliament report calls on the european commission to consider new tools to strengthen the fight against fraud in this area, beyond a simple policy of fines, which may not be deterrent. it is worth recalling that cartels between large groups cause losses of between eur 181 and 320 billion, or about 3% of eu gdp, to the detriment of consumers' purchasing power. the report also deplores the fact that after four years of investigation, the commission has no further results in its infringement case against google. the report thus reaffirms the vigilance of the european parliament in defending consumers, the driving force behind european growth.
in writing. ‒ the annual report on the union's competition policy presented to parliament fails to conclude that the objectives of pure and perfect competition in the single market have not been achieved in the goods and services sector. the abuses of dominant positions and cartels, against which the text suggests some laudable measures, are evidence of a risk of market power in certain sectors characterized by the presence of oligopolies. the text also clearly calls for the continuation of projects to open up the network and energy industries to competition, in line with the objectives of the juncker plan. i voted against this text, refusing to approve a failed single market project and plans for large-scale liberalization.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the messerschmidt report on competition policy, despite some positive points, for example on unfair tax competition or support for banks without profit for the real economy. on the substance, i cannot agree with the rapporteur that 'the open market economy with free competition is enshrined in the treaties' (paragraph 1). it is a denial of the right of the peoples to choose the rules which govern them, since a model is imposed on them which is engraved in the marble of europe. it is also because this policy, applied in a strictly dogmatic way, has largely failed its objectives: the disappearance of entire sectors of our industry; the undermining of public services; the increase in prices and the reduction in the quality of services in many "liberalized" sectors - electricity, rail, postal services, etc.; the exclusion of smes from public contracts with collateral damage to local employment and the increasing use of posted workers; replacement of public monopolies by private oligopolies uncontrolled by the political authorities; the european union has always been a party to the treaty of rome, and it has always been a party to the treaty of rome. the balance is far from positive. this is not due to the inadequacies of competition policy, but to its abuses.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which sets out the state of play of competition policy and the application of state aid within the european union. i am glad that the text adopted this year highlights the google case, against which the european union must urgently take action, and the need to deal with social dumping and the misuse of the structural funds in the context of competition policy. the tax aspects are also essential and unfair practices in this area must be combated in order to ensure fair and balanced competition between member states.
in writing. ‒ this report highlights the unmet objectives of fair competition in the single market, particularly in the area of goods and services. it also highlights the abuse of dominant positions and cartels, against which the report proposes measures which are laudable, although feared. the risk of oligopoly formation in certain sectors is particularly high and the legislator will have to be attentive to this. finally, the commission proposes to open up the network and energy industries to competition, thus recalling the objectives of the juncker plan. i therefore refuse to support a text which advocates a single market project and liberalisation throughout europe, in all sectors. i voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by my colleague morten messerschmidt on the annual report on the eu's competition policy, presenting the european commission's legislative activities under the state aid, cartel and merger/acquisition rules. the text calls on the commission to revise its 2006 antitrust/cartel fines guidelines. the lack of concrete results in the google survey is also regrettable. the report was adopted by a large majority, which i welcome.
in writing. ‒ i supported the annual report on eu competition policy. competition policy plays a key role in creating conditions for innovation, productivity, job creation and growth in europe. the report calls on the commission to implement a number of measures to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market, including the implementation of rules on infringements of competition law, state aid and merger control. i'm very happy about the adoption.
in writing. ‒ the report contains some interesting elements, such as google's abuse of a dominant position and the demand for stronger investigations into tax aid. but as a whole, this report takes up the whole of the european doctrine on the primacy of the construction of the single market and the virtues of competition. it is this approach that is forcing all public monopolies and undoing our public services one by one. i therefore preferred to vote against this report rather than to join in this advocacy of the destructive logic of quality public services for the citizens.
in writing. ‒ the annual report on the union's competition policy presented to parliament fails to conclude that the objectives of pure and perfect competition in the single market have not been achieved in the goods and services sector. the abuses of dominant positions and cartels, against which the text suggests some laudable measures, are evidence of a risk of market power in certain sectors characterized by the presence of oligopolies. the text also clearly calls for the continuation of projects to open up the network and energy industries to competition, in line with the objectives of the juncker plan. i voted against this text, refusing to approve a failed single market project and plans for large-scale liberalization.
in writing. - vote against. competition policy is one of the tenets of the european union, which requires that markets be opened up more by eliminating all obstacles to competition. the report considers that "competition prevents excessive concentration of economic and financial power in the hands of a few players, which in itself represents a risk to the independence of european political power vis-à-vis the large industrial and banking groups". this policy has therefore failed, as certain sectors have seen the emergence of oligopolies (banking, retail). the big brands, often condemned for collusion, put a lot of pressure on suppliers through joint purchasing centres. smes remain the losers, disadvantaged by regulations that favour large groups, depriving them of public contracts. the state can no longer protect its strategic sectors and the european competition policy pursues the objective of eliminating the last barriers to the single market. the commission's position is therefore not effective in relation to the main monopolies, and the commission's position is incompatible with a policy of state strategy and the consequences for smes.
in writing. ‒ vote against this report which goes against the interests of the member states and their smes by increasing the pressure on smes without preventing the dominance of a few players such as the major economic powers. the report also makes most targeted state aid illegal and lacks concrete references to the social consequences of certain policies.
in writing. ‒ the annual report on the eu's competition policy is based on the ideological premise that only unlimited and barrier-free competition will enable europe to emerge from the crisis and return to growth. it even says that "competition policy is itself a safeguard for european democracy". the usual catechism is then recited, for example, the "third set of measures for the liberalization of gas and electricity" should be implemented "without delay". or "continue to move towards the completion of the single transport market". unlimited competition is disastrous for the peoples of europe. if the medicine kills the patient, it is not because the dose is insufficient but because it is bad. the dose should therefore not be increased but changed. i vote against it.
in writing. ‒ the european union's competition policy has always considered the free play of market rules and pure and perfect competition as the guarantors of growth and employment. it has failed in this respect on a rather broad scale. monopolies have been replaced by equally predatory oligopolies. smes are too often denied access to large public procurement contracts. the privatisation of former public utilities such as energy, transport and telecommunications has mainly maximised the profits of a few players. the banking sector is getting a lot of aid, but it is not helping the real economy. finally, the commission's control of state aid prohibits any policy of support for strategic or distressed economic sectors by the states, i.e. any sovereign economic policy. a too dogmatic competition policy is therefore counterproductive, while the freedom to undertake business is often hampered by the burden of administrative and fiscal constraints.
in writing. this annual report on the eu's competition policy praises the effect of the single market and competition policy on member states' economies. it recommends further reducing the scope of services of general economic interest (sgeis) exempted from notification, such as social housing, and derogations from state aid for sustainable energy. in the name of the sacred principle of free and undistorted competition, it proposes to break down national borders and artificial barriers a little more, while at the same time being concerned about social dumping and eliminating monopolistic energy suppliers, even though the united states has backed down. it is in an anti-protectionist dogmatism in the name of globalised free trade which nevertheless leads to massive deindustrialisation. the report also states that competition policy is itself a means of safeguarding democracy, reflecting the liberal ideology behind it. the analysis of smes is incomplete: it is mainly the economic depression caused by austerity that is contracting credit. finally, there is no provision for the requirement of reciprocity in public procurement... i therefore opposed the adoption of this text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text on the commission's annual report on its activities to enforce the provisions of the european competition policy. the text calls for a better fight against social dumping and the misuse of the structural funds by certain member states. the text also recalls the need to guarantee an open internet and to enshrine net neutrality in european law.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this text because it supports the liberalisation of the european railway sector at all costs. in the previous parliament i opposed the limited liberalisation that the european conservatives wanted and i still support the same position today. liberalisation is not a sign of progress for rail transport.
in writing. ‒ european competition policy is now at the heart of the new juncker commission's strategy to increase competitiveness and stimulate economic growth within the union. however, this policy cannot be effective without strict compliance with the rules at european level. we emphasized these elements when we voted yesterday on the annual report on the union's competition policy. i am pleased to have voted in favour. the text stresses the importance of effective and innovative policy and the need to combat dubious practices. i would particularly like to see us combating social dumping and the fiscal war between european partners. everyone has to play by the same rules. these are real problems for our social and fiscal model.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament voted today on the annual report on the european union's competition policy, presented by a conservative mep, mr messerschmidt. in this text, the rapporteur sets out the classic right-wing view of the primacy of competition over the general interest, the superiority of competitiveness over the quality of public services. the transport sector, for example, calls into question the state's management of certain key sectors, whereas experience shows that where transport is not profitable, public power is needed to ensure the continuity of the public service. once again, the conservative right is seeking to weaken social cohesion to prepare the ground for deregulated liberalism. if sometimes compromises with the european right are useful in advancing our proposals, then futile compromises only serve to dilute our message and our political positions, as would have been the case with this text. in line with the group of the progressive alliance of socialists and democrats, i have therefore decided to reject this report.
in writing. ‒ this report sets out the european union's competition policy and gives its opinion on the commission's annual report. i supported this text which again calls for an end to the state aid scheme for the banking sector and stresses the lack of effect on bank loans, asks the commission to review its 2006 guidelines on antitrust fines and finally calls on the commission to combat the problems of social dumping, on which we will remain uncompromising.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, which takes stock of competition policy in the union, particularly in the energy, transport, public services and digital sectors. the report regrets in particular that the proceedings against google have still not achieved a tangible result in its case of infringement of competition law, namely the preferential treatment granted by google to its own services in the display of search query results. i am also glad that parliament rightly points out that worrying practices such as social dumping or the misuse of the structural funds distort competition in the union.
in writing. ‒ the european union's competition policy is the source of two injustices. it is a failure in the face of large groups like google and it is incompatible with a state strategy promoting strategic sectors that support smes and supporting them in return. i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ european competition policy has failed to achieve its objectives by increasing pressure on smes without preventing the dominance of a few players. it therefore makes most of the targeted state aid illegal. i therefore voted against, along with the whole french delegation.
in writing. ‒ this annual report on competition policy is in line with the reports adopted in recent years by the previous reports. as always, he is advocating greater openness to competition, calling into question state aid and calling for more liberalization, with the key element being the systematic dismantling of what remains of our public services. the aim is to improve the quality of transport services, particularly rail services, and to manage port and airport networks. we would have known. the demand for "universal and high-quality public services" put forward by the gue/ngl was of course rejected in favour of a logic of maximising the privatisation of profits and socialising losses. competition is, by the very nature of the report, placed on a pedestal, described as 'a safeguard of european democracy'. you have to say it and the greeks among others will appreciate it. not surprisingly, i voted against it.

written explanations of vote
in writing. ‒ this annual report does not seek to redefine the role of the central bank, since it cannot criticise the legitimacy and effectiveness of its action. the ecb's reaction times to deflationary risk are not justifiable and the report does not describe any of the reasons for this. the reform of banking regulation in the euro area is also not in depth, while european banks, having put national economies at risk through their activities, their irresponsibility in managing private funds and the risks taken in risky market operations without sound equity levels, are still not sufficiently involved in the refinancing of the real economy. finally, the ecb's action is still disconnected from national economic realities and supranational monetary policy does not respond to the needs of the economy and the imperatives of reducing public debt. i voted against this report, which shows the difficulties the ecb is having in reforming itself and justifying the relevance of its strategies.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this deliberation because i agree with the conclusions of this report.
in writing. ‒ the very existence of the ecb is contrary to the principle of monetary sovereignty to which i am committed. the 2013 balance sheet is only a reflection of the policy of confiscation of our monetary independence.
in writing. this ecb report, which is surprised at the lack of progress in the euro area economy, aims to save the euro at any cost, even at the expense of the member states. unfortunately, the rescue of the single currency has consequences for the budgetary policies of the member states, since it contributes to a cure of austerity and a risk of deflation by contracting domestic demand. the european union must understand that the euro is a currency that is not suited to such different economies and can only lead people to ever greater austerity and precariousness. it is becoming more than urgent for nations to get their national currencies back in order to revive growth. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. i voted against the 2013 annual report of the european central bank. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the 2013 annual report of the european central bank is a reflection of the policy of confiscation of our independence.
in writing. ‒ the european central bank report reflects the european union's inability to propose a lasting way out of the crisis. the ecb has drawn on its last resources by deciding to lower its key interest rates to boost borrowing by households and businesses and to restore export competitiveness to our companies. given the very limited effects of this policy, criticism of the single currency euro has been reinforced. yes, the eurozone is a zone of macroeconomic divergence on the brink of deflation. the european council in luxembourg on 14 and 15 december adopted a resolution on the situation in the community and the european parliament's opinion on the situation in the community. finally, in challenging the role played by the ecb, i naturally voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ the european central bank is a key institution in the european economic and financial system. the ecb's role is to ensure price stability and thus to maintain inflation rates close to but below 2%. in a context of very low economic growth, this is proving to be an extremely difficult task. the ecb has nevertheless succeeded in using innovative and unconventional practices to stabilise inflation within the european union. i welcome these efforts and encourage the ecb to continue to do so. a good monetary policy such as that of the ecb is indeed necessary but it will not be sufficient to bring our economies back on track. each member state must be aware that appropriate structural reforms are more than indispensable and that monetary policy alone will not be able to improve the economic situation within the union. i also welcome the new role of the ecb as a banking supervisor. i believe that this decision will increase investor confidence in the european banking sector. this measure is in line with the investment plan of the european commission under jean-claude juncker. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because i cannot endorse the results of an institution whose legitimacy i also question. the very existence of the european central bank is an attack on the principle of monetary sovereignty. beyond that, the ecb's 2013 balance sheet reflects the policy of confiscating our independence: the direction of our monetary policy is thus decided by a wholly illegitimate board of governors, whose president, mario draghi, does not hesitate to state at the beginning of this annual report: "the achievement by governments of new decisive steps towards the establishment of a banking union will allow us to restore confidence in the financial system and to ensure that the euro is not a mere instrument of the european union's monetary policy". the ecb, like the other eu institutions, is therefore blinded by the ideology of a united states of europe, even as the euro crisis has demonstrated the failure of monetary convergence to achieve a single currency. the report is guided by the dogmatism which every patriotic member of parliament had to oppose. i dare you.
in writing. ‒ this report looks at the european central bank's (ecb) annual report for 2013 and welcomes the ecb's determination to be pragmatic in its efforts to save the euro and its responsiveness in a particularly difficult context. it is worrying to note that economic activity in the euro area remains relatively sluggish and that there is a real risk of deflation in the euro area. this situation, together with high unemployment rates in many euro area member states, threatens the stability of the euro area. this confirms the current policy orientation of the european commission, which i support, namely the creation of the conditions for a revival of investment, both public and private, through structural reforms in the member states and the implementation of the so-called juncker plan. for these reasons i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the report on the european central bank's activity in 2013 focuses on monetary policy on the one hand and financial stability on the other. in a difficult economic environment of sluggish growth, persistently high unemployment and the risk of deflation, the report considers it crucial to create the conditions for a revival of both public and private investment in the euro area and welcomes the introduction of the new instruments - the single supervisory and resolution mechanisms - to ensure greater financial stability.
in writing. ‒ the annual report presented to the european parliament does not seek to redefine the role of the central bank, since it cannot criticise the legitimacy and effectiveness of its action. the ecb's reaction times to deflationary risk are not justifiable and the report does not describe any of the reasons for this. the reform of banking regulation in the euro area is also not in depth, while european banks, having put national economies at risk through their activities, their irresponsibility in managing private funds and the risks taken in risky market operations without sound equity levels, are still not sufficiently involved in the refinancing of the real economy. finally, the ecb's action is still disconnected from national economic realities and supranational monetary policy does not respond to the needs of the economy and the imperatives of reducing public debt. i voted against this report, which shows the difficulties the ecb is having in reforming itself and justifying the relevance of its strategies.
in writing. ‒ the continuous decline in the european central bank's key interest rates since 2013, which continued in 2014, is unprecedented. the refinancing rate of private banks has never been lower in europe, much lower than in the united states. despite all these facilities, private banks have not played their part: no increase in loans to households and businesses. the interest rates on these loans remain high compared with other economic indicators. another inconsistency of the ecb is that the intermediation between the ecb and the member states, entrusted to private banks, is borne by the states and therefore by the taxpayers. the report that has been presented overlooks a problem too important to remain silent: the european union's inability to implement a recovery policy. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any information on the amount of the aid granted to the bank. the euro rescue was really a bank rescue. by refusing to impose a voluntary and consistent policy of credit and interest rates on these banks, the ecb has deliberately prolonged the economic crisis in the euro area. that is why i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it underlines the crucial role of the european central bank and its impact on the real economy in times of crisis. it stressed the need to ensure a good balance between the use of monetary, fiscal and structural levers in order to return to the path of growth. the ecb has no magic bullet to offer until the member states, including france, have carried out the necessary structural reforms to make their economies more competitive.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this text, refusing to support the monetary policy of the central bank, since it does not criticize its legitimacy or effectiveness. the lack of reaction to the deflationary risk is not explained, nor is the reform of banking regulation thorough. the irresponsible behaviour of some european banks, particularly in the management of funds in risky investments, without relying on solid and real funds, is also not highlighted. banks are not required to make a concrete commitment to the real economy. i voted against this text because the ecb is incapable of reforming itself and of defining coherent strategies. the latter is still disconnected from national economic realities and supranational monetary policies and therefore fails to meet the requirements for reducing public debt.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of my colleague pablo zalba bidegain's report on the ecb's annual report 2013, which calls on member states to push forward labour market reforms to improve competitiveness, increase potential growth, create new job opportunities, increase flexibility and optimise the conditions for firms to create jobs. in addition, the report notes that the trend towards shorter working hours appears to have reversed by the end of 2013, indicating a possible gradual improvement in the labour market. i welcome the fact that this report was adopted by 461 votes.

in writing. ‒ 2014 was a year of news for the european central bank. so it is a bit out of date to formulate a political opinion on its 2013 report in march 2015. the bidegain report itself goes very far beyond this framework and comments on the recent action of the ecb. it is not sufficiently critical of the policy pursued and of the cost of supporting the single currency. the ecb has used up the interest rate weapon (reduced to the historical low in september), then the unconventional tools (tltro and abs launched in 2014, quantitative easing initiated in early 2015) without succeeding in reviving economic growth. in addition, under the banking union, the ecb took over the supervision of systemic institutions, thus depriving the states of their supervisory power. the euro area, which the ecb represents, is more than ever an area of macroeconomic divergence. the ecb not only failed to revive european economies, but it also failed to fulfil its mandate of price stability (deflation risk) and economic convergence.

madam president, madam commissioner, this report of the epp, which has been laundered with lukewarm water, unfortunately does not sufficiently express the great challenge of the european budget in these times of crisis, namely to become a means of recovery. yes, it is imperative to resolve the payment crisis in order to restore credibility and room for manoeuvre to the european budget, and in this respect we will - as you know - pay particular attention to your proposals for a debt-clearing plan. but this question of the crisis in payments must not hide the dysfunctions of the union, nor the gaping budgetary gaps, some of which are structural. i would like to mention a number of problems: the delays in programming the structural funds, to the extent that we have to change the multiannual financial framework at a time when europe is in urgent need of investment; the youth employment initiative, which has so far failed to meet the objectives which parliament had entrusted to the commission and the member states; budgetary constraints, which deprive the union and the member states of the means to respond to the global challenges of the fight against terrorism, the ukrainian crisis and the great climate challenge. and, most importantly, there are our difficulties in funding innovation, the energy transition, the fight against climate change, blue growth. in short, everything that should stimulate growth in the future but which today cannot find the means either at union or national level. if investment in europe is a priority, we must have the courage to leave room for manoeuvre to the member states by giving the treaty on stability, coordination and governance (tscg) greater flexibility, for example by removing contributions to the union budget from the calculation of deficits. of course there is mr juncker's plan, but as it stands it would reduce funding for research and infrastructure projects and give the eib an extension to finance projects that are not very good. i ask you, commissioner, how can you accept that your prerogatives are being challenged? the question of financing the juncker plan must, in our view, be returned to the annual budgetary procedure and be given all the necessary leeway. finally, i would like to emphasize the last point in our resolution, the structural question of the budget: the union's own resources. commissioner, you have assured me of your determination on this matter and i thank you for that, but we must hurry to get this project under way as soon as possible.

madam president, one year after the first cases of ebola, a first assessment is necessary. it is clear that despite the warnings, the local and international responses were far too late and are therefore partly responsible for the scale of the epidemic over 9,000 deaths. one of the main causes of contagion is burials with local rites, so there are still pockets of cases. but despite all this, the epidemic was, fortunately, contained fairly quickly. however, we can add that the rainy season will bring opportunities for other fevers, including malaria, and new panics. that, despite our requests, no consideration has been given to setting up reception centres in the member states, that the eur 4.9 billion planned and the eur 2.4 billion already paid have not been the subject of the setting up of control structures. we shall see how this is done at the meetings of the donors in april and june. for all these reasons, we will remain very vigilant not to relive 40 years of endowment to africa that ended in bottomless wells, with no benefit to the local populations.

kalniņa-lukaševica,president-in-office of the council. – mr president, vice-president dombrovskis, commissioners, rapporteurs and honourable members, it is a great pleasure for the latvian presidency to have this opportunity to discuss with you today the european semester, which has become, in less than five years, a core process for economic policy coordination in europe. the economic situation does not look as bleak as it did some time ago, and recent data give cause for moderate optimism, but i believe we all acknowledge that europe is not yet where it wants to be. the economic recovery is fragile, the legacy of debt weighs heavily on most member states and the employment situation remains difficult. the european semester was created in 2010 for europe to exit the crisis through better coordination of our economic action. this coordination has not always been easy and it still is not. the economies of member states differ and so do their policy priorities. but with the semester we have a common framework in which to discuss these policies, and their impact on europe as a whole, and to agree on the way forward. we are now looking more carefully at the implementation of the policy recommendations issued under the european semester. parliament is right to highlight in the resolution that more should be done in that context. the commission is working closely with each member state to pursue implementation. the council is also doing its part, taking a collective look, at ministerial and at expert level, at how the commonly agreed policies are being implemented, exchanging best practices and generating peer pressure. rebalancing and restructuring our economies cannot be done overnight. that is why we need to stay the course, and i am convinced that our joint efforts will pay off. turning now more specifically to this year’s semester and the 2015 annual growth survey: as you may know, the latvian presidency has engaged the council in broad discussions on the annual growth survey. obviously, the ministers of finance and employment have contributed but we have also debated the annual growth survey in the competitiveness, energy and environment councils. the transport council will address the issue this friday. this is further proof of the semester being embedded into our way of conducting economic policy, and more broadly all policies that contribute to growth and jobs. as far as finance ministers are concerned, yesterday in the ecofin council, vice-president dombrovskis presented the country reports on the economic policies of member states, prepared as part of the european semester. the council had a first exchange of views on them. it will discuss the in-depth reviews in may and the country-specific recommendations for all member states in june. the latvian presidency also decided to link the council debates on the european semester to broader sectoral policy initiatives. taking the example of energy, the annual growth survey was examined by the energy ministers in the same context as the new energy union and energy infrastructure proposals. looking at things from the energy policy perspective, the european semester is a tool for implementing, for example, the internal energy market. at the same time, the energy union is necessary to generate more growth in europe. what, then, are the results of the council’s work on the annual growth survey? first, i am pleased to say that the council fully agrees with the overall approach of the annual growth survey. by this i mean the integrated approach based on three mutually—supportive pillars: investment, structural reforms and fiscal responsibility. each of these is a necessary ingredient for reaching our growth and jobs objectives. on investment, as you may know, the council is taking forward the investment plan for europe diligently. yesterday, only two months after the commission presented its proposal, the ecofin council adopted a general approach on the european fund for strategic investments (efsi) proposal. for the presidency it is important to deliver concrete results that can benefit citizens. the presidency is now ready to negotiate with parliament and we will do our utmost to find an agreement by this summer, as called for by the european council. i know this house shares with us the sense of urgency and i hope it will be able to progress swiftly. we look forward to the first trilogue. the great potential of efsi is obvious. but it is just as obvious that we need to pursue in parallel the other strands of the investment plan. i refer in particular to improving the investment climate and, more generally, the business environment in europe. one of the most effective ways to do this is to reduce the regulatory burden at both european and national level. but we also have to ensure the necessary regulatory certainty for economic operators. moreover, we should not look at the efsi in isolation. eur 315 billion is a lot of money, but if we can harness synergies between the efsi and other eu programmes, structural funds and national funding, we will do even better. lastly, talking about investment, i want to highlight the need for special efforts to facilitate small and medium-sized enterprises’ access to finance, both at the stage of start—ups and also at the critical growth phase. the council looks forward to the initiatives that the commission will be taking on the capital markets union. looking now at the second pillar, structural reforms, these remain as necessary as ever. we must acknowledge that a lot has been done in many member states, and also that most of the reforms require a long—term perspective. a national education system, for example, cannot be overhauled within a year. council debates on the annual growth survey are, in fact, a great vehicle for exchanging experiences between member states on what works on the ground. they also contribute to our collective knowledge on how to prepare reforms in an inclusive way, engaging the relevant stakeholders. the pursuit of the european single market is strongly related to structural reforms at national level. here the discussions within the council point to the need to adopt a pragmatic, sector-oriented approach. to be effective, europe should focus on the sectors with highest potential, in particular the digital economy, energy, transport, telecommunications and services. under services, retail, business, construction and tourism services are among those that we want to look at as a priority. what emerges from these council debates is the emphasis on implementation and enforcement of existing single market legislation. your draft resolution on single market governance shows that our views converge on many issues. looking now at the last, though not the least, pillar of the annual growth survey, fiscal responsibility, we first have to recognise the significant progress made, since the crisis, in getting our public finances in order. the euro area as a whole now has a neutral fiscal stance and this is no small achievement, considering where we started from. unfortunately, we cannot rest on our laurels. public debt, in particular, is an issue that warrants our full attention if we are to safeguard the recovery and also to prepare ourselves to confront any crisis. hence, the council insists that all member states stay on course with fiscal consolidation – but not with any kind of consolidation. it should be differentiated, depending on the fiscal situation of each member state, and overall it should be growth friendly. in practice this means, for example, giving priority to tax reforms that can generate growth and securing public spending in growth areas such as education and research. before finishing, i would like to say a few words on ‘digital europe’. as you may know, it is one of the three priorities of the latvian presidency. i see it is also well covered in your resolution. we have used the council discussions on the annual growth survey to look too at the potential of the digital economy for the eu growth and jobs agenda. it is clear that europe needs a digital transformation to re-establish its status as a leading player in the global digital economy. digitisation should cut across all policy fields, from industrial to environmental policies. to digitise europe, member states need to reinforce their efforts at national level, but there are also a number of initiatives that we need to pursue at european level. in this regard, the council also looks forward to the commission presenting a comprehensive and ambitious digital single market strategy later this spring. i could continue further on the priorities and considerations of the council with regard to the annual growth survey or the european semester in general, and there are a number of other important issues raised in your resolutions that i could address. but i believe it is more important that we now engage in a discussion on the european semester and where our priorities this year should lie. i thank you very much and i look forward to hearing your views.
vice—president of the commission.– mr president, let me start by thanking the rapporteurs, mr rosati, mr gáll—pelcz and mr gutiérrez prieto, as well as the shadow rapporteurs, for their work. the european semester is our key tool for fostering convergence in europe’s economic and social policy and making sure that everyone plays their role to bring back jobs. the european semester will work only if we build a shared understanding of the key economic and social policy challenges. this is why your reports and today’s debates are so important. as highlighted in parliament’s reports, in spite of an ongoing recovery, the economic situation remains fragile and requires urgent action. we agree that structural, fiscal and monetary policies have to be combined to tackle the current challenges effectively, and that social considerations must enter more explicitly into the formulation of economic policies. i am pleased to see parliament’s support for the commission’s economic policy priorities: investment, structural reform and fiscal responsibility. firstly, we need a coordinated boost to investment. your support for the investment plan is highly welcome. the council agreed yesterday on a general approach on the european fund for strategic investments (efsi), and we strongly hope that it will be possible to finalise a legislative act by june so that the efsi can be fully deployed from mid—2015. the fact that several member states intend to contribute via their national promotional banks is also very good news. secondly, we need structural reforms. they are needed for competitiveness, for investment, for a better adjustment capacity and, ultimately, to create quality jobs and sustain our social market economies. labour markets and social systems face heavy fallout from the crisis. unemployment is still unacceptably high, especially among young people and the long—term unemployed. inequality and poverty have risen. we must create new jobs without adding to labour market segmentation. commissioner thyssen will elaborate on this. product and services market reforms are also needed in order to stimulate competition and innovation and to reduce prices for customers and costs for businesses. ambitious reforms are a task not only for member states but also for the european level. the commission has, in recent weeks, delivered strategies on the capital markets union and the energy union, and the digital single market will follow soon. the commission will also put forward a fresh internal market strategy by the end of the year, and commissioner bieńkowska will address this in a moment. thirdly, we need to pursue fiscal responsibility. without downplaying the achievements so far, most member states still need to work on their debt sustainability. at the same time, member states with more fiscal room for manoeuvre have an opportunity to increase their investments. these priorities are translated into country—specific analysis and conclusions in the economic governance package adopted by the commission at the end of february. the package took into account the commission’s communication on the best use of flexibility within the stability and growth pact. to make this three—pillar strategy work we must make better use of our system of economic governance. our common challenge is to stimulate implementation of our policy recommendations in the member states. to do this we believe that it is important to increase transparency and dialogue, as well as ownership of, and commitment to, the implementation of reforms. as a first step this year, we published the commission’s country analyses much earlier in the semester cycle. these reports present a clear view on the economic situation and on policy implementation. we now have three months of additional time for discussions and feedback on the analyses before the commission issues its recommendations in may. my fellow members of the commission and i, with other commission representatives, will travel to a number of member states for discussions with parliamentarians, social partners and governments. europe needs to re—embark on a path of real economic convergence in terms of growth and jobs and to address social concerns. to get there, member states must deliver on structural, fiscal and social policies and the eu must strengthen key common policies in fields such as energy, the digital single market and taxation. i look forward to a constructive and fruitful debate with you today.

grow again in 2015. but the pace of recovery is slow and the social consequences of the crisis are severe. this challenging backdrop requires an ambitious policy agenda. the 2015 annual growth survey member of the commission.– mr president, honourable members, the single market is a core part of the european semester, which is of course a joint exercise between the commission and the member states. i can compare the single market to a launch pad to get europe out of the crisis; it will allow us to unlock the investment potential in europe and, hopefully, create opportunities for our consumers and investors. but, if we are to make the most of it, we need to remove the remaining barriers and bottlenecks. i want to thank very much ms gáll-pelcz, mr rosati and mr gutiérrez prieto for their report. it is timely; it covers the most important issues and most urgent tasks. on the single market our first priority should be to make existing single market rules work to their full potential. we need better implementation – as ms gáll-pelcz said – effective monitoring and stronger enforcement. the commission has already set up a single market governance strategy to promote that. this includes implementation objectives for all legislation – in particular there will be a zero tolerance approach to the service directive. there will also be further development of online governance tools, such as your europe, solvit and the online single market scoreboard. we also duly stated the conclusions of the parliamentary cost of non—europe report. the european parliament expressed regrets that the annual single market integration report was not published this year and there was no sign or single market topic in the annual growth survey. let me be very clear: we are not reducing our efforts. on the contrary, we want to improve the quality and the impact of the reporting; we want to integrate all possible instruments and we are, of course, looking now at how to do this and working very intensively on this. for example, we are looking at streamlining the reports. we are looking at putting more focus on economic indicators because i deeply believe streamlining single market governance will help our wider efforts on the single market. this year, as was also mentioned, we will launch two major initiatives centred on the single market. the first one: the digital single market package, which will be released on 6 may 2015, and then for the end of this year we are planning the internal market strategy. all the proposed actions will be based solid economic grounds and impact assessments. there will be an objective assessment of what works and what does not. i can assure you that we will take the time to ask the right questions and to answer them properly. let me put a few of them. is harmonisation in the area of goods as efficient as it should be? can we improve or even extend the application of the mutual recognition principle in goods and services? how do we address the link between goods and services? how do we tackle the remaining barriers in goods and services? how do we get rid of discrimination over access to goods, services and online content cross—border? how can we get rid of the obstacles to cross—border e—commerce? how do we reduce the administrative burden on our companies to the minimum? these are only some of the questions we need to answer. and we need to do it in partnership with you and the member states. that is why this debate today is so useful. i really count on our close cooperation in the course of this year and in the course of the whole mandate.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat fraud. mr president, madam president, mr vice-president of the commission, ladies and gentlemen, the european semester is the quick response to the shock of the sovereign debt crisis, particularly in greece. crisis resulting from the scandalous absence of government in the euro area for ten years. when states agree to give each other the same currency, they must ensure that their entire territory constitutes an optimal economic zone. without convergence of tax and social legislation, without coordination of economic policies, without a genuine government, it is vain to pretend to escape instability and tragedy. to give substance to this governance and coordination, i make three recommendations: first, the allocation of a share of the european union's unpaid invoices to the member states' accounts to assess whether they are running an excessive deficit. it's a matter of credibility, a prerequisite for trust. we talked about this at length yesterday in connection with the 2016 budget. secondly, the standardisation of the presentation of the contributions of the states to the budget of the european union in their public accounts. it's a matter of consistency and readability. finally, the presentation of public accounts and the procedures for certifying their veracity should be harmonized. the aggregation of all these public accounts would express the true budget of europe and would undoubtedly facilitate cooperation between governments.
mr president, this european semester highlights a positive fact: growth is returning to europe. however, it remains a fragile and heterogeneous phenomenon. it is true that europe is suffering: it is suffering from a lack of investment - the rosati report says it very well. investment is still 20% lower than in the pre-crisis period. so it is true that the juncker investment plan is one of the answers. of course, we support this plan, but it will only be successful if trust is restored. but today we still have smes closing their doors, employees who are unemployed, young people leaving europe because they have no work and, of course, economic insecurity which prevents companies from investing. it is time for europe to regain the confidence of investors. there is no growth without trust. and there is no trust without fiscal consolidation and debt relief. i have seen the example of spain, which i visited last week. i have seen that the reforms already undertaken have led to a reduction in unemployment and the creation of new jobs. the situation is not the same in all member states. france, for example, is a country with many assets: it has many resources, it can rely on its extraordinary human capital, its dynamic regions and its smes. what a waste! because, in the absence of reforms of lasting impact, france is falling behind and threatens to drag the whole of europe along with it. that is why i want the commission to be firm. france must respect the rules of the stability and growth pact. the commission must of course listen to the people - as we have seen in the case of greece - but it must not listen to all the sirens. giving france two more years to implement its reforms is a heavy responsibility: to pass the burden of debt on to future generations and to delay economic recovery.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the european semester is not an end in itself. it is a tool for analysing public policies which will implement the objectives which are at the heart of these public policies. far from being an accounting exercise, this coordination must measure the effects on the ability to revive the economy while reducing inequalities. this requires respect for the three pillars of sustainable development: economic, social and environmental. the report shows that much remains to be done. firstly, tax harmonization, the elimination of this competition and of this fiscal dumping between states. in public procurement too, to help smes, small businesses and artisans through calls for tenders that not only aim at low costs but also at a more sustainable economy and jobs that cannot be relocated. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. in the end, beyond our differences, this report on the governance of the single market tries to find this balance between the economic, social and environmental dimensions. that is why, on behalf of the green group, we shall vote in favour of this report.
mr president, while fiscal consolidation in the euro area countries is far from complete, the european institutions have still not understood that it is the austerity corset that prevents any lasting recovery and any parallel reduction in unemployment. the commission is counting on the rescue of the euro, which was supposed to be catastrophic only yesterday, and the fall in oil prices to keep the economies of european countries afloat and boost employment. but it may not last. while the unemployment rate, especially among the youngest and least qualified, has exploded in france and the countries of the south, the proposed measures do little to hide the sense of helplessness in the face of the consequences of the measures which the commission cherishes. the youth employment initiative and the youth guarantee are mere caucuses on a wooden leg, which do not sufficiently address the essential issues of training and low-skilled workers. with the unemployment rate in the euro zone at 11.5% compared with only 7.3% outside the euro zone, the european union is putting a modest veil over the real debates to be held on the single currency and on smart protectionism.
in writing. the european parliament gives its opinion on the annual growth survey 2015, the comprehensive analysis document initiating the european semester, which is intended to ensure the coordination of economic policies in europe. the distribution of powers between the various parliamentary committees leaves me in doubt. the report on employment and social aspects in the context of the annual growth review provides a clear analysis of the disastrous consequences of the austerity policies in the peripheral countries of the union, but also of the accelerated fiscal consolidation measures which have broken the mechanism of the recovery. i welcome the excellent work of the socialist rapporteur, sergio gutiérrez prieto, who has convinced a majority of members to support a plan to combat dumping and tax evasion and to call for the introduction of an ambitious financial transaction tax. the report of the committee on economic affairs, however, contradicts this analysis, referring to the 'success' of the troika programmes in greece, portugal and ireland, while calling on the other states to show the same ambition in modernising their economies. the troika's record is disastrous: economic recession, explosion of unemployment and significant increase in debt.

in writing. ‒ i voted for this text for two reasons. the first is that we must give priority to local production, in france for the french, then at european level, and finally at international level. the suspension of certain import concessions would help our agricultural production. the second is that turkey has since 1996 imposed a ban on the importation of live cattle and restrictions on the importation of beef. i respect the protectionist decision of a sovereign state, but i would like to see the principle of reciprocity applied and that we in turn can exercise our rights to defend our production, and in particular our agriculture.
in writing. ‒ this report concerns the codification in eu law of regulation no 1506/98 suspending certain concessions on the importation into the union of agricultural products originating in turkey. i support this text, which is merely an exercise in codifying positive law without any substantive changes. that is why i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ the gfcm, the regional fisheries management organisation, plays an active role in the development, conservation, management and exploitation of living marine resources in the mediterranean sea. following an evaluation of its performance, a procedure to amend the gfcm's constitutive text was launched. the new agreement clarifies its objectives and functions to enhance its effectiveness. it sets a clear overall objective: to ensure the sustainable use of resources from a biological, social, economic and environmental point of view. it also clarifies its functions, with the promotion of common fisheries management through multiannual management plans, the establishment of fisheries areas with regulated access, and the collection and dissemination of data. it integrates the main elements of the common fisheries policy, such as the objective of maximum sustainable yield, the ecosystem approach and respect for the precautionary principle, the reduction of discards, and the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. because the sustainable use of marine biological resources in the mediterranean and the protection of the marine ecosystems that support them play a vital role in promoting blue growth and sustainable development, i support this agreement.

in writing. ‒ since the new commission took office in november 2014, president juncker has focused on the recovery of growth in the union. the union's priorities are to promote strong growth and consolidate the recovery on the basis of three pillars: budgetary discipline, structural reforms and investment. the european parliament adopted this report. i am glad that i voted in favour of this text. i believe that growth can be restored in europe on a lasting basis if the union encourages and facilitates investment in europe and abroad and if it involves smes to a large extent in the recovery of growth. in addition, it is important to strengthen coordination between the different policies of the member states and to ensure the economic and budgetary cohesion of the union.
in writing. ‒ this report supports the european commission's approach to growth and recovery, which is based on three pillars: investment, structural reforms and growth-friendly fiscal consolidation. these pillars and reforms are part of the solution to reduce unemployment and poverty and to return to sustainable growth. i therefore supported this text, which also calls for greater involvement of national parliaments in the discussions on the european semester and for greater appropriation at national level of the country-specific recommendations. it is essential that europe becomes more competitive and continues its efforts to combat tax fraud and evasion and to strengthen the labour market.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text on the annual growth review drawn up each year by the european commission and which launches the 'european semester'. i support the three-pillar approach fiscal consolidation, investment and structural reforms to support the return of sustainable growth and job creation in europe. if europe is not to fall back into a crisis as terrible as the one it has just experienced, we must now continue along the path of better coordination of our economic policies, by strengthening and deepening the european semester. this requires, in particular, greater involvement of national parliaments in the development of country-specific recommendations, to ensure greater democratic legitimacy of the process. member states should also be encouraged to implement the recommendations made by the commission. they are intended to help people get back on the path to growth and employment. finally, the european semester must also be geared to better integration of financial markets, an active fight against tax fraud and evasion and an improvement in the efficiency of the labour market.
in writing. ‒ this report is based on the fact that the main directions of economic policy must be decided in brussels. i am opposed to it in order to defend democracy and the social and political rights of our citizens.
in writing. ‒ the supranational objectives of the european semester are expressed here in proposals for structural reforms which refer to two challenges in european employment and social policy: the search for greater flexibility in the labour market in a context of free movement of workers and a fundamental trend towards the harmonisation of employment protection rules. the convergence of economies and labour market systems is not based on any legitimacy or feasibility of these proposals. the text submitted to the european parliament is therefore a charm and is based more on political considerations than on real needs.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the final resolution on employment and social aspects in the context of the annual growth survey, a document published in november 2014 by the european commission which aims to ensure the coordination of economic policies within the union. it provides a lucid analysis of the disastrous consequences of the austerity policies in the peripheral countries of the union, but also of the accelerated measures of budgetary consolidation which have broken the mechanism of recovery in the other states of the european union. the quality of the recommendations in this resolution owes much to the excellent work of the socialist rapporteur, sergio gutiérrez prieto, who was able to convince a majority of meps to support, among other things, a plan to combat dumping and tax evasion and to call for the introduction of an ambitious tax on financial transactions.

in writing. this second report on the european semester for the coordination of economic policies focuses more particularly on employment and social aspects. the european union's austerity policies and the decline in investment spending are preventing and will prevent any recovery in growth and a fall in unemployment. the fall in the price of the euro (which european leaders welcome, but previously did not want) should allow for recovery. unfortunately, this situation is likely to be short-lived, as in the case of the fall in oil prices - a fall which does not improve households' purchasing power in any way, since prices at the pump have fallen only slightly. it is now urgent that the union should put an end to this policy of austerity and a rush to save a single currency which is not fit for purpose. i therefore voted against this text.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text on the social dimension of the european semester for the coordination of economic policies. the european semester is a very important tool, created in response to the recent economic and financial crisis and the sovereign debt crisis, to ensure that europe never again finds itself in a critical situation from which it is only just recovering. in practical terms, the european semester is an annual cycle of economic policy coordination, through which the european commission analyses the member states' plans for budgetary, economic and structural reforms and then makes recommendations to them for the coming year. in parallel with this, the commission also publishes its report on the alert mechanism, the heart of which is a scoreboard of indicators including social indicators which allows the commission to determine whether real imbalances exist in a member state and to recommend measures and reforms to address them. in this exercise, while compliance with the budgetary rules in force is essential, the commission should also take into account the social context of member states in financial difficulty.

on behalf of the ppe group. mr president, commissioner, thank you for your comments. you have rightly pointed out that the state of the bar stock is a matter of concern. the european union must respond and put in place coherent management measures. the european commission has recently, as you said, taken emergency measures to close pelagic trawl fisheries from 26 january to 30 april, i.e. during the spawning season. these emergency measures are temporary and are not intended to be permanent. we must therefore prepare now for the future and look to the long term. i have therefore decided to table a resolution on behalf of the committee on fisheries containing proposals for the sustainable management of the bar. we call for a multiannual management plan to be drawn up at european level, in accordance with the rules of the common fisheries policy. this plan will have to be based on sound scientific advice. this requires a precise assessment of the state and demarcation of the stock, as well as the migration patterns of the species and the precise breeding sites. the resolution calls on the commission and the member states to rely on the european maritime and fisheries fund, which provides for significant funding for the collection of scientific data. it is also necessary to assess precisely the share of the various trades fishing for cod and the share of recreational fishing in these catches. we need this information to make good decisions. when we work on a management plan for the bar, we will have to look at the different types of measures that can be taken. as you have just said, there are several options, such as setting a total allowable catch (tac), introducing a minimum landing size or introducing biological rest periods during spawning, among others. these are, at this stage, only options and it will be up to the legislator to make decisions in the light of scientific advice. i would like to take this opportunity to remind the council that management plans are entirely a matter for the codecision procedure. a management plan for the bar must take account of commercial fishing, but also of recreational fishing, as you said, which accounts for almost a quarter of the catches. i think it is necessary to introduce quantitative limits for this fishery. the measures to be taken must be prepared by involving closely all the parties involved in the cod fishery, in a spirit of compromise. the advisory councils will have an important role to play in this respect. running the bar is everybody's business. it is only together that we can find solutions to protect this beautiful species while preserving the activities of those who live in it.

in writing. ‒ although i largely agree with mr brok's report, i preferred to abstain on the final vote. the report does indeed outline an ambitious foreign policy for the union, adapted to the current and future challenges - terrorism, irregular immigration and energy security in particular. i also welcome the condemnation of the russian military intervention in ukraine and the reaffirmation of a common strategy towards russia contained in this report. however, i do not find in mr brok's text the commitment to freeze accessions to the union made by mr juncker last july. a pause in the process of enlargement of the union is necessary. the wave of accessions in 2004 and the accession of croatia in 2013 have considerably complicated the functioning of the union. the preaccession assistance instrument (pai) set up by the commission is a considerable source of money which would be preferable to be used to consolidate the achievements of the europe of 28. the current focus seems to be on completing the institutional adjustment to the previous accessions and on the internal problems facing the union.

in writing. ‒ this report presents an evaluation of the european common foreign and security policy. i am convinced that in the context of the deterioration of the union's security environment at its eastern and southern borders, the european union's influence in the world must be the first priority of an effective common foreign and security policy. as such, it is necessary for the union to commit itself to supporting its eastern neighbours and containing russia, to strengthening security and stabilisation in the south and to increasing its resources to serve these objectives. while the past few months have sometimes shown a lack of coordination of the union's external policies, i believe that this report presents a precise and sharp analysis of the situation and of the ways in which improvement and reforms can be made. for these reasons i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which calls for a more proactive, credible and strategic european foreign policy, based on a common vision of the union's interests and values and a common assessment of the threats to the security of our continent. the report also rightly calls on the member states to urgently strengthen their capacity to contribute to territorial defence, to commit more resources and to take the mutualisation and sharing approach seriously by intensifying their cooperation. some 130 million euros per year would be saved if these closer cooperation arrangements were implemented. the challenges are many: dealing with instability in eastern and southern europe, combating the jihadist threat, protecting europe's values and interests, improving the union's energy security, combating organised crime and trafficking, playing a leading role in conflict resolution and strengthening respect for the rule of law and human rights worldwide.
