in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this annual report, which takes stock of the state of respect for human rights and democracy in the world in 2013. the text recalls that the european union places the human person and human dignity at the heart of its action. the text calls for the systematic inclusion of binding clauses on human rights in the union's international agreements, including trade agreements with third countries. parliament also reiterated its unequivocal support for the abolition of the death penalty and expressed concern at the continuing high number of executions in china, iran, indonesia, saudi arabia and vietnam. the resolution also strongly condemns attacks on christian communities in africa, asia and the middle east, and more generally on religious minorities. i would prefer to abstain on the paragraph which 'encourages the institutions of the union and the member states to contribute more to the debate on the recognition of same-sex marriage', because i believe that this is a matter for the exclusive competence of the member states.
in writing. ‒ this report is more than a state of the world's human rights, it is an action plan for their universal establishment. once again, human rights are the true trojan horse of the european institutions in enshrining the principle of interference: it is a matter of distributing the good and bad points, even taking sanctions if national laws do not correspond to the european vision. this report exploits emotions to justify the dismantling of the national sovereignty of the member states, particularly in the area of immigration. this report seeks to devote the rights of active minorities to the detriment of the common good and genuine respect for the inherent dignity of the human person. it thus highlights 'in particular the guidelines to promote and protect all human rights of lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and intersex (lgbti) persons'. one might start by questioning the new adjective given to the "lgbt" influence group and thus the legal and political recognition of the status of "intersex". it is legitimate to ask why a particular minority, regardless of sexual orientation or religion, should be favoured under community law. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ this resolution calls for increased cooperation between the european union and the league of arab states against terrorism, and in particular islamist terrorism. it is rather balanced, taking account in particular of the necessary balance between freedom and security, and encourages the member states of the union to be more firm and more cooperative with the arab league states in the common fight against terrorism. the resolution rightly recalls that some arab league states, which sometimes have very close relations with some eu member states, have shown guilty indulgence towards islamist terrorist groups. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, while at the same time wishing to see a deepening of cooperation in the fight against terrorism, particularly with the countries most exposed, namely egypt, syria and iraq.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this surprisingly balanced resolution which calls for cooperation between the member states of the european union and the states of the arab league in the fight against terrorism.
the terrorist threat in europe is becoming more and more present, especially with radical islamists. it is therefore necessary for the european union to maintain relations with the league of arab states in order to combat terrorism and to take appropriate measures. this resolution is balanced and i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the draft resolutions on relations between the union and the league of arab states envisage enhanced cooperation in the fight against terrorism. it appears to be balanced, since it aims to tackle, in association with the states of the regions concerned, the rise of islamist terrorism. although it is not in principle the union's responsibility to deal with the foreign policy of the member states, this is a common sense measure which i support. i therefore voted in favour of the motions for resolutions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which, unusually, proposes a balanced view of the measures to be taken to combat islamic terrorism. the report provides for close and multilateral cooperation between the member states and the league of arab states. it also reaffirms the need to strike a balance between the measures needed to ensure our security and the care needed to avoid encroaching on the freedom of our fellow citizens. the report also stresses the need to rethink the eu's responsibility for the spread of terrorism, particularly as it continues to maintain privileged relations with countries suspected of financing terrorism. because our security is non-negotiable, the patriotic members of the house have supported this resolution.
in writing. ‒ this resolution welcomes the signing of a memorandum of understanding between the european union and the league of arab states to enhance dialogue and cooperation in the fight against terrorism. in view of the threat posed by terrorist groups, there is a need to strengthen the exchange of information on crisis situations and the sharing of assessments and good practices with a view to defining concrete actions to respond to the current threats related to the radicalisation, recruitment and displacement of terrorists and foreign fighters, as well as the return of these fighters to their place of origin. i believe that this is the right approach and that these policies cannot be effective without the close cooperation of the countries of origin and directly affected by terrorism, so i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. in the face of the global threat of terrorism, we must provide a global response. that is why i voted in favour of this resolution to strengthen our cooperation with the league of arab states in the fight against terrorism. it is crucial that we share our assessments and best practices, to prevent the recruitment and movement of terrorists and 'foreign fighters', as well as to address the underlying drivers of radicalisation. i am very much involved in this matter, as i am the rapporteur for the european parliament on a text for the prevention of radicalisation and recruitment of european citizens by terrorist organisations. everything must be done as soon as possible to deal with this growing global threat, and i welcome the rapid establishment of this strategic dialogue.
in writing. ‒ the european union is facing a terrorist threat which is already affecting many countries. it is clear that the member states of the union and the states of the arab league must strengthen their cooperation in order to combat this scourge together. in particular, this will involve strengthening our exchange of information on the recruitment and movement of terrorists and foreign fighters, as well as the practical fight against radicalisation, arms trafficking and terrorist financing. this memorandum of understanding between the european external action service (eeas) and the league of arab states (las) is therefore absolutely necessary. the fight against terrorism requires coming together and acting together. the resolution also stresses that counter-terrorism measures should not be misused to suppress legitimate protest voices or to violate human rights. it also recalls the inalienable right of religious minorities to be protected.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this debate because i believe that measures to manage cod fishing activities must be taken at european level if this species is to be safeguarded. i also believe that such measures should take due account of scientific knowledge and promote local management and the principle of regionalisation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, which consists of an assessment of stocks, the establishment of a total allowable catch (tac) and quotas under a multiannual management plan, quotas which will have to apply to recreational fisheries. this proposal corresponds to the wishes expressed by the french fishermen and i therefore supported it.
in writing. following a request from the united kingdom, the european commission has banned pelagic trawl fisheries for cod in the english channel, the celtic sea and the north sea until the end of april. however, this prohibition appears to be unfair and ineffective, with pelagic trawl fishing accounting for only 25% of catches. pelagic fishing is mainly carried out by the french, recreational fishing (75%) by the british, who are the origin of the ban request. the motion for a resolution presented here is in line with the requests of french fishermen, since it aims to assess stocks and, above all, to establish quotas (including for recreational fishing) as part of a multiannual management plan. i therefore voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ the resolution calls on the european commission to ban pelagic trawl fisheries for cod in the english channel, the celtic sea and the north sea until the end of april, following a request from the united kingdom. this prohibition, which is totally disproportionate, shows how far the technocrats in brussels are disconnected from the daily lives of the fishing industry. this prohibition is ineffective because it affects only 25% of catches, while the remaining 75% is made up of recreational and other types of small-scale fishing. it should also be noted that pelagic net fishing is mainly practised by french fishermen, while recreational fishing is mainly practised by english fishermen. the prohibition is therefore discriminatory, since it will have the effect of penalising the french shipowners in the first place. the commission has already proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of the environment against the risks arising from the use of certain substances in the production of certain products. i voted for this motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on european measures for the management of the cod, which i tabled on behalf of the committee on fisheries. the resolution proposes a roadmap for the establishment of a european multiannual management plan for the bar. this plan, which will have to be based on scientific advice, will be prepared in consultation with all the actors concerned. it will have to contain concrete long-term management measures for both commercial and recreational fisheries. the resolution identifies various possible management measures: reduction of tacs, increase of minimum landing size, introduction of biological rest periods, quantitative restrictions for recreational fisheries. these are only options at this stage which will have to be decided by the legislator, in the light of scientific advice and after extensive consultation with all the actors concerned. i now ask the european commission to launch a public consultation on the bar with a view to proposing a proper management plan for this species.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution which aims to propose measures to promote sustainable fishing, while also reiterating the unjust ban on fishing for pelagic trawlfish in the english channel, the celtic sea and the north sea, imposed by the commission last april. the proposal is to set up an assessment of the stock of bluefin tuna with a view to determining a total allowable catch (tac) and quotas under a multiannual management plan for recreational fisheries. this is a measure that has long been requested by french fishermen and is also being done in a spirit of preserving our ecosystem.
in writing. ‒ in january, the european commission took emergency measures to close the european waters to pelagic trawlers until 30 april 2015. these measures are intended to ensure the preservation of the species but are not intended to be permanent. the european parliament therefore calls, through this resolution, on the european commission and the member states to assess the state of the stock of barley and its delimitation. i believe that the european commission should quickly propose a multiannual management plan for the resource, taking into account scientific advice and in consultation with the relevant stakeholders, and i therefore voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. in the interest of preserving stocks of endangered marine species in european waters, i voted in favour of this resolution on european measures for the management of the stock. a multiannual management plan based on scientific advice should be established for this species, which is common in both commercial and recreational fisheries. the european parliament, through this resolution, urges the european commission to put in place long-term measures, such as increasing the minimum landing size or introducing biological rest periods, to improve the management of this species, while managing as well as possible the impact they may have on the actors concerned, in particular french fishermen.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution for two reasons: firstly, there is no denying that the situation of bar stocks is a matter of concern and requires an appropriate response; the commission has also proposed that the fishing industry be given a new role in the fisheries sector, and that the fishermen who make their living from this fishery be given a new role, something which is not possible with the moratorium used by the european commission in the absence of more precise legislation. it is therefore essential that the european parliament should take up the matter. i will be vigilant in the drafting of the legislative text and will make sure in particular that it does not harm any of the sectors involved.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution which proposes a roadmap for the implementation of a sustainable management plan for cod fishing, identifying several possible measures. the committee believes that a public consultation should be launched quickly in order to propose a genuine management plan for this species.
in writing. ‒ for years, scientists have warned us that the bar is over-exploited, but the commission has never been able to convince member states of the need for european-wide controls to preserve this species. at present, the restrictions are limited to technical measures: minimum landing size and mesh size limit. so much so that the commission had to enact an 'emergency measure' banning fishing for certain trawlers until the end of april. the purpose of this resolution is to ask the commission to assess the state of stocks and to propose a multiannual management plan for bluefin tuna with catch quotas, which should help save the species. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution in the interests of protecting the environment and preserving the species.
in writing. ‒ the front national meps voted in favour of the resolution on sustainable fishing for hake, as it is a balanced text aimed at avoiding the extension of the moratorium on fishing for hake beyond 30 april 2015, while proposing sustainable fishing measures beyond that date. the resolution rightly points out that restrictions should not be imposed on commercial fishing alone, which accounts for only 25% of catches.
in writing. ‒ the cod is a late-maturing, slow-growing fish, popular with both commercial and recreational fishermen. i was in lorient in january 2015 for a forum on the sea in the presence of alain cadec, chairman of the european parliament's committee on fisheries, when the commission took its unilateral decision to close the cod fishery. i was calling for the need for multiannual management of quotas, which in my view covered two key principles: firstly, the necessary definition of a total allowable catch (tac) and quotas for bluefin tuna, and secondly, planning for the management of activities over a long period of time. this motion for a resolution goes in that direction and i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. the purpose of this resolution is to review the ban on pelagic trawl fisheries for cod in the channel, celtic sea and north sea, which had been requested by the united kingdom, until the end of april. first, that prohibition is ineffective since it concerns only 25% of the cod caught in those seas and is unfairly discriminatory since it concerns only pelagic trawl fishing, which accounts for only a minor part of the total catches concerned. it is the french fishermen who are the main users of this practice, while recreational fishing is more commonly practised by the british. the improvements contained in the resolution, which respond to the demands of french fishermen, are in the right direction, and i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on the sustainable exploitation of the bar, whose stocks are in a worrying state. the text calls on the commission and the member states to assess the state of the stock of blue whiting and its demarcation, migration and exact breeding grounds, if necessary by using the european maritime and fisheries fund, which provides considerable funding for the collection of scientific data.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution proposing a roadmap for a multiannual european management plan for cod, as it will be prepared in consultation with all the actors concerned and will contain concrete and innovative long-term measures for both commercial and recreational fisheries.
in writing. ‒ i supported this resolution proposing a roadmap for the establishment of a european multiannual management plan for the bar. the commission could launch a public consultation in order to propose a proper management plan for this species. this plan will have to be drawn up in consultation with all the actors concerned and will contain concrete long-term management measures for both commercial and recreational fisheries. options that may be considered, but which will have to be decided by the legislator, include setting tacs (total allowable catches), increasing the minimum landing size, introducing biological rest periods or quantitative restrictions for recreational fisheries. this resolution is a real signal to the european commission and we hope that it will be heard.
in writing. ‒ following a request from the united kingdom, the european commission has banned pelagic trawl fisheries for cod in the english channel, the celtic sea and the north sea until the end of april. this prohibition appears to be unfair and ineffective: pelagic trawl fishing accounts for only 25% of catches, while the remaining 75%, not affected by the ban, is due to recreational fishing and other types of fishing (line, bottom trawl, net, etc.). it therefore appears that the scarcity of resources cannot be seriously combated by a discriminatory measure which affects only 25% of the catches. it should be noted that pelagic net fishing is mainly carried out by the french and that recreational fishing is mainly carried out by the british, who are the origin of the request to ban pelagic net fishing. the proposal by the chairman of the committee on fisheries, alain cadec, is to assess stocks, establish a total allowable catch (tac) and establish quotas under a multiannual management plan, quotas which will have to apply to recreational fishing. this proposal corresponds to the request made by the french fishermen. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ like other fish species, stocks of cod, fished mainly in the north atlantic between ireland and portugal, are declining, with the species's future recovery threatened if measures to regulate this fishery are not taken quickly. the fishery is characterised by a large proportion of recreational and even sport fishing, with catches representing 25% of the total number of catches. in order to ensure better management of the stocks of bluefin tuna for the conservation of this species, the resolution calls on the commission to take concrete measures such as stock assessment, a multiannual plan taking into account breeding periods, or the study of the establishment of fishing quotas. although i regret the rejection of my group's amendments calling for the extension of the emergency measures and the adoption of a regionalised approach to the management of this fishery, i voted in favour of this text which calls for better control of this fishery to safeguard the bluefin tuna and thus the biodiversity of our oceans. this is the right thing to do, even if it is a position taken by the european parliament without any legislative consequence.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution initiated by my colleague alain cadec, which proposes a roadmap for the establishment of a european multiannual management plan for the bar. this proposal follows the temporary ban on fishing for bluefin tuna announced as a matter of urgency in january 2015 to stop the decline in stocks. unlike other species, the bar is not subject to a specific management plan. the resolution proposes options to replenish resources and protect the interests of small-scale fisheries. parliament stressed that future recommendations should be based on scientific advice.

in writing. ‒ in the context of the 28th session of the united nations human rights council, the european parliament recalls the inalienability of human rights, whether civil, political, social or economic, and the priorities of the union in this field, particularly with regard to its partners where human rights violations are most evident. this resolution also seeks to address a subject which i believe is important, namely the links between climate change and human rights. environmental changes threaten the livelihoods of particularly vulnerable populations in low-income countries and in coastal and small island low-lying states that lack the economic resources to adapt to radical environmental changes. in this respect, climate change is an obstacle to the realisation of internationally recognised fundamental rights. because i believe that the states parties to the conference of the parties on climate change will have to take a stand on this issue, participate in the legal definition of the term 'climate refugee' at the international level and adopt ambitious mitigation and adaptation measures, i voted in favour of this resolution.

aimed at the completion of this internal energy market and without the firm application of the legislation of the third package on the internal energy market, the energy union will be impossible. we diversification of its energy sources. it must reduce its energy dependence and promote energy efficiency, particularly in buildings. the european union will thus be more competitive. thirdly, for the gue/ngl group mr president, commissioner, we are faced here with a profound flaw inherent in the present european construction which places the right to competition above the right to social progress. while one state - germany - decides to set up a minimum wage, neighbouring countries and the commission have exerted anti-social pressure to ensure that this minimum wage does not apply to lorry drivers. this is the way in which european employees are condemned to a life of social service. we must not accept such a logic. the commission and our parliament must support any initiative which allows for social harmonization from the top: the implementation of a progressive minimum wage in each country, a revision of the directive on posted workers in the sense of equal treatment of all workers in the european union. we have a responsibility to put social progress before the deadly right to compete.
mr president, commissioner, i welcome the presence of many european transport unionists in this chamber, who are listening to us. social dumping is a vicious circle, pitting employees against each other and favouring large firms over small ones. in the transport sector today, there is talk of fierce competition in labour costs because workers are particularly mobile in this sector. dentressangle in the road transport sector, ryanair in the air transport sector: these companies are not playing the game. in the shipping industry, it is the same: a new form of modern slavery is developing every day in this respect, with the exploitation of undeclared employees. commissioner, everyone in this house agrees that we have a real problem with social dumping in transport. yes, let's move! let us create a european labour inspectorate to monitor and punish unscrupulous employers. let's put together a blacklist of these companies. let's set minimum standards for working conditions and wages. this is precisely the opportunity to introduce a minimum wage throughout europe. as for transport, we must - it is true - move faster: strengthen the rules on cabotage in the road transport sector, clarify, in particular, the problem of national flags in the maritime transport sector. the german and french laws have recently changed so that every lorry driver is paid the minimum wage, particularly during his passage through the country. it is not a question of waiting for each state to introduce its own legislation. it is up to europe to take responsibility and provide a common response. if we do not act now against social dumping in this sector, this poison can put an end to our project, the european project. mr president, madam commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, social dumping impoverishes workers and undermines the european project. they must be fought with determination. the internal market and competitiveness cannot be used as an excuse to call into question the improvement of working conditions in all countries and i welcome the decision of the german government to introduce a minimum wage for cabotage. it is not a question of defending any particular country, but of defending an idea and a conviction. in december, the european parliament had already shown its determination by refusing to vote on an act which did not include illegal cabotage as a serious offence. it is now time for the european commission to take a serious look at the protection of social rights in transport. finally, i would like to point out that the application of a minimum wage to cabotage operations, which are clearly covered by the directive on posted workers, is fully compatible with european law. road transport undertakings must comply with the conditions of remuneration of the countries in which they carry out cabotage operations. in france there is a minimum wage and the government's initiatives will help to ensure that european legislation is properly respected.
mr president, commissioner, because of the very specific nature of international road transport - which is different depending on whether it is transit or cabotage - the risky link to the posted workers directive or the rome i regulation - which is often done in a haphazard way - has many very harmful consequences. firstly, a great disruption to the working environment of international lorry drivers, who are either shamefully exploited or have their jobs destroyed, as the national chains have lost thousands of driver jobs. secondly, in response to these facts, the action taken by the member states - and this is the subject of today's debate - can have serious consequences for the functioning of the single market itself. thirdly, the uncertainty in which the institutions find themselves about the attitude to adopt, which is, madam commissioner, your case today. i therefore strongly urge the commission to look into this problem and to adopt a specific legal framework for workers in international road transport, which will make it possible to defend their rights and ensure the proper functioning of this sector, which is so important for the union. it should be remembered that 72% of goods within the union are transported by road, making it an essential market tool. the present uncertainties and approximations can therefore no longer be tolerated.
mr president, commissioner, the commission is at a crossroads: we are discussing a highly european subject, road transport. without prejudice to smes, which throughout europe - as we know - create jobs, we need a number of clarifications today. the first is the distinction between transit and cabotage activities. it is extremely important that you be clear on this. the second point is the link between the work we have done on the directive on posted workers and the organisation of the work of road hauliers today. we really need a very clear clarification on this subject, a legal framework, as some of my colleagues have said, because we cannot allow ourselves to be dragged down the slope of social dumping and unfair competition between companies. i understand from the debate i'm hearing here tonight that we're going way beyond that. we are in a debate which is no longer a european debate: we have returned to national debates, in which everyone is defending his own piece of meat. yes, we need the commission to be a social commission, as jean-claude juncker has said and promised us. so you have to take a step forward and be firm about this sector.
madam president, commissioner, the issue we are dealing with this evening is of paramount importance for the future of european road transport and, more generally, for our vision of a social europe. as you know, international road hauliers can currently spend seven days loading and unloading their lorries in a transit country before they arrive in their destination country. it's called cabotage. however, these lorry drivers are not entitled to the same minimum wage or social protection as their colleagues in the country they are crossing. the activity is very similar and is carried out well in the same territory. in my country - france - the most highly-employed country in europe, french road hauliers are therefore in direct competition with other european road hauliers on their national market, which has led to the loss of 21 000 jobs in france in 15 years. we are also going to vote soon on a grant of two million euros for the fired truck drivers of the mory ducros transport company. a european solution is needed to fill the legal vacuum. i think that the rules on cabotage should be redefined and that a specific regime should be created for highly mobile workers. yes to mobility and competition, but no to a mad race to social dumping.
madam president, it is not surprising that parliament is concerned about the roma today. since 2010, the european union has been increasing communications, recommendations and regulations to force member states to achieve roma integration. the aim is to enable roma to find jobs and housing and to provide their children with an education. at the same time, the european union has spent billions of euros on roma. for example, the european social fund has paid out €13.3 billion between 2007 and 2013 to finance the integration of roma. all these efforts have largely failed. in france, for example, the andatu programme in the rhône department is being hailed as a success. it has cost 2,600,000 euros over three years and has only served to obtain residence permits and to receive the income of active solidarity, without succeeding in integrating them into the labour market or into french society. let's be realistic, it would be better to change the policy and put pressure on romania and bulgaria to treat their roma with dignity instead of trying to integrate them elsewhere, even when they don't want to.
in writing. international roma day is an essential event to better combat prejudice and to denounce the discrimination and persecution that roma still suffer too often. the european roma inclusion strategy adopted in 2011 is still not sufficiently implemented in the member states. thus, roma still do not have access to the same healthcare as other european citizens. roma children are less likely to attend school and in some countries even receive training normally intended for disabled children. in addition, roma often live in unacceptable hygiene and sanitation conditions, while discrimination in employment persists. the eu's roma inclusion strategy must be continued and expanded. the european commission therefore has a responsibility to be more vigilant about the effective application of the directive by the member states and to apply sanctions when necessary. the inclusion of the roma is an issue for this minority but also a challenge for europe. a challenge to the scourge of populism. a challenge to the european idea, because the roma are the heart of our europe. this europe is full of diversity and multiculturalism.

in writing. ‒ this request, which concerns greece and more specifically attica, the region most affected by unemployment in greece (26.3%), proposes the mobilisation of commitment appropriations (eur 5.046 million) to help the broadcasting sector in greece, following the dismissal of 928 people in 16 broadcasting companies. the causes mentioned are the fall in household purchasing power, which has led to a collapse in demand, and the deterioration of credit conditions. the aid consists of subsidies for vocational retraining and training and unemployment benefits. however, these causes are only the consequence of the dramatic contraction in domestic demand and the fiscal austerity in force in greece, under the pretext of fiscal consolidation and reduction of the external deficit. i have decided to vote in favour of this aid, which is essential for the economic recovery of this greek region. although the globalisation adjustment fund is a means of tackling the problems caused by austerity and the opening up of the world to the four winds of globalisation, it seems essential to provide financial assistance to these sectors currently threatened by the crisis.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament voted today on the annual report on taxation, a text brought by the socialist mep eva kaili. the text recalls the extent of tax fraud and tax evasion in europe: each year, almost €1 trillion is avoided from the tax revenues of the member states, even though public finances have been severely affected by the economic and financial crisis. the resolution contains several strong messages that the european parliament wants to convey to the council: the discussions on the financial transaction tax (ftt) have gone on too long, the 11 member states participating in enhanced cooperation must finally take their responsibilities to set up this instrument of fiscal justice. the commission is also proposing to make the common consolidated corporate tax base (ccctb), the first step towards tax harmonization, compulsory in the european commission's proposal, which is expected in june.
in writing. ‒ in the wake of the luxleaks scandal involving the current president of the european commission, mr jean-claude juncker, ms kaili's report quite logically denounces tax fraud by calling for sanctions. the national front, which calls for an end to aggressive tax optimisation, is of course in favour of this because it is the member states and, with them, their honest taxpayers who are the first victims. i therefore voted in favour of this text, which is rather in the right direction, but i remain vigilant against the temptation of some to impose tax harmonization on us which would deprive the member states of their sovereignty in this area.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. the report commends the efforts made to increase transparency on tax evasion. however, this is optimism and blindness. european law provides for the free movement of capital between the member states of the union and with third countries. the strategy of tax optimisation with tax havens, which are usually island-based, would thus not be resolved. the measures envisaged will only shift the problem by increasingly sophisticated tax engineering on the part of multinationals. tax harmonization is a trick, since competition will always lead some countries to adopt aggressive policies. after having opened up the frontiers, the union is surprised that vat, a tax which was initially impossible to avoid, is subject to such behaviour, and therefore proposes a harmonization of rates, which would be contrary to all sound economic sense, as the needs of the countries differ so much. finally, we have the financial transaction tax, which the current commissioner moscovici refused in 2013 when he was minister of economy... in short, this report ignores the will of the states and the fact that they must remain sovereign in tax matters.

i'm the reporter. mr president, madam commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, we are facing a review today, albeit a technical one, which follows the very significant delay in the implementation of the operational programmes. in fact, all funds under shared management in the period 2014-2020 are concerned. at 31 december 2014, more than 300 operational programmes were not yet adopted and could not benefit from the deferral procedure provided for in article 13 of the financial regulation. all member states are concerned. indeed, more than 21 billion euros would have been lost without this revision. in some countries, the bulk of the commitment appropriations for these programmes are even affected. some examples: for the czech republic, 99.6% of funds would be lost, for romania, 80%, for spain, over 60%, and for the united kingdom, over 50%. fortunately, article 19 of the multiannual financial framework allows for an amendment to be introduced by 1 may this year to transfer the allocations from 2014 to 2015 in the event of non-adaptation of these programmes. for all these reasons, you will understand why we are voting in favour of this amendment. however, given the territorial impact for all countries and the equally considerable amounts at stake, this foreseeable revision adds to the worrying dysfunctions of our budgets. firstly, this situation raises the question once again of the sincerity of our budgetary decisions, since at the time they were taken we were behind schedule and we knew it. secondly, in the context of a chronic investment deficit in europe, such a delay in the arrival of the structural funds, linked to the validation of the operational programmes, is hardly acceptable and delays investment on the ground. thirdly, this delay in implementation will also have an impact on payment appropriations because by shifting commitments by one year, the entire payments could be shifted by that amount, which would add additional pressure on the union's payment appropriations at the end of the period of the multiannual financial framework. we are all familiar with the snowball effect, the accumulation of unpaid invoices which undermine the union's credibility by leaving thousands of project promoters in the face of this budgetary cavalry. i hope that this revision will not aggravate the current crisis in payments, but it may in writing. ‒ the fund was called in 2015 for an amount of over eur 6 million to support the reintegration of dismissed employees of the mory-ducros group. i strongly support this request and would like to stress the importance of such a european instrument to help and support european citizens directly affected by globalisation. this aid will finance the vocational reorientation of these workers and their reintegration into the labour market.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the granting of eur 6 million in aid to former employees of the french carrier mory-ducros. the french company had to close down in may 2014 after experiencing severe economic difficulties for several years. while almost half of its employees were re-employed by another company, 2 513 workers are now unemployed. the french authorities have applied to the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf). the fund allows, under certain conditions, financial assistance to be granted to employees made redundant as a result of major changes in international trade, such as globalisation or the global economic crisis. this support from the union is essential and is in addition to the measures already taken by the french state to facilitate the reintegration of dismissed persons into the labour market. the funds will enable them to receive personalised and regular support in building their new career path, advice or various types of training to maximise their chances of returning to a sustainable job. it is now up to the council to approve the french authorities' request so that the €6 million in aid can be put into effect and benefit french workers.
in writing. ‒ our delegation almost always votes on requests to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund, because it is a programme to support employees in companies that are sometimes forced to lay off workers under the pressure of market deregulation, the consequences of the disastrous ultra-liberal policies applied within this european union that is unable to defend the people who make it up or the companies that make it live.
in writing. ‒ this draft council decision aims to establish the social protection committee. the committee has an advisory role and is responsible for advising the ministers for employment and social protection on the objectives of the european semester. it is intended to monitor the social situation in the european union and to strengthen cooperation between member states in the field of social protection. as with the employment committee, the council does not need the opinion of the european parliament to adopt this draft. in addition, the committee has a thematic and multilateral monitoring role for reforms undertaken by the countries of the union. the countries must submit national reports to the commission, which then examines them. once again, therefore, we are dealing with the establishment of yet another committee which interferes in the affairs of the member states of the union. i therefore voted against.

in writing. ‒ this regulation amendment provides for the transfer of unused commitment appropriations in 2014. over 300 programmes, or 47% of all operational programmes, are covered by these appropriations. in addition, the regulation makes €172 million available to the asylum, migration and integration fund, which promotes legal immigration within the european union. this change is likely to exacerbate the problems of late payment. but we still have 24 billion unpaid bills (11 billion in 2011). however, this amendment is purely technical and i therefore abstained.
in writing. ‒ the aim is to carry over to 2015 21 billion of appropriations not used in 2014 due to the late adoption of regulations and programmes for certain european funds. i am pleased to see that the european agricultural fund for rural development (eafrd) and fisheries are included in the budget lines. however, the recommendation also provides for €172 million to be made available for the asylum, migration and integration fund, which, as its name suggests, aims to facilitate legal immigration. this recommendation by the european parliament is completely out of touch with reality: in a damning 113-page report published in february 2015, french experts from the court of auditors estimate the cost of asylum at more than €2 billion per year for our national community alone. the cost of those who arrive is added to that of those who do not leave: only 1% of the unemployed actually leave french territory. i therefore could not vote in favour of this recommendation.
in writing. ‒ the revision of the multiannual financial framework aims to transfer to subsequent years €21 billion in commitment appropriations not used in 2014, equivalent to 15% of the 2014 budget! if this is a purely technical revision, however, it should be noted that €172 million will be made available to the asylum, migration and integration fund and to promote legal immigration to the eu, a highly controversial policy. it also reveals serious and even scandalous elements such as the stock of unpaid debts which grows year by year, thus showing a totally sclerotic management. the amount reached 24.7 billion in 2014 compared to 11 billion in 2011. and we're still waiting for a plan to clear it. in the meantime, the costs are borne by the local authorities. this absurd system justifies for some a new federal leap which is nothing but a leap into the void and would be an intolerable attack on the sovereignty of the states. the only answer to this appalling management is to leave the member states full sovereignty over their budgets and the allocation of investments. i therefore abstained, taking into account the purely technical aspect of the text.

in writing. ‒ this proposal for a council decision authorises member states to become parties to the international maritime organisation's international convention on standards for the training, licensing and watchkeeping of personnel on fishing vessels. competence in fisheries is normally vested in the union under the treaties, but only member states can ratify this convention. it provides that minimum qualifications will be required for seafarers and standards of vocational training. it thus contributes to the harmonisation of equal treatment of workers. in addition, there will be no increase in training costs for member states, as the union already funds training in the fisheries sector, through the european maritime and fisheries fund. i therefore voted in favour of the text.
in writing. ‒ i supported the recommendation to allow member states to become parties, in the interest of the european union, to the international maritime organisation convention on standards for the training, certification and watchkeeping of personnel on fishing vessels. the aim of the convention is to ensure that seafarers are qualified by promoting vocational training and to contribute to the reduction of risks to the safety and health of seafarers and all personnel on fishing vessels. its scope covers vessels of 24 metres in length or more and of 750 kw or more power. the convention encourages member states to apply these safety and qualification standards to ships of the same size but of lower power. i voted for this recommendation because it is important to ensure a minimum level of training in the fisheries sector and to guarantee working conditions and safety on board to prevent accidents at work. by adopting this recommendation, the union thus authorises the member states to ratify the convention.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which, in accordance with the council's recommendations, aims to authorise all member states to ratify the international convention on the training of personnel on fishing vessels of the imo (international maritime organisation), adopted by the ilo (international labour organisation) in july 1995. the report stresses that european directives take precedence in the event of intra-community disputes, but ratification of the convention by all member states will guarantee a minimum level of qualification for seafarers and standards of vocational training that will help to reduce risks.
in writing. this report concerns the council's proposal to authorise the member states of the union to become parties to the international maritime organisation's international convention on standards for the training, certification and watchkeeping of personnel on fishing vessels. at present, only four eu member states have ratified the convention. it aims in particular to reduce the risks to the safety of fishing vessel personnel by requiring them to hold a certificate attesting to their qualifications and medical fitness. the union does not have the right to sign this convention, as only the member states have the right to do so. however, the case law of the court of justice requires an authorisation from the union to allow member states to ratify the convention, since fisheries are among the exclusive competences of the union. in the field of fisheries, the member states are thus placed under the union's supervision, but the aim of this report, namely the accession of the member states of the union to this convention, can be welcomed. that is why i voted for it.

in writing. this vote concerns the draft amending budget following the adoption of the amendment to regulation (eu, euratom) no 1311/2013 to allow the carry-over of unused commitment appropriations in 2014 (eur 21 billion, or 15% of the 2014 budget) to subsequent years, in accordance with article 19 of the multiannual financial framework. the legal acts laying down the rules for the implementation of the funds were adopted later than planned, which in fact delayed the conclusion of the agreement on the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020. these year-to-year carryovers feed into the stock of unpaid invoices (which amounted to around eur 24 billion at the end of 2014, despite the eur 4.8 billion obtained in the trilogue at the end of 2014). we are told that this is a matter of technical adjustments, but in the end it is the local authorities who are paying for these delays and arrears. however, in line with the obrycht/thomas report, i have decided to abstain on this draft amending budget.

in writing. ‒ the purpose of this proposal for a regulation is to introduce an obligation for car manufacturers to install an ecall in-vehicle system in certain types of motor vehicles. the device would ensure that emergency calls are handled properly by the emergency services and that a gps signal is sent to enable rescuers to easily locate the accidented vehicle. the expected benefits are a reduction in the number of fatalities and the severity of injuries suffered by road users, as well as a reduction in congestion-related costs. however, this system seems questionable as regards the protection of users' privacy. we cannot guarantee that these provisions have no other purpose than the safety of users. it is likely to increase the price of cars. although an amendment provides that users can disconnect this geo-location system fairly easily, it would be more appropriate if users could only activate this system voluntarily if they so wished. these uncertainties about privacy and consumer spending power, as well as the impact assessment, will lead me to vote against this proposal for a regulation. however, i voted in favour of the amendment which aims to make it easy for users to disconnect the ecall system manually.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it provides for greater safety and access to care following a road accident. every second counts when it comes to medical care.
in writing. ‒ the aim of this text is to oblige car manufacturers to install the ecall system on a general basis. the european commission's initiative, this automatic emergency call system is supposed to allow an accident-prone vehicle to call emergency services instantly while sending its precise location, whether its occupants are conscious or not, and regardless of the eu country in which the vehicle is located. based on the 'e112' (enhanced 112), the single european emergency number 112, ecall would allow for faster intervention by the emergency services, adapted to the severity of the accident and the type of vehicle involved. the vote was only on an amendment to allow users to easily disconnect the ecall system and i therefore voted in favour. however, i remain perplexed as to the relevance of the introduction of this system: the impact analysis seemed to me very unsatisfactory and therefore cannot be used to promote this dubious 'technological development'. apart from the impact on the production cost and thus on the selling price of the vehicle, how can we be sure that this data will not be used for purposes other than emergency services?
in writing. the aim of this recommendation is to introduce an obligation for car manufacturers to install the ecall in-vehicle system in certain types of motor vehicles. the proposal for a basic regulation requires that new types of passenger cars and light commercial vehicles be built in such a way as to ensure that an emergency call to the number 112 is automatically triggered and a gps signal is sent to enable rescuers to easily locate the accidented vehicle, as from 1 october 2015. it also provides for rules on data protection and privacy, taking into account the nature of the information transmitted by this service. i oppose this recommendation because, under the guise of protecting citizens and improving road safety and prevention, two problems arise: what assurance is given to ensure that the data will not be used for purposes other than rescue and that there is no risk of invasion of citizens' privacy? secondly, how much will the cost of manufacturing the vehicles increase and what additional costs will the consumer have to bear? in view of these factors, i have decided against this text.
in writing. on 19 march, the committee on the internal market and consumer protection approved the council's position without amending it. the commission's recommendation requires that new commercial and passenger vehicles be equipped with a system allowing a call to the european emergency number, 112, in the event of a serious accident. the objectives pursued are praiseworthy but the proportionality of the proposed means with the stated objectives is questionable. this type of equipment raises questions about the protection of personal data. in addition, this system is not new, with manufacturers offering it on some models. this compulsory system will have a cost which will ultimately be borne by the consumer. i regret the shortcomings of the impact assessment. i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament's proposal for a regulation aims to introduce an obligation for car manufacturers to have an on-board ecall system that allows emergency calls to be handled properly by the emergency services. vehicles will have to be built in such a way that they guarantee the automatic triggering of an emergency call to the number 112 as well as the sending of a gps signal to allow rapid location. these provisions raise questions about privacy and the use of geo-location data for purposes other than rescue. furthermore, the impact assessment does not suggest that the benefits will outweigh the financial costs of such a device and the risks it poses to the user's right to privacy. we may even question whether the stated intention is the real objective to be achieved. that is why i voted against this proposal for a regulation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the introduction of the ecall deployment regulation. this mechanism provides that in the event of an accident the ecall system will automatically trigger the emergency number 112. by october 2015, all new passenger cars and light commercial vehicles will have to be equipped with ecall. drivers and passengers will now be assured that emergency services will be on hand in case of an accident. this is a major step forward in road safety.
in writing. ‒ i opposed this text which, under the praiseworthy pretext of strengthening road safety, presents risks in terms of protecting the privacy of our citizens. the text provides for the geolocation of crashed vehicles by the ecall system. however, there is no guarantee that these data cannot be used for other purposes. the system will also have a direct impact on the cost of car production, as it will require the installation of ecall in new types of passenger cars and light commercial vehicles. the consequence will therefore be a further decline in the purchasing power of the citizens of the eu member states. the european union, which is so committed to freedom of movement, is therefore proposing a measure here which restricts the freedom of citizens through the security issue.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the commission has again tried to adopt technocratic directives, motivated solely by ideology. because of the biofuel crops in southeast asia, which lead to deforestation and pollution, our good environmental friends wanted to stop all biofuel crops in europe. but what neither ngos nor environmentalists have understood is that europe does not need to destroy its forests to cultivate land. fortunately, the member states have once again proved that they alone are capable of defending the interests of their citizens. in the council of the european union they succeeded in forcing the rapporteur on this project and the commission to reduce their ambitions. the compromise reached will enable us to save the funds already invested in the first generation biofuels industry and thus save tens of thousands of jobs. by preserving first generation biofuel crops, we will be able to preserve the know-how that will facilitate the transition to advanced biofuels.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this revision of the fuel quality and renewable energy directives because it does not aim to maintain the existing agrofuels industry by encouraging technological innovation. the proposed amendments to the legal framework for biofuels respond to the commission's concern to increase the share of next generation (advanced) biofuels. the aim is to limit the use of agricultural land for the production of biofuels and to reduce the use of agricultural products by encouraging the use of waste. the commission's objective was to reduce the share of first generation biofuels to 5% of all fuel used in europe. the agreement finally sets this proportion at 7%, which covers the considerable investments made in europe over the last few years. the compromise text covers industries which are currently operating on the model before the revision of the fuel quality directive. the model now favoured, however, is to avoid the use of agricultural land in favour of more innovative technologies.
in writing. ‒ there was no final vote on this text presented at second reading. i therefore voted only in favour of the amendments to protect the investments already made by the agrofuels sector. it would be wrong to give up first-generation biofuels abruptly. many studies, including the ecofys report published on 12 november, challenge the method of calculating indirect changes in soil conditions, which was used by the commission to abruptly amend its 1998 and 2008 directives. if research into advanced biofuels is to continue, it is necessary to take account of the considerable investments already made. i am thinking in particular of our farmers who have relied on these future energies to overcome the serious crisis in their sector. the second generation of biofuels does not yet seem to be able to take over from the first. the 7% ceiling proposed by the council and finally approved by parliament therefore seems to me to be more reasonable because it is more respectful of investments which have been made in the long term, for the long term.
in writing. this recommendation for a compromise between parliament and the council aims to amend the positive law on biofuels in the context of the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions. for years, in order to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from transport, the eu has encouraged the production of biofuels from food crops. unfortunately, this policy has not reduced co2 emissions. the eu is therefore trying to revitalise itself by promoting the production of biofuels from non-food sources. it's about time! the commission was considering setting a 5% ceiling for the share of fuel produced from food grains. the council decided on 7%. the compromise emphasises reducing the use of agricultural land in biofuel production in favour of investment in research into more advanced renewable fuels. this compromise is a good compromise and i have decided to vote in favour of it.
in writing. the european union is promoting biofuels, including next generation . it presents this initiative as the main solution to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. however, many have criticised the current policy, including the european parliament. the commission presented a legislative initiative in october 2012. the second reading in the european parliament produced a compromise, which is the subject of this text. i voted against this one. indeed, if i am sensitive to environmental issues, they must be tackled effectively, putting aside the ideological presuppositions of the dangerous 'green ayatollahs'.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament's draft resolution deals with the adoption of the directives on fuel quality and renewable energies. the original aim of the text was to limit the use of agricultural land for the production of biofuels and to support new types of fuel derived from the use of waste such as biomass. the target of reducing the share of biofuels to 5% of the total share of fuels has been reduced to 7%, preserving the considerable investments made in europe by companies in the sector. in order not to destabilise the biofuels sector, i voted in favour of this text, which is the result of a compromise between the european parliament and the council.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the fuel quality and renewable energy directives. in this text we are adapting these two directives to the new environmental characteristics of biofuel production. we did not want to jeopardise the investments already made in the first generations of biofuels. nevertheless, legislation encourages producers and investors to switch to a more environmentally friendly generation of biofuels. i am also sensitive to the effects of indirect land use change. however, the method of calculating these effects is disputed, so i think it is premature to include it in the legislation at this stage.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text as it is the result of a compromise between parliament and the council on the revision of the european policy on biofuels. i am in favour of sustainable development as long as it is done in accordance with the principle of freedom, and i can only welcome this text which promotes biofuels with a view to reducing greenhouse gases. the directive also advocates a reduction in the use of agricultural land for the manufacture of biofuels and the use of more innovative and farm-friendly technologies.
in writing. ‒ this text aims to define the eu's biofuels strategy, and in particular to encourage operators to use so-called 'advanced' biofuels, which i support. the european commission's initial proposal was too broadly based on taking into account indirect land use changes from biofuels. this factor has not yet been scientifically proven and its estimation is still too risky to be included in this directive. that is why i voted in favour of the text agreed by the legislators, whose moderate approach to the casi/iluc factors seems to me justified at the moment.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because if we want to achieve the environmental objectives set for 2020, we must not be without ambition in the transport sector. like the rapporteur, i hope that we can encourage the penetration of advanced biofuels into the fuel market as much as possible. the european union must have an incentive effect on this sector in order to attract investment in return. in my view, innovation in renewable energy and clean fuels will both guarantee a greener european union than its global competitors and create jobs in a sector of the future.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which raises a fundamental issue for all those involved in biofuels. throughout the negotiations - with my colleagues from the epp group - we have defended a balanced position. our role as meps is not to change direction along the way - as some would like to do - but rather to accompany and encourage a change of direction in order to meet environmental needs but also not to divert the citizens of the european union. i regret, however, that we have not been able to pursue the logic of encouraging the next generation of biofuels without setting a binding target at european level. i am glad, however, that agreement has been reached on the iluc factor. the calculation of this factor on the accounting for effects linked to indirect changes in land use is scientifically disputed and it would have been absurd to incorporate it into the directive as such. the analysis of this factor must be continued, as indicated in the text voted.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this revision of the fuel quality and renewable energy directives because it does not aim to maintain the existing agrofuels industry by encouraging technological innovation. the proposed amendments to the legal framework for biofuels respond to the commission's concern to increase the share of next generation (advanced) biofuels. the aim is to limit the use of agricultural land for the production of biofuels and to reduce the use of agricultural products by encouraging the use of waste. the commission's objective was to reduce the share of first generation biofuels to 5% of all fuel used in europe. the agreement finally sets this proportion at 7%, which covers the considerable investments made in europe over the last few years. the compromise text covers industries which are currently operating on the model before the revision of the fuel quality directive. the model now favoured, however, is to avoid the use of agricultural land in favour of more innovative technologies.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe it strikes a balance between the need to introduce a significant amount of biofuels into energy consumption and the need to reject an absolutist view on this point, which aims to preserve agricultural land from biofuels altogether.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this project which aims to reduce first generation biofuels (produced from crops on agricultural land). the main reason given is that this activity would result in significant deforestation and pollution. this is true in south-east asia but not in europe where existing agricultural land is used. in the end, a compromise was reached: first generation biofuels should not exceed 7% of final energy consumption in transport by 2020. they will then be gradually replaced by other, more environmentally sound biofuels.

in writing. ‒ directive 2009/28/ec on the promotion of the use of energy from renewable sources requires a 10% share of energy from renewable sources in transport by 2020. the aim of the commission's proposal is to initiate the transition to a biofuel policy which will reduce greenhouse gas emissions significantly. we know the disadvantages of this alternative to food production. the report therefore aims to limit the use of conventional biofuels, i.e. agrofuels which compete with agricultural products for food, to 6% of total energy consumption in transport. the report also introduces a target of 1.25% for so-called 'advanced' biofuels, such as those produced from algae. the text also proposes that the impact of land use change be taken into account in the overall co2 production balance generated by this new use. i therefore support the progress made in this text, despite its shortcomings, and i vote in favour of it.

in writing. the european parliament is to vote on a recommendation for a compromise between parliament and the council to amend the positive law on biofuels in the context of reducing greenhouse gas emissions. the eu has for years been pushing for the production of biofuels from food crops in an effort to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from transport. but this policy has had a negative effect and has not reduced co2 emissions. the eu is therefore trying to re-evaluate itself by promoting the production of biofuels from non-food sources. the commission was considering setting a 5% ceiling for the share of fuel derived from food grains. finally, the council has set a rate of 7%, which covers the massive investments made in the european union. the compromise emphasises reducing the use of agricultural land in biofuel production in favour of investment in research into more advanced renewable fuels. i think that this is a compromise in the right direction and i have decided to vote in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this agreement on the proposal for a directive on indirect land use change (casi). the agreement aims to encourage the production of next-generation biofuels, which require less agricultural land for their production. the epp group to which i belong fought and won the case for this agreement not to affect the investments made and the jobs created by the production of first generation biofuels.
in writing. ‒ the proposed amendments to the legal framework promoting biofuels in greenhouse gas emission reduction targets respond to the commission's concern to increase the share of next generation (advanced) biofuels. the aim is to limit the use of agricultural land for the production of biofuels and to reduce the use of agricultural products by encouraging the use of waste. the commission's objective was to reduce the share of first generation biofuels to 5% of all fuel used in europe. the agreement finally sets this proportion at 7%, which covers the considerable investments made in europe over the last few years. the compromise text covers industries which are currently operating on the model before the revision of the fuel quality directive. the model now favoured, however, is to avoid the use of agricultural land in favour of more innovative technologies. i think this compromise is well balanced and i therefore vote in favour of the text.
in writing. ‒ energy and climate issues are now at the heart of the union's priorities. the use of biofuels had emerged as a solution for europe's energy supply. however, some agrofuels have been shown to have a harmful effect on the environment. the european parliament voted in favour of the directive on tuesday, which combines and amends two existing directives on fuel quality and renewable energy. i voted in favour of this conciliatory text. the share of biofuels for transport will not exceed 7%. the aim of this directive is not to call into question the investments already made in biofuel research and production, while encouraging the development of a more environmentally friendly generation of biofuels.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament today delivered its opinion on the agreement reached with the council on the revision of the fuel quality directive, which is intended to cap the share of 'first generation biofuels' in final energy consumption in the transport sector. these biofuels, derived from food products, have negative effects both on the environment (intensive agricultural production, water pollution by pesticides and fertilizers, massive deforestation, reduction of biodiversity, etc.) and on the socio-economic level (competition for food crops, increase in food prices, impact on local populations, etc.). for all these reasons, it is essential that the european union should set a ceiling on these biofuels. the agreement reached with the council does not go far enough to limit the negative consequences of these biofuels. i therefore decided to abstain on this agreement, because it proposes a 7% ceiling for first generation biofuels (the european socialists proposed 5%). the text also fails to take up parliament's objective of setting the share of second generation biofuels, made from waste and non-edible plants, which are a viable biofuel solution, at 2.5%.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text, which is the real culmination of the negotiations on this complex issue. although it endorsed many compromises with respect to parliament's first reading position, there was an urgent need for a text on the issue of indirect land-use change (ilc), which causes famine and deforestation in developing countries and runs counter to the eu's greenhouse gas emission reduction targets. we approve the cap on the production of first generation biofuels and welcome the inclusion of provisions to encourage the development of advanced biofuels.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report which reflects the position of our group. we have, throughout this dossier, maintained a balanced position by not calling into question the investments already made in the sector but by encouraging the development of a new generation of biofuels which are safer for the environment. we also refused to include in this directive a method of calculating the effects of indirect land use change (casi effect), which is scientifically disputed, but we are in favour of further studies in this area. among the important points of the agreement, it is also noted that first generation biofuels should not represent more than 7% of final energy consumption in transport by 2020; this is a very important point, and it is not a question of putting into question the investments already made.
in writing. ‒ based on the finding of the poor 'climate' balance of agrofuels, this revision has the stated objective of reducing greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions by incorporating the effects of the increasing use of agricultural land for the production of agrofuels called 'indirect land use change criterion' (casi iluc). the amendment also proposed lowering the share of agrofuels in fossil fuels from 10% to 6% (supported by the ep), compared with 5% in the commission's initial proposal. but in reality the 'casi criterion' is not taken into account in the calculation of the 'climate quality' of agrofuels and will only be the subject of a commission report based on the information provided by the producers. that's what i'm talking about! voted by a large majority in the european parliament, this revised legislation is not up to the climate challenges, the member states, including france, bearing a large responsibility in this bad compromise! i therefore voted against this text, in order not to join the eu in sending the wrong signal a few months before the paris climate change conference.

in writing. this recommendation concerns the reduction of the use of lightweight plastic carrier bags in the union. the text requires member states either to ban the free supply of plastic bags in shops by the end of 2018 or to set a ceiling on the average consumption of disputed bags per inhabitant (90 bags per person per year by 2019 and 40 by 2025). in addition, the member states will also be required to establish appropriate labelling to indicate that the bags are biodegradable, and they will have a multitude of sanctions, such as taxes, to enforce this requirement. while the intention to reduce the environmental problem of bags is initially laudable, the measures envisaged may lead to negative consequences by encouraging the production of water-intensive paper bags or vacuum over-packaging. it will not reduce plastic production in any way... this text is indicative of the attitude which denies the sovereignty of the member states. i therefore abstained on that recommendation.
in writing. the aim of the text is to encourage the reduction of the use of plastic bags. the fact is that while these are used by the final consumer for only a few minutes, the damage to the environment is disastrous. 99 billion plastic bags are used every year in the european union. the text was adopted by the council on 2 march 2015 and an agreement was reached to ask member states to reduce the number of bags used and/or to ensure that they are no longer provided free of charge to consumers after december 2018. i voted against this text because the policy of the european union is not in line with the objectives, which are laudable. it does not take a global view of the problem and treats lightly, from an economic point of view, the fate of nearly 20 000 workers in the sector.

in writing. ‒ in the face of growing concerns about global warming and the depletion of the ozone layer, the union is trying to legislate more to encourage member states to limit and reduce their production of environmentally harmful gases. on tuesday, the european parliament adopted the regulation on the monitoring, reporting and verification of carbon dioxide emissions from the shipping sector, amending the current directive 2009/16/ec. this proposal, which i supported, aims to control emissions of this gas more closely, while taking account of the realities and constraints of this economic sector. small vessels, which account for 40% of the sector but less than 10% of emissions, are excluded from this agreement. in addition, actions entailing additional administrative burdens, such as mandatory reporting, were not included.

in writing. the aim of this text is to adopt reliable statistics and harmonised definitions at european level. it is intended, for comparative purposes, to address statistical gaps and the heterogeneity of definitions in the member states and to guarantee the independence of the national statistical institutes in order to avoid known statistical manipulations. the text also makes it possible to increase the accessibility of data in the interests of transparency. nevertheless, while it may be in the right direction, some measures seem to me to be abnormal, such as the possibility of inspections in the member states by european officials and the possibility of fines in the event of incorrect statistics. this desire for transparency must not be at the expense of the sovereignty of the nations. finally, this text on statistics does not propose new statistical models of harmonization as for gdp or the calculation of "well-being". bhutan invented the "gross national happiness" (gnp), why not also look (apart from the above anecdote) at a modernized indicator? so, following his remarks, i decided to abstain on that point.

in writing. the aim of the text put to the vote is to adopt reliable statistics and harmonised definitions at european level. it aims to remedy the statistical gaps and the heterogeneity of their definitions in the member states, for comparative purposes, and to guarantee the independence of the national statistical institutes in order to avoid the statistical manipulations known, for example, in greece. it is also a question of increasing the accessibility of data, in the interests of transparency. nevertheless, while this approach may be a step in the right direction, some measures are close to unjustified interference, such as the possibility given to european officials to carry out inspections in the member states, with the possibility of fines in the event of erroneous statistics. while the objective of reducing the manipulation of statistics is a good one, it must not be at the expense of the sovereignty of the member states. nor does it question the relevance of statistical indicators such as gdp, which are widely criticised in academic literature. nor is there any discussion of a more relevant indicator of 'well-being'. it is a global reflection that must be carried out, not a reform with constant definitions. so i decided to abstain.
