in writing. ‒ this legislative proposal proposes to establish a framework for the management of cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea, i.e. to implement a policy for the recovery and maintenance of the species, setting an optimum catch volume that can be taken each year without threatening the reproduction of the species. i welcome the adoption of the amendment calling for the targets to be met by 2015 and at the latest by 2020. however, more needs to be done and global action is needed to maintain the balance of the ecosystem. i therefore regret that the amendments proposed by my group concerning both by-catches and the possible effects of overfishing on other species (birds, marine mammals, etc.) have been rejected. the opposition between the interests of fishermen and the ecosystem is artificial and fruitless. the interests of fishermen lie in the protection of marine resources and the ecosystem and therefore require responsible fishing that respects the rights of fishermen and takes account in particular of smallholders. the rapporteur has asked for the text to be referred back to committee to take account of the most recent scientific advice, and i support that.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this proposal for a regulation is to introduce a landing obligation from 1 january 2015 in order to eliminate discards of fish. although this is an important measure, the proposed regulation is still vague as to the fate of those who have landed. it also imposes heavy material and financial constraints on fishermen. this will require many extra trips, but it will not be possible to use these fish discharges for human food. moreover, since landed catches are counted against quotas and unintended catches to be landed have to be physically separated from other catches, this would consequently increase the working time and the cost of fishermen's work. the proposal for a regulation would, in particular, classify any breach of the obligation as a serious infringement. because of the increased weight of vessels, these measures pose a risk to fishermen in case of rough seas. small-scale fishing is likely to collapse under the weight of these constraints. it would therefore appear that, although the intention of this proposal for a regulation is legitimate, the measures envisaged are far too restrictive and difficult for fishermen to implement. i therefore voted against the text.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this text, which only proposes to amend the landing obligation and not to abolish it, which i consider necessary because it places too heavy a burden on fishermen, especially small-scale fishermen.
in writing. ‒ this cadec report on the landing obligation proposes to phase out discards by introducing a landing obligation on 1 january 2015 with a very limited tolerance still being granted to fishermen in the years to come. the proposal does not specify the fate of the fish landed, although the desire to reduce the number of fish discarded is welcome. the proposal also places heavy financial (landed catches) and material constraints on fishermen (e.g. unintended catches to be landed must be physically separated from other catches). finally, it puts fishermen at risk by increasing the weight of vessels, which can be dangerous in rough seas. the priority should be to improve the selectivity of fishing methods and gear and i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. the common fisheries policy introduced fundamental changes to the rules in force until now in 2013, with an obligation to land catches. the committee on fisheries considered that the changes introduced by the european commission's draft regulation, known as the 'omnibus', should be strictly limited. the obligations impose heavy constraints on fishermen, in particular financial and material constraints. in addition, there is a parallel market inherent in this landing obligation. i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a regulation aims to phase out discards by introducing a landing obligation from 1 january 2015. the aim of reducing fish discards, although laudable, should not be used as a pretext for adopting an incomplete regulation, particularly on the fate of waste landed by fishermen. the proposal for a regulation also places new constraints on fishermen: financial constraints, since landed catches will be charged against quotas; and material constraints, since landed catches will have to be physically separated from the catches that can be consumed. rather than considering exclusively binding legislation, it would have been better to support the improvement of fishing techniques. as such, the renewal of equipment, made necessary by these new regulations, should be covered by the emff. i voted against this text in support of the fishermen.
in writing. ‒ the implementation of the landing obligation follows the adoption of the reform of the common fisheries policy which entered into force on 1 january 2015. this landing obligation shall be phased in in accordance with the timetable laid down in article 15 of the basic regulation of the common fisheries policy. the landing obligation is a generous measure, but it is very difficult to implement, especially for semi-coastal and small-scale fisheries. it is therefore necessary to make fishing gear more selective. the annual reports on the implementation of the landing obligation will make it possible to analyse the impact of this measure and the difficulties faced by the operators. the non-compliance with the landing obligation will become a serious offence as from 1 january 2017.
in writing. ‒ i preferred to vote against this proposal for a regulation which, while pursuing a laudable objective, offers bad solutions to the problem of excessive discards of fish. in addition to the shortcomings of this proposal for a regulation, which does not specify the fate of the fish landed, i believe that it presents solutions which are far too restrictive for fishermen. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the fishing opportunities for the stocks concerned are not exceeded. another unjustified financial constraint is that fishermen will have to make extra trips to land, which means more fuel used, longer working hours and, ultimately, more work. in addition to these obligations, the landing solution is not without risks for the fisherman since it will necessarily lead to an increase in the weight of the vessels, which can be dangerous in case of rough seas.
in writing. ‒ this report is one of the last milestones in the implementation of the reform of the common fisheries policy, as voted in the previous parliament. the purpose of this text is to introduce progressively from 1 january 2015 to 1 january 2019 the obligation to land or the prohibition to discard all catches. the commission has also adopted a proposal for a regulation on the conservation of fishery resources in the baltic sea. the proposal is intended to improve the management of the marine environment and to improve the quality of fisheries resources. considering that this text respects the political agreement reached when the reform of the common fisheries policy was voted, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the landing obligation under the new common fisheries policy aims to avoid the large discard of catch left for dead, which undermines the viability of stocks. mandatory landing will also allow for better monitoring of the actual quantity of catches in fishing areas. like the rapporteur, i support the idea of an omnibus regulation applying only to the fishing areas affected by the landing obligation in 2015 and not for the following years, in order to remain consistent with the whole of the legislation on this subject. finally, while i support compulsory landing, i am mindful that it must be accompanied by measures to find outlets for non-marketable catches, to avoid waste, and to control those outlets.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this proposal for a regulation is to introduce a landing obligation from 1 january 2015 in order to eliminate discards of fish. although this is an important measure, the proposed regulation is still vague as to the fate of those who have landed. it also imposes heavy material and financial constraints on fishermen. this will require many extra trips, but it will not be possible to use these fish discharges for human food. moreover, since landed catches are counted against quotas and unintended catches to be landed have to be physically separated from other catches, this would consequently increase the working time and the cost of fishermen's work. the proposal for a regulation would, in particular, classify any breach of the obligation as a serious infringement. because of the increased weight of vessels, these measures pose a risk to fishermen in case of rough seas. small-scale fishing is likely to collapse under the weight of these constraints. it would therefore appear that, although the intention of this proposal for a regulation is legitimate, the measures envisaged are far too restrictive and difficult for fishermen to implement. i therefore voted against the text.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this text which does not sufficiently protect the fisheries sector, which can put fishermen at risk, because this report exposes fishermen to a risk: that of increasing the weight of vessels. this is a dangerous factor in case of rough seas. it also weakens the already highly stressed small-scale fisheries.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this proposal for a regulation is to introduce a landing obligation from 1 january 2015 in order to eliminate discards of fish. although this is an important measure, the proposed regulation is still vague as to the fate of those who have landed. it also imposes heavy material and financial constraints on fishermen. this will require many extra trips, but it will not be possible to use these fish discharges for human food. moreover, since landed catches are counted against quotas and unintended catches to be landed have to be physically separated from other catches, this would consequently increase the working time and the cost of fishermen's work. the proposal for a regulation would, in particular, classify any breach of the obligation as a serious infringement. because of the increased weight of vessels, these measures pose a risk to fishermen in case of rough seas. small-scale fishing is likely to collapse under the weight of these constraints. it would therefore appear that, although the intention of this proposal for a regulation is legitimate, the measures envisaged are far too restrictive and difficult for fishermen to implement. i therefore voted against the text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, mr alain cadec, on the implementation of the landing obligation. the landing obligation is a welcome measure aimed at improving resource conservation, but its implementation remains complicated. i therefore welcome the introduction of provisions which will make it possible to assess the real economic and social impact of the implementation of this measure.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the landing obligation. article 15 of the common fisheries policy regulation imposes an obligation to land all catches. this obligation will be phased in between 2015 and 2019. as a result, fishermen will have to land all unmarketable bycatches. as the landing obligation is a fundamental change for fisheries, the report stressed that 2015 would be a test year for its implementation.
in writing. ‒ the report aims to give additional time to the introduction of the new obligation for fishermen to land all the fish they catch. previously, fishermen simply landed the fish for resale, discarding those that did not fit the size or species criteria. these releases were causing a considerable waste of the resource at a time when the signs of its sustainability are becoming more alarming. i therefore supported the end of these practices in a previous vote, while at the same time wishing for greater flexibility for sinners. small-scale fisheries must be given time to implement this necessary reform, but without jeopardizing an already delicate financial balance. by allowing for a gradual adaptation to the obligation to stop discharges by 2019, this report meets these two imperatives: the preservation of resources and the maintenance of activity in often peripheral areas. on the other hand, concessions to fishermen must not allow them to abuse them and thus nullify the effects of this regulation, which is why i abstained.
in writing. ‒ this report obliges fishing vessels to stop unintentionally discarding fish caught in trawls and to keep them with the obligation to land them. there is a risk that species may be caught when they are protected, or that the fish caught are too young. until now, these fish were thrown into the sea. although this measure appears to be a measure of good sense, parliament's decision raises a number of problems: these catches will reduce the fishing quotas authorized, force fishermen to make more trips and therefore increase their costs (fuel, crew salaries, etc.), and make adjustments to the vessels since incidental fisheries will have to be separated from the others. it would have been desirable for the same purpose if parliament had been more concerned with the possibility for fishermen to equip themselves to improve selectivity (filets calibrated according to the targeted fish). it's not. it is important, however, that this new obligation be accompanied by financing which is not provided for. for all these reasons, i am voting against the parliament's proposal.
in writing. - i voted against this bill. while it is commendable to want to phase out discards, this will place heavy constraints on fishermen: catches will be charged against quotas, fishermen will be forced to make additional trips to land and unintended catches to be landed will be separated physically, which will be a financial and material loss. i could only vote against such a project.
in writing. ‒ one of the main objectives of the current reform of the common fisheries policy (cfp) is to phase out discards in all fisheries in the european union (eu) by introducing a landing obligation. i voted for the cfp when it was adopted with two reservations, one concerning the necessary modernisation of the fleet for obvious reasons of safety at sea and energy efficiency of vessels, the other concerning zero-emission, which i formulated as follows: [...] if the so-called 'zero-remove' measure is intended to increase the selectivity of fishing gear, it must not condemn the sector. its application will have to be conducted by fisheries, on a case-by-case basis, after feasibility and socioeconomic impact studies. the report proposes, without going back on the mechanism, a gradual and adapted implementation of the landing obligations, which i vote for.
in writing. ‒ priority should be given to improving the selectivity of fishing methods and gear rather than introducing an overly complex landing obligation. it should have been provided that the equipment renewal would be supported by the emff, since these new equipment are made necessary by european regulatory developments. a derogation or, at least, an extended transitional period should also be granted to small-scale fisheries to give them time to adapt. as it stands, the vote on this proposal for a regulation is therefore negative.
in writing. this report on the landing obligation aims to phase out discards by introducing a landing obligation from 1 january 2015. a low tolerance will be granted to fishermen in the coming years. the commitment to reduce the discarding of fish is commendable, but it is regrettable that there is no clarity on the fate of the fish landed. in addition, fishermen would also be subject to significant financial (landed catches) and material constraints (e.g. unintended catches to be landed must be physically separated from other catches). the overloading of vessels can also be a hazard to fishermen in rough seas. i therefore voted against this report, considering that more should be done to encourage the improvement of the selectivity of fishing methods and gear.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text on the obligation to land all fish caught. this obligation, which will come into force gradually between 2015 and 2019, is in contradiction with several european regulations which therefore needed to be amended.
in writing. the 2013 cfp reform introduces fundamental changes to the rules applicable to fisheries: in particular, an obligation to land all catches is imposed; this means that fishermen will have to land all unintended catches which are not marketable either because of the lack of a quota or because they are smaller than the minimum conservation reference size. the compromise reached strikes a good balance between the need to implement this landing obligation and the need to give fishermen some flexibility to implement this obligation. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ reducing fish discards is a laudable objective, but the proposed regulation, even if amended in the right way, is still far too restrictive for fishermen, who bear all the obligations and risks. thus, landed catches are charged against quotas and cannot be used for human consumption (hence a lower selling price); fishermen will have to make additional trips to land; any breach of the landing obligation will be classified as a serious infringement (points system). in addition, unintended catches to be landed must be physically separated from other catches and the increase in the weight of vessels is a hazardous factor in rough seas. i therefore oppose this text.
in writing. ‒ illegal fishing is now a major problem in the eu, threatening the survival of several marine species. the union must act to protect biodiversity and preserve these endangered species. in view of the urgency of the situation, parliament adopted the report on the implementation of the landing obligation by a very large majority. i am glad that i voted in favour of this key measure. however, while the proposed landing obligation will make it possible to contribute to the conservation of marine resources, it remains difficult to implement and monitor. therefore, parliament agreed to a gradual review, with a system of sanctions only applicable from 2017. the text also stresses the responsibility of member states to put in place adequate measures to manage landed catches which cannot be marketed.
in writing. ‒ this report obliges fishing vessels to stop unintentionally discarding fish caught in trawls and to keep them with the obligation to land them. there is a risk that species may be caught when they are protected, or that the fish caught are too young. until now, these fish were thrown into the sea. although this measure appears to be a measure of good sense, parliament's decision raises a number of problems: these catches will reduce the fishing quotas authorized, force fishermen to make more trips and therefore increase their costs (fuel, crew salaries, etc.), and make adjustments to the vessels since incidental fisheries will have to be separated from the others. it would have been desirable for the same purpose if parliament had been more concerned with the possibility for fishermen to equip themselves to improve selectivity (filets calibrated according to the targeted fish). it's not. it is important, however, that this new obligation be accompanied by financing, which is also not provided for. i therefore vote against the text.

in writing. this report on the implementation of the bologna process is far from the aspirations of the world of higher education and research, nor does it meet the expectations of young people in the various countries of the union who expect more jobs. the report aims to adapt the university system of the member states to globalisation, following the american model, instead of leaving it to university staff to train students to the best of their ability. we cannot, on the one hand, deplore the unprecedented rate of unemployment among young people, who are forced to resort to flexicurity measures to delay their entry into the labour market, and, on the other hand, impose austerity which creates economic depression. the union has therefore chosen to hide its face by increasingly promoting erasmus+ and thus creating a transnational and european elite. this is however ridiculous when we know that the union deprives swiss students of this provision as a result of the will of the swiss people, expressed by direct universal suffrage, to challenge the dogma of free movement with the countries of the union. this is the manifest hypocrisy which justifies my voting against this text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the monitoring of the implementation of the bologna process. this process, which started in 1999, aims to create a european higher education area, including better quality of teaching, greater mobility and mutual recognition of university degrees. since 1999, all 47 current members of the bologna process have implemented major reforms in their higher education systems. the report calls for an evaluation of the bologna process to give it a new lease of life, for example by further developing the mobility of university staff and teachers.
in writing. launched in 1999, the bologna process was intended to create the conditions for better mobility in education, greater competitiveness and adjustment to the labour market. this report, although it does have some positive points such as the demand for more investment in education and the objective of greater student mobility; the report also contains criticisms, such as the predominant role of business in education, the fact that studies should follow the interests of the markets, and the lack of solutions to the problem of inequalities in access to education. my group proposed a very comprehensive alternative resolution, but it was not adopted. for these reasons i abstained from voting.
in writing. ‒ the bologna process is a process of rapprochement of european higher education systems that began in 1998 and led to the creation in 2010 of the european higher education area, comprising some 50 states. it aims to make europe a competitive area in the global knowledge economy, the european area of higher education. since the lisbon convention the objectives of the programme have evolved. the first is to harmonise national systems by making a general division into 3 cycles and, since 2007, to introduce quality assurance in both institutions and training. the objectives of lifelong learning and mobility are constantly recalled. the bologna process aims at the commodification of higher education, a reduction in social justice, a loss of intellectual autonomy of institutions and a possible shortening of certain studies. the harmonization of european higher education goes hand in hand with its anglicisation. in my opinion, france must disengage from this process which, in the name of pseudo-advantages, will lead to an anglicisation, thus calling into question the equality of cultures and languages. i therefore vote against.
in writing. ‒ in the face of growing youth unemployment and the lack of opportunities faced by young graduates in the eu, it is important to rethink and reinvigorate european policies targeting young people, such as the bologna process on higher education in the eu. the european parliament adopted the report on the monitoring and implementation of the bologna process, stressing the importance of adapting and updating this measure in the light of the union's new context and challenges. i voted in favour of this text. while this process is successful in many respects, it needs to be revised and improved to better align it with the eu 2020 objectives and the new juncker commission.
in writing. ‒ the bologna process is a process of rapprochement of european higher education systems that began in 1998 and led to the creation in 2010 of the european higher education area, which comprises some 50 states. it aims to make europe a competitive area in the global knowledge economy, the european area of higher education. the objectives of lifelong learning and mobility are constantly recalled. france and the french are victims of this process which is making the anglicisation of higher education official. the european union recognises many obstacles to student mobility, technical obstacles but also language barriers. these barriers were never discussed in the evaluation reports, especially the language barrier. the bologna process aims at the commodification of higher education, a reduction in social justice, a loss of intellectual autonomy of institutions and a possible shortening of certain studies. higher education is seen through the lens of economic growth and its harmonization goes hand in hand with its anglicisation. in our opinion, france must withdraw from this process which calls into question the european spirit of equality of cultures and languages.

in writing. ‒ this report covers the evolution of cinema in the european union, focusing on the process of digitalisation of cinemas, the distribution, accessibility and visibility of films, funding and support programmes for the audiovisual sector (creative europe), the media and the means of promoting and distributing films produced in the european union (such as the lux prize). the inventory of practices and data on the european film industry in this report shows, for example, that in the eu 62.5% of cinema releases are european films and 19.8% american films. on the other hand, 32.9% of the cinema admissions were european films and 65.1% american films. in addition to its shortcomings, this report aims to promote a 'european cinema' by bypassing the tax problems posed by video-on-demand platforms (vàd or vsd in french, vod in english) for the member states, the most emblematic example of which is the american netflix: now having its european headquarters in the netherlands, it escapes the obligation to contribute to the financing of creation in france.

in writing. ‒ i support the kostinger report. in the absence of a common forestry policy, the forestry strategy allows for the coordination and coherence of european and national policies relating to forestry. through its guidelines and recommendations to member states, the strategy enables the sustainable exploitation and management of europe's forestry resources, which are often poorly and under-exploited and potentially rich in growth and jobs. it is an important lever for biodiversity and in the fight against global warming. i am glad to see one of my amendments in this report, calling on the commission to analyse the difficulties in supplying roundwood from the downstream sector and to help this sector. in recent years, exports of unprocessed bulk to certain third countries, such as china, for processing into furniture and then reselling in the european union have been a problem: in the absence of market regulation, many european primary processors have found themselves without supplies and faced higher prices for the raw material they need to run their businesses, putting them in difficulty, with the consequences that we know for employment in rural areas.
in writing. ‒ this text promotes a new strategy for forests. in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, it is not for the european union to legislate in this area, as the envi committee admitted in its opinion, although it asked the commission to 'take its lead in promoting a sustainable forestry policy'. the new strategy does not take into account concrete measures, since, although the "environmental value" is often emphasized, nothing is proposed in this area. the french wood sector is doing well, although it would benefit from better governance at national level: again, the community level is inadequate. protectionist measures would nevertheless be a means of protecting french and european timber, but of course the commission cannot envisage such a policy. i therefore voted against this text.

in writing. ‒ the resolution, which recalls the autonomy of the member states and their legitimacy in pursuing their forestry policy, states that the implementation of the eu's forestry policy should take several years and be coordinated, and that parliament's opinion should be taken into account. the report also places too much emphasis on the environmental value of the forest at the expense of its economic value, ignoring proposals to defend the sector, particularly the problem of exporting raw wood abroad and importing processed products with higher added value. this problem is particularly acute in lorraine. the report also makes no mention of any proposals for protectionism in the face of unfair competition from china in the sector. the ecological impact of these round trips should also be questioned since they are in contradiction with the environmental value and the desire to reduce greenhouse gases. i therefore voted against this report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the new eu forestry strategy. the strategy emphasises the key role of sustainable wood production and use in promoting sustainable business models and encouraging the creation of green jobs. the strategy will also emphasise the need for sustainable forest management. i welcome the adoption of this text.
in writing. - i vote against it. the report rightly emphasizes the economic importance of the forestry sector. but the commission is looking at this issue mainly from the environmental angle, which is important but will not solve the crisis in the sector. the french forestry sector, despite its economic weight, is suffering from a chronic deficit of eur 6 billion. this is mainly due to the fact that france sells its logs to countries such as china which transform them into furniture and france buys these finished products made with its own resources. this is a major shortfall for our industries, which are in particular in need of investment to modernise. no decision is taken by parliament to protect our market, which is the main problem. the european parliament, moreover, wants to increase its authority to the detriment of the member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this new strategy which will emphasise the role of the eu to the detriment of the member countries, which is a flagrant attack on the sovereignty of the states. moreover, this strategy does not take account of the trade problems associated with the abuses of certain third countries.
in writing. ‒ forests cover more than 40% of the eu's land area. the general situation is characterized by an increasing demand for timber and thus threats to forests. the new eu strategy for forests and the forest-based sector focuses on the bioeconomic aspects. and even though it has sustainable development objectives it allows for short-term exploitation of the forest via short-rotation forestry . moreover, the recommendation of forest management plans may remain wishful thinking because it will have to be done without creating unnecessary bureaucratic burden. in the face of such a narrow view of forestry issues that ignores the issues of biodiversity, the impact on agriculture and employment, i abstain.
in writing. ‒ this text promotes a new strategy for forests. first of all, because it is not for the european union to legislate on this matter, as the envi committee admitted in its opinion, although it asked the commission to 'take its leading role in promoting a sustainable forestry policy'. moreover, the new strategy makes little provision for concrete measures, since, although 'environmental value' is often emphasised, nothing is proposed in this area. in this case, the french wood sector is doing well, although it is benefiting from better governance at national level: once again, the european union seems to be inadequate. protectionist measures would nevertheless be a means of protecting french and european timber, but of course the commission cannot envisage such a policy. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ this report does not propose any concrete proposals to promote a form of protectionism, even european protectionism, to counter the aggressive policies of certain countries such as china. this is the central problem for the wood sector, particularly in france. as the numerous parliamentary reports on the subject have pointed out, the problem is due to the obsolescence of the sawmills but also to the fact that they export their logs and import, in particular from china, finished products (parquet floors, furniture, etc.). the vote is against, for these reasons among others.
in writing. the resolution aims to adopt a new strategy for forests. it is firstly recalled that this strategy remains at the discretion of the member states, which are autonomous and competent to conduct their forestry policy. however, the union is intervening, wanting to become, in the long term, a coordinating force for these policies and insisting that parliament's opinion should be consulted. the report focuses too much on the ecological value of the forest and neglects the economic aspect it can represent. indeed, nothing is said about the export of raw wood abroad and the import of processed wood with higher added value. it would have been wise to have considered a certain protectionism to deal with unfair competition from certain countries, including china, as a remedy to this problem. since the report praises the ecological value of the forest, it would also be appropriate to recall the disastrous impact of such a globalised production process on the environment. i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ forests and other wooded areas cover more than 40% of the eu's territory and the forest area has increased by 0.4% per year in recent decades. i voted in favour of this text establishing a new eu strategy for forests and the forestry sector. this strategy recognises the competence of member states in forest management (principle of subsidiarity) and focuses on strengthening cooperation between member states to deal with transnational challenges such as fires, climate change, natural disasters or invasive alien species. the report i voted for also stresses the need to ensure that forest resources and forestry materials are used and reused efficiently. finally, the increase in the administrative burden for forest owners is rejected throughout the text.
in writing. this own-initiative report aims to put forests and the forestry sector at the heart of the shift towards a green economy and to appreciate the value of the benefits that forests can provide in a sustainable way, while ensuring their protection. it covers areas such as rural development, bioenergy, climate change, ecosystems and biodiversity, forest knowledge, innovation and governance. the current eu strategy dates from 1998, and a new european framework is needed for forests, which are facing new challenges from environmental, societal and political changes. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ this text raises two major problems: firstly, it subjects forestry policy to the commission's discretion and thus once again infringes the sovereignty of the member states. on the other hand, it presents an absurd vision of forestry: seeing in forests, above all, beautiful green spaces for recreation and ecology, it does nothing to protect the economy of wood, while the member states, and in particular france, are subjected to a dramatic situation: the logs are exported to china and returned as processed products. the european timber sector is thus subject to unfair competition, partly because of china's protectionist policies, and the ecological cost of these round trips does not seem to be a matter of concern to the commission, despite the interest it claims to have in protecting the environment. i can therefore only vote against this report.
in writing. ‒ today, almost 40% of europe is covered by forests and wood-related industries employ more than 3.5 million people in europe. the forest is a source of wealth and growth which is not negligible to that of the union. with this in mind, the european parliament adopted the new eu forest strategy, replacing the 1998 text. i voted in favour of this text. it emphasises forest management, sustainable development, the intelligent and respectful use of forest raw materials and the exploitation of the economic potential of forest areas. forest areas are now an important source of employment and it is necessary to regulate this development.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, which is part of the development of a european strategy for forests and the forestry sector. we highlight the three areas of work which we believe will be essential for the coming years in this sector: the prevention of fires and natural disasters, the fight against climate change, and the sustainable management of forest raw materials (wood, cork, textile fibres). in addition, as forestry is a sector in perpetual change, we encourage innovation through forestry research and training, including support from european programmes and funds.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which sets out parliament's priorities for promoting sustainable forest management and the competitiveness of the forestry industry. forests cover more than 40% of the eu's territory, and wood is a natural, renewable, reusable and recyclable raw material. forests play an economic, social and environmental role and account for 3.5 million jobs. with this report, europe is finally tackling the dramatic problem of the plundering of european forest resources by emerging countries. europe is failing to protect its forest resources, while all the other major countries are introducing export taxes. this free access increases the price of wood for the european industry, especially for sawmills, which can no longer supply themselves. the number of sawmills in france has fallen by 15% since 2000. the report explicitly calls on the commission to analyse the supply difficulties of the downstream sector, linked to the increase in demand in third countries, in particular for roundwood, and to support this sector.
in writing. ‒ the report rightly emphasises the economic importance of the forestry sector. but the commission is looking at this issue mainly from the environmental angle, which is important but will not solve the crisis in the sector. the french forestry sector, despite its economic weight, is suffering from a chronic deficit of eur 6 million. this is mainly because france sells its logs to countries like china which turn them into furniture. france imports these finished products made with its own resources. this is a major shortfall for our industries, which need investment to modernise. no decision is taken by parliament to protect our market, which is the main problem. parliament also wants to increase its authority to the detriment of the member states. i am voting against this text.
in writing. ‒ forests cover 40% of the eu's territory since 1998, a european forestry strategy has been implemented in cooperation between member states. in the face of increasing threats to forests due to climate change, loss of biodiversity, urban sprawl, and the growing demand for bio-based products, including those derived from forests and wood, the eu forest strategy needs to be revised to ensure sustainable forest management. in its resolution, the european parliament proposes a renewed framework which reaffirms the imperative of sustainable forest management ensuring the maintenance of biodiversity and ecosystems while allowing for multifunctional use of forests, the development of the wood sector and the production of materials for the development of new products and materials. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution of the european parliament, without any illusions however about the reality of its impact because they do not impose any obligations on the member states.

in writing. youth unemployment is a worrying phenomenon in europe, so it is legitimate to be concerned about it and, indeed, to intervene in regions where youth unemployment exceeds 25%, with an increase in prefinancing from 1 to 30% at constant budget seems to be a necessity. however, this seems to be a wishful thinking: as we have seen in france, with measures such as jobs for young people or jobs for the future, these programmes often fail. the transition to employment will only be possible if jobs exist and these measures will not create jobs ex nihilo. the commission's promise to make all the funds available by 2015 is commendable, but it will not be enough: youth unemployment is not due to the weakness of this pre-financing but to the disappearance and lack of jobs. the only solution is to protect our production from social dumping, to practice prudent protectionism at the level of each member state and to enable them to take the necessary measures to create jobs and to get out of the crisis. only then can we get young people out of unemployment.

mr president, commissioner, tax whistleblowers have uncovered a number of major scandals, from the hsbc case to luxleaks. without these sources, the justice system, and public opinion, would never have heard of these cases. we must therefore protect those who have the courage to report illegal activities, often risking professional or personal reprisals for defending the general interest of the citizens. but i believe that the protection of whistleblowers must be comprehensive and also cover cases of corruption in the broad sense, especially by political leaders, or breaches of labour or environmental regulations. why not also denounce illegal immigration networks and trafficking? the limit must be the respect for private life in matters of taxation. this is not to encourage an unhealthy form of dealing. the libel complaint must be pursued. in addition to serious sanctions to be imposed on active fraudsters, financial institutions and consultancies must also be targeted, since they are also guilty of deliberately organising such fraud. this is the case, for example, of pricewaterhousecoopers in the luxleaks scandal. in the context of the directive on business confidentiality, the european union must ensure that it remains consistent and that its scope is well defined. if this balance is achieved, the national front is in favour of this directive on the protection of whistleblowers and journalists.

madam president, public opinion is asking itself: what is europe doing about the explosion of migration flows from the middle east and africa? the successive minutes of silence, punctuated by the multiplication of tragedies in the mediterranean, is a pathetic admission of impotence. it is in these circumstances that we turn our attention to frontex, the agency which the european union has set up to monitor and contain, in cooperation with the member states, all attempts to cross our external borders illegally. frontex has been established in warsaw for 11 years. not all of his employees are polish. for other staff, the host country - in this case poland - undertakes to provide benefits which facilitate the personal settlement of staff and their families. it's the subject of a siege agreement. i have just learned that poland has not yet signed this agreement. i am surprised and i hope that the president-in-office of the council will urge the polish authorities to make this possible as a matter of urgency. we have to provide the european union with a government, without which there can be no control of migration flows.
madam president, the council's proposals are unworthy and turn their backs on our duty. to believe that further tightening of controls will prevent migrants from escaping the chaos is an ineffective and deadly illusion. our immigration policy plays into the hands of the mafia, who take advantage of the desperation of those fleeing poverty and war that ravage their country. so what do you do? let's get back to our principles! let us act against what is a political failure and a humanitarian catastrophe. rescue people in distress, via a european search and rescue mission over a wide operational area. let us renew the solidarity we showed when we welcomed hundreds of thousands of vietnamese boat people. let's put in place an ambitious resettlement program, beyond that shamefully low figure of 5,000 refugees. let us offer these migrants who are in danger legal pathways of immigration rather than turning a blind eye to the corpses that lie at the bottom of the mediterranean. we have no excuse, the shipwreck is ours too!
mr president, the terrible truth is that the recent human tragedies in the mediterranean are a consequence of your migration policy. today, smugglers alert the italian navy to recover the boats. so, of course, when we triple the resources to bring migrants to european shores instead of returning them to the port of departure, we are objectively accomplices of the smugglers! mrs joly, you were the investigating judge: is not the definition of complicity 'help, assistance, provision of means'? you have increased the obstacles to the expulsion of illegal immigrants, who are now only returned in 1% of cases. to put an end to these tragedies and to illegal immigration, it is first of all important to allow the states to restore their borders and to implement a voluntary policy aimed at stopping the vacuum pumps and returning ships to their port of origin. this is an effective and humanistic policy which must be adopted, and which australia has followed with success. secondly, there is an urgent need to restore the rule of law in syria and libya, countries which your irresponsible foreign policy has handed over to islamic fundamentalists and human traffickers. and then, stop your hypocrisy. you want immigration, that's your project. we need only hear mr juncker say that we must open the doors to prevent people from entering through the windows. but have you asked the people of the european nations what they think? because i have not heard of the peoples of the european nations in this chamber for an hour. and i'm not surprised!
mr president, albert einstein said: "foolishness is doing the same thing over and over again and expecting a different result". listening to our conversations, there are questions! while an effective rescue system at sea should have been put in place, it was decided to reinforce operations triton and poseidon to a minimum. the new budget corresponds to that of mare nostrum, but can we really speak of a european rescue operation when 12 member states refuse to participate? while legal channels should have been created or strengthened, a voluntary pilot project of resettlement is being set up, without any concrete proposal on the number of places available. the conclusions say nothing about humanitarian admissions, visas or family reunification. i would remind you that it is not because there are trafficking networks that there are refugees, but because displaced persons cannot reach a place of safety that there are trafficking networks. it would have required an intra-european solidarity mechanism, but the result is almost non-existent. the announced prospect of half a million people arriving on european shores in 2015 could have prompted states to address the issue of the temporary protection directive or article 78 (3) of the treaty. the european council statement says nothing of this! europe, without distinction, is in the crosshairs, but responsibilities should be duly assumed, because it is impossible to act if cold-blooded states do not give themselves the means to act and to act together.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the problem of migration is certainly not a problem of today or of the next few months. it is certainly not a cyclical problem, but a real structural problem for the years to come. political crises, wars, the desertification of the countryside, economic crises, poor governance - all these will cause more and more men and women to leave their countries and risk their lives in search of better living conditions. the establishment of rescue and humanitarian reception systems or the strengthening of frontex is good, but it is notoriously insufficient. what is needed is to tackle the problem at its source, where it exists, as pope francis has urged us to do, in this very house, where his speech was unanimously applauded. what practical steps can you take? first, we have to start with reality. we are helping a number of these countries of origin. in return for this help, we must also demand better governance from them. we must demand that they participate in real development that benefits the whole of their population. that's what we have to do. at the same time, it is also essential to address immigration applicants, in particular by informing them that communication works very well in these areas, that they risk their lives and those of all their loved ones, and that the networks they use are, in reality, real mafia networks. the european union's action can then be concrete, and not simply protective of itself.
in writing. france and europe are facing a veritable migration flood which is only getting worse as the months go by. the causes of this uncontrolled immigration are well known: the current libyan government's inability to control its borders and to combat mafia networks of smugglers, the population explosion affecting the african continent and the european migration policy, which is a real appeal to illegal immigration. as such, the various declarations of intent by the european parliamentarians are totally contrary to the aspirations of the peoples of europe, who want to see a policy of deterrence on immigration. that is why, rather than welcome illegal migrants to our shores, we should send them back to where they came from. the european commission should take as a model australia, which has a strong policy to combat immigration and has led to a significant drop in illegal entry. the member states of the union must turn their backs on ingenuity and naivety and take up this issue hand in hand to protect our borders from this migratory pressure which has become unbearable.
in writing. the council's positions, taken as a whole, are nonsensical and absurd. we all know that mass immigration today is not good for the men who try it or for those who welcome it. the council is still persisting and is strengthening existing mechanisms which have been phased out, when it is a question of changing the paradigm. firstly, the council is basing itself on two erroneous claims: the attractiveness of illegal immigration and the voluntary return of migrants who have arrived in the union. who will the council make believe that the men and women who crossed the mediterranean in unworthy conditions to reach the territory of the union will decide to leave voluntarily? the report that will be presented also repeatedly blames the member states, which would be subject to binding solidarity and would be required to set rates for the distribution of asylum seekers. it is clear that the council has no desire to preserve social peace in europe or the national cohesion of its peoples. your dreams of immigration will make people suffer on both sides of the mediterranean.

in writing. more than 1 500 people have disappeared in the mediterranean since the beginning of the year. tragedy is repeated, as migrants and asylum seekers are forced to risk their lives to reach the european union. while the union can and must do more, all member states without exception must also shoulder their share of responsibility and show solidarity in saving lives and welcoming more refugees. the decisions of the european summit are far from being relevant to the issues at stake. we need a european-wide operation for rescue and search at sea, with the participation of all states. it is also our responsibility to fill the gap created by the absence of safe and legal pathways for refugees to europe. there are concrete solutions: a mandatory european resettlement programme, a european system of humanitarian visas, the possibility of applying for asylum in the embassies of the countries of the union, the activation of the directive on temporary protection. finally, we must not forget the need to strengthen our dialogue with third countries and to help stabilise the situation in libya, which has become a platform for smugglers and criminal networks.
in writing. ‒ this report provides an overview of the expenditure of the ec and the member states on the various eu policies. the report is based on an internal audit by the commission and on the court of auditors' report on the implementation of the eu general budget. the budgetary management by the commission and the member states is systematically called into question. the report raises concerns about shared management actions. the court of auditors has serious doubts about the data provided by the member states but also by certain institutions. this repetition of uncorrected errors over time discredits the functioning of the whole and demonstrates the sclerosis of this pattern. the most frequent cases of fraud are linked to public procurement and conflicts of interest. the most problematic sectors with the highest error rates are still agricultural and rural policy and regional development policy. it is for these reasons, among others, that i voted against the discharge for the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2013.

in writing. ‒ the draft report is intended to give discharge to the general budget of the union for the financial year 2013. discharge is the procedure by which the european parliament closes the budgetary year of the european union for a given year. the text criticises in particular the management of policies resulting from shared competence between the european union and the member states, and attempts to insinuate that their 'exclusive' management by the union would increase performance levels. these language elements are part of a strategy of federalisation of the union. the report also sets out the findings of irregularities and fraud in the management of the common agricultural policy and european funds (erdf and esf) without ever engaging the responsibility of the union. the disbursement of european funds to countries whose administrative structure does not allow an efficient absorption rate is a mechanism for diversion and fraud. finally, the union is faced with payment deficits, which undermine its credibility and legitimacy - two essential qualities when giving lessons in budgetary management to many member states. i voted against this report.

in writing. ‒ these discharge reports are prepared by the court of auditors, which examines the budget of each european institution, agency, undertaking and committee to check how their resources have been used. if the court of auditors considers that the resources have been used properly or are justified, it shall request discharge. if this is not the case, recommendations are made to the institution which is at fault, which must correct them, and the court proposes to postpone its decision. the first thing to note is that we are looking at budgetary discharges in 2015 from 2013 which is more than late and unnecessary. as regards the general budget of the eu, i voted against this grant. the error rate of the european commission remains too high for a european institution, and its procedures are too complex. moreover, several european policies, including agricultural and regional policy, remain problematic because they lack guarantees of legality and regularity. i therefore voted against this grant.

in writing. ‒ this proposal for a regulation aims to combat youth unemployment by increasing the pre-financing rate to 30%. the increase in the pre-financing rate would ensure a faster mobilisation of funds and accelerate the implementation of actions undertaken by member states under operational programmes adopted by the commission. it would help in the development of projects, if the text were not too vague. no information is given on which projects will be selected, or whether the programmes will not already be funded by other eu funds. increasing pre-financing will not affect the quality of programmes or their results on youth employment. the intention is good, but the text does not offer a suitable solution to youth unemployment. so i refrained.

in writing. this report with a proposal for amendment is intended to amend the regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the european social fund (esf) in order to increase the amount of the initial pre-financing for the youth employment initiative. the aim is to increase its pre-financing to reach eur 1 billion by 2015. the full amount will be allocated for 2014-2015 instead of being spread over the period 2014-2020. the youth employment initiative (yei) is intended to help combat youth unemployment, particularly in the regions most affected by the scourge. this is the case, for example, in greece or in france, where the unemployment rate among young people often exceeds 50%. unfortunately, this policy is only a palliative and not sustainable, since the eu does not tackle the fundamental problem of austerity and ultraliberal policies. however, i decided to abstain on this text.
in writing. ‒ the mobilisation of european funds is a real headache for project promoters, especially for some associations that do not have sufficient working capital to advance funding. the proposal for a regulation therefore concerns the increase in the pre-financing rate from 1% to 30% of the overall envelope in order to accelerate the use of the funds provided for by the youth employment initiative (yei). the amount of pre-financing is to reach almost eur 1 billion for 2015. this decision reflects the increasing difficulties faced by project promoters in co-financing their youth employment activities with european funds. the intervention of several actors in employment support policy (departments, regions, states, intercommunities, european union) considerably weakens their effectiveness. the increase in the rate of prefinancing by the yei is therefore welcome in principle, but it should be remembered that only an ambitious and clear national economic, educational and social policy can promote the occupational integration of young people. i abstained on that text.
in writing. ‒ the economic and financial crisis has led to very high unemployment rates across the union. the younger generation is particularly affected by this scourge. this is why the youth employment initiative was created in 2013. this initiative focuses in particular on young people who are not in education or training in regions of the union where the unemployment rate is above 25%. to make this programme more effective, an additional €1 billion, obtained by increasing pre-financing from 1% to 30%, will be paid directly to the initiative. this will enable projects to increase youth employment to be financed more quickly. i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ the european legal regime governing state aid is largely questionable. first of all, it is a confiscation of a state prerogative and, in fact, a loss of sovereignty. i support the freedom of member states to support and promote certain sectors and certain undertakings in the context of national economic strategies. the report before us aims to consolidate the rules for the application of articles 107 and 108 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) and, ultimately, to support the strengthening of this framework for state aid in the union. while many of our international competitors enjoy this freedom, i cannot accept that france and the other member states should be subject to these strict rules which bind their economic activities. that is why i voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ while the european commission's motives for relaxing the state aid regime (articles 107 and 108 tfeu) in favour of certain economic operators are not objectionable, i am opposed in principle to the system of sanctions for state aid: member states must remain free to intervene in a particular economic sector.
in writing. this report should allow the proposal to be approved to define the categories of horizontal state aid for which the commission is empowered to adopt exemptions. if certain sectors are now eligible for state aid (innovation, culture, forestry, sport, etc.) since the codified regulation extends the scope of exceptions to the principle of prohibition of state aid, it is the very principle of articles 107 and 108 that is objectionable since they establish a real supervision by the commission of the member states in their public policies. in the name of the sacred and holy principle of free and undistorted competition, this prohibition of state aid, although accompanied by exceptions, creates a feeling of legal insecurity and testifies ever more strongly to the supremacy of european law over national law, which i challenge in the name of the sovereignty of nations. so i decided to vote against it.
in writing. ‒ the economic difficulties since 1974 and the financial crisis of 2008-09 make the commission's action difficult in relation to member states, which are traditionally interventionist and anxious to meet public expectations. article 107 (1) lays down a general principle of the prohibition of state aid in so far as it affects trade between member states. there are a number of exceptions. the commission has exclusive powers to enforce these provisions (article 108 tfeu). if the european commission's motives for relaxing the state aid regime (articles 107 and 108 tfeu) in favour of certain economic operators are not objectionable, the state aid penalty regime must be rejected in principle. i voted against this text because member states must remain free to intervene in certain economic sectors.

in writing. ‒ this report proposes to codify council regulation (ec) no 994/98 of 7 may 1998 on the application of articles 107 and 108 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union to certain categories of horizontal state aid. the text allows the commission to declare that certain aid for small and medium-sized enterprises, research, environmental protection, broadband infrastructure, employment and sport, and regional aid are compatible with the internal market and are not subject to the notification requirement. i support this text, which is merely a codification of positive law without any change in substance. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the text under examination concerns the application by the commission of the treaty provisions on the exemption from incompatibility of certain horizontal state aid. parliament voted to codify this regulation. this is purely formal and has no substantial impact. it provides greater legal certainty with regard to european legislation.
in writing. ‒ the european legal regime governing state aid is largely questionable. first of all, it is a confiscation of a state's prerogative and, in fact, a loss of sovereignty. i support the freedom of member states to support and promote certain sectors and certain undertakings in the context of national economic strategies. the report before us aims to validate the codification of the rules for the application of articles 107 and 108 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) and, ultimately, to support the strengthening of this framework for state aid in the union. while many of our international competitors enjoy this freedom, i cannot accept that france should be subject to these strict rules which constrain its economic activity. that is why i voted against this text.

in writing. the purpose of the present case is to approve the proposal to define the categories of horizontal state aid for which the commission is empowered to adopt exemptions. although the consolidated regulation extends the scope of exceptions to the principle of the prohibition of state aid (to innovation, culture and heritage conservation, natural disasters, the forestry, sports or broadband infrastructures), it is nevertheless the very principle of articles 107 and 108 that is objectionable, since they establish a genuine supervision by the commission of the member states in their public policies, in the name of the dogma of free and undistorted competition. this general prohibition of state aid, although accompanied by wide exceptions, also creates a feeling of legal uncertainty, as positive law is modified in line with developments in the case-law of the cjeu. i believe that the member states must remain sovereign in their public aid policies and i have therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text which simply codifies council regulation (ec) no 994/98 of 7 may 1998 on the application of articles 107 and 108 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union to certain categories of horizontal state aid. the regulation has been substantially amended several times, so that its provisions are now found in the original act and scattered in subsequent amending acts. in the interests of clarity and simplification of the law, ensuring greater legal certainty and better information for citizens, it was therefore appropriate to codify that regulation. this process preserves the substance of the text in its entirety and merely brings together in a readable form the various modifications made to it.

in writing. ‒ this report proposes to grant discharge for the 2013 budget year to the european parliament, which had a final current appropriation of eur 1.75 billion and a commitment rate of 99.02%. the audit of the reliability of the accounts did not reveal any serious deficiencies, so i voted in favour of discharge. however, i objected to paragraph 50 of the resolution, which states that 'in order to generate sustainable savings in the union budget, it is imperative that parliament and the council establish a roadmap for a single seat, the need for which has been stressed by parliament in several of its previous resolutions'. i am not in favour of such an idea, which could in the long run call into question the status of strasbourg as the seat of the european parliament. that is why i voted against this paragraph.
in writing. i voted in favour of granting discharge to the european parliament. i repeat my support for the european parliament's seat in strasbourg. like my fellow meps, i call on the secretary-general to be more transparent about his ambitions for the european parliament. finally, i take note of the results of the 2014 european elections and hope that lessons can be drawn from them in the run-up to the next elections.
in writing. ‒ i would like to reiterate my commitment to defending the official seat of the european parliament in strasbourg and that is why i voted against the amendment on a single seat. this amendment is a subtle way of calling into question the official seat, in defiance of the treaties. i would like to remind you that the treaties clearly establish the seat of the european parliament in strasbourg and only an agreement at member state level could change that. i regret the attitude of these members who clearly show by these amendments their disinterest in european construction and the symbol of country and reconciliation which the seat of parliament in strasbourg represents. despite this amendment, i voted in favour of the deprez report on the estimated state of revenue and expenditure for the financial year 2016, section i - parliament.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it highlights the need for our institution to move towards greater transparency in the way it organises itself, and so that public money is used in accordance with the objective pursued. among the proposals adopted were: the request for increased controls on the recruitment of local assistants, greater transparency on the expenditure of the budget allocated to meps for their general expenses (rent of parliamentary premises, computer equipment, operating expenses, etc.), and the elaboration of members' declarations of financial interests. as regards the question of the seat of the european parliament, i opposed any amendment aimed at calling into question the seat of strasbourg: i would remind you that this question is a prerogative of the council, which decides unanimously on this question, as is enshrined in the treaties.

in writing. i voted against this report calling for the discharge to be given on the implementation of the budget of the european external action service. the court of auditors explicitly notes that the european external action service (eeas) is not operational, due, inter alia, to its administrative burden. the court notes that the allowances paid to staff are a concern because the controls are not yet sufficiently rigorous. in addition, some social benefits were paid but not all recipients were entitled to them. the lack of transparency on this is unacceptable and makes possible possible fictitious jobs. the court is also concerned about the lack of interest of the eeas in public procurement procedures, to which it has not paid sufficient attention. in general, the court finds that the quality of the information is below the required criteria and that the institution's efforts should be directed mainly to this subject. for example, the eeas did not include in this report the findings of olaf investigations and procedures, nor did it indicate the progress made with regard to the new anti-fraud strategy for eu delegations, which was scheduled to be finalised in 2013.

in writing. this report calls for the adoption of the discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the eu for the financial year 2013, section iv concerning the court of justice (cjeu). the report notes that in 2013, the cjeu had a total of eur 354 880000 in commitment appropriations and the overall budget implementation rate was 96,3%. it regrets the decrease in this rate in 2013 compared to 2012 (98,6%). i note, however, that a number of observations and advice can be made with regard to the court of justice for better management. it is therefore essential to make better use of the resources already available to the court of justice. secondly, in terms of organisation: more efficient scheduling of hearings, increased use of outsourcing, given the very high amount of unused appropriations (eur 2 200 000) allocated to external translation, reduction in the cost of days spent away from the staff, definition of objective criteria to determine what constitutes an excessive time taken to reach a decision, information on the reasons for the high number of contracts concluded in the framework of a negotiated procedure and a reduction in the number of official cars made available to its members and staff. it is inconceivable that the court of justice does not apply a more rigorous and transparent management even though european citizens are affected by the austerity imposed by the eu. i therefore voted against this report.

in writing. ‒ this report recommends that the discharge be given to the european aviation safety agency in respect of the implementation of the budget for the financial year 2013. with a budget increase of 5.15% and no notification of comments in the annual report of the court of auditors, one can ask the question of the relevance of the information which has been communicated to us. the vote on discharge makes it possible to get to know agencies that nobody ever hears about, which raises a real question about the european union's ability to make its public action known and appreciated. i abstained on the vote on this report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text on the discharge for the 2013 budget for the european aviation safety agency (easa). discharge is granted, the budget of eur 167 million, up by 5,15% compared to 2012, having been implemented without significant error. the discharge, which may be granted, postponed or refused by the european parliament, constitutes the final control of the annual budget. the discharge process is the political part of the control of budget implementation. it shall base its opinion on the reports of the court of auditors and on the clarifications provided by the bodies concerned. the discharge decision may be accompanied by recommendations to improve certain aspects of budget implementation.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text on the 2013 discharge for the european medicines agency, which plays a key role in protecting and promoting public and animal health. discharge is granted as the budget has been implemented without significant error. the discharge, which may be granted, postponed or refused by the european parliament, constitutes the final control of the annual budget. the discharge process is the political part of the control of budget implementation. it shall base its opinion on the reports of the court of auditors and on the clarifications provided by the bodies concerned. the discharge decision may be accompanied by recommendations to improve certain aspects of budget implementation.

in writing. ‒ the report on the proposal for a regulation on monetary funds, presented to the european parliament, rightly seeks to correct certain shortcomings in these short-term investment instruments. the strict limitation of constant liquidity was necessary to reduce systemic risk when the holders are characterised by mimetic movements, in particular in the event of massive asset depreciations where losses are borne by the sponsoring banking institution. the framework for securitisation and derivatives is a good balance between the objective of risk finance and the fight against the derivatives of financial structures that are difficult to identify. but this text is not based on a sound study and assessment of the consequences of the regulatory changes, especially in view of the possible circumvention of these provisions and the impact on the economy. the lack of longterm vision in this text explains my abstention from voting.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the securitisation framework and the request for additional requirements for constant liquidity value (clv) money funds, but i am afraid that the accumulation of regulations will be counterproductive.
in writing. monetary funds are financial instruments which allow cash to be invested in the short term and in principle without risk. the amount of these loans is considerable, estimated at eur 1 trillion. about 22% of short-term debt securities issued by governments or companies in europe are held by money funds, which also hold 38% of short-term debt issued by the banking sector. it is always regrettable that securitisation or derivatives are not more widely prohibited in this report. similarly, the impact study of the abolition of the cnavs could have been more precise on the consequences for european management by country, for example. finally, i think that this text seems rather pragmatic and goes in the right direction, but it is difficult to assess the impact of the new regulation in the event of a major crisis. i therefore decided to abstain on this report.
in writing. while i am in favour of the ban on constant net asset value (cnav) funds, i consider that the text is very vague as it contains many exceptions to this ban. for example , navs are allowed for funds linked to the public debt of the union; the funds for small investors, which a priori include only charitable organisations, non-profit organisations and public administrations and foundations. finally, the report on the proposed regulation does not go far enough, since it does not ban securitisation or derivatives, which are the cause of the terrible subprime crisis. i abstained on that vote.
in writing. ‒ monetary funds are short-term financing instruments that have a very rapid impact on the real economy. they represent €1 trillion of financial transactions in europe. although the use of mmfs carries certain risks, they remain the most stable and reliable financial instruments in the non-banking sector. monetary funds were heavily criticized during the crisis, especially the riskiest of them, the cnav (constant liquidity value funds). the other types of money funds, vnav (variable liquidity value funds) have proved more resilient. action was therefore needed to regulate the money market in the european union. the european parliament's report shows a desire to limit the risks associated with the most risky monetary funds, the navs. the latter are thus divided into three categories: small investors' cnavs, public debt cnavs and lvnavs (low-volatility funds). that's an encouraging first step. however, the significant risks posed by navs must be borne in mind throughout the legislative process. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i abstained on this report on the proposal for a regulation on monetary funds. if i consider that it is necessary to prohibit constant net asset value (cnav) funds, the text is, in my view, too vague, since it contains exceptions to this prohibition. the nacs thus remain authorised for funds linked to the public debt of the union; funds for small investors which, a priori, include only charitable organisations, non-profit organisations, public administrations and public foundations; finally, low-volatility funds, whose definition depends on very strict and rigid criteria. the report on the proposed regulation does not go far enough, since it does not absolutely prohibit securitisation or derivatives, which were the cause of the 2008 financial crisis.
in writing. ‒ this report proposes to create a regulatory framework for mmfs with the aim of ensuring stronger investor protection and improving financial stability by limiting the risks of contagion in the event of default. i believe that this report is a step in the right direction towards regulating the banking sector and its financial products, and i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. monetary funds are a short-term investment channel, an alternative to bank deposits. they allow diversification of credit risks. they are therefore used by many actors: businesses, public administrations (especially local authorities), financial institutions, but also social actors (charities, social housing, etc.). i therefore think it is important to frame them at european level. this is all the more so as, as the crisis has shown, they can be a factor of instability for the whole internal market. it is essential to set out precise rules so that they are able to respond to investor claims for reimbursement in all circumstances, without recourse to external support.
