in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which aims to ensure the uniformity of prudential requirements for mmfs across the union. the monetary funds provide short-term financing for financial institutions, businesses and public administrations, and in this way contribute to the financing of the european economy. the report aims to provide mmfs with a regulatory framework that protects investors and enhances financial stability. i welcome that vote.
in writing. ‒ the commission's proposal to introduce new legislative instruments to promote development represents a leap forward to overcome the lack of investment in the european union. in its desire to encourage the development of monetary funds to provide short-term financing for financial institutions, companies and public administrations, the commission is right to take the view that there is a flagrant lack of investment in the european union. however, developing this type of financial instrument ultimately only promotes debt securitisation practices, the same ones that led to the 2008 crisis, i.e. speculation instead of productive investment. i therefore voted against this proposal which offers us dangerous answers to the lack of investment. it is the availability of credit and its conditions that we must work on, not its exchange.
in writing. - abstention from voting. the draft regulation on european monetary funds aims to limit the constant liquidity funds that were involved in the 2008 financial crisis and are already banned in the united states. the same initiative by the european union, except in a few specific cases, because they represent 50% of the funds in the european union: funds linked to public debt, funds for small investors, funds with low volatility. that said, some criticisms: the 3% liquidity mattress which was intended to deal with a large outflow of investors was not retained and there is no precise impact study of the suppression of these funds on european country management. what are the consequences of this? it is therefore difficult to assess the impact of the new regulations in the event of a major crisis, which is regrettable and can be dangerous.
in writing. ‒ finally, the proposal recognises the major risks of shadow banking , which refers to all activities and actors contributing to the non-bank financing of the economy. money market funds (mmfs) provide short-term financing to financial institutions, businesses and public administrations and contribute to the financing of the european economy. in order to safeguard the integrity and stability of the internal market, the proposed regulation introduces new rules aimed at both making the monetary funds more resilient to new financial crises and at safeguarding their role in financing the economy. the report proposes the creation of three cnav funds (constant net worth), with a five-year maturity clause for one of them. this regulation is paltry in the face of the risks that finance takes on the real economy. it is tantamount to absolving the role of non-bank financing and the power of private money creation. i vote against.
in writing. ‒ after more than a year and a half of debate, the proposed text reverses the original proposal to abolish money market funds with constant liquidity, which represent the main risk of financial instability. this is regrettable, especially since the csf and icso have recommended their outright removal. the text also lacks clarity on how the liquidity value on new vlfv funds is calculated. it is also regrettable that investment in securitisation vehicles, even highly supervised ones, is possible. the abolition of the sponsors' mechanism and the main rules governing the management of monetary funds should be welcomed. in the end, we cannot approve this text which is not fully logical, probably under pressure from the financial industry. our abstention reflects the lingering doubt about the effectiveness of reforms that are otherwise necessary.
in writing. this report relates to the issue of monetary funds. the aim is to adopt a draft european regulation on them. these are financial instruments for short-term investment with no cash flow risk in principle, with an estimated volume of eur 1 trillion. while the existence of these monetary funds can hardly be criticised, the text can nevertheless be criticised for not restricting securitisation or the use of derivatives sufficiently. the impact assessment accompanying the text is also too vague as regards the consequences for european management by country. in these circumstances, i decided to abstain from voting.
in writing. the report on the monetary funds presents several problems. despite the high level of uncertainty and speculation which characterizes the monetary funds used by banks as a quick source of liquidity for investors, the report does not aim at their abolition, but just the phasing out after five years of a certain type of monetary fund. in view of the turmoil caused by these financial instruments in the united states, i voted against this report, which provides no real guarantees as to the use of these funds and which consolidates speculative finance.
in writing. it is always regrettable that securitisation or derivatives are not more widely prohibited. the impact study of the abolition of the cnavs could have been more precise on the consequences for european management by country for example. sometimes the accumulation of regulations can be counterproductive. in this case, the text can be regarded as rather pragmatic. however, it is difficult to assess the impact of the new regulation in the event of a major crisis. i'd rather not.
in writing. ‒ the economic and financial crisis that has shaken europe's financial systems has sent an alarm to european policymakers about the importance and need for greater control of monetary funds. since the systems differ from one member state to another, the commission has tried to propose a text which is to apply to the whole of the union. this text was the subject of intense negotiations in parliament. it not only includes elements impacting the financing of the european economy but also concerns the systemic risks that these investment funds pose to the world economy. parliament adopted a compromise text on wednesday which seeks to satisfy all the member states as far as possible. i voted in favour of this agreement and i support the work of my colleagues in the econ committee who have been careful to protect the interests of the french sector.
in writing. ‒ in 2013, the european commission proposed a draft regulation on monetary funds, which provide finance to the economy and public administrations. it aims to regulate shadow banking, non-bank financing, which operates like shadow banks and offers constant remuneration despite fluctuating markets, in order to strengthen the stability of the financial system. the proposal covers three constant value monetary funds (c-nav), but does not include them in the same way as conventional banks. meps from both the right and the social democrats voted against the requirement to hold reserves, as in conventional banks, and against limiting the remuneration of fund managers and prohibiting money funds operating in the eu from also operating in tax havens. i therefore voted against this false framework which does not respect the eu's international commitments in this area and which does not measure up to the necessary financial regulation. this is just a first reading. it is now up to the member states to take a position on this text in the council.
in writing. ‒ the report presented to the european parliament endorses a legal development. it therefore seems to me consistent and appropriate, in the interests of clarity and legal certainty, to vote in favour of this text which repeals a regulation which no longer has any reason to be maintained in the european legal order, as serbia has concluded an association agreement with the european union covering the areas concerned.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this text which again seeks to remove competences from the member states.
in writing. this is a report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on common rules for imports of textile products from certain third countries not covered by bilateral agreements, protocols or other arrangements or by other specific eu import arrangements. this is a recast of ec regulation no 517/94, the only countries concerned are belarus and north korea. the regulation under examination sets annual quantitative limits on imports of several textile products originating in these two countries, the management and distribution of which are the subject of a commission implementing regulation, and allows the union to put in place safeguard and surveillance measures. i therefore voted against the text because it goes against the sovereignty of the member states. i also believe that it would be more useful to regulate the import of textile products from asian countries such as china, bangladesh and india, which are unfair competitors and have killed our european textile industries, as in the vosges department.
in writing. this report is a simple codification of ec regulation no 51/94 of 7 march 1994 on the common rules for imports of textile products from certain third countries not covered by specific union import arrangements. member states should communicate their import statistics to the european commission so that it can take the necessary delegated acts. i voted against this text, rejecting the mechanism of delegated acts in principle.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this text because, while it is in theory a mere revision of ec regulation no 51/94 of 7 march 1994 on the common rules for imports of textile products from certain third countries not covered by specific import arrangements of the union, it is in fact a further infringement of the sovereignty of the member states. the new obligations are imposed on member states, which must immediately forward all their information to the european commission, the great authority - the only one competent to adopt delegated acts: 'in the emergency cases referred to in article 13, the member state or member states concerned shall immediately forward to the commission and the other member states the necessary import statistics and economic data'. i therefore rejected the text, because i am attached to the prerogatives of sovereign nations.
in writing. ‒ this report proposes the codification of an existing regulation on the common import regime in general and on imports of textile products in particular. this proposal does not introduce any major change in the substance of the text. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' in the context of the directive on the protection of consumers. i support this text, which makes technical amendments and strengthens the coherence and legal certainty of the union's import regime. that is why i voted in favour of this report.

for the gue/ngl group mr president, in 2000, the arusha agreements put an end to several years of civil war in burundi, several years of clashes, mainly between hutus and tutsis. they brought to power the first hutu president in the country's history and helped to develop a process of national reconciliation and the establishment of a new constitution. the outgoing president's decision to seek a third term in office challenges this delicate balance. it's been brewing for weeks. the confirmation of this decision by the ruling party congress provoked a wave of protests and the response was a full-scale repression. ngos in the region have already reported several deaths and hundreds of arrests. the imbonerakure, members of the ruling party's youth league, are at the forefront of the abuse. hutu and tutsi voices are calling for the president to come to his senses. even voices within the ruling party, such as those of the president's spokesperson and the party's spokesperson, were suppressed. these people have even been removed from office. more than 20,000 burundians have already fled the country, fearing for their safety. the european union must put its full weight on the balance and put pressure on the president and the authorities of the country. it must, if necessary, question its support for the country, which depends for more than 50% of its budget on external aid, and, if necessary, also question its support for the electoral process, which can only exist if we have the assurance of transparent and fair elections. we know that the voices of the european union and the european parliament are heard in burundi. we must not allow the destabilization of this region to continue. we must act quickly to avoid another bloodbath.

in writing. the marrakesh treaty was adopted on 27 june 2013 by the diplomatic conference for the conclusion of a treaty to facilitate access to printed works by visually impaired and persons with reading difficulties. this is a great step forward for the rights of the blind. it will enable them (if the treaty enters into force and their state ratifies it) to convert a book free of charge into a format that is more accessible to them. the adaptation may also be carried out by an organisation acting on their behalf (the so-called authorised entities). however, attention should be paid in particular to the risk of increased circulation of digitised works, since the treaty does not mention the format in which the paper work can be transformed (risk in the case of audio recordings, for example). although it has its shortcomings and risks, this treaty is a step forward for the rights of the visually impaired, but i am not convinced that the european union should be able to adopt it as a supranational institution. it is up to the member states of the union to have it adopted by their national parliaments.

for the greens/efa group madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, what we are facing today is not a simple disease: it is a plant pest that is coming to europe! at present, there is no treatment available, either for insects or for treating the trees. we are in an absolutely dramatic situation. today, in europe, we are dealing with only one strain: xylella pauca. there are three others that, if they reach our continent, will cause even greater catastrophe. they will affect citrus, grapes and many other species, more than 309 in all. the first step is to extend the entry bans to products from all areas where strains of the genus xylella are present. i am thinking not only of central america, but also of florida, california and mexico. we must impose a quarantine on all products from these areas. secondly, the measures adopted today do not provide for support for small producers. in puglia, for example, the average area is 1.5 hectares. i call for the immediate mobilisation of the crisis reserve to help small producers. we also call for a total ban on the export of any plants at risk from the infested zone, without any possibility of circumvention. the territories - be it spain, greece or france - and the islands such as corsica, sicily and sardinia - must be protected. if they're not protected, it's over. morocco has already banned the importation of all plants from italy into its territory. finally, we must plan for the future now, i.e. allow the construction of double-closed greenhouses so that the plants are grown inside, without the possibility of insect attacks. these measures are not in the text. we have to go further. this is a european health emergency!
madam president, this dramatic crisis, which particularly affects olive trees in italy but can also affect oak and chestnut trees, is of course endangering local crops. two different problems arise. first, to find the scientific solution to stop this epidemic, which is not easy. secondly, we must take strong decisions and apply a form of protectionism to prohibit the importation of plants which are not needed. the rule of your economic system, which is deadly in this case, is free trade. when france tried to enforce protective measures by banning plants from the infested areas, it was accused of violating the rules of free movement of goods. the crisis thus highlights the contradictions of european policy and of course proves the need for strict protection rules. it also adds weight to the criticisms of our industrial model, which tends to homogenize crops. a bacterium does indeed slaughter in genetically homogeneous cultures as a virus can do in factory farms. in any event, this case should prompt the commission to think about the genetic diversification of crops, but also of livestock farms.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution calling for a new alcohol strategy. initially very hygienic and directive, the final proposal proved rather protective for french producers. it included amendments on three main points: the recognition and protection of designations of origin, the fight against unfair competition and prohibited practices in french production, and finally the need to adapt the regulations to smes and artisans. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of the environment against the risks arising from the use of certain substances in the production of certain products. the fight against alcohol abuse is still a matter for the member states, provided that the commitments made by the commission in the framework of the transatlantic treaty do not completely destroy our wine and beer sectors. this resolution will therefore not result in a legislative proposal from the commission. i would, however, expect the commission to tackle products which are really dangerous to health, which citizens consume without even having the right to be informed: pesticides, gmos, meat from animals slaughtered without being stunned. if the european commission wants to defend our health, this is where it must start.

in writing. ‒ two years after the rana plaza building collapse in bangladesh, which killed 1 100 people and injured more than 2 500, this report takes stock of the current situation. the european union, in cooperation with the government of bangladesh, the united states and the ilo, launched the sustainability compact on 8 july 2013, in which bangladesh committed to take action to improve standards and working conditions in the ready-to-wear sector. progress has been made with the adoption of a new law strengthening labour law and freedom of association and the recruitment and training of labour inspectors. in parallel, two private initiatives, accord and alliance, have evaluated more than 2000 ready-to-wear factories and helped close more than 30 factories deemed too dangerous. however, we are still far from the objectives set out in the sustainability pact and it is essential that bangladesh continues its work on labour law reform and that the european union and businesses maintain their commitment; i have therefore supported this resolution.

in writing. - i voted against it. of course, we cannot be indifferent to the plight of the migrants who are currently trying to reach european shores. that said, even though the issue is difficult to resolve, the measures advocated by parliament are inadequate, as president schultz's recent statement shows. the priority of border control is not being given, parliament is providing for an increase in funds for rescue operations but nothing for the control of migration. there is no firm will to fight the smugglers. there is no reference to any policy of aid to the countries of origin or to any willingness to take action against those who promote such migration. the european union acts as if it wants to increase legal immigration to avoid illegality, which also poses problems of reception, integration, etc. parliament is not aware of the future consequences of its policy. even though the host countries are considered to be rich countries, they are faced with difficult economic situations (unemployment, etc.) which do not bode well for the integration of migrants. moreover, the european union imposes its policy on the member states.
in writing. ‒ 1,500 people have already died in the mediterranean since the beginning of the year, 700 remain 'missing'. it is high time that each state took up its responsibilities. the resolution contains good elements on asylum policy and refugees but attempts to use the emotion of the recent tragedy to push the idea of strengthening frontex. an eu agency that violates the most basic human rights of migrants and whose mandate is not to rescue migrants but to file and return them. it presents frontex's triton operation as the equivalent of italy's mare nostrum, an all-rescue operation with a budget three times the european one. finally, this resolution does not in any way question the root causes of migration: the european union's trade and agricultural policies in african countries are ruining local economies; its foreign policy, particularly in libya. and then there's the issue of climate migrants. these are the reasons why these people are forced to leave their homes. i abstain so as not to give the impression that i am opposed to something being done, even if what is proposed is quite inappropriate.
in writing. the recent tragedies in the mediterranean linked to mass immigration from africa have given rise to a vast act of hypocrisy on the part of the european union. on the one hand, we deplore the tragedies that have occurred, and on the other hand, we promote all the possible and imaginable appeals. this will result in a sustained flow of migrants and thus potentially lead to accidents. the war in libya, which is the cause of the increase in tragedies, has also not been affected. instead of implementing a courageous policy, as australia has done, by returning all illegal boats to their countries of origin, eu "figures" such as jean-claude juncker and martin schultz are calling for ever more immigration and ever less generosity for the citizens of european countries. as this resolution is largely pro-immigration and counterproductive, since it helps to increase the means used by the union in the fight against immigration, while amplifying the already existing air calls, i have decided to vote against it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text on the recent tragedies in the mediterranean. more than 1,500 people have lost their lives at sea since the beginning of the year trying to reach europe illegally. italy is struggling to cope with this unprecedented wave of migration. the text welcomes the tripling of the resources allocated to the triton rescue operation. it also called on the union to step up the fight against smugglers and traffickers of human beings, who are the main culprits in shipwrecks. i voted for amendments opposing the allocation of asylum seekers by quotas between member states because the asylum systems of european countries are overloaded. in france, the cost of asylum is rising steadily to reach 2 billion euros a year. in addition, only 1% of rejected applicants are effectively returned to the border. 99% of them are therefore illegally and insecurely staying in france or in another schengen country. it is therefore preferable to give priority to the establishment of safe reception camps for refugees under the auspices of the un in the vicinity of their countries of origin rather than allowing them to risk their lives by making a perilous crossing of the mediterranean at the mercy of smugglers.

in writing. ‒ the eib's operations should be clarified and the lending to projects outside the european union better regulated. the eib too often finances projects that could be financed by private investors, in particular to maintain its credit rating and to be able to finance itself on its own account. it must retain its vocation, which is to correct imbalances.
in writing. the debate on the eib shows the political and economic schizophrenia of the union. on the one hand, the annual activity report rightly deplores a collapse in private and public investment of around 27% since 2009. on the other hand, the european institutions continue, report after report, to advocate a policy of austerity in the name of the euro, the sacred cow of brussels, a policy which we know perfectly well kills investment and hinders the financing of smes. to be effective, the eib must operate in a completely re-engineered economic environment where the union and its policies no longer have a place. there will be no sustainable investment if the union sticks to a policy that has deindustrialised the continent and demoralized entrepreneurs. in addition, the system of allocation of investment by the eib seems to us to be very workable, since it leaves almost no room for manoeuvre to the member states, which are best placed to determine the suitability of projects. for example, the juncker plan will retain only the most profitable projects, to the benefit of a few large cities and agglomerations and to the detriment of rural areas and medium-sized cities. i decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text on the 2013 annual report of the european investment bank, which plays a key role in supporting public and private investment in the member states and the union, but also in implementing the €315 billion juncker investment plan. in the current difficult economic environment, the eib's involvement helps maintain social cohesion by stimulating job creation and infrastructure.
in writing. the 2013 annual report of the european investment bank reports an increase of 37% in eib financing activities, a decline of 18% in public and private investment, including a 35% decrease in lending to smes over the period 2007-2013. the report suggests that investment should be directed towards activities with european added value, and on the potential for job creation, especially in countries with the highest unemployment rates, as well as in research and social affairs, and suggests improving governance and transparency of investment. i voted for this report, which seems to me to be moving in the right direction and would correct some of the mistakes in the eib's investment strategy.
in writing. the report proposes that priority be given to projects with european added value. however, many high value-added investments have a national rather than a european dimension. this priority criterion will further complicate access to eib financing for smes and local and regional authorities. in addition, financing projects domiciled in non-eu countries poses a problem at a time when the real economy is becoming scarcer in financial instruments. in 2013, the eib financed €8 billion of projects domiciled in third countries. the eib's financing share outside the eu should be redirected towards smes in the internal market. finally, the geographical distribution of eib financing reveals significant differences in the loans granted to the various member states. in 2013, france received eur 276 million in loans, compared with eur 537 million for germany and eur 2.3 billion for italy. these allocation problems raise questions about the transparency of procedures and criteria adopted by the eib's governance committee. i therefore abstained on this report.
in writing. ‒ meps adopted the annual report of the european investment bank for the financial year 2013. i voted in favour of this report. however, i regret the dramatic decline in lending to smes and stress the importance of further support for smes in the future in order to encourage investment in europe and indeed to stimulate the recovery of growth.
in writing. ‒ the european investment bank (eib) is a european financial institution that finances projects in europe and in third countries in the fields of infrastructure, energy, research and innovation, etc. the european parliament's annual report on the eib's activities in 2013 calls for support for public and private investment and contains some criticisms of the investment plan launched by the juncker commission in july 2014, including the fact that part of the allocated funding is taken from other projects. so it's a game of pure illusion! the report also laments that half of the member states will not achieve their national targets for education and reducing greenhouse gases by 2020. and it's worse for jobs and poverty. the austerity policies are called into question in view of their effects on economic growth, the sharp deterioration of social conditions, the increase in imbalances between european regions and their democratic consequences. i could therefore only vote in favour of such a report, even though it is most likely to have no effect on the policies being pursued.
in writing. ‒ this motion for a resolution conceals the hypocrisy of the eu's food and agricultural policy bodies behind good intentions. it aims to promote a reliable and sustainable agricultural sector throughout the union, a prosperous and diversified rural economy, a clean environment and family farms supported by a dynamic, fairer, internationally sustainable and properly financed common agricultural policy . one of the most important is the need for food security. however, small-scale farming models cannot be adopted in france or the united states, where 48 million people are struggling to feed themselves and receive food aid. food sovereignty is essential for food security and the models advocated in this resolution do not contribute to it. moreover, these very good intentions are far from the actual policy pursued by the union. i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this debate because it will be an opportunity to feed the debate needed for the sustainability of our planet.
in writing. the resolution aims to improve food security, combat waste, develop agriculture in the third world and protect soils. this is a non-binding resolution, which takes the opportunity of the 2015 world expo in milan to encourage the union to promote these actions. this report shows the schizophrenia of the union, which on the one hand promotes free world trade and free and undistorted competition, thus favouring an 'americanized society' even in its food, and on the other complains about food insecurity in the union, in particular the situation of 80 million people living below the poverty line, of whom nearly 3 million die every year from food-related diseases. finally, the text makes no mention of a change in the agricultural model based on productivism and does not call into question treaties such as ttip, which encourage the importation of bad sanitary or food practices such as gmos into the union. so i decided to vote against it.

in writing. ‒ the 2015 milan world expo opened on 1 may with the theme 'feeding the planet'. this is a question that concerns europeans, of course, but also citizens of the world. european food security policy must be part of a global vision. the challenge is to meet the doubling of food requirements by 2050 in a context of water scarcity, a decline in arable land and a new energy situation dictated by the fight against climate change. the world organization of agricultural markets must be re-designed taking into account the two main aims of the common agricultural policy, namely to guarantee food security and to save the living fabric of farmers and their families, both in our own country and in the poorest countries. a targeted global food stock system is also needed, consisting of emergency stocks to reduce hunger and stocks to regulate commodity prices. this system should be managed by the un through its world food and agriculture organization, fao.

on behalf of the ppe group. mr president, commissioner, we are not magistrates, judges or lawyers here, and it is not for us to decide the guilt or innocence of the accused who are tried by the indonesian courts. but we are public officials, elected in our nations by citizens to represent values, which today command us to demand from the indonesian authorities that our citizens, like all the defendants, have the right to fair trials, respecting the law and the procedures of the defense, all things that have not been granted to a french national who is now threatened with execution in indonesia. we are elected public officials who have a duty to condemn the death penalty, as you have just done. the death penalty is banned by the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. we are also elected officials and human beings who have a duty to express our indignation at the gruesome staging of executions in indonesia today, as in other countries you have mentioned, commissioner. we're running out of time. the european union is a partner of indonesia. we held a dialogue on human rights between the european union and indonesia in jakarta last november. we have concluded a cooperation and partnership agreement with indonesia. we are making funds available to indonesia, through the regional funds, for its higher education, for its good governance. we cannot ignore the indonesian authorities. i therefore call on european officials - some of whom should be in jakarta today to defend european citizens - to go beyond the extremely polite and dignified communiqués and diplomatic approaches which have so far failed to produce results. this is a very important issue today for european citizens who ask for our help. i am counting on you to convey to the indonesian authorities a message of firmness which in no way violates their sovereignty or their right to fight narcotics and drugs. however, the death penalty for a french citizen, as is currently being carried out by the indonesian judiciary, will not be the end of this fight.
on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, a country is great not only because of its power but also because of the brilliance of its ideas, its causes and the generosity it brings to the most important moments of its history. ladies and gentlemen, this declaration is not mine: it was signed by robert badinter when he was keeper of the french seals in 1981. well, that is the same message i want to send, on behalf of the european parliament, to the indonesian authorities. yes, mr. president widodo, you can be great, your generosity can burst into the world's face, if your power serves life. you wanted to send a strong message to the citizens of indonesia and the rest of the world? for the gue/ngl group mr president, i would first of all like to thank all the political groups for agreeing to put this debate on our agenda, as requested by the gue/ngl group. many of us here are committed to the fight against the death penalty. we would be failing in our responsibility if we did not act immediately. on tuesday evening, eight people were executed, one indonesian and seven foreigners. fourteen executions have taken place since the beginning of the year, compared to none in 2014 and only five in 2013, after a five-year moratorium. in indonesia, as in other countries, the death penalty is being used again, mainly for drug trafficking. according to the attorney general of indonesia, the country is waging a war against horrible crimes that threaten the survival of the nation. there is no justification for this barbaric punishment, especially since it is aimed at lamp-workers, small smugglers who are often poor and vulnerable, often foreigners and deprived of the basic rights of consular assistance and translation. there aren't many drug lords on death row. worse, the indonesian constitutional court had agreed to hear on may 12 the appeal of the two australians executed on tuesday. 125 death row prisoners are currently languishing in indonesian prisons. 57 for drug trafficking. among them were 27 foreigners, including 4 europeans, all convicted in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this debate because this proposal for a regulation allows for the adoption of additional legislative provisions, at least for the most frequently used indices, in order to improve governance and limit conflicts of interest and any other weaknesses.
in writing. this report concerns indices used as benchmarks in financial markets. the libor scandal has made us aware of the importance of these indicators and the need to control them. there are two types of indices: those resulting from objective contributions and those calculated from nonpublic information. investors use them for their anticipation. this report deals here only with major indices such as the money market reference rates such as libor or euribor. if these indices are distorted, there can be adverse effects on financial markets as we have seen. i abstained on this text because, although the report calls for the strengthening of the power of esma and the national authorities, i regret that it does not address the indices of commodity markets or those of third countries.
in writing. ‒ the proposed regulation on benchmarks is a response to the various scandals linked to the manipulation of certain data. the most famous case is the libor case, in which the banks involved were fined a record amount. indeed, manipulations of the index can have serious consequences for the activities of certain financial institutions. given the magnitude of the financial sums involved, it is regrettable that this draft legislation does not cover all the truly systemic indicators with the same legal force. that is why i wanted to abstain on the vote on this text, which has been postponed.
in writing. ‒ benchmarks are used to determine the value of financial instruments, financial contracts and the performance of investment funds. they therefore have a considerable bearing on the impact of the financial market on the real economy. recent scandals have exposed the manipulation of euribor and libor, the most important benchmarks in the union. the manipulation of benchmarks can cause significant losses to consumers and investors, distort the real economy and undermine market confidence. this regulation will therefore restore the integrity of benchmarks by making their management more transparent. administrators of benchmarks will be required to register with the european securities and markets authority (esma) and to publish a declaration of compliance specifying the use of their benchmark and its reliability. they will also have liability (code of conduct) and record-keeping constraints, as well as audit and review requirements. this type of regulation is very advanced and will only exist in the european union. the negotiations will require a system of equivalence and reciprocity with reference indices from third countries. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to abstain on this report, which deals with the problem of the manipulation of benchmarks and the scandals that this manipulation may have generated. i certainly support the measures proposed in the report to make banks more transparent in order to prevent misappropriation. critical indices must therefore comply with the icso rules, which means that they must be handled in accordance with a code of good conduct which includes the reinforced communication of all the elements to the supervisory authorities. however, i regret that the final decision on whether an index is critical is taken by the european securities and markets authority (esma) and not exclusively by national authorities.
in writing. ‒ this report proposes the creation of a common framework to ensure the reliability and integrity of benchmarks used in financial instruments and contracts. i voted in favour of this text, considering that it will improve financial governance in europe, avoid conflicts of interest and strengthen the quality of data, the methodologies used, controls and the protection of users of benchmarks.
in writing. the regulation on benchmarks in financial instruments and contracts is part of the review of the european policy on market abuse. the aim of this text is to prevent the recurrence in the future of scandals such as those caused by the manipulation of libor and euribor. the latter are benchmarks for interbank interest rates, set by the banks themselves. in order to ensure public confidence in financial markets, which are essential for the functioning of our economy, we need reliable indices. within the european union we must be able to avoid the manipulation of all benchmarks, whether in terms of interest rates, exchange rates, oil prices or macroeconomic forecasts. the broad scope of this text is therefore a good thing.
in writing. ‒ this european parliament report aims to introduce strict regulation of benchmarks in financial instruments and contracts. these benchmarks, calculated by aggregating data, may relate to interbank lending rates such as libor and euribor, oil markets or commodity markets. they are used to set the rate of many contracts and financial instruments. in concrete terms, this means that the administrators of indices with a significant impact on financial markets will be subject to the control of a college of supervisors and the european financial markets authority. in parallel, rules on internal control and the prevention of conflicts of interest will apply to non-critical index administrators. these provisions, which are a step towards the consolidation of the european financial system, now have to be confirmed by the member states.
in writing. ‒ the scandals that have erupted in the cases of manipulation of libor and euribor rates indices have shown the scale and seriousness of certain frauds in financial circles. by emphasizing transparency around these so-called systemic indices, the proposal for a regulation is a new positive element in banking regulation, which i support. however, the proposals to lower the thresholds below eur 500 billion of outstanding financial products were not incorporated in the report, making the proposal for a regulation timid and more lax in terms of calculation method and transparency for indices considered non-critical. i therefore abstained on this report, which is incomplete and does not allow for a far-reaching reform of banking regulation.
in writing. ‒ i abstained on the proposal for a regulation on benchmarks in financial instruments and contracts. the project is a response to various financial scandals such as libor, where the banks involved manipulated the price of this index. the proposal for a regulation merely improves the transparency of the method of calculating the benchmarks and provides the supervisory authorities with all the information necessary to ensure that they are drawn up correctly. however, this proposal does not remove the root cause of the problem, namely the conflict of interest of certain banks which are both in a position to publish the indices and to benefit from the price changes which they can anticipate in their favour.
in writing. ‒ this proposal for a regulation concerns benchmarks in the context of financial instruments and contracts. after the various financial scandals that europe has experienced since 2008, for example libor, the legislator decided to take action against banks manipulating indices. the proposal for a regulation seeks to ensure that the method of calculating benchmarks is transparent and that all the necessary information is provided to the supervisory authorities responsible for ensuring that the benchmarks are correct. however, conflicts of interest are at the root of the problem, as some banks publish indexes and profit from them by speculating on their value. so it's a crime to initiate. i abstained on that text.

in writing. ‒ a benchmark is a value or indicator calculated on the basis of a representative set of data or information. it is used to value financial instruments or contracts, or to measure the performance of an investment fund. the london interbank offered rate (libor) and the euro interbank offered rate (euribor), which serve as benchmarks for interbank interest rates, are examples of benchmarks. any risk of manipulation of benchmarks can undermine market confidence, cause significant losses for investors and, above all, distort the real economy. the commission and parliament's report propose improving the control and governance of the referral process to avoid manipulation. the report stresses the need to combat conflicts of interest and ensure transparency. but these few efforts pale in comparison with the manipulation of these indices that has already occurred in the past. in particular, the text does not propose the creation of alternative indices measuring the real economy rather than speculative forecasts. i vote against it.
in writing. ‒ the libor and euribor manipulation scandal has tarnished the credibility of benchmarks and made it necessary to rethink their regulation. however, it is one thing to frame upstream the producers of evidence, it is another to sanction in a truly dissuasive way. the record fines imposed on the banks involved in liborgate, amounting to billions of euros, are clearly nothing compared to the profits generated. the proposed regulation is complex to implement and especially to monitor, not to mention the forthcoming level 2 texts. the simple transparency proposed for most indices does not always allow for detection of manipulation. a truly dissuasive sanction would involve liability for the assets of decision-makers, administrative bans for institutions found guilty and a ban on purely speculative products based on indices.
in writing. this vote concerns indices used as benchmarks in financial markets. in the wake of the libor scandal, some have become aware of the importance of these indicators and the need to control them. these are indicators on which investors base their expectations. there are two types of contributions: those resulting from objective contributions and those calculated on the basis of nonpublic information. in this case, the report only deals with major or systemic indices, i.e. those which are likely to have dangerous consequences (such as the money market reference rates libor, euribor, etc.). if these are distorted (for example by conflicts of interest), this can have a significant impact on financial markets. the report envisages strengthening the power of the european financial markets authority as well as national authorities. however, it is regrettable that it does not address commodity market indices or third country indices (only an approval from esma is required). i therefore decided to abstain on that text.

in writing. ‒ the proposed regulation on benchmarks is a response to the various scandals linked to the manipulation of benchmarks by those who publish them. the most famous case was libor, the overnight interbank rate, for which the banks involved were fined a record amount (deutsche bank alone, for example, paid $2.5 billion to the us in april, sg, barclays and rbs $1.8 billion to the eu). the magnitude of the sums involved may make it regrettable that legislation does not cover all the truly systemic indicators in the same way. it is satisfactory that no exceptions to the scope of the regulation have been made, whereas some wished to exclude professional indexes from the scope of the regulation. however, since this is now an additional constraint on the banks, we cannot vote against it. so i choose to abstain.

in writing. ‒ i supported the silva pereira report on financing for development because it allows the european parliament to contribute to the eu's position on official development assistance (oda). the oda is essential to implement a european development policy and thus convince the countries of the south to fight against global warming in preparation for cop 21. the report notes the failure of eu member states to meet their 2005 commitments to spend 0.7% of their national income on oda by 2015 and calls for multiannual budgetary timetables by 2020 to meet this target. the report also highlights the importance of innovative sources of development finance such as the financial transaction tax and stresses the need to mobilise national resources in developing countries to manage public finances and fight corruption. i voted for this report because it is a message to the member states and to the french government in preparation for the cop 21 in december 2015.
in writing. the report calls on eu member states to meet their official development assistance targets (of 0.7% of gni). it is a non-binding text that envisages the impossible and hopes to solve all the ills (poverty, hunger, etc.) that affect the planet. while i obviously want the poorest countries to develop and to improve their living conditions (including through subsidies), i think it is more profitable to embark on a genuine policy of co-development, of controlling migration flows and of supporting governments in their fight against corruption or fundamentalism, for stable countries that guarantee security and therefore economic growth. nevertheless, the eu tries to give itself a good conscience in this text, often forgetting that it is these ultra-liberal rules that impoverish countries. the report also calls for the promotion of public-private partnerships and joint financing, which i oppose. for these reasons i have decided to vote against.
in writing. ‒ this report takes stock of the eu's financing of development. it recognises that the use of official development assistance is not sufficiently monitored by the external action service and that its effectiveness has not been demonstrated. the report also highlights the positive contribution of immigrants to the development of their home countries through the growth of financial flows from the diaspora. it therefore shows that immigration benefits the countries of origin more than the countries of destination. finally, the report recommends using public-private partnerships as a lever for development. these public-private partnerships risk increasing the influence of the large cac 40 companies on the african continent. as a principle, i am opposed to the european union's external action and therefore voted against the report.

in writing. ‒ parliament called on eu countries to respect their commitments on external aid. first, at the financial level, the states must respect their commitment to allocate 0.7% of their gnp to development. so far only four eu countries have achieved this target, namely denmark, luxembourg, the netherlands and sweden (belgium is about to join this group). secondly, it is important to think about innovative ways of financing development. several initiatives have already been launched and need to be strengthened. i am thinking in particular of unitaid, whose more than half of the funds, from the "air ticket tax", fund access to hiv treatment in low-income countries. the idea of a financial transaction tax, which would generate funds for development, must also be put into practice. finally, the union and the states must implement win-win partnerships. the international conference on financing for development in addis ababa in july, which will set the first framework for the next global development goals, should be an opportunity for representatives of the international community to address all these issues.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the non-binding resolution calling on the eu member states to respect the target of devoting 0.7% of their national income to official development assistance (oda), as a key instrument for financing development, and to set a precise timetable for achieving this target by 2020. in voting in favour of this resolution, i wanted, like the overwhelming majority of my fellow members of the european parliament, to stress the need to mobilise national resources effectively in developing countries. these domestic resources, which are more predictable and more sustainable than foreign aid, must be a major source of financing for the development of these countries. the resolution underlines the european parliament's wish that the european union should assert its political leadership in the process of defining the framework for sustainable development and that it should maintain its position as the world's leading contributor to international development aid. we therefore also call on the european commission, the council and the member states to do everything possible to ensure that the european union plays a leading role in the negotiations which will take place in the near future in the framework of the addis ababa international conference on financing for development.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on financing for development because it is a half-admission of the lack of real control over the use of funds. paragraph 48, for example, states in a subtle way that there is a problem with the transparent and efficient implementation of aid and funding, that there is a problem of corruption and mismanagement and that there is often a lack of 'accurate, timely and comparable data' on income and expenditure. paragraph 42 emphasises 'the positive contribution of migrants to the development of their countries of origin and calls for more effective and innovative cooperation on migration policy between countries of origin and destination; draws attention to the significant and growing financial flows of remittances from the diaspora". this pro-immigration observation ignores the fact that emigration to europe often represents a brain drain that is detrimental to the countries of origin.
in writing. - i voted against it. this report advocates migration by arguing that migrants contribute positively to the development of the countries of origin because they cause financial flows between the diaspora and the country of origin. we strongly oppose such reasoning. in addition, this report shows a lack of control over the use of funds, which is intolerable.
in writing. ‒ the report on financing for development highlights the need to combat poverty and to support the un sustainable development goals. obviously, goals are commendable. the text thus recalls the central role to be played by the united nations in the establishment of orderly and cooperative international trade, the first steps of which are being taken through 'international tax cooperation', under the auspices of the un, and an active crackdown on tax havens, tax evasion and illegal financial flows. i am, however, opposed to certain elements of the report, such as the emphasis on public-private partnerships as a means of financing and the idea that better access to international markets is a condition for development. i am voting for this text to support these ambitious tax proposals, but i regret that on every issue the rapporteurs are forced to repeat the mantras of liberal dogma which gives their text a stupid tone.
in writing. ‒ the report outlines the eu's objectives and commitments in terms of development finance but fails to establish clear rules on anti-corruption, which is the logical counterpart to the aid given to the countries concerned. this is all the more crucial given that 1.5 billion people live below the poverty line and suffer from health, education and living standards deficiencies in the countries receiving eu aid. secondly, the report rightly calls for more effective cooperation between countries of origin and emigration in the management of flows. unfortunately, much more is needed and financial aid should be conditional. it is known that most deportations cannot take place because the countries of origin do not accept to recognize their own nationals as such. the report also advocates the use of public-private partnerships in developing countries, which raises many concerns, particularly as regards the additional debt involved. for these reasons, the vote is therefore against.
in writing. this non-binding resolution is an alignment of good feelings. the rapporteur regrets that 1.5 billion people live in extreme poverty and proposes to eradicate poverty... to do this, it wants to require eu member states to respect their official development aid targets (of 0.7% of gni). if we can only support the development of the poorest countries, including through subsidies, this must not be a 'whitewashing' operation by the eu in its promotion of 'happy globalisation' to the hilt. the extreme poverty in these countries cannot be blamed by a modest disguise of the source of the situation. the report also calls for the promotion of public-private partnerships, which would only make the situation worse, and of mixed financing, which could lead to a debt bubble. finally, he highlights the positive contribution of immigrants to the countries of origin, which increase financial flows... for these reasons i have decided to vote against.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text which calls on member states and other developed countries to maintain or increase their level of official development assistance. the aim is to contribute to the reduction of global poverty through economic and social development and good governance, particularly in fragile and conflict-affected states. over the period 2014-2020, the union's contribution to development finance will be eur 19,7 billion for cooperation, eur 6,8 billion for humanitarian aid, plus eur 2,2 billion from the emergency aid reserve and a contribution from the european development fund (edf) of eur 30,5 billion. only by creating conditions conducive to the personal and collective development of people in their countries of origin will we be able to avoid tragedies such as those experienced by migrants who try to cross the mediterranean and die at sea, sustained by the false hope of a better future in the european union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on financing for development, which calls for an ambitious global partnership as a condition for achieving the sustainable development goals (sdgs). eu member states must meet their 2005 commitment to spend 0.7% of their national income on official development assistance and set a timetable for achieving this target by 2020. moreover, it is not enough to give money, it is necessary to mobilize resources effectively in developing countries. the report calls for an extension of the european commission's remit to help strengthen the capacity of the tax administration, public financial management and the fight against corruption. finally, as mentioned in the text, official development assistance cannot cover all the financing needs of developing countries, the private sector must engage in these countries and invest in a more responsible manner.
in writing. this report sets out a european union position for the international conference on financing for development, to be held in ethiopia in july 2015, which aims to prepare the post-2015 sustainable development agenda. the report calls on the eu to honour its commitments on investment and development aid (at least 0.7% of gni). the report supports measures such as taxes on financial transactions to finance development, condemns tax havens and emphasises the role of civil society. amendments from my group were also adopted, notably on taxation and the position of women. i voted in favour of this report, which i thought was a step in the right direction.
in writing. ‒ this report suggests that development aid funds are not sufficiently controlled. he also advocates a perverse view of development: development should not come from money sent home by expatriates or from public-private partnerships with western companies that will put developing countries even more in debt. it is obvious that these countries must themselves create wealth, just as the states of the european union, which should finally have reindustrialisation policies to ensure growth and employment. the inability of the european institutions to understand how to create wealth is once again evident both within and without. in these circumstances, i am against this report.

in writing. ‒ this report is a half-admission of the lack of any control over the use of these funds, a fact denounced by the front national since the beginning. it highlights the positive contribution of migrants to the development of their countries of origin, which is astonishing. they would contribute to the growth of financial flows between diasporas and countries of origin. the report supports the creation of funds for these diasporas and calls for further efforts to reduce the costs of capital transfers and to improve their effect on local development in the countries of origin. the report also advocates the use of public-private partnerships as a development lever for developing countries, thus favouring the only companies capable of providing these services, which are predominantly western companies. the committee on budgets warns that such mixed financing could lead to a debt bubble, particularly in sub-saharan africa and the caribbean. if we want to combat immigration and promote the stability of the continents and their autonomy, we should simply do the opposite. i am naturally opposed to this text.
in writing. ‒ this report provides an update on the financing of development aid in the european union, on the implementation of the post-2015 development objectives. the report reminds member states of the commitment they made in 2005 to raise their official development assistance (oda) to 0.7% of gross national income (gni). this objective was to be achieved by 2015. at the end of 2014, the average commitment of the member states is only 0,47 per cent of gni. only five countries in the world have fulfilled this commitment, including four members of the european union: sweden, denmark, the netherlands and luxembourg. the report condemns tax havens and tax evasion and calls for investment in key areas such as education and health, including the importance of sexual and reproductive rights despite the efforts of the right wing in the house. these are good reminders, and i have therefore voted in favour of this resolution, although i have no illusions about its impact, particularly in france, a country which is continually reducing its development aid, including to the poorest countries. at a time when the eu is making this issue one of the pillars of its migration policy, it is important to recall the hypocrisy of the member states.

in writing. ‒ i voted against the motion for a resolution on green growth slots for smes. the proposal calls on the commission and the member states to facilitate the development of smes in the green economy financially, including through the juncker plan. but if the intention is good, the means are paltry. no financing solution is actually proposed. encouraging member states to implement favourable tax provisions for these smes is difficult in the current budgetary context, and is also contrary to the objectives of public-accounting consolidation imposed by europe. the reference to the junker plan is also ineffective, since the plan itself is not provisioned. as for encouraging member states to attract foreign investors, this is advice that applies to the whole economy and not just the green economy. the resolution calls on the member states to deregulate in order to remove obstacles to the internal market. the european union's deregulation is too seldom concerned with administrative hassles. they are usually aimed at weakening social and even environmental standards, which would be particularly inappropriate in a so-called green economy.
in writing. ‒ this green growth project for small and medium-sized enterprises has many positive aspects, since it advocates a reduction in burdens and regulations, or the promotion of entrepreneurship in secondary education. but other aspects are much less defensible. the union is, in fact, still interfering with the member states' competence: the aspect concerning school curricula, although praiseworthy in substance, is an intrusion into the member states' competence. it is also a text which will weaken the states in the face of unregulated globalisation, in a context of crisis where only protectionism will be able to defend their interests. for all these reasons, i have decided to vote against this text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by my colleague philippe de backer on the green growth opportunities for smes. the report calls on the commission to support as much as possible, through the budget of the horizon 2020 programme, european smes that are involved in environmental sustainability, which is a real driver of growth. smes are the backbone of the european economy and an important engine of growth and job creation. i welcome the fact that this report was adopted by a large majority.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on promoting the green economy for smes. in order to make the green economy a real driver of job creation and growth, it is necessary to define clear and transparent rules, allowing smes to easily access funding opportunities, and to establish an appropriate european framework for research, development and innovation.
in writing. ‒ this backer report, 'green growth hubs for smes', calls for encouraging green investment in smes by means such as supporting the financing and development of smes in the green economy, better information on available financing options, simplification of regulations, a tax policy that encourages venture capital, or a stimulus to entrepreneurship in secondary education. this report is an alignment of vague intentions and proposals, some of which are already being applied in the member states. while some of them can be supported, others are more in line with the competence of the member states, such as the proposals on education or environmental regulations. the report also contains a neo-liberal patina and calls for ever more deregulation. i therefore decided to abstain from voting on this report.
in writing. - i abstained. the proposal calls on the commission to support financing policies for the development of smes in the green economy, using a variety of means. the commission is therefore requested to ensure that member states have tax policies that are favourable to smes, that they improve their information on available funding in relation to the green economy, that they favour smes in the juncker plan, that they act to limit regulation at national level and that they promote entrepreneurship in education programmes. the resolution does not, however, offer much concrete information, particularly on the development of instruments to support the development of projects in this field. moreover, as is often the case, it tends, in spirit, to want to limit the competences of the states that we consider exclusive, as is the case with education. it even encourages the commission to act against the member states, particularly in the area of regulation, which is of course unacceptable. this is because this proposal is in keeping with the neoliberal logic which is the dogma of the european union.

the agenda calls for the joint debate on csdp (article 36 teu) on:- report by arnaud danjean, on behalf of the committee on foreign affairs, on the implementation of the common security and defence policy (based on the annual report from the council to the european parliament on the common foreign and security policy) (2014/2220(ini) (a8-0054/2015),- report by eduard kukan and ind tarrekand, on behalf of the committee on foreign affairs and the committee on budgets, on the financing of the common security and defence policy (2014/2258(ini) (a8-0136/2015), and- report by ana gomes, on behalf of the committee on foreign affairs, on the impact of developments in european defence markets on defence and security capabilities in europe (2015/2037(ini) (a8-0159/2015).
the rapporteur. madam president, madam high representative, never since the launch of the common european security and defence policy, 16 years ago now, has europe faced so many simultaneous crises at its borders and on its soil, as well as multifaceted threats to its external and internal security: regional conflicts, civil wars, terrorism, migration tragedies, nuclear and conventional proliferation. the enormous geopolitical transformation under way is posing unprecedented challenges to our continent, particularly in its eastern neighbourhood and on its southern flank, if not in their nature - wars and terrorism, we have known them for a long time - but in any case in their scale. in the face of these dramatic developments, the european union and its member states have a dual duty to act: to protect themselves and to act in our environment to reduce instability. unfortunately, we must admit that the impression that prevails among our fellow citizens, but also outside our borders, is that of european impotence: in ukraine, syria, iraq, the middle east, libya, the horn of africa, the sahel. there are very few crises and conflicts today in which europe, either collectively or through its member states, plays a truly decisive role in terms of its interests, its values and its diplomatic, economic and military weight. even where the action of some europeans seems the most assertive and robust, such as that of france in the sahel, the scale of the diplomatic, military and economic task, our budgetary constraints and our capacity limits leave no illusions about the very relative impact of what is undertaken by a few. in this context, the common security and defence policy could and should be a major instrument for europe to finally assume its responsibilities for its own security and that of its environment. i am a realist, so i am not saying that this common policy is the only one possible, because national policies and multilateral partnerships such as the atlantic alliance are essential structures for the defence of the continent and our nations. this is recognized in the treaties. the common security and defence policy is not, and will not be in the near future, a genuine defence policy. it is an instrument, a policy for crisis management, and we must consider it as such first. the problem is, the seizures are here. they are becoming more intense, more and more close, and our management is becoming less and less able to meet these challenges. the guidelines you have proposed, madam high representative, with the defence ministers you met yesterday in brussels for the european council in june, are in the right direction, and i commend you for the determined action you have taken since you took office. these guidelines are based on the same observation as the one i have just made, namely dissatisfaction, insufficiency and urgency. you have stressed that the european union is currently deploying 11 civilian missions and five military operations. the professionalism and dedication of our civilian and military personnel is remarkable and we must commend them. but the respect we owe to these personnel, who are deployed in difficult theatres on behalf of the european union, also obliges us to recognise that these missions and operations become, far too often, forms of alibi for our presence. i would say that our visibility sometimes overrides our effectiveness in the judgment we make on these missions. i therefore hope that you will carry out this evaluation work successfully. in conclusion, because time is running out and there is a lot to be said also on the industrial and capacity level, naturally i would simply like to point out to you that today we do not need creativity, inventiveness or imagination. we need to be able to read. everything we need in terms of security and defence is in the treaty: enhanced cooperation, permanent structured cooperation, flexibility with article 44, financing and solidarity mechanisms, all of this is in the treaty. we are counting on you, madam high representative, to remind the member states of this.
madam president, we are talking about a common european security and defence policy. the terms are already distorted. it is, in fact, a shared defence and security policy - the report implies this - with nato and america. the report calls for the european authorities to take defence matters seriously in the run-up to the june summit. but what is the point of wanting a common defence policy when our geopolitical options are decided elsewhere? european defence policy has become that of the united states, it is no longer that of the european citizens in its common dimension. the real french patriots are currently rejecting this european security policy, which is a policy of european insecurity and chaos.
madam president, the report on the european security and defence policy calls for the uniformity of the foreign policy positions of the european countries. no effective common foreign policy has been established. the european countries each have their own history with a capital h, their own geography, and therefore a different perception of interests and a different understanding of the world. therefore, such a foreign policy needs an external federator, as general de gaulle prophesied, which explains the mention of nato in this report. the irresponsible and belligerent positions of this parliament show us how disastrous a european army would be. who would control such an army and for what interests? can we reasonably think of sending our french soldiers to be killed in a war if my people are against it? we can die for our country, but we cannot die for the brussels commission. can we reasonably imagine that a nuclear power such as my country, france, would delegate this responsibility to irresponsible technocrats? delegating the spirit of defence is to kill the reason for the existence of nations and france will never accept this. the rapporteur, mr president, has asked for a blue card. madam president, mr philippot, grandiloquence is one thing, precision is another. i would simply ask you, since we are discussing a specific report today, to which chapter of that report do you refer when you speak of a 'european army', since, of the 56 articles in that report, that term is not mentioned anywhere?
answer is "blue cardboard". when we talk about common defence and if we listen carefully to each other's speeches, to the very concrete and precise proposals for a european army that have recently come from the european institutions, you know very well that this project is in the pipeline. it was fortunately rejected at the beginning of european construction, with the european development fund in 1954, and i fear that it will return today, to the great misfortune of the peoples of europe.
madam president, this report is concerned with the lack of mutual understanding and solidarity among the countries of the european union in the field of defence. but the modest nature of military operations under the common security and defence policy is only a reflection of the profound divergences of interests between the various member states. the idea of a federated european army is therefore a dream that only the pro-european minds can believe to be a foreboding one. the divisions over the war in iraq or even the intervention in libya are evidence of this. in addition, this sharing is driven by cuts in national defense budgets. it is questionable whether brussels is not imposing austerity to promote the european army and thus satisfy the bellicose attitude of mr juncker, whose ideas have not thawed since the end of the cold war. the only interests which a european army would serve are those of external federalism, denounced in his time by general de gaulle, i mean the united states and its armed wing, nato. it is also scandalous that this report proposes to finance military interventions from the budget of the european union, whereas this is clearly prohibited by article 41 (2) of the treaty on european union. this report is therefore the work of europeans who believe that there can be no salvation outside the union. in the face of these desires, it is urgently necessary to reduce the share of france's defence budget to 2% of gdp and to promote bilateral, targeted and temporary cooperation as it should.
madam president, madam high representative, ladies and gentlemen, this report by arnaud danjean is in fact encouraging the dispossession of our sovereignty in favour of a european army. whether or not the term is used, that is the objective. european security must, on the contrary, be based on the willingness of states to develop their own armed forces. france, the united kingdom and italy are still making a special effort. they must maintain this effort, even increase it, especially in the case of france, whose army is being destabilized year after year. when germany announces that it is going to make a special effort to defend itself, i can only welcome it, because it is unacceptable that europeans should let down their guard in the face of asia and the islamic world, which are becoming increasingly militarized in both quantity and quality. but european defence must not consist in erecting a new wall to the east of the union against russia, nor must it aim at the creation of a transatlantic army to replace the european armies. any other logic will make the european union not a promise of peace but a promise of war. the rapporteur. madam president, madam high representative, i would like to say that the words you have just spoken on the practical aspect of what should inspire us are perfectly in line with the philosophy of the report i have presented and that my colleagues - i thank them - have been pleased to add to their contributions. i think that the debate today has shown this quite clearly, in the positive reception it has received. the question we have to answer today is how do we do better together in the face of security challenges that are of unprecedented scale and complexity? let me say that those of us who have been very ideological in our approach, with attitudes which are sometimes totally unrealistic in relation to what is in this text, are wrong. to those who fear or hope for a european army, for example - we have heard about it today - i say that they are misguided in their debate. that is not the purpose of this report and this discussion, nor even of the council meeting in june. the point is how we as a group of 28 can face challenges. because these are challenges that no member state can meet alone. it's as simple as that. the answers are, indeed, first in the treaty. i appreciate the fact that you're using your institutional and political influence to push this philosophy, which is a pragmatic philosophy, of flexibility. that's what we need today. we can't do everything with 28. we may not have to do everything together in terms of security and defence because the reality in europe is heterogeneous. but we must, as a political body, make sure that those who want to do more and go further in terms of the integration of defence policy can do so. i think that the paths you propose and those we propose are perfectly compatible, complementary, and go in the same direction. i hope that they will be heard by the member states.
