mr president, any strengthening of legislation against money laundering and the financing of terrorism is, a priori, in the right direction. however, such strengthening must not entail sacrificing the sovereignty of the member states, since it is the member states that are best placed to combat these mafia networks effectively. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of the environment. we must not be naive, money laundering and terrorist financing networks take advantage of the absence of borders between member states. the free movement of capital and persons and the freedom of establishment in the 27 countries have created a legal environment favourable to the development of these criminal activities. in the absence of increased police and judicial cooperation between the member states, the application of the schengen agreement and the principles of free movement should therefore be suspended.
mr president, this text amends the community regulation of 29 may 2000 on insolvency proceedings. it is designed to protect creditors in cases where the insolvency of a company is of a cross-border nature. it has the merit of conferring jurisdiction on the courts of the member state in which the debtor undertaking has its principal centre of interests. the reality of the place of business of the company is thus used as a criterion for the attribution of jurisdiction, which makes it possible to exclude forum shopping, that is to say the abusive search by cross-border debtors for the most favourable national jurisdiction. however, this provision has the disadvantage of overly restricting the possibility for the creditor to bring secondary proceedings before the courts of his own state where the debtor has assets in that state. that's why i'm hostile to it.

mr president, allow me to congratulate you for a minute and to cry out in anger. i congratulate you because i too want to welcome the european commission's proposal for a programme. finally, it is a recognition of the scale of the migration phenomenon in europe. it's about time! for the past five years, there have been a series of terrible shipwrecks in the mediterranean. it's about time! we have long been vigorously denouncing the failure of the dublin system. it's about time! because we have been advocating for years for a revision of the blue card directive. this awareness, which comes late, is a awareness which has the merit of existing and, above all, of proposing actions, of formulating innovative and - i want to emphasize this here - courageous pragmatic proposals. i am also angry because i too want to denounce the scandalous reactions of certain member states, which are a bit like the two-faced janus, the roman god with two faces, who on the one hand recognize in their states, through sympathetic speeches, the need for solidarity and who on the other hand, with the other face, as soon as a courageous solution such as that proposed in this programme is put on the table, directly oppose it, like certain heads of government whom i will not name. this strategy paper is a real breakthrough. i ask the council to encourage the member states to turn words into action, to act and to translate these proposals into action. at the same time, we should all express european solidarity, with long-term measures to address the causes, as was very appropriately mentioned this morning.
commissioner, you have presented a european programme on migration and this proposal has at least one merit, namely that it exists. the programme contains some good proposals - it has been said - namely the tripling of the financial resources for triton and poseidon, the financing of the eu navfor med operation, the strengthening of partnerships, a more robust return policy. all this is in the right direction, but i am very sceptical about your proposal to relocate asylum seekers. my country, france, is one of the five countries which already receive 75% of asylum seekers. in fact, we welcome almost 300,000 additional migrants every year. we are also providing important resources within the framework of the frontex agency. so can we really decide on a distribution mechanism based on accounting terms without taking into account our traditions? i would like to ask for clarification, commissioner. when do you plan to start this mechanism? under what conditions will the allocation be decided, for example, when fingerprints are taken on board vessels? and by whom? under what authority? i agree with you, commissioner, that solidarity should not be just a word but should be translated into action. but the solution is not to be found in a system of distribution which is, by definition, rigid and which, on the contrary, risks favouring or encouraging migratory pressure and depriving the states of a vital part of their sovereignty.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, faced with the disaster of its immigration policy and its inability to prevent the flood of migrants, the european union is proposing a plan that only it could have devised: to distribute illegal immigrants among the various european countries and to call for a common asylum system. it is out of the question for the commissioners to decide for the french how many illegal immigrants they must accept on their soil. it is also clear that this organized management of illegal immigration will have a normalising effect and create an additional air demand. as a result, there will unfortunately be more illegal immigrants, more shipwrecks and more deaths at sea. the european union has also invented a justification for its favourable position on more immigration: immigration would be good for growth! it's amazing you admit, with all your shame, that your aim is to provide cheap labour in order to weigh down the wages of all workers in europe, and this against the will of the people. it is therefore a further attack on the sovereignty of our country, an affront to the french people, the majority of whom are opposed to immigration, and a way of increasing the problem rather than solving it. as usual, the european union's desire to expand its powers will lead to disastrous results.
mr president, when the commission proposes refugee quotas, providing the crisis with a european response, it is the member states who, motivated by their selfishness, torpedo this solution. so is there any point in discussing this european programme on migration, when the member states have already agreed on a military operation? will targeting the ships stop the flow of migrants fleeing war and poverty? no, you can't! is this the way to deal with the traffickers? no, you can't! will we have settled the matter, even provisionally? no, you can't! we will add chaos to chaos and suffering to suffering. have we lost both our heads and our hearts? by refusing even the minimum of european solidarity, the member states are betraying europe. when françois hollande and manuel valls oppose solidarity in europe, i feel an irrepressible sense of shame and anger at seeing europe and its values trampled underfoot.
mr president, i would like to focus my speech on the most immediate and spectacular response to this difficult issue of migration, namely the naval military operation in the mediterranean which has just been launched. this is very unusual of me, but i will express the deepest reservations and the deepest doubts about this operation. i fear that the stated ambitions are excessively difficult to achieve. at best, it seems to me, this device will have perhaps - perhaps - a deterrent effect. and yet... it will be extremely difficult, legally and operationally, to really tackle the smuggling and trafficking networks. the martial language we have been fed for weeks is quite understandable in this difficult situation, but i think it is hard to really cover the reality of the operational and legal constraints we are going to face. beyond the grand declarations of martial law, much more thorough work must be undertaken with and towards the african countries from which and through which the majority of these waves of migration come. we have interlocutors in those countries, we have points of reference, including in the field of security, and i think that is where we must work first, because when we tackle the problem on the shores of the mediterranean, it is already too late.
mr president, the least we can say is that the european commission has not left anyone indifferent to its programme on migration: some lament its lack of ambition, others cry out the opposite. but all agree that the task was not easy. how can we propose an ambitious and innovative programme when the current context seems to call more for minimalist recipes and calculations through the narrow end of the electoral lens? the european council gave us a sad example of this last april. i therefore welcome the commission's position, which has been translated into action. there is no discourse on migration without the term "solidarity", but its application remained in the virtual field. the emergency distribution mechanisms proposed by the commission aim to break this taboo by giving substance to solidarity both between member states and with third countries. of course, the operational details are still to be defined, but this is a step in the right direction, which parliament has been calling for for many years. parliament also called for a comprehensive approach to migration, and that is what we are being asked to do: to define the entire migration path from the country of origin to the country of destination and then on to the country of transit. this is consistent with our analysis, which wants to look at migration in the short, medium and long term. finally, i would like to make two suggestions to the commission: first, continue your work of teaching and explaining the proposals, to avoid fruitless confusion which is more to do with sensational speeches of fear than with reason, and secondly, hold on!
mr president, i would like to welcome the commission and congratulate it on its commitment. this is a genuinely european action, which commits our governments to working together. that said, frontex will play a very important role, and i would like to ask you, commissioner, and also you, madam president, why poland has still not signed the headquarters agreement, when frontex has been based in warsaw since 2004. if we want to be fully operational and welcome staff who are not necessarily polish at frontex, it seems to me that we need to get this headquarters agreement signed. i thank you for your replies and for the diligence you will show in this matter.
in writing. the masters of the european union have taken off their masks in the face of the terrifying mediterranean graveyard. we knew the incompetence of these institutions in the matter of immigration because they were unable to control and contain the ever-growing flows. the perfidy of the commission and the council is now becoming apparent, which want to accelerate the flood of migration at the expense of the lives of millions of men, women and children whom you are trying to make believe that europe is an eldorado open to all. instead of adopting the australian method of returning migrants, which has proved to be effective and humane, you are misguided into a quota policy which will only cover a tiny fraction of the migration flows and will fill the pockets of smugglers and mafias thriving on this new system of human trafficking. what a paradox that the european union, which boasts of being at the forefront of risk assessment, fails to take account of the dramatic and irreversible consequences of a blatant call for mass immigration into europe: insecurity, poverty, overpopulation, uncontrolled social spending and the destruction of the national cohesion and cultural unity of the european nations. your irresponsibility is a violation of the people.
in writing. the european agenda on migration is an undeniable first step towards the establishment of a comprehensive european union migration policy. this strategy emphasises cooperation with countries of origin and transit as well as the strengthening of the common european asylum system. the union and its member states can no longer allow people to risk their lives to seek asylum. in order to avoid shipwrecks, it was necessary to propose a military naval operation under the auspices of the un in the mediterranean to dismantle smuggling networks and combat the smuggling of migrants. in parallel, legal and safe pathways for applicants to the union must also be developed. embassies, consulates, the establishment of a european humanitarian visa system, the processing of asylum applications directly in third countries are all possible solutions. the union could also charter its own boats to bring refugees and asylum seekers safely to our continent. i therefore welcome the commission's proposal to achieve a fairer distribution of refugees and asylum seekers among the member states, although the proposals on legal migration are lacking in ambition.

mr president, the fight against money laundering and, therefore, against organised crime and terrorism, yes! but do you seriously believe for one moment that organized crime and terrorism run through the ordinary circuits of banks? the perverse effect of this system is that in my own country, france, under the influence of state regulation, every banker has been turned into a spy, a surveillance officer, a whistle-blower of his clients. for example, after having paid off a personal debt of €10,000 some time ago, which was perfectly in my bank account, i had to explain myself to my banker, who called me, finding this transaction abnormal and asking me what i was doing with my money. i said that at my age, young mistresses are more expensive than they used to be. that was inaccurate, i'm a faithful husband to his wife. that answer didn't seem satisfactory. the circuit is then set in motion: tracfin is informed, the financial brigade investigates... these are absolutely perverse effects of this legislation. the same is true of the kredietbank in brussels, the european parliament's agency, where even your european passport is not enough to prove your domicile! this is financial terrorism.
in writing. ‒ this draft resolution aims to update the third anti-money laundering directive. this directive applies a risk-based approach and aims to strengthen the european union's defenses against money laundering and terrorist financing. to this end, the council and parliament have introduced various amendments to safeguard the integrity and stability of the financial system. the commission would be responsible for coordinating the risk assessment of money laundering and terrorist financing. the directive provides in particular for the provision of beneficial ownership information in respect of companies. each member state could consult this information. the text provides in particular for the introduction of maximum administrative pecuniary sanctions. i believe that these measures are necessary to combat this ferocious problem. i therefore voted in favour of the text.
in writing. ‒ i supported the directive on the fight against money laundering because it is necessary to adapt the european legal framework for the supervision of financial circuits and to ensure greater transparency in their operation. the aim is to oblige member states to keep central registers accessible to the competent authorities (financial intelligence units, banks) or to organisations and persons with a legitimate interest (investigative journalists). the text also extends the scope of application of the natural and legal persons concerned by lowering the threshold to eur 10 000 for cash payments, which will have to be subject to special supervision. the directive also provides for financial penalties of a minimum threshold of eur 1 million or eur 5 million if the infringement involves banks or financial entities. the commission will be responsible for coordinating the assessment of money laundering and terrorist financing risks affecting the internal market. i voted for this directive because we need to adopt clear rules to strengthen our control over illegal money laundering activities which benefit organised crime and terrorism.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this text is to prevent the financial system from being used for money laundering and terrorist financing. it seems to me to be a step in the right direction and a good thing, in that money laundering and the financing of terrorism are common sense objectives which we must fight against with the utmost firmness. the changes proposed in this text, made necessary by the changing nature of terrorist financing and money laundering, seem to me appropriate and that is why i am voting for this text.
in writing. ‒ we need strong european legislation to combat money laundering. this will enable us, among other things, to combat the financing of terrorism. this legislation is the result of a compromise between security and privacy. in the fight against terrorism and money laundering, we must have a european response. greater transparency in this area will help to achieve this. i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the adoption of the recommendations of krisjanis karins and judith sargentini and timothy kirkhope and peter simon on the prevention of the use of the financial system for money laundering and terrorist financing. by requiring member states to keep information on beneficial owners of legal persons and trusts in a centralised register, by harmonising competences across borders within the union, both between member states and between their financial intelligence units, and by providing for a european analysis of terrorist financing to be carried out by the commission, the european union is embarking on an ambitious project which represents a major step forward in the transparency of access to beneficial owners information. the union will undoubtedly be at the forefront of the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing in the coming years.
in writing. ‒ i have taken a position in favour of this directive to combat money laundering, which is used in particular to finance terrorism. the text is the result of a compromise between parliament and the council and is designed to strengthen the integrity and soundness of the european financial system. for example, gambling is regulated and providers must exercise due diligence for transactions of €2,000 or more; the text is realistic, however, since it leaves a margin of manoeuvre to the member states, which would be allowed to exempt these services, with the exception of casinos, from certain obligations in limited and justified circumstances. i also support the approach developed by the directive which is based on an assessment of the risks, which would be assessed by the commission for those which could affect the internal market. i would nevertheless criticise the council's position which makes no distinction between those who hold or have held important posts in the national territory or abroad.
in writing. ‒ the aim of this report is to revise directive 2005/60/ec with a view to strengthening the rules applicable in the context of the internal market and preventing the misuse of the european financial system for criminal purposes. i also voted in favour of this text, considering that in the current context of the terrorist threat, financial transfers must be made more transparent and better controlled in order to avoid money laundering that allows terrorist networks and activities to be financed.
in writing. parliament endorses the commission's proposal to revise the anti-money laundering directive at second reading. as criminal organisations are always finding new ways to circumvent the rules, it is necessary to change our legislation. this is all the more important as money laundering is a source of funding for terrorism and the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction. i have long called for increased resources to prevent the financing of terrorist activities. the adoption of this directive is one of those means, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the total amount of money laundered represents 5% of global gdp each year. the european parliament has called for stricter rules on money laundering to combat tax evasion and terrorist financing. fraudsters will no longer be able to use the anonymity of offshore companies and accounts to hide their financial transactions. the owners of businesses will now have to be registered in central registers kept by the member states. these registers will be accessible to the competent authorities and their financial intelligence units, as well as to persons with a 'legitimate interest' such as journalists. these provisions place the european union at the forefront of the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this debate because i am in principle in favour of any progress in the repressive direction of the relentless fight against terrorism.
in writing. ‒ on wednesday 20 may, i voted in favour of a new directive to strengthen the eu's rules against money laundering and terrorist financing. the actual owners of companies will now have to be registered in the central registers of eu countries, which are open to both the authorities and to persons with a 'legitimate interest', such as investigative journalists. this is the first time that a directive will oblige member states to keep such central registers. meps also approved a regulation on 'transfers of funds', which aims to improve the traceability of payers and beneficiaries and their assets. the vote is a strong signal from the european parliament against tax evasion and the financing of terrorism. the eradication of such illegal practices requires strong political will and cooperation at all levels. both money laundering and terrorist financing constitute obstacles to the smooth functioning, stability of the financial system and the well-being of society.
in writing. ‒ every year, money laundering accounts for 2 to 5% of global gdp. money laundering, terrorist financing and organised crime are major problems that require a european response. in this context, it is therefore crucial to advocate the adoption of clear rules that strengthen the vigilance of all the professionals concerned and allow for greater financial transparency. financial transparency is an indispensable tool in the effective fight against money laundering. that is why i supported this directive on money laundering. it obliges member states, for the first time, to keep central registers containing information on the beneficial owners of companies and trusts. the commission had not considered these registers, but parliament had advocated their introduction to put an end to the anonymity of offshore companies and accounts used by fraudsters to conceal their financial transactions. the conditions for access to this register are not as ambitious as we had advocated, but it is a first step that must be encouraged. parliament will remain vigilant to continue to defend the widest possible access to information.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the revised directive on the prevention of the use of the financial system for the purpose of money laundering and terrorist financing. the fight against terrorist threats must be a priority. cutting off the supply of funds is therefore an essential weapon in the fight that our democracies must wage against criminal organizations and terrorist groups. this directive provides that information on beneficial owners is to be kept in a central register maintained by each member state. access to information is not restricted to the competent authorities but to any person or organisation that can demonstrate a legitimate interest in accessing such information. in my view, this decision meets two demands of the citizens: greater transparency and security.

in writing. ‒ these new anti-money laundering rules make it possible to make progress in the disclosure of the real owners of companies and entities. the new directive requires that central registers be set up in all eu countries listing the ultimate owners of companies. the idea is that tax authorities, especially tax authorities, can have reliable information that allows them to see who owns what and thus be able to estimate the wealth of certain individuals or to see precisely between whom suspicious transactions are made. such registers should also be accessible to persons with a 'legitimate interest', such as investigative journalists. this is a real step forward, especially since some european countries, including france, have announced their intention to make these registers public. i therefore supported this text and call for rapid implementation and the utmost transparency. i regret, however, that trusts (complex structures of ownership of companies or entities) will benefit from a specific regime exempting them from these rules: the fight against money laundering and tax evasion must apply to everyone and even more so to those who try to hide their assets and transactions through these opaque structures.

in writing. ‒ the draft regulation of the european parliament and of the council amends the community regulation of 29 may 2000 on insolvency proceedings. it is designed to protect creditors against insolvency in crossborder transactions. this text assigns jurisdiction to the member state in which the debtor undertaking has its principal centre of interests in order to combat the abusive search for the most favourable national court. on the contrary, the text deprives the creditor of the possibility of initiating secondary proceedings before the courts of his own state where the debtor has property there. as a defender of the rule of law, i finally voted against this text.

in writing. ‒ this text amends the community regulation of 29 may 2000 on insolvency proceedings. it is designed to protect creditors in cases where the insolvency of a company is of a cross-border nature. it has the merit of conferring jurisdiction on the courts of the member state in which the debtor undertaking has its principal centre of interests. the reality of the place of business of the company is thus used as a criterion for the attribution of jurisdiction, which makes it possible to exclude forum shopping, that is to say the abusive search by cross-border debtors for the most favourable national jurisdiction. however, this provision has the disadvantage of overly restricting the possibility for the creditor to bring secondary proceedings before the courts of his own state, provided that the debtor has assets in that state. it is therefore a clear attack on national sovereignty and therefore out of the question for me to support it. despite the positive aspects of the report, i am voting against it in order to defend the sovereignty of the states.

in writing. ‒ this report concerns the european self-certification mechanism for importers of certain ores and metals originating in conflict or high-risk areas. this text attempts to address the problem of illegal mining in conflict zones. importers of these metals or ores can obtain a responsible importer certificate based on an oecd guide to the matter. the companies concerned must keep all traceability elements showing that they are not buying from illegal mines. the checks are carried out by the member states each year and the rules relating to infringements are made by the states which may decide to withdraw the certificate of responsible importer. i abstained on this report to avoid the resale of minerals extracted from illegal areas, while expressing reservations about the desire of some to impose our european values on all countries of the world. i think that the scope of the legislation should be extended to other metals and that much more stringent measures should be taken, particularly for marketing companies.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of a report which, in my view, lays the foundations for an effective and realistic system and puts an end to the financing of conflicts by the exploitation of conflict minerals by the belligerents. by making traceability of minerals mandatory for key players in the industry, the purity of imported minerals is ensured. the support to be given to european smes in implementing this traceability makes this gradual approach operational. the award of the conflict-free label must be the consecration of a transparent and peace-making system. in three years' time it will be time to evaluate the operation of this system and, why not, to increase the obligations and the number of ores covered by this legislation if the applicability of the process is demonstrated. for the time being, we can be pleased that we have opted for an ambitious line which represents a great step forward in preventing armed conflict linked to minerals.
in writing. ‒ i preferred to abstain on this report which provides for the establishment of a self-certification mechanism for importers of certain minerals and metals originating in conflict or high-risk areas. this procedure will certainly help to limit as far as possible what is commonly called the trafficking in blood diamonds and other precious metals obtained illegally or by violence. the european mechanism would build on the relevant oecd standards that allow metal importers to obtain a responsible importer certificate, in particular if they fulfil due diligence obligations in their supply chain. the traceability of imported metals should be ensured and the activities of the importer verified by an importing third party body, while member states will be responsible for verifying the application of the regulations and, where appropriate, taking corrective action in the event of an infringement. however, the measures as provided for in the text will lead to unilateral sanctions on european companies by increasing the processing costs of certain metals, even though competing companies, especially asian ones, will certainly not have to submit to such constraints.
in writing. ‒ the present report proposes to set up a european self-certification mechanism for importers of certain minerals in order to break the link between mining and trade in minerals, on the one hand, and the financing of armed conflict, on the other. the report also aims to support the development of a european market for responsibly mined conflict minerals and to improve the ability of operators throughout the supply chain to comply with due diligence obligations. i believe that in such a complex matter it is necessary to propose a fair and realistic system to achieve the objectives envisaged, and i have therefore decided to support the establishment of a compulsory system upstream for ore importers and smelters and refiners, and a voluntary system downstream for small and mediumsized enterprises. i support the objectives of this report but consider that a vote in plenary in favour of a mandatory system of traceability and certification throughout the supply chain, i.e. over 880,000 companies, will be difficult to implement, so i decided not to block the forthcoming discussions with the council and therefore abstained on this text.

in writing. ‒ i abstained on the european mechanism for self-certification of importers of certain minerals and metals from conflict zones. i am of course in favour of not using minerals extracted from conflict zones to finance the belligerents. this is particularly the case in the democratic republic of congo and the great lakes region. europe accounts for 35% of world trade in the minerals concerned (gold, tin, tantalum, tungsten). nearly 900 000 companies, many of them smes, are involved in this trade. under the mechanism proposed by the european commission, importers of these metals create responsible importer certificates themselves, i.e. self-certify. however, the mechanism, as amended by the european parliament, should oblige european companies to get involved in checking that their supply chain is not corrupted by 'blood minerals'. so this is good news, but it is not yet the final agreement on legislation and it is clear that this mechanism is essentially based on the goodwill of importers.
in writing. in writing. ‒ parliament voted in favour of a european self-certification mechanism for importers of minerals and metals from conflict or high-risk areas. beyond the unanimously shared objective of cutting off the sources of funding for armed groups, there is a duty of realism which we owe to the citizens of europe. it is impossible to propose a system of compulsory self-certification for the whole production chain. how can an sme be sure that the ore it uses to make its product does not come from a conflict zone? i am of the opinion that, like the consumer who is not responsible for the manufacturing process of the clothing he wears, companies which use minerals cannot be fully informed of their origin. this is why i support a gradual but more effective approach: a mandatory system for the first actors in the chain (melting/refining plants and importers) and the creation of a label for the other actors in the chain in order to create a responsible supply system. unfortunately, the position of parliament is unrealistic. i fear that the effects will be neutralized by excessive control, which will be contrary to the interests of the local populations.

in writing. ‒ i abstained on the final vote on my colleague iuliu winkler's report following a proposal by the european commission to set up a voluntary european self-certification mechanism for importers of tin, tantalum, tungsten, their ores and gold from conflict or high-risk areas. it is essential to end all funding of armed groups through trade in these four minerals, to fight corruption and to ensure effective development assistance; i therefore advocated an approach that goes beyond the original proposal of the european commission. i have, for example, supported the proposal to make due diligence compulsory for the first actors in the chain. it is regrettable, however, that the final text is not operational because of the demagogy displayed by the left. it sets objectives and instruments which are not applicable in practice and contains a number of contradictions which will help to put parliament in a bad position in future negotiations with the council and the commission. i regret that the sensationalist and media temptations of some people are at the expense of an effective fight against the financing of armed groups.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a european self-certification mechanism, under supply chain due diligence, for importers of minerals from conflict zones. in this vote we have called for binding legislation to be adopted on the traceability of the use of four minerals: tin, tantalum, tungsten and gold, which have been mined in countries affected by war for several years. future legislation should therefore allow for systematic certification of these minerals by the european union to ensure that they do not in any way fuel conflict and human rights violations in conflict zones, such as rape, regularly used in some countries as a weapon of war. we are well aware that this binding legislation could place a burden, particularly financial, on some european companies, but the moral and human stakes are too great for the european union and the european parliament to remain passive on this issue.
in writing. ‒ this text is a significant step forward in regulating the import of minerals from conflict zones, particularly the great lakes area. these rare minerals, tin, tantalum, tungsten and gold, must no longer be used to finance the many guerrillas and paramilitary groups in the region, which are guilty of violent extortion, act with impunity and often force the local population to participate in the extraction. europe, which is one of the main markets for consumer electronics (including mobile phones and plasma displays) using these minerals, could not sit idly by and lag behind. the united states has been grappling with the problem since 2010. that is why i supported this text which goes much further than the commission's proposals by imposing a compulsory system of mineral certification. the 880 000 european companies using these metals will therefore have to participate in a traceability system along the entire supply chain, compared with only 19 previously. in this way we will ensure that these conflict minerals do not end up in our products and do not finance the criminal and heinous abuses of these armed groups.
in writing. this legislation aims to regulate the extraction by european companies of certain minerals and gold which play a key role in financing certain armed groups or security forces in conflict zones such as the great lakes region. a certification is therefore proposed. of course, the multinationals did not want it to be mandatory but only optional. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the conclusion of the agreement on the basis of the information provided by the member states. even the american version of this legislation, on which the commission and the rapporteur rely, is binding. finally, my group's amendments were passed. the text is ambitious, i vote for it.
in writing. ‒ the aim of this text is to restrict and provide a precise framework for the trade in minerals in areas of war or violent conflict or in the future. many factional groups, bandits and perhaps, in the future, islamists, are able to obtain weapons and ammunition through the exploitation of these minerals, known as "blood". this is particularly the case in the great lakes region of africa. however, while one cannot help but be appalled by this situation, the commission's proposal is not satisfactory in this case, since it retains a self-certification mechanism for companies that would import metals into europe. fortunately, parliament has succeeded in amending this text so that companies must check that their supply chain is not tainted by blood minerals. this text, although it is intended with a good intention, is not satisfactory enough for me to vote for it. so i refrained.
in writing. this european self-certification mechanism for responsible importers of tin, tungsten, ores and gold from high-risk conflict zones is the very example of an administrative standard that is binding on industry and probably useless in effect. this mechanism does not seem to be adequate to address the problems raised in this report. how can we think that self-certification, i.e. the award of a label by the company itself and with a completely hypothetical control by the administrative authorities, can have any interest? this is one of the many numbers of the eu institutions to raise awareness of the tragic events taking place in conflict zones, and which highlights their total impotence. while the report's intention to avoid the resale of these minerals is commendable, it again shows the european institutions' desire to impose their "values" on the whole world. it is up to the member states to take responsibility and adopt real coercive measures. i therefore decided to abstain on that text.
in writing. the european commission's initial proposal was to set up a european self-certification mechanism for importers of tin, tantalum, tungsten, their ores and gold originating in conflict or high-risk areas. but the import of these minerals, which are found in many of our everyday objects, has dramatic consequences in importing countries that are too often ignored in our own. self-certification is far from sufficient because it will leave the industry in too comfortable a position in the face of the massacres perpetrated daily around the world for the extraction of these minerals. that is why i co-signed amendments to substantially strengthen this proposal by creating a mandatory monitoring mechanism for supply chains, from producers to importers of these minerals. the resolution also calls for the establishment of a european union-wide system of controls on the sale of minerals. since these amendments were adopted in plenary, i decided to vote in favour of this very ambitious report, which still needs to be agreed with the council.
in writing. ‒ this text attempts to address the problem of rare earths being illegally exploited in conflict zones and thus contributing to the conflict. the project chosen is a self-certification mechanism for enterprises, based on an oecd guide. importers shall self-certify by fulfilling due diligence obligations in their supply chain. they must keep in their possession traceability evidence that they are not buying from illegal mines. the procedures and activities of the importer shall be verified by an independent third party. the member states will be responsible for the verification and enforcement of the regulation. in principle, taking measures to avoid financing conflicts is a good idea. unfortunately, the mechanism chosen, self-certification, is ineffective on the ground and will only penalise european companies. it is clear that minerals will leave conflict zones to be processed by companies in less-friendly countries than those in the eu and thus return to the soil of eu states in the form of finished products. i refuse to give my consent to this mechanism, which i strongly doubt, and i prefer to abstain.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. the objective of the report is to support the development of a market in the union for responsibly sourced conflict minerals and to improve the capacity of actors in the supply chain to comply with the duty of care. this vote is a mess. some might welcome the few amendments that have been passed by a small majority, but they are not backed up by a structure that allows them to be applied. the commission and the council being closed to any progress on the commission's proposal, parliament could have been in a strong position. a comprehensive approach would have been required, with means to combat corruption, manage development aid and to link this to an instrument whose constraint could have been graduated over time for the 880 000 european companies. the european parliament could have taken a major action; with this vote he has only made an unheard-of appeal.
in writing. ‒ i welcome today's vote to end the sale of minerals (gold, diamonds, tantalum, tin, copper) to armed groups and to introduce a duty of care for all importing companies in the european union. these raw materials are used every day in the construction of various technologies (mobiles, tablets, etc.). however, their extraction affects the lives of hundreds of thousands of people. the commission's initial proposal was limited to the establishment of a non-binding european self-certification mechanism for only those companies directly importing raw materials up the supply chain. the scope of this mechanism would then have been very limited. with the support of civil society and citizens, left-wing parliamentarians and particularly socialists and democrats, we have succeeded in putting in place mandatory legislation for all companies in the supply chain. it is a victory over the european right, which wanted a discount mechanism. above all, it is a victory against the trafficking of 'blood minerals', against armed groups and for the establishment of a real european development policy.
in writing. ‒ the financing of armed groups through the trade in tin, tantalum, tungsten, their ores and gold must cease. in voting on this text, i wanted to support a realistic and progressive approach which would have made due diligence mandatory for the upstream supply chain, i.e. smelters, refiners and importers, and voluntary for the rest of the companies in the chain. that is why i abstained on the final vote because a mandatory approach across the whole chain, i.e. over 800 000 european companies, whether multinational or small or medium-sized enterprises (smes), seems difficult to apply and implement. a gradual approach, notably through the revision clause allowing for a gradual widening of the scope of the regulation, would have been preferable. i also wanted to ensure that the discussions and negotiations on this text could continue.
in writing. ‒ the trade in minerals such as gold, diamonds, tantalum, tin and copper fuels armed conflicts, especially in africa. to seize the mineral lands, armed gangs spread terror through crime and rape. the european commission's initial draft on trade in these 'blood minerals', published in march 2014, was limited to an optional mechanism for importers to self-certify, which was ridiculous in view of the s.thanks to a left in parliament, we were able to find a majority to put in place legislation that obliges european companies, or not, to indicate the origin of minerals throughout the supply chain. t. an important step forward in the fight against the financing of conflict in mining regions this victory was achieved despite the protests of a large part of the right and the extreme right, more concerned with serving the interests of a few firms than saving the populations who are victims of the violence of armed gangs. the same people who will refuse to take in migrants in danger even after refusing to tackle the causes of their exodus. i will .
in writing. ‒ the draft regulation lays down a commendable principle: that of not encouraging the financing of armed groups which participate in guerrilla and terrorist actions and aggravate civil and interethnic wars, particularly on the african continent. these conflicts also fuel the migratory flows of refugees seeking to escape massacres. we cannot therefore ignore this issue. however, this text will lead to economic sanctions being imposed unilaterally on european companies importing minerals from conflict zones. the new rules will increase the processing costs of certain metals, which will have a negative impact on the european steel industry. finally, before regulating in the name of morality, the european union would be wise to first control the use of its funds in certain areas. i therefore choose to abstain.
in writing. ‒ the exploitation of minerals in conflict zones has been denounced for many years and has been the subject of wide-ranging citizen mobilizations. the european union imports a large amount of these minerals (tin, tantalum, tungsten, gold, etc.). trade is often the cause of these conflicts. it is the source of massive corruption and fuels the financing of armed militias in these regions. these european companies are therefore largely complicit, directly or indirectly, in the crimes committed in these regions. at the time of the plenary vote, an alternative majority was available to extend the original legislative proposal to impose a transparency obligation and thus information on all companies in the supply chain. it may not seem enough, but it's a first step. the european parliament has adopted a position which will be submitted to the council. let us hope that this position will be maintained. allowing mineral wealth to be exploited for the benefit of the people is essential in many of the poorest countries. i hope that we can make some initial progress in this area. following...
in writing. ‒ this text concerns an amendment to annex iii to directive 2011/65/eu of the european parliament and of the council as regards an exemption for cadmium in general lighting and screen lighting applications. it provides for the delegated act to be rejected and updated in line with the technologies available in europe. i also consider that the key justification of the commission for granting the new specific exemption is that '[i]n quantum cadmium-free boxes do not yet exist' and therefore that this justification is clearly unfounded. i therefore voted in favour of this point.
in writing. ‒ the motion for a resolution deals with the prohibition of cadmium, a heavy metal which is dangerous to consumer health and the environment. the metal is still used in the manufacture of led screens and for lighting, thanks to an exemption valid until 30 june 2017. with the technological progress made, cadmium is no longer essential for the manufacture of certain led screens. the commission is also proposing to extend the exemption until 2017 to take account of technological developments and to incorporate the position of the european parliament. for all these reasons, i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which aims to ban the dangerous heavy metal cadmium. the text also calls on the commission to take account of the position of the members on the subject. the envi committee members wanted to draw the commission's attention to a problem which was already anticipated by the industry in this field. cadmium, which has recognised harmful effects on health and the environment, is already excluded from the manufacture of displays by two of the largest distributors on the market, samsung and nanoco, which have replaced it with 'quantum boxes', nanostructures of semiconductors without cadmium; only large american companies continue to endanger consumers by continuing to use cadmium. i welcome the fact that parliament is seeking to ban this product, but i ask the commission to respect the views of members on this matter.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this motion is to object to the adoption by the european commission of a commission delegated directive amending, for the purpose of adapting it to technical progress, annex iii to directive 2011/65/eu concerning an exemption for cadmium in general lighting and screen lighting applications. point 39 of the annex to the legislation on the restriction of the use of certain hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment provides for a derogation for cadmium for use in lighting or display systems, which expires on 1 july 2014, with the possibility of being extended if the progress of scientific and technical progress does not allow the substitution of this substance in electrical and electronic equipment by another product. the delegated directive adopted by the european commission extends the exemption provided for in point 39 until 30 june 2017, which, according to the assessments of experts and the progress of scientific and technical progress, is not justified, as significant developments have been observed regarding the availability of products using cadmium-free quantum box technology on the market. i therefore consider that such an exemption no longer applies and have voted in favour of the objection.
in writing. the european union has standards to limit the use of harmful substances in electrical and electronic equipment. however, exemptions may be granted where justified. this is the case for cadmium, which is used for lighting and for the illumination of television, tablet and computer screens. by means of a delegated act, the commission extended the exemptions for cadmium. however, it did not have sufficient information to support this extension. that is why i voted for this resolution, which calls on the commission to carry out a new evaluation.
in writing. ‒ a number of scientific studies have shown that cadmium, a heavy metal used in the screens of some lcd tvs and other electronic devices, poses high risks to human health. however, a range of new models of tv sets using cadmium-free quantum boxes are now available on the union market from leading retailers in the member states. the european parliament has therefore refused to extend the derogation which cadmium has hitherto enjoyed in lighting and illumination applications, as there was no other solution.

in writing. since 2013, the xylella fastidiosa bacterium has been wreaking havoc in the italian olive sector. the resolution calls for the eu to take action to prevent the spread of a plant health crisis in several sectors of european agriculture and horticulture. measures have already been taken to control the bacterium at local level in the puglia region, but a more global action plan is needed. the resolution calls for increased vigilance at customs when goods and travellers enter the union. the bacterium is transmitted by both the infected plants themselves and by insects. finally, i am glad that parliament is taking account of the threats to the livelihoods of the people in the affected areas by providing them with compensation.
in writing. ‒ the puglia region in southern italy has been suffering from an outbreak of xylella fastidiosa, a bacterium that affects olive trees, since 2013. already 10% of the olive groves in the province of lecce have been infected. carried by vector insects, this bacterium is already spreading to neighboring regions. a suspected case has even been reported near nice. the absence of treatment to treat the infected plants, the large number of species likely to be infected, and the likelihood of its spread in the european union, make this bacterium a very serious threat to agriculture. the european parliament therefore calls on the commission to take targeted measures to prevent further damage, such as the removal and destruction of listed host plants (citrus, olive, vine, plum, almond, tobacco, rose laurel, oak, thorn etc.) within a radius of 100 metres of any plant affected by xylella fastidiosa. in parallel, aid will have to be granted to farmers to replenish stocks of olive trees and other tree crops affected.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution which calls on the european commission to combat the spread of xylella fastidiosa in europe with determination. a number of measures are needed, including the strengthening of measures to prevent and control the spread of this disease, the development of effective means of control, compensation for producers, and strict control of imports of plant products. the fight against xylella will illustrate the eu's determination to protect its territory and agriculture from the growing health risks due to increased trade and insufficient plant protection resources.

in writing. xylella fastidiosa is a serious threat to the production of certain crops in southern europe, particularly olive trees. it is already causing significant damage in puglia, italy, and could have far-reaching economic, environmental and social consequences. no treatment is currently available to treat infected plants that remain infected throughout their life or wither rapidly. given the difficulty of containing the spread of xylella fastidiosa once it has infested a production area, it is necessary to give priority to import-oriented preventive measures. unfortunately, the commission is mainly focusing on internal measures to combat the epidemic, without taking into account the need to take measures to prevent the introduction of the disease into the european union from third countries. i therefore support this resolution which calls on the commission to take all necessary measures to limit the spread of the disease and on the member states to compensate producers for the eradication measures and the loss of income which would be associated with these measures.

in writing. parliament approved the decision to increase the pre-financing of the european social fund to support member states in their fight against youth unemployment. while this decision and the desire for rapid implementation are admirable, it does not solve the existing problems: the eu's budget deficit rules still prevent states from advancing funds, no impact analysis has been carried out and the overall cost of implementation is still unknown, the commission's monitoring of the scheme is still weak and there is still no guarantee that the promised funds will be released by the eu. the real weakness of the union is not a lack of pre-financing or speed, but the absence of a real employment policy, of support for the member states, the socioeconomic failure of european policies. the only solution, we can never say enough, is to protect our production from social dumping, to practice prudent protectionism at the level of each member state and to enable them to take the necessary measures to create jobs and to get out of the crisis. only then can we help the young people.
the agenda calls for the debate on the council statement on japanese whaling in the antarctic (2015/2702 ((rsp)).
madam president, japan is in breach of international law which has banned commercial whaling since 1986. it is continuing to hunt, claiming that it is a scientific hunt. his goal would be to study the age of whales to find out their reproductive rate. it's not credible, because you don't have to kill whales to study them, you can just observe them with satellite or underwater cameras. in fact, japan is laughing at us. he's a commercial fisherman. if he killed 11,000 whales between 1987 and 2013, it was to eat them. in fact, on march 31, 2014, the international court of justice ordered japan to stop whaling in the antarctic. japan has complied for a year, but it has just announced that it will kill 333 whales in the antarctic in 2015. it is urgent to put pressure on japan to comply with international law. whales must be protected, for they are, as cuban writer enrique serpa says, the embodiment of strength in the protean world of the sea.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the latest forecasts for economic growth and inflation in the european union appear to be converging. in april, the zone reportedly emerged from price deflation with zero inflation for a year, after four months of negative inflation. so, officially, everything's going for the best in the best of all worlds. of course, these figures hide a very different reality. firstly, these results are the result of a flood of financial means put in place to revive economic growth, whether through national budgets, the ecb's quantitative easing programmes or mr juncker's mythical plans. big money, small effect. secondly, this statistical swallow does not make the economic spring: + 0.4% in the union, + 0.6% for france in the first quarter of 2015, when the united kingdom was 2.80% in 2014. finally, i should like to remind you that this increase is also the consequence of a new method of calculating gdp imposed at union level, of which the national front is the only one to speak. criminal activities such as prostitution, drug trafficking and smuggling have been gradually integrated into a new method of calculating gdp, resulting in an artificial increase in economic growth. unfortunately, households are not experiencing the recovery that is being touted, either in employment or in the order books of smes. the accounting illusion and the communication plan of the governments and brussels cannot hide the reality. there is no real recovery and we are still in a structural recession.
