member of the commission.– madam president, i wish to thank everyone for their interest and contributions to this discussion. the commission takes good note of the elements and arguments put forward during these interesting debates. i will convey the substance and climate of the current discussion to my dear colleague arias cañete, who is responsible for energy. i am sure he will take into account all proposals ahead of the next steps.
author. madam president, itai dzamara is a young journalist, human rights activist, pacifist of the occupy africa unity square movement, and a sit-in organiser who has been calling since 2014 for the resignation of 91-year-old robert mugabe, who has been in power since the country's independence in 1980. two days before his disappearance, mr. dzamara participated in one of these peaceful demonstrations denouncing the economic and social situation in the country, and not without reason: unemployment approaching 80%, poverty exceeding 70%, hyperinflation that has ruined the country, chronic hunger, not to mention the ebola virus and sexual violence suffered by two thirds of women. in late 2014, as the crackdown was being re-initiated, the european union lifted sanctions against zimbabwe. i find it difficult to understand why, and why she has maintained these almost exclusively in respect of robert mugabe and his wife. there is no shortage of oligarchs close to power in the country. there is concern that the 234 million in development aid is benefiting them rather than the zimbabwean population. so, yes, we must do everything we can to find out what happened to itai dzamara, to protect his wife and his political friends. does resuming dialogue with that country at least serve any purpose in this context? that is the specific question i am asking you, commissioner.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the political and economic situation in zimbabwe is indeed very worrying, and we are entitled to demand an explanation for the disappearance of mr itai dzamara, which has now been going on for more than two months. this opponent of mugabe's dictatorial regime has been denouncing the catastrophic situation in his country. but how did we get here? before famine, poverty, aids, arbitrary land expropriation, and the racist murder of white farmers, zimbabwe was known as southern rhodesia. this former british colony was one of the most prosperous countries in black africa and was its wheat-growing barn. it is generally believed that it was the "agrarian reform" in particular that plunged the country into misery and chaos. this "reform" consisted in the ruthless expropriation, without compensation, of thousands of white farmers whom the country's authorities blamed for all the ills. if i am generally opposed to the right of interference, which the european union continues to abuse, how can i remain indifferent to this terrible ethnic cleansing? so, yes, let's demand answers about mr dzamara's disappearance but let's stop turning a blind eye to the state racism promoted by an old marxist dictator who dreams of becoming the monomotapa emperor.
author. mr president, the mass graves that have been opened in thailand in recent weeks have revealed to the world the plight of migrants in that country, interned in appalling conditions, dying of hunger, exhaustion or disease, when families cannot pay their ransom. the crackdown on trafficking has forced thousands of these unfortunates to take to the sea. on board were men, women, and children, mostly bangladeshis, and especially rohingya fleeing persecution in burma. they're rejected from all sides. unhcr says 25,000 people have fled since january, the largest influx to the region since the vietnam war. nearly 3,000 migrants have reached the coasts of malaysia, indonesia and thailand in recent days, and nearly 8,000 are believed to be lost at sea, seeking refuge. there, as here, the national authorities are evading their responsibilities. since 2013, the european union has spent only 325,000 euros on the rohingya refugee camp in thailand, a paltry sum. the union must do everything in its power to ensure that the rohingya, the damned of the earth, are no longer persecuted in their country, burma. so that they can no longer be prey to predators and can be welcomed in good conditions where they seek refuge.
in writing. ‒ this report begins by denying the sovereignty of the member states in matters of foreign policy, since it aims to make it impossible for any state to oppose the union's foreign policy. the rapporteur, arnaud danjean, wants to force all the member states into a community foreign policy, advocating common external interventions in which no state can refuse to participate. the idea behind this report is the necessary abandonment of national defence capabilities since most states are no longer able to maintain their own armed forces. the solution would therefore be to establish a single european defence, which i oppose, so that france can retain its sovereignty and its defence. i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this debate because i am in favour of greater coherence between external and internal policy instruments and of greater cooperation and coordination between member states, particularly in the fight against terrorism and organised crime, as well as in the areas of cybersecurity and immigration. this is the first step towards a european army...
in writing. ‒ the danjean report on the implementation of the common foreign and security policy is profoundly contrary not only to my convictions but also to the self-interest of each member state of the european union. firstly, the common foreign and security policy (cfsp) is an old europeanist whim that has repeatedly failed. i would remind you that france had already rejected the disastrous european defence community (edc) in 1954, which had basically the same objectives as the cfsp. the european union has therefore not yet understood in 60 years that our citizens do not want the mutual defence of the member states. moreover, such a policy would be ineffective and even dangerous, since the member states do not have the same interests in defence and foreign policy. the links between the cfsp and nato, from which i would like france to withdraw, are another reason why i am voting against this report.
in writing. ‒ this report on the implementation of the common security and defence policy merely reproduces the annual report which the council sent to the european parliament. the report uses ambiguous semantics in order to strive for uniformity in the foreign policy positions of the member states. the report also seeks to take advantage of austerity policies in the management of defence budgets to encourage the pooling of military resources at european level. the aim is to create a european military projection force under the authority of the commission. finally, the report clearly states the convergence of european defence objectives with those of nato. because the external security policy depends on the vital objectives of each member state, the european union is not the appropriate level to conduct an effective fight against the new threats that lurk on the european continent. that is why i voted against this text which calls for the stripping of national sovereignty.
in writing. ‒ the report on the implementation of the common security and defence policy highlights the need to adapt the european security and defence policy to current challenges. cyber defence, increased defence budget, the fight against terrorism and conflict resolution in the eu's neighbourhood are elements that need to be put in place. the international context requires rapid, effective and coordinated action by the member states. it is not isolated interventions that will change the situation but closer cooperation. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of mr danjean's report on the common security and defence policy, which i share in its recommendations, and i welcome its adoption in plenary. i am convinced that it is more than necessary to strengthen the means at the disposal of the european union to implement a credible and operational defence policy, capable of guaranteeing the strategic autonomy of our common space. this requires greater involvement of the member states on the ground and greater sharing of responsibilities. common defence capabilities must also be strengthened, in particular through the implementation of common programmes such as the european surveillance drone and governmental satellite telecommunications. finally, it is essential to concentrate our efforts on the european defence industry; the consolidation of the european defence technological industrial base is therefore indispensable. all these measures will have to enable us to adapt our efforts to the level of the threats we are facing in the european union today.
in writing. ‒ i strongly opposed mr danjean's report on the implementation of the common security and defence policy, which seeks to use the security and economic challenges facing the member states to justify a gradual stripping of their sovereignty in favour of a european army that will be nothing more than nato's lieutenant. the report deplores the fact that some member states are not taking part in the main military operations currently being conducted by the union, which raises doubts as to the freedom of states to take part in a given conflict. i am also concerned about the possibility, mentioned in the report, of introducing 'tax incentives' to force member states to 'military cooperation'; this proposal is nothing but the actual implementation of a tax blackmail. the increase in defence spending recently decided by the german government proves that the states have the possibility of investing in a large national army. the objective of solidarity in the field of defence must not be used to acknowledge the death of national defence.
in writing. ‒ this report takes stock of the common foreign and security policy in 2014, and in particular of the implementation of the common security and defence policy (csdp). it is a realistic constant of the gradual deterioration of the security environment in the neighbourhood in southern and eastern europe, in a context of the us refocusing on asia and unconcerted cuts in national defence budgets. it calls on the member states to implement and respect the conclusions of the european council of december 2013, which recognised the need to strengthen the csdp, to improve its effectiveness, visibility and impact, to increase capacity development and to strengthen the european defence industry. considering that the european council next june needs to critically assess the implementation of the decisions taken at the european council in december 2013 and present concrete measures in line with the commitments already made and not implemented, i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. the european union has a role to play in preserving international peace and security. this is both a matter of making our work visible on the international scene and of ensuring our own security. i voted in favour of this report, which once again underlines the inconsistency of a talk of self-interest which is not followed by concrete means of strengthening the common foreign and security policy. i regret the reduction in defence budgets in a number of member states. france cannot continue to provide the defence efforts that benefit its european partners on its own. this is all the more regrettable given that many threats, including terrorism, are at the doorstep, or even within, our territories.
in writing. ‒ the level of instability at europe's borders must encourage europe to provide a stronger response in terms of security and defence. it is vital that member states use defence tools more effectively and increase the pooling of their military forces. the external and internal security policies must also be more closely integrated. the security challenges facing the union cross borders and require better-adapted tools. i am thinking in particular of our counter-terrorism and cybersecurity strategies. finally, the union's action must focus on its immediate neighbourhood by developing civilian and military missions to manage crises and the aftermath of crises. the situation in the countries of the southern mediterranean and in the east, in ukraine, has shown that a security approach must go hand in hand with an approach to economic development.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on the implementation of the common security and defence policy. the report aims to revive the debate on the com munitization of defence and security policies. it lists the new threats to the european territory, in particular the terrorist risks which have been increasing for several years. the only purpose of this is to give credit to this report, which is not misleading. the union does not seem to understand that the maintenance of defence and security necessarily requires border management. no one can claim to be safe from an outside threat unless he manages the gates to his territory in the best possible way. the community will only have the effect of severely affecting national sovereignty, but it will not be able to solve the problems. the solution lies in increased cooperation between states, which have control over their foreign and defence policies.
in writing. ‒ i voted resolutely against this resolution, which provides for a genuine safeguarding of national sovereignty and freedom and excludes any possibility of establishing a strong and independent europe, built around free nations.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the danjean report on the implementation of the common security and defence policy. the report aims to relaunch cooperation between member states in the field of foreign and defence policy, in particular in view of the international environment and new threats such as cybersecurity, organised crime and terrorism. the main proposals in this report relate mainly to the financing of cfsp operations, the training of personnel, the sharing of resources and the development of a common strategy against new threats. however, this report once again ignores the responsibility of nato and the european union for the development of conflicts on europe's borders. in libya, the middle east and even ukraine, euro-atlanticists have played the role of sorcerers' apprentices by supporting extremists, islamists in the south, russophobes in the east. peace on europe's borders will only be restored if the european states pursue a policy independent of the united states and the gulf monarchies. giving more resources to the european "hawks" would only serve to spread war and despair to our borders.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. the aim is to combat terrorism and organised crime, strengthen cyber defence and tackle illegal immigration. the security environment in the european union and its neighbours to the east and south has reached a level of instability which must require the union to become a decisive and united actor. i am in particular in favour of strengthening the european defence agency and the industrial and technological base for european defence.
in writing. ‒ i would like to commend the quality of the annual report on the implementation of the common security and defence policy, drawn up by my colleague, arnaud danjean. this report comes at the right time: the multiplication of crises at the doorstep of europe and the prospect of the european council on 25 and 26 june devoted to security and defence matters required us to produce an objective analysis of the situation. a defence europe should be a priority for the european union, which, by the values it defends, has a duty to protect its citizens and a responsibility to intervene in conflict zones to reduce instability. unfortunately, we often feel that a 'defence europe' is just a pipe dream. this is the result of the lack of cooperation between member states, some being reluctant to provide the operational means, others the financial means, while security and stability are the problem of all. i hope that the next european council will present more ambitious conclusions for the future of the common security and defence policy by allowing the most advanced states to move forward through strengthened and more flexible cooperation.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to vote against the implementation of the common security and defence policy. this text begins by denying the sovereignty of the member states in matters of foreign policy, since it tends to make it impossible for a state to oppose the union's foreign policy. the rapporteur, arnaud danjean, therefore wants to force all the member states into a community foreign policy, advocating common external interventions in which no state can refuse to participate. finally, the idea behind this report is the necessary abandonment of national defence capabilities since most states are no longer able to maintain their own armed forces. the solution would therefore be to establish a single european defence, which i oppose, so that france can retain its sovereignty and its defence.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by my colleague arnaud danjean on the common defence and security policy. the report takes stock of the union's external policy situation and welcomes in particular the engagement of hr/vp frederica mogherini in defence matters, and also points to the need for greater military and strategic cooperation between the different member states in order to ensure the best possible defence of the european union. i welcome the fact that this report was adopted by a large majority.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's annual resolution on the eu's common security and defence policy (csdp). this resolution, drafted by my colleague, ump arnaud danjean, calls on the european union and its member states to assume more responsibilities immediately in the framework of the common security and defence policy, which must become a major instrument for ensuring the security of the european union and its environment, in the current context of unprecedented instability on the eu's borders. in this context of multiple crises, unprecedented since the launch of the european security and defence policy 16 years ago, member states must make rapid and substantial progress in equipping the eu with operational, industrial and capacity resources to prevent and manage international crises and to assert the eu's genuine strategic autonomy on the international stage.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on the implementation of the common security and defence policy. this report clearly aims at stripping the member states of their sovereignty and favours the creation of a european army subordinate to nato. paragraph 24 for example 'deplores the persistent problems of build-up of forces experienced during the launching of military missions; notes that with the exception of eutm mali, to which 23 member states are effectively contributing, the current union military operations only concern a maximum of half a dozen member states each; encourages member states to provide more forces for operations.' it is therefore simply regrettable that the member states still have a choice of which missions they participate in. the report not only advocates the creation of a single defence market, but also considers that member states are not capable of having effective research programmes.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it supports the strengthening of the european common defence and security policy and thus paves the way for the creation of a european army. i believe that each state must remain in control of its own national defense. moreover, this european army would in reality be at the service of nato and the united states, as point 9 admits, which calls for 'total complementarity with nato'. france's interest is to develop a policy of balance between the great powers, in line with the policy initiated by general de gaulle.
in writing. - i voted against it. the aim of this report is to build a common security and defence policy. to justify this, the text describes the threats that would be posed to europe in order to convince of the need to create this common defence policy. the report also deplores the lack of resources for the european union to play an international military role (point 6). the european union regrets the lack of involvement of some of the member states in the recent conflicts. we may even fear that sanctions will be taken against those states which are not sufficiently cooperative (point 28 with reference to tax incentives). there is also a desire for allegiance to nato, which is unacceptable. it is clearly a text of surrender of sovereignty in a highly strategic area, defence, which guarantees precisely the independence of a nation.
in writing. - i voted against this report. this report, under the guise of standardizing and upgrading the union's defence capabilities, leads us towards a european army, vassal of nato, in which the member states will be stripped of their sovereignty. it forces a uniformity of states' positions on foreign policy, which prevents any disagreement, and even suggests 'tax incentives' to force member states to participate in all military operations! we are firmly opposed to this.
in writing. ‒ following mr juncker's statement on the need to create a european army, this report is timely for the commission. he advocated greater autonomy for the common european security and defence policy (csdp), particularly vis-à-vis nato, by requesting the same budgetary capacities. the treaty of lisbon increased the eu's exclusive competence in this area, but left purely military matters to the states. but among the austerity measures, the states have cut back on budgetary expenditure. the european commission and mr danjean are therefore seizing this opportunity to gradually transfer national resources and thus the management of defence matters to the community budget and the european defence agency. this report by the ump and the other two submitted for vote are in the same vein and now find enthusiastic support in the european parliament in the wake of the ukrainian crisis. i am opposed to the bellicose policy of european defence and i am voting against this report which does not hesitate to distort the very interpretation of the treaties in order to limit the sovereignty of the states even further. in any case, france has no business in such an agglomeration.
in writing. ‒ this text begins by denying the sovereignty of the member states in matters of foreign policy, since it seeks to make it impossible for a state to oppose the union's foreign policy. the rapporteur, arnaud danjean, therefore wants to force all the member states into a community foreign policy, advocating common external interventions in which no state can refuse to participate. finally, the idea behind this report is the necessary abandonment of national defence capabilities since most states are no longer able to maintain their own armed forces. the solution would therefore be to establish a single european defence, which i oppose, so that france can retain its sovereignty and its defence. i therefore voted against.
in writing. this report on the implementation of mr danjean's common foreign and security policy is a serious attack on one of the elements of national sovereignty. the report, which is faithful to the policy of small steps but which denies this will, proposes to add a stone to the utopian edifice of a 'european army' which was already rejected in 1954 under the name of the european defence community. it is about pooling and sharing, that is, pooling and sharing national defence through the common foreign and security policy. worse, the pretext of austerity and the breakdown of national defence budgets is used to promote this pooling and thus accelerate the process of a european army. the cfsp is also just one aspect of the eu's policy of submission to the wishes of the us and nato. this pooling of resources and the embryo of a european army is inefficient, since the interests of the various member states diverge. the interests of the american "foreign federator", as general de gaulle called it, will therefore be served more and more. i voted against this text, of course.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on the implementation of the common european security and defence policy. in the current context of instability at the eu's borders and in its immediate neighbourhood, unprecedented since the creation of the csdp in the late 1990s, this text stresses the need for the european union to adapt urgently to the new security challenges facing it. this is to use the tools already existing in the lisbon treaty and to make csdp more closely linked to the union's foreign policy, humanitarian aid policy and development policy. this resolution also calls for closer coordination of national action. the aim is to ensure that the union becomes a decisive and united actor in the face of each of these threats.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the implementation of the common security and defence policy, a text which is part of the european council's perspective of 25 and 26 june 2015, when security and defence issues will be discussed. the many crises and threats facing europe today call into question the means that the european union deploys for its own security and that of its environment. as this report shows, the common security and defence policy must be a major instrument for europe to play its part.
in writing. ‒ defence is one of the most important royal functions. a country which can no longer decide its defence policy or judge the use of its armed forces in its own interests has lost all sovereignty. the recent geopolitical crises, including those on the doorstep of the european union, have shown that not all member states have the same analysis or the same interests. there is no question of my approving the subjugation of france and the loss of its sovereignty to an entity as illegitimate and undemocratic as the european union, let alone nato, which is in fact manoeuvring and deciding on the use of a european army. i shall of course vote against this text.
in writing. ‒ in the face of the increase in crises and conflicts in certain parts of the world over the last decade, the union needs to have the appropriate instruments to respond effectively. the main instrument is the common security and defence policy, but at present it does not allow the union to respond properly to crises and to assert itself on the international scene. the european parliament has adopted the report by my colleague, mr arnaud danjean, on the implementation of the common security and defence policy. i have spoken in favour of this report and i support the points for improvement. in particular, the common security and defence policy should enable the union to respond in a more coordinated way and to try to act in a sustainable way.
in writing. ‒ i supported the parliament's annual report on the implementation of the common security and defence policy (csdp). the global environment is becoming more and more unstable. the war in eastern ukraine, the conflicts in syria and iraq, and terrorism in africa are just a few examples. in the face of the proliferation of conflicts and crises, we have a duty to act both to protect ourselves and to reduce this geopolitical instability. our report calls for the development of a common security and defence policy in which the eu would be a decisive player. while european commitment is welcome in some regions, such as the horn of africa, the eu clearly lacks leadership in most operations conducted by member states. at the next european council in june 2015, we expect states to take concrete measures to improve the union's territorial defence capability.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report by my colleague arnaud danjean, which is in line with the european council of 25 and 26 june 2015, when security and defence issues will be discussed. given the current geopolitical context, with the increase in crises and conflicts, it is necessary and urgent for the european union to act to ensure its protection and the stability of its environment. it is urgent that we strengthen the common security and defence policy of the european union, with particular emphasis on the development of cooperation, assistance and the financing and solidarity mechanisms provided for in the treaty.
in writing. ‒ the report is intended to persuade the eu authorities to reform or relaunch the common security and defence policy at the june 2015 summit. the report highlights the deterioration of the security environment (us rebalancing in asia, the middle east, ukraine) and the emergence of 'new threats' such as cybersecurity, organised crime and terrorism. it should be noted that the summit in december 2013 was a failure for the supporters of european defence. the report must also be placed in the context of the recent nato summit and the constant demand from the americans that the member countries of the alliance spend 2% of their gdp on defence. the report's demands relate mainly to the financing of operations, the training of staff, the sharing of resources and the development of a common strategy on the various major threats. i voted against this text because of its blatant desire to make the foreign and defence policies of the member states, one of the last surviving areas of sovereignty, a community policy.
in writing. ‒ this report is a logical follow-up to the danjean report and aims to strengthen the common security and defence policy by increasing its financial and human resources. this report goes further than the one on the implementation of the csdp, as it 'calls for the union's role in defence matters within nato to be strengthened', i.e. for the union to simply take the place of the member states. the report also calls for the pooling of resources, whereas the costs would be borne by the member states. it then stresses that by withdrawing the individual financing for operational military or defence expenditure, member states will eventually lose their independence. they will no longer be able to choose whether or not to participate in missions, since, according to the 'principle of solidarity', no state could refuse. i therefore naturally voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this debate because i am in favour of greater coherence between external and internal policy instruments and of greater cooperation and coordination between member states, particularly in the fight against terrorism and organised crime, as well as in the areas of cybersecurity and immigration. this is the first step towards a european army...
in writing. the report by eduard kukan and indrek tarand on the financing of the common security policy cannot in any case be supported by me, because of my opposition to the common foreign and security policy. i would briefly remind you that this policy of sharing the foreign and security policies of the member states is ineffective and even counterproductive, and it seriously undermines the sovereignty of the member states. on this particular report, which is supposed to provide funding for the cfsp, my opposition is similar. not only must states retain full control of their defence capabilities, but they must also retain the absolute necessity to decide on the allocation of resources that they intend to allocate to these same capabilities. i am shocked by the european union's repeated desire to control the budgets of the member states. the states are sovereign in this matter as in all others. for these reasons, i am voting against this text.
in writing. ‒ this report seeks to respond to the observation that there is no european solidarity in external military interventions. for example, the french army's intervention in mali was not supported financially and materially by the germans. however, the success of the operations will have a positive impact on the fight against terrorism for all member states. it is this contradiction that the union is trying to address in order to conceal its lack of credibility in this area. the report therefore seeks to replace intergovernmental diplomacy with a common european security policy, rather than giving member states full control of their defence budgetary policy. the aim will now be to encourage, through fiscal and budgetary arrangements, the pooling of each member state's military capabilities. to this end, the report stresses the need to deepen the europeanisation of the union's external policies by making full use of the legal possibilities offered by the lisbon treaty. for all these reasons, i voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ the current international context calls for more cooperation between member states in the field of defence. this also means more rigorous rules on the financing of the common security and defence policy. the budget allocated by the member states to defence is not large enough for the european union to guarantee security in its neighbourhood. i voted in favour of the report on the financing of the common security and defence policy.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report, which is only a logical follow-up to mr danjean's report on the csdp, which is aimed at strengthening the csdp and its financial and human resources. the report by eduard kukan and indrek tarand also states that the eventual defence of europe will be left to nato, that is to say, to the united states. the idea of pooling resources and thus providing the csdp with its own budget was also put forward. while in theory this effort to rationalize the budget may seem commendable, since it is a matter of simplifying the organizational structure around the csdp, this empowerment would represent a further step towards european defence, that is to say towards a loss of sovereignty with the disappearance of national defenses. the report also calls for the abolition of the individual financing of military or defence operations, which would lead, under the principle of solidarity, to depriving member states of their independence, since they would no longer be able to choose which missions they participate in or not.
in writing. ‒ the present report aims to express the european parliament's concerns about the lack of funding for the common security and defence policy and calls, in particular, for more flexibility and coherence in the implementation of this policy. if europe is to make progress in this strategic area and meet the challenges of the present, budgetary commitments should be proposed that are commensurate with our ambitions. in addition, it is necessary to strengthen the coherence and complementarity of the common security and defence policy with national defence policies, with a view to reducing duplication and financial transparency of missions and operations. for these reasons i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. in the face of public deficits, pooling member states' resources is a better response than uncoordinated cuts in defence budgets. moreover, when member states wish to engage together civilly and/or militarily, they must be able to implement means of close cooperation. these means exist in the treaty of lisbon. i therefore call on the vice-president of the commission and high representative, federica mogherini, to encourage heads of state and government to take full advantage of the treaty provisions. flexible financing and decision-making will allow missions and operations under the common security and defence policy to be deployed quickly and efficiently, which is all the more urgent today in view of the security challenges we face in europe.
in writing. ‒ the union is facing new challenges that are difficult to grasp because they are of different natures: security-related challenges such as terrorism, but also humanitarian and development-related challenges such as managing migration flows. our defence policy must be able to respond to this. to this end, member states must show greater solidarity by pooling their resources and coordinating their foreign policies more closely. tools to enable funds to be released more quickly for interventions must also be available.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on the financing of the common security and defence policy. the member states must retain their prerogatives in this area. to do this, they must of course also be free to choose the budgets they wish to allocate to it. far from adopting this principle, the union prefers to focus on the pooling of resources. this report shows the ineffectiveness of the union's action. i would remind you that the french people are particularly keen to preserve these policies, which are a safeguard against the wishes of a european defence project. these reports are not the only purpose of their proposals, but are steps towards a succession of proposals that are increasingly risky.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on the financing of the common security and defence policy. the report concludes that the member states are not meeting the helsinki objectives set in 1999. these objectives included the deployment of a european ground force of 50,000 to 60,000 men, based on the resources made available by each country. in addition, air and naval forces were to complement this land force. the report also notes that in recent years funding for civilian missions under the csdp has declined. this decrease even forced the commission to postpone payment of eur 22 million to 2015. however, in view of the bellicose and disastrous foreign policy pursued by the european union in africa, the middle east and even on the european continent, in ukraine, it is to be welcomed that the helsinki objectives have not been achieved. with the present leadership, giving the european union military means would be like letting children play with guns.
in writing. ‒ this report is a logical follow-up to the danjean report and aims to strengthen the common security and defence policy by increasing its financial and human resources. the text goes further than the csdp implementation report, since it 'calls for the union's defence role in nato to be strengthened'. in other words, the union is replacing the member states. the report also calls for the pooling of resources, with the costs remaining with the member states. the report also stresses that by withdrawing the individual financing for operational military or defence expenditure, member states will eventually lose their independence. they will no longer be able to choose whether or not to participate in missions, since, according to the 'principle of solidarity', no state can refuse to participate. for all these reasons, i have decided to vote against this text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by my colleagues kukan and tarand on the financing of the common defence and security policy. the report makes several proposals for cost savings and efficiency gains, such as the lack of transparency in the choice of private companies in the protection of civilian personnel in conflict zones, and also calls for more coherence and synergy between military and civilians in a conflict zone in order to maximise costs. i welcome the fact that this report was adopted by a large majority.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the financing of the common security and defence policy (csdp). no member state can face alone the security instability that is unfolding at the gates of the union. it is therefore necessary to make the common security and defence policy an effective strategic instrument which can guarantee the security of european citizens and promote european interests and values.
in writing. ‒ like the other members of the national front, i voted against the report on the financing of the common security and defence policy. like the danjean report on the implementation of this policy, this report aims to pool the resources of the member states to lead to the creation of a single european army. it is almost like dreaming when one reads the first paragraph of the report, in particular, which 'deplores the modest nature of the csdp interventions, in particular military operations, which are essentially small-scale military training missions instead of major contributions by europe to the maintenance and enforcement of peace; is convinced that the european union cannot be content to focus exclusively on post-crisis or exit support instruments, but must, on the contrary, be able to intervene across the whole spectrum of crisis management.' the european union, which is not even able to control its own external borders, now has the ambition to make "major contributions" to the imposition of peace throughout the world. ridicule does not kill.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because, in the logic of the danjean report, it wants to pool resources to enable the creation of a european army.
in writing. - we voted against this report. the aim of this report is to strengthen the common security and defence policy (csdp) by pooling its human and financial resources. on paper, this seems positive since the csdp would thus have its own budget and resources. in reality, it is a question of withdrawing the individual funding of the member states and thus their independence, since they will no longer have the possibility of choosing which missions they wish to participate in. we are against this idea.
in writing. ‒ the report regrets the modest nature of military interventions under the common security and defence policy (csdp), calls for a more rapid and flexible deployment of missions and advocates civil-military cooperation in research. it also called for systematic participation by all states in the athena financial mechanism, which provides for the financing of the common costs of the member states' military operations (except denmark) and also for research into nuclear, radiological, biological and chemical weapons. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. i do not have to choose between plague and cholera, between the nato war-mongering army and its reproduction at european level to go and intervene in ukraine and sow confusion at our borders or elsewhere. i am opposed to this report and to that of the ump member, and i denounce the irresponsibility of the greens in allowing a baltic rapporteur of the most warmongering persuasion to take over this matter.
in writing. ‒ this report is a logical follow-up to the danjean report and aims to strengthen the common security and defence policy by increasing its financial and human resources. the text goes further than the csdp implementation report, since it 'calls for the union's defence role in nato to be strengthened'. in other words, the union is replacing the member states. the report also calls for the pooling of resources, with the costs remaining with the member states. the report also stresses that by withdrawing the individual financing for operational military or defence expenditure, member states will eventually lose their independence. they will no longer be able to choose whether or not to participate in missions, since, according to the 'principle of solidarity', no state can refuse to participate. for all these reasons, i voted against.
in writing. this report is concerned about the lack of mutualisation and solidarity among eu countries in the field of defence. but the modest nature of military operations under the common security and defence policy is only a reflection of the profound divergences of interests between the various member states. the idea of a federated european army is therefore a dream that only the pro-european minds can believe to be a foreboding one. the divisions over the war in iraq or even the intervention in libya are evidence of this. in addition, this sharing is motivated by cuts in national defence budgets: one wonders if brussels is not imposing austerity to promote the european army and thus satisfy the bellicose attitude of mr juncker, whose ideas have not thawed since the end of the cold war. it is also scandalous that this report proposes to finance military interventions from the eu budget when this is clearly prohibited by article 41 (2) of the treaty on european union. in the face of these desires, it is urgent to reduce the share of france's defence budget to 2% of gdp and instead to promote targeted and temporary bilateral cooperation. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on the financing of the common european security and defence policy. the text stresses the need for the union to adapt urgently to the new security challenges that have emerged at its borders and in its immediate neighbourhood. the measures contained in the resolution propose, in particular, the establishment of permanent financial procedures for cooperation between the commission, the eeas, the european defence agency, the european space agency and the member states. the aim is to ensure that the union becomes a decisive and united actor in the face of each of these threats.
in writing. ‒ it is perfectly logical that those who advocate a common defence policy should want to put in place the means to finance it. it is equally logical that those who oppose such a betrayal of the sovereignty of the peoples should refuse to finance its implementation. i therefore vote against this text in full accordance with my previous vote.
in writing. ‒ the union's security, both internal and external, is now a matter of crucial importance. threats are multiplying and the union must be able to defend its territory and protect its citizens. in this context, i voted in favour of the resolution on the financing of the common security and defence policy. i stress the importance of promoting concrete measures and pragmatic solutions so that the union can have a real impact.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report on the implementation of the common security and defence policy, which only strengthens and encourages an ever-greater militarisation of the european union. i reject the csdp (common security and defence policy) which is pushing the eu towards an increasingly militarized vision and therefore towards more and more military operations, whereas the eu should be focusing on political dialogue and peace processes, putting its full weight on the scales. this approach requires colossal budgetary capacities at the expense of other policies. the gue/ngl denounced the automatic financial participation of each member state in the union's military missions as calling into question the purely civilian nature of these missions, knowing that today the civil and military aspects are increasingly mixed and confused. the gue/ngl also condemned the use and development of armed drones and the illicit practice of extrajudicial targeted executions. i reject this leap forward, which unfortunately is supported by a majority of the european parliament for reasons that are as varied as they are ambiguous.
in writing. ‒ this report is part of the perspective of the forthcoming european defence summit in june. it stressed in particular the threat posed by russia and called for an end to the increasing dependence of the defence industries on the outside world. the integrated defence market is also highlighted. but why limit scientific cooperation in defence matters to the european union alone? in this respect, temporary partnerships, bilateral or multilateral, and of fixed duration, which can be cancelled at any time, must be the solution. i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ in favour of a european army, i agree with the conclusions of this report.
in writing. ‒ the gomes report on europe's defence capabilities follows the same logic as the danjean report and the report by eduard kukan and indrek tarand, which ultimately aim at pooling the defence capabilities of the member states of the european union. i am firmly opposed to any idea of sharing, not for ideological reasons but for pragmatic and efficient reasons. it is unthinkable to imagine an integrated european defence market in the short, medium or even long term. this federalist logic must be rejected in its entirety and in its details, since it is clear that the existence of such a market would restrict the decision-making capacities of the member states and their most basic sovereignty. france, like the other member states, cannot confine itself to such a geographically restrictive view of its interests. as such, scientific cooperation in this field must be subject to temporary and reversible partnerships and not to mandatory transfers of technology imposed against the will of the states. i therefore naturally vote against this text.
in writing. ‒ this report anticipates the next european defence summit scheduled for june. it rightly points out the various threats facing europe: hybrid wars, terrorism and the growing dependence of 'european' defence industries on the outside world. the report uses the emergence of common threats as a pretext to push the union to strengthen the development of an integrated european defence market. the technocrats in brussels should be reminded that such a market is simply unthinkable. scientific and military cooperation between several states is by its nature reversible, since it depends on the temporary framework of bilateral or multilateral relations between them. this is why the member states must not confine themselves to 'european' partnerships and develop military cooperation with third countries, such as russia. i am opposed to the principle of creating a european army under the aegis of nato, and i voted against this text, which is part of the line of the two previous reports.
in writing. ‒ the report on the impact of developments in the european defence market on common security and defence capabilities highlights the need to coordinate the economic policies of the member states related to the defence market. although defence remains primarily a matter for member states, the optimal functioning of the single market requires european countries to cooperate and remove trade barriers in this area. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report, which has no other aim than the creation of a single european defence market. in line with the danjean and kukan reports, the aim is to use the security and economic challenges facing the member states to promote the pooling of resources. the idea is simple: a european defence market will supply the european federal army with equipment. the report also urges the commission to take punitive action against member states accused of failing or misapplying the 2009 defence directives. the aim is therefore to "mother" the recalcitrant states so that they sell their sovereignty and the interests of their national industries. finally, the strategic partnerships with russia are again highlighted; the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. on all fronts, the european union is seeking to disarm nations, but patriots will continue to fight to preserve their countries' strategic interests.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which calls on the member states in the run-up to the european defence summit in june 2015. beyond the adoption of policy frameworks for defence cooperation, states must take concrete action through the establishment of enhanced cooperation. these are particularly relevant in the case of the defence equipment market. it also recalled the possibilities for the defence industries, and in particular smes, to finance their projects through european funds. finally, i support the rapporteur's request for a common position on the use of armed drones. i remain convinced that defence is also a european issue.
in writing. ‒ this report presents the main developments in the european defence market and their implications for security and defence in europe. i note with concern that the report shows, in particular, that recent developments could jeopardise european autonomy because of the various budget cuts. the report calls for the establishment of a common strategy, greater regulatory coordination and the deepening of the internal market in the field of defence industries, with a view to preserving european autonomy. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on the impact of developments in european defence markets on security and defence capabilities in europe. it draws up a series of recommendations aimed at achieving an integrated defence market. the more foolish the latter are, the more they must compensate for the dependence of european states on defence and security. however, we know that the union seeks to take irreversible and binding decisions. that is why i voted against this report, to express my strong and unanimous rejection of these excesses.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the gomes report on the impact of developments in european defence markets on security and defence capabilities in europe. the report highlights new threats such as cyberterrorism, terrorism and hybrid wars in eastern europe. it also stressed industrial cooperation between certain member states and russia, particularly in the fields of space, science and the military, which was seen as a form of dependence. if the partial and russophobic nature of this observation is already a problem in itself, the solutions advocated are not better. the aim is to promote the emergence of an integrated defence market and to combat protectionist practices in the member states in the field of defence. in other words, this report wants to extend european integration to the defence market, so that the european union can further reduce the sovereignty of the member states and have more leeway to pursue its disastrous foreign policy.
in writing. ‒ this report is part of the perspective of the forthcoming european defence summit in june. the text particularly stresses the threat posed by russia and calls for an end to the increasing dependence of the defence industries on the outside world. the integrated defence market is also being put forward, which is the opposite of common sense: defence scientific cooperation must not be confined to the union, let alone be part of a consistent policy. in this respect, temporary bilateral or multilateral partnerships with a fixed duration, which can be cancelled at any time, must be the solution: yesterday's friend can, overnight, turn into a potential enemy. the technocrats of the european union want to push integration into their union even further, in defiance of the sovereignty of the member states, from whom they want to take away all foreign and defence policy. that is why i voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by my colleague ana gomes on the evolution of european defence markets. this report points to the decline in defence spending by states and the lack of coordination among states on this issue. the committee also expressed concern at the decline in state investment in european defence companies and the increased dependence on non-european defence companies. i welcome the fact that this report was adopted by a large majority.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the impact of developments in european defence markets on security and defence capabilities in europe. at a time when the european union is facing unprecedented multiple and direct threats, we need to structure a european defence market, the only one capable of guaranteeing the dependency of the european defence sector and encouraging better cost sharing.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it seeks to create an integrated defence market. i believe that in matters of defence a state must retain the power to enter into temporary partnerships with whomever it wishes, concluded in a freely negotiated bilateral or multilateral framework. i also condemn the interference which this text advocates in the negotiations by states on their defence procurement contracts.
in writing. - i voted against it. the report calls for the financial and human resources of the common security and defence policy to be strengthened. here again we find the willingness to abandon any form of sovereignty for the member states by obeying nato which would direct the various operations. the financial pooling sought by this project would accentuate the creation of a european defence, which would be tantamount to the loss of our sovereignty in this area. the commission wants to abolish individualised financing, which clearly means the end of the independence of the member states, which will be unable or unwilling to participate freely in military action.
in writing. ‒ in the war-mongering vein of the european defence reports, this text promotes 'the progressive establishment of a european defence equipment market'. the main aim is to avoid any cooperation with russia in sensitive areas such as satellite launching, soyuz rockets or strategic air transport. the text also aims to "combat protectionist practices by member states" and to further limit the sovereignty of states in the field of defence. there's no way we're taking on the defense of irresponsible warmongers. i am voting against this text.

in writing. this report on 'europe's defence capabilities' follows the line of the previous danjean and kukan and tarand reports, which aimed at pooling the defence capabilities of the member states of the european union on the pretext that this would avoid duplication, reduce costs and improve management. but why stop at the european level and not start at the world level (and beyond)? what would have happened to the shared elements in the iraq war when more than 80% of the eu countries had taken a stand for george bush? 20% of charles de gaulle would stay in france, the rest would go to the americans? what would have been done in libya where the german government has repeatedly expressed its reluctance (and rightly so)? this would limit the member states' capacity to act. the divergent interests of the member states show the futility of such a project which can only satisfy brussels' "best" ally: the united states. let us first propose targeted and temporary (and therefore reversible) bilateral agreements, particularly in the technological field, and not in a mandatory way. for these reasons, i voted against.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on the impact of developments in defence markets on the security and defence capabilities of the european union. this text recalls our growing dependence on exports from outside the european union and the increase in foreign investment in the european defence sector in some countries. this could lead to a lack of transparency and to the transfer of control of strategic industries, resources and technologies at national and european level. this resolution calls for enhanced cooperation between member states and the development of an effective and independent european defence industrial and technological base. it is about ensuring europe's ability to protect its citizens, its interests and its values.
in writing. ‒ this report highlights the threats (hybrid wars in the eastern neighbourhood, terrorism) and mentions the risk of increased external dependence of 'european' defence industries due to the crisis and vis-à-vis russia, with which some states maintain commercial and scientific relations in the military field. to counter these threats, the text makes a series of recommendations to enable the emergence of an integrated defence market (common position on exports, control of dual-use technologies). it also addresses funding issues (e.g. whether or not to join horizon 2020) and management methods (pool and sharing). it advocates combating protectionist practices in the field of defence. like the previous texts, it is therefore part of the federalist logic of the establishment of a common european army. i am not going to endanger the independence of france in the field of defence and defence industry, so i am naturally voting against this text.
in writing. ‒ in the face of the increasingly reduced defence budgets of the member states and the increase in armed conflicts and international crises, the union must be able to mobilise its resources properly and effectively in order to play a key role on the international stage and contribute to global stability. in this context, parliament adopted a motion for a resolution on the impact of developments in european defence markets on security and defence capabilities in europe. i am glad that i voted in favour of this text. this proposal highlights the importance of strengthening the capabilities and competitiveness of our european defence industry through the development of an industrial strategy. the union's existing capabilities must be used to strengthen our european security and defence policy.
in writing. ‒ this report is in line with the june defence summit. it stressed the threats (hybrid wars in the eastern neighbourhood, terrorism) and the risk of increased external dependence of 'european' defence industries as a result of the crisis, in particular vis-à-vis russia, with which some states maintain commercial and scientific relations in the military field. to counter these threats, the report makes a series of recommendations to enable the emergence of an integrated defence market (export controls and control of dual-use technologies). it also deals with the problems of financing and management methods. it advocates combating protectionist practices in the field of defence. it should be stressed that any integrated defence market is unthinkable. scientific cooperation in this field should not be confined to europe or be the subject of a permanent policy for any state but should be based on temporary and easily reversible partnerships, without forced transfers of technology and concluded in a bilateral or multilateral framework. i vote against it.

the agenda calls for the debate on the question with request for an oral reply (o-000048/2015) to the commission on the elimination of the practice of early and forced marriage of girls, by iratxe garcía pérez and anna maria corazza bildt, on behalf of the committee on women's rights and gender equality (b8-0552/2015) (2015/2654 (((rsp)).
in writing. in 2014, the united nations children's fund (unicef) estimated that more than 250 million women worldwide were married as children. worse still, some 130 million women have been subjected to female genital mutilation (the total or partial removal of their external genitalia), mainly in africa and the middle east. in fact, it is estimated that nearly 10 million girls and teenagers are forced into marriage each year. it is high time the un raised the age of marriage and criminalized forced marriages despite local customs and traditions. this practice of degrading women is a form of modern slavery that cannot be tolerated. marriage of a child undermines her education, limits her opportunities, endangers her health, and increases her risk of being a victim of violence. girls are often married off to older men, and while forced marriage affects boys as well, it exposes girls first to early pregnancy and childbirth, the leading cause of death among 15- to 19-year-olds, according to a united nations report. the european union, which promotes equality between men and women, must therefore encourage this in its international agreements and support the end of forced marriages.
in writing. forced marriage of young girls is a real scourge that seriously undermines the dignity of women. therefore, any progress towards reducing these practices should be welcomed and encouraged, particularly in developing countries. however, this struggle, however legitimate it may be, must not be used as a pretext for the implementation of policies of interference in the internal affairs of states, especially since this scourge affects the member states of the union strongly, starting with france. according to the ngo plan france, nearly 70,000 girls have been forced into marriage in france. according to the ngo, most of these girls are immigrants from turkey, the maghreb and sub-saharan africa. so it is appropriate to sweep our own front door before we teach the nations.
in writing. in our european and christian civilization, marriage is the protective institution of women and an essential guarantee for children. if this institution, the foundation of our societies, is threatened from within by ideologies which the union likes to promote, the fact remains that a new threat is coming from outside our borders. the mass immigration to which europe has been subjected for decades has brought to our shores populations alien to our culture. the destruction of our models of assimilation and integration, caused by the resignation of the elites in the spheres of public education, culture and the defence of national cohesion, has fostered communitarianism and practices that we cannot accept. the early and forced marriage of young girls is therefore the consequence of these two dynamics and the root of the problem should be addressed by defending the cultural integrity and unity of the european nation states. the dignity and equal treatment of women are not strangers to the people of europe, but we are the best defenders of them. it is not a question of universal rights either, but it is a common identity of the nations of europe.
in writing. this oral question addresses a major problem of forced and early marriage of girls. for example, nearly one in nine girls worldwide is married off by force, and in developing countries one in two children is born to teenage mothers. the cultural and social pressures on girls in these countries are considerable. forced marriage often appears to be the only possible future for these girls, who are thus reduced to the status of objects when they are not simply sold as a commodity. this problem should not, however, make us forget that in france, as in other european countries, such practices also exist. young girls living in the european union are subjected to family pressure and forced into marriage in their parents' country of origin. it is also necessary to denounce all mutilative practices, such as circumcision, which must be combated in france as in the european union. parliament must also take an interest in these problems.

in writing. this proposal for a european parliament decision on the opening and the mandate for interinstitutional negotiations on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (eu) no 1308/2013 and regulation (eu) no 1306/2013 as regards the aid scheme for the distribution of fruit and vegetables, bananas and milk in schools should make it possible to continue to finance the distribution of the above products to young children aged between six and ten years. there are still some shortcomings in this text, of course, but parliament's proposal has three major consequences. on the social side, it helps to reduce child malnutrition and ensures that all children have access to food. from a health point of view, this text promotes the fight against childhood obesity and encourages healthy eating. finally, at the economic level, it supports agricultural sectors in crisis, particularly in overseas regions such as guadeloupe and martinique. so i decided to vote for it.
in writing. ‒ the aim of this european programme is to continue to finance the distribution of milk, vegetables and fruit (including bananas) to children aged between six and ten. the programme has three major impacts:- social impact: by encouraging access to these foods among children from all sections of the population, the programme helps to combat child malnutrition, which continues to increase as a result of the crisis; - health impact: this programme contributes to the fight against obesity and, more generally, against the dietary habits responsible for an increasing number of serious diseases in children; - economic impact: by supporting producers of milk, vegetables, fruit and bananas from guadeloupe and martinique, the programme provides additional outlets for sectors in crisis. it is, however, worth pointing out the contradiction of the european commission's wish to support the crisis-stricken sectors in the outermost regions, while at the same time negotiating a free trade agreement with the united states that will put an end to health, social and economic dumping. i voted for this text.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this debate because this annual action is intended to respond to a possible agricultural crisis. it would then offer the european union a budgetary weapon to respond to a crisis that could hit a sector already very weakened by the russian embargo and the uncertainties of the climate and stock markets. however, despite this mechanism, the incomes of european farmers are still too unstable. in the years to come, this challenge will have to be met in the same way as the farm bild in the united states. i am in favour of the creation of an agricultural insurance fund.
in writing. this report deals with the creation of a reserve which can be used to support agricultural sectors in crisis. to do this, the commission wants to reduce direct payments, i.e. the funds farmers receive under the cap (common agricultural policy). direct payments are support to farmers in the form of income which is not linked to production but which depends on compliance with certain standards defined by the cap ("greening"). the amount of the reserve for crisis management in the agricultural sector is eur 441,6 million at current prices. the reserve is set at an adjustment rate for direct payments, which will mainly apply to those exceeding eur 2 000. this is not only insufficient but it is even more disadvantageous for farmers, since they are the ones who are punched. it is a false solution which has nothing to do with mutual aid because the amounts foreseen for the crisis reserve are taken from the farmers, legitimate aid which is dedicated to them. once again, farmers are paying the price for the inconsistency of the union's policy. it should be remembered that funds allocated to agriculture under the cap have already been reduced by 20% in 15 years. that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council fixing the adjustment rate provided for in regulation (eu) no 1306/2013 for direct payments in respect of calendar year 2015 should make it possible to set up a reserve to be used in case of crisis to support the agricultural sectors. however, the creation of this reserve of eur 441.6 million will be offset by a reduction in direct payments, i.e. the aid farmers receive under the cap. this is bad for our farmers because we are actually reducing their aid without any additional support. this sad fact is only the result of european agricultural policies which have reduced the funds allocated to farmers by 20% in 15 years, a drop which particularly affects my country, france. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council fixing the adjustment rate provided for in regulation (eu) no 1306/2013 for direct payments in respect of calendar year 2015. under the guise of common sense, this measure conceals the union's difficulty in responding to the problems of the citizens of the member states. the effect of this proposal will be to reduce the direct payments required by the common agricultural policy. let us be clear: we are being asked to take money from farmers and give it back to them in another form. this is much more like a communication measure than a real measure, because this proposal, behind a striking and misleading effect, will not produce any of the expected effects.
in writing. ‒ the agricultural sector is particularly sensitive and exposed to the various cyclical changes. in order to anticipate and be able to cope with the occurrence of a major crisis in this sector, it was proposed to set up a crisis reserve. this reserve will be established through a reduction of direct payments of 1,393041% for the calendar year 2015 for all member states except bulgaria, croatia and romania. in the event of a crisis, this reserve will be mobilised to enable farmers to continue their activities. i voted in favour of this report, which is a sign of european solidarity.
in writing. ‒ i rejected this proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council fixing the adjustment rate for direct payments for the year 2015. the objective may seem to be a good one in itself: to create a reserve of funds to support the agricultural sectors in crisis. i am very attached to french agriculture and could have supported such an initiative if it had not been intended to finance such support by the farmers themselves, cutting off from them, in particular, the aid which is currently dedicated to them and which they greatly need. the proposal for a regulation provides for a reduction in the aid provided for by the cap. the funds allocated to agriculture under the common agricultural policy have already been reduced by 20% in 15 years. under the guise of a equalization mechanism, this proposal for a regulation will in fact lead to the commission cutting farmers off from direct payments. it will now be up to the latter to pay the price that brussels has left them with through its suicidal austerity policy.
in writing. ‒ this report provides for a reduction of direct payments of 1,393041% in all member states, except bulgaria, croatia and romania, amounting to eur 441,6 million, through budgetary discipline mechanisms to support the crisis reserve for 2016. this reserve is intended to be used to support the agricultural sector in the event of a major crisis. nevertheless, it is worth asking whether it is normal that farmers, who are currently victims on all markets and throughout the year of a crisis of mainly diplomatic origin, should still be harmed the following year when the aid is regulated. i believe that farmers are entitled to expect solidarity from the european institutions. weighing all these factors carefully and taking into account the importance of having a functional reserve in a context of multiple crises and risks to the dairy sector following the abolition of quotas, i voted in favour of this report.
