in writing. the noichl report includes some commendable objectives, including the promotion of equal pay between men and women, the increase in the participation rate of women, access to employment for pregnant women, etc. however, other aspects are at least objectionable. the report intends to make ldcs an individual right, thus leading to a 'children's right' which i cannot support. it also includes comments on the situation of ethnic minorities such as the roma who have little to do with the subject. considering that this text concerns areas of competence which fall within the full sovereignty of the member states, and denying the european union and its institutions the possibility of legislating on societal matters out of respect for the principle of subsidiarity, i have decided to vote against. ‬
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report on the strategy for equality between women and men in the european union after 2015. although equality between women and men is one of my priorities, this report contains measures which, by their unrealistic nature, ultimately penalise the progress of women's rights. on the other hand, i voted for the alternative resolution tabled by my political group, which proposes concrete objectives to develop female entrepreneurship and reduce the gender pay gap, still over 16%. the epp resolution also calls on the european institutions and the member states to take urgent action against violence against women, whether in the family or in the workplace, and to combat stereotypes that reproduce inequalities.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the noichl report on the eu strategy for equality between women and men after 2015. we must all work for equality between women and men, both in private life and in professional life, and throughout life. there are too many pay gaps in employment and career that make women poor. the european union must be the guarantor and the driving force behind equality of citizens and the representation of women in all spheres of society, in accordance with the european charter of fundamental rights.
in writing. ‒ i voted resolutely against this text. i am of course in favour of equality between men and women, but the tendency of the left to want to include in this type of resolution provisions which are not relevant and which are the responsibility of the national authorities is unbearable. my position is clear: as long as provisions (such as the lmp) which are part of the national debate are found in the texts on equality between men and women, i will oppose them.
in writing. this report presents parliament's position in the context of the preparation of a new european commission strategy on women's rights and gender equality. the report calls for concrete action on issues such as violence against women, discrimination in the workplace, reconciliation of family and working life, the role of the media, the place of women in leadership positions, in education, in institutions and in external relations. in addition to these aspects, the report mentions the importance of sexual and reproductive rights, including abortion and lgbt rights. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the report proposed by maria noichl contains some good elements, because it is true that there is still much to be done on such important and concrete issues as wages, reconciliation of private and professional life or access to employment for pregnant women. however, it is totally unacceptable in many other respects. firstly, it does not respect the principle of subsidiarity and blatantly infringes the prerogatives of the member states and even of third countries. the european union is not responsible for policies on abortion and contraception or sexual education and therefore has no place in this report. the text also mixes in considerations about ethnic minorities such as the roma and makes ldcs an individual right, thus creating a right to the child that i cannot support. it presents a very materialistic view of the matter, aimed at making women as menial employees as men are unfortunately. that is why i am strongly opposed to this report.
in writing. ‒ in the context of the 20th anniversary of the adoption of the objectives of the beijing platform for action and the deadline for the millennium development goals, progress in gender equality will be reassessed worldwide. in this context, the european union has published a new strategy for equality between women and men after 2015. at this plenary session, meps adopted the commission's proposal. i voted against this report because i believe that it touches upon matters which are within the competence of the member states. i would like to stress in particular that the elements concerning sexual and reproductive rights and sexual education fall within the principle of subsidiarity.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the vote on the maria noichl report which calls on the commission to develop a european strategy for equality between women and men for the next five years. women still suffer from widespread discrimination in terms of pay and pensions and are more at risk of poverty and social exclusion. the physical and moral violence against women remains a worrying reality, including on the internet and social networks. stereotypes against them persist, especially in the media. the report calls for a directive to combat violence against women, for an end to discrimination in the labour market and for the elimination of stereotypes through education. the text also recommends measures to improve the balance between private and professional life, in particular by rethinking parental leave. finally, it addresses the essential issue of sexual and reproductive health and rights, proposing sex education programmes in schools, while advocating access to safe and legal abortion and the promotion of assisted reproduction in the member states.
in writing. ‒ women spend twice as much time as men on household chores and childcare; their pay is always lower than that of men; their rights, such as abortion, are regularly called into question; and finally, a third of them have already been sexually or physically abused... this is the situation of women in the european union. the report by maria noichl is a progressive text and proposes many solutions to combat inequalities, such as the introduction of more flexible forms of work so that men and women can better reconcile work and family life. it suggests that parental leave be shared between both parents but with strong incentives for fathers, such as non-transferable parental leave. the report also proposes the introduction of mandatory quotas to ensure greater representation of women in decision-making, the guarantee of access to abortion and the promotion of assisted reproduction, all of which could be the starting point for a new push by the european union for women's rights. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the aim of this report is to provide the european parliament with a contribution to the european commission's preparation of a new eu strategy for equality between women and men after 2015. it is important that efforts and actions are made to achieve genuine equality between men and women and we have always made this a priority. to do this, the commission's new strategy must take account of the central role of the member states in pursuing this objective. however, i chose to abstain on the final vote on this report because it contains good elements such as the fight against violence against women and support for women's participation in decision-making and entrepreneurship. however, some of the provisions of this text fall within the competence of the member states and not of the european union.
in writing. ‒ there is unanimous support for women in their task of ensuring the delicate balance between their family and professional lives. it is also vital to commit ourselves to defending the rights of the most vulnerable human beings, often in situations of dependence, such as children, the elderly or the disabled. however, as you read the proposals, how can you not be struck by the terrible contradictions that mark this report, particularly between its aims and the means it recommends to achieve them? it should be explained how it is possible to defend women by advocating gender theory and gender indifference or how it is possible to defend the lives of the most vulnerable by defending abortion as an inalienable right. how is it possible to defend the balance of the family by destroying its very conception and natural definition? the good intentions of all are held hostage by intellectual theories that are scurrilous and above all disconnected from reality. the report will therefore do no one any good and will only fuel the voters' disgust with the european institutions if they do not rid themselves of certain deadly ideologies. i vote against it.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the adoption of this report on the european union strategy for equality between women and men. it is a good report, fairly comprehensive, and covers many of the issues that need to be addressed, such as violence against women, access to financial resources, education and health, and equal pay. it also takes up some very interesting points put forward by my group on the consequences of austerity policies on women. i also want to denounce the attempts by the right wing of this house to empty the text of its content, particularly in the area of reproductive rights and the fight against violence against women. i also denounce the national front, which has been particularly virulent in the debates on both the right to abortion and the fight against discrimination and harassment of lgbti people. they failed, and i congratulate myself. i regret, however, that the paragraph on gender studies and feminist research was rejected by a few votes. i voted for this report but i remain convinced that much more needs to be done for women's rights in europe, for solidarity and for equality for all.
in writing. ‒ the diagnosis made in this report is relevant but the solutions are inadequate. it is noted that european competitiveness is based on creativity and innovation and that, therefore, this creativity should be developed by improving the protection of intellectual property rights. at present, the fight against infringements of intellectual property rights is very long and costly, especially for smes. counterfeiting, which used to be mainly for luxury goods, is now also found in consumer goods. but the solutions proposed in this report are not appropriate. the creation of a european supervisory body would be costly and unnecessary. on the contrary, intergovernmental cooperation should be given priority and the economic interests of the states should be defended, in particular through border controls. for these reasons i voted against this report.

in writing. the report rightly points out that intellectual property rights (ipr) are a major asset for the economies of the member states. but i voted against this text which seeks to transfer the protection of ipr to the commission: intellectual property belongs to the member states and the protection of rights related to it can only be done in the framework of intergovernmental cooperation.
in writing. ‒ the report on the strategy for the protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights in third countries asks the right questions but gives the wrong answers. indeed, intellectual property rights (ipr) are a very important part of the strength of the european economy. moreover, smes are the first victims of counterfeiting. i can only approve of the desire to fight this disease better by legal means. however, the infringements of state sovereignty which this relationship entails are simply unacceptable. i very much regret the desire to strengthen european integration in this area, whereas the fight against counterfeiting is most effective at national level and in the control of the external and internal borders of the european union. the creation of another european body would be costly and unnecessary. there is also a major risk of a strengthening of the dispute settlement logic. for all these reasons, i can only vote against this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on the strategy for the protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights in third countries. while special attention should be paid to smes, which are increasingly faced with illegal competition, the solutions proposed in this report will not in any way stem this phenomenon. the effectiveness of the fight against counterfeiting depends in fact on the control of our national borders. how can we expect to manage the flow of goods from a territory if it is penetrated from all sides? the only solution to safeguard the quality of french products, their value and thus the survival of their manufacturers, would be to identify the origin of counterfeiting and to have the possibility of stopping it.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament voted in favour of the report on the strategy for the protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights in third countries. this report is parliament's support for the european commission's intention to revise this strategy. we must protect our technology and our innovative sectors in our trade relations with third countries. it is important to adapt to new global challenges which are profoundly changing the context of intellectual property rights. i voted for this report.
in writing. ‒ i opposed this report which, while it mentions the real and concrete problems of infringements of intellectual property rights, in particular the increased possibilities of counterfeiting via online sales platforms, is totally wrong about the solutions to this problem. the european union is once again using real problems to increase its powers to the detriment of the member states and the interests of their citizens. the report advocates, along these lines, the integration of international standards promoted by the wto in the field of ipr, including the principle of dispute settlement mechanism - the famous idea that leads to the establishment of private courts allowing multinationals to sue states (as provided for in the ttip). more importantly, the report calls for the strengthening of european integration in this area through enhanced cooperation led by the commission. the best way to combat counterfeiting is to ensure control of the european union's borders, and only intergovernmental cooperation would allow us to be truly efficient in this.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report presents the european parliament's position on the european commission's communication of july 2014 on the strategy for the protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights in third countries. this communication was adopted in the context of the political and legal situation created by the rejection of the acta treaty in july 2012 and considers that the debate between intellectual property rights holders and end-users must lead to the necessary improvement and adequate harmonisation of internal european intellectual property rights policies with a view to improving protection and enforcement standards worldwide. i think that this is a necessary step and i have voted in favour of the report.
in writing. intellectual property rights cover a range of legal instruments: copyrights, licenses, patents, registered trademarks and geographical indications. these are being converged within the internal market, but it is equally important to create common standards with our trading partners. this helps to ensure the quality of the products our consumers have access to by ensuring their traceability throughout the supply chain and by fighting against counterfeiting. this is why i support the commission's strategy on the protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights, while inviting it to go further.
in writing. ‒ the protection of intellectual property is of paramount importance for europe. if we are to maintain our full capacity to innovate and create, and to maintain the technological and scientific advances necessary for the growth and competitiveness and know-how of our enterprises, we must act in three directions. firstly, the european union must ensure that existing commitments made with third countries are respected; to defend ourselves better in multilateral organisations; convince our partners that better protection of rights will boost the confidence of european businesses wishing to invest abroad. secondly, the union must have a more ambitious strategy for the defence of intellectual property rights in its negotiations for free trade agreements with third countries, in particular on the specific issue of geographical indications. thirdly, we must maintain a balance between the firm protection of intellectual property rights and our innovative industries on the one hand and development policy on the other. for example, within the wto, a system of licences targeted at vital medicines should be promoted to lower their price and to allow better access to them.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the strategy for the protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights in third countries. this is to protect creativity and innovation, drivers of european competitiveness and pillars of the europe 2020 agenda. the text recognises that the union needs to develop a more ambitious strategy for the protection of intellectual property rights vis-à-vis its trading partners. counterfeiting is no longer limited to luxury goods but also affects consumer goods such as toys, medicines, cosmetics and foodstuffs. in 2013, nearly 36 million items suspected of infringing intellectual property rights were seized, worth more than €760 million. in addition to profiting from organized crime, counterfeit products pose serious health risks to consumers. the report adopted calls for the creation of a detailed legal framework, accompanied by an effective control mechanism, including, if necessary, repressive measures and sanctions, the implementation of which must not, however, unduly burden legitimate trade.

in writing. ‒ the knowledge industries are one of the pillars of our globalised economy and are constantly growing. indeed, the number of new european patents and new community trade marks registered more than doubled between 2003 and 2012. but this positive development is facing a major threat: counterfeiting. according to the oecd, these ipr infringements cost the world economy €200 billion a year. the report proposes to improve the institutional framework for ipr and to protect them adequately and effectively. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the acquis in the field of intellectual property rights. the report also stresses the need to set up technical assistance programmes for third countries in the field of intellectual property. the competitiveness of the european union has been and will increasingly be based on creativity and innovation, which is why such a report is so important. that's why i voted for it.
in writing. ‒ following the rejection of the acta (anti-counterfeiting trade agreement) treaty by the european parliament in july 2012, the european commission considered a strategy for the protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights in third countries and published a communication laying down the basis for this strategy in july 2014. there are commercial interests in maintaining the balance between rights holders and end users, which is a complex issue. as such, it is important that the commission analyses the possibilities of organising a public debate on the protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights in third countries. it is also necessary to consider the question of improving and properly harmonising member states' policies on intellectual property rights, which could improve standards of protection and enforcement at international level. i therefore supported this report which calls on the commission to start thinking about the very complex question of the balance between rights holders, economic operators and end users.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the call for better protection of intellectual property rights and for combating counterfeiting through legal procedures. but the general content of the report reduces the sovereignty of the member states by drawing a desire to strengthen: - on the one hand, the integration of international standards, agreements (wto) and the obligations and arrangements arising from them (such as a dispute settlement mechanism) in the field of ipr; - on the other hand, european integration in this field through enhanced cooperation and led by the commission in a perspective of relationship between the union, beyond the member states, and third countries. i therefore vote against.
in writing. ‒ protection of intellectual property rights (ipr) is necessary in particular to protect the work of artists and to prevent counterfeiting. however, particularly in the case of trade with the countries of the south, iprs are used as a pretext to maintain dominance over these countries. whereas the public interest in access for all to knowledge, health, technology and natural resources should be emphasised, iprs are used to maintain monopolies, such as those of pharmaceutical companies, which put their profits ahead of the public interest. furthermore, the countries of the north and the south are treated as equals in the economic and political balance of power, which can only be to the disadvantage of the countries of the south, whose intellectual property rights are not as well protected as ours. i voted against this report because i am opposed to an intellectual property of domination and hegemony. the european parliament seems to have forgotten that it has largely rejected the acta agreement on counterfeiting.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by mr pavel svoboda entitled 'intellectual property rights: an eu action plan'. the protection of intellectual property rights is a condition for the future of our european enterprises, the sustainability of our know-how and the sustainability of our jobs. as such, the fight against commercial counterfeiting of copyrighted content must be at the heart of our concerns and involve all actors in the digital ecosystem. counterfeiters are becoming more daring and are taking advantage of new technologies to move their counterfeit goods via the internet, making it very difficult to catch counterfeits. i think mr svoboda's report is going in the right direction, in particular by involving all the actors in the supply chain through a due diligence obligation. i also appreciate the attention in this report to raising public awareness of intellectual property rights and promoting legal offerings online. in this time of crisis, it may be necessary to make our citizens aware of the impact of piracy and counterfeiting on value added in a globalised economy, and the job losses they cause.
in writing. ‒ i have chosen to oppose this report which continues the process of harmonising copyright at european level in the spirit of european integration and the establishment of a single european market. this type of standardization process, in addition to being harmful to national specificities which often protect freedoms more than european provisions, such as the "moral right" aspect of the french concept of copyright, can also be dangerous in terms of protecting consumer freedoms. in this area, the transposition of the infosoc directive into national law in 2001 led to the hadopi law in france: the 'creation and internet law' was thus intended to protect copyrighted content circulating on the internet. it cost the french state almost €12 million. in addition to being costly, such measures threaten citizens' digital freedoms.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report follows the action plan presented by the european commission to create an effective intellectual property policy at european and national level. the report supports the commission's approach overall, in particular on the need to protect intellectual property rights, the need to organise awareness campaigns among end-users and european citizens, the role of rights holders and the need for an intellectual property strategy including a legal framework adapted to the developments of the internet. i support this constructive approach and have voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the european parliament voted in favour of the commission's policy on the protection of intellectual property rights (ipr), particularly in the area of electronic commerce. the cultural and creative industries account for 4.5% of the union's gross domestic product and 8.5 million jobs. these are not insignificant figures; the european commission has published a report on the implementation of the eu's ipr directive in the field of intellectual property. iprs help to maintain high standards of consumer, public health and environmental protection in the internal market.
in writing. ‒ effective enforcement of intellectual property rights is essential for innovation and competitiveness of our businesses as well as job creation. the commission's current approach does not make a sufficiently clear distinction between physical counterfeiting and digital copyright infringements. the european union therefore needs a comprehensive ipr strategy, including a comprehensive and robust legal framework to combat counterfeiting and piracy, and one that is fit for the digital age. this includes increasing legal and affordable offers. this response must be a step towards the european digital single market.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on intellectual property rights: an eu action plan. new technologies are making information exchanges ever faster, with an increase in the number of recipients and the distance between them. this requires a reflection which should lead to appropriate protection of intellectual property rights. the union should be cautious in its approach to this issue, including in linking it to the opaque ttip negotiations. it is therefore better to focus on practical measures. to do this, we must consider the responsibility of those who play a major role in the dissemination of information: the providers of access.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this resolution because i cannot imagine that the european commission could take over the issue of intellectual property law and claim the exclusive right to legislate in this area.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this proposal for an eu action plan on the protection of intellectual property rights. the proposal does not provide any concrete solution, although it is important to protect these rights, which are a source of wealth for our economy, except for the creation of an expert group on the protection of intellectual property. the draft submitted therefore falls within the scope of the memorandum of understanding. more importantly, the vagueness of this proposal should be a cautionary tale, as intellectual property rights have often been used as a pretext for government intrusion into the private sphere. this was the case in france with the adoption of the hadopi law which allows the monitoring of internet users' downloads, in the name of copyright protection. but i am opposed in principle to any provision to extend the monitoring of their electronic communications to as many people as possible. i will, however, remain attentive to proposals which seek to protect the intellectual property rights of companies, and in particular of smes, provided that these proposals do not infringe the fundamental freedoms to which we all attach importance.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the communication entitled 'towards a renewed consensus on the protection of intellectual property rights: an eu action plan'. intellectual property rights are essential for competitiveness, employment and cultural diversity. in europe, protecting these rights is paramount in the context of the increasing use of the internet today.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report to establish an action plan to strengthen the protection of intellectual property rights in the european union. by voting overwhelmingly in favour of this report, which was entrusted to my colleague from the epp, pavel svoboda, we asked the european commission and the member states to put in place a comprehensive legal framework adapted to the digital environment, to combat infringements of intellectual property rights (ipr) more effectively within the european union. since intellectual property rights are a key factor for competitiveness, innovation and economic growth in europe, european legislation must protect them effectively. beyond the political message to the european commission and the member states, this report also has the merit of proposing concrete solutions to combat ipr infringements.

in writing. - i voted against this bill. intellectual property rights were not part of the negotiations leading to the treaty of rome in 1957 and had to be harmonised through multiple successive directives over the years. this effort at harmonisation has borne fruit, as there are now very few differences between national laws. unfortunately, the european legislative process is so cumbersome that the reports and directives proposed in this area are already inadequate: the world and technology have moved too fast. we oppose this text because we want to protect our sovereignty and our specificities, and to preserve the french concept of copyright.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the svoboda report on intellectual property rights (ipr). the aim of the text is to curb the entry of counterfeit products and to develop defence measures in the sectors most affected. in this context, it advocates the deepening of the european due diligence system, applicable throughout supply chains to prevent infringements of ipr. it also provides for facilitating agreements with service providers, particularly on the internet, to limit the sources of income of offenders. the report, supported by the s&d group, goes further and places particular emphasis on the involvement of all actors in the supply chain, also emphasising consumer awareness and information. the revenue from iprs is also a source of funding for research and innovation. they are also an effective instrument for cooperation between universities and enterprises. finally, they promote a value dear to french socialists: cultural diversity.
in writing. ‒ intellectual property is seen as 'a driver of jobs and growth' essential to 'the proper functioning of the market', boosting innovation and competitiveness in knowledge-based sectors. the text therefore aims to improve the protection of intellectual property rights (copyright, trademark and patents) within the union. but far from encouraging open research and knowledge sharing, it strengthens the position of dominant players in the market to the detriment of users. in the absence of a balanced proposal, i shall abstain.
in writing. ‒ since 1957, many directives on intellectual property have been adopted to facilitate the establishment of a single market and thus reduce divergences between national laws in this field. the report aims to reform copyright and in particular the 2001 'infosoc' directive. the balance sheet of this directive is rather poor. it is important to preserve the french conception of copyright, even if it must necessarily adapt to the information society. a possible liability of the access providers would be a line of thought. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ it is important to preserve the french concept of copyright, even if it must necessarily be adapted to the information society, in particular the moral law aspect, and to consider the possible liability of access providers. the report does not offer such guarantees and therefore calls for a vote against.
in writing. ‒ the report on the strategy for the protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights in third countries makes commendable findings, but the solutions are at least questionable. the fight against infringement of intellectual property rights (ipr) is a pressing need in the public interest, particularly for smes, which are often the first victims. but this report is yet another attack on the sovereignty of the member states, since it further strengthens european integration in this area by proposing, in particular, the creation of a new european body, whereas a policy at national level, coupled with controls at the external and internal borders of the union, would be much more effective. for these reasons, i have decided to vote against the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on an eu action plan for the protection of intellectual property rights. the text calls for action to be taken against ipr infringements and the moral and economic damage they cause to european companies. a union action plan in this area is particularly important, especially for smes, whose vulnerability to market losses caused by counterfeiting trade exposes them to bankruptcy. the resolution calls for greater awareness among the general public, and more specifically among the younger generations, of the consequences of infringements of intellectual property rights.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because the lisbon treaty and the charter of fundamental rights place a heavy emphasis on respect for intellectual property rights, which are a driver of european competitiveness. the union is faced today with a large number of infringements of intellectual property rights, the volume and value of which are alarming. these violations discourage growth and creativity. the effective enforcement of intellectual property rights must therefore be ensured.
in writing. the european parliament resolution on the enforcement of intellectual property rights addresses the economic, social and health consequences of non-respect of these rights, as well as methods to better respect these rights. our group has made a number of progresses, such as respect for the charter of fundamental rights of the european union and the principle of proportionality. the failure to respect intellectual property rights can harm innovation, smes, creativity and cultural diversity, especially on the internet, and that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the report on intellectual property rights: an action plan for the eu seems to me ineffective in its functioning and questionable in its aims. the draft initially submitted to the european parliament was purely and simply a declaration of intent and was therefore ineffective. i have serious doubts about certain provisions in view of the consequences of the 2001 infosoc directive. as a defender of france's interests, i am very much committed to the preservation of the french model of copyright, particularly in its moral aspect. one way of thinking about this is to consider the possible liability of the providers of access. for all these reasons, i am voting against this report.
in writing. ‒ in 2012, statistics showed that there were more than 90 000 cases of infringement of intellectual property rights at the eu's external borders. in order to strengthen the union's competitiveness, it is necessary to put in place adequate protection against counterfeiting and unfair competition. the european parliament adopted a union action plan for the respect and protection of intellectual property rights at the plenary session. i am proud to have voted for this text. this european strategy will make it possible to introduce new instruments to ensure a high level of protection of intellectual property rights and to support the competitiveness of european smes.
in writing. ‒ a reform of intellectual property law has become necessary in view of the increasing number of infringements. that is why i supported this resolution calling on the commission to submit a proposal to adapt the regulation, in particular to the new trading platforms. copyright, because of the changing nature of its scope, must be regularly amended. i welcome the adoption of this resolution, which proposes, among other things, the introduction of preventive information and awareness-raising measures, but also european aid to improve national redress mechanisms. however, we will remain vigilant to ensure that the commission's proposal does not impede competition and supports creativity and innovation by ensuring a safe, adequate and secure environment for inventors and creators.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the protection of intellectual property rights. these are rights that are essential to the preservation of cultural diversity and the artistic world. in times of crisis, they are the main source of income for cultural professionals. any infringement of iprs must be fought, whether offline or online, with the sale of counterfeit goods on the internet, for example. to do this, europe has several instruments at its disposal. cooperation between customs in cross-border trade needs to be facilitated, the legal framework needs to be adapted to the digital age and consumers need to be better informed. the commission has chosen to set up awareness campaigns to make europeans understand the real consequences of ipr infringements for society and we welcome this initiative. we reiterate our call for a comprehensive ipr strategy that brings together all relevant actors, from member states to public authorities at all levels, including local, regional and national.
in writing. ‒ the cultural and creative industries sector, which makes intensive use of intellectual property rights (ipr), generates almost 4.5% of the union's gdp and accounts for up to 8.5 million jobs. in these times of financial crisis, ipr revenues are often the main source of income for artists and creators; the guarantee and safeguarding of fair remuneration for holders of such rights are therefore key elements of the action plan. to achieve this, the report aims to involve all actors in the online and offline supply chain, each with a role to play in the fight against ipr infringements. in addition, it is proposed to improve civil procedures for the protection of intellectual property for smes and creators, as they play a key role in the cultural and creative industries sector and often lack the capacity to enforce their rights. to protect innovation, creativity, competitiveness, growth and cultural diversity, i voted for this report.
in writing. ‒ generally speaking, the european union is faced with many infringements of intellectual property rights and this has a negative impact on growth, job creation, creativity and innovation. it is in this sense that i have supported this report which calls for all the actors concerned to be involved in combating infringements of intellectual property rights and to help small businesses in pursuing this objective. the report also encourages the commission to carry out targeted awareness campaigns to raise awareness and inform consumers, and to set up a harmonised european system for the notification and removal of illicit goods and content. the ultimate aim of this action plan is to achieve a modern, pro-competitive and consumer-friendly framework for intellectual property rights.

in writing. ‒ this report concerns the protection of intellectual property rights (ipr) and addresses the economic, social and even health problems posed by infringements of these rights, particularly via the internet. it is necessary to protect intellectual property rights, particularly in the cultural sector, and to consider how best to enforce these rights, by encouraging and protecting creation. it is also essential to help smes to enforce their innovations against large groups, for example through simpler access to justice. my group, the gue/ngl, has fought a real battle to demand that all application of iprs be made in compliance with fundamental rights and in particular the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, and that all application be subject to the principle of proportionality. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which is in favour of better protection of ipr and encourages more rigorous monitoring of the application of legislation in this area.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, a seven-year-old child would understand that the energy market cannot be an open and competitive market and that it is part of the natural state monopolies for energy security. the electricity market is an example: what is expensive is the excess production capacity that can be used only occasionally, during peak demand. let us not forget that the european union has a very important role to play in the world economy. so why is this house in favour of liberalising the energy sector? why did you choose energy insecurity? firstly, because of incompetence, because many people are not familiar with this market. secondly, to obey the speculative finance, present here and to the commission. because, make a spot market for electricity, gas or oil, and you can, through derivatives, buy or sell a hundred times, a thousand times the production, create shortages, play on prices and speculate. finally, to obey the united states, and therefore to make war on russia, to go from energy security with russia to energy insecurity without russia. this parliament is dominated by the liberal kleptocracy.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, it took a major crisis with russia for us to finally have a serious debate on the european energy security strategy. it's about time. we face at least two challenges. the first is our energy dependence. we import more than half of the energy we use, which costs us about $400 billion a year - more than a billion a day! according to the figures, 95 per cent of our uranium, 90 per cent of our crude oil, 66 per cent of our gas and 40 per cent of our coal come from abroad. and russia accounts for almost a third of these resources, all types combined. the second challenge is climate change. we're told that to limit the temperature rise to 2 degrees celsius, we need two-thirds of our fossil fuels to stay underground. that's the problem. so what is the proposal from the commission and the member states? we're told we need to diversify our sources of supply. but the same system remains unchanged, because we hear that we have to plan for more gas pipelines, more oil pipelines, and this brings us back to fossil fuels. we are also told that it is imperative to exploit the indigenous resources. what are these indigenous resources? it's the unconventional gases, the shale gases. we in europe do not want shale gas! we are also talking about nuclear energy, but we will be dependent on uranium supplies, since we are not independent in this respect, and we will also be dependent on the russians in relation to rosatom. the solution is therefore to develop renewable energy sources, which are part of european sovereignty and contribute to energy efficiency. that's the real solution.
madam president, the overall energy strategy outlined in the saudargas report is rather in the right direction. the latter echoes the objectives of the delvaux report, which proposes three binding guidelines: a 40% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions, 30% renewable energy and 40% efficiency gains. these objectives are more ambitious than those adopted by the council and can only be welcomed. however, there are a few issues, notably the exploitation of shale gas and, more broadly, unconventional fossil fuels. it is not enough to stress and only stress that the extraction of these fuels is not very clean. this is why many of us believe that the use of hydraulic fracturing - a technology that is poorly understood in europe - poses risks and harmful effects on the climate, the environment and public health. the economic benefits will be far below what some experts have expected or promised. the operating costs are much higher than in the united states and the gas stocks are also less important. in fact, the american oil companies themselves are backing down by halting drilling in poland and hungary. even the impact on employment is limited, as experts estimate that the total number of workers in this sector has increased by between 0.1 and 0.2%. we therefore call on the member states not to persist in what could be a major wrong against the planet and the younger generations. we must stop exploring for and extracting unconventional fuels. we have the means, if we are willing, to support energy policies that are favourable to employment and the preservation of the planet.

answer is "blue cardboard". mr president, i did not set the four objectives i mentioned, the commission itself did. i think that before there is fluidity - as i said in my speech - it will be a long time before all citizens are registered before they can cross the border freely. in my view, this is not a question of ad hoc means. the principles of proportionality and necessity must be established. there is a colossal amount of money being spent - no financial problem in this matter - on a result which will be above all liberticidal for all those who will return to the european union, without having the slightest effectiveness.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, should we not be cautious about something or someone who claims to be intelligent from the start? unfortunately, the smart borders package does not seem to be exempt from this precautionary rule. first of all, be careful about its purpose: the question of law enforcement agencies' access to the personal data collected is now under discussion. this debate is obviously not about the smart borders package alone. law enforcement agencies are increasingly accessing data on people who are not normally suspected of any crime. so the question is what is it? a border management system or another security tool? secondly, prudence with regard to its impact on fundamental rights. on the one hand, the scheme aims to facilitate the journey of certain privileged travellers and, on the other, it aims to combat the overstaying of travellers who are a little less fortunate. will this differentiation between travellers not lead to a form of discrimination? what would be the basis for assessing the criteria for granting or refusing access to the registered traveller programme? finally, as regards cost, a smart border seems to be a border that costs a lot of money, which is probably not lost on the industry players. in addition to the intense lobbying that this system must provoke, is there not reason to question its cost-effectiveness? as already mentioned, the experience of the united states has largely called this report into question: more than 1.5 billion dollars of investment for only 1 300 refusals of entry. as the european union and its member states struggle to find the budget to save lives in the mediterranean, one can wonder if the gamble is really worth it.
mr president, since 2013, the commission has been wanting to put in place what it calls 'smart borders'. the aim is to register foreigners who frequently come to the union in order to speed up border controls and to check the biometric data of all foreigners who want to enter the territory of the union. this project seems to me to be objectionable for two reasons. firstly, it is a dangerous project for freedom, because it intends to computerise the personal data of millions of people; it is the same liberty-killing logic as that of the pnr project on the use of passenger data. secondly, these 'smart borders' are a front for strengthening the schengen system. but schengen is a terrible failure because every day migrants manage to enter the union illegally, especially in greece and italy. we need real state borders, not these pseudo-intelligent borders.

in writing. ‒ this report proposes to give the european parliament's consent to the so-called 'doha' amendment to the kyoto protocol. the kyoto protocol, which entered into force in 2005, contains binding reduction targets for 2008 to 2012. in december 2012, the doha conference adopted an amendment establishing a second commitment period from january 2013 to december 2020. under this amendment, the european union, its member states and iceland commit themselves to limit their average greenhouse gas emissions to 80% of the 1990 baseline. i believe that the eu's agreement to the doha amendment must be given before the end of 2015 and ratified as soon as possible by the member states and iceland in view of the paris conference, so i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ in line with the brzezinski doctrine, russia is presented in this report as the absolute evil that the union must fight with all its strength. the text places the entire responsibility for the georgian war on russia, even though the international commission on the subject, headed by h. tagliavini, concluded in 2009 that the georgian authorities bore this responsibility. the report also criticises the enhanced cooperation between russia and georgia, but also the annexation of crimea to russia, which it calls an 'illegal annexation' even though the crimeans have sovereignly decided to do so, and a recent poll conducted by one of the leading german institutes showed that 93% of the inhabitants of crimea support this annexation. it is incomprehensible that the european union did not want to get involved in ensuring that the referendum took place under the best possible conditions. the rapporteur therefore concludes that russia can no longer be considered as a strategic partner. while the union's sanctions against russia have caused our producers to reduce their exports, and at the same time american exports to russia are increasing, the european union is confirming, by its atlanticist submission, that it is the idiot of the global village. i therefore voted against this report.

mr president, i am glad that we have been able to do so much in such a short time. the efsi is a new financial instrument available to private investors, but in order for them to take up and commit to it, two obstacles and two risks must be removed. the fragmentation of the internal market is the first obstacle: investors in the economic field are demanding uniformity and stability of the rules, that is to say the urgency of speeding up the removal of the barriers which still encumber the european market. the second obstacle is monetary: the lasting settlement of the greek crisis and the installation of a credible government in the euro zone must put an end to the questions and doubts about the euro. finally, while it is true that the efsi is a guarantee given to investors in return for a risk not borne by the markets, i would like to warn against two risks linked to its implementation. the first risk is that we will not be able to provide the partnership that smes expect, in contradiction with the requirement of additionality introduced in our regulation, and the second risk is that we will open the way to a deconsolidation of public investment expenditure and the associated debts.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament adopted yesterday in plenary the agreement reached with the council on the regulation establishing a european fund for strategic investments (efsi) which translates the juncker plan to boost investment in europe. i voted in favour of this agreement, which takes up parliament's demands to guarantee democratic control and transparency of the efsi. the agreement will also allow member states' contributions to the efsi and investment platforms (which may include public banks and local authorities) to be excluded from the calculation of budget deficits. this is a strong signal for the revival of public investment in europe and in our territories. with the commitment of the members of the committee on transport, we have succeeded in limiting the contribution to the efsi of the connecting europe facility, which finances the transeuropean transport networks. the agreement therefore makes it possible to clearly include a reference to transport projects, with a view to allocating efsi funds. finally, this agreement will allow the efsi to be operational quickly to meet the urgency of reviving investment. we will have to follow closely the implementation of the juncker plan, which aims to create more than eur 315 billion of investment.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the creation of the european fund for strategic investments. this investment plan, initiated by juncker, provides for €315 billion to encourage the financing of viable investments in europe, particularly in the fields of energy and digital technology: €240 billion should be devoted to investments and €75 billion to enterprises, mainly smes. the aim is to provide an additional contribution to eib investments, based on mainly private investments, by supporting more ambitious and riskier projects. this plan represents an extraordinary opportunity for europe, which must demonstrate to its citizens more than ever its capacity to overcome the crisis. the success of the fund requires a number of conditions, including the reduction of obstacles to the completion of the single european market, the implementation of structural reforms in some countries and the mobilisation of all the actors involved. we also need to ensure more transparency in the implementation of this plan, and the european parliament has ensured that responsibilities are clearly allocated in the governance of the fund, and has also ensured that its working arrangements and democratic accountability are improved.

in writing. the report provides the european parliament's opinion on developments in the economic and budgetary governance of the euro area and the union. in fact, this report encourages the eventual creation of a future economic government in europe whose aim is obviously to see the euro adopted by as many eu countries as possible. for good economic governance, the member states must respect convergence rules, rules which are becoming increasingly binding, after the maastricht criteria, the golden rule, the two-pack and the six-pack and finally the tscg, which really subject our economies and our governments to the dictates of brussels, even if these criteria are only very little respected by the member states. the report does, of course, advocate strengthening economic governance and reforms that the states must put in place. as a supporter of the sovereignty of the states, i strongly oppose this method of governance and a supranational body such as the european union should not dictate to the states their budgetary, economic or social choices. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ this report recommends strengthening the governance of monetary union to move towards harmonisation of economic and fiscal policies among euro area member states. indeed, the macroeconomic divergences in emu threaten the stability of the monetary area and confirm that the euro area is a non-optimal monetary area as explained by paul krugman, nobel prize winning american economist. the harmonization of the structural policies of the member states, which is the commission's aim, therefore means nothing more than a lowering of the wages and social protection system of the french. this anti-democratic project is once again violating the sovereignty of france. only a concerted and early exit from the single currency would allow the states to regain their monetary sovereignty. the adjustment of parities between national currencies would thus eliminate differences in competitiveness. exchange rates could even fluctuate between two boundaries under a semi-fixed exchange rate system to avoid currency war. i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ i opposed this report, which clearly favours greater economic integration of the member states of the union, in total disregard of the principle of subsidiarity and the sovereignty of the european nations. it should be remembered that the convergence rules give the commission the power to sanction any country which does not comply with the austerity requirements dictated by brussels. the members of the european parliament are therefore insisting on forcing the member states to adopt the same standards, even though the differences between the countries are too great in economic and budgetary terms, as in so many other respects. the requirements are also unrealistic: from the very beginning of the euro, two of the founding members of the union, belgium and italy, did not meet the maastricht criteria (a deficit not exceeding 3% of gdp and a public debt not exceeding 60% of gdp).

in writing. ‒ the berès report sets out the desired evolution of the union's economic and budgetary governance framework. it is very clear that it is in favour of greater integration through greater policy coordination and specific recommendation mechanisms. the federalist logic at work leads to further interference by the european union in the budgetary policies, but also in the substantive reforms, wage and social policies of the member states. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the euro. since the 2008 crisis, states have been pressured to give up some of their fiscal sovereignty, have accepted a ruinous redistributive mechanism for bailing out failing states (the european stability mechanism) and have abandoned bank supervision (the first pillar of the banking union). the complexity of the procedures and the lack of transparency in the decisions of the eurogroup are additional elements against these european convergence policies. the fn wants the states to retain the choice of their economic and budgetary policy and disputes the legitimacy of the single currency, and therefore of the convergence it implies. the report is therefore against.
in writing. this report calls once again for a utopian economic governance of the euro area based on convergence criteria (respect for a certain level of deficit and public debt) which are not based on any macroeconomic basis. indeed, according to jp morgan, the countries of the euro area are even more economically dissimilar than the countries of the world beginning with the letter m. the solution to an optimal currency area is to ensure that the factors of production, including labour, are highly mobile. however, barriers such as language or cultural differences make this quite impossible. it also requires large budgetary transfers between the core of the zone and the periphery, which are unimaginable as the greek case shows. these various solutions are, moreover, an intolerable attack on sovereignty and democracy, since they foster a supranational superstate which does not meet the expectations of the peoples. such a policy would give substance to the assertion that the construction of europe is a matter of "enlightened despotism" whose effectiveness is questionable when we consider the economic disaster to which austerity has led. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which takes stock of and sets out the challenges facing the euro area's economic governance framework, the central elements of which are the prevention of deficits, debt levels and excessive macroeconomic imbalances, and the coordination of economic policies. the weak results in this area must be acknowledged and, like the epp group of which i am a member, i regret that, since the launch of the euro, the consolidation efforts to implement the stability rules have been slackening. this lack of compliance is one of the fundamental causes of the sovereign debt crisis that has affected several euro area countries since 2009. that is why i am in favour of a sustainable fiscal consolidation and structural reforms that will increase competitiveness and invest in order to improve growth.
on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, commissioner, it is important that the european parliament can give its opinion before the commission writes its roadmap for a capital market. before you go any further in this project, i would like to draw your attention to four points. the first is to remember what happened in the banking sector. you cannot develop a capital market without, at the same time, developing supervision adapted to the progress you want to achieve. you said you wanted these capital markets for financial stability. you will then have to strengthen the european character of the supervision and regulation of these capital markets. in the same way, you will be forced to watch what happens in the shadow banking sector, otherwise you will create bubbles and tools for speculation that will not serve the noble objectives you claim. the second dimension to be taken into account is the specific disinterest in the euro area. we cannot pretend that the capital markets were totally ignorant of the currencies in which they were trading. now, as you know, you have a real challenge on your hands. as regards the third dimension, you say that all this is to enable smes to have better access to the capital markets. i guess so. but it is also necessary to use such an approach to direct capital flows where we consider we need them to finance the european project. from this point of view, there is a priority in relation to the imperatives that are linked to a strategy for the ecological transition that you must carry and that you must keep in mind when you are going to move along the path of these capital markets. finally, i should like to make one last observation. i have hardly seen any mention of taxation in your texts. i think that we cannot talk about a capital union without talking about taxation. i look forward to your suggestions in this regard.
on behalf of the enf group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the use of resources in our economy is at the crossroads of many problems which the rapporteur rightly raises: waste, dependence on imports of raw materials and energy, and the lack of a recycling economy. while the importance of short circuits is highlighted and the report claims to set a new paradigm, it does not propose any real structural changes that would give member states the tools needed for a sustainable circular economy. the increase in international trade is not in doubt. yet it is one of the main drivers of overuse of resources and pollution. the text also seeks to strengthen a regulatory framework that is already suffocating our producers and artisans, who are the pillars of local economies and the hopes of a well-established circular economy. yes, the local level is paramount and we must take it into account in our analyses. to do this, the member states are legitimate and functional. finally, in the field of hydrocarbon imports, i would like to remind you that the union's diplomatic blunders are damaging this circular economy project. the links between our nations and the producers of the persian gulf are still too strong, while the continental relations with russia are becoming more and more eroded. let us be realistic, ladies and gentlemen, the future of the environment is our land and the great continent of europe.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i share your conviction that the economical use of our resources is an urgent necessity. the circular economy concept aims to establish this imperative as a development doctrine. but is it possible to move towards such a model when the priority is given to the most anarchic liberalism, to compulsory globalisation at all levels? a true circular economy is about being able to live, produce and work in the country, and giving priority to technological research. it is also about empowering citizens rather than imposing even more regulations and constraints on them. it is not by strengthening the regulatory powers of the european commission, or by shedding a tear over food waste, that we will succeed in preserving our environmental heritage and in reducing malnutrition in the world and poverty in europe.
mr president, commissioner, the debate is clearly about the need to impose binding targets or simply to set indicators. but indicators have been around for a long time. the commission has, let us say, been very slow to tackle the question of the circular economy, and we are now seeing that, on the specific issue of waste - i am talking here about municipal waste - if we do not have a firm ambition, nothing will happen. that is why we, the group of the progressive alliance of socialists and democrats, are supporting the idea of objectives today. they have to be realistic. it should not be overregulation, but proper regulation, and it is up to you to implement it. we trust you and we will support you in this endeavour. secondly, the circular economy can be beneficial for employment. indeed, from the moment a product becomes competitive because a discarded product is less competitive , it creates jobs and innovation. we believe that today the territories must be able to practice this circular economy to fight against globalisation. we have to put resources into it. there is a budgetary aspect to this and it would be good if the european fund for strategic investments, which is part of the juncker plan, could take a strong interest in this.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this debate as the committee had recommended in the background.
in writing. ‒ the report by igor šoltes from slovenia deals with the proposed appointment of bettina michelle jakobsen from denmark as a member of the court of auditors. the text presents the curriculum vitae of ms jakobsen, deputy auditor general of the danish court of auditors since october 2009, and then gives the answers to the questionnaire to which she was submitted. i note that mrs jakobsen worked at nato headquarters from 1997 to 2002 and more recently at the eib (european investment bank). in her answers to the questionnaire, the applicant stressed her desire to be objective and impartial. the committee on budgetary control voted unanimously in favour of his nomination. i, for my part, have refrained from doing so, waiting to see whether the deeds will be in accordance with these good intentions.
in writing. ‒ this report proposes the appointment of ms bettina michelle jakobsen as a member of the european court of auditors. ms jakobsen's cv shows a strong background in denmark for 25 years as an assistant auditor at the citizens' chamber, responsible for carrying out audits in key areas related to citizens in various ministries. she has also held international positions with nato and the eib. the report also includes answers to a questionnaire sent to the company. it emphasises the objective, neutral and impartial performance of its duties, indicating that the control of public finances is an important element. we have a duty to report to the citizens and to the committee on budgetary control on the use of public funds, especially european funds. i did, however, abstain on this vote in order not to support the european institutions.
in writing. ‒ i chose to abstain on this report concerning the proposal to appoint bettina michelle jakobsen to the court of auditors. it is true that one cannot help but be impressed by ms jakobsen's background: deputy auditor general at the head of the citizens' chamber, responsible for carrying out audits in the main areas related to citizens in various danish ministries, her experience of more than 25 years in public finance may seem an asset. however, i question the legitimacy of the court of auditors and i am not particularly convinced by the assurances given by mrs jakobsen that she will carry out her mandate with objectivity, neutrality and impartiality: given her previous posts at nato and the eib, it is almost certain that she supports a globalist view. that is why i have abstained on this text.
in writing. ‒ this report proposes the appointment of ms bettina michelle jakobsen as a member of the court of auditors. in view of the experience of ms jakobsen, currently deputy auditor general in denmark in charge of the audit of the state's accounts in the public accounts committee, and following her successful hearing in the parliamentary committee in charge of budgetary control, i voted in favour of this appointment.
in writing. ‒ i abstained on this vote because i do not recognise the legitimacy of the court of auditors as an institution.

written explanations of vote
in writing. ‒ the draft resolution would like each member state to consult the union before concluding an international trade treaty. this is a further step towards further federalising the union, in defiance of the sovereignty of the member states. as a member of the europe of nations, i would like each member state to remain free to conclude trade agreements, whether with other member states or with third countries. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this debate because it is limited to a straightforward codification of the existing texts without any change in their substance.
in writing. ‒ once again, an attempt is being made to impose a 'common trade policy' on us, which is being dictated by erroneous geopolitical considerations rather than by the well-considered interests of our countries. i voted against this because i believe that each member state should be free to negotiate the trade agreements it considers to be in the interests of its own people.
in writing. ‒ this report concerns the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing union procedures in matters of common commercial policy with a view to ensuring the exercise by the union of the rights conferred on it by the rules of international trade, in particular those established under the auspices of the world trade organisation (wto). in the committee on legal affairs our members have said that each member state should be free to negotiate trade agreements itself without a decision from the european union and it is on this principle that i have decided to vote against this report.
in writing. i voted against this report setting up union procedures on the common commercial policy . i consider that each member state must retain the exercise of the rights conferred by the various rules laid down by international trade law.
in writing. ‒ making legislation simple and accessible is a priority for the european institutions. as such, codification makes it possible to group together different regulations dealing with the same subject into a single text in order to facilitate its application. i voted in favour of this report on the codification of the exercise by the union of the rights conferred on it by the rules of international trade.
in writing. ‒ the report aims to put in place procedures to ensure that the union exercises the rights conferred on it by international trade rules, in particular those established under the auspices of the wto . i am opposed in principle to article 3 of the eu treaty, which states that trade policy is the exclusive competence of the european union, with the commission as the sole interlocutor, both internally and externally, and the commission as the negotiator representing the 28 member states. under the treaties, they are not entitled to attend the negotiations and, where they are present (wto, etc.), they can only speak at national level and not at european level. this stripping of the sovereignty of the member states in trade matters thus prevents each nation from pursuing policies in the interests of its businesses, industries or citizens. denying each member state the possibility of negotiating trade agreements which are necessary or strategic for its country is a denial of freedom and development which would be to be reversed by renegotiating the treaties. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this report is to codify council regulation (ec) no 3286/94 of 22 december 1994 laying down community procedures in matters of common commercial policy with a view to ensuring the exercise by the community of the rights conferred on it by the rules of international trade, in particular those established under the auspices of the world trade organisation (wto). the legislation provides that where the union, having received a complaint on behalf of a european industry, a complaint on behalf of european undertakings or a request from a member state to initiate proceedings in the field of the common commercial policy, follows formal international consultation or dispute settlement procedures, the decisions to initiate, conduct and close such procedures shall be taken by the european commission after informing the co-legislators. i have voted in favour of this text, considering that it is merely a codification of existing legislation without any substantial changes.
in writing. ‒ the text codifies certain european rules on trade. the european commission will now be able to initiate, conduct and close international dispute settlement procedures from the moment it receives a complaint from european companies. this new procedure will improve the coherence and effectiveness of the european trade policy, which is the exclusive competence of the union. the member states will of course be informed.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text because it allows the processing industry in french guiana to survive, which depends in part on the exploitation by venezuelan fishing vessels of the living natural resources of the exclusive economic zone off the coast. given the economic and social importance of this activity in the region, venezuelan fishing vessels have been allowed to fish for several decades on the condition that part of the fish is landed in guyanese ports.
in writing. ‒ after lengthy negotiations, the aim is to allow access for venezuelan fishing vessels to french guiana waters. but this authorization is not without its counterparts: martinique vessels will henceforth be able to fish for vibnual or tuna off venezuela. in addition, 75% of the fish caught by venezuelan vessels will be landed in guyana for processing. indeed, there are longstanding links between venezuelan fishermen and french guiana canneries. it will be argued that french guiana should be able to develop its own fisheries and exploit its large fishery potential, which includes various species of shrimp and 200 species of fish. however, the counterparts so far seem to me to be satisfactory, in particular the limitation of illegal fishing by venezuelans. that is why i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ this report on fishing opportunities in eu waters for fishing vessels flying the flag of venezuela off the coast of french guiana is intended to allow venezuelan fishing vessels access to french guiana waters (41 in 2013) 12 miles offshore and allowing fish processing in french guiana. however, this report was delayed by the conflict between parliament and the council, since the council had initially adopted the agreement without consulting parliament. in return, martinican fishing vessels have the opportunity to fish for certain fish off the coast of venezuela. guyana has a large fishery potential which is still under exploited and it would be worth developing its own fisheries. however, as things stand, there are countermeasures and these limit illegal fishing by venezuelans, especially since there are historical links between venezuelan fishermen and french canneries in french guiana. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ following the floods that affected romania, bulgaria and italy in 2014, the european union decided to mobilise the solidarity fund to help these countries with €66.5 million. the cost of the 2014 spring floods in romania was estimated at eur 170 million, or 0,13% of gni. even if this amount is below the threshold for mobilising the solidarity fund, which has been set at 0,6% of gdp in relative terms or at eur 3 billion in absolute terms, the relative provision for neighbouring countries referred to in article 2 allows the mobilisation of these funds to be triggered. the floods of summer 2014 cost romania, bulgaria and italy respectively €172 million, €80 million and €2.24 billion. these amounts are below the required thresholds. nevertheless, the applications were accepted as the damage caused by these floods exceeds 1.5% of the gdp of the regions concerned. the commission has decided to compensate these regions for 2.5% of the cost of these natural disasters, which does not seem to be excessive. that is why i voted for this proposal.
