explanations of vote by oral procedure
written explanations of vote
in writing. ‒ the establishment of a multimodal ticketing system in europe would be a further step in the federalisation of the union. the protection of personal data remains very vague and no real mechanism is foreseen. the risk of a monopoly situation is high, which would automatically lead to higher costs for users. as a defender of the sovereignty of states and of the europe of nations, i am firmly opposed to any attempt to federalise the union. as consumer protection is also one of my priorities, i voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this debate because the ultimate aim of this decision is to offer travellers a multimodal and crossborder solution, without interruption, door to door, thus promoting access to quality public transport for all.
in writing. ‒ clearly, this project to create an integrated multimodal ticketing system has many advantages, especially for those of our fellow citizens who are regularly travelling across our old continent. the proposal is all the more attractive because it is based on galileo, the european geolocation system, which is a competitor to the us gps. however, the undeniable advantages of this project are counterbalanced by major disadvantages: since mobility is facilitated, there is a risk that this will result in a reduction in controls. at a time when the union is experiencing unprecedented immigration and a high risk of terrorist attacks, facilitating mobility and reducing controls does not seem to me to be a good solution; the price of tickets may increase significantly to pay for the system (except in the case of outsourcing); the commission has not yet adopted a proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment in the event of accidents. the question of the protection of personal data is too vague. that is why my colleagues and i have finally voted against it.
in writing. ‒ this project to create an integrated multimodal ticketing system is a key tool for the realisation of the single european transport area and the single european market promoted by the union. the integrated ticket would thus make it possible to travel with a single ticket and to choose the optimal solution useful to the user. the report sets out a number of objectives, ranging from equipping all modes of transport with intelligent transmission systems by 2023 to establishing a single national information system to link regional and local timetables, in order to promote greater use of public transport and to promote the environment. even if there are positive points in it to promote mobility and reduce constraints for users such as the use of the galileo system, we cannot support this report because our differences are too great. the facilitation of mobility may entail risks because of the reduction of controls, but it is also possible to foresee an increase in the prices for implementing this system. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ the european single market provides for the free movement of goods and people in all the member states of the union. as such, transport policies in europe are fundamental issues. there is a need to increase the sustainability, cost-effectiveness and energy efficiency of our transport. this report proposes the establishment of an integrated multimodal ticketing system in europe. this system will provide access throughout the union to comprehensive information on transport options throughout the union. it will greatly facilitate access to transport for european travellers. it will also help to lay the foundations for a single european transport area. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i opposed this report, which is part of the logic of a single european transport area, and therefore of the single market and of the strengthening of integration. the objectives of a multimodal ticketing system are to standardize transport services with an increase in the importance of cross-border services. while some of the potential benefits of such a system seem interesting - such as facilitating mobility within the european territory or allowing users to choose the optimal solution for their journey - there are many points to be criticized in this project. in addition to the fact that the single market is based on a globalist ideology to the detriment of citizens, the facilitation of mobility risks leading to a reduction in controls, even though the union is currently experiencing uncontrolled immigration which poses serious problems in terms of security and social welfare. the introduction of such a system could also lead to a cost to the price of tickets that would be a heavy burden on citizens. finally, on the issue of the protection of personal data, the report remains very vague and this lack of transparency poses a risk to the respect for citizens' privacy.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report proposes the creation of an integrated multimodal ticketing system within the european union. such a system aims to facilitate and encourage the multimodal travel of european citizens and will address the issues of sustainability, economic viability, energy efficiency and environmental friendliness in transport. conscious of the need to offer, in the long term and despite the technical and material difficulties of such a project, the possibility of continuous travel to individuals throughout the union through multimodal, crossborder and innovative solutions, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the commission has made an ambitious proposal to eventually create an integrated ticketing system for travel throughout the union and across several modes of transport. european citizens would have a single ticket and an electronic reservation system. this requires that the offers of private and public operators in the 28 member states are accessible to all on an online platform. such a prospect would not only make traffic more fluid, but would also be a major step forward for the free movement of persons. we hereby call on the commission to make efforts in this direction and set a date for 2020 to assess progress.
in writing. ‒ the introduction of a single ticketing system for transport in europe is a practical and useful step forward for european citizens who travel across several eu member states for both business and personal reasons. the european parliament wants european operators to develop a single integrated ticket for passengers using several modes of transport in different countries. this implies the sharing of timetable information between the different operators in due course. we will be closely monitoring progress towards the practical implementation of this single ticket. if the private sector's progress is not sufficient by 2020, then the commission will have to come forward with a legislative proposal.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on the creation of an integrated multimodal ticketing system in europe. this text is designed to facilitate mobility within the european area. this would make it easier for travellers to cross borders without difficulty. it seems that, apart from the risk of fewer checks, the present situation does not lend itself to facilitating travel. indeed, what about the migration flows and the already very weak monitoring of them at the border crossing? in addition, the increased terrorist threats in recent weeks have forced us to be cautious rather than more open. public decision-makers are meant to protect citizens by controlling their territory and ensuring control of those who enter it. the union is preventing us from doing so and would like to subject our states to more flows. so this project is neither serious nor responsible.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it does not take sufficient account of the protection of personal data, creates a monopoly situation and leads to an increase in costs.
in writing. ‒ as a member of the committee on transport and tourism from 2004 to 2014, i voted enthusiastically for this resolution which calls for the implementation of a single ticket for transport in the european union: a very concrete and very practical step forward which would make life easier for travellers in europe. the ease, convenience and availability of travel information provided by such integrated multimodal ticketing systems will attract european travellers to public transport. in addition, such a system would put an end to websites and mobile applications that prevent the purchase of tickets for domestic and crossborder journeys, which i welcome, being from a crossborder constituency par excellence. the commission's proposal is based on the principle of subsidiarity, which is the basis of the treaty of rome.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this debate because it amputates the galileo project and because, overall, the european union's migration policy is a disaster
in writing. ‒ in may 2015, the commission published its 'european agenda on migration', a much-awaited policy document since the beginning of the new commission's mandate and especially in view of the tragic events in the mediterranean sea in recent months. with this agenda, the commission is finally taking stock of the scale and scope of the migration phenomenon in europe, at a time when we have been calling for years for european management and a genuine european migration policy. i welcomed the commission's intention to increase the union's resources for managing migration and refugee flows, to strengthen frontex's capacity and to triple the budget for european rescue operations, and the commission's immediate budgetary proposal translating these announcements into clear and concrete budgetary commitments. i therefore welcome today the swift agreement reached between parliament and the council to increase the european budget for 2015 by eur 75 722 000 (in commitment appropriations) in this respect, which is proof that the european union is capable of dealing with emergency situations and taking action.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of an amendment to the 2015 budget. it is essential that additional funding be allocated as quickly as possible to deal with the tragedies in the mediterranean and the increase in migration flows. the budget allocated of eur 75 million is not up to the challenge, but it was crucial that parliament approve this decision quickly to respond to the humanitarian emergency that is playing out on the eu's doorstep. this decision must be accompanied by a new approach to european funding for migration. an ambitious union policy, both to deal with the emergency and to look at the medium and long term, can only be achieved if it is adequately financed. it is not the first time that parliament has sounded the alarm by calling for a substantial increase in the appropriations allocated to the union's migration policies. this increase in funding must of course be accompanied by strict control of the use of funds and greater transparency in the procurement and subcontracting procedures, because of the abuses already noted in the use of these funds in the member states.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament supported the commission's proposal to increase the budget for migration by the end of the year in order to respond to the unprecedented crisis europe is currently experiencing. the financial, technical and human resources of the european external borders agency frontex, the european asylum support office and the european police office europol will be strengthened. the asylum, immigration and integration fund (amif) to support member states' actions will also be increased. in total, these agencies will receive an additional €75 million. i welcome this decision, which responds to an urgency and a need, given the migratory phenomenon we are experiencing with more than 150 000 migrants having crossed the mediterranean since the beginning of the year.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to vote against the report on draft amending budget no 5/2015. the report focuses in particular on the resumption of the frontex surveillance agency. if the latter was supposed to guard our borders, we can only see that it has failed and that today it is mainly used to bring boats of illegal immigrants back to europe, to ensure that they do not sink at sea. the report calls for a substantial increase in frontex funding to eur 89 million. if such an increase seems to be in the right direction, we know that in practice we cannot fight illegal immigration in this way. frontex must either be abolished or be radically redesigned so that it can effectively and finally fulfil its mission: to stop all illegal immigration to the european union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, mr eider gardiazabal rubial, on the draft amending budget to deal with migratory pressures. the report strengthens the union's capacity to deal with asylum and migration by increasing the financial resources of three agencies: frontex, europol and easo. the report proposes to create 23 additional posts at these three agencies to meet the increase in activity. the appropriations for two other agencies (amif and isf) were also increased. i welcome the fact that this report was adopted by a large majority.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on draft amending budget no 5/2015 of the european union for the financial year 2015 coping with migratory pressures. this amending budget would strengthen the union's resources in the field of asylum and migration by increasing the budget of the agencies concerned, while keeping the level of payments in 2015 unchanged, as it is a redeployment of appropriations from the galileo programme, which has fallen behind schedule.
in writing. ‒ following the tragedies in the mediterranean linked to the influx of migrants, the union presents draft amending budget no 5 for the financial year 2015 aimed at 'strengthening eu resources for the management of migration and refugee flows'. the commission has therefore decided to: 1) increase the appropriations for the frontex agency (26.8 million), to triple the funding for operations triton and poseidon for the remainder of 2015, the effectiveness of which is more than hypothetical since it is limited to completely unnecessary monitoring missions; 2) to better distribute the "burden" of asylum in order to "accept an ever-increasing number of migrants". in total, this means an increase in funding of €89 million in commitment appropriations, the bulk of which is taken from the galileo programme budget. it goes without saying that this plan will prove to be completely useless and even harmful since it creates a gigantic air demand. the only solution is to re-establish national borders and adopt a policy of firmness along the lines of australia. so i decided to vote against it.
in writing. - i voted against it. the project will remove €89 million from the galileo programme budget to benefit refugee aid programmes. under the guise of a better distribution of the burden of asylum, we are actually giving ourselves a good conscience by accepting even more refugees than we can in any case take in under decent conditions.
in writing. ‒ this report proposes to approve an increase in resources for the management of migration flows. in reality, the main aim is to strengthen the security capabilities of frontex and europol rather than to prevent human tragedies in the mediterranean or to eliminate the causes of immigration suffered by migrants who are forced to leave their countries. the most indecent and grotesque aspect, however, is the way in which this extension is financed: a cutting of the galileo programme, which is vital for the union's technological autonomy and also for information on migration in the mediterranean. i am voting against these short-sighted budgetary maneuvers.
in writing. ‒ this draft budget provides for an increase in order to better manage migration flows. the budget provides for an increase in the appropriations for the frontex surveillance agency. it is worth noting that this budget allocated to frontex is intended to strengthen border surveillance, whereas we know that it is too late to monitor and that we must take concrete action against immigration. the total increase is €89 million and a good part of this would be taken from the galileo budget which should not be cut. while we might have thought that this increase in appropriations would go our way to combat immigration in particular, we see that as always the union does not propose a concrete solution. the member therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ the proposal is to increase the union's resources for managing migration and refugee flows. the commission is also proposing to increase the number of member states that have not yet adopted the euro. the final figure would be €89 million more, at the expense of the galileo satellite positioning system. we are against this text.
in writing. ‒ following the tragedies in the mediterranean linked to the influx of migrants, the union presents draft amending budget no 5 for the financial year 2015 aimed at 'strengthening eu resources for the management of migration and refugee flows'. the aim is therefore to increase the appropriations of the frontex agency (26.8 million), to triple the funding of operations triton and poseidon for the rest of 2015, the effectiveness of which is more than hypothetical since we limit ourselves to completely useless monitoring missions; to better distribute the "burdens" in the field of asylum in order to "accept an ever greater number of migrants". in total, this means an increase in funding of €89 million in commitment appropriations, the bulk of which is taken from the galileo programme budget. it goes without saying that this plan will prove to be completely useless and even harmful since it creates a gigantic air demand. the only solution is to re-establish national borders and adopt a policy of firmness along the lines of australia. so i decided to vote against it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text on the budgetary aspect of eu migration policy for 2015. the aim is to increase the financial resources of three eu agencies - frontex, the european asylum support office and europol - and to create 23 posts between them. the appropriations for the asylum, migration and integration fund and the internal security fund are also increased. the operation remains financially neutral, with the unused appropriations from the galileo programme being redistributed to these agencies.
in writing. ‒ following the tragedies in the mediterranean caused by the influx of migrants, the eu presents draft amending budget no 5 for the financial year 2015 aimed at 'strengthening eu resources for the management of migration and refugee flows'. the commission has therefore decided to increase the appropriations for the frontex agency (26.8 million) in order to triple the funding for operations triton and poseidon for the remainder of 2015, while their effectiveness is more than hypothetical since they are limited to completely unnecessary monitoring missions, and to better distribute the "burden" in the area of asylum in order to "accept an ever greater number of migrants". in total, the increase in funding was mainly in the form of commitment appropriations of eur 89 million, the bulk of which was taken from the galileo programme budget. it goes without saying that this plan will prove to be completely useless and rather harmful, since it creates a gigantic air demand. the only solution is to re-establish national borders and adopt a policy of firmness along the lines of australia. so i decided to vote against it.
in writing. ‒ in the face of the urgent migration situation, the commission proposed to reallocate some lines of the budget surplus to cope with migratory pressures. i voted in favour of this amending budget. the amendment aims to strengthen the union's capacity to deal with asylum and migration by increasing the financial resources of three agencies (frontex, the european asylum office and europol). other funds related to migration and security issues have also been strengthened.
in writing. ‒ this amending budget, which increases the eu's budgetary appropriations for migration and asylum, is a first step towards helping the union and the member states to better cope with the reality of migration. this phenomenon requires an urgent response, but also a longer-term one. however, the amounts allocated will not be sufficient to meet the real needs and to finance the measures of the european programme on migration. it is essential that the european budget for 2016 address these shortcomings. the proposal to increase easo's staff by four posts is clearly insufficient in view of the increasing role of the agency. the priority is given as always to frontex. of course, it is crucial to strengthen search and rescue operations at sea to save lives. but beyond that, it's time for a paradigm shift. instead of being locked into the costly and inefficient logic of border control and return policy, let us develop a real policy of welcoming and integrating migrants. legal migration is not a problem but an opportunity, which will bring real economic and social added value to the european union, for the benefit of all.
in writing. ‒ once again we had to decide on migration policies. this time it was a question of integrating the budgetary consequences of the 'european agenda on migration', which gave rise to the surrealist debates known in the council, where the member states hesitated to allocate some 40 000 asylum seekers, or 0.005% of the european population. the title of the amending budget says it all: 'coping with migratory pressures'. the message is clear, it is not about meeting the protection needs of syrian and eritrean refugees (to name just a few) seeking protection in europe, but only about strengthening fortress europe. while i can support an increase in the budget allocated to the development of a genuine common european asylum system, i have my doubts when we see that it is primarily a question of identifying potential asylum seekers in order to better deport them in the event of rejection of their application. we have little information on the actual use of these funds, which were financed by a redistribution of appropriations to the detriment of the galileo project. i refuse to risk giving the commission a blank cheque in this context and therefore voted against.
explanations of vote by oral procedure
written explanations of vote
in writing. ‒ the end of milk quotas, which came into effect on 31 march, together with a russian embargo on this sector, has put producers in difficulty. it is the rural areas that are obviously most affected, particularly isolated areas such as mountainous areas. the european union is trying to solve the problems it has created with this proposal. this report attempts to reintroduce some market measures. it is therefore an initiative, albeit modest, which is in the right direction, and that is why i supported it.
in writing. ‒ in a particularly difficult context for the european dairy sector, i voted in favour of this report. the milk package is a useful instrument for maintaining the stability of dairy farmers' incomes and for anticipating certain economic accidents. i would like the commission to make this text one of its priorities and to step up controls on large retailers and to encourage concentration in the sector and greater territorial differentiation.
in writing. ‒ until 31 march, milk quotas limited milk production in each country in order to avoid a too sharp fall in the price paid to farmers: the abolition of these quotas constitutes a serious threat to french producers. the fact is that while european farmers can now produce as much as they want, it is primarily the countries with low production costs that will benefit. the end of quotas will thus increase competition between the french sector (the second largest european producer of cow's milk after germany) and the large producers in northern europe, which are not subject to the same standards as our farmers. international competition will therefore encourage all forms of dumping and an increase in imports, leading to a loss of market share for dairy products manufactured in france. the report was intended to introduce some measures to remedy the most obvious adverse effects of this total liberalisation of the milk market. however, the timidity of the proposed measures and their catch-all nature led me to abstain.
in writing. ‒ as of 31 march 2015, the milk quotas have effectively and definitively ended in the union. this has caused great tension and concern for the dairy industry. already hit hard by the crisis, deregulation of markets and the eu's lax standards, our farmers, especially small farms, are at risk of losing even more purchasing power (many often sell at a loss in this sector!). in addition, the russian embargo following the union measures has aggravated the difficulties of the sector. although the text contains measures to protect farmers, such as the introduction of concrete aid in areas at risk and the strengthening of the power of producer organisations in contract negotiations, it does not in any way call into question the liberal agricultural policies pursued by the union for years. worse, paragraph 72 of the act mentions 'the possibility of using risk management instruments, such as futures markets, to take advantage of the volatility of the sector to increase its competitiveness'. a sector that is totally liberalized and subject to the laws of the market! i therefore abstained on this report.
in writing. ‒ the motion for a resolution on the implementation of the milk package suggests once again that the european union must correct the undesirable effects of its agricultural policy, and this at the expense of the dairy sector. the end of the milk quotas, previously introduced by the union, has been effective since march 2015. this has raised serious concerns about falling prices and the disappearance of small farms in rural areas, in a context of russian counter-sanctions that have worsened the sector's difficulties. the commission's proposal proposes to take concrete aid measures to preserve the territorial balance and enable the sector to cope with the liberalisation imposed by the union. this motion for a resolution seeks to resolve the difficulties of a strategic sector of the french economy. it also demonstrates the eu's leadership by not allowing the member states to pursue their own policies. for these reasons i abstained on the vote on this text.
in writing. ‒ i wanted to support this report which seeks to stem the disastrous effects of the end of milk quotas which expired on 31 march 2015 in line with the decision taken in the 2003 cap mid-term review. the text thus recalls the important role of dairy farming in terms of land use planning, rural employment and economic, environmental and social development of many european agricultural regions. taking into account the adverse effects of the russian embargo on our agricultural production, the report gives a genuine recognition of the crisis in the dairy sector and calls on the commission to intervene by introducing additional targeted market measures, in particular to counter the effects of the downward pressure on prices resulting from the lack of adequate instruments to prevent the crisis, a drop in world demand, the volatility of prices at world level. although he remains timid about what measures should be taken to protect our farmers, i have therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the aim of this own-initiative report is to take stock of the implementation of the milk package and to propose a new european milk policy following the end of the quota system. in view of the serious situation of the dairy sector, with its prices falling, i am convinced that market law alone will not prevent a new crisis similar to that of 2008. new regulatory tools must be put in place to avoid overproduction in the long term to the detriment of the whole of europe. as such, some solutions exist, such as strengthening contractual arrangements between producers and distributors, developing dynamic crisis management tools and making essential use of the milk market observatory, set up during the last reform of the cap. i believe that it is essential to help dairy farms and to ensure that farmers are able to meet the demands of the market, and i therefore voted in favour of this report, which must not be forgotten and which must be heard by the commission.
in writing. the common agricultural policy has long been marked by the milk quota system. the commission notes that the measure is not intended to compensate for the additional costs of the milk levy. i voted in favour of this text which takes stock of the implementation of this new regulatory model. for the past two months, farmers and processors have had to fill in compulsory declarations of quantities of milk supplied. these are accompanied by contracts between the states and the producer organisations, aimed at planning production while ensuring the balance between the different links in the milk supply chain. finally, the change of regime in the dairy sector must be accompanied by increased vigilance against market disturbances. the data provided by the european milk market observatory will be valuable in this respect.
in writing. ‒ european milk producers are facing major structural challenges with the end of milk quotas and cyclical challenges with the consequences of the russian embargo. they must have assistance from the union to deal with them. firstly, the union must have the tools to respond to crisis situations, given the particularly volatile nature of the food market. it must also be able to protect producers against certain unfair trading practices from third countries. secondly, the union must help the dairy sector to regain its competitiveness. this sector needs all our support because it has been very destabilized by the abolition of milk quotas. export markets need to be diversified and new outlets identified. finally, the recognition of producer and farmer organisations needs to be improved.
in writing. ‒ as milk quotas ended on 31 march 2015, this report provides a timely and useful assessment of the implementation of the 'milk package', which is why i voted in favour. dairy farming plays an important role in many agricultural regions in europe in terms of land use, rural employment and economic and social development. although the dairy sector has long-term potential for growth and job creation, the market outlook is currently uncertain, with very high price volatility, in the context of the prolonged russian embargo. it is therefore important to: facilitate the exchange of information and the consultation of producers in order to enable them to take account of market developments and to anticipate crises; promote inter-branch management tools; adapt the market intervention tools, since intervention prices must be adapted to production costs in the member states; the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the new rules and will continue to monitor the implementation of the new rules. finally, unfair trading practices, which severely limit the profitability and ability of firms to invest and thus adapt to markets, must be tackled.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the future of the european milk sector: review of the implementation of the milk package. it is trying very hard to bring some measures to the crisis left by the disappearance of milk quotas. many farmers complain that this is being done in favour of large industrial groups capable of mass production, which is having a negative effect on the final price of milk. the small farms suffer the direct consequences of this suppression by selling their milk at a loss. it should also be noted that this does not encourage short circuits, which are carried by local farmers and herders and not by the powerful in the sector. the union is therefore trying to remedy a situation which it has itself created.
in writing. ‒ i abstained on this report because, beyond certain measures of common sense, it advocates securitisation of agricultural production, particularly on futures markets, which i am totally opposed to.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because the 'milk package', which came into force in 2012, is an important tool to address the challenges facing the dairy sector, particularly in terms of market management now that the quota system has disappeared. the abolition of quotas could lead to a further concentration of milk production to the benefit of the larger dairy farms and to the detriment of the smaller producers, whom we must therefore protect. i regret, however, that the implementation of the milk package has been rather disappointing so far. it needs to be improved, and i support in particular the development of additional tools to better anticipate and deal with crisis situations and market volatility, which is a major challenge for producers.
in writing. ‒ the crisis facing milk producers since the end of the milk quota system shows that the european union was insufficiently prepared for a situation of extreme gravity that we could have predicted. the existence of dairy farms is not only essential to our economies, it is also essential to the identity of our countryside. the current episode of extreme price volatility combined with unfair trading practices in certain sectors of the supply chain exposes farmers to an unstable situation, placing them in a state of vulnerability and discouragement that is strictly intolerable. europe's role is to support efforts to modernise and invest in agriculture so that it can face global competition. it is certainly not to be destroyed by the mere force of market law. it is urgent to propose a new european milk policy which will establish mechanisms for more relaxed regulation of the dairy sector.
in writing. ‒ the end of milk quotas, which came into effect on 31 march, together with a russian embargo in this sector, has put producers in difficulty. it is the rural areas that are obviously most affected, particularly isolated areas such as mountainous areas. the european union is trying to solve the problems it has created with this proposal. this report attempts to reintroduce some market measures. i therefore decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of my colleague john nicholson's report on the implementation of the milk package. in view of the end of milk quotas on 31 march 2015, the union had put in place a measure to ensure a better balance between milk producers and their buyers so that producers are not disadvantaged by traders. the report recalls the importance of milk producers for europe's food independence and their vulnerability. the text also stresses the inadequacy of the current security measures to deal with the new challenges that the end of milk quotas will create. i welcome the fact that this report was adopted by a large majority.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the future of the european dairy sector. in view of the difficulties affecting national milk markets, notably due to the russian embargo, it is essential to give priority to this issue and to strengthen targeted market measures in order to make the dairy sector viable, competitive and sustainable in the union.
in writing. ‒ last year saw a sharp fluctuation in the prices of milk and certain components for milk production. as it stands, the prices paid to producers are well below the costs of production. to top it all off, the end of production quotas aggravates these trends by no longer guaranteeing fair incomes and by seriously undermining the viability of small farms. in the end, we are seeing a strengthening of large producers at the expense of small ones, concentrating production more and more, against consumer choice, environmental rules and the activity of rural areas. this resolution rightly raises alarm bells for dairy farmers, but it does not call for any change in the current production rules. it merely calls for playing with the current instruments, when they have no impact on the trends of funds! i am, on the contrary, in favour of price controls and i am calling for a mechanism of remunerative prices on production volumes to compensate farmers for their work. that is why i opposed the adoption of this report, which does not provide any financial solution to the current crisis in our countryside.
in writing. - i abstained on this text. it is true that he has the merit of trying to help dairy farmers who are in a worrying economic situation. it aims in particular to strengthen the power of producer organisations to negotiate milk sales contracts. however, this text will not work miracles. the end of milk quotas has plunged milk producers into lasting difficulties, by unwarrantedly submitting their production to the law of the market. much more serious is the fact that this text endorses the new system by giving in to the ultra-liberalism prevailing in the country, particularly in paragraph 72.

explanations of vote by oral procedure
written explanations of vote
in writing. ‒ this report particularly promotes public-private partnerships, which are presented as beneficial for the european economy. these public-private partnerships prove to be so disastrous financially for public authorities that there are many examples where initial funding projects are abandoned in order to limit the explosion of costs. the question of the development of such partnerships in third countries is therefore a matter of concern, particularly for emerging countries which could soon be victims of the same plunder as that suffered by french public authorities. moreover, access to national markets by foreign firms through these partnerships is questionable. companies from 'protectionist' countries will be able to win easily accessible public contracts without necessarily having to reciprocate. once again, the union tolerates this kind of distortion of competition without anyone reacting. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that smes are the engine of job and wealth creation in developing countries, and that they generate about 90% of jobs. it is therefore essential to engage more closely with smes and start-ups, both local and private, as they are essential for the mobilisation of resources and job creation at national or european level, in public-private partnerships to mobilise long-term funding, stimulate innovation in technologies and business models and define private sector accountability mechanisms.
in writing. ‒ this report is a very liberal catechism, which says that there can be no economic dynamism unless there is more "interaction" between the public and private sectors, through joint ventures and other joint projects: the text emphasises ppps (public-private partnerships). in fact, it turns out that ppps are primarily used to deregulate and liberalise public sectors, such as health care. that is why i voted against this text.
in writing. this report on the external impact of the union's trade and investment policy in third countries tries to make us believe that public-private interactions, joint ventures or joint projects are inherently good for the economy. while it is good in areas such as research to engage more in public-private partnerships, this should not encourage or favour ppps, the negative effects of which we know, since the final costs are often higher (and even more so than if there had been public borrowing in many cases). the report therefore encourages the use of such a system, particularly in emerging countries, to cope with the lack of financial resources. however, other measures such as customs duties are never mentioned in european policies. so i decided against your report.
in writing. ‒ the european economy is still suffering from a significant slowdown due to the crisis. it is necessary to stimulate job creation and restore real competitiveness and productivity within the union in order to restart sustainable growth. investment outside the single market could be a major source of growth for eu enterprises. this report aims to strengthen the instruments of our companies, especially smes, enabling them to compete in foreign markets. increased participation by european enterprises in large-scale international projects, particularly in public-private partnerships, could bring substantial productivity and competitiveness benefits. i would like to stress the importance of reciprocity and fair competition in our trade relations with third countries. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report, which is based more on beliefs than on facts in relation to development, in this particular case, particularly for third countries. the idea is that only interactions between the public and private sectors in joint projects or joint ventures would boost economic dynamism, the model being public-private partnerships. the costs of public investment in the latter are too often overlooked, even though they can be an alternative for infrastructure financing. the problem is that in this context our public procurement is open to companies from countries which are protective. the report calls for a complete reduction in this asymmetry, but does not give any real prospect of negotiation. while the desire to ensure that our companies have access to third-party public procurement is welcome, it is inconceivable to try to introduce wto-style dispute settlement mechanisms once again, to the detriment of national courts.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report aims to examine the challenges posed by public-private partnerships for european smes in the context of the union's common commercial policy. the approach advocated is to strengthen the competitiveness of european companies when participating in public procurement in third countries. given that there are a number of potential economic benefits and inherent risks that can be shared between the public and private sectors, i believe that european companies should be able to participate in large-scale international projects in the form of public-private partnerships and that the european institutions should take steps to promote this participation. for these reasons i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the internal market operates in accordance with the principle of free competition, not only for the benefit of european operators but also for companies established in third countries. this policy of openness also applies to public procurement. conversely, some of the union's trading partners continue to favour national operators, mainly when it comes to concluding public-private partnership contracts. we have asked, by voting on this text, that free trade agreements with third countries, negotiated by the commission on behalf of the european union, include clauses opening public procurement procedures to european companies.
in writing. ‒ the text codifies certain european rules on trade. the european commission will now be able to initiate, conduct and close international dispute settlement procedures from the moment it receives a complaint from european companies. this new procedure will improve the coherence and effectiveness of the european trade policy, which is the exclusive competence of the union. the member states will of course be informed.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this resolution because i am opposed to public-private partnerships on principle
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by my colleague jan zahradil on the external impact of the union's trade and investment policy in third countries. the report encourages the union to promote public-private partnerships involving european companies in countries outside the union. the text recalls that these partnerships can have extremely positive effects for smes and european companies, but that they must be reciprocal, since european markets are already very open, unlike those of many third countries. i welcome the fact that this report was adopted by a large majority.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the external impact of the union's trade and investment policy on public-private initiatives in third countries. the establishment of public-private partnerships in third countries, in accordance with the principles of good governance, would create decent jobs and combat poverty in developing countries and open up new employment and growth opportunities for european companies that still face obstacles to their development abroad.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the resolution on the external impact of the union's trade and investment policy on public-private initiatives in third countries. the front national is opposed to public-private partnerships, which are a tool for deregulation and liberalisation, and which open up the health sector to the private sector in particular. the report by mr zahradil is entirely in line with the logic of ppps. that is why i supported amendment no 1, which fundamentally rewrites this report, but which unfortunately was not adopted.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it is in favour of public-private partnerships (ppps), which i am opposed to. ppps are very costly for public investment.
in writing. - i voted against it. while the costs of public-private partnerships are very high, they are described in this text as the solution for developing infrastructure in emerging countries. the report recommends the establishment of well-defined policies to address the differences in openness between our public procurement and that of other countries. unfortunately, there is no indication of what can be done in the field of negotiations. the creation of information and assistance platforms to support our companies in accessing public procurement in third countries is recommended, as is the establishment of dispute settlement mechanisms with these third countries. however, we refuse to support this text because we believe that public-private partnerships are not a good solution and because the commission is always trying to gain more and more power.
in writing. - i voted against this report. we cannot support public-private partnerships (ppps), which are catastrophic in terms of the cost of public investment, giving a free hand to private multinationals, without allowing small and mediumsized enterprises (smes) to have a certain weight. we therefore disagree with the commission, which considers these partnerships to be good. we therefore condemn the asymmetry which allows firms in protectionist markets to access our open public procurement.
in writing. ‒ the zahradil report sets out to consider the creation of a new legal framework for public-private partnerships (ppps). it also seeks to promote an international definition of ppps, listing their advantages, limitations and prospects for improvement. the report is commendable for its clarity in calling on the commission to take a very high view of the openness it has imposed on european public procurement, even though many of our partners are not acting with the same naivety (the discussions on the transatlantic treaty with the united states show this daily). the rapporteur also makes some interesting points, specifying in particular that ppps should not be a first step towards privatising the public services of the countries concerned. the report goes too far, however, in asserting that public-private partnerships should be the preferred instrument for encouraging the development of the countries of the south. it also tends to see ppps as both an effective substitute for declining public spending and a good way to revive growth in europe. in view of this flawed reasoning and the liberal tropism of the rapporteur, i abstained on this report.
in writing. ‒ the report begins by stating as a well-established fact that 'societies benefit from an environment favourable to interaction between the public and private sectors'. the text aims to promote public-private partnerships, particularly in developing countries. the report calls for the markets of these countries to be opened up to european companies, which will be able to meet their important infrastructure needs. i vote against this law which is unjust and which plans to plunder developing countries.
in writing. this report tries to make us believe that public-private interactions, joint ventures or joint projects are inherently good for the economy. however, while this willingness to break down the walls between the public and private sectors is sometimes necessary and beneficial, particularly in research, this should not be seen as a blanket endorsement of public-private partnerships, whose harmfulness is well known: the costs are passed on to future generations and the projects are often more expensive than pure public investment. the report encourages its development in the emerging countries to cope with the lack of budgetary resources! one of the resources that remains taboo for the europeans could be customs duties which have been largely abolished under the auspices of the wto. the report also calls for the "absorption of the asymmetry of openness" between public procurement in the eu and in other countries, without disclosing any means of achieving this. i therefore voted against this text which extols the merits of public-private partnerships.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the union's trade and investment policy in third countries. this text states that a country's societies and economic structures benefit from an environment conducive to interaction between the public and private sectors and to cooperation between public and private entities, including through joint projects and joint ventures. public-private partnerships are a driver for economic growth, innovation, competitiveness and job creation, both inside and outside the single market. they also play a strategic role in the modernisation of infrastructure, including energy, road, digital and water supply infrastructure. the report also points out that eu companies are well placed to win and manage these markets.
in writing. i voted against this rapporteur who shamelessly promotes public-private partnerships in developing countries. we know that these new public procurement models are a financial ditch for local authorities to the benefit of companies, who use them to make a fat profit off the taxpayers.
in writing. ‒ the report recommends that enterprises in the member states develop public-private partnerships in third countries. however, it does not envisage any serious way of allowing these same companies access to external markets protected by protectionist measures, whereas public procurement in the union must be open, even without reciprocity. again, this is pure ideology, a dogma imposing practices that have proven ineffective and even harmful (the example of the georges-pompidou hospital in paris alone should disgust anyone of sound mind with the concept of public-private partnership). worse still, this ideology is still applied at the expense of the economies of the countries of the union, because the other states of the world retain the protections that are in their interest and do not hesitate to take all the necessary measures to safeguard the sectors they consider strategic. once again, in the name of an absurd liberal dogma, it is the union's businesses, and therefore the citizens, who are the butt of the farce. i shall of course vote against this report.
in writing. ‒ in the face of increased trade between the european union and third countries, and the growth of european investment in third countries, it is important to protect the interests of our businesses and ensure the competitiveness of the european economy. in this context, the european parliament adopted a report on the external impact of the union's trade and investment policy in third countries. i voted in favour of this report. the text also stresses the importance of public-private partnerships in trade between the union and third countries.
in writing. ‒ public-private partnerships (ppps) are long-term contracts between the government and a private partner, whereby the private partner provides and finances a public service using assets and sharing the associated risks. the public sector can thus benefit from and benefit from the experience of the private sector in its construction. these ppps represent a number of potential benefits and inherent risks. increased participation of european enterprises in international projects under these ppps could have positive effects on job creation, productivity, competitiveness, technology and innovation. however, this development must take place in the context of positive reciprocity in public procurement and access to ppps. investors must have sufficient legal and good governance guarantees for their long-term investments, and smes must be able to become more competitive in international markets. i therefore supported this report, which calls for measures to promote the participation of european companies, especially smes, in ppps.
in writing. ‒ this report explains that public-private interactions, joint ventures and joint projects are good for economic dynamism (including public-private partnerships). public-private partnerships are catastrophic in terms of the cost of public investment and are described as the way to develop infrastructure in emerging countries, given the lack of budgetary resources. the tools to be implemented by the commission, council and parliament according to this report are: - to address the asymmetry of openness between our public procurement and that of other countries by requests for openness! however, no real negotiation is envisaged;- creating information and assistance platforms for our companies to have access to third-party public contracts;- working on the establishment of mechanisms for settling disputes with third countries so that our investments are well protected. this may mean the shunting of national courts. we obviously disagree with this report both in the use of ppps and in the commission's desire to take advantage of its power. i vote against it.
in writing. ‒ this report deals with public-private partnerships (ppps) and their promotion in relations with third countries. the initial observation, which 'considers it regrettable that the union has kept its public procurement very largely open to international competition', can only be shared. however, the conclusion drawn is cynical: if free trade has wreaked havoc in europe, there is no reason why the union's trading partners should not also pay the price! the report therefore focuses on the enormous infrastructure needs in developing countries and calls for the opening up of markets for european companies. the 'economic partnership' agreements (epas) for african countries, but also free trade agreements of all kinds with tunisia, mexico, vietnam, etc., are covered here. with my group in the gue-ngl, i oppose deregulation and liberalisation of the public sector, the diversion of development funds to private enterprises and the damage already caused by ppps in developing countries, particularly in the agriculture and health sectors. i therefore voted against this report.
explanations of vote by oral procedure
written explanations of vote
in writing. ‒ the fruit and vegetable sector will need to be reformed in the coming months. the melo report, to which i have made several contributions, makes a number of recommendations to this end. the most important are: - adapting and clarifying the rules governing the creation of producer organisations so that the sector is better organised collectively; - increasing support for producer organisations; - introducing crisis prevention and management instruments; - combating unfair trading practices in the food chain, especially in the retail sector; - strengthening sustainability and environmental protection; - stimulating innovation and research; - promoting short-circuits and school fruit and vegetable consumption programmes; - applying reciprocity in external trade; - fighting more effectively against the import of organisms harmful to plants. i will support this important own-initiative report on the economy and employment, particularly in the mediterranean regions, which are the largest fruit and vegetable producing areas in europe.
in writing. ‒ the economic crisis has been particularly difficult to negotiate for the fruit and vegetables sector, which is mainly composed of small and medium-sized farms and enterprises. it is a significant part of european agriculture, generating a turnover of 120 billion euros a year. the consumption of fruit and vegetables has fallen sharply, especially among younger people, increasing the risk of obesity. the union's bellicose foreign policy towards russia has led to an embargo by russia, worsening the crisis facing producers. i therefore consider it essential to help this sector and this report is in the right direction, although it does not mention unfair competition from third countries. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it encourages the commission to redouble its efforts to protect farmers from unfair trading practices by large retailers. it makes little sense to invest resources in strengthening and creating po (a slow and difficult process) if the bargaining power in the food chain continues to be predominantly retailer-owned. moreover, since many member states are adopting national measures to address these problems, some coordination is necessary at union level in order to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market.
in writing. the text on the fruit and vegetable sector since the 2007 reform seeks to support this sector economically through the development of producer organisations but also to participate in health education, especially among children who are less and less aware of nature. all these are commendable objectives and therefore the text seems to be moving in the right direction. however, there are gaps: there is no mention of the differences in pay between eu and non-eu countries, the use of illegal labour by some farmers, or the phytosanitary standards and their implementation. i am in favour of this text despite these shortcomings because i support the national fruit and vegetable sector, which must be given special attention because of the number of jobs it represents.
in writing. ‒ the resolution proposal on the fruit and vegetables sector aims to help a sector in a very difficult economic situation. producer organisations will receive compensatory aid to help them cope with the negative consequences of the restrictions imposed. the fruit and vegetable sector is strategic for europe's food self-sufficiency, but also for its economy. it provides livelihoods for 500 000 europeans in all member states and contributes 18% of the total value of agricultural production. since this text is favourable to french fruit and vegetable producers, i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the recent political and health crises illustrate the need to strengthen competitiveness, resilience and innovation in the fruit and vegetable sector. the latter is facing serious problems of competitiveness and organisation. this report is parliament's response to the commission's report on this subject. it does not advocate a change in the current architecture of the fruit and vegetables sector, but identifies successes and progress that can be made. it stresses the need to increase the level of organisation in the sector and make it more attractive, or to combat unfair commercial practices. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i wanted to support this report, which gives a snapshot of the state of the fruit and vegetable sector since the 2007 reform. the text acknowledges in particular that, in comparison with private trading companies, producer organisations are subject to a number of restrictions, in particular as regards the use of the funds invested, the structure of the income or the need to sell. the rapporteur also stresses the need to support the fruit and vegetable sector throughout the union, given its importance in terms of added value and jobs and its importance for health through healthy and balanced diets. the report rightly calls on the commission to redouble its efforts to tackle unfair trading practices in the food supply chain, which have a negative impact on producers' revenues, reduce their incomes and put them in a precarious situation, threatening the sustainability and stability of the sector. french farmers themselves are particularly threatened by certain practices of retailers, which is why i support the agri committee's desire to protect our farmers better.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report aims to provide an overview of the state of the european fruit and vegetables sector since the 2007 reform. parliament called for the strengthening of producer organisations and inter-branch organisations and for the improvement of the tools to support their actions in europe and at international level. as such, when the cap was reformed, i introduced many tools to strengthen this weight, particularly in trade negotiations. however, it is clear that these tools are still underused in many countries. france has a leading role to play in this respect, in order to assert its vision of producer organisation and interprofessionalism in europe. the report also discusses crisis management and the intervention price. it should be recalled that the member states, including the french government, are required to be solely responsible for fixing the intervention prices. i voted in favour of this report because it is balanced.
in writing. the european union is pursuing a policy of supporting the fruit and vegetable sector by promoting producer organisations, which receive financial support. this form of market regulation should improve the competitiveness of european producers while stabilising their incomes. the role of these organisations is also to attract more young people to agricultural occupations, to reverse the negative demographic trend that the sector is suffering from. the aim is also to encourage the consumption of fresh fruit and vegetables. as the report points out, the eu's per capita consumption of alcohol is 387 grams per day, whereas the world health organisation recommends 400 grams.
in writing. ‒ the report aims to encourage farmers to join producer organisations (po), in order to increase their bargaining power, strengthen their position in the food supply chain and thus increase their income in a struggling agricultural sector. it is essential to increase their competitiveness and to address certain unfair trade practices in third countries. the union must help its farmers to find new markets for their products and facilitate exports in the context of the russian embargo and the ongoing trade negotiations being conducted by the european commission.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the situation of the fruit and vegetables sector after the reform of the common organisation of the market in 2007, as it helps to strengthen a specific policy for the fruit and vegetables sector. producer organisations are the main element. as a means of collective organisation on the market, they are essential in defending producers' incomes. to enhance the effectiveness of collective action by producers, it is also necessary to strengthen producer organisations and to provide for the possibility of involving producers who are not members of a producer organisation in their actions, in particular in the area of good product valuation, crisis management or anticipation and environmental actions. finally, there is a need to strengthen interprofessional networks for their role in improving dialogue within the sector and in general information and food education.

member of the commission.– mr president, honourable members, let me thank you for your strong interest in this proposal, and allow me to recall briefly what our intention was when we tabled this proposal. remember, the financial crisis hit the world economy and some of our societies very hard. structural weaknesses in corporate governance have become more evident, and a broad consensus emerged that short-termism has played an important role in causing and deepening the crisis. this directive is one of the contributions to addressing these shortcomings at eu level. it will also contribute to putting the eu back on the path of long-term sustainable growth. over the last few years capital markets have become more driven by the prospect of quick trading gains rather than by conscious and engaged investment. even investors such as pension funds, whose very mission is to secure a long-term return on investment, have followed the markets and put short-term pressure on companies. we need to encourage more long-term financing and long-term shareholder engagement. this also means more competitive companies on the global stage. we believe that by enhancing corporate governance, we would give investors the necessary tools to engage and protect their rights. this should make european companies more attractive for investors. i would like to thank mr cofferati and all the shadow rapporteurs for their efforts in defining parliament’s position. i welcome the compromise found, and the commission is ready to engage in negotiations with the co-legislators. let me now express some views on several of your amendments. first, concerning transparency obligations on companies about tax matters and tax rulings – the so-called country-by-country reporting. as the honourable members know, the commission is committed to fighting tax evasion and aggressive tax planning and will analyse whether additional disclosure of certain corporate tax information should be introduced. on 17 june, the commission launched a public consultation on possible options, which will feed into the impact assessment work that will be concluded at the latest in the first quarter of 2016. second, concerning measures to incentivise long-term shareholdings through increased voting rights or dividends: while the commission agrees with the overall objective, the question is: how best to achieve this? we should avoid discouraging investors, especially cross-border and foreign investors, from investing in european companies, and we should not lose sight of the interests of minority shareholders. finally, concerning related party transactions, the commission notes that the amendments tone down the original commission proposal. i believe that we need a harmonised threshold for the application of rules on related party transactions in the single market. currently, 40% of shareholders are cross-border based, and the lack of a uniform definition of related party transactions leads to fragmentation and increased costs both for investors and for companies.

on behalf of the enf group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the financial crisis has shown that banking institutions favour short-term returns, thus underperforming our productive apparatus. shareholders, eager to increase the return on their investments, have taken reckless positions that threaten the sustainability of our companies. in order to combat these financial abuses, the report provides for, inter alia, the extension of shareholder and stakeholder participation in corporate governance. the directive also calls for greater transparency between companies and investors. we believe that these measures are in the right direction. we regret, however, that they do not go further, because it is naive to think that this project will lead to better regulation of the international financial system. only a large-scale joint project to tax financial transactions will limit stock market speculation and encourage shareholders to invest in long-term assets.
mr president, this text aims to replace financial capitalism with responsible capitalism. the aim is to encourage investors to hold their shares longer and to divert them from the temptation of short-term profits. to this end, the text seeks in particular to identify the shareholders. the identification of shareholders is a good thing: it will lead to the establishment in each company of a list of shareholders for the sake of transparency. however, care should be taken to ensure that the consultation of this list does not entail excessive costs. the text also seeks to reward shareholders who keep their shares for more than two years by allowing states to give them a double voting right. this right is a good idea, whether the beneficiaries are the state or the employees of the company. it will prevent foreign companies from taking over. the double voting system, if it is designed in this way, will be an instrument of a kind of economic patriotism.

the rapporteur. madam president, commissioner, we have been talking all afternoon about issues such as yemen or human rights, and we could also have talked about the israeli-palestinian conflict, all of which are at the heart of the report on stability in the middle east and north africa (mena) region. this report is a bit lengthy, but it is in line with the commission's desire to give a strategic direction to european action in this region. we have had to go through all the different subjects in this report: syria, libya, iraq, yemen, tunisia, the fight against the islamic state group. at the same time, we have not sought to draw a clear and long-term strategic line from the accumulation of individual cases. the principles we have adopted in this report are first and foremost principles of responsibility. there would be nothing worse for us in the european parliament than to divide ourselves by taking up this challenge, when our south is already in the state we see and our imperfection has been proven. so we have been constantly trying to listen to each other and find a consensus. in this respect, i would like to thank very warmly all the fictitious rapporteurs, mrs mănescu for the ppe, mr nart for the liberals, mr belder, mr smith for the greens, mr iglesias, mr permuy, mr castaldo, mrs vergiat. whatever the political orientations, apart from those which are frankly anti-european, we have tried to build a common position, responsible and capable of being heard. the following are the principles that have guided us, and you must admit that it has not been easy to define them. first, do not think that the challenge of security has to be reduced to security itself. of course, we must rise to this challenge, and there is no excuse for terrorism, neither economic nor social. it has an ideological basis. we are also assuming our responsibilities in this respect by calling for a strengthening and better coordination of europe's security action. but at the same time - and this is the strategic line we want to adopt - we know that peace and stability can only be restored if we deal with the long-term causes: the democratic and human rights issues, which we have just discussed, the economic and social issues. two of the three parts of the report are devoted to economic and social questions, to the question of democracy and to human rights. this is what allowed us to find a consensus, in a balance where there would not be a single cause, but multifactorial actions. yes, we must intervene on the security question, we must strengthen europe's action, we must give assistance to the states, we must help to guard the borders better, we must of course do everything we can to train those who must provide security on our southern flank and at the same time we must deploy economic and social actions. the second fundamental line of this report is quite new and it structures the whole approach. it is to admit that europe cannot - as it has a tendency to do, as we have heard in previous debates - hope to solve all the problems in syria, iraq and yemen by itself, through a number of invocations or interventions. this report is based on a balance between the desire to have concerted, long-term, coherent action and, at the same time, to rely on the states on the one hand, but also on all the multilateral instruments that exist, especially in the south. in conclusion, madam president, i believe that we have found a strategy on both these aspects and have succeeded in coming together around the idea that europe must be more present in order to take more determined action.

on behalf of the enf group. madam president, this report on the limits of radioactivity in food and feed is not acceptable as it stands. the proposed levels of radioactivity are the same as in 1987, after the chernobyl disaster. the limits proposed by the commission are calculated for an accident occurring more than 1 000 kilometres from the frontiers of europe. this assumption allowed the experts to bet on a low contamination rate of 10%. the rate would be much higher if the accident had occurred in the heart of europe. the protection of the population is therefore not assured. this protection is even paltry when compared with that which is applied in japan. in this country, the limits of radioactivity in food are 8 to 20 times lower than ours. this is the example we must follow in order to better protect our populations. after all, if you want to increase your powers, you have to accept the homework that comes with it. for our part, there are only two possible options. either the european institutions set standards that really ensure our food security, as japan does, or they refuse to do so and in that case the member states must be able to do so for them, under article 36 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. that is the meaning of the amendments tabled by our group.

on behalf of the efdd group. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i believe that good intentions do not necessarily lead to the right policies or legislation. the rapporteur, mrs reda, has undoubtedly shown a great deal of goodwill and personal generosity in tackling this thorny problem of copyright. but she has obviously forgotten some principles that are urgently needed. the protection of culture also means the protection of copyright, which is both the fair remuneration for artistic creation and the protection of the moral rights of artists. i regret that this moral right was never mentioned in the report. it's the moral right of artists that determines everything else. the creator must be able to ensure that his work is not devalued or distorted artistically, politically or ideologically. the panorama exception, which the rapporteur defends at all costs, opens a breach in the protection of this economic and moral right. and if you take away the right of authors to control the exploitation of their work, they have no respect for their own person. contrary to the crazy rumors circulating on the internet, this control does not in any way hinder the possibility for anyone to photograph public works. it merely provides the necessary guarantee that the work will not be exploited for obscene, political or ideological purposes by unwise or malicious persons. we must therefore reject this so-called panorama exception and vote against amendment no 3 and paragraph 46. on behalf of the enf group. madam president, the reda report sought to establish freedom of panorama, that is to say the right to freely distribute photographs of monuments without the permission of the architects concerned and without copyright. fortunately, an amendment was made to this disastrous initiative which did not sufficiently protect the copyright of architects. this will allow each state to strike a more reasonable balance between copyright and the rights of photographers. france, for example, does not recognize freedom of panorama, but has a much more subtle system which it calls the "accessory theory". this theory protects the copyright of architects, but still allows the free distribution of photographs of a building when it is only an accessory element of a larger landscape. the amendment to the reda report will enable france to maintain this fine system, and i am delighted about that.
madam president, while it is clear that new rules must be introduced, this battle over copyright is perfectly in line with the opposition between the defenders of the nation and the globalists. the european union is seeking to do away with national particularities in favour of a global trade without rules. breaking down national barriers to copyright and data protection regulation, as jean-claude juncker has called for, always means fewer controls and restrictions. this would, of course, benefit the large multinationals, such as google or amazon, which are already eager to avoid paying taxes in europe. i had already asked the commissioner for culture about the tax practices of video-on-demand platforms. in addition, we will need to find a framework that protects creators and small authors while allowing free expression on the internet. indeed, intellectual property has become a political weapon and it is under this pretext that we can ask internet users to remove critical videos. this development must not pave the way for a union without frontiers and must leave the member states free to continue to legislate in favour of respecting, preserving and promoting their identity.
