madam president, first of all, i am opposed to any harmonisation in the field of copyright, if only because of the ambiguity of the term copyright in the english version, whereas the two concepts are the product of different philosophies. the infosoc directive exists, then. this directive did not allow for the harmonisation of copyright. that's good. the work of the mission in france, led by pierre sirinelli, a distinguished law professor, gives a snapshot of what the revision of this directive proposed by my colleague julia reda would entail: the weakening of copyright, which i strongly oppose. secondly, no revision of the e-commerce directive is proposed, which guarantees a very protective regime for internet service providers. we can even speak of irresponsibility. with this draft revision, you risk giving birth, once again, to a dead text to the detriment of the authors. who can predict what the internet will be like in five years? the european union is an obsolete software which produces only floppy disks. we still have evidence of this today.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to say that i regret that the question of the panorama has so much monopolized the debate, simply because so many untruths have been told. i'm going to make things right again. in no way is this about banning the posting of holiday photos on the internet or elsewhere, but simply about saying that it is not fair that an artist, because he chooses to produce his works in public space, cannot receive a fair remuneration when they are used commercially. the aim of this report was to adapt the issue of culture and copyright to the digital world. indeed, the disruptions induced by digital uses are many: they change the relationship of our citizens to culture, but not only to culture, because they also change the way in which trade and services operate. they even change the way we think about social and work relations today. why special treatment for culture? after all, it is true that culture is of great economic importance: it is the third largest sector of activity in europe, and it represents more than 500 billion in turnover per year, but i reject this purely commercialist view of culture. it also has political, symbolic and humanistic significance. when we talk about barriers, obstacles, impediments and copyright, personally, it goes against my conception of european culture. is it necessary to remind people that there is no culture without an artist, that copyright is a fundamental right and that it is right and good for everyone to be able to make a living from their work? i am pleased that the text which is being proposed, unlike the one which was originally on the table, puts artists back at the centre of the debate, a place they should never have left. our copyright regime allows for a diverse and thriving culture. i hope the commission... madam president, by voting on this report now after it has been adopted by the committee on legal affairs, we have the opportunity to send a strong message to the commission. we have the opportunity to tell the commission, as it prepares the revision of the copyright directive, that we are in favour of adapting copyright to the digital age, but against its demolition or its re-examination. we have substantially reoriented and rewritten the initial draft report presented to us by mrs reda in the committee on legal affairs, and on this occasion we have reaffirmed and re-affirmed strong priorities and principles: fair remuneration for the work and talent of authors and creators, respect for european cultural diversity, affirmation of the principle of territoriality, the need to make progress on portability - this is perfectly compatible - the need to combat piracy and counterfeiting, which are real scourges, the need to set up a system of liability for platforms, hosts and all intermediaries who are currently in a system of irresponsibility, the need to adapt copyright to the digital age and not to dismantle it, to strengthen it and not to weaken it. all this is possible because the report, as we have strongly amended it in the committee on legal affairs, contains concrete ways of doing this. we are waiting with great interest, commissioner, for the proposal for a revision of the directive that you will present to us, but please know that we will be committed to respecting the principle of intellectual property of artists and creators.

in writing. ‒ i did not support the resolution on the negotiations on the transatlantic trade and investment partnership because today's vote should have allowed the european parliament to send a strong signal to influence the ongoing negotiations between the commission and the united states. the compromise amendment on the isds mechanism was vague as to the wording of the rejection of the mechanism. this ambiguity about replacing isds with a new system was not satisfactory. moreover, the resolution did not sufficiently protect both public services and the quality of european technical, social and environmental standards. for these various reasons, i voted against this report, which leaves too much uncertainty about the demands of the european parliament in the negotiations for a possible transatlantic free trade agreement.
in writing. ‒ one of the stated aims of the ptci promoters is to 'converge' eu and us regulations. the united states refuses to ratify the major conventions on labour, the kyoto protocol on global warming, the convention on biological diversity, the unesco conventions on cultural diversity, and so on. in almost all cases, their regulations are less restrictive than those in europe. in the case of 'convergence', there is every indication that the us - which, unlike the eu, is fiercely protective of its interests - will seek to impose its own regulations on 'partners' whom it tends to regard as its vassals. there is no question of accepting the low-cost products of north american agribusiness: hormone-laced beef, lactic acid-sprayed meat carcasses, bleached poultry, meat with ractopamine hydrochloride, gmos, animals fed animal flour, products containing pesticides and other toxic additives that are banned in our country. the lange report does not set any red lines, no boundaries; it even validates the odious investor-state dispute settlement (isds) mechanism, the so-called "arbitration tribunals" that will allow american firms to subject our states to their diktat.

in writing. ‒ the commission is currently negotiating with the united states the terms of the transatlantic trade and investment partnership (ttip). the european parliament warns the commission of a number of points which need to be clarified, without expressing any clear opposition to this agreement which we have always opposed. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. they call for the possibility for companies to bring cases against member states before a private court to be banned, but they point to the benefits of public international arbitration. they advocate action to increase food transparency and to exclude agricultural imports from third countries from the treaty, without addressing the danger posed by the us agri-food industry to farmers and consumers. they want to fight all forms of dumping but the agreement will lead to social harmonization from below or a sharp increase in our trade deficits in the best case. these recommendations are nothing but a slap in the face because they cannot improve the terms of an agreement whose foundations are harmful to europeans. i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament adopted its position on the negotiations for the transatlantic trade and investment partnership (ttip). as the only institution directly elected by the european citizens, the parliament must play an important role in monitoring the negotiations with the united states. ttip will not be at the expense of european norms and standards. we will not make any concessions on the european union's social, environmental and health acquis. i am also opposed to private arbitration for conflicts between investors and states. we must protect european companies operating in the us market while preserving the right of states to regulate. these red lines will guide my vote on the european parliament's approval of ttip. i voted in favour of this resolution which reminds the commission that the high standards of european standards are not negotiable.

in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report sets out the parliament's recommendations to the european commission in the context of the negotiations on the transatlantic trade and investment partnership (ttip). at present, no fundamental chapters are closed and the two sides are concluding the first part of the negotiations before addressing the most essential issues. in this context, the european parliament, which has a veto on the final adoption of the agreement, wanted to define its priorities and red lines. i have particularly focused on the agricultural aspect of these recommendations. despite the real economic opportunities for our agriculture that will result from this agreement, i believe that the european agricultural model must be protected. the text of the recommendations takes up this position, namely that our sanitary and phytosanitary standards should not be called into question, that our quality marks and products under pdo and pgi should be fully recognized and that sensitive products should be given special consideration, and that they should be excluded from the negotiations. for these reasons i voted in favour of these recommendations, which i consider to be balanced and realistic, since they do not seek an agreement at any price, but leave the negotiators sufficient room to manoeuvre in order to reach a satisfactory agreement.
in writing. ahead of a new round of negotiations on the transatlantic trade and investment partnership (ttip), it was important that parliament could pass on its recommendations and red lines to the european commission. we must not lose sight of the ambitious objective of creating a large free trade area, which would be a major asset for the european economy. however, caution is needed: liberalisation must serve employment policy, not lead to social dumping. the europeans also want to maintain a high level of requirements in terms of geographical indications and data protection. i supported the compromise that was voted, calling for the isds to be replaced by a mechanism where the notion of arbitration disappears, leaving room for full-fledged judges subject to transparency rules.
in writing. ‒ there are two main reasons for the justified public distrust of this trade agreement. the first is that the peoples have not been involved in the debate and do not know what is happening. i regret that the heads of state or government have given the commission a mandate without first discussing it in their member states. i hope that the national parliaments will have to give their consent to these negotiations in the end. the second is that we are not on equal footing with the americans. take the example of public procurement. in the united states, a large proportion of public procurement is reserved for us smes to promote growth and employment. the americans are quite right to do so at home. but if we want to level the playing field, then we should do the same in our homes. let us face the reasons for many of the doubts and concerns expressed by europeans. until we make progress on these two points, we will not be able to have a satisfactory agreement. that is why i did not approve this resolution.
in writing. ‒ after much discussion in parliament and the postponement of the vote at the previous part-session, mainly due to the disagreements within the s&d group, we finally adopted an important text reminding the negotiators of our red lines. it was imperative to recall that public services and audiovisual services should be excluded from the negotiations, just as it was imperative to recall that we are against lowering our standards and that we want in particular the protection of our agricultural model, the exclusion of sensitive products, the recognition of geographical indications, the need for reciprocal access to public contracts... as for the question of the investor-state dispute settlement mechanism, we categorically reject the mechanism in its present form. we call for the system to be reformed so that it functions as a genuine public court with transparency requirements and an appeal mechanism. it will also have to respect the right of states to regulate what is essential in this area. this agreement could be an opportunity for many of our sectors but we must remain very vigilant and make sure that our red lines are not crossed.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution by my colleague bernd lange on the negotiations on the transatlantic trade and investment partnership (ttip). the text was intended to set out parliament's guidelines for these negotiations, recalling in particular the need to preserve european levels of protection of health, the environment and consumers, and the protection of europe's cultural diversity. the text also supports a new approach to investor-state dispute settlement, calling for the isds private arbitration to be replaced by a system based on professional judges, an appeals system and guaranteeing the right of states to legislate. the potential of the agreement for the european economy is finally recalled. even though the conclusion of these negotiations is still a long way off, it was necessary for parliament, which will have a veto on the agreement to be concluded, to make its position on the subject known. this resolution was adopted by a large majority of 436 votes in favour, 241 against and 32 abstentions, which i welcome.

in writing. ‒ this european parliament resolution on ttip is a soft text which sometimes says everything and the opposite, but never sets any red lines for the commission. this text does not call for the abolition of isds arbitration tribunals , but calls, if possible, for an appeal mechanism and a permanent international court (possibly but not necessarily, in the medium term, for disputes to be settled by an international arbitration court with professional judges). the text proposes to exclude services of general interest (such as water, health, social security, education, social services) from the scope of ttip so that states can continue to provide them. for the other public services, it is not clear what will happen (sncf, edf, etc.). the text proposes the establishment of regulatory cooperation between the us and the eu, structured cooperation with the aim of economic efficiency, without prejudice to the powers of us and european legislators (2). the european parliament has been at one with the commission on almost all issues, has drawn almost no red lines on ttip and has only made declarations of intent. i vote against it.

in writing. the lange report on the transatlantic treaty is a scandalous attack on democracy and demonstrates the non-representativeness of this parliament. while 97% of european citizens expressed concern about ttip, meps decided to ignore it to satisfy obscure interests. and all this for a hypothetical increase in long-term growth (0.4% growth over ten years according to studies financed by the commission), which is estimated to be lower than the cost of sanctions against russia. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all transport services by road, rail and inland waterway. the dispute settlement mechanism which will allow a private company to take legal action against a state if a standard does not suit it is also perennial. the treaty would therefore regulate the playing field for multinational companies in defiance of the sovereignty of the member states. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the transatlantic trade and investment partnership between the european union and the united states. the european commission is responsible for conducting the negotiations, but the european parliament has a significant responsibility and power, as it will have to approve the agreement and can give its political guidance to the commission to influence the negotiation. the tipp will increase trade and therefore job creation through the prospect of additional outlets for our companies, especially our smes. i will, however, remain very vigilant to ensure that it does not weaken the european standards which protect us and which i am committed to. that is why i voted in particular for amendment no 117 which calls for the replacement of the investor-state dispute settlement mechanism (isds) by 'a new system subject to democratic principles and control, where any cases will be dealt with in transparency by independent professional judges, appointed by the public authorities, in open court, and which will include an appeal mechanism, a mechanism which will ensure the consistency of judicial decisions and respect for the jurisdiction of the courts of the european union and its member states and which will prevent public policy objectives from being compromised by private interests'.
in writing. ‒ parliament has today sent an important signal, and has recalled its red lines on ttip. the exclusion of public services and audiovisual services from the negotiations, the protection of our standards and our agricultural model, the protection of our choice of company, the recognition of geographical indications, the need for reciprocal access to public procurement, these are some of the red lines for which i am proud to have voted. the european parliament has managed to break out of a deadlock by demonstrating not only the need to protect our investors abroad but also to abandon the investor-state dispute settlement mechanism as it currently operates. the latter must be reformed to respect the right of states to regulate. it must function as a genuine public court. it will have to meet transparency obligations and include an appeal mechanism. we must tell the truth to the citizens who are too often exploited by dishonest political machines. today we sent a message of caution to the negotiators: parliament will not accept anything.
in writing. i voted against the european parliament resolution on the negotiations for the transatlantic trade and investment partnership, known as 'ttip', simply because the adoption of this resolution means support for the continuation of the negotiations. for more than two years now, european citizens, but also many local authorities and smes, have strongly opposed this agreement, which directly threatens existing rights and protections in europe. the great transatlantic market is a threat to the construction of political europe, which has become absolutely essential today if we are to hope to save the union. we know all too well that common markets without political and democratic institutions capable of imposing rules on the markets only increase competition between states. a free trade agreement of this magnitude cannot be achieved without the objectives of respecting and implementing the economic, social, environmental and cultural rights of european and american citizens.
in writing. ‒ the lange report on the transatlantic treaty is a scandalous attack on democracy and demonstrates the non-representativeness of this parliament. while 97% of citizens in the member states expressed concern about ttip, meps decided to ignore it (after postponing debate and voting in order to reach a discreet agreement behind the scenes) to satisfy obscure interests, all for a hypothetical increase in long-term growth (only 0.4% over ten years according to studies funded by the commission!), which is estimated to be less than the cost of sanctions against russia. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all transport services by road, rail and inland waterway. the dispute settlement mechanism which will allow a private company to take legal action against a state if a standard does not suit it is more enduring. this treaty would therefore set the playing field for multinational companies in defiance of the sovereignty of the member states and the peoples. i voted against it, of course.
in writing. ‒ after lengthy debates and socialist melodramas, particularly on the dispute settlement mechanism, we have finally adopted the report on ttip, which sets out parliament's interests in the negotiations between the european commission and the us authorities. i voted in favour of this report, on which i tabled 50 amendments, most of which have been accepted. however, if we have succeeded in including our red lines, we must continue to be vigilant during the continuation of the negotiations in order to defend the interests of our citizens and our companies. europe cannot be the only continent that is still in a world in motion. yet the far left and far right have managed to find allies in the french greens and socialists to maintain the status quo in our relations with the united states. are they so pleased to see our companies struggling in american public procurement? are they satisfied with the continuation of trade disputes (boeing vs airbus)? why refuse to even negotiate to put all the issues on the table? the policy of the ostrich is not worthy of the leading commercial power we are. those who voted against underestimated europe and overestimated the united states.
in writing. ‒ today, parliament adopted a resolution on the transatlantic trade and investment partnership (ttip). the text does not constitute a final vote on the ptci but reflects the recommendations made by the european parliament to the european commission in the negotiations with the united states. although this resolution contains recommendations which are in the right direction in terms of the protection of social rights, i have decided to vote against this text because it does not quite clearly reject the establishment of private arbitration tribunals. the french socialists have always firmly rejected the creation of such private courts between the state and investors, which undermine the democratic foundation of our courts and call into question the legislative sovereignty of public authorities. finally, on the protection of public services, i regret that the resolution does not guarantee that only the services explicitly mentioned are covered by the agreement in order to strictly limit the scope of the ptci. on this fundamental issue, as well as on regulatory cooperation on social, environmental or agri-food standards, the resolution adopted does not go far enough in its recommendations to the commission for the continuation of negotiations.
in writing. ‒ the transatlantic trade and investment partnership, better known by its acronym ttip, is a free trade agreement between the european union and the united states, which aims to stimulate additional reciprocal economic growth. nevertheless, the absolute necessity to preserve our lifestyles, and therefore our high european standards, seems hardly compatible with certain aspects of the american model, hence the differences, particularly on the famous arbitration courts or the application of environmental and food standards. in addition to the disagreements over the substance of the treaty, the asymmetry between the two parties (the united states being an 'imperialist' federal state speaking with one voice against the european union which often speaks with 28 dissonant voices) should make us extremely cautious. this was not a vote for or against ttip; the commission has already taken a number of decisions on the basis of the information available to it. therefore, as this report may be in favour of or against a 'smart ttip', i have chosen to abstain.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on the free trade agreement between the european union and the united states, in particular because of the clause on the private arbitration mechanism, the so-called 'isds', which, despite a vague compromise amendment, is still included in the resolution. the isds could allow for arbitration where multinationals would challenge the choice of european or french legislators and their jurisdictions. private justice has no place in commercial disputes between democratic states. that is why i say that if, at the end of the negotiations, private arbitration were to be included in the agreement between the european union and the united states, i would reject ttip.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which addresses the european parliament's recommendations to the commission on the negotiations on the transatlantic trade and investment partnership with the united states (ttip/ptci). among these recommendations, we have been able to recall the red lines we have always defended, namely the protection of our standards and choices of society, the exclusion of sensitive agricultural products, the exclusion of audiovisual services and public services, reciprocal access to public procurement and the recognition and protection of our geographical indications. as regards the investor-state dispute settlement mechanism (isds), we reject the isds in its current form. as the text states, it must be reformed, respect the right of states to regulate, comply with rules on transparency and include an appeal mechanism. it must function as a genuine public court. we will remain attentive to the concerns expressed by european citizens and will be vigilant as to the development of the negotiations.
in writing. the negotiations between the european commission and the united states to conclude a general free trade agreement are being conducted in the most opaque manner. this treaty would lead to the dismantling or weakening of all the standards (social, environmental, etc.) which protect european citizens. above all, it places the rights of investors above those of the states. the freedom to legislate and the sovereignty of the peoples, protected from the interference of multinational corporations concerned for their own profits, must not be called into question. the mechanism for private arbitration between states and investors has not been clearly removed from this resolution, which serves as a negotiating mandate for the commission. this is despite the fact that our national courts have full jurisdiction to hear such cases. the european parliament has missed the opportunity to assert itself as the voice of the european citizens and to echo their concerns about isds by adopting a resolution which is still too ambiguous. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. ‒ this text is a declaration of intent. despite the attempt by some amendments to limit the scope of the text and to try to force the commission to reduce the scope of this ttip agreement in the making, we can only oppose the principle of this agreement. the national front is leading the opposition to this agreement, which is putting many traditional sectors (or not necessarily) of our country at great risk. most of the amendments limiting the text were rejected. the text as a whole was approved by a very large majority of members, which in my humble opinion is a betrayal of the elites. i therefore vote against this text, which is of major importance for the future of our children.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament has succeeded in voting on the ttip (tafta), the great transatlantic market which wants to keep up with the emerging countries. the resolution, which is based on illusions about the opening up of public procurement in the united states or the possibility of better regulation of financial services, even aligns the untruths about the purely technical role of the regulatory cooperation council with the maintenance of current plant health or environmental rules while their change is already underway or the protection of the cultural and audiovisual sectors, without taking into account the digital. martin schulz, president of the european parliament, has put his full weight in the balance, multiplying procedural scams to ensure the support of the "grand coalition" by even proposing a last-minute compromise made of convoluted formulations on the isds (investor-state dispute settlement) private arbitration mechanism. as a result, the latter remains part of the negotiations and could, like everything else, serve as a model for the whole world. the european parliament, which has not been involved in the mobilization of european public opinion, voted 436 in favour, 31 against. it goes without saying that i am one of the 241 who voted against.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to vote in favour of this report on the stabilisation agreement with macedonia. the report calls for the stabilisation agreement with macedonia to be validated. the national front is opposed to this reckless and unlimited enlargement policy, particularly with the countries of eastern europe and the balkans. however, i chose not to participate in systematic opposition. the aim of this text is simply to bring the association and stabilisation agreements concluded and ratified previously into line. the negotiations started in december 2012 and culminated in the signing of a protocol on 25 october 2013. opposition to this protocol, which is merely a legislative adaptation, would be a fruitless opposition. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. this report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on long-term shareholder engagement and corporate governance statement aims to facilitate long-term shareholder engagement, including shareholder identification, the transmission of information and facilitation of the exercise of shareholder rights, as well as to ensure transparency of the engagement policies of institutional investors and asset managers and to set certain requirements with regard to the remuneration of directors and transactions with related parties. i am in favour of this spirit of corporate governance and the commitment of shareholders over the long term and i have therefore voted for this report which goes in that direction.
in writing. ‒ the report on the european parliament's proposal for a directive promotes long-term shareholder engagement and improved corporate governance. increasing shareholder and stakeholder engagement would thus help to improve the financial and non-financial performance of our companies. the report also provides for greater transparency between investors and companies. the financial crisis has shown that institutional investors (financial institutions, hedge funds, pension funds) and asset managers favour short-term returns, which leads to underperformance of our productive apparatus. the growing divergence between the interests of investors and those of companies lies in the fact that shareholders take excessive risks because it is the return on their investments that is at stake. although this report does not go into the question of existing tools to combat speculation in financial markets, we believe it is a step in the right direction. that is why i voted for this text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this directive in plenary, although i had rejected the report in the committee on legal affairs. i am glad that the compromise proposals tabled in plenary, in a spirit of appeasement by all the political groups, have found an echo in the rapporteur. the text now provides for the possibility of an advisory vote on the remuneration policy and no longer refers to the ratio between the average remuneration of directors and employees. it provides for the possibility for member states to ensure that shareholders have an advisory vote on the remuneration ratio, but excludes the participation of employees in this procedure. finally, i welcome the fact that the text provides for an exception to the rule that the value of shares should not play a predominant role in the criteria for financial performance. the text is now balanced. all this is in the right direction, in the interests of our companies, their development and the growth of the european economy.

in writing. ‒ i support the principle of transparency, whereby large companies publish information on their activities in each country where they are located, as i have supported transparency requirements for the activities of so-called extractive industries and credit institutions. however, i abstained, like the whole of the epp group, on the complex system as presented in this report, in order not to anticipate the position that the taxe committee will take on the specific case of tax information, which is at the heart of its work.
in writing. ‒ in this report on shareholder rights, we have succeeded with the left forces in introducing the obligation for multinationals to disclose the taxes they pay in each country. this country-by-country tax return allows you to see where taxes are paid and therefore, theoretically, where profits are made. therefore, when there are very large disparities in taxes paid or very low taxation compared to the size of the company, it is easy to assume a pattern of tax fraud or tax evasion. this country-by-country reporting system will facilitate the fight against tax evasion. that is why i supported this report against the manoeuvres of the right, which first tried to reverse this aspect before trying to slow down its adoption as much as possible.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it aims to promote long-term shareholder engagement and transparency in the governance of european companies. it is a means of combating the tax-optimising practices of multinational companies, a subject which has recently been the subject of the luxleaks scandal. it also gives shareholders the right to decide on the remuneration of company directors. the council and the european parliament will engage in a dialogue on this text.
in writing. sergio cofferati's draft law aims to introduce more transparency and to encourage a longer-term commitment of shareholders to the company, by involving them more in the governance of the company. the text provides incentives for the remuneration of managers to be better linked to the long-term performance of the company. it also ensures that the interests of the company are protected and provides for member states to put in place mechanisms to promote long-term shareholding and the sustainability of companies. finally, the socialist group has won a major victory by introducing a country-by-country reporting requirement for companies to disclose all the activities of their subsidiaries, country by country - including taxes paid, including in tax havens. this is a key point in detecting and understanding tax optimisation maneuvers before citizens and before governments. i therefore voted enthusiastically for this report, which is in line with my political commitment and my parliamentary work in the special committee on tax returns.
in writing. ‒ the report finds that "in many cases, shareholders favour excessive short-term risk-taking by managers". indeed, this behaviour 'undermines the long-term financial and non-financial performance of the companies and leads to insufficient levels of investment'. to address this, the report proposes to promote long-term shareholder engagement and to increase transparency between companies and investors. the intention is commendable, but the means to implement it are still too weak. the report proposes to publish the turnover of asset managers' portfolios, or to take measures to favour long-term shareholders, whose floor is set at 2 years, i.e. lower than the average turnover of pension funds: tax benefits, loyalty bonuses and additional voting rights... it would have been more effective to remove shareholders' voting rights in the short term. nevertheless, in order to encourage awareness of the harmful effects of the financialisation of the economy, i am voting in favour.
in writing. this report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council amending directive 2007/36/ec to promote long-term shareholder engagement and directive 2013/34/eu as regards certain elements of the corporate governance statement aims to facilitate long-term shareholder engagement, including shareholder identification, the transmission of information and facilitation of the exercise of shareholder rights, as well as to ensure transparency of engagement policies for institutional investors and asset managers and to set certain requirements regarding the remuneration of directors and transactions with related parties. i am in favour of a long-term shareholder approach (through tax incentives or greater rights and decision-making powers), and i have decided to vote in favour of this report, which is a step in the right direction.
in writing. this report concerns the amendment of two directives on shareholder participation and corporate governance within the european union. more specifically, it deals with new rights and obligations of shareholders to promote long-term investment, the regulation of remuneration and the fight against short-term speculation. it also includes a number of measures to ensure greater transparency in the sector. it specifically requires companies to publish their tax obligations in each of the countries in which they operate. this is a major step forward in tax transparency and contributes to the fight against tax havens in europe.
in writing. ‒ this report aims to promote long-term shareholder engagement and transparency in the governance of european companies. two main points were voted: large companies and public interest entities should publish country-by-country information related to revenue earned, taxes paid on profits and subsidies received; shareholders will be entitled to vote on the remuneration policy of company directors. we voted for both of these points. the publication of the figures should make it possible to fight a little better against the tax optimization practices of multinational companies, a subject that has recently made headlines with the luxleaks scandal. the council and the european parliament will engage in a dialogue on the text in order to reach agreement on the final version of the legislation. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which is moving in the right direction.
in writing. ‒ the financial crisis has created a need for transparency in financial markets on the part of public authorities and public opinion. the commission and parliament have been working hard on these issues and have wanted to propose a number of measures to reform the financial markets and to avoid certain deviations. with this in mind, the european parliament adopted the commission's proposal on long-term shareholder engagement and the corporate governance declaration. the text stresses greater transparency in the activities of institutional investors and the remuneration of directors. i voted in favour of the commission's text.
in writing. ‒ in the wake of the financial crisis, weaknesses in european business regulation were identified, in particular the absence of taxation that is conducive to long-term investor commitment and a lack of financial transparency. the report provides an appropriate response to these problems by a series of proposals, such as the publication of lists of shareholders in english. the commission's proposal is to be adopted by the end of the year, and i hope that the council will be able to accept it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on shareholder rights. this text is a genuine step forward in encouraging longterm investment and transparency in business management. the introduction of country-by-country reporting will make it possible to detect - finally - tax optimisation schemes. in this time of crisis and tax evasion - i am thinking in particular of the luxleaks scandals - this directive is of paramount importance in order to put an end to the fraudulent maneuvers of multinational companies to the detriment of our citizens and smes. multinational companies will now have to openly declare the taxes paid in each country in which they operate - including tax havens - so that citizens and authorities can see where they actually pay their taxes, despite the temptation of our colleagues on the right in this house to remove these transparency measures. i am therefore pleased that the majority has been obtained to support the measures which we, the socialists and democrats, have taken.
in writing. the use of tax dumping by companies in europe is a burden that threatens the european project and puts member states in competition. i voted for the cofferati report because it is an expression of a european political will to combat the abuses of multinationals. it is urgent that the european union should take action to put an end to such practices. companies will now have to report on the activities of their subsidiaries country by country, revealing their turnover, the number of full-time posts, the total salaries, etc. this is a real breakthrough: multinational companies will no longer be able to hide their profits behind opaque accounts. the left wing forces in parliament, and in particular the s&d group, fought for these amendments to be voted on. it is a question of avoiding a new luxleaks, but above all of affirming our european project based on solidarity between countries. on the contrary, the conservatives in parliament, by fighting country-by-country reporting, have shown which side of the tax battle they are on. the report also calls for more transparency and dialogue. this should help to break away from the short-term logic of business.
in writing. ‒ the emissions trading system introduced by the kyoto protocol in 1997 has been interpreted as a 'right to pollute'. so it had the opposite effect. carbon dioxide emissions have not decreased, as previous forecasts and modelling had suggested. multinational stateless corporations take advantage of this system by using their financial power to buy emission rights from smaller companies. small and mediumsized enterprises are therefore the ones who suffer most from this system, even though they are by far not the biggest polluters. a stability reserve, as provided for in this text, would be only a modest palliative to a system in crisis because of its inefficiency, which, moreover, is a penalty for industry in the member states which are already in difficulty. for all these reasons, i opposed this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in the union. i would just like to draw the commission's attention to a phenomenon which has been observed: countries which have a large relocation of their industries have a corresponding reduction in their greenhouse gas emissions. this quota policy must not be used as an instrument for the destruction of our industries and hence of our jobs.
in writing. ‒ it is now clear to everyone that the ets is not working. but rather than question it, the technocrats so dear to mr schulz prefer to create a "market stability reserve" to overcome this proven dysfunction. this departure from the principle of market self-regulation - to which eurobieats are usually attached - thus appears as a terrible admission of failure. but for our industries, this solution is tantamount to the creation of a new indirect tax. and this will be all the more detrimental to them since their non-european competitors are not subject to it. in fact, this system only benefits unscrupulous speculators who use the ecological pretext of reducing co2 emissions to make pollution a market value like any other. it is not surprising that high-level fraudsters are taking advantage of this flawed system that you have set up, as a group of rogue dealers seem to have done with a gigantic fraud estimated at over 5 billion euros. i voted against this report, of course, just as i voted against the tajani report in the itre committee.
in writing. ‒ this report, which is intended to create a market stability reserve for the eu's greenhouse gas emissions trading system, was prompted by the fall in prices on the ghg emission allowance market (the 1997 kyoto protocol polluting rights). the forecasts for co2 price developments were therefore contradicted by the reality, namely the fall in prices. the reserve that we want to create does not fundamentally challenge the system. moreover, it will obviously favour the large companies in the polluting sectors, which have the funds to buy back the emission allowances, to the detriment of medium-sized industries and smes. this report does not solve the situation at all and reproduces market failures in this ets system while making companies less competitive and adding complexity that only the big multinationals will be able to understand and finance to pollute more. i therefore voted against.

in writing. ‒ the european emissions trading system is designed to reduce carbon emissions in the union in an economically efficient way. this should enable the european union to meet the criteria of the kyoto protocol. however, the system has shown its limitations. it was time to reform it so that it could achieve its ambitious goals. the introduction of a market stability reserve will reduce supply and demand imbalances and allow for greater flexibility in the quota market. investors will then start investing again in low-carbon technologies, which will result in a reduction in greenhouse gas emissions in the union. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i opposed this report because it does not draw the consequences of the failure of the right to pollute promoted by the kyoto protocol. the report encourages the creation of a stability reserve following the fall in prices on the greenhouse gas emission allowance market. the objective, which was to regulate carbon dioxide emissions downwards, has missed its target, and the market stability reserve is failing to transform this system. in addition, the largest and most polluting companies were found to be able to afford to buy back emission allowances, with medium-sized companies being the most upset by these measures. the failure of the ems, which reproduces market failures and is in line with the objectives of financialization of the environment sector, has therefore led me to reject this text.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this report is to establish a market stability reserve for the eu's greenhouse gas emissions trading system. with an entry into force in 2019, such a scheme aims to halt the fall in the price of the carbon tonne and introduce elements of flexibility in a market defined by a rigid supply. i had advocated that it should come into force in 2021 to give the industry time to get used to the idea that licences frozen during the last mandate should not be cancelled but should be placed in reserve as soon as the new mandate was established. i also championed the idea of an innovation fund, which was included in the final agreement for a maximum of 50 million licences before the launch of a new fund in 2021. finally, the issue of the competitiveness of european companies in the globalised market and carbon leakage was raised and will be addressed in the review of the ets directive before the end of 2015. i fully support the agreement reached with the council and i voted in favour.
in writing. the european union has established an emissions trading system (ets) to reduce carbon emissions while taking account of economic realities. however, the system suffers from a surplus of "polluting rights", which weighs down on the price of carbon and discourages investment in green energy. the vote will reform the functioning of the ets from 2019 onwards: in order to reduce the total supply of allowances, the surplus will be placed in a market stability reserve. the european union is thus demonstrating its determination to achieve its environmental objectives in the run-up to the 21st conference of the parties on climate change in paris.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament gave its backing on wednesday to a reform of the european co2 emission allowance system (ees). an automatic market stability reserve should support the price of allowances from 2019 onwards. this will allow a part of the allowances to be automatically withdrawn from the market and placed in a reserve fund if the surplus exceeds a certain threshold. this amendment to directive 2003/87/ec will help to better regulate one of the pillars of our climate policy and make it easier to achieve our greenhouse gas emission reduction targets. however, it will be essential to monitor the application of these rules, particularly by the most energy-intensive industries. this reform is also a signal from europe to its international partners ahead of the cop 21 conference to be held at the end of the year in paris. we call for an ambitious agreement on environmental protection and the fight against climate change at global level.

in writing. ‒ while europe has the potential to become a global maritime power, it favours deregulation and competition as the driving force behind its development. environmental protection and social policies are relegated to declarations of intent. this business model is not working. the text presented puts an end to an incongruity and an injustice. it includes seafarers, who were excluded from it, in the scope of the community directives on workers' rights. the ambition of the directives concerned is, however, short-sighted. the subject of the vote concerns the integration of seamen into their perimeters, and i vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ in france, seafarers already enjoy a high level of protection. the application of these directives to all european countries would therefore limit unfair competition from other countries and combat social dumping. i voted yes.
in writing. the morin-chartier report on seafarers aims to standardize the social protection of seafarers and to bring the whole of the european union into line with french standards in this field. although i am usually opposed to any standards imposed on states by the eu, i believe that this text makes it possible to combat social dumping and unfair competition effectively. france has not excluded people at sea from the application of the directives, since it enjoys a high level of protection. these recommendations therefore amount to subjecting the rest of the european union to the same rules as france. i therefore decided to vote in favour of this report in the sole interest of avoiding unfair competition.

in writing. ‒ the proposal for a directive aims to amend six existing european directives which exclude seafarers from their scope. the application of these directives varies widely from one member state to another: eight member states (austria, bulgaria, the czech republic, spain, france, portugal, sweden and slovenia) did not exclude seafarers, others excluded them from only one directive. the social partners in the shipping industry have different views on the abolition of exclusions, some in favour of exclusions, others not. the exclusions provided for in these directives are not applied in france: french seafarers already enjoy a high level of protection. by accepting the recommendations of the report, all european countries would be subject to the same rules and would be placed on the same level as france. this will limit unfair competition from other countries and will help to combat social dumping. i voted for this text.
in writing. ‒ the european union's directives on labour law must apply to all sectors of activity, to all categories of workers and regardless of the country of the union. this report makes it possible to remedy the unfair exclusions which have hitherto affected seafarers in the application of directives on labour law. some countries, including france, had chosen not to apply these unjustified exclusions. i voted for this report which helps to eliminate the exclusions which impede the rights of seafarers. it is necessary to improve the working conditions of seafarers, while taking into account the specificities of this sector of activity, but this must under no circumstances be done at the expense of their rights. seafarers, like all workers, have the right to social protection and to safe and appropriate living and working conditions on board ships. the attractiveness of a sector, as they say, does not depend on the deterioration of living, working and employment conditions, but on the contrary on their improvement. this is how young people can be encouraged to work in this sector.

in writing. ‒ the main objective of green growth is to achieve a low-carbon economy based on the efficient use of resources. one of the direct consequences of this type of growth is structural economic change, mainly driven by the more or less artificial scarcity of resources, technological change and innovation, the opening up of new markets, the evolution of the industrial fabric and consumer demand. this change, like all changes, would necessarily lead to all-round changes in the economy, the destruction of jobs and the creation and requalification of other jobs. the green economy will increasingly weigh on the circular economy and thus on prices. it should be remembered that resource prices have increased by 147% in 15 years. it is very clear that all these changes are part of the process of changing society, in favour of a consumer society that is also dematerialized from human activities. europe, which is largely absent from this major change, is not in a position to respond to all these changes, which is probably why europe now has 24 million unemployed.

in writing. - i voted yes. there's a lot of interesting stuff in this text. the aim is to create jobs and support industry. however, it is not enough to rely on the green economy. it is interesting to note that local authorities are seen as the level which is recognised as being the most competent to make a difference. it is important, however, to monitor the sustainability of these jobs, which must not be false solutions to combat unemployment. many areas will benefit from support under this project, including agriculture, which i can only support. i therefore support this report, which should create stable, sustainable and non-transferable jobs.
in writing. ‒ i am voting for this initiative, which enables a transition to a green economy, which is both a challenge and an opportunity for the labour market to be revitalized. it will be necessary to remain vigilant in implementing these drastic changes where the skilled workforce will have to respond to new skills needs or else it will have many employment consequences. its positive impact should allow the creation of stable, sustainable and non-delocalised jobs.
in writing. ‒ i welcome this own-initiative report from parliament which takes note of the environmental challenges and irreversible damage of the modes of consumption and production of productivist capitalism, but also of the potential for green job creation. the rapporteur stresses that the 'just transition' model could increase gdp by 1% while creating more than 2 million jobs. it attaches great importance throughout its report to the defence of decent, quality and sustainable jobs. it calls for support for the green conversion of smes, the main providers of jobs and green innovation. finally, it called for the development of training and skills in these sectors. all this with a follow-up of statistical data to assess the quality of the jobs created. the report focuses on employment aspects and therefore does not address the carbon market. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment-related aspects of the environment. i vote for it.
in writing. ‒ the objective of green growth is to achieve a low-carbon economy based on the efficient use of resources. it reflects a structural economic change mainly driven by the more or less artificial scarcity of resources, technological change and innovation, the opening up of new markets, the evolution of the industrial fabric and consumer demand. this would bring about a profound transformation in the whole economy and in a wide range of sectors. jobs would be created, others replaced, others redefined. this green economy would be doubled by the truly urban circular economy, which would have a significant impact on prices. the resources, it should be noted, have increased by 147% in 15 years. these two aspects of the new economy are part of the great change in society brought about by the dematerialization of human activities. for 50 years europe has not been able to bring about this profound change in the labour market. the 24 million unemployed in europe are proof of this.
in writing. the lambert report on the green jobs initiative aims to bring about a green economy based on the efficient use of resources. the various benefits that green growth is supposed to bring in terms of jobs, innovation, transformation - benefits that should be accompanied and encouraged by an effective transition - are recalled. however, this report does not in any way call into question the main causes of ecological change such as globalisation. it does, however, emphasize certain sectors such as waste treatment, insulation, biomass, organic agriculture, which i think it is important to support, since they cannot be relocated. this transition must be accompanied by the necessary training, but it must not be at the expense of our industrial base. i voted for this text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this green jobs initiative. the aim is to create new green jobs and to reduce energy and raw material consumption and greenhouse gas emissions through action along the value chain. according to the commission, the green goods and services sector grew by more than 50% between 2000 and 2011, generating more than 1.3 million jobs. similarly, the renewable energy sector is expected to create 20 million new jobs in europe by 2020.

in writing. ‒ the measures taken by the commission to support green growth should directly and indirectly promote the creation of jobs that are not subject to cyclical fluctuations and are therefore stable. however, all the successes anticipated in the text will depend primarily on the availability of a skilled workforce. the national front delegation is not opposed to the principle. however, these changes are drastic and could have serious consequences for employment if skills do not follow (much is said about jobs created but nothing about jobs saved). it will therefore be necessary to ensure that the transition is made in a pragmatic and supervised manner and that green workers are effectively supported in the transition. i am voting in favour because, from the point of view of employment and social affairs, this green jobs initiative should create stable, sustainable jobs which cannot be relocated.
in writing. ‒ wasting resources, climate change, pollution of all kinds, as well as inequality and social exclusion are hindrances to growth. to overcome this, the european parliament's report makes proposals to encourage job creation in the so-called green economy, in particular through the efficient use of resources (reuse and recycling). in other words, to try to counter the consumerist and disposable model. concrete proposals are put forward, such as support for the ecological conversion of smes, the establishment of targeted training programmes for workers, their participation in the evolution of jobs in order to promote their quality and sustainability. the resolution also stresses the potential of sectors such as energy efficiency through, for example, insulation of buildings, and the need to develop a european industrial strategy, including in the renewable energy sector. this goes beyond the commission's proposal for a so-called 'green jobs initiative'. i therefore voted in favour, but i have no illusions about the willingness to implement such measures to go beyond the fine speeches of the commission and the member states.
in writing. ‒ many of the amendments tabled were aimed at greater harmonisation and financial transparency in order to effectively combat tax fraud and evasion. the report provides for the adoption of a formal definition of the concept of 'tax haven'. it also plans to make public information on companies exploiting natural resources in developing countries. the desire to create the development of efficient tax administrations with a view to greater financial autonomy for developing countries in the coming decades is another positive aspect of this report. despite these good initiatives, many other parts are either too vague or not binding enough, which is why i abstained.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which highlights the need to strengthen financial and technical assistance to developing countries and regional administrative and fiscal frameworks in order to adopt solutions to improve transparency and cooperation in the fight against tax evasion, such as an automatic information exchange mechanism and the publication of country-by-country information, taking into account the needs and constraints of developing countries.
in writing. ‒ the text aims to promote the development of efficient tax administrations with a view to greater financial autonomy for developing countries in the coming decades. this objective is all the more legitimate in the context of a decline in eu funding.
in writing. as a development conference is being held in addis ababa, the fight against tax evasion seems to be a major issue for the countries of the south. indeed, at a time when the contributions of rich countries to development aid are declining because of fiscal austerity, tax evasion has become a major issue for the tax revenues of developing countries. this would cost them around €100 billion a year, significantly reducing their already low tax revenues (between 10% and 20%). developed countries lacked the financial means to contribute to the development of the developing countries, but it was necessary to find other sources of financing to help them build infrastructure, create jobs, stabilize themselves politically, etc. i regret that this report does not go far enough to call for the necessary transparency measures such as country-by-country information or the establishment of a list of tax havens. it even excludes the publication of essential information by natural resource companies in the developing countries. the text on tax havens is encouraging, but it does not go far enough. so i decided to abstain because it does not go far enough in the fight against money laundering, corruption and shell companies.
in writing. ‒ this report aims to promote greater efficiency in the tax administrations of developing countries in order to strengthen their financial autonomy. the measures described in this draft will thus enable them to collect taxes better and thus to cope better with the decline in the european union's allocations. the aim of these proposals is also to combat tax dumping between member states. the report as a whole is hardly to be criticized. in detail, we would like to point out that we are in favour of the information on beneficial ownership of companies being made public in open formats. this is a way of combating money laundering and the opacity that surrounds shell companies. we also want the concept of tax havens to be defined at international level and we believe that it is necessary to establish sanctions for those who resort to this kind of practice. i therefore voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ the third international conference on financing for development will be held in ethiopia in july 2015. in this context, the european parliament has prepared a report on the challenges of tax evasion and tax fraud in developing countries. the european union is working to eradicate both of these phenomena within its own borders. tax transparency is an absolute necessity. in our globalised economy, it is important that the union's partners have the same provisions on tax transparency to ensure fair trade competition. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ promoting the development of efficient tax administrations with a view to greater financial autonomy for developing countries is obviously a necessity, especially in a context where the european union, due to the economic and budgetary situation, is increasingly reducing its allocations to these countries. the report therefore promotes a legitimate objective, together with the fight against unfair competition in tax matters between states. some of the measures taken in this report are quite beneficial, such as the adoption of an internationally recognised definition of tax havens by the end of 2015, a need for simplification which should also go hand in hand with the establishment of sanctions against operations using this evasion. i am, however, more cautious about other suggestions in the report, such as the call for the member states to agree on a common consolidated corporate tax base: on the surface this may seem a legitimate simplification, but this approach is in the spirit of harmonization which carries within it the logic of increasing the union's powers, and therefore a loss of sovereignty for the member states.
in writing. ‒ this report, together with the report by silva pereira on financing for development adopted in may 2015, forms a 'package' of parliament's position for the 3rd international conference on financing for development to be held in addis ababa in july 2015. this report proposes to address the taxation and tax governance challenges faced by developing countries and the need to enhance the transparency and efficiency of national and international tax systems. the report also calls on the european commission to present without delay an ambitious action plan to support developing countries in the fight against tax evasion and the establishment of fair, balanced, efficient and transparent tax systems. considering that it is necessary to reach a comprehensive agreement on the post-2015 development agenda, which includes credible mechanisms for mobilising national funds and combating illicit financial flows, i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ in the preamble to her excellent report, my italian colleague elly schlein recalls the telling figures: illicit financial flows are equivalent to a loss of usd 1 000 billion per year for developing countries (peds), or ten times the amount of aid they receive to eradicate poverty. the report, which was adopted by a large majority, contains very ambitious proposals, some of which i defended in the taxe committee on aggressive tax optimisation. it also called on the commission to submit a proposal for companies operating in europe and the least developed countries, whether listed or not, to disclose, including to the public, their country-by-country accounts (country-by-country information). it also called for an internationally recognised definition of tax havens, sanctions for operators who use them and a blacklist of countries, including eu members, that do not combat or tolerate tax evasion by the end of 2015. finally, with this report, the commission is called upon to adopt as a matter of urgency an action plan to help the developing countries to combat tax fraud and evasion in a practical way. i am satisfied that the lines are finally moving in europe, and i voted for it without hesitation.
in writing. ‒ the report notes that "tax revenues remain low in most developing countries, making them particularly vulnerable to tax evasion and avoidance by taxpayers and businesses". it therefore promotes "fair, balanced, rational and transparent tax regimes" which "provide the essential funding to governments to cover citizens' rights to basic public services, such as health and education for all" and which "help to reduce the effect of inequalities". to help these countries fight tax evasion, the report calls for the publication of country-by-country information by multinational companies. for each territory in which they operate, they will have to indicate the names of all subsidiaries and their respective financial performance, relevant tax information, assets and number of employees. the report also calls for an international definition of tax havens, sanctions for operators who use them and a blacklist of countries, including eu member states, that do not combat tax evasion. i am voting for this text which dares to attack the multinationals.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on combating tax evasion and illicit financial flows, which is essential to eradicate poverty and growing inequalities in developing countries. multinational companies should adopt a country-by-country reporting regime, which would require them to publicly report on their financial performance, the names of all subsidiaries, their tax data, assets and numbers. information on the ownership of a company should also be made public in order to prevent anonymous shell companies from being involved in money laundering or financing illegal activities. we also call on eu financial institutions to ensure that companies receiving eu support do not participate in tax evasion.
in writing. the issue of tax evasion is of particular importance for developing countries, as illicit financial flows represent a loss of resources far greater than the aid received to eradicate poverty. the schlein own-initiative report highlights two aspects of the assistance that the european union could provide to developing countries in the fight against tax evasion. the union would have a first lever: to ensure that its companies are exemplary in tax matters. the report calls on the institutions concerned (eib, ebrd, etc.) to ensure that companies receiving their support do not participate in tax evasion. the report also calls on the commission to require multinationals operating in europe and the developing countries to publish a country-by-country information report. a second means of action would be to mobilise the member states: for example, no cooperation agreement should be signed without the concept of good governance; a weak democracy feeds tax evasion and increases the burden on the poorest. it is essential that the union, to the extent of its capabilities, assist developing countries in achieving better tax governance; i have therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ this report addresses the issues of tax evasion and tax fraud in third countries and opaque tax havens. it is a criticism of tax-free regimes which attract capital that should be taxed in other countries and which generate ferocious tax dumping. this report contains a good analysis of a system that allows banking and financial information to remain private the report therefore calls for a comprehensive action plan to combat tax evasion in developing countries, including the generalization of the un model tax treaty, the strengthening of financial and technical assistance to developing countries, the adoption of automatic mechanisms for the exchange of information and the creation of an international body to promote the comprehensive reform of existing international tax rules. this is not going far and one might say that the eu member states could start by sweeping their own doors. i voted in favour, however, because i thought that, beyond the list of good intentions, it was the right thing to do.
in writing. ‒ the principles and beliefs underlying this report seem rather positive. the increase in pollution should make us think about our lifestyle and consumption. the proposals in this report are intended to influence the work of the commission by the end of 2015. these include incentives to move towards an 'eco-design' policy for products and towards 'zero waste', thus developing recycling of these products. the report calls for very restrictive standards for new buildings and for a plan to renovate the existing building. these demands do not address the root cause, which is the liberal materialistic ideology and its cult of infinite growth. the report is ultimately a quitus for the commission to issue new unnecessary requirements. so i objected.

in writing. this report on the transition to a circular economy is an own-initiative report by parliament, which informs the commission of the nature of the proposals it is required to make by the end of 2015. the circular economy aims to produce goods and services while significantly reducing the consumption and waste of raw materials and non-renewable energy sources. while the development of the circular economy and everything related (green economy, conversion, etc.) is a good idea, this model is the opposite of the eu's. it is a globalist, free-trade model that favors sustained growth, often in defiance of environmental, fiscal or social standards. the circular economy which is based on short circuits, local preference and local production, avoiding imports too far away to contain pollution, has nothing to do with our model, but it is a form of economy which we should support without going into the imposition of excessive standards as is the case here for the building sector. i therefore voted against this report, which should allow the commission to legislate on this point in place of the states.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament's own-initiative report calls on the commission to make proposals on the circular economy. this is a series of measures aimed at moving towards eco-design of products and 'zero waste'. the report also calls on the commission to impose very restrictive standards on energy consumption in buildings to be renovated and in new construction. while it is necessary to pursue a long-term policy that respects the environment, it is unthinkable to increase the burden of environmental standards without any compensation for economic actors. the success of a viable circular economy is in fact inseparable from the implementation of smart protectionism at least at european level and the promotion of short producer-consumer circuits. in the absence of these two conditions, this new legal arsenal will only have the effect of undermining the competitiveness of our companies and once again favouring imports from countries which do not respect any basic social and environmental standards. this is a text which is ridiculous for the environment and harmful to our businesses. that is why i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on resource efficiency and the transition to a circular economy. it is very important that we make progress on environmental protection and recycling in europe. however, it must be understood that our economy is in crisis and that certain restrictive measures may stifle our businesses. to remain competitive in the global economy and to respect the environment are two compatible objectives, which must be balanced to be as efficient as possible. in this report i also supported the proposal to encourage the creation of agreements in the member states whereby the food retail sector distributes unsold products to charitable associations. this is a provision already in place in france and which will have to be applied throughout europe to combat food waste.

in writing. ‒ on thursday 9 july, i voted in favour of the report on resource efficiency and the transition to a circular economy. the measures adopted are a clear message to the commission, which will make its proposals for the circular economy by the end of 2015. in the near future, we will have fewer resources for a larger population. such a transition to more sustainable and resource-efficient economic models is a concrete solution to these challenges. the report calls for a binding waste prevention target by 2025 and a recycling target of 70% of municipal waste and 80% of packaging by 2030. it also proposes other targets, such as reducing marine litter by 50% or food waste by 30% by 2025. if europe is to be more efficient, it must make the best use of its resources. it is also essential to ensure that we do not add too much to the already existing legislative constraints, which would undermine the competitiveness of our companies. to achieve this, it is essential to strike the right balance between the environment and the economy, between ambition and realism.

in writing. ‒ the circular economy is an economic and industrial system that is low in carbon and energy and low in natural resources that are not, rarely, slowly or costly renewable, based on eco-design of products and services that must promote recycling at the best cost. the report before us supports this concept. the commission is therefore asked to improve the sustainability, reuse and recycling of products and to ban toxic chemicals and promote eco-design. it also calls for binding waste reduction targets to be achieved by 2025. i am voting for this non-legislative text, with no illusions about its effects.
