in writing. this report on the transition to a circular economy is an own-initiative report by parliament, which informs the commission of the nature of the proposals it is required to make by the end of 2015. the circular economy is about decoupling economic growth from resource use. its objective is to produce goods and services while greatly limiting the consumption and waste of raw materials and non-renewable energy sources. however, this definition and economic model is the exact opposite of the economic model supported by the eu. indeed, the circular economy is based on short-circuiting, on local preference and not on the import of products crossing the planet on cargo ships. the report envisages a whole series of measures such as the 'zero waste' objective, the imposition of restrictive standards in the building sector (at a time when the construction sector is in crisis in france). i voted against this report, which is only intended to give the commission a free hand to legislate for the member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the efficient use of resources. it advocates a transition of the european economy towards a circular model, with the establishment of a more coherent legislative framework for sustainable production and consumption. it is not just a question of fighting the union's dependence on dwindling resources, but also of reducing our waste, especially food. this is particularly important and i am pleased that this report calls on the commission to encourage the creation of agreements in the member states whereby the food retail sector distributes unsold products to charitable associations.
in writing. ‒ the adoption of the resource efficiency report emphasises that the circular economy is a virtuous circle that we must absolutely encourage following the adoption of the resource efficiency report. to reduce waste, to use our resources efficiently, to create a new economy, the measures we have just adopted are a clear message to the european commission, which will make its proposals for a circular economy at the end of the year. however, we must remain cautious, because many very ambitious, if not too ambitious, proposals have been put forward in this report. in our constant desire to set an example for the rest of the world, we risk shooting ourselves in the foot by killing the competitiveness of our smes and our companies. we must not oppose the environment and the economy: we must support our companies, especially the most innovative ones. we also need a global vision for effective legislation, a european vision for the circular economy. before a waste target is set at european level, we must have harmonised calculation methods for all member states.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament adopted a text setting up european legislation to combat the waste of food, products, energy and materials. i am glad that i voted in favour of this report. europe is doing this to protect consumers and to combat a scourge that may have long-term consequences for our planet. we throw away nearly 90 million tonnes of food a year, an unacceptable waste that we want to stop.
in writing. ‒ the unsustainable use of resources not only causes environmental damage, but also poses an economic risk. the global economy uses the equivalent of 1.5 earths in resources to produce and absorb waste. it is estimated that this number will reach the equivalent of two planets by the 2030s. continuing on this path would lead to an ecological and economic impasse. that is why i have voted in favour of this report, which opens the way to a paradigm shift. the report also calls for the renovation of housing stock, the cascading use of resources and the abolition of environmentally harmful subsidies. a common framework for the assessment of progress is also proposed with a view to achieving uniform and transparent progress within the union. although it has no legal value, this text encourages the commission to take action to meet the environmental challenge.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution on the circular economy which encourages the european union to manage its resources more efficiently. given that it would take a planet and a half to support the resource consumption of our global economy, it is high time we found sustainable access to raw materials. the objective is to increase resource efficiency at european level by 30% by 2030. beyond the environmental benefits, this improvement could help create two million sustainable jobs and lead to an increase in gdp currently estimated at 1%. to achieve this, legislative measures are needed, including new legislation on waste management before the end of the year. on the question of food waste, i voted in favour of an ambitious target to reduce food waste and encouraged the establishment of agreements in the member states to distribute unsold food to charitable organisations. i have also asked the commission to assess the possibilities of increasing the use of environmentally friendly and biodegradable food packaging. finally, i would like to reiterate my conviction that there is a need for an extension of legislation on eco-design and for a plan of measures to combat planned obsolescence.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report on the circular economy and accompanying measures such as reducing waste generation and resource efficiency. with the adoption of this text, we have sent a clear message to the european commission with a view to its forthcoming proposals on the circular economy by the end of the year. in this context, it is important to support both our enterprises, by setting ambitious but realistic proposals, and research. finally, i would like to emphasize the introduction into the text, thanks in particular to the french delegation of the epp, of a request for the establishment of agreements between large supermarkets and food aid associations so that they can benefit from the unsold products. this is part of a more united europe and a first step in the fight against food waste.
in writing. the fight for the environment requires better waste management and new consumption habits. it is with this in mind that the european parliament adopted the pietikäinen report on the circular economy. we want to encourage the commission to make proposals quickly on this subject. the main challenge of moving to a circular economy is extending the life of a product. this implies a fight against planned obsolescence. it is also necessary to facilitate the reuse and processing of products by turning to eco-design. this serves two purposes: to reduce our waste and to relieve the enormous pressure we are putting on our natural resources. parliament proposed concrete measures to initiate this transition, including: introducing constraints to reduce energy waste by 30% on resources compared to 2014; increasing recycling targets to 70% for municipal waste by 2030 and 80% for packaging waste by 2030. while i welcome the collective awareness of these issues, i will remain vigilant to ensure that these proposals are translated into action.
in writing. ‒ the circular economy is about decoupling economic growth from resource use. in the end, it is a new doctrine of development that is at stake. this parliament's own-initiative report sets out the commission's proposals for the end of 2015. this is a series of incentive measures, including a policy of 'eco-design' of products; the commission has also proposed that the european union should be able to take action to achieve 'zero waste', to impose very restrictive standards on buildings that actually consume energy and to renovate existing buildings to this end, to develop 'industrial synergies' to use cascading resources. this policy, which may appear to be responsible and farsighted, is in contradiction with the economic model advocated by the european union. the basis for a viable circular economy would be to promote short circuits, work and production at home and thus limit international trade. the text is therefore ridiculous and harmful, since it is a blank cheque to the commission to issue new unproductive requirements for the member states. i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ the circular economy aims to reduce resource and raw material consumption and pollution by improving recycling, energy efficiency, reducing waste and improving product design. some amendments from the right have weakened the resolution, removing the binding 2030 targets to maintain only a vague reference to 2050. the reduction of food or industrial waste, which accounts for a large proportion of waste, has been excluded from the scope of the directive, the industry lobby insists. the commission removed this issue from its work programme in december 2014. in this resolution, parliament is asking for a proposal by the end of the year. this resolution is complementary to the one on green jobs. without much illusion that the commission and the member states are prepared to go further with these ideas, i nevertheless see some ways of working towards the definition of another economy. i therefore voted in favour of this, but i have no illusions. the epp and fn voted against.
in writing. ‒ this report supports several proposals in the event of a radioactive emergency, including giving the commission the power to act as a matter of urgency by means of implementing regulations to lower radioactivity thresholds or to sanction member states that allow products to circulate in excess of the permitted limits. despite the presentation of the report, the limits defined in it are the same as in 1987, even though japan adopted new, stricter standards after the fukushima disaster. i regret that the national front was not heard when it asked for the possibility for member states to suspend the free movement of goods and persons in an emergency, as the current limits are not satisfactory. i consider this text to be largely cosmetic and in no way constitutes a breakthrough on the nuclear safety front. i therefore voted against this report.

in writing. the text on maximum permitted levels of radioactive contamination after a nuclear accident aims to revise three regulations dating from the 1980s and 1990s which defined the limits of radioactivity allowed in food after a nuclear accident. this well-intentioned text is a miserable one. if we look at the text in question, the limits are the same as those laid down in a regulation that is almost thirty years old. this inaction is particularly damaging, even as countries like japan introduced standards after the march 11, 2011 earthquake that are up to twenty times lower than those of the european union. the minimum would be to allow member states to suspend the dogma of free movement in the event of a nuclear accident to guarantee the food security of the french. this cosmetic text could be improved and be really effective if it were amended. as it stands, i can only vote against.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this text is to revise three regulations dating from 1987, 1989 and 1990 which define the limits of radioactivity allowed in food following a nuclear accident. it is cosmetic in nature and does not substantially alter the levels of contaminated food which have remained too high and no longer meet the new public health requirements. the text also does not provide for member states to suspend the free movement of products in the event of radioactive contamination of certain foodstuffs. finally, it gives the european commission more oversight power than it seems able to properly assume. for all these reasons, and because the amendment tabled by the enl group was rejected, i voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ this report sets maximum permitted levels of radioactive contamination for foodstuffs, for foodstuffs of minor importance and for feedingstuffs which may be placed on the market after a nuclear accident or any other radiological emergency which may lead to or has led to significant radioactive contamination of foodstuffs and feedingstuffs, and the procedures for making these maximum permitted levels applicable. i support this report, which is balanced. however, i have opposed the rapporteur's change of legal basis from a simple consultation of parliament under the euratom treaty to a codecision procedure under article 168 (4) (b) and article 114 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. in fact, according to recent case law of the court of justice and an opinion of the parliamentary committee on legal affairs, such an amendment could be annulled in the event of a dispute with the council. i was not able to win on this point of form, but i voted in favour of this report which is important for the public health of european citizens.
in writing. ‒ following the fukushima disaster, the european union had to update its legislation setting maximum permissible levels of radioactive contamination after a nuclear accident. this report therefore incorporates the new data as defined by the international commission on radiological protection (icrp). the aim is twofold: to reduce as far as possible the exposure of the population to radioactivity following a nuclear or radiological crisis, while ensuring a gradual recovery of economic activities. this legislative update should also consolidate existing euratom standards in the field of health protection. article 31 of the euratom treaty on the development of standards for the protection of the general public and workers against the dangers of radiation is, in my view, the appropriate legal basis for this regulation.

in writing. ‒ the resolution aims to establish a capital markets union. the commission wants to encourage direct financing for smes by simplifying the rules for raising funds and by relaunching securitisation or venture capital. the integration of smes into this type of financing mechanism risks fuelling the financial bubble and increasing the risk of a stock market crash similar to the famous subprime crisis. above all, the use of these mechanisms reflects the commission's inability to reorient the activities of banking institutions towards the financing of enterprises. without a large law separating commercial and retail banking, coupled with a legal and fiscal framework that provides incentives, the financial flow from banks to businesses will remain limited. that is why i abstained on this text, pending concrete proposals.
in writing. ‒ the serious consequences of the 2008 crisis have illustrated the fragility of the european financial system. it is now vital to boost investment in enterprises, and in particular smes, in the long term. building a genuine capital markets union covering the 28 member states would be a significant step. it would help to mobilise more investment for smes and attract more international investment to europe. above all, it would make the financial system more stable by diversifying sources of financing, as the crisis has shown that companies are too dependent on the banking system. this resolution lays the foundations for the construction of this union. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ this resolution is parliament's contribution to the debate on the construction of a capital markets union launched by the european commission. the commission's findings clearly show that investment in the real economy in europe has been declining for several decades, despite a significant increase in the size of the european and international financial sector over the same period. this situation persists even though there is a large reserve of dormant capital, notably held by the insurance sector, which could be used more efficiently. in this context, the establishment of a capital markets union could create a coherent regulatory environment across the union and bring capital markets closer to smes with a view to stimulating financing of the real economy. such a project should be based on a more efficient allocation of savings, on a better mitigation of risks, in particular cross-border risks, and on the existence of an effective complementary channel for financing the real economy. i believe that there is a need to boost investment, and therefore innovation and the creation of wealth and jobs in europe, and i therefore voted in favour of this resolution.

in writing. ‒ this resolution sets out the opinion of the econ committee on the commission's forthcoming draft on the capital markets union. the aim is to develop alternative financing methods to bank financing, in particular for smes, by facilitating access to capital markets (securitisation, venture capital, stock markets). the instability of markets has been one of the main causes of the major crises of recent years. moreover, banks have since then cleaned up their balance sheets to a large extent and are receiving considerable support (tltros from the ecb) to fulfil their role as lenders to the real economy. we must force them to do so and to stop playing the markets by establishing a real separation of investment and retail banking. this would be the real way to stimulate investment, which would be less risky than the capital markets union. the report, while providing for some nuances in relation to the main lines of the commission's green paper, does not call into question the principle of this policy. so it is wise to abstain.

in writing. ‒ with this motion for a resolution, the european parliament has expressed its desire to create a coherent regulatory environment across the union to encourage the development of capital markets. i support such a project, which would enable europe to respond better to financial crises similar to the one we experienced in 2007 and to respond to the problem of long-term investment. the text defines three priorities which form the development axis of the project: more efficient allocation of savings, better risk mitigation through deepening cross-border markets, and the creation of complementary channels to finance the real economy.
in writing. ‒ the capital markets union is a set of proposals to diversify the financing of companies, which are heavily dependent on banks in europe (almost 80% of the total). to this end, the commission intends to develop direct financing on the capital markets, in particular for smes, by simplifying the rules for raising funds, relaunching securitisation or promoting venture capital. we are not sure whether it is appropriate to relaunch market financing, particularly securitisation, which was the main factor in the instability of the last crises. banks must return to their role as lenders to the real economy, which they are no longer doing satisfactorily. they should be able to do so, having cleaned up their balance sheets since the end of the crisis. for the banks to play their part, what is needed first of all is a real separation of commercial and retail banking, and market regulation that will enable them to regain their vocation. the capital markets union, led by commissioner jonathan hill, a former city lobbyist, looks like a promotion of shadow banking and the investment banking model that led to the subprime mortgage crisis. i abstained until i had concrete proposals.
in writing. ‒ this resolution deals with the construction of the capital market within the european union. a whole program... the text, unsurprisingly, takes a neoliberal approach. while austerity policies are plunging the countries of the european union into a recession which is particularly affecting the most vulnerable social groups, we are being offered a text which merely acknowledges the crisis and offers only a vague 'moralisation' of financial capitalism, while calling for it to be developed even further and made ever more 'attractive'. always the same dogmatism. it is time to put a stop to excessive speculation in the financial markets, which only brings crises, mass redundancies and growing inequalities to the real economy. a european approach should finally allow for the regulation of these capital markets which have gone mad and give priority to public infrastructure and investment, but also to smes, and encourage long-term commitment, to the benefit of all. i voted against this text, of course.
in writing. ‒ the european commission will adopt in the coming months a european agenda on security for 2015-2020 which will address the various actions to be implemented to increase security in europe. radicalism, terrorist financing, cooperation between europol and other european agencies, and arms trafficking will be the main topics on the agenda. the subjects on this agenda seem to be moving in the right direction, although i have very strong doubts about the question of radicalism. while many young europeans, and especially many french, are joining terrorist organisations, particularly to fight in syria, the european commission's feeble attempts to put an end to this phenomenon have all failed. the union cannot effectively combat this scourge unless it gives the states back control of their borders. i am in favour of the re-establishment of internal frontiers as a prerequisite, so i voted against this text.

in writing. ‒ the motion for a resolution deals with the european security programme. it contains elements which go beyond the competences conferred on the union by the treaty of lisbon and, with them, the sovereignty of each member state. while security is a major issue requiring cooperation between nations, it must not become a pretext for the concentration of power in the hands of technocrats who have proven themselves incompetent and failures. the union's immigration policy is a failure, as is its policy against the jihadist networks and the islamic state. these criminal networks thrive mainly because of the absence of border controls within the schengen area. the european software is deficient and therefore it should be replaced by a return to national sovereignty, combined with european cooperation where necessary. i voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ this resolution sets out the european parliament's position on the european agenda on security for the period 2015-2020, as proposed by the commission. in view of the complex, hybrid, asymmetrical, unconventional, international and difficult to predict threats to internal security, as highlighted by the recent attempted terrorist attacks in france, a european response is needed that is coherent, comprehensive, multi-layered and coordinated. i believe that the priority given by the european commission to combat terrorism, violent extremism, crossborder organised crime and cybercrime is going in the right direction. in this type of debate, it is even more necessary to strike a balance between respect for fundamental rights and security requirements. i think that this resolution is unbalanced in this respect and that is why i abstained.
in writing. ‒ last april, the commission adopted its european security agenda, a key strategic document which aims to set the broad guidelines for the european union's internal and external security policy. the european parliament's resolution is our contribution to this programme. it sets out clearly the priorities of our parliament. in the light of the serious challenges and threats terrorism, violent extremism, cross-border organised crime and cybercrime facing the european union today, the european union needs to act in a coordinated manner and strengthen its efforts. in particular, our resolution strongly calls for more transparency, accountability and democratic control in security policies, an optimisation of the use and implementation of the legal instruments in force in the union, a more unified intersectoral and interagency approach and a better reconciliation of the internal and external dimensions of security.
in writing. ‒ while the commission presented its roadmap on security last april, it was essential that parliament contributed to it. i have therefore supported parliament's resolution on the european security programme, because i believe it is a balanced response between security requirements on the one hand and fundamental rights requirements on the other. the complex and evolving threats to the internal security of the union today require more than ever a comprehensive, coherent and coordinated response at european and international level. the unprecedented nature of the current crisis requires, among other things, an upgrade of european security and judicial systems, tools adapted to the media and digital jihad that allows terrorists to reach every point of european and international territory, as well as an offensive against the financial flows that fuel the fight against terrorism. however, we cannot be satisfied with a purely repressive approach, since the causes of this phenomenon are complex and inextricably linked to social, economic and even psychological factors. any solution requires measures to prevent radicalisation before it leads to violence.

in writing. this report on security challenges in the middle east and north africa and prospects for political stability is concerned about the destabilisation of the middle east generated by the ongoing conflicts in the region. it never addresses the root causes of this destabilisation, namely the western and self-interested interventions in iraq and libya. the solutions put forward in this text only go in the direction of a dramatic inflation of the powers and competences of the european union to the detriment of the diplomacy and defence of each member state. instead of seeing egypt as a necessary and effective partner in the fight against terrorism, the eu is now meddling in egypt's affairs and denouncing the way the country is dealing with the islamist threat: yet another proof of the eu's intolerable political interference under the guise of 'moral' and 'humanitarian' intervention, which, when it leads to military interventions, is precisely at the origin of the chronic instability of the region. federalist logic depriving the member states of their diplomatic prerogatives, political interference and lack of respect for sovereign states are all reasons why i voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ i abstained on this text on the security challenges in the middle east and north africa and the prospects for political stability. the report, which is now before the european parliament, calls on the member states to redouble their efforts to welcome asylum seekers and to deal with the cases already lodged without delay. i think it would be preferable if safe camps under the auspices of the united nations could accommodate people fleeing conflict close to their countries of origin, so that they do not risk their lives trying to cross the mediterranean, are not handed over to unscrupulous smugglers and do not end up stranded in the slums of europe.

in writing. ‒ in the face of the increase in conflicts in the middle east and north africa and the growing political and social instability in these regions, the european parliament adopted an own-initiative report on the security challenges and prospects for political stability in these regions. i voted in favour of this text. it is important to identify possible actions to be implemented and to encourage member states to cooperate in order to help the political, economic and social stabilisation of these regions.
in writing. ‒ the resolution on security challenges in the middle east and north africa (moan), for which vincent peillon is rapporteur, draws an alarming conclusion on the situation in the region, which is at war with the islamic state group and is hit by acts of terrorism. this resolution, which i fully support, calls on the european union to strengthen its political support for this region, which is now under threat as a wind of freedom swept through it during the arab spring. strengthening its position by increasing the presence of its representatives, organising more frequent summits with the arab league, establishing better cooperation in many areas (prevention of radicalisation, culture, education, security), dialogue with civil society, defending human rights and women's rights are all challenges that the european union must address. it must now speak with one voice to exist diplomatically and become a major political actor. the report envisages continuing and strengthening the union's cooperation with the nafo countries and proposes a new paradigm: that of genuine political cooperation which goes beyond economic issues.
in writing. ‒ this report by vincent peillon on security challenges in the middle east and north africa is a typical example of an eu that curses the consequences of phenomena whose causes it cherishes. the report rightly expresses concern about the destabilisation of the middle east caused by the conflicts in syria, iraq and libya, but never addresses the real causes of this situation. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to cover the protection of the environment and the protection of the environment from harmful substances. security issues are also once again being used as a pretext to increase eu prerogatives to the detriment of diplomacy and national defenses. the text is also critical of egypt, which, rather than being seen as a partner in the fight against islamist terrorism, is being singled out for its "human rights violations", which is far from constructive from a diplomatic point of view.
in writing. ‒ the report starts from the fact that the eu is partly responsible for the clear failure of the policies pursued in north africa and the middle east in recent years, with the multiplication of conflicts (iraq, syria, libya, yemen, etc.), the spread of jihadist areas and the security role of the governments of the region. that is a good start, but it is the only point of agreement i could find. it does not say anything about the responsibility of certain member states or of the european union's "allies" (the united states, israel, the arab states). conflicts are seen mainly through the lens of religion. the fight against terrorism is only approached from a military point of view and the management of migration flows from a security point of view. finally, the same economic recipes are always put forward: the establishment of free trade areas, the organization of the brain drain, the exploitation of natural resources... in the midst of the review of the european neighbourhood policy, this is therefore a slip in the bucket, far from the major challenges facing the region. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ this report underlines the importance of an external policy of the union and therefore wishes to extend the powers of the european neighbourhood policy. it is an interference in the sovereignty of the member states with the aim of depriving them of the possibility of pursuing an independent foreign policy, subjecting it totally to that of the union. the report also extends the union's 'values' to its external partners on the grounds that the union's association agreements are based on fundamental universal values and the defence of human rights, equality and human dignity. it opens the door to new waves of mass immigration, declaring itself "favourable to increased mobility within the neighbourhood area ... through facilitation of visa issuance and liberalization of visa regimes". i therefore opposed this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this debate as the committee had recommended in the background.
in writing. ‒ i question the will of the technocrats in brussels to encroach ever more on the prerogatives of the eu member states, especially as the foreign policy pursued by brussels seems to be decided in washington.
in writing. this report on the european neighbourhood policy aims to increase the eu's competence in relations with the eu's neighbouring countries. this neighbourhood policy is in fact a policy of interfering in the internal affairs of countries neighbouring the eu and dictating to them the reforms necessary for potential and future membership of the union. it also calls for a stronger defence europe, which i strongly condemn, since this remains and must remain a national competence, especially when it comes to dealing with russia. we thought the cold war was over, but it's back in a different form thanks to the eu... finally, of course, this policy advocates free movement of people and goods within the neighbourhood area as if the eu did not already have all the difficulties in controlling movement within the schengen area itself. i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. the kukan report on the review of the european neighbourhood policy is a dangerous leap forward. it was originally intended to integrate the countries of central and eastern europe when the european union was enlarged to include this area. today, ms mogherini, vice-president of the european commission and high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy, is taking this policy to the southern mediterranean and the eastern borders of ukraine. this interference by the eu is dangerous and very imprudent, given the geopolitical situation of many of the countries covered by the text. i therefore voted against mr kukan's report.
in writing. ‒ the kukan report on the review of the european neighbourhood policy (enp) aims to increase the union's competence in relation to its external policy: 'whereas the enp remains a strategic priority of the union's foreign policy; whereas the revision of the enp should be carried out with the aim of strengthening this policy and continuing efforts to achieve an overall, comprehensive and effective common foreign and security policy of the union'. the european neighbourhood policy aims at both increasing the union's profile in its area of influence, preparing the accession of new candidate states and exporting the union's 'values' without taking geopolitical realities into account. i voted against this text because i am opposed to the union's increasing power in the field of foreign policy.
in writing. ‒ one of the european union's main priorities is to guarantee the security of its citizens. there have indeed been no armed conflicts within the european borders for many years. unfortunately, the same cannot be said of the neighbourhood. we are witnessing great tensions on the borders of the union, both north and south. the european neighbourhood policy is therefore a crucial element in stabilising and securing the neighbouring regions. for this reason, the eu strategy needs to be revised and modernised. we cannot stand idly by in the face of events at our borders. it is about the security of our citizens and the stability of these regions. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this report is to present the european parliament's position on the ongoing review of the european neighbourhood policy launched by the european commission. the european parliament is clearly in favour of a renewed policy which is more strategic, targeted, flexible and coherent, and able to respond adequately and rapidly to the needs of the neighbouring countries. given the current strategic economic and security challenges in europe's southern and eastern neighbourhood, the european neighbourhood policy must respond appropriately to fragmented national realities. the security aspect of this policy should also be strengthened, while maintaining a budget allocation of two thirds for the mediterranean and one third for the eastern partnership. i have voted in favour of this balanced report.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report provides a good diagnosis of neighbourhood policy. it must be able to adapt to different situations. it cannot be the same in eastern europe, the south of the mediterranean or the caucasus. the challenges and crises are not the same. a more effective neighbourhood policy will therefore have to be based on differentiated relations between countries, in order to define and implement more appropriate and therefore more effective partnerships.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to vote against this report on the review of the european neighbourhood policy to increase the union's powers in relation to non-eu neighbouring countries. the rapporteur stresses the importance of an external policy of the union and therefore wishes to extend the powers of the european neighbourhood policy. this is an unacceptable interference in the sovereignty of the member states, which are being deprived of the possibility of conducting their own foreign policy, or at least of being subject to the eu. the rapporteur is not content to interfere in the politics of the member states, but he also wants to impose the union's 'values' on its external partners by claiming that the union's association agreements are based on fundamental universal values, the defence of human rights, equality and human dignity. the report supports and defends a completely irrelevant immigration policy by declaring itself 'favourable to increased mobility within the neighbourhood area ... through facilitation of visa issuance and visa liberalisation'.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by my colleague eduard kukan on the review of the european neighbourhood policy. the report aims to contribute to the commission's ongoing review of the outdated european neighbourhood policy (enp) by calling for an enp better adapted to today's challenges, with a clear and ambitious political vision and strategic objectives and priorities for the short, medium and long term. i welcome the fact that this report was adopted by a large majority.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the revision of the european neighbourhood policy. in the face of the new challenges in southern and eastern europe, the european union must adapt to avoid destabilisation within its own member states. the dialogue between the union and its neighbours must be intensified in order to re-establish stable, secure and democratic areas for all people. while stressing the need for mutual accountability and a common commitment to the union's values and principles, future action will need to take a case-by-case approach with neighbouring countries.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the resolution on the revision of the european neighbourhood policy, as this report is clearly designed with the eu enlargement in mind. the rapporteur has confirmed this on several occasions, notably by tabled an amendment aimed at strengthening the role of the commissioner for enlargement, or by calling on the high representative to draw inspiration from the european economic area in order to gradually integrate the neighbourhood countries. this is the well-known small-step technique. paragraph 58 is also revealing: 'stresses the importance of the free movement of persons and supports increased mobility within the neighbourhood area, in a safe and well-managed environment, through facilitation of visa issuance and visa liberalisation, in particular for students, young people, artists and researchers; calls on the commission to further encourage, in cooperation with the member states, partnerships for mobility within the neighbourhood and to develop the possibilities for circular migration schemes, which would open safe and legal pathways for migration.' we want even more immigration, even though the people in europe are against it.

in writing. ‒ the current upheavals in the neighbourhood in eastern and southern europe require an ambitious and strategic redefinition of our neighbourhood policy. faced with these new challenges, the eu must be able to think more politically about its action. this report responds to the plurality of expectations for european leadership, from neighbours to the crossroads of several 'close strangers'. the kukan report is a real project to promote our values, by supporting democracy and human rights, as well as the necessary revalorisation of the attractive factors proposed by the eu. on the other hand, the text stresses the need for a reconfiguration of the intelligent approach of our neighbours. the deepening of dialogue with civil society and the strengthening of the control of aid measures are in line with this. finally, as the prospect of trade and free trade agreements alone is no longer an effective lever for strengthening our partnership with the neighbourhood, the report opens up the possibility of sharing knowledge and creating networks at different levels, thus going beyond the union's economy. i voted for this report, which goes further towards establishing a safer, more democratic and more prosperous neighbourhood.
in writing. ‒ the eu's european neighbourhood policy aims to reward good students, like ukraine, in the service of its neoliberal agenda. in the framework of the eastern partnership, the eu continues its cooperation with azerbaijan, where no elections have been declared free by international observers since 1993. this policy has enabled european companies, through multiple free trade agreements, to plunder these countries, particularly in the mediterranean area, leading to the impoverishment of the populations, the development of conflicts and migration. this report therefore does not take stock of these failures. even the last revision in 2011 contained better passages calling for "helping partners to build democratic, pluralistic and secular states" or stressing "the need to ensure a minimum wage". i am voting against this policy of economic and political subjugation of our neighbours in the service of the geopolitical interests of the eu and big business.

in writing. this report on the european neighbourhood policy aims to increase the eu's competence in relations with the eu's neighbouring countries. it is part of the same logic of interference that characterizes the eu so much to avoid having to face its own foulness. the new policy thus encourages the partner countries to submit to the structural reforms dictated by brussels in the hope of future accession to satisfy, not the interests of the member states, but those of the us external federator. these objectives must also include a strengthening of europe's defence against a designated enemy in the east. this is a real dispossession of the sovereignty of the member states in foreign affairs, who are being asked to invest in the eu's neighbourhood policy 'by harmonising their efforts'. in short, an alignment with the american vision, that of neo-colonialism which imposes its values on its "partners" until it implements free movement of people and mobility within the neighbourhood. in the face of this sheer madness, i voted against.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text on the european neighbourhood policy (enp). the text says that the enp is now obsolete and must be adapted to the current security, economic and political challenges. the eu needs to formulate an ambitious political vision with clearly defined strategic objectives and priorities to support democracy, the rule of law, good governance, judicial reform and institution building in the eu's neighbourhood.
in writing. ‒ mr kukan's report is part of the broad consultation process led by the high representative to review the european neighbourhood policy (enp). while the enp was created to promote the emergence of a 'ring of friends' around the european union, we are now faced with a 'ring of fire'. this situation of instability at our borders has dramatic humanitarian, economic and social consequences and threatens our security. in this context, the text proposed by the committee on the environment, public health and consumer protection offers several lines of thought. first, the enp must be thought of in strategic terms. despite our status as a major trading partner and the accompanying measures we offer to our partners, the union's influence in the region is declining. we need a clear and coherent policy, designed for the long term and implemented with a strengthened political presence. secondly, the european union must not apply the same undifferentiated concept to all our partners: we must provide tailor-made assistance according to the aspirations of each country, and assess the progress made in concreto, by consulting civil society more widely.
in writing. ‒ the report advocates strengthening relations between the european union and neighbouring countries, with a view to future enlargements and to giving the eu greater powers in foreign policy. the eu not only seeks to dictate its sacrosanct values and economic principles, but also to impose them on as many countries as possible. the immigration part is particularly worrying: while the schengen area is already a source of trafficking of all kinds, the report would like to facilitate movement between the eu's neighbouring countries and the eu. when one considers that turkey is one of these countries and that it has a very porous border with war zones in syria, one can only wonder about the ideological blindness that presides over such recommendations that are clearly contrary to the fundamental interests of the citizens. i shall of course vote against this text.
in writing. ‒ the european commission is currently carrying out a review of the european neighbourhood policy in order to better adapt it to the challenges and needs of the countries concerned and to develop an effective policy. the european parliament wanted to contribute to this reflection by proposing a review of this policy. i voted in favour of this text and i stress the need to introduce a differentiated and tailor-made approach depending on the countries targeted. the countries covered by this policy have different histories and different levels of development. a differentiated european approach would make it possible to act effectively.
in writing. ‒ since the launch of the european neighbourhood policy (enp), the eu's neighbourhood has undergone significant changes and the commission recently launched a public consultation to carry out a thorough review of the enp and the principles on which it is based. i supported this report, which is one of parliament's contributions to the revision of the enp. the aim is to develop an ambitious and forward-looking neighbourhood policy; the enp must be more strategic, targeted, flexible and coherent. european support must be differentiated according to the recipient and better targeted. in terms of defending european values, it is fundamental that support for democracy, the rule of law, good governance, state building, human rights and fundamental freedoms is at the heart of the enp. at the same time, the union and the member states must continue to offer their assistance and know-how in the implementation of reforms. the new enp must also take account of the security dimension which has become more acute and has evolved significantly in the union's neighbourhood. finally, it is also a question of establishing strong partnerships with the union's 'neighbours of neighbours'.
in writing. ‒ the objective of this report is to increase the powers of the european neighbourhood policy with the aim of establishing a genuine 'union external policy'. it follows the same logic as the previous reports aimed at establishing a defence europe. the report also makes dangerous proposals on immigration, including the idea of strengthening legal immigration. in view of these attacks on the sovereignty of the states in matters of foreign policy, the logic of increasing the union's powers and the desire for interference expressed in this text must be opposed. i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ following the events of the arab spring, the renewal of the european commission and the ukrainian crisis, a review of the european neighbourhood policy was needed. the commission therefore launched a public consultation on this subject last march, to which this report intends to contribute. some of its recommendations are in the right direction: support the development of a thriving and active civil society in the union's partner countries; establish genuine freedom of movement for persons; go beyond the perennial free trade areas to meet the social aspirations of the people. however, beyond the good intentions, narrow and self-interested motivations quickly reappear in the form of the 'conditionality principle': if the countries of the european neighbourhood want to benefit from partnerships in any form, they must respect conditions, in particular economic and migration conditions. we all know what that means. the countries of the enp are thus first perceived in terms of their geopolitical interests, whether they are energy suppliers, outlets for european products or immigration gendarmes. for all these reasons, i have chosen to abstain.
in writing. ‒ i agree that copyright and intellectual property must evolve to take account of technological and digital progress. the report does not mention the issue of piracy or tax evasion by certain multinational firms such as google or amazon. the harmonization of copyright would be to the detriment of the protection of french authors, since french legislation is much more favourable. finally, this report goes against respect for the sovereignty of the member states. for these reasons i voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it was the result of collective work which resulted in a balanced text, very far from the original text which was only intended to reduce copyright to nothing without at the same time protecting users. this own-initiative report, which has no legislative consequences, does, however, provide a basis for the future challenges of the directive which will be presented by the commission in the autumn.
in writing. ‒ the report starts from a simple and undeniable observation that copyright and intellectual property law need to evolve to take account of the rise of the internet and new technologies, among other things. the report raises several issues, such as the reform of intellectual property rights, in particular the infosoc directive, or the concern about the exceptions linked to panoramas, but the main focus is on the introduction of concepts from anglo-saxon law, such as copyright, and on respect for the french and continental conception of copyright. we will need to find an environment that protects creators and small authors while allowing free expression on the internet within the framework of net neutrality. finally, the report does not mention the issue of piracy and tax provisions, in particular the evasion practiced by large multinationals such as google or amazon.
in writing. ‒ reform of intellectual property law has become a strategic and power issue. france is faced with the challenge of preserving its internal conception of copyright in the face of the intrusions of anglo-saxon concepts such as "copyright". the enl group, of which i am a member, tabled two amendments which call for: - particular attention to be paid to the question of the legal regime of a single european title; - to ensure that the minimum durations prescribed by international standards are not less than those laid down by french law. finally, the report does not deal with the issues of piracy and taxation, two strategic issues. for all these reasons, i voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ the digital age has created new challenges in respect of copyright. it is essential to adapt our legislation to technological progress. the digital revolution allows for continuous innovation that requires special attention. however, the digitisation of the european single market cannot be done at the expense of creators. we need to ensure that authors have the protection of their rights that is appropriate for the digital age. however, care must be taken that authors are not deprived of some of their rights on the pretext of a revision of the legislation. i will be vigilant when the revised directive on the harmonisation of certain copyright is published. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the vote on this report, which is so far removed from the original text, which was only intended to reduce copyright to nothing without at the same time defending users. i voted against paragraph 46, which was an amendment i had tabled in committee and which was voted on, but it was the most effective way of getting the panorama exception out of this report. i believe that the status quo which prevails today and which is acceptable to all member states, as commissioner oettinger has said, must remain the rule. each country is thus free to include this exception in its legislation or not, depending on its cultural peculiarities. that is also why i formally opposed amendment no 3, which was aimed solely at reinstating a mandatory exemption from the panorama right in the 28 member states. the report also includes the responsibility of web hosts, which i think is a good start to look with good intentions at the future proposal for a directive.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report aims to provide parliament's position on copyright reform in view of the forthcoming revision of directive 2001/29/ec on the harmonisation of certain aspects of copyright and related rights in the information society in the context of the digital internal market package. this report clearly positions the european parliament in favour of adapting copyright to the digital age, but is equally clearly opposed to calling it into question. i am pleased that this report maintains the necessary balance between fair remuneration for the work and talent of creators, respect for european cultural diversity, the fight against piracy and counterfeiting, on the one hand, and easy access for consumers to its services by introducing a liability regime for platforms, intermediaries and hosts, on the other. for these reasons i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report was adopted by a large majority in the european parliament. it is a consensus position, and therefore a stronger one, to defend copyright and related rights, before the commission puts its proposal for the digital single market on the table.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to vote against this report on the harmonisation of copyright. this is again a political will to move towards the unification of standards and union law. in many cases, however, and particularly in france, the european law advocated in this report is of a much lower quality than the existing national law. the report also has many shortcomings, failing to address crucial issues such as computer hacking or the tax provisions of such a harmonization of the law. this report is, in essence, contrary to the principle of the sovereignty of the member states, which is of course contrary to the values i defend on a daily basis as a member of the europe of nations and freedoms group.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by my colleague julia reda on copyright, which proposed improvements for the future copyright reform. this report is the result of a complete re-writing of the text, the original version of which was catastrophic for european culture, since the rapporteur was, whether intentionally or not, ignorant of the mechanisms governing cultural production. its proposals directly threatened artists, smes and the 7 million jobs that allow citizens to benefit from the diversity of european culture. the intensive work of negotiation has made it possible to extract all the harmful parts of the text and to make a balanced report, guaranteeing both the defence of the authors and a wide access to culture. this new version makes concrete proposals to adapt copyright to the challenges of the digital age, calls for greater accountability of technical intermediaries and recalls the importance of the cultural and creative sectors for the european economy, as well as the fundamental nature of the principle of territoriality of rights, at the heart of the financing of culture in europe. the text was adopted by a very large majority and will send a clear message to the european commission.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the harmonisation of certain aspects of copyright and related rights in the information society. this resolution is the result of difficult negotiations which fortunately prevented the adoption of a text which in its original version called for the demolition of the very principle of copyright. while it is necessary to adapt copyright legislation to the digital age, it is also necessary to continue to protect our european creators and their work so that they are fairly remunerated for their contributions. it is important to develop in europe an enabling environment for the cultural and creative sectors, which contribute to higher growth and employment.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on the harmonisation of certain aspects of copyright and related rights in the information society, because i am in favour of preserving the french and continental conception of copyright in the face of the intrusions of anglo-saxon concepts such as 'copyright' in the report. paragraph 28 of the report refers to a 'single european title' without defining or specifying the legal regime, which would be dangerous harmonization. paragraph 32 refers to the international standards laid down by the berne convention, which only sets minimum periods of less than those prescribed by french law. the system of exceptions and limitations to copyright specific to each member state should be protected. the authors must be guaranteed a fair remuneration and the moral right to the fruit of their creations. in the context of the information society, however, the legitimate rights of end users (consumers in particular) must be respected. in particular, a distinction must be made between commercial and non-commercial use.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the reda report because it promotes excessive and dangerous harmonisation of copyright. the final version voted by parliament is fortunately less catastrophic than the version originally proposed by the pirate member of parliament, mrs reda. thus, for example, the dangerous "freedom of panorama" which it enshrined, and which would have been contrary to french tradition, was abandoned.
in writing. ‒ i am voting against this report which does not protect the french concept of copyright against the intrusions of the anglo-saxon concept. the term used in this report is "copyright", which is the english term for copyright, different from the french definition. it is difficult to vote in favour of a text which uses an english-language semantic incompatible with a french-language semantic.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this resolution is to assess the implementation of the 2001 infosoc directive, which deals with 'the harmonisation of certain aspects of copyright and related rights'. the compromise resolution, drafted in a balanced way, defends copyright while allowing certain exceptions to promote the dissemination of information and artistic productions. the resolution proposes to 'strengthen the exemptions for public interest institutions such as libraries, museums and archives' and to allow 'an exception for research and education purposes, which would not only cover educational establishments but also approved teaching and research activities'. the text also denounces geographical restrictions that block access to content for consumers depending on the country. the resolution also condemns the extremely low remuneration granted to authors by content platforms. i am abstaining in order not to condemn a good intention, but also to not approve of so many inaccuracies.
in writing. ‒ the european union, through this report, is once again trying to harmonise at european level. it should be remembered that this european harmonization of intellectual property law is unnecessary. in addition, many points are not addressed, such as the question of piracy or the sensitive subject of tax provisions. in addition, certain provisions would reduce the sovereignty of states. i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text on the harmonisation of certain aspects of copyright and related rights. the epp group, of which i am a member, has been working to balance this text in order to reconcile the interests of creators and citizens-users. the aim is to strengthen and adapt copyright to the new challenges of the digital age, while ensuring that the greatest number of people have access to cultural content. i am committed to the principle of fair remuneration for the work and talent of authors and to the maintenance of sustainable funding mechanisms for cultural creation. these are essential to continue to support economic activity in the cultural sector, which accounts for 7.1 million jobs in europe.
in writing. ‒ the original aim of this text was to provide a country-by-country overview of the implementation of the 2001 copyright directive, particularly in the light of the new digital environment. through a long negotiation process, we have reaffirmed the principle of fair remuneration for the work and talent of creators, and the need to maintain permanent funding mechanisms for cultural creation. the challenge is also to continue to offer europe an environment favourable to economic activity, namely the cultural and creative sectors, which generate jobs (7.1 million jobs) that are not "delocalizable" and attractive to the younger generation. the european parliament sent a very clear message this morning to the european commission, which announced its intention to propose before the end of the year a revision of the 2001 copyright directive, as part of the completion of the european digital market: yes to adapting copyright to the digital age, no to challenging it.
in writing. ‒ this report is based on concepts from anglo-saxon law such as copyright and therefore threatens the french and continental conception of copyright. the problem of piracy and the question of tax provisions are not addressed or are too evasive. yet this is an area where unfair tax competition is rife within the european union itself, as mr juncker is well aware. the other elements of the text (rights related to copyright, the notion of originality still undefined and questions of ownership) leave the great gap between the copyright and copyright regimes. it is therefore a mediocre text, because it is incomplete and does not respect the legal tradition of copyright developed in many states of the european union. i therefore vote against.
in writing. ‒ if the original draft report were to be adopted today, it would make it very difficult to publish any calendar with photographs of modern architecture in my hometown of pilsen. i therefore voted in favour of the amendment, which i co-authored, and which sought to preserve the so-called freedom of panorama, that is to say, the freedom to photograph, for example, public buildings or works of art permanently displayed to the public. the bill didn't pass, but at least they managed, with my support, to remove the mention of restricting photography from the report, so that the freedom of the panorama was preserved, thanks to public pressure.
in writing. ‒ since 2001, a european directive has governed certain aspects of copyright and related rights. in autumn 2015, the european commission will propose a further reform of this directive. in this context, parliament adopted an own-initiative report outlining the state of play of the application of the 2001 directive and proposing possible developments. i voted in favour of this report, which has nevertheless been the subject of several criticisms with regard to freedom of panorama. i would like to reassure the public that the panorama exception has been respected in the report. freedom of panorama remains the responsibility of the member states.
in writing. ‒ meps adopted today the own-initiative report by julia reda on the harmonisation of certain aspects of copyright. i voted for this report which, thanks to the work and involvement of the socialists, proposes a whole series of balanced recommendations to the european commission in order to protect cultural diversity and the remuneration of authors, while guaranteeing the viability of this sector in an environment that is changing rapidly with the new information and communication technologies. in this report we call on the commission to maintain the principle of the exception to copyright, which exempts users in certain cases from requesting permission to reproduce protected works, without extending its application to the digital field and leaving a certain margin of manoeuvre to the member states in defining their exceptions to copyright. the text we voted also reaffirms the possibility of negotiating rights on a territorial basis and clearly rejects the principle of 'fair use' in the united states, which can limit and weaken the exclusive rights of the author.
in writing. ‒ digitisation and the popularisation of the exchange of content via virtual platforms have forced states to adapt their legislation by carrying out major copyright reforms. the commission had indicated its intention to harmonize these legislative frameworks at european level by means of a directive. this report, which was intended to anticipate such work, initially proved to be a very unbalanced text leading to the destruction of copyright, without protecting users. finally, after collective work and tough negotiations, we reached a compromise that deals in a reasoned way with the problems of geo-blocking (the practice of addressing content only to users in a given area), the single european title or private copies. i therefore welcome the adoption of this text which preserves the cultural wealth within the union while creating a draft common framework for copyright.
in writing. ‒ copyright cannot be considered a barrier, when it is copyright that allows artists to make a living from their art. however, ms reda's original project threatened artistic creation and diversity in europe by calling into question the european copyright framework, proposing the total harmonisation of exceptions or the reduction of the duration of rights. the european socialists and democrats have, however, managed to put aside these proposals that are dangerous for the sustainability and vitality of creativity in europe by finding a balance between the different stakeholders in order to strengthen a sustainable creative economy in europe. the compromise adopted excludes the introduction of fair use or a total harmonisation of the exceptions, as mrs reda wanted. by avoiding this bottom-up approach, the position of authors in the cultural landscape and the sustainability of european creation are strengthened. that is why i voted for this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which reaffirms the principle of fair remuneration for the work of creators and stresses the need to maintain sustainable funding mechanisms for cultural creation. the text also lays down concrete proposals to adapt copyright to the challenges of the digital age by strengthening it and ensuring a balance between respect for intellectual property and the access of the greatest number of people to cultural content. the challenge is important as it is a question of building an environment favourable to the cultural and creative sectors which creates jobs and remains attractive to the younger generation. with the adoption of this text, we have sent a clear message to the commission in the context of the forthcoming revision of the 2001 copyright directive.
in writing. ‒ the main focus is on the introduction of concepts from anglo-saxon law such as copyright, and the respect of the french and continental conception of copyright. attention is also paid to other elements of the text such as rights related to copyright, the concept of originality still undefined and questions of ownership, which leave the great gap between the copyright and copyright regimes. the question of piracy and taxation is not addressed in the report or is too evasive. however, google and its partners repatriate their profits made in france to parent companies with favourable tax treatment, within the union itself... this further harmonization of intellectual property law in europe is pointless. it is preferable to adapt the principles developed by french law. i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ the current copyright framework dates from 2001 and does not take account of developments, particularly in the digital domain. the revision is due to take place by the end of the year. this own-initiative report sought to assess the current framework and practices in order to make a number of recommendations for the review. the debate on this issue is always very sensitive, since it is not only about copyright itself, but also about the whole of cultural policy and the practices of europeans with interests that may seem contradictory. the debate took time, but the result presented was a fair balance between the rights and interests of creators and users. the european parliament calls for fair and appropriate remuneration to be guaranteed for all categories of rights holders, including (and especially) for the digital distribution of their works. it also proposes to relax the rules, particularly on geographical blocking, to allow greater access to culture and knowledge for all. so i chose to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ the european democracy fund aims to 'promote and support democracy, the rule of law and respect for the universality and indivisibility of human rights and fundamental freedoms'. it is a question of promoting interference in the internal affairs of third countries, in the name of democracy and at the expense of european taxpayers, through the union budget. the fund also promotes communitarianism, which i am opposed to. i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this debate as the committee had recommended in the background.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this text: in addition to the human rights interference that is the main cause of the communitarian demands, this report calls for the strengthening of the human and financial resources of a structure that is both expensive and useless, or even harmful, as it appears as a real propaganda instrument.
in writing. the text on the evaluation of the activities of the european fund for democracy (efd) aims at increasing the contribution of the member states to the fund and its actions. the emff aims to promote and support democracy, the rule of law, human rights, etc. all these are worthy goals that i can only support. however, it is clear that, as is so often the case with the european union, statements of principle and laudable intentions are very often transformed into very negative ideological consequences. france loses a lot of money every year as a net contributor to the budget of the european union. there is no question of accepting an extension which is only intended to stir up enmity with our neighbours, particularly with russia, by blaming them for all the ills. the rapporteur welcomes the support for ukraine, for example. for these reasons, i am opposed to this text.
in writing. ‒ the european endowment for democracy aims to promote and support democracy, the rule of law and respect for the universality and indivisibility of human rights. its operating budget is financed by the commission and its promotion activities by contributions from member states and third countries. the report calls for increased contributions from the member states and calls for greater efforts to combat, in particular, 'russian propaganda'. the rapporteur is already pleased that the emff has helped activists in ukraine. apart from the human rights interference for which it is responsible, this fund is a costly (€4.4 million) structure, useless and used only for political propaganda purposes.
in writing. ‒ promoting and supporting democracy, the rule of law and respect for human rights are among the main objectives of the union's foreign policy. in recent years, however, the countries in the union's neighbourhood have faced a number of political, economic and security problems that have put pressure on democratization efforts. this report highlights the importance of the european democracy fund, particularly in the light of the changing international context. it called on the member states and the commission to increase their contributions to the programme to continue the efforts already made. it calls for increased funding and human resources capacity for greater efficiency. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report proposes an evaluation of the activities of the european endowment for democracy since its creation. the fund shall in particular assist civil society actors by financing initiatives in favour of the establishment of a pluralist society, democracy, the promotion of the rule of law and fundamental freedoms. since 2012, the fund has supported 158 projects, with eur 4,5 million for the southern neighbourhood and eur 4,4 million for the eastern neighbourhood. the fund has therefore been involved in supporting the processes of democratisation and the establishment of stable and sustainable democratic systems in the countries in transition. i consider this report to be a balanced evaluation and i have voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to vote against this text on the evaluation of the activities of the european fund for democracy since its creation. the purpose of the fund is to promote and support democracy, the rule of law and respect for the universality and indivisibility of human rights and fundamental freedoms. the commission and the member states are the main donors to this fund with dubious aims, since the values it claims have too often been misused and used to justify various intervention operations, sometimes called 'humanitarian'. on the other hand, the report clearly defends communitarianism, which is so foreign and so contrary to the values of the french republic that we, the french members of the european parliament, are the only ones to defend it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, mr andrzej gryb, on the evaluation of the activities of the european fund for democracy. the european democracy fund is an independent fund that provides grants to support local actors in the neighbourhood of the union, always with the aim of promoting democracy, the rule of law and respect for fundamental principles. the report considers that the fund has fulfilled its main objectives. i welcome the fact that this report was adopted by a large majority.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the new approach of the union to human rights and democracy and on the evaluation of the activities of the european fund for democracy since its creation. the fund supports democracy, the rule of law, human rights and fundamental freedoms, the respect for which is one of the foundations of the european union's external policy. since its creation, the european democracy fund has, among other things, provided more than €10 million to help neighbouring countries. this action must not be discouraged in view of the particularly difficult international situation. democracy remains a value shared by the majority of the world's population and the european union must be an active defender of it.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the resolution on the evaluation of the activities of the european fund for democracy (efdem) simply because this structure is useless and expensive. as recital a of the resolution states, 'the promotion and support of democracy, the rule of law and respect for the universality and indivisibility of human rights and fundamental freedoms are among the main objectives of the union's foreign policy'. the european union already has sufficient means to support democracy, namely the foreign ministers of the member states and their respective diplomatic services, not to mention the high representative for foreign affairs and her european external action service, whose usefulness is highly questionable. it would therefore be better to abolish the edf.

in writing. ‒ since april, burundi has been plagued by an alarming situation. despite the constitutional provisions that prohibit a president from serving more than two terms, president nkurunziza has announced his candidacy for a third term. this announcement plunged the country into violence, resulting in a coup d'état and the death of seventy burundian citizens. the ruling power refuses to negotiate. we must act now. nearly 200,000 refugees have already fled the country. the resolution calls on the member states to respect the commitments made in the regional action plan for burundian refugees. it also calls for an end to violence and restrictions on access to information. i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ this resolution calls for an immediate end to the violence and political intimidation against the opposition in burundi. following the announcement in late april that president nkurunziza, who has been in power since 2005, would run for a third term, the country is experiencing a serious political and humanitarian crisis that has spread throughout the region. as such, the maintenance of the electoral calendar in a critical political and security context is a matter of concern and the european union should provide all necessary assistance with a view to ending the violence and organising free, peaceful, transparent and credible elections. i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to vote in favour of this resolution on the current situation in burundi. the resolution, surprisingly, contains no element that defends interference in the internal affairs of a sovereign state. the crisis that this country has been experiencing since president nkurunziza decided to run for a third term is a matter of internal politics, over which we have no right or power to regulate: the citizens of burundi must take their destiny into their own hands. parliament therefore called for a solution to the crisis to be found by burundian politicians in order to avoid an escalation of the situation in an already unstable region. parliament also called on the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that the european union's financial instruments are used effectively and to ensure that the budgetary and financial resources allocated to the community are used in a proper manner. failure to comply with these conditions would seriously damage burundi's image and make it appear as an unreliable partner.
