in writing. ‒ this legislative resolution authorises member states to ratify the protocol established by the international labour organisation (ilo) in 2014. this protocol relates to the c29 convention on forced labour, adopted in 1930 by the ilo and ratified by france in 1937. the c29 convention called on signatory countries to prohibit forced labour, with the understanding that this did not include certain forms of compulsory labour (those required of military personnel, civic duties, public service work following a conviction, etc.). it encouraged the acceding countries to take appropriate measures to ensure that workers receive a fair wage guaranteeing them free and dignified living conditions. the new protocol of 2014 notes that the convention is not respected by all signatory states. it therefore reminded them of their obligations in the fight against forced labour and called on them to cooperate in the judicial field in order to be more effective. in these times of economic crisis, it seems to me useful that france should be allowed to ratify this new protocol. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution.

in writing. ‒ the fight against forced labour dates back to an ilo convention of 1930. this convention (not ratified by the united states) calls for countries to eliminate forced or compulsory labor altogether. the 2014 protocol follows up on this convention and indicates that the fact that forced labour is still not eradicated everywhere must be addressed quickly. the council of the union authorized the member states this year to ratify the convention, since the union as an entity cannot do so. since some member states of the union, including france, have already signed the convention, it is only right that we continue along this path and fight against forced labour in the world. i therefore voted in favour of this recommendation.

in writing. ‒ the fight against forced labour is organised on the basis of a convention of the international labour organisation (ilo) of 1930 (which entered into force on 1 may 1932). the 1930 forced labour convention (no. 29), ratified by all the member states of the european union, calls on countries to eliminate forced or compulsory labour as soon as possible. it also sets out specific conditions for forced or compulsory labour for the transitional period before total abolition (hours, pay, care, etc.). a review was planned for 5 years after the entry into force of the convention to take stock, in 1937. it should be noted that this convention has not been ratified by the united states. the protocol is therefore a logical follow-up to the 1930 convention on forced labour, which france had already ratified. so it is only right that we continue along this path. furthermore, there is a legitimate fight against forced labour in the world. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ forced labour is an intolerable form of exploitation of human beings which nevertheless remains a reality. almost 21 million people are currently victims of forced labour worldwide, including 1.6 million in europe. the first victims are most often the most vulnerable populations, especially irregular migrants, who often have difficulty in asserting their rights and demands. as a result, they are often subject to blackmail by their employers. this lack of respect for human rights and fundamental rights on european soil is intolerable and that is why it was necessary to finally update the convention against forced labour, which dates back to 1930. it is essential to strengthen labour law and not to let it weaken as recent european policies have tended to do. i therefore voted in favour of this report by my colleague patrick le hyaric, which proposes new binding instruments to oblige the states to implement plans to combat these illegal forms of forced labour.

in writing. ‒ under a european regulation of 2009, trade in seal products was prohibited throughout the community. the union had, however, maintained two exceptions to this ban: one for inuit communities, for whom trade in skins or other derived products is necessary for their subsistence, and a second allowing small-scale marketing of seal products in the context of marine resource management. however, these two exceptions were not acceptable under wto law, whose dispute settlement body issued its findings in june 2014, invalidating both exceptions. european legislation had therefore to be adapted accordingly. by amending the exemption granted to the inuit community to take better account of animal welfare considerations and by removing the other exemption, the union is bringing itself into line with international trade law. however, special provisions for inuit and indigenous communities will be maintained to preserve their traditional ways of life. however, it is regrettable that the commission did not carry out an impact assessment of this regulation, which would have allowed a better understanding of the effects of the abolition of these two exceptions.

in writing. ‒ in 2009, the european parliament and the council adopted regulation (ec) no 1007/2009 banning trade in seal products within the european union. however, two exceptions remain: products from inuit hunting (ci derogation) and products from hunting for the sole purpose of sustainable, small-scale and non-profit-making management of marine resources (grm derogation). norway and canada, both exporters of seal products, have challenged this decision in the world trade organization (wto). the wto dispute settlement body (dsb) ruled to uphold the general ban on seal products but rejected the two exceptions on the grounds of an obstacle to free competition. in order to comply with the dsb decision, the proposed text deletes the derogation grm and specifies the conditions for the application of the derogation ci . i am against the use of private justice to arbitrate between the general human interest of protecting biodiversity and the interests of the seal traders. however, the text proposed to us maintains the measures for the conservation of seals while allowing the inuit to hunt them, i vote in favour.

in writing. ‒ regulation (ec) no 1007/2009 prohibits trade in seal products derived from and imported from the european union. it provides for two exemptions: the indigenous community exemption, which allows such trade if it is carried out by the inuit or any other 'indigenous community'; the derogation for the management of marine resources, which allows products from hunting for the sole purpose of sustainable management of marine resources. following the complaint lodged by norway and canada with the wto, the latter suspended the second exception, forcing the european union to revise its regulation. it is therefore proposed that only the exception for indigenous communities should be retained, which is a pity, but is still preferable to no derogation at all. the vote will therefore be in favour.
in writing. this report on trade in seal products relates to regulation 1007/2009 which prohibits trade in seal products within the eu and includes 2 derogations. however, following a conflict, the wto banned seal hunting and rejected the two exceptions. the purpose of this report is therefore to redefine the scope of the first exception. the report advocates the exemption for the inuit, who could then sell the seal products that are killed for subsistence purposes rather than throwing them into the sea. the second derogation, however, is for small-scale hunting. i voted for this text because i defend local traditions and the sovereignty of the people, but as a member of the intergroup on animal protection, i will remain vigilant on this report and this subject since i consider that encouraging the marketing of these seal products in the eu (while it has been banned since 2009) will encourage seal hunting.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report on the proposal to amend the european union regulation on trade in seal products. since 2009, this trade has been prohibited in the european union, with the exception of products from hunts conducted by inuit or other indigenous communities ('ci derogation') and products from hunts conducted for the sole purpose of sustainable, small-scale and non-profit-making management of marine resources ('grm derogation'). the report proposes that the commission may adopt measures to limit these exceptions if it is established that seal hunting is carried out for primarily commercial purposes, rather than for subsistence purposes. the aim is to bring the union into line with the recommendations and decisions of the world trade organisation in this area.
in writing. ‒ regulation 1007/2009 prohibits trade in seal products within the european union and includes two derogations. following a challenge, the wto banned seal hunting and rejected the two exceptions and this report must redefine the framework for the first exception. the inuit could thus commercialize seal products if the animals were killed for the sole purpose of subsistence rather than being thrown into the sea. the second derogation, for small-scale hunting, is, on the contrary, denounced in this report. i support sovereignty and the defence of local traditions and for these reasons i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ we have adopted legislation amending the european regulation banning trade in seal products within the union, for products manufactured in the union but also imported. the new proposal is in line with the wto conclusions and recommendations and sets out very carefully the conditions under which seal products obtained from hunting are allowed to be placed on the market. i am glad that i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ regulation 1007/2009 was adopted, which prohibits trade in seal products within the european union. this regulation has two exceptions:- the ic (indigenous communities) exemption allowing trade in seal products if they have been hunted by the inuit or any other "indigenous community". - the grm (marine resources management) derogation authorising products from hunting for the sole purpose of sustainable management of marine resources. the wto ruled in favour of a total ban on seal hunting and rejected the two exceptions as unjustified in view of the moral concerns about animal welfare and the difficulty of distinguishing between individuals killed for the subsistence of 'indigenous communities' and those killed for commercial reasons. this report seeks only to redefine the framework of the first ci exception in order to comply with the wto conclusions and recommendations. the 'indigenous communities' must be allowed to continue to live according to their traditions and customs. this is especially true since hunting is the main source of livelihood for these communities. it is regrettable that the wto has prohibited the indigenous populations from sustainably regulating the overpopulation of seals. i therefore voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ since 2009, trade in seal products has been banned in the european union due to the threat to the species and hunting in particular. some states, notably canada and norway, have requested exemptions from international law from the wto to allow certain communities, such as the inuit, to continue to hunt but also to maintain fish stocks that would be threatened by the increase in the number of seals. while inuit and other indigenous communities must be allowed to continue to hunt and sell seal products, the threat that seals could pose to fish stocks is not scientifically proven, which is why the european parliament has abolished this exception. the european parliament has been careful to accept only part of the wto's now accepted derogations, as part of the adaptation of european law, allowing inuit and indigenous communities to sell seal products, provided that the hunting methods take into account the welfare of the animal and are part of the traditions of the community and contribute to its subsistence. i think that is a balanced position, and i have therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the european commission recently proposed a directive temporarily banning the placing on the market of cloned animals and products derived from them. the text was substantially amended by the agri-envi joint committee to broaden its scope and to make consumers more confident. it's a positive one. it transforms the directive into a regulation, bans the import of products derived from clones and their descendants, requires a certificate from exporters to ensure that their food products comply with eu rules and sets up a traceability system. it also limits the scope of ttip by de facto blocking imports from the united states where cloning technology is allowed. however, it has a major weakness: to date, there is no technical means of checking whether a product is derived from a clone or not. to overcome this, our group proposed an amendment in plenary to ban all imports of products potentially affected by this opacity, because they come from herds raised in countries where cloning is carried out without any special traceability. the amendment did not obtain the required majority as we hoped, so i abstained on the whole text.
in writing. ‒ since the amendments tabled by our group were rejected, we consider that this text is insufficient and could not be supported as it stands. however, it may still be useful in restricting trade in cloned animals, provided that exporters have a reliable traceability system in place. that's why i finally decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this report on the cloning of animals reared and bred for agricultural purposes is to prohibit the placing on the market of products derived from the breeding of certain animals. this text is a step in the right direction and is a brake on imports from the united states. however, there is no technical means to date to verify whether a product is derived from a clone. our enf members have amended the text to ensure the safety of european citizens and, as we cannot technically verify, it is preferable to suspend imports of products from countries which allow trade in cloned products. i voted against this text because, although it does impose some restrictions on imports, there is still no real traceability of cloned products (certificates are only guaranteed on the good faith of breeders and there is no proof that products are not the descendants of cloned animals). our amendment no 56 was not adopted on this point either.

in writing. ‒ cloning is a form of asexual reproduction, performed in a laboratory, in which animals are generated using genetic material from a cell of another animal. in 2008, the european parliament voted against cloning animals for agricultural purposes. however, it is authorised in certain third countries, including the united states, canada, argentina, brazil and australia. in 2013, the commission therefore strengthened the eu position by proposing a suspension of the use of the cloning technique for farmed animals, the placing on the market of cloned animals or live cloned embryos and the marketing of food products derived from cloned animals within the union. the report before us sets out and strengthens the commission's proposal. it also proposes to ban the import and placing on the market of the offspring of cloned animals. i am voting for this text which protects consumers and farmers alike.

in writing. ‒ animal cloning is a technique that involves reproducing animals from stem cells. in addition to the many ethical constraints, these practices have raised scientific questions. it has been shown that animal cloning results in a loss of welfare for cloned animals and that their mortality rate after birth is considerably higher than for naturally born animals. i therefore voted in favour of this text, which aims to ban the consumption of cloned animals and their offspring in the european union, a ban which includes production, breeding and importation. the text also aims to increase the traceability of meat, embryos and seeds within the european union, which would help to avoid new food scandals.

in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report proposes the development of an internal strategy on fundamental rights based on article 2 of the treaty on european union. the report covers a range of violations that have occurred in europe in the areas of freedom of expression, data protection, the impact of the economic crisis, corruption and the situation in prisons. it also deals with subjects of european competence such as the fight against discrimination and the protection of the rights of migrants and refugees. the rapporteur also proposes the introduction of a rather unrealistic deterrent instrument to prevent violations of fundamental rights in the states, a 'european semester on fundamental rights', which is intended to replace de facto the intervention of the european commission with the traditional action of the court of justice in this field. the epp group considered this proposal, among others, to be more ideological than realistic, and tabled an alternative resolution reaffirming its members' commitment to fundamental rights in europe and addressing the same issues in a more balanced approach. since this alternative resolution was rejected, as were some of our amendments to the main resolution in plenary, i decided to abstain.
in writing. it is regrettable that the left is once again using the pretext of fundamental rights to get the european parliament to adopt many unrealistic provisions which are outside its competence. our party is firmly committed to the protection of fundamental rights in the european union, which are too often undermined. we therefore voted in favour of a resolution which deals with this situation with pragmatism and realism. i was not able to support the resolution adopted by the left. it not only puts the strengthening of security in opposition to the protection of fundamental rights, which are two complementary principles and indispensable to the protection of european citizens; but it also violates the principle of subsidiarity in europe, particularly as regards the family. that's why i abstained.
in writing. ‒ the economic crisis, the effects of which are still very much felt throughout europe, has increased the precariousness and vulnerability of many european citizens, who are no longer able to fully enjoy their civil, economic, cultural and social rights. there is also the unprecedented migration crisis facing europe with the arrival of many refugees, which requires us to rethink our migration policy in a spirit of solidarity. refugees must be welcomed in decent conditions in all member states and the european coastguards must be strengthened. in the long term, a common, effective and realistic european migration and asylum policy will be needed the protection of fundamental rights is a dual responsibility of the member states and the institutions of the union, but the situation can best be assessed at community level. the establishment of a scoreboard under the control of the commission with common and objective criteria across the union would thus make it possible to better assess the situation at eu level.

in writing. ‒ the purpose of this report is to draw conclusions from the hearings of the 'commissioner-candidates' in the context of the appointment of the juncker commission. following the european elections, newly elected meps receive the commissioners-designate in the european parliament and ask them about the political objectives and principles that will guide their actions over the next five years. this report therefore looks at some issues which could lead to changes in the current procedure. the possibilities for the rapporteur include the possibility for states to put forward at least two candidates: one male and one female; a review of the hearings of vice-presidents with horizontal responsibilities; or the opportunity to ask horizontal questions concerning the composition, structure and working methods of the commission, which cannot be addressed by a single commissioner. the proposed amendments are designed to strengthen the democratic control of the european parliament over the appointment of the college of commissioners, so i voted in favour of the text.

in writing. ‒ respect for human rights is a fundamental value of the european union. the european charter of human rights is a binding part of the european legal system. it is true that certain technological advances, particularly in the area of surveillance, used by the wrong people, can have the effect of violating a person's fundamental rights. in such cases, action must be taken to ensure respect for freedom of expression and privacy. however, these technologies also have the potential to protect citizens and the environment. there must be a balance between respect for human rights and the safety of citizens everywhere. i voted against this report. this extremist text, which is supported by the most ideological factions on the left, condemns the use of new technologies in the field of security. we must not deprive ourselves of these effective instruments, which must nevertheless be carefully controlled.

in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report focuses on the growing impact of detection and surveillance systems on human rights in third countries, which according to the rapporteur undermines existing trust in information and communication technologies. the report calls for the eu to include clauses in its agreements with third countries referring to the promotion and guarantee of digital freedoms, net neutrality and uncensored and unrestricted access to the internet. the report also stresses the importance of whistleblowers and their supporters and proposes that they be considered as human rights defenders and that the union protect them against international prosecution and extradition proceedings. this controversial report is marked by a strong ideological logic in that it puts net neutrality before national security. i think that a realistic approach should be adopted to strike a balance between security, in the context of the fight against terrorism, and individual freedom, which is clearly not allowed in this report, and i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ the use of communication and information technologies has fostered strong human rights mobilisations. the use of social media by young syrians, egyptians and tunisians to call for more democracy during the "arab spring" is a striking example. unfortunately, these technologies are used by oppressive regimes to conduct mass surveillance of populations, or to monitor the activities of some of their citizens via their mobile phones or other electronic devices. it is therefore necessary to regulate its use and provides the eu with a regulatory framework. this includes combating the export of surveillance technology by european companies to authoritarian countries and the mass surveillance by certain european intelligence services. parliament also deplored the fact that security measures were increasingly used as a pretext for infringing the right to privacy and reiterated its strong conviction that national security could not justify untargeted, secret or mass surveillance programmes.
in writing. ‒ mass surveillance established under the pretext of the fight against terrorism is a power-driven policy that i cannot accept. however, the report by mr schaake is wrong in proposing, for example, encryption of communications with individuals who are presented as human rights defenders. this is a difficult concept to define at a time when certain governments and the media are distorting geopolitical and political reality to serve certain interests. the text also seeks to strengthen the primacy of eu law, in particular the interpretation of human rights by the european institutions. in view of the lack of ambition and the errors in this text, i voted against it.

in writing. ‒ ms schaake's report on human rights and technology attempts to solve the problem of squaring the circle, or rather the problem of squaring the net: to keep the internet as a neutral space of freedom and information, to guarantee the protection of the personal data of its users, including by encryption, and at the same time not to prevent the legitimate fight against cybercrime or terrorist activities, not to contribute, through the export of certain technologies, to the strengthening of undemocratic regimes and their control of populations. good intentions, that's what i'm saying. the problem is that the lines of thinking proposed are very intrusive and centralising, giving the commission far too much power in these areas. the rapporteur is also only touching on the problems of mass surveillance of europeans by the services of the very democratic united states. the report also proposes sanctions against companies that export to dictatorships, but only technologies that can strengthen them, while with the blessing of the commission, which negotiates free trade agreements with anyone, one could safely and with a beautiful hypocrisy export everything else. because he asks the right questions but gives the wrong answers, i abstained on this text.
in writing. ‒ this report is federalist because it gives european standards primacy over national standards. in this case, the report is intended to regulate the conduct of the member states in all matters relating to freedom of information and the use of cryptographic systems or services. this is an area of direct concern to the strategic interests of states; the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to finance the necessary measures. the european union has no legitimacy to intervene in national legislation and practice, so i voted against this report.

in writing. new information and communication technologies have made it possible to increase the exchange of information in the world considerably and to develop distance trade. as this report underlines, it is important to ensure the security of the means of communication for the benefit of their users. however, it is important to bear in mind that the internet is now regularly used for criminal purposes, including by terrorists. internet regulation must therefore both promote digital freedoms and ensure citizens' security. certain provisions of the text, aimed at prohibiting restricting the use of encryption within the eu or requiring the systematic implementation of end-to-end encryption standards for all communications services in order to make their content more difficult to access for public authorities, intelligence services and surveillance bodies clearly did not go in this direction and would have made it more difficult for our intelligence services to act. that is why i voted against this text.

in writing. ‒ this report deals with the impact of surveillance technologies on human rights in third countries. the report deplores the fact that the right to privacy is being violated in the name of security and the fight against terrorism, calls for an end to mass surveillance and denounces the use of technologies specifically designed to violate certain rights by governments with impunity. parliament therefore called on the commission to submit proposals to determine how european standards can be used to prevent the harmful effects of the export of these technologies to third countries where the rule of law is not applied. some legislative options are being put forward, such as the inclusion of a clause on digital freedom in agreements with third countries or the extension of international protection to whistleblowers. the report has the merit of opening the debate on the need for new european legislation in this area, going so far as to propose increased penalties for companies that sell these products knowing that they are harmful. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which unfortunately is not a legislative report, but which gives priority to the rights of citizens over those of companies.

in writing. ‒ family businesses now represent more than 60% of all businesses and account for 50% of private sector employment in the union. however, these companies often face many obstacles when it comes to changing direction and finding a buyer. the various national laws (taxes, inheritance duties) represent a serious obstacle to the growth of these businesses. the european parliament adopted an own-initiative report calling on the european commission to adopt an integrated policy for family businesses in the union. i voted in favour of this text and i support the importance of such an approach. family businesses are an important part of the local and regional economy and jobs, and it is our duty to promote their interests.
in writing. ‒ family businesses now account for 60% of european businesses and no less than 50% of jobs. the vast majority of these are small and medium-sized enterprises, which account for two thirds of private sector employees. these structures, which are the cornerstones of the economic fabric, have suffered in recent years from the effects of the world economic crisis but also from the fiscal inconsistencies introduced by some member states. that is why i voted in favour of the report 'family businesses in europe' which aims to provide a favourable institutional, legal and fiscal framework for such businesses. the text, which is supported by the european parliament, aims to simplify administrative procedures and to provide theoretical knowledge to business leaders, in order to promote the internationalisation of their activities, which is a real source of growth and job creation. the inheritance rights of these companies must also be simplified and adapted in order to avoid liquidity problems when the assets are transferred.
in writing. ‒ family businesses in europe represent more than 60% of enterprises and almost 50% of private sector jobs. despite a long-term view of growth prospects, these companies often face difficulties in accessing finance or in passing on the business to subsequent generations. i voted in favour of this report which asks the european commission to examine ways of collecting comparable data, to address specific difficulties and to introduce the test for family businesses in the impact assessment. finally, it is important that member states put in place appropriate conditions for the succession of family businesses.
in writing. ‒ the report is favourable to family businesses, their long-term development and, above all, their transmission. the report also recalls that 'legislation on direct taxation and inheritance is a matter for the member states'. i therefore vote in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament adopted today a report on the role of family businesses in the european union. these companies account for 85% of european enterprises and 60% of private sector employment in europe. they therefore have a key role to play, in particular in addressing the effects of the financial and economic crisis and in revitalising the economy. the vast majority of these enterprises are small and mediumsized enterprises, which are suffering more than ever from international competition and the lack of financing available to them. so now more than ever is the time to support them. despite their importance, the characteristics and needs of these enterprises are still poorly understood at european level, given the different realities. since 2009, a rather vague definition has been in place, which has the effect that member states continue to apply rules on aid to these companies, which vary considerably from one member state to another. this report outlines a number of recommendations for the harmonization of these practices. i vote for it.

in writing. ‒ the main positive aspect of this report on the job and growth potential of research and innovation in the blue economy is that it is comprehensive and covers a wide range of issues (fisheries, transport, energy, shipbuilding, etc.). it takes into account all aspects of each issue such as the added value of public action, the management of fish stocks, the preservation of the marine ecosystem, the need for support for the shipbuilding sector. finally, the report stresses the central role of the states in the development of the blue economy (point 9), with the commission intervening only to promote their cooperation. the report, however, points to an ideological bias which leads the author to overlook certain contributions of the private sector to the economy. similarly, there is a need to protect data which is essential for the defence of the fundamental economic interests of states, so the emphasis is on free access to all data and knowledge. finally, the report ignores the long-term and sustainable development of the tourism industry. although this report has some shortcomings, it also presents some interesting points, and i have therefore decided to abstain on this vote.
in writing. ‒ the blue economy represents a significant potential for growth, jobs and investment for eu member states with disappointing macroeconomic performance. the report highlights the issues and issues to be addressed: fisheries, shipbuilding, mineral extraction and maritime transport. the report gives the state a key role in the development of these activities and the union a coordinating role. the text stresses the importance of taking advantage of these sectors while ensuring the preservation of the environment. however, it is regrettable that the text does not include the role that private investors have to play in financing these projects, particularly with a view to a better allocation of resources. the rapporteur also deals with this problem without addressing the question of the union for the mediterranean, which is a crucial issue for the future of the continent. i therefore decided not to vote on this text.

in writing. ‒ france has a rich national heritage which must be preserved at all costs. the resolution, which was put to the vote by parliament, aims to strengthen the preservation of europe's cultural heritage, whether tangible (movable, immovable and underwater) or intangible (oral traditions, performing arts, rituals, etc.). while it speaks of an integrated european approach, it stresses that cultural heritage is naturally heterogeneous, reflecting the diversity and cultural and linguistic pluralism of the member states. the resolution examines the issues of funding, legal bases and digitisation of heritage, highlighting its importance and links with regional development, social cohesion, agriculture, the environment, education, tourism and the labour market. this proposal is a positive one for french cultural heritage, and i therefore voted in favour of this motion for a resolution. i will be careful, however, not to make it a mere pretext for further integration, without any real benefit for the enhancement of our identity.

in writing. ‒ what is a european citizens' initiative (eci)? it is a so-called participatory democracy mechanism, which allows at least one million citizens, from at least seven member states, to ask the commission to act in a specific area, in accordance of course with the treaties. the first eci launched, called one of us , was aimed at preventing eu funding of activities involving the destruction of a human embryo. although it met all the criteria, it was shockingly not followed. not politically correct enough, i guess. the water initiative received a response, but it was not satisfactory: a communication from the commission. in other words, a kind of gentle pat on the head to congratulate the kind petitioners and the assurance that the commission does not really want to commit itself to the crucial points requested by citizens: the exclusion of the water and sanitation sectors from the rules of the internal market (competition, subsidies) and international trade agreements. i agree with the report when it condemns the commission's disregard for this procedure, and therefore for the citizens, and when it points out the need to respect the principle of subsidiarity or makes proposals of common sense. in some respects, however, he goes too far. that's why i abstained.
in writing. ‒ on tuesday 8 september, i abstained on the report on the european citizens' initiative (eci) on the human right to water and sanitation. this is the first ever validated eci, a tool that has been set up to help european citizens take part in the european debate. the text calls on the european commission to propose legislation that makes the right to water a human right and promotes water supply and sanitation as essential public services for all, i.e. that they are not subject to internal market rules and that water services are excluded from liberalisation. the report is undoubtedly a step forward in this respect, but it is also a demagogic report. the text crystallizes an ideological vision, restricting the freedom of choice of public authorities in terms of management by promoting exclusively public-public partnerships. i also regret the total and definitive exclusion of water services from the rules of the internal market, which i consider contradictory and even absurd, because it opens the door to conflicts of interest and favouritism to the detriment of users.

in writing. ‒ the text put to the vote by parliament is intended to give a positive recommendation for the fisheries partnership agreement with guinea-bissau. until june 2012, fishermen from member states enjoyed access to the territorial waters of that country under an agreement concluded in 1980. since its ratification, the agreement has been renewed several times by means of various protocols. the agreement negotiated by the commission on behalf of the member states is part of the continuity of this partnership. the agreement will have positive effects on the development of guinea-bissau's economy and on french fishermen, who will have the right to exploit the country's marine resources within the limits of 12 tuna seiners and surface longliners and 3 tuna vessels. the agreement is concluded for three years. the agreement is beneficial to both sides, and i have therefore voted in favour of this proposal for a recommendation.
in writing. ‒ the coup d'état in guinea-bissau in 2012 led to the suspension of negotiations on this fisheries agreement. since elections were held in may 2014, the resumption of negotiations has allowed a new protocol to the agreement to be initialled in november 2014. the new protocol provides for fishing opportunities for 28 tuna seiners and longliners and 12 purse seiners. the financial contribution will enable access to water and the sustainable development of small-scale fisheries in guinea-bissau. parliament wishes to receive the minutes of the meetings of the joint committees which enable the management of the use of the financial contribution for the development of the fisheries sector.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this agreement is to allow european union fishing vessels, including 12 tuna seiners and surface longliners plus three tuna seiners for france, access to the territorial waters of guinea-bissau. this is a win-win partnership, especially since guinea-bissau does not have the means to fight illegal fishing. i therefore voted in favour of this agreement.
in writing. ‒ this report recommends the adoption by the council of the protocol between the eu and the republic of guinea-bissau. this protocol sets out the fishing opportunities available to european vessels and defines the financial compensation granted to the republic of guinea-bissau. the partnership gives european fishermen access to part of the untapped fish stocks in the republic of guinea-bissau, while strengthening cooperation between the two parties in the framework of a development partnership for a sustainable fisheries policy. the financial contribution provided for in the agreement is eur 9.2 million per year, including eur 6.2 million for access to fisheries resources and eur 3 million for supporting the development of the fisheries sector in that country. i voted in favour of this win-win partnership, which benefits both the european fisheries sector and the development of a third country.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text to support research and the economy in countries such as the republic of guinea-bissau. however, we must insist on more reliable information on local fisheries resources.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report because it is beneficial for both parties.
in writing. ‒ this fisheries partnership agreement with guinea-bissau on fishing opportunities and financial compensation is designed to allow eu fishing vessels access to guinea-bissau's waters. in particular, 28 tuna seiners/palangriers, 12 tuna-fishing vessels and several shrimp trawlers and freezer vessels are involved. so for france 15 ships and for a period of 3 years. in return, a fee is paid and shipowners must take on board seamen from guinea-bissau. overall, this is a good deal for europeans and for the citizens of guinea-bissau who are failing to fight illegal fishing. so i voted for it.

in writing. ‒ this recommendation concerns the fisheries partnership agreement with cape verde: fishing opportunities and financial compensation. it is intended to allow access to cape verdean waters for a period of four years for union fishing vessels in return for aid to combat illegal fishing and support for the development of local fishing communities. this agreement should be made in accordance with the best available scientific advice and the recommendations of the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (icsat) and, where relevant, within the limits of the available surplus. cape verde faces three problems: illegal fishing, under-utilisation by some member states of the fishing opportunities set by the agreement (hence redistribution), and concerns about shark catches. as such, the parties agreed to establish a rigorous monitoring mechanism to ensure sustainable exploitation of the resources. this agreement is balanced and i have therefore decided to vote in favour.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the svoboda report on the parliament's approval of a council decision authorising austria, belgium and poland to ratify the budapest convention on the contract for the carriage of goods by inland waterways ('cmni'). this decision will make it possible to regulate certain situations from a legal point of view and to harmonize contracts and standards for inland navigation in europe, to the benefit of both citizens and businesses, which is why i welcome the positive vote of the european parliament.

in writing. ‒ the budapest convention (2005) creates a legal regime applicable to the international carriage of goods by inland waterway. eleven member states of the union have already acceded to this convention, while fifteen member states of the union have indicated that they do not have inland waterways covered by the convention. austria, poland and belgium subsequently expressed their wish to become contracting parties to the convention. their participation will facilitate the wider implementation of this legal instrument, allowing the development of eu inland waterway transport for the benefit of citizens and the environment. the report before us authorizes belgium, poland and austria to join. i vote for it.

in writing. ‒ the budapest convention on the contract for the carriage of goods by inland waterways was adopted by a diplomatic conference jointly organised by the central commission for the navigation of the rhine and the danube commission in collaboration with the united nations economic commission for europe and entered into force on 1 april 2005. it aims to harmonise contracts and standards for inland navigation in europe. the member states cannot ratify or accede to it without the union's authorisation (article 2 (1) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union). austria and poland have expressed their wish to become contracting parties. belgium ratified the convention on 5 august 2008, following the entry into force of the rome i regulation on 24 july 2008. belgium should therefore also be the recipient of the union enabling act, retroactively, in order to remedy the irregularity of the current situation. since each country is free to accede to this convention if it so wishes and since i do not see any disadvantage for france, i shall vote in favour of this text.

in writing. ‒ wars on europe's borders and the rise of daesh have led to a massive influx of migrants into europe. most of them arrive in greece and italy, which, under the dublin regulation, are obliged to take care of these asylum applications. these two countries are not in a position to cope with this situation on their own. we must show solidarity and accept that a certain number of migrants are relocated to our countries through a binding quota mechanism. in july the council decided to reject this mechanism, relocating only 32 000 refugees against the 40 000 envisaged in the commission's proposal. the report also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the rights of refugees are respected and that the eu's efforts to combat terrorism are not undermined. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of ska keller's report on the migration situation in europe. the introduction of a new distribution key, which is fair for all member states and fair for refugees, seems to me to be quite appropriate and encouraging for european solidarity. a new emergency relocation mechanism that takes into account both the interests of refugees and the reception capacities of the member states needs to be thoroughly considered. in this context, it is essential to distinguish between asylum seekers and economic migrants. all member states must respect and implement the rules of the common european asylum system. asylum is a right and should remain a right for all those persecuted because of their political opinions, their origin or their religion. in the face of economic immigration, however, it is necessary to be realistic and to analyse a priori the needs of our labour market, since this type of immigration is in any case a matter for the sovereignty of the state.

in writing. i welcomed the emergency distribution mechanism proposed by the commission when it was presented in may last year. i therefore did not hesitate to support mr keller's report. the report broadly supports the commission's proposal, but adds some very necessary nuances. in addition to its mandatory nature, this mechanism must be able to adapt to developments in both refugee flows and migration routes. for this system to be effective, the preferences of member states and those of applicants should also be aligned as far as possible. this would not only avoid secondary movements of applicants between states, but also promote the integration of relocated persons in their host countries. finally, to deal with the urgency of the situation, parliament has agreed to be consulted only this time or in the next emergency mechanism proposed by the commission on 9 september, but it is crucial that the codecision procedure is applied when it comes to deciding on a permanent allocation mechanism.

in writing. ‒ in the face of the refugee crisis, which is still testing our concept of solidarity, the european parliament had to formally validate the proposal put forward by the european commission last may to relocate urgently, and in accordance with a fair distribution key, 40 000 asylum seekers located in greece and italy. the keller report, which is now before the house, is ambitious enough to deal with the situation in a rational and supportive way. it not only encourages the solidarity mechanism for the distribution of asylum seekers (so that countries on europe's external borders are not subject to disproportionate pressure), but also urges states to respect the preferences expressed by migrants, especially those concerned with family reunification. more importantly, it encourages desperately lax governments to commit to the long term. criticising the dublin agreements, the text stresses the need to implement a genuine comprehensive strategy for asylum management, which i hope will take the form of a european asylum system based on solidarity and efficiency. because it is the only coherent response to the migratory flows to which europe is exposed, i voted in favour of this text.

in writing. ‒ in 2014, 72% of the european population lived in urban areas and this figure is estimated to rise to 78% by 2030. urban areas are increasingly strategic economically and socially. with this in mind, the european parliament adopted a report setting out the guidelines for a future european urban policy. i voted in favour of this text, which stresses the need for a coherent and coordinated urban policy within the union.
in writing. ‒ as the rapporteur points out, urban policy is not in any way a matter for the eu. the project lays the foundations for a european urban policy, including the establishment of a timetable. the european institutions are therefore, as usual, keen to give themselves new powers, which would further limit the scope for action by the member states. if this competence is transferred to the european union, the european budget will have to be increased by increasing the already high contribution of the member states. contrary to what they claim in this text, there will be no synergy with the existing programmes. this will only add to the burden of the existing brussels bureaucracy. i therefore vote against the adoption of this text.

in writing. this investment for jobs and growth report aims to promote economic, social and territorial cohesion in the european union. these cohesion policies aim to reduce regional disparities and competitiveness gaps in the union. however, it is already forgotten that these disparities are largely fuelled by the existence of a single currency, which leads to a divergence in productive capacities. in reality, under the guise of 'cohesion', this text is intended to increase the union's constraints on the eligibility of investments and to give greater prerogatives to the large regional authorities to the detriment of the nation states. the union is still trying to divest the states of their sovereignty a little more... the commission thus wants to increase the mobilisation of european funds to reduce regional disparities, even though its policies are responsible for the differences in competitiveness. i also object to the use of funds to promote roma integration. that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ regional disparities and competitiveness gaps are not the main cause of the difficulties faced by the developed european countries. they existed long before the creation of the european union and have never created an obstacle to the development of trade between states. it was the imposition of a single currency, despite these differences between states, that created a decisive advantage for the best performing country at the expense of the others, thus accentuating disparities. one of the objectives of the single currency was to force member states to harmonise their policies, standards and conditions of employment. despite the unwavering commitment of the actors in this direction, this did not happen, because each country had built over the years a lasting balance between all these elements. to touch one of them in order to harmonize with its counterpart in the other countries is to create insurmountable imbalances within each country, sometimes generating social unrest. the only solution is to put an end to this adventure of the single currency and to restore the freedom of monetary policy and sovereignty of each country, which will revive trade and eventually restore full employment. i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ the report uses the growing competitiveness gaps in europe as a pretext for strengthening the eu's cohesion policy, which would reduce regional disparities by replacing the lack of public investment. this means that €350 billion will be invested to combat youth unemployment, to facilitate the financing of smes and to promote the energy transition. these laudable goals hide a sad reality. the strengthening of this cohesion policy will increase the union's constraints on the eligibility of investments and will give more prerogatives to regional authorities, to the detriment of the nation states. the philosophy of this text runs counter to the ideas we advocate. the commission is acting as the fireman. it is responsible for widening the competitiveness gap, and at the same time advocates greater use of european funds to reduce these regional disparities. the solutions offered are also pathetic and even counterproductive. it is impossible to simplify procedures by strengthening administrations, just as it is impossible to create synergies with other funds if the means are not shared. that is why i voted against this text.

in writing. ‒ as i had already done in the parliamentary committee on employment and social affairs, i voted in favour of this report on the implementation, results and overall evaluation of the 2012 european year for active ageing and solidarity between generations. we have seen, in a century, an almost doubling of life expectancy. it is up to us to decide whether the ageing population should be a boon or a burden to our society. if properly managed, population ageing can be a real driver of economic growth. it can also be a pillar of social cohesion through intergenerational exchange. but beware, the ageing population is also a responsibility. a company is often judged by how it treats its senior management. we must be honest, we are lagging far behind and there are profound differences. while we talk about the adaptations needed to meet future demographic trends, we are unable to respond to the current difficulties (health, public pensions, employment, etc.). the european union therefore has a great responsibility in this area.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the resolution on the report on the implementation, results and overall evaluation of the 2012 european year for active ageing and solidarity between generations. the idea of 'active ageing' - improving the health and quality of life of older people for as long as possible by promoting their autonomy and participation in social life - is in itself a positive one. the retention of employment, which is one of these objectives, could be an economic necessity in the light of demographic changes in europe. however, the problem of pensions will not be solved by putting older people to work without thinking that at a certain age retirement is simply deserved. this proposal is ultimately just a clumsy and disguised way of fighting unemployment by keeping the elderly in employment.

in writing. ‒ the report advocates 'active ageing' and tries to drown the fish by defining it as 'the economic, social, spiritual, cultural and civic activities of older people who can continue to contribute to their families, their peers, their community and their country'. the rapporteur does indeed insist on the maintenance of public pension schemes or on the need for rich and affordable public services. but it is the european commission's agenda that is being promoted. she talks about the "silver economy" for "developing the economy of the elderly in europe". the rapporteur therefore calls for 'facilitating the extension of working life for those who wish to do so' by 'reforming the pension system'. it is based on alarmist forecasts: by 2050 the average age of the eu population will be over 50. what are the health conditions according to social classes? and does this forecast take into account the recent arrival of many young migrants and their families? the rapporteur believes that the welfare of older people can only be achieved by maintaining their link with the world of work. vote against this war machine against the right to retire and this hypocritical blabber.

in writing. ‒ this resolution follows the statement by jean-claude juncker, president of the european commission, to parliament last wednesday on the migration crisis in europe. at present, the member states with external borders to the european union - hungary, greece and italy - are the ones receiving the majority of migrants from the mediterranean. the commission proposes the relocation of 120 000 refugees (contained in these three states) to all the member states of the union through binding quotas. france, for its part, would take in 24,000 refugees. the commission also proposes the setting up of 'hot spots' or reception and sorting centres in the countries of arrival. these will ensure decent health conditions for refugees and distinguish between people fleeing persecution zones, who have the right to asylum in europe, and illegal economic migrants, who are to be returned to the border. i believe that the european union has a duty to provide concrete solutions to this humanitarian crisis, and i have therefore voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ we are currently experiencing the most serious migration crisis in our history since the second world war. since the beginning of the year, 366,402 people have arrived via the mediterranean sea, according to the un high commissioner for refugees. in addition, 2,800 people were killed or went missing. in view of the gravity of the situation, i did not want to obstruct this text, which allows a certain awareness of the member states. but i did not want to support it because i am opposed to this permanent and binding relocation mechanism that encourages the creation of an à la carte menu where the preferences of the applicants would dictate our european asylum policy. that is why i am in favour of voluntary interim measures for those who need protection.
in writing. ‒ mrs merkel's announcements welcoming 800 000 immigrants, suspending the dublin procedures are a great invitation to undertake the journey for all immigration applicants, of all nationalities and motivations. how many aylan kurdis will these ads kill? and for what reasons? because germany is generous ? or because its demographic catastrophe is likely to turn into an economic catastrophe in the near future? what kind of a cheap eldorado are these people risking their lives for ? the hell of human rights violated depicted in the ferrera report voted yesterday? europe in the process of third-worldisation, where 25% of the population is at risk of exclusion, where tens of millions of unemployed are stranded, where mass immigration has already proved its harmful consequences? you are coldly exploiting the situation to try to take a step towards the communitarianisation of immigration policies. you are giving a humanitarian veneer to what is, in truth, only the cynical human counterpart of your destructive economic policies. in the end, these men and women are not refugees to you, but future consumers, cheap labour and, you hope, those who will finance tomorrow the slow death of europe's ageing population.
in writing. i particularly welcome the adoption of this joint resolution endorsed by four political groups. it is an ambitious text that is in keeping with the tragedies and challenges we face. the line set by the european parliament is clear and demanding, first on the question of values, first of all solidarity and humanity. the course is also courageous in terms of the mechanisms that should be put in place as soon as possible: firstly, a permanent and mandatory relocation mechanism and also, the strengthening and creation of safe and legal migration routes for refugees. finally, the resolution addresses the root causes of migration. parliament called on the commission and mrs mogherini to convene an international conference on the refugee crisis. this conference should include the participation not only of the eu and its member states but also of un agencies, non-governmental actors and the international community as a whole. in the face of fear and hate speech, the eu and its member states must take all necessary measures to ensure a dignified, exemplary and controlled reception of refugees.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the migration crisis in europe. the text fully supports the proposals made by jean-claude juncker and stresses the need for greater solidarity between member states to better manage the emergency of the massive arrival of migrants in the european union. the introduction of compulsory quotas for processing asylum applications is thus one of the first avenues to be agreed between member states. while we must not ignore the practical problems posed by the arrival of hundreds of thousands of refugees, it is europe's duty to welcome those who are victims of war to their countries of origin. this resolution was adopted by a large majority, which i welcome.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on migration and refugees in europe because the principles of solidarity and fair sharing of responsibilities are core values of the european union. the current crisis requires the implementation of emergency measures.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the resolution of the mainstream groups on migration and refugees in europe. this text perfectly illustrates the gap between the european union and public opinion in the member states. as many polls show, the vast majority of voters in europe want the borders to be re-established and mass immigration to be stopped. the resolution that has been voted in this parliament goes completely the other way. it advocates the maintenance of schengen, which has abolished internal borders while external borders are no longer controlled. it advocates the distribution of migrants within the european union, while the problem is not addressed at the source. it wants to promote legal immigration, whereas the absorption capacity of the member states has long been exceeded. it criticizes those who have seen it coming and warned of the problems we face.
in writing. ‒ driven by the urgency of the situation, the european parliament voted a resolution on immigration and refugees in europe. as has often been the case since the beginning of the humanitarian crisis that has shaken our continent, meps have managed to rise to the challenge by formulating a coherent response, based on a simple observation: the migration flows to europe are not destined to dry up. it is therefore a matter of organising as much as possible, in compliance with the values of solidarity, the schengen agreements and international conventions, to enable asylum seekers to lodge their application for protection without putting their lives at risk. to do this, the resolution before parliament proposes a three-stage strategy, which i fully support. in the short term: abandon the absurd dublin regulation and encourage states to adopt a solidarity and binding mechanism for the distribution of asylum seekers. in the medium term, we must build legal and secure routes to our continent. in the long term: tackling the root causes of migration, such as poverty, inequality and climate change. i voted for this resolution, of course.
in writing. ‒ member states are literally overwhelmed by the massive influx of illegal migrants into europe. the report explains that it is necessary to welcome the majority of these immigrants who are fleeing conflict and persecution from the islamic state. he advocates the establishment of quotas that require each country to receive, house, and care for these migrants. the text calls on all european actors to combat the networks of smugglers who organise human trafficking. we oppose this scandalous report in the strongest possible terms. firstly, the conflicts in libya and the near and middle east are the result of an absurd foreign policy which has been to overthrow totalitarian regimes in favour of islamists. secondly, it is necessary to recall that the majority of illegal immigrants are economic migrants who are not fleeing persecution and therefore do not intend to remain in europe. thirdly, the european union is complicit with the smugglers by not returning the migrant boats to their port of origin. the european institutions are therefore responsible for the human tragedy that is taking place in the mediterranean. i therefore voted against.
in writing. this motion for a resolution welcomes the commission's proposals to deal with the unprecedented influx of migrants. it also approved the emergency relocation of an increased number of asylum seekers from greece, italy and hungary (120 000) and the permanent mechanism amending the dublin regulation. this proposal therefore requires a fair and compulsory distribution key in defiance of the will of sovereign peoples who will have to endure an influx of immigrants from countries with very different cultures and traditions. where the eu had no money to deal with the poverty in greece, it found money to provide for the people of third countries... the text also aims to establish a common european asylum system, to maintain schengen, all in the spirit of european solidarity and human dignity. the text points to the passage "the extreme right" which exploits the current situation. i consider the eu's migration policy to be a real scourge and have therefore decided to vote against this text.
in writing. the political crises in the middle east are generating migration flows unprecedented since the second world war, and thousands of migrants have died trying to cross the mediterranean. for several months now, the european union has been responding inadequately: the distribution of migrants within the member states by means of binding quotas makes no sense in a schengen area that abolishes internal borders. it is a rhetorical appeal to immigration and is encouraging more and more families who think they will be welcomed in europe to risk their lives in the mediterranean. it permanently uproots migrants from their cultural cradle, their language and their land, making it impossible for them to return and complicating their integration into european countries which are already the most generous in the world and which no longer have the means to welcome them with dignity. the text also addresses only the consequences and not the root causes of the migration tragedy, which will only be resolved by military intervention in the air and on the ground, led by an international coalition including russia and the arab countries. for these reasons, i voted against this resolution.

in writing. ‒ the union is facing a serious and widespread migration crisis. it is necessary to act swiftly but in a coordinated manner. the european parliament adopted a resolution following president juncker's statements on the union's emergency measures to deal with the migration crisis. however, i abstained on this text because some measures which are too restrictive could undermine the stability of the union. i am against mandatory and permanent quotas. i think first of all that the union must rethink its migration policy, that it must regain control of this policy.
in writing. ‒ in this joint resolution, the european parliament sets out the priorities and actions to be taken now to save lives and improve the reception of refugees and asylum seekers on our continent. it reiterated its support for the commission's initiative to establish a permanent and compulsory applicant allocation mechanism. the council also called on the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that the eu's external borders are not encroached upon by the countries of the region. the report also calls for the eu to take a more active role in the fight against terrorism and to ensure that the eu is able to take action to combat terrorism. while some are building walls by fuelling intolerable sentiments and rhetoric against refugees, other europeans are choosing humanity by showing their support and commitment to help those fleeing death. this is the message of hope for the future of the union that our national leaders must convey with all their might.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this european parliament resolution on migration and refugees in europe, which calls for the best and quickest response to the emergency we are facing. solidarity between member states will be necessary to overcome this crisis. the legal and budgetary means available to the union, particularly through its frontex agency, must be strengthened. the phenomenon we are experiencing today is not temporary and cannot be managed without a common european policy on the matter. we must also tackle the causes of displacement and therefore probably review our foreign policy towards the areas of origin.
in writing. ‒ i supported this resolution on the plight of migrants and refugees in europe. the european union must respond to this crisis with a comprehensive and coherent immigration and asylum policy. we need an effective implementation of the european asylum system. the dublin regulation should also be amended to ensure that a binding and permanent scheme for the distribution of asylum seekers between member states is established, based on a fair and compulsory distribution key. the new commission proposal on the emergency distribution of an increased number of asylum seekers should also be welcomed. in addition, safe and legal channels must be established to avoid further human tragedies, while effective action must be taken against the criminal and odious networks of smugglers. it is a question of solidarity. it's a matter of values. it's a matter of responsibility. it's an emergency.
in writing. ‒ since the beginning of 2015, the un high commissioner's office says that 366 402 people have crossed the mediterranean to reach the european continent and 2 800 people have lost their lives. the european union and its member states must react and show solidarity in the face of this dramatic situation. this solidarity must not only be between member states but also towards refugees. this is a problem facing the european union and it requires a european solution. on the other hand, the european union, as a global actor, must act at international level to restore peace and find political solutions to conflicts affecting the countries from which refugees come. i voted in favour of this resolution because more than ever we need to show solidarity.
in writing. ‒ in the face of the inertia and the hallucinatory hesitations of member states, the european parliament wanted to express its position on what european migration policy should be in the light of the global humanitarian crisis. this is the most ambitious resolution that has been voted by the european parliament since i have been a member of the european parliament. i welcome the support for the relocation mechanism proposed by the commission and the request for a revision of the dublin regulation. the need to open up legal pathways to european territory is clearly reaffirmed, as is the possibility of asylum applications being lodged at embassies. the resolution also calls for the establishment of a european union-wide network of border controls and for the establishment of a european union-wide network of border controls. if i did not expect a denunciation of the deadly consequences of fortress europe, a minimum of reserve was necessary. i do not want to deny the progress and the need for parliament to weigh in on the states, but i do not want to mix my voice with those of the extreme right, so i have chosen to abstain.
in writing. ‒ in substance, several aspects of this motion for a resolution are positive. it is therefore commendable to wish for a lasting and just peace to the israeli-palestinian conflict. the call for the security of the civilian population and the demand for the lifting of the blockade of gaza are also quite understandable in the light of the current situation in the middle east. however, together with my colleagues from the national front, we believe that the european union should not interfere in foreign policy. this must remain the prerogative of the states. however, this motion for a resolution goes against this principle when it states that the union must develop a comprehensive and coherent vision and become politically involved in the resolution of the conflict. by voting for this text, the european parliament illegitimately assumes exclusive royal competence. once again, the union is blatantly encroaching on the sovereignty of the member states. i therefore voted against this text.

in writing. ‒ in the context of the middle east peace process, this resolution sets out the objectives of the mandate of the high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy, federica mogherini, in the context of the peace negotiations between israel and the palestinians. this recommendation sets out a new approach of the european union to the resolution of the israeli-palestinian conflict, focusing on political negotiations, the use of non-violent means and the priority given to the rights of civilians. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the eu. i support this recommendation and have voted in favour of the resolution.
in writing. the eu must play a leading role in the middle east peace process. peace between israelis and palestinians will only be possible through the peaceful coexistence of two viable states. this is what this resolution, which i voted for, reaffirms. i wish, by this vote, to denounce the main obstacles to the peace process: the colonisation of palestinian territories and the related human rights violations, the blockade of gaza, the rocket fire towards israel, the division of the palestinian authority. the resolution calls on the parties to continue their efforts and welcomes the un's action, in particular on behalf of palestinian refugees. parliament supported the commission, the eeas, ms mogherini and mr gentilini and wanted the eu to play a strong role which could be valuable in a situation which, just a year ago, was mired in the gaza war. i am convinced that the eu must pursue a political solution to the peace process, while avoiding some indirect responsibility in the conflict. for example, there is a need to study more closely the destination and use of eu funds in the region and to make progress on the labelling rules for products from israeli settlements.

in writing. ‒ the report denounces the alleged violation of human rights in belarus. freedom of expression and certain individual freedoms would be trampled underfoot by the government in power. the country has not held free elections since 1994. the report therefore calls on belarus to hold fair elections, to stop the use of the death penalty and to abolish forced labour. while we recognize that belarus does not respect human rights, we oppose any moral condemnation and believe that it is neither our duty nor our responsibility to force a sovereign country to submit to our definition of democracy. it is also quite surprising to see the european institutions reacting with indignation to this situation when they are acting against the people without regard for their will. i therefore opposed this text.
