in writing. this report on social entrepreneurship and social innovation in the fight against unemployment aims to develop the social and solidarity economy by focusing on 5 major areas (education/training, access to finance, visibility at european level, improvement of the legal framework, development of the social economy in the eu and the member states). social entrepreneurship includes forms of entrepreneurship whose main purpose is social or environmental and where the majority of the profits are reinvested in that mission. while this objective is obviously laudable, i note the total contradiction with the competition policies advocated by the eu. moreover, the social and solidarity economy is a sector which, although it is possible to maintain local jobs that cannot be relocated for people with low qualifications and which sometimes gives rise to some successes such as certain scops (for example in the context of the takeover of profitable businesses by its former employees), remains a largely illusory sector, since the remuneration of these jobs is often capped, the scope of these jobs is often narrow and can help only a limited number of people, the state aids granted are subject to little control and we have no concrete analyses on the long-term economic and environmental effects ... i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ social entrepreneurship encompasses all initiatives that integrate social and environmental responsibility into their activities. these organisations emphasise their governance, which is more respectful of stakeholders, the well-being of their employees and their environmentally responsible approach. these initiatives are part of what is known as the social and solidarity economy. the report advocates developing social entrepreneurship and social innovation as these businesses have proven to be more resilient to the effects of the crisis. they are job creators, they care more about the interests of their employees and are therefore better placed to meet the union's objectives set out in horizon 2020. although the draft report is welcome, it is undeniable that the social and solidarity economy does not create enough jobs to make up for those which have been destroyed over the last 40 years under the impetus of the european union. this is yet another attempt to conceal the failure of all european policies in terms of employment. i voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report supports the promotion of social entrepreneurship and social innovation as a key driver of economic development, and in line with the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. the rapporteur calls on the european commission to include social economy enterprises in the action programmes on employment and social inclusion. it also called on the member states to invest in this area at national level, in particular in adapting national tax systems to the benefit of social economy enterprises. i believe that the fight against unemployment is a priority in europe and that social entrepreneurship is one of the solutions to tackle it, so i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the text on social entrepreneurship and social innovation in the fight against unemployment highlights the links between the social economy and local realities. i voted in favour of this text because social enterprises can be promoters of solutions adapted to specific needs. the european union is thus demonstrating its determination to combat unemployment and promote social inclusion.
in writing. ‒ while the social and solidarity-based economy, which is the inspiration for the terms and substance of this report, allows the promotion of social and territorial cohesion in the union, its entrepreneurial dimension has a minimal influence on the economy. this strategy affects only a limited number of jobs and cannot initiate structural change. however, funds are allocated to this strategy and the lack of prior evaluation and impact assessment provided by the european commission is a shortcoming that deprives the legislator of long-term vision. finally, there is a significant risk of the emergence of recurrent and permanent beneficiaries of this strategy, which was originally intended to be a one-off correction for reintegration and the maintenance of the social link. i have opposed this report because i am opposed to the injection of certain jobs into the union and to unconsidered expenditure.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on social entrepreneurship and social innovation in the fight against unemployment, supporting better access to public procurement, better financing and the creation of a legal status of its own in the context of the europe 2020 strategy for this economy, which employs more than 14 million people in europe and is therefore particularly important both in terms of employment and social and environmental impacts.
in writing. i voted against this text, which is honourable but so illusory. this strategy is in fact applicable to only a very narrow range of jobs and therefore to a very limited number of people. the absence of impact studies and controls does not allow a clear idea of the long-term consequences of these measures. this is the latest attempt to cover up the inefficiency and failure of 30 years of employment policy in europe.
in writing. this report on social entrepreneurship and social innovation in the fight against unemployment aims to develop the social economy in solidarity by focusing on 5 major areas (education/training, access to finance, visibility at european level, improvement of the legal framework, development of the social economy in the eu and the member states). social entrepreneurship includes forms of entrepreneurship whose main purpose is social or environmental and where the majority of the profits are reinvested in that mission. social innovation is part of the concept of the social and solidarity economy. while this objective is laudable, it is in total contradiction to the eu's policies of increased competition. moreover, the social and solidarity economy is largely illusory, since the remuneration of these jobs is often capped, which encourages social dumping, the scope of these jobs is often narrow and can only help a limited number of people, the state aids granted are subject to little control, the long-term economic and environmental effects are little analysed, etc. these proposals are a counter-fire to the ineffectiveness and failure of the eu's employment policies. i therefore voted against.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report on the role of enterprises, cooperatives, associations, mutuals and foundations in the fight against unemployment. the report highlights that the social and solidarity economy represents 2 million enterprises, or 10% of enterprises in the european union, and employs 14 million people, or 6.5% of workers. the purpose of this text is to set up regulatory frameworks in the member states to develop this type of enterprise, which creates jobs even during the crisis.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report by my colleague, veronica lopé fontagné. in order to achieve the objectives set out in the europe 2020 strategy, social economy enterprises have demonstrated their ability to provide innovative solutions to boost social cohesion and inclusion and job creation, including during periods of economic downturn. in addition, social economy enterprises are closely linked to local and regional realities and offer solutions adapted to specific needs. the social and solidarity economy must be clearly identified as a priority for job creation and social cohesion. to do this, all member states must put in place legal frameworks and we must push for the creation of a european label for the recognition of these structures, which often lack legal recognition.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which highlights the role of the social economy as a way out of the economic crisis. i regret, however, that he continues to confuse the social and solidarity economy with social business. despite the crisis and the unprecedented destruction of jobs, the social and solidarity economy has proven its resilience, far superior to that of other types of enterprises, and its ability to create new jobs in an unfavourable economic environment. the ep report stresses that the social economy is an important driver for achieving a more sustainable economic and financial model, which creates social and territorial cohesion and respects the environment, as mentioned in the eu treaties. it called on the commission to establish a legal framework for all social and solidarity-based economy enterprises by adopting european statutes, which the member states have still not adopted despite repeated requests from the sector. after the toïa report (2009), this is another important report showing that the social economy represents a viable alternative to the traditional business model, an economy that serves people, is innovative, and is more responsive to the needs and challenges of society.
in writing. ‒ the aim of this report is to take stock of european employment policies in order to find the appropriate solutions to reduce the unemployment rate without attacking social protection systems. the rapporteur expresses his willingness to tackle the unemployment rate among young people and the elderly and the high regional disparities. to this end, they advocate measures to encourage the unemployed to return to work, to improve the skills of employees, to anticipate the needs of enterprises, to encourage apprenticeship, to encourage the employment of young people and older workers and to develop entrepreneurship. the guiding principle of the text is to defend the mobility of workers within the eu in order to reduce regional disparities in unemployment. as usual, they do not address the root causes of structural unemployment, namely unfair international competition, the loss of monetary and legislative sovereignty and the shrinking budgetary room for manoeuvre. the only way forward for the european institutions so far has been competitive disinflation, characterized by lower social charges and a slowdown in wages. i therefore voted against this text.

in writing. this report on creating a competitive labour market in the 21st century eu aims to take stock of the policies pursued to make the labour market more competitive while trying to preserve the social protection system. it is clear that these two objectives are inherently contradictory, since the more the european union encourages states to be competitive, the more citizens see their social protection melting away like snow in the sun. the report also deplores the high level of unemployment in the eu, particularly among young people and the elderly, but the paths of reform envisaged are at best questionable and unoriginal. worse still, this report promotes the mobility of workers when it is known that this threatens the peripheral countries of the euro area. i therefore voted against this text.

in writing. ‒ these two annual reports on the monitoring of the application of eu law detail the legal proceedings brought against member states for not transposing european commission directives quickly enough. in this context, the european court of justice has delivered 31 judgments against member states, mainly in areas relating to consumer protection, the environment, transport or the internal market. the text recalls that the member states have an obligation to transpose fully and effectively the commission's directives. if not, the lisbon treaty provides that the court of justice can sanction countries that do not respect european law. the report even recommends that these sanctions be tightened. we are firmly opposed to the european dictate which is to impose on the peoples of europe political and economic orientations which are not their own. the european union is a totalitarian organisation which flouts individual freedoms and the national sovereignty of the member states. i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ the 30th and 31st annual reports on the monitoring of the application of eu law for the years 2012 and 2013 take stock of the infringement procedures brought against member states for delayed or incorrect transposition of eu directives by the commission, in the exercise of its role as 'guardian of the treaties' (article 17 teu) and of its powers as defined in articles 258 to 260 of the treaty on the functioning of the eu (infringement procedure). in 2013, the court of justice of the european union delivered 52 judgments (article 258 tfeu), 31 of which were unfavourable to the member states. this is one of the sad innovations of the lisbon treaty: at the request of the commission, the court of justice can impose penalties for delay in transposition without waiting for a second judgment. i therefore voted against this report despite some positive points, such as the recognition that 'certain policies imposed on member states, in particular the privatisation of public goods, constitute a direct breach of the principles on which the union is founded' and 'article 345 tfeu provides that the treaties in no way prejudice the system of property ownership in the member states'.
in writing. this report on the 30th and 31st annual reports on the monitoring of the application of the eu advocates a number of points that i oppose, such as the full transposition and effective implementation of the common european system as a top priority or the fact that the charter of fundamental rights is considered a treaty like any other. in addition, i strongly condemn the introduction of the possibility for the cjeu to fine states which have delays in transposition or the call on the commission to be more strict on the transposition of environmental directives in particular. with its myriad standards and new regulations every day, the eu is becoming more and more of a cold, bureaucratic monster like the ussr in its day, only with ultra-liberalism to add to it. although the report contains some positive measures, such as condemning the obligation on states to privatise certain public assets (which is contrary to article 345 of the feu treaty) and expressing concern about austerity measures, i decided to vote against it.

on behalf of the enf group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, at the end of august, angela merkel opened germany's borders wide to migrants and said she wanted to welcome 800 000 of them. fifteen days later, the german chancellor was faced with the wall of reality, and she was forced to make an impressive headline, suspending schengen and sending police to her borders to stop the influx of illegal immigrants she had triggered. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, you have unleashed a phenomenon of airborne noise which you cannot control and which will overwhelm us! you will take responsibility for this to history. this madness must be stopped now, by a firm and clear policy, australian-style, so that the tide will dry up, while there is still time, and this chaos will end! when you are wrong, you try to stop me from speaking, but believe me, the people of europe hear me! on monday, the emergency meeting of interior ministers on the migration crisis in the european union resulted in a complete disagreement between those who want to impose migrant quotas and those who refuse. germany, through its minister of the interior, immediately threatened financial sanctions against those who refused. this blackmail is completely indecent. it is now president schulz, the socialist president, who is making an undemocratic and unbearable coup, with the complicity of the pse and the epp, by imposing an emergency vote. but france - because i am interested in france, sorry - has very big problems of assimilation, but also 7 million unemployed, 10 million poor, 1.5 million households waiting for social housing. she can't take anyone. it is therefore absolutely necessary to put an end to the schengen system once and for all, to allow each country to control its borders and each people to make its own free choices. before you, europe was peace! today, it is a war of influence, an economic war, antagonisms and conflicts between european countries. what a success!

madam president, failure, fiasco, setbacks... there is no shortage of words to comment on monday's council. expectations were high for this meeting. it's a waste. so it is the next one, on 22 september, that may offer us a last-chance solution. but i don't really feel like commenting on the comments about a meeting because what is really at stake is whether the european union can pass its crash test or whether it is on the verge of a sudden shutdown. this is a real assumption in the context of the current humanitarian crisis. the fractures in europe are growing, the misunderstandings are getting worse, the decisions are becoming less and less common and more and more unilateral. too many member states are turning their backs on the common asylum policy, which exists and can be exercised, while lamenting the absence of a common migration policy. that's totally inconsistent. in the meantime, the displaced persons are on european territory and the protection system is not working quickly enough. two final remarks: we must talk to the relevant actors at international level. federica mogherini is convinced of this, and others are too. we have to help them. we have to anticipate before we even agree, if we can. member states must ensure that refugees are given dignified and controlled reception and integration conditions.
madam president, yes, europe must play its full part in welcoming refugees so as not to leave the burden of taking them on the shoulders of the countries neighbouring syria. but this deal has to be arranged. and we have, in my view, two real emergencies before us. the first is to set up reception and control centres at the external borders of the union to identify and register those who arrive, to interview them and to grant them temporary admission to the european union. the second urgent need is the capacity to receive refugees on the ground, especially in transit countries. i was there a few days ago with my colleague nathalie griesbeck. the needs are immense: hardwood structures, blankets, doctors, sanitation, water, interpreters and lawyers. it is to these two questions - external borders and reception, particularly in transit countries - that we want, that we now demand, concrete, rapid and effective answers in the hours and days to come.

on behalf of the s&d group. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, with just a few weeks to go until cop21 in paris, and with the international community having just adopted the new sustainable development goals, this report and this debate are timely. i would first like to congratulate the rapporteur. this text gives us the opportunity to recall the crucial role played by local authorities in defining and implementing european and international development policy. as a provider of basic public services such as health, education, especially water, sanitation, we can see how much the expertise of these authorities in these key areas will count in the success of our commitment to eradicate poverty. the 11th sustainable development goal on cities now allows local authorities to be fully recognised as central actors in international cooperation. i think we can modestly see this as a victory for the european union and especially for our parliament, which for the last 10 years has been constantly stressing the key role of decentralisation and decentralised cooperation in improving the living conditions of the poorest people in the world. the commission must now take up this report and the proposals it contains, in order to promote a development policy based on multi-level governance. as such, it is high time that decentralisation became a fully-fledged sector of financial concentration of the european union for developing countries. i would like to conclude by quoting former un secretary-general kofi annan, who, when the millennium development goals were launched in 2000, stressed that their achievement would be local or not. these words echo with equal force at the dawn of the new objectives that will be ours until 2030.
on behalf of the enf group. ladies and gentlemen, i thank our colleague for his contribution, but i must confess that i am not convinced. this report is first of all a reflection of the failure of previous policies towards states, and particularly african states. over the past 60 years, more than a trillion dollars has been spent on development aid. nearly half of africans still live on less than a dollar a day. in the last half century, wars and massacres have killed ten million people, and there have been eighty coups d'état. eleven countries have been involved in civil wars for 15 years, which have cost, in addition to human lives, nearly two hundred billion dollars, not to mention the corruption which is estimated by the african union at one hundred and fifty billion dollars a year. how can we talk about development aid in these circumstances? a nascent economy requires stable institutions, functioning public services and prospects for young people. addressing the lower communities as we do will not solve anything. to combat corruption, control migration flows and promote development, three priorities are needed: to make aid conditional on a project logic and no longer on a counter logic, to ensure transparency and control in order to eradicate corruption networks and to sanction the actions of multinational companies that prey on raw materials or on markets for juices without consideration for local populations. finally, trust in the new generations who want to be independent and who are struggling to free themselves from local administrative or cultural rigidities. aid for aid purposes will not help if we continue to support structurally corrupt powers.

in writing. the case is about allowing eu member states to ratify the protocol on forced labour convention of 1930 because 80 years later there are still cases of forced labour which is strictly unacceptable. the convention, which is one of the eight core ilo conventions defining basic labour standards, has been the subject of a protocol to address shortcomings in its implementation and also tackles trafficking in human beings. the provisions of the protocol thus establish the obligation to prevent forced labour and to ensure protection for victims and access to redress mechanisms, such as compensation. more specifically, the protocol aims to: (i) establish decent working conditions; and (ii) protect victims of forced or compulsory labour and punish offenders. so i voted for it.

in writing. ‒ i supported this recommendation on the council's decision to authorise member states to ratify the 2014 protocol to the forced labour convention, 1930, of the international labour organisation (ilo). the ilo convention on forced labour is one of a set of eight conventions that seek to define basic international labour standards. yet, the ilo estimates that more than 20 million people worldwide are still victims of forced labour. we must fight with all the necessary firmness against these unacceptable criminal practices. the 2014 protocol, which contains measures to implement and strengthen legislation on prevention, but also on protection and compensation of victims, contributes to this and imposes legal obligations on states parties. the protection of human rights requires a responsible and firm attitude. we must ensure that the ilo criteria are implemented. the resolution was therefore well worth supporting.
in writing. ‒ the forced labour convention is one of the eight core ilo conventions, which define the basic international labour standards. but more than 80 years later, and despite the convention's near universal ratification, forced labour still exists. in 2014, the international labour conference adopted the protocol to the forced labour convention with the aim of addressing implementation gaps and strengthening measures to prevent trafficking in human beings for the purpose of labour exploitation, as well as protection and compensation for victims of forced labour. the proposed decision aims to enable member states to ratify the protocol to the forced labour convention, 1930, of the international labour organisation (ilo). i therefore voted in favour of the adoption of this text.
in writing. ‒ forced labour is still a reality in the world, with the international labour organisation estimating that nearly 21 million people are victims of forced labour. it is good to re-launch the fight against this situation and to update the legislation to combat forced labour. this is what the protocol adopted by the ilo in 2014 proposes to do. this legally binding instrument is intended to combat 'modern' forms of forced labour. by implementing this protocol, states undertake to develop national policies and plans to combat forced labour, in particular by introducing sanctions obligations against instigators of these crimes, improving the protection and compensation of victims of forced labour. the latter are often the most vulnerable populations, including migrants who are particularly vulnerable to abusive and fraudulent practices. the report submitted to the european parliament proposes ratification of this protocol. i voted in favour of this report because it can improve the binding instruments in the fight against trafficking and make a step forward in respecting human rights.

in writing. ‒ 25i-nbome is a potent synthetic derivative, a classic serotonergic hallucinogen, which has been subject to control measures at union level since 2003. there were 4 deaths related to 25i-nbome in three member states and 32 poisonings. ah-7921 is an atypical structure analgesic that can be easily confused with doxylamine, an antihistamine with sedative and hypnotic properties. between 2012 and september 2013, 15 deaths and 6 cases of poisoning were reported in three member states. mdpv is a synthetic substituted-cycle derivative of cathinone and is subject to control measures under the 1971 united nations convention on psychotropic substances. between september 2009 and august 2013, 108 deaths and 525 cases of poisoning were reported in eight member states and norway. methoxetamine is an analogue of ketamine and phencyclidine, which are internationally controlled substances. in the united kingdom, the number of deaths from methoxetamine-related causes has increased from 6 in 2004 to 20 in 2006. given the risks, this proposal must invite member states to submit this to checks and i therefore voted in favour.

in writing. - i voted for this report. although some passages remain unclear, the overall picture is very satisfactory: it will make it possible to assign the protected geographical indication (pgi) to non-agricultural products, such as laguiole knives or calais lace. this extension will help to protect the 'made in france', a symbol for consumers of traditional know-how and a guarantee of quality.
in writing. ‒ i voted enthusiastically for the report by my colleague virginie rozière, which calls on the european parliament to support greater protection of geographical indications in the union. at present, while agricultural gi's (champagne wine, agen prunes, etc.) are largely protected, the same is not true of non-agricultural products such as laguiole knives or marseille soaps. the extension of the gi to more than 800 handicraft products - which parliament, through the rozière report, calls for - would only bring benefits, both for consumers and for workers. this system would give europeans access to reliable information on products that are recognised as being of quality. the extension of the gi to manufactured products would also have the effect of combating counterfeiting and the associated relocations. at a time when some european countries, such as france, are trying to promote 'territorial diplomacy' in their trade relations, parliament's initiative is more than welcome. the commission is now being urged to propose a legislative initiative on non-agricultural pgi. that is why i have co-signed a letter to commissioner katainen on this matter.
in writing. ‒ the use of geographical indications (gi) now protects agricultural products of a particular geographical origin that have specific qualities or are produced using traditional methods. the report before us envisages extending this principle to non-agricultural products based on traditional techniques and crafts of a very high standard, and which are an integral part of regional and local culture. fifteen member states (including france since june 2015) have adopted this system. i am glad that the commission has taken this step, and i am glad that it has done so. the protection of geographical indications for non-agricultural products is a tool for preserving cultural heritage and traditional know-how, and it guarantees fair remuneration for producers. it remains to be seen whether these pgi will be respected in the context of the large transatlantic market. in the meantime, i vote yes.
in writing. ‒ this report proposes to extend protection to non-agricultural products, including certain french products. through a protected geographical indication, the producer can promote know-how and offer quality products to consumers. in france, it is estimated that this geographical indication will lead to an increase in the demand for products in certain sectors. as it is a question of protecting the 'made in france', i voted for this report.
in writing. ‒ the report aims to extend the protection of protected geographical indications (pgi) to non-agricultural products. in france, for example, this would allow protection to be given to goods which refer to a geographical origin and traditional know-how. the most cited example is the laguiole knives. pgi allows the producer to promote his products and offers the consumer guarantees of quality. in practical terms, pgi is a way of promoting 'made in france' commercially and making it safe against counterfeiting. the text presented here is an improvement which deserves support.
in writing. the report aims to apply the protection of geographical indications to non-agricultural products such as laguiole knives and calais lace, among others. a protected geographical indication allows the protection of a name or symbol which refers to the geographical origin of a product and to traditional know-how, while providing consumers with guarantees as to the quality of those products. these pgi are of crucial importance as they increase the international demand of the beneficiary firms (by some studies, by almost 25%!). i believe that this is a way of protecting the "made in france" and i have decided to vote in favour of it.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution to extend the protection of geographical indications of the european union to non-agricultural products. i am in favour of a legislative proposal to establish a single european system of protection, including a mandatory product registration process and a single european register of non-agricultural products which are protected by a geographical indication. i think it is important, however, that this new system should be able to coexist with the rights already attached to products. such legislative provisions on geographical indications would help to preserve and enhance traditional and high-quality know-how, thus enhancing europe's historical, cultural, economic and social heritage. this would also facilitate the choice of consumers who would be assured of the authenticity and quality of the product through reliable information on the place and method of production. these provisions would also have the advantage of encouraging innovation by supporting smes, combating imitation and counterfeiting and encouraging fair competition. finally, this protection system would stimulate european exports and allow us to gain market share, while at the same time protecting the products concerned in the context of the common commercial policy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the possible extension of geographical indications to non-agricultural products. many european and french products could be affected by this european system, notably the laguiole knife, the calais lace and the cherbourg umbrella. the extension of geographical indications to non-agricultural products would represent a real economic and cultural opportunity in europe, as well as a recognition of know-how. direct and indirect employment in the non-agricultural geographical indications sector represents more than 4 million jobs in europe. it is urgent to establish protection of geographical indications at european level, which would not only protect our companies from counterfeiting and unfair competition, but also guarantee consumers quality know-how and products. this european protection must be put in place by ensuring that the system is simple and inexpensive so that our companies, and in particular our smes, can have access to it.

in writing. ‒ the structural funds are governed by a set of procedures and budgetary rules which oblige the states to finance part of the projects, the rest being co-financed by the structural funds. this share varies according to the level of development of the regions. in the greek budgetary situation, because of the enormous european budgetary pressures, it is impossible to provide the necessary contribution to the disbursement of european funds, however small. this is a paradox that must be noted: the greeks can hardly use european funds because the european budgetary rules prevent them from taking out the necessary share of the financed projects. with this new proposal, structural financing will now be able to cover 100%, which represents a saving of €2 billion for the greek treasury. the 5% reserve made on european funds can also be released, bringing cash reserves estimated at eur 500 million. finally, the prefinancing rates for the next budgetary period are increased. i supported these new rules, but i regret that they were adopted after the blackmail imposed on the greek people last july. the funds should have been released much earlier instead of being used as a bargaining chip for shameful blackmail.

in writing. ‒ the proposal is to grant germany a financial contribution of eur 7 million from the european globalisation adjustment fund following the dismissal of 2 881 employees at opel. the purpose of this aid is to facilitate the reintegration of workers made redundant. while the german company saw its sales fall by 39% between 2007 and 2013, the whole european automotive sector is affected by a continuous decrease in the number of newly registered cars (-25% between 2007 and 2013). while these redundancies are directly linked to the current economic crisis and unfair competition from emerging countries, the responsibility of the american parent company general motors, which has forced opel to sell its cars only on the european market, should not be dismissed. on the one hand, this application fulfils the conditions for granting financial contributions from the egf. on the other hand, we believe it is important to help the german workers who have been made redundant and who, like the french, are suffering the disastrous consequences of unbridled globalisation. that is why i voted for this text.

in writing. ‒ today, the european aviation sector is under very high pressure, especially in the face of the emergence of competitors from the gulf countries. some european airlines, such as alitalia, have had to restructure and have been forced to lay off some of their staff. in order to support european workers, italy has applied for the globalisation adjustment fund. i voted in favour of this request for eur 1.4 million. this aid will make it possible, in particular, to offer specialised training to workers made redundant, facilitating their reintegration into the labour market.

in writing. this report on the role of local authorities in developing countries in development cooperation tells us that it is essential to ensure good, transparent and accountable governance of local authorities and civil society organisations. the report urges the european union to promote decentralised cooperation as a means of implementing the development of a post-2015 framework and encourages national governments to transfer resources to the local or regional level (decentralisation). the report considers that this would be a means of combating corruption, particularly in multinational companies. i strongly oppose the recommendations of this report because i believe that the organisation of states is a choice that directly affects them and that decentralisation will in no way limit corruption. on the contrary, in europe, decentralisation increases costs, constraints and encourages arrangements at the local level. finally, this report seeks to undermine the sovereignty of states and that is why i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on 'the role of local authorities in developing countries in development cooperation'. the report excludes states from european development aid policies. the beneficiary states must be able to allocate development aid according to their national policy wishes.
in writing. ‒ the report recommends promoting decentralisation in developing countries and encouraging governments to transfer some of their powers to local authorities. the rapporteur believes that decentralisation would be the most effective way of combating corruption in elected officials, particularly by the representatives of the large groups, and would help to meet the needs of those they administer. to this end, national governments are strongly encouraged to make large budgetary transfers to local authorities. the european commission, true to itself, is trying to spread its mistaken vision of territorial organization. decentralisation does not in any way limit the corruption of elected officials, nor does it make budgetary savings possible. we see that in europe, and especially in france, it is a source of red tape, of unnecessary duplication of administrative work and is costly for the taxpayer. finally, territorial organization is a matter for the states and the european institutions do not have to interfere in the national affairs of sovereign countries. that is why i voted against this text.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, at the beginning of september the revelation of the volkswagen fraud shocked both sides of the atlantic. diesel cars on the market in the united states emitted 5 to 35 times the amount of nitrogen dioxide allowed by u.s. standards. the question is only approached from an ideological and environmental point of view, whereas it is primarily a technical question. i would like to remind you of a basic law of thermodynamics: all combustion produces emissions, all is a proportion of the various gases emitted, but pollution remains. a technical detail: to make more efficient engines, the combustion rate in the cylinders must be increased. this means that the vehicle uses less fuel per kilometre, releases less badly burned hydrocarbons, and gains acceleration power. volkswagen diesel engines no longer produce carbon monoxide, which is good for health and the environment, but a lot of nitrogen oxides, which is more objectionable, of course. this brings us to the heart of the matter, for carbon monoxide, when in contact with nitrogen dioxide, would convert it into simple nitrogen, a perfectly harmless gas. the father of modern chemistry, lavoisier, said 250 years ago: "nothing is lost, nothing is created, everything is transformed". what is wrong with volkswagen? the mistake of its engineers was to produce powerful engines that produced little carbon dioxide and a lot of nitrogen dioxide, when they claimed otherwise. from a legal point of view, it's a big scandal, but from an environmental point of view, what they did is neutral. the american standards are impossible to meet for small cars and they were not set to protect the environment but to undermine the irresistible rise of the european volkswagen group, which in july 2015 became the world's leading car manufacturer. in short, the volkswagengate is a side-effect of the economic war between the united states and a section of european industry. the analysis must therefore be technical, even chemical and strategic. the environmental aspect is only a tool for the use of antagonistic powers. the environment is a lever of protectionism in the 21st century. europeans must get rid of all naivety in this area. this is particularly urgent in view of the cop 21 which will take place in paris in december.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the calendar of sessions for 2017. the main issue in the proposal was whether or not to keep strasbourg as the seat of the european parliament. the idea of making brussels the sole seat of the european parliament raises several problems. firstly, why should it be in brussels rather than in strasbourg? it is equally possible to argue that parliament should meet only in strasbourg, where lobbyists are less present. the choice of brussels as the sole seat would help to centralize the european union more. the concentration of power will necessarily be to the detriment of the member states. the additional cost is often greatly exaggerated. since members are constantly on the move (returning to their constituencies, various missions, etc.), the expected benefits would ultimately be quite small. in addition, the abandonment of strasbourg would result in a significant loss of income for the inhabitants of strasbourg and for many businesses, not to mention the significant costs of moving and settling in brussels. the proposed timetable maintains the seat of the european parliament in strasbourg, so i voted in favour.

in writing. - i voted against this protocol. the text includes provisions on tunisia's participation in european programmes, which will allow tunisia to benefit from technical and financial assistance from the eu. this text is a thinly veiled attempt to bring tunisia and the eu closer together and to support its 'democratization', an attempt that has been totally unsuccessful if we consider that the support provided by the eu and the us has resulted in the coming to power of the islamists and a strong loss of internal stability. any discussion with tunisia should be conditional on the results or efforts of tunisia in the fight against illegal immigrants, against terrorism and in the promotion of democracy.
in writing. ‒ the panzeri report called on the european parliament to give its opinion on the project to integrate tunisia into certain european union programmes. i am convinced that there is a kind of imperative for the european union that tunisia, at the origin of the arab spring, should succeed in its democratic transition, despite the economic and security challenges it faces. it is in the interests of both the region and the european union that the tunisian experience should bear fruit. in the face of rampant unemployment and the deterioration of trade with its european trading partners, it is essential that the european union help tunisia to get back on a proper economic and social development path. at a time when more than 40% of tunisian young people are unemployed, i welcome the eu's willingness to include tunisia in some of its programmes, particularly in the fields of higher education, general education, training and youth. in line with my commitment to an ambitious and protective free trade agreement with tunisia, i voted for the panzeri report.
in writing. ‒ this is to allow tunisia, as a member of the european neighbourhood policy and at its request, to participate in eu cultural, social or economic programmes. in this case, tunisia is particularly interested in joining the research and development programme, horizon 2020. it emphasizes competitiveness as the objective and value of research, to the detriment of the humanities and laboratories for "non-profit" research. in fact, i am abstaining in order not to hinder potential future cultural, social and research collaborations that can help support the country's fragile democratic transition in the wake of the arab spring. i hope that this agreement will pave the way for more cooperation in other areas, such as education and the erasmus programme. i would point out, however, that at the moment the financial contribution requested from tunisia to join these programmes is too dissuasive, whereas ukraine has enjoyed substantial discounts. it is the double standard of the union's foreign policy.
in writing. ‒ this protocol asks the council to approve an agreement between the european union and tunisia, a framework agreement. this document provides for the definition of financial and technical rules which would give tunisia the possibility of participating in eu programmes. through this agreement, tunisia would be able to benefit from technical and financial assistance from the union. it is true that tunisia is facing political and economic difficulties today. but the european union is showing hypocrisy. the european parliament, together with the united states, is partly responsible for this situation by its interference. moreover, instead of worrying about the tunisian economy, the eu would do better to sweep up its doorstep and help its neighbours who share a common history and civilization. serbia for example. if the european union is serious about having ties with tunisia, it must start by working on security and immigration issues. any partnership between this country and the member states should be conditional on performance obligations in this area. for these reasons, the member voted against.

in writing. ‒ since july 2007, the european small claims procedure has simplified and accelerated the settlement of legal disputes. costs were reduced by 40% and the average length of the procedure was reduced from 2 years to 5 months. the commission nevertheless found that these results were still insufficient. 45% of companies involved in litigation do not initiate proceedings because of the cost involved. the report therefore proposes to set the ceiling for small claims at eur 10 000, compared with eur 2 000 today. it also recommends better use of electronic means and videoconferencing to reduce travel costs. the legal fees will be capped at 10% of the sums involved and the parties involved will be able to pay them through an online payment method. finally, 86% of citizens are not aware of this procedure. therefore, the communication on the website portal should be improved. the proposal will speed up procedures and reduce costs for businesses and citizens involved in litigation. i therefore voted in favour of this text.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this text because it is aimed at reducing pollution by nitrogen oxides and sulphur dioxide, but it seems to be unfavourable to french and european industries for a very risky ecological benefit. it creates a new handicap for them in relation to industries in non-european countries. it's a symbol of the art of shooting yourself in the foot.
in writing. ‒ this is a proposal for a directive to limit emissions from a certain category of combustion plants in the 'medium' category (rated thermal output between 1 and 50 mw). these combustion plants are used for a wide range of uses including electricity generation, domestic/residential heating and cooling and the production of heat or steam for industrial purposes. in the eu, 143 000 installations are affected. they are a major source of sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and particulate matter emissions, and are currently not regulated at eu level (while small and large installations are). the proposal aims to limit the emission of pollutants from these installations. the commission's thresholds are still too high and the right wing is trying to exclude the peripheral regions of the eu from the scope of the directive, but it is in the direction of reducing emissions of pollutants, so i am voting in favour.
in writing. ‒ medium combustion plants are used in a wide range of applications and have a rated thermal output of between 1 and 50 mw. these plants therefore fall between small plants which are covered by the ecodesign directive (2009/125/ec) and large combustion plants which are covered by the industrial emissions directive (2010/75/eu). the aim of this text is therefore to fill a certain legislative gap and to contribute to the reduction of pollution by nitrogen oxides, sulphur dioxide and dust. of course, these regulatory changes are the responsibility of the member states and have a considerable impact on industry. for example, states must apply a stricter emission limit in areas that do not comply with the european air quality standard; they must also keep a public record of the date of registration of combustion plants; the commission will also consider whether to register or permit an existing installation at least one year before the date of compliance. the text thus follows in the footsteps of these standards which are hostile to industry, but which are concealed by a risky environmental and public health benefit. this text is contrary to national and european interests. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ the text aims to set a framework for pollutant emissions from medium combustion plants, those between small plants covered by directive 2009/125/ec (so-called 'eco-design') and large combustion plants, which are covered by directive 2010/75/eu (the 'industrial emissions' directive). the aim of this text is therefore to fill a certain legislative gap and to contribute to the reduction of pollution by nitrogen oxides, sulphur dioxide and dust. regulatory changes are the responsibility of the member states and the burden on industry. despite an apparently laudable objective, it imposes standards outside the commission's purview for a very risky environmental and public health benefit. this text is contrary to the national interest and the general european interest and cannot be supported.
in writing. this report on the limitation of emissions of certain pollutants into the atmosphere aims to fill a legislative gap and to contribute to the reduction of nitrogen oxide pollution. the average combustion plant is used in a wide range of applications. they are located between the small and the large thermal installations. the text imposes new constraints on member states, on the application of a stricter emission limit in areas which do not comply with european air quality standards, etc. most of these measures, devised by the most technocratish brains in the commission, will certainly have a negative impact on industry, while the environmental benefits seem to be very small... i therefore decided to vote against this absolutely harmful text which would pollute the legal environment of national industries.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the regulation of emissions from combustion plants with an output of between 1 and 50 mw. it introduces more flexibility than the european commission's original proposal, by requiring different schemes and application deadlines depending on the size of the industrial units. the report recommends that emission limits apply from 2025 for existing installations between 5 and 50 mw, and from 2030 for those between 1 and 5 mw. it proposes that certain installations, including district heating systems, biomass units, those in isolated areas and overseas territories, and specific installations linked to a national natural gas transmission network, be exempted until 2030. the text also proposes that in areas where air quality standards are not met, member states should consider applying stricter limits to installations. the aim is to harmonise operating conditions in the eu and to fight for environmental protection while maintaining the flexibility needed to avoid putting energy companies at risk.
in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal for a directive which aims to improve air quality in europe. by setting maximum emission limits for the most harmful pollutants for health and the environment (sulphur dioxide, nitrogen dioxide and co2) from medium-sized combustion plants, this directive aims to strengthen health and safety standards for plants which until now have depended solely on national standards. this harmonization is therefore a real health breakthrough in europe.

in writing. ‒ in order to achieve the 2030 climate targets, the union is trying to reduce air pollution by limiting emissions from certain pollutants. the european parliament adopted a resolution on the regulation of emissions from medium-sized combustion plants (from 1 to 50 mw). i voted in favour of this text and i would like to stress the flexibility offered by this agreement. the text proposes different schemes depending on the size of the industrial installations. the text also includes exemptions until 2030 for certain types of installations such as district heating systems or installations linked to biomass.
in writing. ‒ even if this text is less ambitious than what environmentalists advocate, it will put an end to the european legal vacuum in this area. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the emission limits for large combustion plants are respected, but not for medium combustion plants such as those used to produce electricity, heat or steam for industrial purposes. the member states had made very lax proposals to limit emissions, but environmentalists fought to improve the text. we have gotten measures to be taken to increase the energy efficiency of these facilities.
in writing. ‒ at present, emissions of air pollutants from medium combustion plants i.e. electricity generators or heating systems for domestic or industrial use are not regulated at eu level, unlike small and large plants. these plants produce large quantities of sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and dust. in total, some 143 000 installations are affected in the european union. that is why i voted in favour of the resolution to limit emissions from medium combustion plants. with more than 400 000 deaths a year attributed to air pollution, and with its considerable environmental impact and economic damage, action is urgently needed to ensure better air quality for european citizens. and while the ceilings are ambitious, we call on member states to introduce stricter limits in areas that do not meet european air quality standards.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which sets emission limits for two pollutants from medium-sized combustion plants (1 to 50 mw): sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxide. the text makes it possible, in particular, to fill the european legal vacuum in the field of medium combustion plants, since the commission's initial proposal did not regulate them. it should also be noted that the commission will have to take into account the results of its study on carbon monoxide, which is subject to monitoring. the report thus makes progress in the control of certain pollutants in the atmosphere.
in writing. ‒ while pollutant emissions from small and large combustion appliances are covered by european legislation, there is a legal vacuum on medium combustion appliances. these devices, with a power of between 1 and 50 mw, are numerous in our daily lives, for example as electrical generators or domestic and residential heating systems. the epp rapporteur wanted to lower the ambitions of the european commission, but the socialists fought back and 150 000 appliances will have to meet new ecological requirements. on the eve of cop 21 in paris, i therefore voted in favour of this report, to enable the european commission to propose binding legislation quickly, which will enable us to continue to achieve our objectives in terms of reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

in writing. ‒ the report proposes to limit greenhouse gas emissions from medium combustion plants, i.e. those with a thermal output of between 1 and 50 mw. this category has not been covered by european standards until now, although it is a major source of gas emissions and concerns nearly 150 000 installations in the european union used for domestic or industrial purposes. i regret that the text has not been able to impose lower emission thresholds as we would have liked, but it is important to continue to set limits for new installations such as these. i also regret certain parts of the directive concerning the exclusion of the outermost regions, in particular the french overseas departments. the retreat of the french and spanish right wing, justified by so-called technical problems in the implementation of these standards, is entirely reprehensible. this excludes a large proportion of european citizens and the territories on which they live from the protection of nature and fragile ecosystems. i am voting for this directive, however, because its aim is to reduce emissions of polluting gases and it allows the european parliament to send a new signal a few weeks before cop 21.
in writing. ‒ the report recommends changing the maximum milk fat content of dietary acid casein (from 2.25% to 2%) and the maximum moisture content of dietary casein (from 10% to 12%). these changes will be required by producers and actors in the agri-food sector. the commission said that these changes would improve the competitiveness of european producers, who would then be placed on a 'level playing field on the world market'. the report also confirms the intention to delegate to the commission the power to adopt acts which will enable the regulation to be adapted rapidly to 'international standards and future technical progress (sic) '. in the context of the obscure negotiations of the itcp, it is recommended to oppose attempts to align with international standards that are strongly subject to the commercial purposes of globalist institutions. i therefore opposed this report.

in writing. ‒ this report on caseins and caseinates intended for human consumption is intended to harmonise and update the regulations on certain lactoproteins used in the production of foodstuffs intended for human consumption. the report proposes two main changes to the maximum moisture content of dietary casein (from 10% to 12%) and the maximum milk fat content of dietary acid casein (from 2.25% to 2%). however, this development should allow for alignment with international standards, such as those described in the codex alimentarius, the provisions of which should not, however, be a barrier to world trade. the commission also mentions the competitiveness gains of this directive for producers and the report finally confirms the willingness to delegate to the commission the power to adopt acts. the support for global harmonisation is therefore stronger here, especially as the eu trade policies on which it is based generally lead to a downward revision of food safety standards (especially with the uncertain future of the ptci negotiations). i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ this report recommends harmonising the regulations on the use of certain lactoproteins in the agri-food industry. the rapporteur proposes to increase the maximum moisture content of casein from 10% to 12% and to lower the maximum milk fat content of casein from 2.25% to 2%. these measures are part of the european commission's desire to align itself with international standards which are designed to protect the consumer but which must not in any way restrict trade. the aim of the european institutions is to increase the competitiveness of agri-food players before the ratification of the transatlantic trade and investment partnership, which will exacerbate competition with us firms. we therefore oppose this text, the adoption of which will lead to a lowering of food standards to the detriment of the consumer. that is why i voted against this text.

republic cannot consistently ignore the interests of france. it is not in france's interest to submit blindly to a policy decided in berlin, brussels or washington. it is in his interest and your duty in writing. ‒ the purpose of this directive is to make online payments more secure within the eu member states. to this end, it is proposed to open the market to two new payment service providers (psps), namely account servicing psps and third party psps. the text as a whole attaches particular importance to consumer protection. however, with regard to third party psps, there are still some uncertainties regarding the confidentiality and exploitation of information collected by the provider. for this reason, i have decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which aims to make online payments safer by establishing data protection and liability rules for all online payment service providers.
in writing. ‒ the aim of this directive, which has been under discussion for a year and a half, is to make payments via the internet or mobile devices safer and cheaper within the union by opening up the market to two new payment service providers (psps), account servicing psps (aspsps) and third party psps (tp-psps). the text imposes transparency and information requirements on these payment service providers. finally, the announced objective is to increase security by extending the so-called strong authentication requirement to online payments. however, the problem remains the legal vacuum surrounding the third party psps. no details are given on the confidentiality and use of information collected by third party psps when collecting consolidated information on the various accounts held by the payer or when initiating payment with the account holder psp. that's why i abstained.
in writing. the aim of this directive, which has been under discussion for a year and a half, is to make payments via the internet or mobile devices safer and cheaper within the union by opening up the market to two new payment service providers (psps), account servicing psps (aspsps) and third party psps (tp-psps). the expected effect is a reduction in transaction costs while increasing the level of security of online payments. the text also imposes transparency and information requirements on psps. the text thus benefits consumers as a whole. however, this directive creates third party payment service providers, which will be able to initiate payments at the request of the payer without holding the funds concerned. furthermore, the problem remains the legal vacuum surrounding third party psps. no details are given on the confidentiality and use of the information collected. so i decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ the aim of this proposal is to make online payments in the european union more secure and less costly for customers. the report also calls for the introduction of a european standardisation body to ensure that the european union's standards are complied with. they will be responsible for making payments at the request of customers. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of electronic money, which is a key element of the eu's financial services. consumers are protected in the event of theft, loss or misappropriation of the payment instrument within 8 weeks of the transaction. however, the legal vacuum surrounding the activity of the psps, especially on the exploitation of the data collected, leaves me skeptical. these providers will have at their disposal the means of authenticating customers, which undermines their confidentiality. if the report's objective is to secure online payments, why don't they better regulate the activity of third party psps? i have abstained on this text to denounce this inconsistency.
in writing. ‒ the revision of the payment services directive in the internal market will further de-fragment the european market for payment services. in order to ensure the smooth functioning of the internal market, it is imperative that payments be made as quickly and efficiently as possible. the revised directive will reduce the costs of this fragmentation, estimated at around eur 130 billion per year. payments will be cheaper and more secure. this will also allow for the emergence of new players, which will foster greater innovation capacity, for example for online payments. i voted in favour of this new directive.
in writing. ‒ this report aims to create an integrated payments market across the union, complementing the existing legal framework. these provisions aim to reduce the costs of payment services by encouraging competition in the sector and promoting innovation, including through mobile and online payment methods. supporting these objectives and considering that users' banking data will be better protected during transactions, i supported this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on payment services in the internal market. i believe it is important to ensure free competition between all categories of payment service providers. this will increase choice, efficiency, transparency and security of payments.
in writing. ‒ the report aims to make online payments safer and cheaper by opening up the market to payment service providers who can pay without owning the funds, but still have the information on the accounts in question. however, no guarantees are given as to the use of data by third party payment service providers and the protection of personal banking information. this new possibility, as interesting as it may be, may leave a significant legal gap. it is not conceivable to open such a loophole in the exploitation of personal data. as a supporter of freedom of enterprise and innovation, i remain convinced that the issue of personal data protection is one that cannot be ignored by a politician. the european union cannot once again implement new mechanisms at the discretion of the market without examining the problems that may arise. that's why i opposed it.
in writing. ‒ i abstained on this debate because there is a legal vacuum with regard to third countries and the security of payments is not really guaranteed.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this directive is to secure online payments made within the member states. in this context, it is proposed to open the market to two new payment service providers (psps), namely account servicing psps and third party psps. the text as a whole is very much concerned with consumer protection. however, with regard to third party psps, some provisions remain unclear, particularly as regards confidentiality and the use of information collected by the provider. so i refrained.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by my colleague antonio tajani on payment services. the vote validates the agreement reached with the european commission and the council, which allows for increased security of transactions and reduced costs. payment service providers will be required to adopt secure authentication technologies, ensure that personal data is passed through secure channels and that it is only shared with the user's consent and in the smallest possible way. the report was adopted by a large majority, which i welcome.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which makes it possible to adapt consumer payments to new forms of payment (mobile, electronic). the aim of the text is to promote the efficiency of the payment system as a whole and to offer consumers greater choice, while ensuring data and payment protection and imposing the obligation to inform consumers of their rights.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on payment services in the internal market. in recent years, the european payments market has undergone major and profound technical changes. in order to support growth in europe, it is necessary to accompany these technical innovations by offering new payment services adapted to current needs. i therefore supported this proposal for a directive to enable citizens, consumers, entrepreneurs and traders to benefit from a wider range of payment services, the security and transparency of which will be enhanced.
in writing. ‒ in recent years, online payments have undergone profound changes. until recently, they were exclusively organised by banking operators. now other players are taking advantage of the emergence of new payment techniques to penetrate the market. this is why the european legislator has committed itself to giving this development a legal scope. the new payment services directive (psd2), on which parliament delivered its opinion at the last plenary session, is precisely intended to regulate these new practices, which have been adopted by many european companies. i therefore voted for the tajani report to give a strong support to these regulatory efforts. i am convinced that legislation is needed in this area, but i want to remain vigilant: the new provisions must at all times protect european citizens, and in particular their personal data. innovation can and must contribute to the well-being of our societies, but to do so it must be accompanied by strong safeguards in the public interest.
in writing. ‒ the proposal aims to repeal the current payment services directive (psd). the aim is to extend the scope of this directive in order to improve the functioning of the internal market for payment services. with the emergence of new types of payment services and the rapid growth of electronic and mobile payments, the retail payments market has experienced significant technical innovations that are challenging the current legislative framework. by facilitating transactions within the union, the commission hopes to foster growth. low consumption has little to do with means of payment. it is more a question of increasing the income available to individuals. the text nevertheless proposes to strengthen control of payment institutions in order to combat money laundering and terrorist financing. particular attention shall also be paid to the shareholders of payment institutions. to encourage this, i vote for but not enthusiastically.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this directive is to make online payments more secure within the eu member states. to this end, it is proposed to open the market to two new payment service providers (psps), namely account servicing psps and third party psps. the text as a whole attaches particular importance to consumer protection. however, with regard to third party psps, there are still some uncertainties regarding the confidentiality and exploitation of information collected by the provider. for this reason, i abstained.
in writing. the vote aims to adopt a new payment services directive to open up the market to new players. the expected effect is a reduction in transaction costs coupled with an increase in the level of security of online payments. however, this directive creates a new category of third party payment service providers, which will be able to initiate payments at the request of the payer without holding the funds concerned. uncertainty remains about the processing of information by these new actors. so i decided to abstain.

in writing. ‒ on 4 october 2010, the rupture of a waste reservoir in hungary led to the release of nearly one million cubic metres of highly alkaline red mud, caused flooding in several villages, killed ten people, injured nearly 150 and polluted large areas of land, including four natura 2000 sites. this is the worst industrial disaster in hungary in decades. as we mark the fifth anniversary of this tragic accident, it is important to recall how responsible management of industrial sites and better disaster prevention are essential to preventing such accidents from happening again. that is why i did not hesitate to support this resolution, which reminds us of our responsibility as legislators in ecological and environmental matters.
in writing. ‒ five years ago, hungary was facing the dramatic consequences of a ruptured waste tank. red mud from alumina and aluminum had caused the death of ten people. today, parliament was considering a legislative framework to prevent such a disaster. more concretely, this issue raises the need for a stronger grip of public authorities at union level. the community administration is using this sad anniversary as a pretext to tighten the screws on its control. although article 15 calls on 'member states to strengthen their national environmental inspection bodies', this possibility was immediately mired in a torrent of calls for strengthening at community level. that is why i voted against it.

in writing. ‒ on 4 october 2010, the collapse of a waste tank in hungary released nearly one million cubic metres of highly alkaline red mud containing aluminium, which flooded several villages, killed ten people, injured nearly 150 and polluted large areas of land, including four natura 2000 sites. five years later, the european parliament seized the opportunity to call for better prevention of industrial disasters, including those linked to mining waste and waste in general. it called on all member states with red mud pools to examine whether it had been correctly classified as hazardous and to revise all permits based on erroneous classifications. the resolution also calls for legislation on access to justice in environmental matters, the establishment of a 'european system for risk-sharing in the event of industrial plant disasters' and better application of the polluter-pays principle. it called for greater emphasis on research and for sufficient resources to be provided in the member states to inspect industrial sites. although the industry has sought to minimize its costs in terms of site security by influencing right-wing mps, i vote in favour.

in writing. ‒ in 2010, a ruptured waste tank in hungary led to the release of nearly one million cubic metres of highly alkaline red mud. the mud flooded several villages, killing 10 people and injuring 150. they have caused extensive damage and pollution to large areas of land, including four natura 2000 sites. i voted in favour of this resolution which pays tribute to the victims and calls on the european union to draw lessons from this disaster. in particular, member states are asked to take account of the classification of red sludge as hazardous waste within the meaning of directive 91/689/eec and to monitor existing basins. i believe it is important to set safety requirements for the management of waste from the extractive industry, to ensure its safety. it should be remembered, however, that the transposition of the environmental liability directive has not resulted in equal responsibilities in all member states. care should therefore be taken not to impose additional administrative and financial burdens on companies located in countries where strict standards are already applied.

in writing. ‒ the resolution seeks to demonstrate that no serious lessons have been drawn from this disaster. again, as is too often the case in industrial accidents, the repair and compensation are paid for by public money and not by the industrialists responsible for the disaster. this is why the european parliament has asked the european commission to propose new harmonised rules requiring manufacturers to provide sufficient financial security to ensure that the polluter pays principle can be fully applied. the commission should also put in place inspection requirements which could be coordinated at european level to avoid conflicts of national interests. all member states have a duty, even in times of austerity, to properly finance the authorities responsible for industrial inspections in order to avoid an accident and to enforce the rules in force. the same applies to the bodies responsible for measuring the toxicity of industrial waste and the solutions for its treatment.
