in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on the application of the directive on the implementation of equal opportunities and equal treatment of men and women in matters of employment and occupation. the text calls on the european commission to revise the european legislative framework in order to strengthen and make more effective the directive aimed at ending pay discrimination based on sex. i particularly supported the provisions calling on member states to make efforts to make services available to pregnant women or mothers that can help them not to have to choose between work and family life.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by my colleague anna zaborska. this report concerns the application of directive 2006/54/ec, which consolidates and modernises the union acquis in this field by merging the previous directives. the european parliament has consistently called for stronger action to improve the implementation of equal pay provisions at european level in the past and adopted resolutions to this effect in 2008 and 2012. in her report, ms zaborska stressed that member states had, in general, brought their legislation into line with eu legislation. however, it draws attention to the fact that, as things stand, transposition has proved insufficient to allow full implementation and enforcement, as a large wage gap continues to exist. the aim is to address important remaining problems such as: adequate and uniform assessment of work, the application of equal treatment provisions in relation to pension schemes, effective control systems, the role of the social partners and access to legal aid for victims of discrimination.
in writing. this own-initiative report proposes a reform of directive 2006/54/ec of the european parliament and of the council on the implementation of the principles of equal opportunities and equal treatment of men and women in matters of employment and occupation. the fact that the wage gap has remained unchanged or even widened since the implementation of the directive and the ineffectiveness of the principles of equal pay enshrined in the texts make this reform necessary in order to strengthen the guarantees of full application. to this end, the proposed measures aim in particular to harmonise the definitions of key terms of equal pay, or to establish financial penalties for undertakings which fail to comply with these principles. i vote for it.
in writing. ‒ the zaborska report on equal opportunities for men and women in employment and occupation aims to take stock of the progress of directive 2006/54/ec on this subject. although this text may appear to be well-oriented in view of the stated objective of ensuring equal pay for equal work and combating undignified pensions, it is undermined by communitarian demands of various kinds and puts forward proposals for measures which are too restrictive for the employer, thus risking endangering the freedom of enterprise as it exists in france. france is also one of the few countries which have already applied the original directive; the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for adoption by the end of the year. i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. i abstained on this report, although i strongly support equality between men and women in all areas. however, the text of the report contains a number of measures which are ineffective and may, in addition, end up being used against women themselves. as an example, i would mention the proposals for mandatory quotas for the representation of women and men on boards. these measures really don't help women.
in writing. ‒ equal opportunities for men and women in employment is a political priority for me, and we must take all the necessary decisions to achieve this. these measures must be effective and appropriate to the objective pursued. i do not want europe to interfere in matters where it has no place. these positions, which are being defended by some of my colleagues, do not in any way respect the principle of subsidiarity. that's why i abstained on some passages.
in writing. ‒ i supported this resolution which aims to strengthen european legislation on equal opportunities and equal treatment between men and women in employment and work. this equality is provided for in the european directive 2006/54/ec. however, its implementation in the member states does not seem to be sufficient: the gender pay gap in the union averages 16.4%; employment rates are generally lower for women; the differences in pension levels remain significant. the implementation of the 2006 directive needs to be strengthened and genuine equality of opportunity and treatment between men and women needs to be established, by reducing pay gaps, increasing women's economic independence, improving women's access to the labour market, establishing equality in decision-making processes or eliminating discriminatory structures and practices. for those who still doubt it, let us remember that this institution will have major positive effects for the benefit of society as a whole.
in writing. ‒ while the text is a priori well oriented (ensuring equal pay for equal work, avoiding undignified pensions, etc.), it is undermined by lgbt and ethnic minority communitarian demands and proposals for measures incompatible with the freedom of enterprise, the cradle of employment. france is also one of the few countries to have applied the original directive. the lack of enforcement by other countries should not be exploited to add constraints which are neither useful nor within the union's remit, such as the social policy of entrepreneurs. i voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ inequality between women and men in the labour market remains a sad reality. this is despite a large body of legislation, the principle of equal pay having been enshrined in the treaties since the beginning of european integration and transposed into european law by the 2006 directive on equal opportunities and equal treatment. the revision of this directive is therefore necessary, in particular in order to create truly binding instruments capable of effectively combating discrimination. the report proposes a series of measures to improve pay transparency and combat discrimination in pension schemes. i welcome the fact that there are provisions to combat gender stereotypes, and that the deconstruction of these stereotypes from an early age is a necessity, despite the opposition of the right and the far right. worse still, i have seen that the far right, particularly the fn, have almost systematically rejected measures promoting equality between men and women, including in social matters, in the name of rejecting any binding european provision. however, there is an urgent need to implement binding measures to combat such discrimination. that is why i voted for it.

in writing. ‒ the visa information system (vis), established in 2004, was designed to strengthen european cooperation on the issue of control at the external borders of the union. by creating a common fingerprint database, the vis was supposed to facilitate visa application procedures and strengthen controls. this resolution was then more a technical formality than anything else. however, there is a need to address this visa information system, especially in view of the unprecedented levels of illegal migration faced by member states. the usefulness of the vis is indeed relative, since the states no longer have control over the borders, although, for example, controls were reintroduced in hungary as a result of the schengen agreements, which are clearly not effective. it is important, despite the apparent vacuity of this resolution, to do everything possible to combat the dogma of absolute freedom of movement in the face of the constant risk of terrorism. that is why i voted in favour of this resolution.

in writing. ‒ france will host and chair the 21st conference of the parties to the united nations framework convention on climate change 2015 (cop21/cmp11), also known as paris 2015 , from 30 november to 11 december 2015. it is a crucial deadline, as it must lead to a new international climate agreement. i voted for the pargneaux report because i want to see an international agreement that is binding on the greatest number of people, and in particular on the countries that are the biggest emitters. but this agreement will have to be realistic. indeed, just because there is an agreement in paris does not mean that we will have found the solution to climate change and its accompanying disruptions (floods, hurricanes, droughts) that we are observing more and more frequently. i also think it is important not to stigmatise certain sectors, such as agriculture. instead, we must work together to find viable solutions. the summit can only be considered a success if we get concrete solutions and binding commitments.

mr president, today, 27 october 2015, the european parliament is going to dedicate a new freedom, net neutrality. the stakes are high. it is about allowing every internet user, rich or poor, to access the site of their choice without discrimination, from the smallest personal blog to the largest websites of multinational companies. this equality of access to the internet is necessary. it is regrettable that the text before us is unclear. if it were to be voted on as it stands, it could lead to an outrageous filtering of content on the internet that would compromise citizens' ability to get information. i shall therefore support the amendments which seek to avoid this risk. the federal communications commission guaranteed net neutrality in the united states on february 26, 2015, and the u.s. government has since announced that it will not interfere with the internet. the european parliament must prove today that it is capable of doing the same for europe.
the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the following areas: mr president, we are about to adopt a basic regulation with two titles: firstly, the end of homelessness. in june 2017, after years of gradual capping, it will be the end of the tariff surcharges for those of our fellow citizens who cross borders, and i am not just thinking of those who are lucky enough to travel, but also those who travel across borders for professional reasons. i am thinking in particular of frontier workers, and this is a remarkable achievement. the second fundamental element is the incorporation of the net neutrality principles into our european legal corpus. i think this is a considerable step forward and i would like to respond to the concerns and criticisms that have been expressed about the outcome of the negotiations between parliament and the council. does this clearly enshrine a principle of neutral and non-discriminatory treatment of internet traffic? yes, it is. does this text open up obvious loopholes that would allow the principle of neutrality of internet access to be violated? i do not think so, although we can always write a clearer text ex abstracto. but is this possible gain in clarity worth the risk of putting all our achievements to the test? it is on this question, and on this question alone, that our differences will be expressed later. i will not take that risk, because we cannot reopen negotiations once they have been concluded, and at the same time tell the commission and the member states that we will be vigilant both on the implementation of this regulation and on the next texts already on the agenda.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report to amend the agreement between the european community and the swiss confederation providing for measures equivalent to those laid down in council directive 2003/48/ec on taxation of savings income in the form of interest payments. the decision will make it possible to subject switzerland to the same obligations as eu members but also to limit the possibility for taxpayers to evade their reporting obligations to the tax authorities. the report also proposes the exchange of information on income, account balances and proceeds from the sale of financial assets. tax transparency and the end of banking secrecy both within and outside the eu is a priority in order to safeguard tax revenues of the states.
in writing. ‒ the end of banking secrecy through the automatic exchange of information at the level of the eu countries, which was enacted in march 2014, had to overcome the reluctance of austria and luxembourg. one of the conditions for the abandonment of banking secrecy by these countries was the acceptance by switzerland of similar measures. following negotiations, a memorandum of understanding between the eu and switzerland was concluded, providing for the exchange of banking information within the framework of the standards proposed by the oecd at international level. as i am against capital flight, i voted in favour of the report on this protocol.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution which aims to make it more difficult for eu citizens to hide tax money in swiss bank accounts.
in writing. ‒ the end of banking secrecy through the automatic exchange of information at eu member state level, which was achieved in march 2014, required overcoming the reluctance of austria and luxembourg. one of the conditions for the abandonment of banking secrecy by these two member states was that switzerland should accept similar measures, in order not to create unfair competition. the memorandum of understanding, which is the subject of the kofod report, provides that the european union and switzerland will automatically exchange information on the financial accounts of their respective residents as of 1 january 2018. because i am in favour of fiscal transparency and therefore of the end of banking secrecy, in order above all to preserve france's tax revenues, i logically voted for this text: despite all the good i can think of the swiss confederation, which defends its identity and sovereignty, it is unthinkable to let a country practice banking secrecy at the gates of the eu, unless capital flight is perpetuated.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the eu, of the protocol amending the agreement between the european community and the swiss confederation providing for measures equivalent to those laid down in council directive 2003/48/ec on taxation of savings income in the form of interest payments. under this jumbled vocabulary is hidden a common sense measure that will guarantee member states to reduce their tax losses: this is an agreement between switzerland and the eu to ensure the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts. the principle of tax transparency and the end of banking secrecy are therefore anchored here, which should protect us in the future from all kinds of cahuzac business. the kofod report provides for some key measures, such as limiting the possibility for taxpayers to evade their reporting obligations to the tax authorities or the obligation for the states concerned to report not only on revenues but also on account balances and proceeds from the sale of financial assets. the vote was therefore in favour of this gradual end to tax impunity.
in writing. ‒ in order to convince the austrian and luxembourg authorities to ratify the agreement on the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts, which was signed in march 2014, the european union negotiated with the swiss government the end of bank secrecy, which created unfair tax competition in europe. the agreement with switzerland, which will take effect from 1 january 2018, provides for the automatic exchange of data between the member states of the union and the government of switzerland on income, account balances and capital gains on the sale of financial assets. these measures will considerably reduce the ability of europeans to evade taxation in their home countries and will enable member states to recover tax revenue owed to them. we are in favour of this cooperation, which will limit tax evasion in europe. that is why i voted for this text.
in writing. ‒ this report proposes to make the exchange of information in the tax field between switzerland and the european union automatic and compulsory, with the aim of making tax fraud and tax evasion more difficult. this agreement, which will come into force in 2018, mainly concerns information on bank accounts of swiss or european residents. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that tax fraud and tax evasion penalise european citizens by depriving the state of its means of action.
in writing. i supported this agreement between the european union and switzerland on the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts. strengthening our international cooperation is essential in the fight against crossborder tax fraud and evasion. it is therefore important that this agreement be in line with the latest international developments as developed by the organisation for economic co-operation and development (oecd).
in writing. ‒ the aim of this report was to enable the exchange of information on the financial income of non-residents between switzerland and the european union. by endorsing the automatic and mandatory nature of the transmission of information, this report is a real step forward. there are still too many problems of financial opacity linked to switzerland. there is a real need to enable member states to have accurate and automated tracking of information on the financial income of their nationals, without the latter being able to use the swiss system to evade it. in defence of financial transparency and the sovereignty of states over their nationals, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the end of banking secrecy through the automatic exchange of information at the level of the eu countries, which was enacted in march 2014, had to overcome the reluctance of austria and luxembourg. one of the conditions for the abandonment of banking secrecy by these countries was the acceptance by switzerland of similar measures. following negotiations, a memorandum of understanding between the eu and switzerland was concluded, providing for the exchange of banking information within the framework of the standards proposed by the oecd at international level. as i am against capital flight, i voted in favour of the report on this protocol.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which endorses a protocol to the eu-switzerland agreement to facilitate and make automatic the exchange of financial information.
in writing. ‒ this kofod report concerns the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the eu, of the protocol amending the agreement between the european community and the swiss confederation providing for measures equivalent to those laid down in council directive 2003/48/ec on taxation of savings income in the form of interest payments. the agreement therefore aims to ensure the exchange of information on the financial income of non-residents. even if the text contains shortcomings in terms of the level of information provided, the automatic and mandatory nature of the exchange of information and tax evasion, i voted in favour of this text, which is in the right direction.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this agreement with switzerland because it guarantees the exchange of information on financial accounts between residents of switzerland and the european union. it thus promotes tax transparency and helps to curb capital flight to switzerland.
in writing. ‒ the agreement, negotiated by the council on behalf of the european union, provides for the automatic exchange of information between switzerland and the european union (from 2018) concerning the financial accounts of their respective residents. this measure will apply, for example, to french residents holding an account in switzerland. the whole of the provisions of this text is part of a logic of fiscal transparency which i support. the end of banking secrecy will also help to stop the flight of our capital to the doorsteps of europe, to a country which does not practice this transparency. i voted for this report.
in writing. ‒ on 27 may 2015, the european union and switzerland signed an agreement on the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts, aimed at increasing tax cooperation and compliance at international level. the aim is to deal with situations where a taxpayer seeks to conceal capital corresponding to income or assets on which tax has not been paid. but the proposal does not require full and detailed disclosure of account holders' full name, surname and tax identification number. in other words, bank secrecy is maintained! the rapporteur welcomes the agreement, which does not require parliament's opinion to be implemented, but is timidly critical of this point. this is all a charade, i'm not doing it.
in writing. ‒ this agreement confirms the end of banking secrecy in switzerland as of 1 january 2018, already enacted in march 2014 at eu level. this was done despite the reluctance of austria and luxembourg. one of the conditions these countries imposed was that switzerland should accept similar measures, so as not to create unfair competition. switzerland will apply measures equivalent to those provided for in the european texts (revised directive 2003/48/ec). it will thus comply with the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts as required by the oecd global standards in 2014. the information to be exchanged will also cover not only income (interest, dividends) but also account balances and proceeds from the sale of financial assets, which significantly limits the remaining possibilities of tax evasion. this agreement is therefore to be welcomed.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text on package travel and assisted travel. developments in the travel market, in particular the growing trend of online bookings, called for the adaptation of the directive which dates from 1990. the new directive broadens the definition of package travel to include most travel bookings with different elements (flight, hotel booking, car rental, etc.). it includes 'connected services' for which the user's data is automatically collected between the different stages of the booking by one or more companies with commercial links. the voted provisions will allow travellers who buy package holidays online to benefit from the same protection as those purchased from a travel agency. in addition, it will be possible to cancel a package for free if the price of the package increases by more than 8% or if "inevitable" events such as natural disasters or terrorist attacks strike the destination. three nights must also be offered to the holidaymaker if exceptional and unavoidable circumstances prevent repatriation.

in writing. ‒ the report in question is a european parliament recommendation on the regulation on the regulation of the activities of internet service providers and the end of roaming charges within the union. in this recommendation, parliament reiterated the council's position. two aspects are worth highlighting: 1. part of the text aims to abolish roaming charges, which are surcharges imposed on consumers when they make calls from abroad. i voted in favour of their abolition from 2017, with the understanding that consumers will not be able to abuse them by purchasing subscriptions in a member state where they are not resident and where those subscriptions are cheaper. the abolition of roaming charges is accompanied by exceptions which will allow operators to limit their use so that they are not penalised; 2. another part of the text is supposed to defend "net neutrality". however, in many respects this is not respected. access providers will be able to discriminate between encrypted and unencrypted files, between online tv and other video platforms, etc. i therefore voted in favour of the amendments which guarantee net neutrality.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it seeks to ban mobile roaming charges and fair access to the internet. i welcome the vote on this measure, which has been requested for many years by european citizens. it's about time!
in writing. ‒ as regards the second reading, there was no final vote on the text itself, only on the amendments. the overall objective is to review the regulation on the regulation of the activities of internet service providers and, in particular, to end mobile internet roaming charges in the union, which is a good thing. however, the first aspect of the regulation is rightly disputed by many consumer associations. it allows access providers to grant preferential paid streams to businesses. national regulators will have very little room for manoeuvre against this practice. this therefore challenges the principle of "net neutrality" which requires that all flows and speed of access to all sites be treated without discrimination. i therefore voted in favour of all the amendments which were intended to guarantee this neutrality, but which were ultimately rejected by the votes of the epp and s&d members, that is to say by the european union of socialists and democrats...

in writing. ‒ the report is about the revision of the regulation on the regulation of the activities of internet service providers and the end of mobile internet roaming charges in the eu. the text will give providers the possibility to grant companies better internet access. the proposal therefore calls into question the principle of 'net neutrality' according to which all flows and access speeds must be treated without discrimination. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to cover the whole of the european union, including the european union's maritime transport sector. this will result in horizontal market concentration, leading to a reduction in the number of players to the detriment of consumers' purchasing power. i therefore voted against the rejection of the council's proposal.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the creation of a single european market for electronic communications. this text will allow the total elimination of roaming charges from 2017. the cost of telephone communications from one member state to another will then be similar to the cost of national communications. it was the european parliament which, in negotiations with the member states, insisted on the abolition of roaming charges. this regulation directly benefits european citizens and is a major step towards the creation of a coherent and efficient single market.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of adopting the draft regulation on the single market for electronic communications at second reading. i believe that this text represents an ambitious reform of electronic communications. among the provisions in this text, i welcome the abolition of telephone surcharges for calls within europe. the end of roaming will change our communication habits considerably and make it a little easier for citizens to move freely in our common space. as regards net neutrality, i think the text strikes a satisfactory balance, since it allows the development of innovative services while introducing a binding principle for operators and well-defined traffic management rules. in general, this reform will only be fully satisfactory if it is followed by measures to deploy broadband in the union and, above all, to rethink the liability regime for digital platforms. only such a framework will ensure fair competition between all digital market players.
in writing. ‒ this legislative report proposes to ban roaming charges for the use of mobile phones abroad (voice, sms/mms or data) from june 2017. a transitional period has been agreed from april 2016 to june 2017, during which the charges will not exceed €0.05 per minute for voice calls, €0.02 for sms (text messages) and €0.05 per megabyte for mobile internet use. the report also clarifies the rules on the right to access the internet, prohibiting providers from blocking or slowing down access to internet content, applications or services, unless a court decision allows it or if the decision is aimed at preventing network congestion or fighting cyber attacks. the single market for electronic communications is a vital step towards completing the internal market and facilitating the daily life and mobility of citizens in europe, and i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the adoption of this text by the european parliament completes an important first step towards a single european market for electronic communications. i supported this text, which illustrates the europe of the great projects, the europe we support and encourage. the end of roaming charges, as of 15 june 2017, is one of the flagship measures of this legislation. this measure will then directly benefit european citizens by allowing them to use their mobile phones at no extra cost when travelling in other member states of the european union.
in writing. ‒ it is essential that the union progresses towards the completion of a genuine single telecommunications market. roaming charges and the difficulties of accessing content on the internet from one member state to another are obstacles faced every day by european citizens travelling within the union. this also affects trade between member states. the agreement reached between the european parliament and the council is a good compromise. roaming charges will end in 2017 and the principle of net neutrality is enshrined in the text of the compromise. the european union will have to ensure that the regulation is properly applied by the member states, but it will also have to go further in creating a 'connected continent'.

in writing. ‒ net neutrality is one of the founding principles of the internet, according to which data exchanged on the internet, as well as users, must be treated equally. in practical terms, an isp cannot restrict access to certain sites or favour others by modulating connection speeds. the same logic applies to their customers. the proposed text creates loopholes in this principle, which cannot tolerate any ambiguity. he suggests three cases in which an isp could circumvent this principle: court order, defence against cyber attacks, and traffic management. the commission considers that the measure is selective because it does not comply with the requirements of article 107 (1) tfeu. the internet should instead be seen as a universal service, like the post office, so necessary today for everyday tasks, such as administrative or civic procedures. that is why i have supported all the amendments which have sought to restore the force of this principle.

in writing. ‒ the luxleaks scandal revealed that many multinationals have benefited from ultra-advantageous tax arrangements in luxembourg through highly paid audit firms. tax dumping, such as in luxembourg, switzerland and ireland, has deprived many member states of considerable tax revenues. the commission has therefore put forward a proposal for a directive aimed at introducing the automatic exchange of information between national tax administrations. the purpose of this proposal is to discourage large groups from using these processes. this text is again in the right direction. nevertheless, we regret that the ecofin council has abandoned the idea of retroactivity in data exchanges. the entry into force of the new legislation has been postponed, thus giving the legal services of multinational firms the opportunity to adapt their tax optimisation methods to the new european legislation. finally, although it helps to intensify the exchange of information between member states, the directive does not provide a better framework for the tax practices of these unscrupulous companies. i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ the recent tax scandals in europe have revealed many flaws in european taxation. the lack of transparency in this area has led to unfair competition and is a hindrance to the completion of an effective single market. the first victims are the european citizens and smes. it was time to work towards greater cooperation and transparency in tax matters. the mandatory and automatic exchange of information on cross-border tax rulings is a first step in this direction. the agreement will reduce the tendency for member states to engage in unfair tax competition. of course, particular care will have to be taken to ensure that member states comply with this legislation. i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ this report proposes the european parliament's negative opinion on the council of ministers' decision to maintain a low level of transparency in tax matters. this decision applies in particular to the tax rescript, which is a procedure allowing citizens and businesses to obtain from the administration their situation with regard to tax law. the council of ministers restricted the scope of the text to crossborder orders and limited the european commission's power of control. parliament wants to make it automatic and compulsory to exchange information on cross-border tax rulings issued by multinational companies. i have supported this report because i believe that this decision is a missed opportunity to strengthen the fight against tax evasion between member states.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which aims to guarantee an automatic exchange of information on advance tax rulings taken in respect of tax fraud. it is important that the european union takes strong measures to strengthen its fight against tax fraud and tax evasion. i am particularly in favour of the european commission being able to impose sanctions in the event of non-compliance with this legislation.
in writing. ‒ the report sought to enable the establishment of an automatic exchange of tax data between member states' administrations. by encouraging the states to avoid abusing procedures which create a fiscal competitiveness gap, this report is moving in the right direction. although a more watered-down version is certainly welcome (this parliament report is only for opinion), it is important to fight against all forms of tax or paralegal fraud, and this report is a good example of this. i voted in favour of this report because i want taxpayers and businesses to be more honest.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report in the interests of transparency and efficiency. the text will make it possible to set up an automatic exchange of information between the member states on advance tax rulings in respect of tax arrangements which, in particular, allow them to be taxed at a lower rate.
in writing. ‒ the ferber report is on the proposal for a council directive amending directive 2011/16/eu as regards the mandatory automatic exchange of information in the field of taxation. the text follows the luxleaks scandal over tax evasion by large companies in luxembourg with the approval of the luxembourg authorities (it should be recalled that mr juncker, the current president of the commission, was the country's finance minister and prime minister for more than 25 years). it is intended that the directive, and therefore the compulsory exchange of information, should apply to all advance tax rulings, whereas the commission is content with advance cross-border rulings and advance pricing arrangements. the commission (which, it should be recalled, is headed by a person who we have every reason to believe was aware of the luxembourg situation) is also proposing that this compulsory exchange should not be retroactive, when parliament wants to apply it to all agreements and rulings still in force today. the text is a step forward in the commission's less-talky stance and echoes the oecd's stance on tax evasion. so i decided to vote for it.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report because it introduces an automatic exchange of information in tax matters. it thus marks progress in the fight against fiscal dumping by certain european states, notably luxembourg.
in writing. - i voted for this text. it aims to bring about full transparency on tax rulings and similar measures. this will discourage governments and companies from using it excessively. the entry into force of this directive has been postponed, which will give some member states (luxembourg, ireland, the netherlands) time to terminate the most 'questionable' agreements. it is hoped that competition will eventually become more open, on rates alone.
in writing. ‒ in 2015, the european institutions finally won over to the renewed fiscal voluntarism: in february, the taxe special committee began its work; in march, the commission presents a first legislative proposal. the commission has also adopted a second directive in june, and at the same time a number of key directives are being revised. the commission has also concluded that the contested tax ruling is not imputable to luxopco. in practice, there was hardly any exchange of rescripts between administrations, which the ferber report aims to put an end to by introducing an automatic exchange of tax information. parliament has reached the most ambitious compromises on this text, which is essential in the face of the council, whose ambition is reduced by unanimity. parliament therefore reiterated its call for the widest possible cooperation: exchange of all remaining rescripts. in addition, it is essential that the commission has access to these exchanges of texts in order to carry out investigations if necessary. i voted in favour of this report because i want to make these demands, which we share in the committee on taxation, public.
in writing. ‒ advance tax rulings are information that the tax authorities give to taxpayers about the arrangements that will be applied to the calculation of their taxes. these decisions are made to provide legal certainty to taxpayers, often by confirming the tax treatment of a large or complex commercial transaction. it is the lack of transparency on these "case by case" tax decisions that allows large companies to artificially reduce their taxation, as seen in the luxleaks case. the text proposes to remedy this by making it compulsory to communicate these decisions to the commission by means of a quarterly report containing precise information. i regret that these reports are not made public and remain in the hands of the commission. nevertheless, it is in the direction of greater fiscal control and i am voting for it.
in writing. ‒ the luxleaks scandal gave rise to a proposal for a directive aimed at introducing the automatic exchange of tax returns or similar measures (validation of transfer prices, various arrangements) between member states' administrations. the idea is to have transparency on these practices, in order to discourage states and companies from using them excessively (fiscal dumping). the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of the environment against the risks arising from the use of certain substances. the exchange would be done retroactively, up to 10 years back for the rewrites, and their access would be extended. the ecofin council, meeting on 6 october, took a much less forceful position. it was the first version, with parliament issuing only an advisory opinion. the member states have thus abandoned retroactivity and have also delayed the entry into force of the directive, giving the most compromised members (luxembourg, ireland, the netherlands) time to terminate the most questionable agreements and present a polite image. the exchange is still a step forward in these often opaque practices. we must therefore support this report and deplore the fact that ecofin has so far strayed from it.

in writing. i am voting in favour of this report, which marks a significant step forward in the fight against tax evasion, fraud and tax havens. the commission proposes to approve the amendment of council directive 2011/16/eu on the automatic and compulsory exchange of information in the field of taxation. the new directive will make it possible to systematically exchange information on the advance tax returns drawn up by each member state, which may have a direct or indirect impact on the tax bases of other member states. the amendments would thus oblige member states to provide, on a quarterly basis, precise information on these returns, including in particular a description of the criteria used to set the tax transfer prices or a clear identification of the states likely to be concerned.

in writing. ‒ tax disparities between the member states of the european union, together with the free movement of capital and people, have encouraged the use of tax optimization and tax evasion by certain multinational firms. these practices are harmful to the public finances of the countries of the union and profoundly affect cohesion between the member states. it is enough to recall the 'luxleaks' scandal, where a member state was accused by the other member states of tax dumping for having benefited from these optimisations by introducing favourable taxation. while these practices are not always illegal, they are intolerable in the light of the values of the european union and the spirit of cooperation which ensues. that is why i have voted in favour of a directive on tax returns which would make it automatic and compulsory for the exchange of information in this field between the countries of the european union. this measure should restore transparency and strengthen the competitiveness of smes by taxing the added value of each actor where it is created.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which sets out the european parliament's position on the automatic and mandatory exchange of information in the tax field. tax fraud and tax evasion remain intolerable and a fair distribution of the tax burden between citizens and businesses must be found. unfortunately, the council did not wait for the european parliament to take a decision, since an agreement had already been reached in the council at the beginning of october; the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect, and it is worth noting that this agreement is less ambitious than the position adopted by the european parliament. for example, the european parliament wanted the scope of the directive to apply to all tax returns and not just to cross-border tax returns. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. we must continue these efforts in the area of tax transparency.
in writing. ‒ following the luxleaks scandal, pierre moscovici proposed a first package of measures to combat tax dumping. the main one is to make it compulsory to exchange information on tax returns including tax gifts between the member states and the commission, with a retroactive effect of 10 years. the council, at first reading, opted to reduce the retroactivity to five years and refused the commission access to this information, effectively depriving it of any capacity to investigate. the european parliament has reacted: in this report we propose that all tax returns in force be automatically and compulsorily placed on a platform accessible to the commission, without any retroactive criteria. i strongly support this report because the fight against tax dumping is a priority for me. favouring multinationals puts public finances and our social standards at risk. but we must go further by adopting a european tax on multinationals, the only instrument capable of putting an end to the race to the bottom in europe.
in writing. ‒ the luxleaks scandal gave rise to a proposal for a directive, presented in the spring by commissioner moscovici, to introduce the automatic exchange of information between member states' administrations on tax rescripts or similar measures they grant (validation of transfer or assembly prices). the idea is to have transparency on these practices, although most of them are legal, in order to discourage states and companies from using them excessively (tax dumping). i voted for the adoption of this text.

in writing. ‒ this motion for a resolution, drafted in haste by the main pro-european groups (epp, s&d, alde and greens/efa), is the european parliament's response to the volkswagen case. it is pleased that the amendment tabled by the greens and the radical left calling for the creation of a committee of inquiry has been rejected. another positive point is that the pollution thresholds for nitrogen oxide emissions, which were totally unrealistic, have been raised from 80 mg/km to 168 mg. however, this text contains several elements that run counter to the interests of the european automobile industry, which is already facing increased global competition. the tone of the proposal is moralising. co2 emissions are constantly denounced, even though their role in global warming (which is vastly overestimated) is far from scientifically proven. finally, the technical characteristics to be respected by manufacturers are decided in the interest of the power which defines them. it would therefore be appropriate for standards to remain the responsibility of the member states rather than the commission. finally, this proposal strengthens the union's powers and exaggerates the negative environmental impacts of diesel engines. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which condemns fraud by car manufacturers. i regret that millions of consumers have been misled or misled by false information about the emissions of their vehicles. i welcome the investigations under way in several member states and around the world, and i support the commission's call on national supervisory authorities to encourage them to carry out extensive checks on a wide variety of brands and vehicles.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this text which considers a strategic industrial issue from a purely ecological point of view in the context of a global trade war. the infringement by volkswagen is a real one, involving the emission of a pollutant, nitrogen dioxide (nox), while the diesel engines of the german car giant have indeed reduced emissions of carbon monoxide, a particle that oxidizes rapidly in the atmosphere to produce carbon dioxide. the text states the importance of choosing a product 'on the basis of the comprehensive and unbiased technical characteristics provided to it', whereas these characteristics are generally decided in the interests of the power which defines them. these characteristics are thus part of the non-tariff barriers that are at the heart of the ptci negotiations, and it so happens that the united states has reduced co2 emission rights to harm diesel engines. the scandal, which originated in the united states, undoubtedly serves the interests of our 'american partners' to the detriment of european manufacturers, who are leaders in the diesel engine industry. finally, this case is a lever to strengthen eu legislation and the commission's grip on a key part of european industry.
in writing. ‒ another motion for a resolution born of a political and media scandal and which, as a result, misses the strategic issue for the automotive industry. the resolution, following the volkswagen scandal, was based on a false premise: the diesel engines involved in the infringement had emitted more nitrogen dioxide than was permitted; however, the text argues that this endangers public health without taking into account that the cars concerned have, on the other hand, emitted less carbon monoxide, a much more harmful gas. the resolution also makes a mistake in criticising the choices of the european automobile industry and in asserting the need to rely on 'impartial' technical characteristics: it should be remembered that these technical characteristics constitute real non-tariff barriers, which are currently threatened by the united states, which, through ttip, wishes to impose its own standards to the detriment of its european competitors. since this resolution is intended to act on emotion and not in the interests of our industry, i have therefore voted against it.
in writing. ‒ the volkswagen scandal revealed that the german company had configured its diesel engines to evade nitrogen dioxide emission controls. this motion for a resolution deals with this offence only from an environmental point of view, whereas this is a strategic issue between two trading powers, germany and the united states. the text also fails to mention that this infringement limits the emission of carbon monoxide, a gas which is extremely harmful to the environment. finally, it is essential to understand that emission limits for pollutants constitute non-tariff barriers because they are biased by the arbitrary decisions of national authorities which cannot be impartial in this strategic sector. although i have no sympathy for the large groups who are constantly trying to circumvent national legislation, i do not think it is wise to leave the commercial aspect of this matter out of the question. the rapporteur also takes advantage of the situation to strengthen eu legislation to the detriment of the member states, which will lose autonomy in a sector of activity that is highly strategic in terms of jobs. i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on emission measurement in the automobile sector which i believe can pave the way for thorough investigations to shed light on the volkswagen case. i wholeheartedly support the call for a reinforced european emission control system and the application of real-world driving tests, which are essential for measuring all pollutants and urgent for all those who, like me, advocate an innovative and responsible european industry. the establishment of a european supervisory authority which would supervise the type-approval of vehicles by the national authorities is also necessary to safeguard itself independently against any attempts to infringe. finally, i welcome the european parliament's willingness not to condemn diesel technologies in a peremptory way. it was important to combine ambition with realism, at a time when europe is technologically ahead in clean diesel and many european citizens with modest incomes own diesel vehicles.
in writing. ‒ this legislative report revises national emission ceilings for certain pollutants to improve air quality and human health. the text introduces new limit values (such as sulphur dioxide, ultrafine particles or methane) from 2020 and 2030. it also proposes a binding 2025 interim target for all pollutants except ammonia. other measures include access to finance for air quality improvements and emission control programmes. there was much opposition, both on the level of ambition of the reduction targets for 2020, 2025 and 2030, and on the addition of new pollutants. since we do not currently have an effective technical or technological means of reducing the emissions of enteric methane (waste from livestock), i co-signed an amendment, the content of which was taken up by the plenary, to exclude these emissions from the directive, so as not to penalise the agricultural sector. i regret, however, that my amendments to protect small farms and to exclude ammonia were not adopted. i have nevertheless voted in favour of opening negotiations between the european parliament and the council, in support of the main objectives of this report.
in writing. following the volkswagen scandal, this text adopted by a large majority in the european parliament on emission measurements in the automobile sector condemns fraud by car manufacturers. i believe that consumer confidence must be restored quickly and that there must be a thorough investigation into cases of fraud in car emissions tests. it is not our job, however, to undermine the whole automobile sector, which is essential to the european economy, or to condemn the use of diesel for good.
in writing. ‒ a few weeks ago, the us environmental protection agency (epa) revealed a large-scale fraud by the volkswagen group. the german manufacturer has reportedly fitted some of its cars with software to conceal the real level of polluting gas emissions in the event of a check. the european commission will not only condemn such fraud, but also have to strengthen testing and controls to better protect consumers. moreover, i would like a committee of inquiry to be set up to shed light on what happened so that it does not happen again.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution. the automobile industry makes an immense contribution to the whole european economy, so the sector must not be the victim of fraud by a few. the fraud in car emissions tests must be thoroughly investigated and appropriate sanctions applied, but this must not be an opportunity to ideologically put diesel aside. while many of our citizens on low incomes drive diesel vehicles, europe has a real technological lead in terms of 'clean' diesel. we must therefore urgently bring the conditions of the type approval tests closer to the real driving conditions. the commission should also review the vehicle approval system and ensure that the approval and certificates issued by the competent national authorities can be independently verified and possibly reassessed by the commission and the member states.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament this week voted on a strong resolution following the revelations of the 'volkswagen scandal'. firstly, fraud in car emissions testing must be thoroughly investigated and appropriate sanctions applied. secondly, given the scale of the crisis, it is imperative that europe establishes real-life emissions tests that respect legal emission limits and are fully implemented. thirdly, parliament wants to be fully informed of the work being done by the european commission and the technical committee for motor vehicles (ctvm). finally, i regret that our request for a committee of inquiry did not receive a majority. it would have been an opportunity to make a mark, and above all to put the responsibility for clarifying matters in the hands of another body than the european commission.

in writing. ‒ whether or not to increase the number of judges at the european court of justice is not a trivial matter when we know that its case-law has done as much for community integration as the many reforms of the european treaties. today, the number of cases decided by the general court has been for several years lower than the number of cases brought and is constantly growing (more than 65% between 2000 and 2010). all this obviously entails costs and lengthened time for procedures. the increase in the number of judges is the structural solution adopted by the council, the commission and parliament. i have proposed with my italian colleague laura ferrara amendments to increase the number of judges at the court by 12, seven of whom are judges at the civil service tribunal, which is due to disappear. a total of 40 judges instead of the current 28 seems to be an appropriate and less costly response than a doubling to 56 judges as envisaged. the reform of the european court of justice has been under discussion for almost five years now. it is high time today to get out of what has become a gas factory.
in writing. ‒ the aim is therefore to double the number of judges in the tribunal to 56 judges, whereas the court's initial request was to appoint 12 judges. the arguments used for this reform are the increase in the number of cases whereas the figures and the statements of the judges are contradictory, or the too long trial period, which is still a false argument because it is acceptable in the eyes of the echr, given the uncompressible time due to translation and the complexity of cases in competition matters in particular. in committee, the elected enl members proposed to increase the number of referendaires and translators and not the number of judges. this reform increases eu spending very lightly at a time when people are suffering from austerity. in addition, the procedural legality of the whole process is tainted since, in reality, the subject under consideration is not the appointment of 12 additional judges, but that of 28 additional judges and the abolition of a specialised court (tfp). i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ the proposed reform is to double the number of judges at the general court of the european union (from 28 to 56) whereas the court's initial request was for the appointment of 12 additional judges. it should be noted that the two courts directly concerned by the proposal (the civil service tribunal and the general court) and the staff concerned were not even consulted. the reasons given (increase in the number of cases and extension of the trial period) are unfounded and contradict the available figures, the statements of judges of the general court and the case law of the echr. gilles lebreton and i proposed an increase in the number of referees and translators, not the number of judges. at a time when the european union is imposing austerity measures of unprecedented violence, it is proposing a costly and unnecessary reform. in addition, it is proposed to abolish the civil service tribunal, which is illegal under the treaty. i therefore voted against the amendment.
in writing. ‒ the objective of this reform is to double the number of judges in the general court to 56, whereas the initial request of the court of justice of the union was to appoint 12 additional judges. these appointments are supposed to help to reduce their workload, which has been steadily increasing due to a sharp increase in the number of cases, which is incorrect. in reality, the council proposed to double the number of judges to satisfy the national authorities of the member states who could not agree on the nationality of the judges to be appointed without concern for the interests of european taxpayers who are already suffering from the austerity cures imposed on them. in the name of the separation of powers, the europe of nations and freedoms group has tabled an amendment to the effect that no member of parliament or european official who has worked in the decision-making or legislative process can become a judge. i therefore voted in favour of the single rejection amendment tabled by our group.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the adoption of the reform of the court of justice of the european union. since 2012, the number of cases handled by the court has increased by 43%. the main reason for this dysfunction is a cruel lack of judgment. the consequences are that the right of european citizens to be heard within a reasonable time is infringed and the functioning of the single market is hindered. in this critical context, the european parliament took its responsibilities by calling for the appointment of 12 new judges in 2015 (already provided for in the 2015 union budget), followed by the transfer of the 7 judges of the civil service tribunal and its staff, and then the appointment of the last 9 judges in 2019. i particularly welcome the inclusion in this reform of two evaluation reports prior to the second and third phases, which i called for during the negotiations, and whose purpose is to assess the actual budgetary needs of the court throughout the reform. these reports must be such as to assist the court in its tasks while respecting the budgetary exemplarity to which the european institutions are bound.

in writing. ‒ the text aims to establish technical rules that will both preserve fisheries resources and safeguard the interests of fishermen. the first point raised by this draft was the request of the black sea coastal member states to be allowed to continue to use trawls and gillnets. this request was the subject of a compromise: trawling along the black sea coast is exceptionally permitted, but this derogation cannot constitute a legal precedent. the second point was raised by several states, including spain, which requested derogations to continue harvesting red coral, a protected species. this was also the subject of a compromise: states which have established or will establish, within the next three years, a national management framework, will be able to continue exploiting red coral, but in the event of a threat to this species, the commission will intervene. these derogations will expire at the end of 2015. these measures strike a healthy balance between protecting the environment and allowing member states to obtain derogations. i therefore voted in favour of this text.

in writing. ‒ the gabriel mato report transposes into eu law the measures adopted by the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm) at its annual sessions in 2011, 2012 and 2013. the gfcm is a regional fisheries management organisation established in accordance with article xiv of the fao constitution. its main objectives are to promote the development, conservation, rational management and optimum use of living marine resources, as well as the sustainable development of aquaculture in the mediterranean, the black sea and the intermediate waters. the cgpm has the authority to adopt binding decisions (recommendations) in its field of competence. the transposition provides for technical measures for the sustainable exploitation of red coral, the reduction of incidental catches of seabirds, sea turtles and cetaceans, and the conservation of monk seals, sharks and rays in the gfcm area. the report also implements into union law certain measures concerning the fishing of small pelagic stocks in the adriatic sea. i support the agreement reached in the trilogue between parliament and the council on 26 march 2015.

in writing. ‒ this report should define and regulate the placing on the market of novel food products. in this text, the council has removed all the security measures adopted by parliament. as a reminder, novel foods are all foods that did not exist in the european union before 1997. they cover, for example, food based on insects, nanomaterials or other products. it is therefore necessary that such products, as defined in this way, may be placed on the market only in accordance with the precautionary principle, accompanied by a specific labelling, and after their safety in relation to health and the environment has been demonstrated. the main regret i have in this report is that nanomaterials are not simply banned from food. the consumer protection is too weak, and only objections are allowed. i abstained on this vague text because, although the report is intended to be more protective, there is a risk with regard to nanomaterials and a legitimate distrust of the commission and efsa.
in writing. ‒ given the council's withdrawal of all the safety measures adopted by parliament and our concerns about:- possible penetration of cells by nanomaterials - lack of a real study on the health impacts - special risk to pregnant women and babies - lack of legislation on this subject for animal feed it is clear that we are calling for a ban on nanoparticles in food. i cannot therefore support this text and vote against it.
in writing. ‒ the aim of the report is to regulate the placing on the market of novel foods, i.e. all food products that did not exist in the european union before 1997, such as insect-based food or nanomaterials. the latter would pose a potential danger to consumers because these nanoparticles could penetrate our cells. this is why we need more regulation, ranging from labelling to prohibition, in accordance with the precautionary principle. the council has not taken all these safety measures at the expense of the europeans who will suffer the harmfulness of these particles. the parliamentary group of which i am a member has called for a simple ban on the use of these foods. this request runs counter to the philosophy of the text, and i therefore voted against the report.
in writing. ‒ novel foods are any foodstuffs for which human consumption was negligible within the union before 15 may 1997. it is very important to regulate these new foods which are now being consumed more widely on the european market. the report clarifies the definition of novel foods in order to adapt european legislation to the realities of the current european market. the procedures for authorising the entry of novel foods into the union will be streamlined and simplified, leading to a much more transparent system. this text is intended to improve the single market. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the james nicholson report on novel foods, which has led to very constructive negotiations at first reading between the european parliament and the council. this report responds to the need to revise the european regulation on the authorisation of the placing on the market of novel foods. the regulation dates from 1997 and is somewhat outdated in view of the evolution of food production methods, scientific progress and the opening of markets to products from third countries. the report by james nicholson is a source of positive developments. it provides for the re-evaluation of the definition of novel foods and the delimitation of different categories of foods falling within the scope of novel foods. the report also contains some provisions which will facilitate the entry into the union of traditional foods from third countries. in the final analysis, i believe that this report facilitates innovation while ensuring food safety for consumers.
in writing. ‒ this legislative report aims to speed up the authorisation procedure for 'novel foods', which is considered too complex, costly and time-consuming, and to take better account of recent scientific and technological developments in the food sector. 'new foods' are foods not covered by the current legislation dating from 1997. they may be innovative and produced with new technologies, or they may be products traditionally consumed in third countries outside the european union. the report extends the definition of novel foods to include, among others, food with a modified molecular structure, microorganisms, fungi, algae, food obtained from cell or tissue cultures, and insects. the european parliament has obtained satisfactory assurances from the council on food derived from cloned animals, the precautionary principle, measures to keep nanomaterials under surveillance and restrictions on animal testing, and i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ this regulation simplifies the procedures for marketing authorisations for novel foods, i.e. foods or food ingredients not consumed in the european union before 1997. for example, goji berries, originally from latin america, were not consumed in europe 20 years ago, but are now widely available commercially and highly prized for their energy-giving properties. globalization and technological innovation have helped diversify our diet. the european union must therefore adapt and support innovation in the food sector without calling into question the precautionary principle and the protection of european consumers. the authorization procedure at european level must therefore be properly regulated and the scope of the regulation clarified.

in writing. ‒ on wednesday 28 october, i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on novel foods. the concept of novel food generally refers to foodstuffs whose consumption in the european union was negligible before may 1997, i.e. before the entry into force of the present regulation. the european regulation on novel foods needed to be revised in order to simplify procedures and above all to adapt to changing markets and new technologies. i therefore believe that this compromise adopted in plenary is balanced. it will ensure strict control of novel foods and good consumer information, while ensuring that safe and innovative food products are brought to market more quickly within the european union. i therefore welcome the adoption of the european parliament's position and hope that agreement between the council and the european parliament on this text can be reached quickly.
in writing. i have approved the draft text to encourage food innovation through a new simplified authorisation procedure for novel foods. the proposal was intended to replace an old regulation which had become inadequate. the agri-food sector is changing, adapting and improving all the time. a legislative framework is needed to respond to the advances of recent years, for example in nanotechnologies and cell and tissue cultures. a new procedure for the authorisation of novel foods will provide greater legal certainty and reduce the administrative burden for smes. when deciding whether to authorise a novel food, the european commission will have to apply the precautionary principle if the safety of the food cannot be assessed or there is scientific uncertainty. the text states that the european food safety authority (efsa) should carry out an assessment whenever a food is likely to have an impact on human health. the text states that animal testing should be replaced, reduced or improved. in addition, repeated animal testing should be avoided where possible. the european commission would be required to publish a summary of each application.

in writing. ‒ the commission proposes that we integrate methane into national pollutant emission ceilings and air quality legislation. for agriculture, this means the integration of methane resulting from the ingestion of grass by ruminants, especially in traditional and extensive livestock areas, which are very often located in less prosperous areas. i am opposed to this idea because these farms have very little potential to reduce emissions, in particular because there is no effective technical solution to prevent cows from emitting so-called enteric methane. it's hard to go against nature. the inclusion of this methane in the directive's obligations would lead to a reduction in herds and even to the abandonment of herbaceous farming systems. this would be tantamount to encouraging intensive farming models that are less favourable to the environment and to fragile territories. i am glad that our assembly has taken account of the realities of agriculture without neglecting the issues of public health and the environment. it will help to alleviate many of the concerns in the livestock sector, which is currently in crisis.

in writing. ‒ with just a few weeks to go until the cop21 in paris, the european parliament is voicing its commitment to curbing the damage to the ozone layer. i share this vital objective for the planet, but i felt it necessary to oppose the measure to introduce emission ceilings for methane, especially the so-called "enteric" one which is produced by cattle. in a difficult economic context, this new standard would have been detrimental to cattle farmers and in particular to milk producers who have opted for extensive farming. i trust the farmers who have already implemented new practices that meet the requirements of reducing greenhouse gas emissions. the cap is being 'greened'. the 'double penalty' of new standards should be avoided. i therefore supported and voted for an amendment to exclude enteric methane emissions from this directive. i welcome its adoption and hope that this decision will be supported by the european council in the next negotiations. in a globalised world, we must be aware that air knows no frontiers and that the issuing of standards in europe must not lead to producers moving abroad.
in writing. ‒ this commission directive proposed to the european parliament continues the work of the 2001 pen directive on emission ceilings for certain air pollutants for sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxide, ammonia and non-methane volatile organic compounds (nmvocs) until 2020. the new directive proposes new thresholds until 2030 by adding methane (a polluting gas largely from agricultural and livestock activities) and fine particulate matter. the rapporteur proposed a more binding deadline of 2025 but refused to include methane (cf. agriculture). the fn elected members of the commission supported the position against the inclusion of methane and against the mention of ammonia in order to limit the regulatory burden on agriculture and certain industries. i therefore voted against.

in writing. ‒ the directive on the reduction of national emissions of certain air pollutants is part of the legislative package on air quality proposed by the commission. the text proposes the setting of very ambitious targets for the reduction of certain polluting gases. it is very important to increase the quality of air as pollution is responsible for many deaths every year. however, we must try to remain realistic and set binding targets which do not jeopardise the economic competitiveness of the european union. the example of the methane reduction target is particularly telling. the main source of methane emissions is the agricultural sector, as ruminants are the main emitters. the agricultural sector is currently experiencing particularly difficult times. to impose this measure on our farmers would only make their situation worse. i therefore voted in favour of this text on the condition that the emission of enterich methane be excluded from the scope of the legislation.
in writing. ‒ this legislative report revises national emission ceilings for certain pollutants to improve air quality and human health. the text introduces new limit values (such as sulphur dioxide, ultrafine particles or methane) from 2020 and 2030. it also proposes a binding 2025 interim target for all pollutants except ammonia. other measures include access to finance for air quality improvements and emission control programmes. there was much opposition, both on the level of ambition of the reduction targets for 2020, 2025 and 2030, and on the addition of new pollutants. since we do not currently have an effective technical or technological means of reducing the emissions of enteric methane (waste from livestock), i co-signed an amendment, the content of which was taken up by the plenary, to exclude these emissions from the directive, so as not to penalise the agricultural sector. i regret, however, that my amendments to protect small farms and to exclude ammonia were not adopted. i have nevertheless voted in favour of opening negotiations between the european parliament and the council, in support of the main objectives of this report.
in writing. ‒ the 2001 european nec directive sets national emission ceilings for certain air pollutants: sulphur dioxide (so2), nitrogen oxides (nox), volatile organic compounds (vocs) and ammonia (nh3). in a new revised proposal, the commission introduces two new pollutants, fine particulate matter (pm2.5) and methane (ch4), and sets new, more stringent national ceilings for the other four pollutants. air pollution kills 400 000 european citizens every year, so the eu needs to set stricter emission ceilings and binding targets for 2025 for all the pollutants it targets. it is wise to make an exception for the so-called enteric methane, i.e. from livestock production produced by the belching and farts of cows. the european ecological revolution we are calling for is synonymous with the preservation of a sustainable agricultural model which respects animal welfare.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the girling report, or nec directive, which aims to set member states' emission ceilings for the main pollutants. i have, however, campaigned for the exclusion of enteric methane from the scope of the directive. the reduction of methane emissions is certainly an important public health issue, but we must be pragmatic. that is why we have fought throughout the discussions in committees to reject the inclusion of enteric methane in the calculation of national emission ceilings. this inclusion could have undermined the competitiveness of our agriculture at a time when the european livestock sector is going through an unprecedented crisis. we cannot make a case for animal welfare in the agricultural sector on the one hand and impose unreasonable constraints on our farmers on the other. this directive is therefore a crucial legislative instrument for monitoring compliance with air quality objectives at european level. but if we want effective legislation, it must first be realistic!

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution setting new, more ambitious national emission ceilings for the main air pollutants harmful to human health and the environment: nitrogen oxides, sulphur dioxide, non-methane volatile organic compounds, ammonia, methane and particulate matter. air pollution is responsible for about 400 000 premature deaths each year in the european union and causes between 300 and 900 billion euro in health-related costs per year. it is therefore urgent to address these serious air quality problems that persist in the union. the reductions set shall apply from 2020 and 2030, with intermediate emission levels for the year 2025. we have decided to keep methane and ammonia in the directive, two pollutants which are mainly from agriculture, while excluding the enteric methane emissions naturally produced by ruminants. negotiations with the council will now be able to begin with a view to reaching an agreement at first reading.
