in writing. ‒ this report comes as the commission prepares the mid-term review of the europe 2020 strategy. it is important to recall that cohesion policy is the main instrument of investment of the union and reflects european solidarity; it also meets the objectives of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth set out in the europe 2020 strategy. the report thus addresses several messages on these two points. as regards the europe 2020 strategy, firstly, it is important to establish a better interconnection of the five objectives of the strategy without creating a new administrative burden or level of complexity. in addition, it is important that stakeholders are more involved in all stages from planning to evaluation; the setting of regional objectives could also be an important element in involving all the actors. the future cohesion policy and the future eu strategy for growth and jobs will have to be presented before the end of the current commission's mandate. i therefore supported this report which also recalls the importance of involving parliament in cohesion policy and the review of the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. ‒ this report celebrates the europe 2020 strategy and the cohesion policy which would contribute to economic development, increased investment and job creation. it also advocated strengthening local and regional authorities at the expense of the member states. it even suggests that local and national authorities should be treated equally in the negotiations, by proposing the signing of a pact between the commission, the member states and local and regional authorities to ensure their participation in the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy. finally, it welcomed the creation of the european fund for strategic investments. i object to all these considerations.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of mr lópez's report is to provide clarification on the use of article 23 of the regulation laying down common provisions on the european structural and investment funds. the text of the report insists that this article be applied in a balanced way. to this end, it rightly provides that incessant rescheduling must be avoided and that the suspension of payment mechanism, which is a discretionary power of the commission, must remain exceptional. the report also calls on the commission to present a white paper analysing the impact and effectiveness of public investment in the long term. i hope that this will oblige the commission to do so. however, independent study would be welcome. among the negative aspects of the report, i note that it places the entire responsibility for the increase in public debt on the budgetary policies of the member states, whereas the european union also has its share of responsibility, in particular through its aberrant monetary policy. the cohesion policy that the report promotes has not brought prosperity or growth. because this text limits the commission's room for manoeuvre, i abstained, despite my disagreement with the european economic governance.

in writing. ‒ this report on the european structural and investment funds for good economic governance echoes the commission's communication on 'guidelines for the application of measures linking the effectiveness of the european structural and investment funds'. while the purpose of this text is to limit the commission's power to impose macroeconomic conditionality on aid, it does not remove these unacceptable provisions and thus reinforces the commission's grip on austerity. secondly, this report attributes the increase in public debt solely to the policies of the member states, whereas most of it comes from a transfer of private debt to the public (notably from the euro or laws prohibiting borrowing at 0% from national banks), reinforced by the austerity policy demanded by brussels. i abstained, however, because it diminishes the scope of the text presented by the commission.
in writing. ‒ article 23 of the common provisions regulation (cpr) establishes a link between the effectiveness of the efsi and the sound economic governance of the member states. this article is intended to make the receipt of european structural funds conditional on the macroeconomic performance of the member states, in particular in terms of deficit or public debt. if a state does not implement the structural reforms recommended by the commission, it may be suspended payments. the rapporteur therefore proposes to ensure that these provisions are applied in a balanced and exceptional manner. the rapporteur acknowledges, however, that the sharp increase in the debt ratio of the member states since 2008 is mainly the result of the mismanagement of the national governments' budgets and does not sufficiently highlight the commission's responsibility through the austerity cures it has imposed on the peoples of europe. the report also explains that cohesion policy has made it possible to respond to the current macroeconomic and budgetary constraints, which we strongly dispute. i therefore abstained on that text.
in writing. ‒ the structural and investment funds have a significant impact on the daily lives of european citizens. they enable citizens to take action and implement their projects. it is very important, however, to ensure that these funds are managed properly so that they can really serve their objectives. macroeconomic conditionality was introduced with this in mind. good governance in a member state is a prerequisite for the structural funds to be disbursed to local entities. however, such measures of reprogramming or suspension of the funds by the european commission are very rare and subject to many criteria for determining a breach of the principle of good governance. the objective of macroeconomic conditionality is to encourage member states to implement the structural reforms necessary for the recovery of the union's economic activity. the principle is commendable. however, care must be taken that decentralised, regional or municipal entities with a certain degree of management autonomy are not affected by bad decisions by a central state. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which stresses the need for great caution in the use of macroeconomic conditionality.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report aims to specify the conditions for the application of the good governance measures concerning the effective use of the european structural and investment funds. the report calls on the member states to make the best use of the flexibility provided for by the existing rules of the stability and growth pact in the use of the european structural and investment funds. it also considered it essential to ensure transparency and accountability by giving parliament democratic control over the governance system. the report also calls for the creation of a council configuration specifically devoted to cohesion policy. i voted in favour of this report in support of these objectives.
in writing. ‒ with regard to the guidelines for the implementation of macroeconomic conditionality in the framework of the structural funds, i wanted to criticise this text, which establishes a direct link between cohesion policy and the economic governance provisions introduced by the stability and growth pact, despite the constant opposition of local and regional authorities, who stress that they are not responsible for excessive national public deficits, since most of them are constitutionally obliged to balance their budgets. the esi funds, which have a proven positive impact on growth, are one of the most concrete examples of the principle of european solidarity, which is the basis of the european commitment of the socialists. we must be determined to preserve them. a too dogmatic approach to the convergence criteria must be excluded in the present case. how can we explain to the inhabitants of a territory that europe does not support them because the burden of debt for which they are not responsible but simply heirs is considered too heavy? it's a double unjust and unjustified punishment. as a former regional president, i can't help it.

madam president, this instrument, together with computers, tablets and all other communicating objects, can be the best or the worst of things. if i use it for work, for information, for education, or to keep my family informed, it's the best, and it's useful. if i use it to organize a smuggling, an attack or for harm to society and people, it is the worst, and it is hateful. and of course, all the mass information that's in these communicating objects ends up in the cloud. how do we tell the wheat from the weeds? this is the whole question of the balance between security and freedom that is being asked today. it is a question that has been recurring and we have been debating it for a very long time. i think that citizens themselves have a number of questions, depending on the news, and if, today, they want to keep their freedom - and this is unavoidable from my point of view - and also want to be protected, we have to find a way to make sure that technology meets the law.

in writing. ‒ the regulation in question sets out rules to make transparent securities financing operations, which are generally referred to as 'shadow banking' and which correspond to a phenomenon with fuzzy outlines involving a whole set of entities whose financial intermediation activities are called 'parallel'. these are not part of traditional banking operations. these operations are thus virtually unregulated and use attractive (low taxation and high interest) but dangerous (no public guarantee) channels. they are made by investment banks, mutual funds, insurance companies, pension or money funds, private equity firms and hedge funds. the need for flexible regulation of these activities has become more urgent, especially since the collapse of lehman brothers in 2008. indeed, the opacity of the operations generated by shadow banking, by not allowing the owners of the securities and their real value to be identified, is partly responsible for the spread of the crisis in the united states, and then in the world by ricochet. the european regulations we were subject to mitigate the risk inherent in this type of activity, in particular by imposing more transparency. so i voted for it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, as the committee had recommended in its report.
in writing. ‒ this report on the transparency of securities financing transactions covers all transactions that use assets to generate financing. this is therefore a significant part of the shadow banking activity carried out by economic agents not bound by banking legislation. this shadow finance is dangerous, as it is not controlled and its growth is exponential. the trialogue last june resulted in an agreement on transparency obligations which is welcome but still insufficient. a simple register will not be enough!! the rapporteur goes further, for example, by proposing stricter controls on the reuse of safety belts, which is a particularly harmful practice. i have decided to vote in favour of this report to regulate this practice. i would remind you that i recently tabled a motion for a resolution on the limitation of shadow banking activities and that efforts in this area must be continued.
in writing. ‒ the securities financing operations regulation is part of a package of legislative measures proposed by the commission to create greater transparency in the shadow banking system. the shadow banking system is the set of activities and actors contributing to the non-bank financing of the economy. like all shadow banking regulations, it is designed to create rules equivalent to those to which banks are subject to prevent the transfer of financial operations from the traditional banking system, which has been highly regulated since the crisis, to the shadow banking system. securities financing operations are a rapid and necessary means of financing the real economy. however, without regulation to increase transparency, they can lead to financial market destabilisation, as in 2008. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ this legislative report aims to improve the financial stability of the union by enhancing transparency in certain market activities, in particular in securities financing operations. securities financing transactions are the borrowing, selling or lending of securities to create liquidity, facilitate financing or simply to reveal their value. the 2008 financial crisis highlighted the weaknesses of the financial regulatory system and the need for increased transparency and oversight of the traditional banking sector and non-bank credit institutions. the report proposes, in particular, that the way investment funds use financing operations be disclosed to investors and the public. i believe that transparency is one of the key measures to reform the financial sector and i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ this report on the transparency of securities financing operations is an interesting approach. by proposing a requirement for transparency and reporting of transactions in a central repository and forcing listed companies that use this type of transaction to inform their investors, it is moving in the right direction. however, this report is only a watered-down version of the previous versions. while the soru report strictly regulated the reuse of collateral and the banking structural reform directive proposed to separate speculative and risky banking activities, the latter version abandoned these important points. however, i did vote in favour of the report, which proposes welcome regulations on this sector, which is not sufficiently monitored.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, mr renato soru, on the transparency of securities financing operations. this report is part of the effort to regulate the shadow banking system. indeed, while securities financing operations contribute to market liquidity and allow central banks to refinance themselves, they can, without regulation, lead to significant market destabilisation, as we saw in 2008. the text therefore seeks to mitigate these negative effects by creating rules equivalent to those to which banks are subject. the report was adopted by a large majority, which i welcome.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the transparency of securities financing operations. this is a significant part of non-bank lending activities. this parallel finance is dangerous in many ways: by the colossal amounts it represents, by its opacity, by the excessive use of leverage, by the spread of risk to a chain of misidentified investors, etc. the trilogue concluded on 17 june 2015 resulted in an agreement on transparency obligations and reporting of these transactions to a central repository. in addition, for listed companies using these operations, it will be necessary to inform investors. it is therefore a step in the right direction. however, it is still not enough. the original report was rather strict on, for example, the reuse of collateral, whereas the version which is being put to the vote is less restrictive. i believe that these operations should be strictly prohibited. moreover, the real reform to avoid risk dispersion is the separation of banking activities. the elimination of the universal bank is a more effective bulwark against the contagion of financial sector risks. unfortunately, this point has now reached a dead end.
in writing. ‒ in financial markets, the development of complex transactions (whether forwards, over-the-counter or temporary) has been exponential since the early 2000s. the regulator is forced to monitor financial innovations remotely. this is the case for temporary securities financing transactions (ctt), whereby an operator may put into reserve securities it holds in exchange for a consideration. these operations are used extensively by banks for refinancing purposes, but are very poorly informed. european and national regulators are not informed of the potential reuse of, for example, retired securities. this creates chains of interdependence that can lead to contagion in a crisis. the soru report sets out three basic rules: an obligation to report counterparties to the european securities and markets authority, an obligation to inform investors, and a limitation on the possibilities for re-use of retired securities. although the problem of financial innovation may have to be tackled more from the outset, i support any regulation that aims to moderate complex transactions, which is why i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. civilian drones have many uses, both economic and recreational. the control of such use is necessary to ensure the safety of air traffic, of vulnerable populations and areas, as well as the protection of data and privacy. for once, european harmonization is desirable, provided it is based on clear, proportionate rules and properly articulated with national and international rules. this is so as not to hinder the expansion of this very recent and particularly dynamic sector in france. i agree with ms foster's moderation, who rejects any regulatory rush and insists on the involvement of all stakeholders - including smes, law enforcement and civil society organisations - in the development of regulation. that is why i voted for his report.
in writing. ‒ the foster report sets out a balanced community regulation. the aim is to build civil drone regulation on what is already being done in terms of international regulations in the field of civil aviation. in order to ensure the safety of air traffic and the safety of the public, there is no reason why international rules should not be drawn up, since national airspace is constantly crossed by foreign aircraft. the text insists that european regulations should strike a balance between ensuring the safety of individuals, the protection of data and privacy and the development of this new sector. the report also stresses the need to involve all stakeholders in the development of community rules: member states, the commission, the national authorities concerned, smes, commercial operators, policymakers, etc. however, this report does not cover military drones, which should remain the exclusive responsibility of the member states. i voted yes.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the safe use of unmanned aerial vehicles (uavs) in civil aviation. as is already the case in civil aviation, international regulations governing the use of civil drones are necessary to ensure the safety of air traffic and the public. the report stresses that eu legislation should be balanced: neither too restrictive nor too liberal. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of personal data. finally, it should be noted that the report emphasises the need for cooperation between all stakeholders in order to achieve the best possible legislation. it therefore advocates that discussions and debates take place between member states, the commission, national regulatory authorities, smes and commercial operators, as well as civil society organisations and law enforcement agencies. as this is a strategic sector (remember the drones flying over french nuclear power stations), it is very important that the commission is not the only one in charge of this dossier.

in writing. ‒ the future european regulation will aim to address justified safety concerns but will also try to give this emerging sector the means to develop in a respectful environment for citizens and airspace. the report aims to ensure the traceability of all machines, but also of operators and owners as a prerequisite for any use. this is a good thing because we could see during the fly-by of the french nuclear power stations that we were unable to find the pilots. a registration system must be put in place to enable drones to be easily identified, even from a distance if possible. the terrorist risks raise fears of a real threat to the safety of france's nuclear fleet, which could cause an electrical blackout or even a major nuclear accident, as we were able to demonstrate in a letter to the french government... which remained unanswered. it is also planned to ensure better airworthiness for drones with a sharing of clear airspace. the main issue is to distinguish between recreational and professional uses and to give different permissions to their users.
in writing. ‒ originally developed for military purposes, drone technology is increasingly being applied for economic purposes. drones used in a professional context have a wide range of uses that may be developed in the future, including safety inspections and infrastructure control (railways, dams and power plants, etc.), natural disaster assessment, agriculture and parcel delivery in remote areas. the resolution adopted by a very large majority by the european parliament emphasises above all the support for the development of this new technology, which indeed has the potential for economic growth and hence for jobs. it stresses the importance of personal data protection and privacy but the proposed recommendations do not seem to me to be sufficiently binding to guarantee a truly safe use of drones. i therefore voted against this resolution which favours a market approach to the sector and does not offer sufficient protection.

in writing. ‒ this resolution calls on member states to increase the use of satellite technology for aircraft tracking and assistance in locating aircraft in distress. the tragedies of malaysia airlines flight 370 and air france flight 447 have indeed highlighted the weaknesses of current air navigation systems. currently, only 30% of the world's airspace is covered by satellites, making search and rescue efforts in the event of abnormal aircraft behaviour or accidents significantly more difficult. parliament proposed that a specific radio frequency be allocated to these monitoring satellites and called on the european commission to promote this system in view of the world radiocommunication conference (wrc-15) in geneva in november. i have voted in favour of the resolution, considering that air safety is a priority in the light of the development of air traffic, the safety of citizens and the terrorist threat.
in writing. ‒ this motion for a resolution concerned the development of technology using satellites to track aircraft in flight on a global scale. while the oral question asked only for the commission's opinion on this subject, the motion for a resolution gives the commission the power to set up such a system. in addition to the necessarily very high cost, this system, which does not seem to be a priority, has many disadvantages. so by digitizing the flight data of airplanes, this system opens the door to a lot of bugs, hacking, and manipulation of information of all kinds, both by terrorists and by unscrupulous interests. while conventional transponders and radar systems have been functioning perfectly well for over half a century, this measure does not seem to be appropriate. i therefore voted against this proposal.

in writing. technology that not only tracks aircraft in flight in areas not or poorly covered by radar, but also enhances aviation safety looks promising. unfortunately, we also have to think about the facilities for finding aircraft that have been damaged at sea or that have been lost. what is less important is to ask the commission to intervene at this stage. this technology is still in the experimental stage, particularly in france, and it has many shortcomings. in particular, security gaps, as hackers claim to be able to obtain flight data, including passenger data, and believe it is largely feasible to generate ghost tracks or, on the contrary, to hide illegal flights, to blur signals, etc. as with all "communication" technologies, there is also the flip side of the coin: potential for malicious or intrusive use. it is first up to the national authorities and the international civil aviation organisation to decide on the feasibility, viability and safety of this new surveillance system before brussels intervenes.

mr president, commissioner, in your communication of 27 october you said that it is the results that matter, not the good intentions. let's see what you got! you want to maintain trust in the schengen area, but it has collapsed under the pressure of migration: borders are reappearing everywhere. you want to put people back to work, but you're the one who's keeping them out of work with your ultra-liberal policies. you want to protect public health, but you give in to the lobbyists who are spreading endocrine disruptors. you want to reconcile the economic with the social, but you do the opposite by selling your soul to the most savage financial capitalism. you want to ensure the survival of europe, and there, rest assured, europe will survive, but it will be without you, commissioner, because it will be the europe of nations.

in writing. this debate on growth and the 2016 package of measures to achieve it in europe via the european semester is just another mirage, with the foreknowledge that the proposed solutions will not change anything. austerity, mass immigration, ultra-liberalism, the single currency and submission to finance have ruined the european union and none of these policies challenges these tenets. apart from this debate, i would like to express my indignation at the fact that the european parliament has authorized a plenary sitting in brussels on 11 november which is contrary to its principles of respect for national holidays. the european union is not a party to the treaty of rome, but it is a party to the treaty of rome, and it is a party to the treaty of rome. one author said that 'those who know the past are best able to build the future', and it seems that today the union is forgetting its history very quickly.
for the greens/efa group mr president, madam commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, aviation is the largest emitter of greenhouse gases of all modes of transport. for each passenger and each kilometre travelled, this mode of transport is three times more harmful to the climate than the car. imagine that a round trip from london to new york generates about as many greenhouse gases as one person needs to heat themselves for a year. and yet, strangely enough, this transport is exempt from taxes: no tax on kerosene or no or little vat for cross-border flights. it's simple, airlines are the champions of the tax break. we're stepping on the head! is it right that kerosene is the only fossil fuel that is not taxed? and why are trains overtaxed, while air travel is not, or so little? the result, since 1990, is that as the price of the airline ticket has gone down, emissions from this sector have gone up by 110%, and they could even triple by 2050 and take us well beyond the 2°c of global warming. with less than a month to go until cop 21, we must call it a day. let us tax kerosene like other fuels and end the minimum vat in the aviation sector. the other challenge is social. the airline industry has become an economic jungle where all sorts of things are allowed: zero-hour contracts, fake freelancers, letterbox companies. employees must have rights guaranteed by european legislation. mrs. bulc, i trust you with this. you told us last june that you would not look the other way on this matter. so let us do something about it, and put an end to social dumping and tax dumping in the airline industry, which are always to the detriment of employees. look at regulation (ec) no 868/2004, which was never implemented to combat unfair pricing practices. let us finally put airlines like ryanair, norwegian airlines and others on a footing by forcing them to respect the law. the regulation must also enable us to combat unfair competition from gulf companies. qatar, saudi arabia and the united arab emirates are giving their airlines tens of billions of euros in state aid to gain a foothold in the airline market. how do you want european companies to follow suit? new rules are needed to combat state aid and unfair pricing practices that distort competition. so you see, colleagues, we are faced with three challenges when we talk about aviation: the climate challenge, the social challenge and the international challenge. we have to get them out today. the epp resolution does not answer this question at all, but the ecologists' resolution provides concrete solutions. if we do not, the planet, the workers and the consumers will once again pay the price.
on behalf of the enf group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, madam commissioner, i should like to say in the preamble that i am rather cautious about the single european sky. the best intentions in the world may well be there, but i fear that under the pretext of simplifying the operation of european civil aviation, we will end up with a gas factory, which is oversized and lacks great flexibility. the resolution we are proposing to the commission is interesting in several respects. first of all, on security, and of course we are always in favour of increased security in all areas. the specific nature of civil aviation - which i know well from having worked for 35 years at air france - requires that safety requirements be as high as possible. it is high time that the civil aviation authorities took measures, for example, to provide medical care for the crew after the germanwings tragedy. i am glad that the joint motion for a resolution calls for support for the competitiveness of european airlines, because we cannot just stand by and watch our historic national airlines, which are part of our country's heritage and influence, go down. of course, efforts must be made by all, including the employees, but our companies will not survive unless they are finally put on an equal footing with their competitors, particularly the companies of the gulf countries and turkey. the latter are heavily subsidised - as has been said - by their governments, not to mention indirect aid, such as exemption from social security contributions, virtually free fuel or exemptions from airport taxes, all of which are a heavy burden on european airlines and which cannot be offset by any aid, since the commission prohibits them in the name of competition. unfortunately, ladies and gentlemen, you are not following this logic. by recommending that the commission accelerate the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions, you will inevitably increase the already heavy burden on our airlines and thus penalise our customers, since the price of the air ticket will inevitably be increased again by one or more taxes.

mr president, alzheimer's disease and related diseases affect about 6 million people in europe and the number of new cases diagnosed each year continues to rise. in france, 225,000 new cases are detected each year and one in four french people have someone in their entourage who is affected, which causes a lot of suffering and distress, both for the person affected and for those around him. this disease causes gradual and irreversible loss of mental functions, including memory, and unfortunately, there is currently no treatment for alzheimer's disease, although some drug treatments can help slow the process. this disease, which is the leading cause of addiction in europe, requires additional research resources and, above all, recognition as a priority health issue in france and europe. i have, moreover, tabled a written statement on this subject with 24 of my parliamentary colleagues from all political groups, because the general and human interest must come first. i would now ask all members of this house to sign this declaration.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text which calls for a revision of the dia1 directive on insurance intermediation from a consumer protection perspective. it offers comprehensive regulation of the insurance sector by integrating all intermediaries, which ensures more complete information for customers. the new directive, known as dia2, extends its scope to all distribution channels for insurance products, thus updating the legal framework by taking account of new players such as bank insurers, comparators, travel agencies or any other intermediary. the registration process is also subject to new conditions to create a single register that will centralise information on market players. finally, the requirements for professional competence and the duty to advise are strengthened. the report is therefore in the interests of consumer protection.
in writing. ‒ this intermediation directive (iad2) follows up on the dia1 directive of 9 december 2002, which was intended to strengthen competition and regulation in the field of insurance intermediation. the 2008 financial crisis exposed the shortcomings of the old legislation, in particular in terms of market distortions. this is why the new directive is so important, since it extends its scope to all the distribution channels for insurance products. dia2 also recommends that clients be better informed about the remuneration of sales representatives and the risk of capital loss they incur on certain financial investments. we welcome this new directive which supports the selfemployed in their dealings with the large financial institutions. registered insurance intermediaries will now be allowed to take up and pursue the business of insurance intermediation in the union under both the freedom of establishment and the freedom to provide services. finally, we are pleased to see that customers will benefit from better information on the increasingly complex financial products they subscribe to. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ this legislative report proposes to review existing legislation on insurance intermediation, with the aim of providing a level playing field for all actors involved in the sale of insurance products and strengthening the protection of insurance contract holders. the new text will provide insurance consumers and investors with greater transparency on insurance product prices and more accurate and comprehensive information on insurance products, enabling them to make informed choices when making purchases. they may also decide not to take out insurance when it is offered as a supplement to the purchase of a good or service (e.g. a car). i have voted in favour of this report because i believe it will help to strengthen consumer protection.

in writing. ‒ to better protect consumers in the insurance sector, it is imperative to consolidate a common legislative framework. the new european provisions improve the obligations of insurance distributors in europe towards their customers. they will now have to be registered with a competent national authority. intermediaries will have to clearly mention information about their products and in particular their cost.
in writing. ‒ this report validated the directive which aimed to create greater competition within the single market, while standardising services. by seeking to regulate the insurance sector and all its intermediaries more closely, the union is once again interfering in national affairs and civil society. and while the original idea was laudable because it related to consumer protection, the causes of this dysfunction are primarily the single market. i therefore abstained from voting, not wishing to support the european single market.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this resolution because it goes against the mif 2 directive, which i oppose.
in writing. ‒ on tuesday 24 november, i voted in favour of a text to strengthen the rules governing the insurance sector within two years, in order to better control the activity of brokers and other intermediaries and to improve the information provided to consumers. more than 70% of insurance products are sold without adequate advice to the consumer. the text will require insurance salesmen to register with the authorities in their country, but also with the european insurance and occupational pensions authority, based in frankfurt, which will check that they are properly qualified.
in writing. ‒ this text promotes regulation of the insurance intermediation market in favour of policyholders and the self-employed. the report amends the mif2 directive and the foundations of the practice of the brokerage profession, in particular as regards the definition of an independent intermediary. insurance companies and banks will no longer be able to stifle independent advisers and monopolize the profession. the objective of regulating the entire insurance sector by including all intermediaries and providing customers with more complete information is a real step forward which we welcome. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, mr werner langen, on insurance intermediation. the report sets out a new directive on insurance distribution, to better organise the business of insurance intermediaries. these professions will have to comply with requirements relating to information, advice and customer protection and will be obliged to be registered in their home member state in order to be able to practise anywhere in europe. this will make it easier and safer for consumers to buy insurance. i welcome the fact that this report was adopted by a large majority.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on insurance intermediation. the report supports the regulation of the insurance intermediation market in favour of policyholders and the selfemployed. it substantially amends the mif2 directive and the basis for the exercise of the brokerage profession. the insurance companies and banks will no longer be able to stifle independent advisers and monopolize this professional activity, which is a good thing.
in writing. - i voted yes. this intermediation directive (iad 2) follows on from the dia directive of 1 december 2002 which aimed at greater competition in the single market while standardising the products offered to consumers, all with a check on the competence and integrity of intermediaries. dia 2 is a reworking of dia 1, which it extends the scope of action to include newer actors offering insurance such as bank insurers, comparators, travel agencies ... it also strengthens the requirements for professional competence and their duty to advise. this will allow the entire insurance sector to be regulated and provide customers with the most complete information possible, while avoiding the banking lobbies.
in writing. ‒ insurance or reinsurance intermediation is the activity of presenting, proposing or assisting in the conclusion of insurance or reinsurance contracts or in carrying out other preparatory work for their conclusion. the report before us aims to clarify and introduce new elements of harmonization of the work of insurance intermediaries within the european union. the main aim of the text, which strengthens the control of these intermediaries, is to promote a genuine internal market for life and non-life insurance products and services. i am opposed to the increasing penetration of the markets by private insurance schemes and i shall abstain on this text which regulates them on the margin.
in writing. ‒ the report supports regulation of the insurance intermediation market in favour of policyholders and the self-employed. it substantially amends the mif2 directive and the basis for the exercise of the brokerage profession, in particular as regards the definition of an independent intermediary. insurance companies and banks will no longer be able to stifle independent advisers and monopolize the profession. it is time that the european parliament stopped giving all the power to the banking and insurance lobbies and allowed the same competent people to do this job in a sustainable way. i therefore welcome the intelligence of this report. the objective of regulating the entire insurance sector by including all intermediaries and providing customers with more complete information is a real step forward. i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ this report deals with the amendment of the insurance intermediation directive (iad1) of 2002 which was intended to allow for greater competition in the single market. however, the implementation of dia1 has been complicated and has created market distortions, and the 2008 financial crisis has led to increased stability in the insurance market. dia2 therefore aims to correct the shortcomings of dia1 by providing better protection for the policyholder and better regulation of the insurance intermediation business. first, dia2 extends its scope to all insurance distribution channels and the registration process is changed to create a single register. dia2 also provides for the provision to the customer or for the search of new information such as the way in which the seller is remunerated and the status of the intermediary. the requirements for professional competence and the duty to advise are strengthened. finally, by adopting the measures provided for in the mifid directive, dia2 incorporates the verification of the client's financial and insurance skills and the provision of capital loss risks to the subscriber.
in writing. ‒ this report concerns the insurance intermediation directive (iiad), which follows on from the 2002 iad1 which was intended to allow for greater competition in the single market while standardising the products made available to consumers and imposing controls on the competence of intermediaries. the 2008 crisis revealed the shortcomings of this system and the very loose interpretation of the member states of the dia1. in 2012, the commission therefore adopted dia2, which extends its scope to all distribution channels for the newly emerging insurance products that form the basis of shadow banking. transparency measures for the customer are also provided, such as information on the way the seller is remunerated and the status of the intermediary. the question of the conflict of interest of brokers is also raised. i think that these are provisions which are designed to make things more transparent for consumers, and i have therefore decided to vote in favour of this text.

in writing. ‒ this report on the role of the european union in the united nations is a further blow to the sovereignty of the member states. it considers that global issues must require coordinated european intervention by increasing the eu's influence, in particular in the united nations general assembly and the security council, where the adoption of a single eu seat is discussed. it provides for a mechanism to compel member states, including those with veto power in the security council, to coordinate their action. it also wants to oblige permanent and non-permanent member states to defend the eu's positions in the un security council. the report recalls that the echr is an example of progress in human rights, even though, according to the commission, it no longer applies in greece, since it is under the rule of the memoranda. it also introduces the principle of 'climate refugee' into international law. in short, this text is a line of pearls, each more europeanist than the other. i therefore voted against.

in writing. ‒ i could not vote for this report but i fully support the position of the epp group and the french delegation to adopt this report. it stresses that the union and its member states share the values and principles of the united nations charter and play a key role in promoting these principles and the objectives of the united nations. the report welcomes the active participation and contribution of the union and its member states to the work of the united nations system in various ways and in various forms, but considers that they should be more visible. it also serves as a reminder of the union's major contribution to humanitarian and development aid around the world, and recalls that the union and its member states are jointly the world's largest provider of humanitarian and development aid.

in writing. ‒ in this report we recall that the european union, on the one hand, and its member states, on the other, play a key role in the united nations and its bodies. france in particular, through its activities, its budget or the values we share. we want a thorough reform of the un system to make it more effective. all of this has led me to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ the own-initiative report on the role of the european union in the united nations and the best ways to achieve the union's foreign policy objectives sets out ambitious proposals to strengthen our weight in this global body. the report stresses the need to strengthen the role of the european union in the united nations general assembly, and more particularly in the economic and social council, including environmental issues. i am convinced that the links between the european union and the united nations must be strengthened, now more than ever, in a context of global instability, and i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ i supported this resolution. the european union and the united nations face common challenges: the pursuit of peace and security, the prevention of conflict, the fight against terrorism, the promotion of human rights, action for sustainable development, the defence of an international system based on multilateralism. the union must therefore contribute to solving these challenges through its foreign policy, while promoting its interests and values. the union must, for example, promote the development of global governance within the united nations and increase its influence and that of its member states within this system. it must win a seat on an enlarged security council. it should work to strengthen the un's mediation capacity and call for peacekeeping missions to be based on coherent mandates. it is the union's responsibility to live up to the role it intends to play, because it must be understood that if the union fails to meet this imperative, its very model will be put at risk.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which suggests ways for the european union to better achieve its foreign policy objectives at the united nations. as stated in article 21 (1) of the eu treaty, the european union and the member states share the values and principles of the un charter. it is necessary to recall that the european union contributes actively to the work of the united nations; the commission has therefore decided to initiate the procedure laid down in article 93 (2) of the treaty in respect of the application of the principle of equal treatment. the european union is able to speak at all un meetings, but also to propose amendments and submit resolutions, but the eu institutions present in the un system enjoy very little visibility. i also supported this report because it recalls that the union is committed to actively supporting a reform of the un system in order to consolidate its legitimacy and effectiveness and to strengthen its authority.
in writing. ‒ since 2011, the eu has enjoyed the status of 'privileged observer' in the united nations and is no longer represented there only through its member states. this resolution therefore intends to provide guidelines for such participation. some of the reforms are interesting, such as the reform of the appointment process of the secretary-general, which has been too opaque so far; the european union is also calling for the abolition of the right of veto of members of the security council in cases of genocide and crimes against humanity, or the introduction of a binding instrument on multinationals in the field of human rights, as proposed by ecuador. but, on the other hand, the establishment of an investment protection regime within the un system - the infamous "arbitration mechanisms" of ttip or ceta - or the establishment of coordination between the wto and the un to "promote a trade and investment strategy" has no place in the multilateral framework based on universal rights and values, and is part of a well-known ultra-liberal drift. i therefore abstained on this report.

vice-president of the commission.– madam president, i would like to thank all who have spoken. three points in closure. firstly, it is very important at a time of increased uncertainty that we have a budget that is agile, has a clear focus on priorities and is oriented towards impact and how to give the people the best value for the money they entrust us to manage on their behalf. that would require us to take the forthcoming mid-term review very seriously. this is our chance to strengthen the agility, focus and capacity of our budget, and also to look to the future as regards the kind of budget we would like to have next time around. secondly, many of the speakers expressed a very understandable concern about the limited flexibility we have. but we still have some flexibility for next year; that is the contingency margin, if needed, of no more than eur 4 billion. we have the contingency margin and, of course, we will only be using it if that is necessary. we will have the possibility towards the end of the year to use a global transfer; in other words, money that is not put to the best use. we should not rush headlong into using this option; we should try to keep it as a kind of cushion. last but not least, we now have a chance to receive funds from our member states, as assigned revenues for priorities that we all recognise are best addressed together. for this we have the syria trust fund and the africa trust fund, and we, the commission, are proposing to provide the platform for addressing priorities in that manner. thirdly, there was a question addressed to me: what is the commission going to do in the long term to deal with the challenge of migration? this is one question that is not going to disappear. it was mentioned that climate change is upon us. the projections of the ipcc tell us that by 2025 there may be 100 million climate refugees. so, we have to direct our resources at tackling the problem at source and tackle the root causes that are causing the problem here in europe. for this reason, we have refocused our development funds more on fragility – i also want to praise prime minister cameron of the uk, who has recently announced that 50% of dfid funds will go to fragile countries. i think we need to do more where it matters the most: for the people affected, but also for our own security. of course, we will have to invest more in the security of europe. the commission has promised to come up with a proposal on how we can strengthen external border controls, and that is an area where i believe that collectively we have a better chance to be successful than acting alone. let me finish by thanking those who have made this budget miracle possible, and may we have it repeated next time around.

in writing. ‒ the resolution calls on the commission and the council not to allow the recycling of plastic materials containing the plasticizing additive dehp for the production of pvc for the manufacture of, inter alia, footwear or floor coverings, because of its reproductive toxicity. dehp has been the main phthalate in common use for the last 50 years. it has been classified as a substance of very high concern under the reach regulation and may not be used without the authorisation of the european chemicals agency (echa). the use of dehp is also prohibited in the production of toys, articles for children and cosmetics. the commission has proposed, in a draft decision which requires the council's agreement, to allow the recycling of old dehp-containing plastics for the manufacture of new products. dehp is known to disrupt the endocrine system of mammals, including by lowering the level of testosterone in the foetus. it can affect the rate of development and reproductive ability of the individual. for these reasons i have decided to oppose the commission's draft decision.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament rejected by a very large majority (603 votes in favour, 86 against) the request to specially authorise the recycling of 'pvc plastics containing dehp', a chemical belonging to the group of phthalates used to make plastic more flexible. this substance is an endocrine disruptor that disrupts the human reproductive system. considered dangerous, it has been gradually withdrawn from the european market since 2014, but can be used on the basis of a specific authorisation. the commission wanted to allow its recycling for seven years on the grounds that phthalate-free plastics would be too expensive, while the european chemicals agency (echa), which has assessed applications from companies, has highlighted the disastrous consequences of this substance on the hormonal system. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of dehp in all other products. i voted in favour of this resolution of the european parliament which puts human health before economic competitiveness.
in writing. ‒ the taxe committee has issued its final report on tax write-offs and other aggressive tax optimisation measures in the european union. his work, following luxleaks, has more generally made people aware of the schemes of certain unscrupulous multinationals that allow them to escape almost all taxes. the damage to the public finances of the member states is considerable: 10 to 15 billion euros a year for france, for example. since most of these installations are illegal, new forms of regulation must be found. the text makes recommendations to the member states and the commission on the implementation of transparency measures and the limitation of the possibilities for rescripts and other similar measures affecting tax competition, where they prove to be unfair. the final report is a statement of the awareness of the situation, but it does not prejudge the measures to be taken. on the exchange of rescripts directive, a corollary of the work of taxe, the council's position of 6 october last was disappointing. i therefore voted in favour, despite some reservations.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which aims to combat tax evasion. i am in favour of the principle that multinational companies should pay their taxes where they make their profits. i believe that at the moment, corporate tax competition which encourages aggressive tax planning and tax avoidance without any common framework is harmful. apart from the loss of public revenue, i consider it unfair that large companies pay very little tax on their profits while citizens and smes have to pay the full price.
in writing. ‒ this report, following the luxleaks scandal, has raised awareness of the schemes of certain unscrupulous multinationals that allow them to evade almost all taxes. the damage is estimated at up to €15 billion per year in france alone. the mandate of the taxe committee will be extended for six months to allow access to certain confidential documents, but we have to decide today on the final report, which i am in favour of. this text makes recommendations to the member states and the commission, in particular on transparency and limiting the possibilities for tax optimisation. examples include luxembourg tax rescripts, the parent/subsidiary regime and the taxation of patent income in the netherlands, and the irish is rate. i support this text in general, particularly in terms of sanctions against multinational companies that practice this fraud. i also support increased protection for whistleblowers. i also think that better cooperation between states is a step in the right direction. but i do not support european harmonisation of the rates of the isd because i remain committed to the sovereignty of the states in tax matters.
in writing. ‒ if we agree with the finding in this report that there are: - many flaws in the tax systems of european countries which allow multinationals to successfully engage in tax optimisation; - too many tax write-offs; - too many disparities between member states; we cannot accept some of its recommendations, particularly on the harmonisation of isf rates, even though we support the oecd recommendations on this matter, sanctions against multinationals that have committed fraud and whistleblowers. we remain in favour of the principle of unanimity in tax matters and look favourably on the encouragement of cooperation between neighbouring states in tax matters, as advocated in this text. for all these reasons i vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ the report aims to combat the tax optimisation practices of large multinationals in order to massively reduce the taxes they have to pay. the shortcomings in national legislation, which are exploited by the large groups without scruple, create a financial damage for the member states which, in the case of france, amounts to more than 10 billion euros per year. the report calls on the member states to strengthen their cooperation in the exchange of data in order to detect more quickly the companies that are engaged in these irregular tax arrangements. it is also recommended that member states introduce transparency measures and limit the possibilities for rewrites. the report also provides for the harmonization of the corporate tax base in order to concentrate competition on rates and to better regulate transfer prices between subsidiaries of the same company. we approve almost all the measures outlined in this report, even if we consider that the project is still not ambitious. on the other hand, we are formally opposed to the harmonization of the sdr rate, which limits the budgetary levers of the member states in the context of a short-term policy. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report of the special committee taxe which had been set up following the revelations of the luxleaks scandal. the aim of this committee was to highlight and provide solutions to unrestrained and unfair competition between member states in the tax field. the report calls for greater fiscal convergence between the eu member states and greater transparency. unfair tax competition between member states too often benefits large multinational companies at the expense of smes and european citizens. in this sense, it is essential that companies pay their taxes in the country where they carry out their economic activity. i consider this report to be a vital step towards the necessary tax harmonization within the european union.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report presents the european parliament's recommendations to strengthen the fight against aggressive tax planning and tax evasion. following the luxleaks scandal at the end of 2014, which revealed the existence of controversial tax practices in some member states, the european parliament responded to citizens' questions by setting up a special temporary committee on taxation in february 2015 (the taxe committee). the report suggests that it is unfair that large companies pay very little tax on their profits while small and medium-sized enterprises and citizens pay the full price, and suggests requiring multinationals to report on country-by-country financial data and introducing a common consolidated corporate tax base. parliament also called for more transparency in the tax agreements between member states and these companies. i support these objectives and consider that the work of this committee has helped to speed up the debate on the fight against tax evasion, so i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. in the face of the economic and fiscal crisis that has been shaking europe for several years, it is important that the eu commits itself to the establishment of a european tax system that does not favour one country at the expense of another. that is why i voted in favour of this report, which will make it possible to ask multinationals to pay their taxes where they make their profits.
in writing. ‒ following the luxleaks scandal, the european parliament set up a special committee to investigate corporate tax evasion and fraud in the european union. a serious and exhaustive survey of the methods used by multinationals was carried out and several recommendations were made to combat these practices which are contrary to the principle of equality before tax. this is not just a luxembourg issue, but one of many other european countries which have given unusual tax advantages to certain entities or even to certain states, leading to undesirable distortions of tax competition. one possible answer is fiscal harmonisation within the euro area.
in writing. ‒ following the revelations of the luxleaks scandal, a special committee was set up in the european parliament: the taxe committee. i voted for his final report on tax rulings and other measures similar in nature or effect. the text supports the establishment of a common consolidated corporate tax base (ccctb). this means that companies will have to pay taxes in proportion to their profits in all the european countries where they operate. in addition, in view of our historical positions and the expectations of european citizens, i voted in favour of extending the commission's investigations into state aid and transfer pricing for the companies mentioned in the luxleaks. i am also in favour of introducing a country-by-country reporting mechanism for multinationals, like the oecd and the french national assembly. finally, i think it's essential to protect whistleblowers.

in writing. ‒ the current european regulatory framework for the improvement and prevention of risks in the working environment consists of 25 directives derived from a framework directive adopted in 1989. the proliferation of legal texts shows the futility and the profound stupidity of the european project as it is conceived today. the strategic framework in question aims to simplify legislation under refit, while parliament wants to undertake further work to broaden the employment forms covered by this framework and to address new challenges. the house also called for the commission to be given greater powers to monitor the implementation of the framework agreement on health and safety at work and to ensure that the labour inspection services are sufficiently numerous and well trained. with my colleagues from the front national and the enl group, we believe that undertaking further work to increase standards and strengthen enforcement does not appear to be the priority in the current context. a revision of the directive on posted workers must be given priority. that is why i voted against this report.

in writing. ‒ since 1989, the principle of establishing standards to improve the prevention of risks in the working environment has been reflected in a european legislative framework comprising some 25 directives. standards are multiplying in every possible area. this makes it difficult to apply in national law and to put into practice. the commission wants to simplify legislation under refit, while parliament wants to undertake further work to broaden the employment forms covered by this framework and to tackle emerging risks such as psychosocial or musculoskeletal disorders. parliament wants to support smes in order to promote the framework agreement on health and safety at work and to ensure the training of labour inspection services. i think that the legislative framework needs to be simplified, as many accidents at work affect undeclared jobs, and it would be more useful to revise the directive on posted workers, for example. i voted against this because, although i think that improving health and safety at work is important, we cannot continue to impose complex standards on companies.
in writing. ‒ 25 european directives are already aimed at preventing risks linked to the working environment. since 1989, the framework directive has guaranteed decent working conditions for european employees, but leaves the member states free to grant them additional social benefits. this type of harmonization helps to combat social dumping in some eastern european countries. however, introducing additional constraints and adopting a stricter regulatory framework does not seem to be a sensible approach, especially in times of economic crisis, as small and medium-sized enterprises and smes would suffer from this type of measure. the text also calls for improving the prevention of accidents and occupational diseases at european level, which will lead to a proliferation of legislative measures that will make it more difficult to transpose into national law and apply it in practice. the text also proposes to integrate new emerging risks such as psychosocial or musculoskeletal disorders into the regulatory framework. i therefore voted against this report.

in writing. ‒ this report, voted by a large majority, should shake the commission, which is dragging its feet in improving the living conditions of workers in the company. the european parliament called for better protection of workers from carcinogens and mutagens and asked the commission to set more exposure limit values for these substances. this is essential in the construction sector where employees are often exposed to asbestos and tar, among other things. the text also recognises the dangers of endocrine disruptors, which are particularly harmful to women. but we must go further and the commission must present a strategy to prevent such risks as soon as possible. it is equally vital to recognize the risks of stress, including burnout. according to the european agency for safety and health at work, more than half of all workers report that they experience stress at work frequently. in europe, stress is the second most frequently reported work-related health problem. it was therefore urgent for parliament to alert the commission to this.
in writing. ‒ every year, more than 4 000 workers die as a result of accidents at work and more than 3 million people are victims of serious accidents resulting in more than 3 days' absence from work. in the face of these alarming figures, europe must act and find solutions in the field of health and safety at work; i therefore voted in favour of this report on the new eu strategic framework for occupational safety and health 2014-2020. the existing health and safety rules must be better enforced and the prevention of work-related diseases improved. health and safety in enterprises must be a priority and information must be better disseminated as they are the source of better performance and competitiveness. the aim is also to improve enforcement controls and to strengthen the coordination of national labour inspectorates. finally, it is important that all these measures can be implemented in a simple way, so as not to penalise our smes and small businesses.
in writing. ‒ working towards more standards and closer enforcement does not seem to be a priority in the current context. in addition, it is well known that a high proportion of accidents at work affect people in undeclared jobs: a revision of the directive on posted workers would be more appropriate. while reducing occupational risks is a relevant objective at european level, the simplification of the legislative framework under refit is a top priority. it is high time we stopped adding standards to the burden of business. i therefore vote against this text.
in writing. ‒ every year, more than 4 000 workers die in accidents at work and more than 3 million suffer serious injuries. the number of accidents at work has decreased in recent years, but progress in the field of prevention, health and safety at work in the union remains below expectations. the report by parliament calls for the highest level of protection of health and safety at work to be ensured for all workers, irrespective of the size of the undertaking employing them, and for an assessment of the practical implementation of the directives on health and safety at work in the member states. the importance of social dialogue and worker representation in reducing the negative impact on the physical and mental health of workers of the increase in precarious work in the union requires addressing psychosocial risk factors. that's all there is to it. this report is paved with good intentions. i voted in favour, but i have no illusions about the possibility of their being implemented by the member states.

in writing. ‒ this text of the resolution on the state of play of the doha agenda is intended to prepare for the december wto conference in nairobi. the doha round is the negotiation of an international free trade agreement under the auspices of the world trade organisation, which has been ongoing since 2001. fourteen years after the start of this cycle, the agreement seems to be on the wrong track, much to the chagrin of the european union, which would like it to succeed, as the text recalls. parliament called for the cycle to be extended with a view to establishing an even more successful international free trade system without constraints on the market and for the adoption of legally binding international standards while dismantling the rules imposed by nation states. the text also proposes that the wto should be able to deal with 'non-trade issues' so as not to 'impede market access' to the detriment of states, which would mean an unprecedented abandonment of sovereignty and the development of a materialistic logic for areas such as health or culture. so despite calls for more democratic transparency in trade negotiations and for an agreement that is favourable to smes and developing countries, i voted against this text.

in writing. ‒ as a supporter of free trade between nations, i support the idea of reforming the world trade organisation (wto). i believe that a more efficient structure of this organisation and a more detailed assessment of individual economies will make it possible to better achieve the wto's main objective. i see it in the removal of trade barriers, which in turn will bring economic development and lower prices for consumers.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the state of play of the doha development agenda in the run-up to the 10th wto ministerial conference to be held in kenya from 15 to 18 december 2015. this is the first time such a conference has been held in an african country. this conference particularly emphasises the objectives of emerging economies. the objectives are varied and concern the vision of our economies, which must be seen in all their diversity. smes and small businesses need to be supported to ensure that trade facilitation is complete. i fully support this initiative, which must succeed in proving today that multilateralism in trade matters still exists.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution which sets out the position of our assembly in the run-up to the next wto ministerial conference. the doha round has several objectives: the creation of new trade opportunities, the strengthening of multilateral trade rules and the correction of current imbalances in the trading system, in particular with regard to the needs and interests of developing countries, and in particular the least developed countries. the means to achieve these objectives must therefore be provided. this requires, in particular, structural reform of the wto and a trade agenda based on a multilateral, free and fair system, for the benefit of all, and with development at its core. common rules must also be obtained and enforced. the wto's cooperation with other relevant international organisations should also be encouraged. in addition, the democratic legitimacy and transparency of the wto must be enhanced by strengthening its parliamentary dimension. the union, as the world's leading trading power, must make progress in the negotiations and ensure that the cycle is concluded in a balanced and realistic manner, while respecting its objectives.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text, which sets out the european parliament's official position for the negotiations to be held in nairobi from 15 to 18 december in the context of the tenth wto ministerial conference. it is essential to recall that the multilateral level of trade negotiations remains a priority for the european union and that the wto has its full support. in this sense, it is important to take into account in the negotiations the special needs and interests of low-income developing countries and ldcs (least developed countries), while stressing that a clear definition of these countries must be established. we also support a reform of the wto which allows for an open, fair and non-discriminatory trading system and an ambitious, comprehensive, balanced and realistic outcome for the doha development agenda. it is also urgent that the trade facilitation agreement be ratified and implemented swiftly. finally, we should point out that our work in the parliamentary committee has made it possible to recall in the text that certain sectors, such as agriculture, remain sensitive and must be treated differently in terms of trade.
in writing. ‒ the doha round is the ongoing negotiation for an international free trade agreement under the auspices of the wto. it started in 2001 and 14 years later the agreement is on the wrong track, much to the chagrin of the commission and the european parliament who would like it to succeed. india is blocking any deal because of its defence of agriculture. the european parliament calls on the wto to establish an even deeper global free trade and to dismantle individual country standards to establish global standards. he even proposes that the wto should be able to deal with these "non-trade issues". these additional surrenders of sovereignty would be dramatic because they would prevent states from legislating. parliament welcomed the sectoral free trade approaches such as the agreement on environmental goods, information technologies, tisa (decommissioning of public services)... it calls for wto agreements to be legally binding. finally, this is a classic global free trade agreement which i oppose.
in writing. ‒ the 10th wto doha ministerial meeting will take place in nairobi from 15 to 18 december. the aim of this resolution is to define the position of the european parliament before the meeting. unsurprisingly, this resolution is a plea for global trade, making it one of the responses, if not the answer, to the current economic stagnation via the all-out pursuit of trade liberalization that ignores the failures of previous negotiations. better still, the resolution goes so far as to call on the more advanced developing countries to take their share of responsibility in economic development. my group, the gue/ngl, has tabled amendments to denounce this hypocrisy and the negotiations dictated by the interests of the northern countries alone. amendments rejected of course. so of course i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ the union and ecuador signed in december 2014 an accession of ecuador to the existing free trade agreement between the union, colombia and peru. this asymmetrical agreement aims to make it easier for ecuador to develop, but above all it asks the european commission to ensure that human, labour and environmental rights are well respected in ecuador. the european parliament notes, however, that despite all its human rights demands to ecuador, the government has reduced poverty by almost half in eight years. i opposed this text, which constitutes a new case of interference by the union in the internal affairs of a sovereign state.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report, which welcomes this new free trade agreement while expressing the human rights paternalism which the union still claims to exercise over these latin american countries.
in writing. ‒ the union and ecuador signed in december 2014 an accession of ecuador to the existing free trade agreement between the union, colombia and peru. this asymmetrical agreement should make it easier for ecuador to develop. the report welcomes this free trade agreement and even calls for monitoring of the banana quota produced by ecuador, which is one of the world's largest producers. unfortunately, this report still interferes with the country's politics by calling for respect for human rights, labour or the environment, but parliament recognizes a halving of poverty in 8 years in ecuador. i do not support this report which welcomes this free trade agreement with a rather strong (though benevolent) interference in the internal politics of ecuador.
in writing. ‒ the union and ecuador signed in december 2014 the accession of this south american country to the free trade agreement in force between the union, colombia and peru. this asymmetrical agreement is supposed to promote the development of ecuador. the report calls on the commission to ensure that human rights are well respected in ecuador. the european parliament also called for banana quotas to be respected, as ecuador is one of the world's largest producers. the european institutions are taking advantage of this agreement to interfere in ecuador's internal affairs. this interference is intolerable, since their government has succeeded in halving poverty in eight years. finally, we cannot but oppose this report which welcomes a free trade agreement. that is why i voted against this text.

in writing. ‒ by voting on the scholz report, the european parliament was called upon to give its directives on the process of accession of ecuador to the trade agreement concluded between the union, peru and colombia. the final text gives strong support to the approach of the european commission and the ecuadorian government, which will, however, have to step up their efforts if they want to achieve ratification of the agreement. the european commission believes that a balance needs to be struck between a firmly protective approach for small ecuadorian farmers and one that does not disadvantage european banana producers (especially in the overseas territories). the ecuadorian government, for its part, is asked, before ratifying the agreement, to put in place convincing measures to combat child labour, deforestation and respect for trade union rights. these are essential prerequisites for the signing of a trade agreement with the union. i voted for this resolution, but i want to remain vigilant. i do not rule out abstaining from voting on the final agreement if it does not take due account of the concerns of the european parliament.
in writing. ‒ the report welcomes the accession of ecuador to the trade agreement currently in force between the eu and colombia and peru. the agreement, concluded in 2012, aims to establish a free trade area with the eu and the south american countries concerned. to this end, it provides for the abolition of customs duties and prohibits any future protectionism: "no party shall adopt or maintain prohibitions or restrictions on the importation of goods from another party or prohibitions or restrictions on the exportation, or the sale for exportation, of goods to another party". in this context, the priority objective, enshrined in the ecuadorian constitution, of developing fair trade, may be called into question by the union. moreover, in a completely neo-colonial attitude, the report welcomes "the important efforts made by ecuador in the field of the environment" even though this country is more committed to the defense of the environment than all the states of the european union. i am voting against this text.
