in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on the accession of ecuador to the trade agreement concluded between the european union and peru and colombia. the aim is to allow that country to join its neighbours, colombia and peru, in the preferential trade relationship they have with the union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the accession of ecuador to the trade agreement concluded between the union and peru and colombia. large business groups are now being established or consolidated on every continent. the asean countries, mercosur, west africa are coming together to form regional groups whose aim is to trade more easily, more freely by reducing trade barriers. europe must use its lead to get our partners such as ecuador to facilitate the import of european products into its territory. it is in this spirit that ecuador should be bound by the existing trade agreement with the countries of the region, peru and colombia. europe will now have easy access to the ecuadorian market. however, ecuador is the world's leading producer of bananas. the risk of an explosion in ecuadorian banana exports to europe to the detriment of european producers (i am thinking particularly of the outlying regions) will be contained by the quota set out in the agreement and, above all, by the possibility of applying safeguard measures at the slightest warning sign. my role will be to monitor this market closely to prevent any risk to our producers and consumers.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on the accession of ecuador to the trade agreement concluded between the european union and peru and colombia. on 26 june 2012, the union signed a free trade agreement with colombia and peru after six years of negotiations. negotiations with ecuador were suspended in 2009 and resumed in 2013 at the request of ecuador. the protocol of accession was finalised on 17 july 2014, allowing ecuador to join the peru/colombia agreement. we are satisfied with this agreement on the degree of openness of public procurement and on market access with the abolition of customs duties for many products and the introduction of transitional periods for other products. the text also recalls the sensitivity of the agricultural sector, especially bananas, given that ecuador is the world's largest exporter. a stabilisation mechanism is provided for under the agreement and will be triggered if certain thresholds are exceeded, so as not to jeopardise our european production. we will ensure that the commission respects its proper functioning and will remain attentive to its effective implementation.

in writing. ‒ the european union is currently engaged in trade negotiations with mercosur. the european parliament thus takes a position on the free trade agreement between the european union and ecuador, which is still under negotiation, as it did with the agreements previously concluded with colombia and peru. the rapporteur, my colleague helmut scholz of die linke, stressed the need to respect social and environmental rights. investments have been made by the ecuadorian government to improve access to health and education and to fight poverty. the agreement, however, mainly promotes the opening of the ecuadorian market to mining companies and the development of neoliberal industrial and economic policies. these economic and industrial exploitations risk permanently degrading areas of the amazon rainforest, causing the displacement of local farmers and worsening the situation of indigenous populations, not to mention the risks to workers' rights. i therefore chose to abstain on this resolution.
in writing. ‒ i support the adoption of an animal welfare strategy for 2016-2020, if it is to extend the content of the one currently in force, which runs until the end of 2015. this strategy enables us to ensure that the various existing laws are properly applied in order to ensure better harmonisation within the internal market. no one needs to create new rules for this. it should also help us to include animal welfare in the scope of the union's trade policy, particularly in its non-tariff component. indeed, it is appropriate to require the rejection of free trade agreements which do not ensure that imported products fully comply with the union's animal welfare standards, in order to prevent any distortion of competition for products from third countries. finally, this strategy should enable us to reaffirm the need to provide sufficient budgetary resources in the cap to help farmers to better meet the requirements of animal welfare legislation, and more particularly in the area of standardisation.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the joint resolution on a new strategy for animal welfare because i believe that animal welfare must be part of the common values cherished by the member states of the union and by any civilized country. i regret, however, that this resolution does not dare to go to the end of its own logic and to put its finger where it hurts. in fact, in the ritual slaughter of animals prescribed by certain religions, notably islam, the needless suffering inflicted on animals demonstrates how the welfare of animals is considered by certain groups of people to be something that should not be respected. the legislation of some member states now allows ritual slaughter only after the animals have been subjected to anaesthesia for religious sacrifice. it is time that this obligation was extended to the whole of the union.
in writing. ‒ i hope that this resolution will enable us to establish a new animal welfare strategy for the period 2016-2020. efforts have been made in the 2011-2015 strategy, but we must now go further and remove all ambiguities. without touching on the competitiveness of our farmers, who are already hard hit by the crisis, i think it is necessary to give a lasting and financial boost to agricultural policies with animal welfare standards: the gradual abolition of cage systems, of farming on quail, of animal suffering, etc. we must also combat extensive farming, which puts us at risk for health and the environment, but also for animal welfare. i voted in favour of all the amendments which go towards more animal protection and i regret that many of my colleagues did not follow this path. i have supported food labelling on slaughter and farming methods, i have condemned the illegal trade in animal species, i have supported the ban on ritual slaughter without anaesthesia or the strengthening of animal protection rules during transport. finally, i also supported funding for research into best practices to eliminate animal testing. i voted for this text.

in writing. ‒ this resolution calls on the european commission to renew its animal welfare strategy for a period of four years. the current strategy is due to expire at the end of 2015. it is a matter of being realistic and measured in our approach. since 2006, when the first welfare strategy was launched, much has been done and parliament has adopted a whole series of legislative acts to improve animal welfare, such as the zootechnics regulation, for which i am the rapporteur, the organic production regulation, the official controls regulation and the ban on the practice of cloning for commercial purposes. the present resolution is therefore balanced, since it has been possible to reject a whole series of excessive amendments tabled by the left-wing groups. sceptical of the idea of implementing horizontal legislation in this area, i unsuccessfully opposed paragraph 3 which calls on the european commission to adopt a comprehensive and up-to-date legislative framework on animal welfare; the commission has not yet adopted a proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos. nevertheless, i voted in favour of this resolution.

in writing. ‒ the text underlines the paramount importance of education in conflict zones. indeed, education has a major role to play in the reconstruction of post-conflict societies. furthermore, children with access to education are less at risk of forced marriage, early pregnancy, membership in armed groups, radicalization, trafficking in human beings. however, the text proposes to integrate teachers from displaced communities, which could quite logically generate a phenomenon of communitarianism. the text also calls for the creation of 'educational corridors' which would enable students from these conflict zones to continue their studies at a european university. in these circumstances, the desire for very long-term integration seems to supplant the original objective of temporary local aid and thus prevents any social reconstruction in the countries of origin. the general idea is good, but its application is not suited to the challenges ahead. so i refrained.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because, according to the united nations, one billion children live in conflict zones, 250 million of them under the age of five and are deprived of their fundamental right to education. an estimated 65 million children aged 3 to 15 are affected by emergencies and long-term crises and are therefore at risk of dropping out of school, and some 37 million children are out of school in primary and lower secondary education in countries experiencing crises. about half of the world's schoolchildren live in conflict-affected areas; in the arab states, 87 per cent of out-of-school children are affected by conflict and an estimated 175 million children are at risk of being affected by natural disasters each year. moreover, some groups, such as poor children, girls and children with disabilities, are seeing their already reduced prospects further diminish in conflict-affected areas or in fragile settings. let us mobilize to save their future!
‒ the education of children in crisis situations and in protracted crises is one of the most pressing issues of our time. although not seen much on television news, it is one of the most negative effects of the situation of millions of people forced to live in refugee camps after being driven from their homes. supporting the functioning of education in such conditions must be a top priority. personally, i think that after protecting lives, health and ensuring adequate nutrition, education must come first. we're fighting for the next generation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the education of children in emergency situations and long-term crises. humanitarian crises have been many throughout history. millions of children have been and are victims of conflict. ignoring them is making them a lost generation. and lost generations are the breeding ground for the next conflicts. to avoid this, a link must be established, a framework for the education of children in all situations. the wars against the terrorist organization daesh, or boko haram in nigeria, show that children are at the heart of these conflicts. to prevent children, witnesses and victims of conflict, from growing up to become adults, perpetrators of conflict, let us maintain an educational link and invest in all generations, wherever they may be.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the education of children in emergency situations and long-term crises. according to the united nations, one billion children live in conflict zones, 250 million of them under the age of five, and are deprived of their right to education. some 65 million children aged 3 to 15 are at risk of dropping out of school and 37 million children are out of school in primary and lower secondary education. and children who are not in school are more at risk of early marriage and pregnancy, of being recruited into the regular army or armed groups, of being trafficked and forced to work. quality education can also play an important role in the long term in the reconstruction of society after conflict. finally, education should be a priority in humanitarian aid, development aid and the allocation of resources from union funds. we call on all the member states of the union to support the commission's objective of increasing by 4% the european humanitarian aid budget for education in emergencies.
in writing. ‒ according to un figures, around half of the world's schoolchildren live in conflict-affected areas and an estimated 65 million children aged 3-15 are affected by emergencies and crises. in view of these alarming figures, the european union and the international community must act urgently. i therefore voted in favour of this text, which calls on the member states to support the commission's objective of increasing the share of the union's humanitarian funds for the education of children in emergency situations to 4%. as we face and respond to the refugee crisis, host countries must ensure that refugee children have full access to education. finally, the union must work with partner countries to improve the education of children in conflict situations and prevent them from becoming targets of armed conflict. the european union must act for the generations of tomorrow.
in writing. ‒ despite the fact that this is a good initiative, there are several problematic points in this text. while the proposal calls on member states to provide access to education for refugee children and adolescents by integrating them into national education systems and facilitating their learning of the host country's language, it also proposes to integrate teachers from displaced communities, which could create a phenomenon of communitarianism. the integration of refugee students in transit into the universities of member countries is also one of the directives of this text which calls for the creation of "educational corridors" to allow students from conflict zones (syria, iraq and eritrea in particular) to continue their studies in european universities. i therefore choose to abstain.
in writing. ‒ we are experiencing one of the worst humanitarian crises the world has seen since world war ii. today, half the world's schoolchildren live in conflict-affected areas. the schooling of children exposed to emergency situations requires almost eur 7.5 billion a year and the funding gap in this area now stands at over eur 4.5 billion. while eu aid is increasing, with €4.7 billion in developing countries for education for 2014-2020 (compared to €4.4 billion for 2007-2013), this is still well below actual needs. the resolution calls for more resources, in particular to achieve the millennium development goals on education, and supports the establishment of a global education emergency financing mechanism to address current shortcomings. unfortunately, rather than reminding member states of their commitments, this resolution calls for more private sector investment. commercializing education and humanitarian aid cannot be the solution. while the military intervention in mali alone has cost about a billion euros, more than ever, i believe it is all a matter of political choices. so i chose to abstain.

in writing. ‒ i abstained on this text on the search for simplification and efficiency in cohesion policy for 2014-2020. it recognizes that administrative procedures are too complex and require real simplification. unfortunately, this text also calls on the commission to provide a road map to the member states and even advocates strengthening direct relations with local authorities to the detriment of national authorities. i cannot therefore support this party which wants to wipe out the sovereignty of nation states in favour of eu/local relations.
in writing. ‒ this motion for a resolution acknowledges that the complexity of administrative procedures reduces the effectiveness of the structural funds in the member states of the european union. the text stresses that beneficiaries, in particular smes and small businesses, may no longer have an interest in making applications, as the costs of obtaining these funds are sometimes too high. simplification would therefore help to increase the absorption rate of funds. we are pleased to see that the european institutions are becoming aware of the negative consequences of their bureaucratic system for economic actors. we are, however, opposed to the commission making further recommendations to the member states. we believe that the main factor in the present administrative complexity is the commission's refusal to review its internal functioning. finally, we are absolutely not in favour of the union strengthening its relations with local authorities as called for in the text. i therefore abstained on that text.
in writing. ‒ cohesion policy is essential to achieve the growth and employment objectives set out in the europe 2020 strategy. the structural funds which make up cohesion policy enable european citizens to finance their various projects. these funds must be made available as soon as possible so that this financing has a direct impact on the real economy and on job creation. in this context, it is imperative that the procedures for obtaining these funds be simplified so that they can be allocated more quickly to the recipients. of course, controls are necessary. it's not just about funding any project. however, we must not get lost in a bureaucracy which would scare away the smallest project promoters. i voted in favour of this report and therefore for a more effective cohesion policy.
in writing. ‒ this resolution calls for greater simplification and efficiency in cohesion policy, despite the efforts already made through better regulation and policy reform in the framework of the 2014-2020 programming period. the european parliament points in particular to the existing over-regulation, including in the process of transposition of european rules by national authorities, and the administrative burden caused by complex procedures which discourage applicants for european funds. the resolution calls on the european commission to provide member states and regions with detailed guidelines and a roadmap to streamline and simplify control, monitoring and reporting activities, including for beneficiaries. i support the objectives of this report and am convinced of the importance of european funds to support economic and social development projects at local level, so i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the search for simplification and efficiency in cohesion policy because i believe that action is urgently needed to ensure that project promoters applying for european funds are no longer discouraged by the complexity of the procedures. management costs, the number of supporting documents and processing times are all factors which discourage potential beneficiaries, especially the 'smaller' ones. while controls are necessary and legitimate, a better balance must be found to reduce the share of european funds absorbed by bureaucracy. much progress therefore remains to be made in simplifying the rules applicable to beneficiaries and fund managers, both on the part of the european commission and on the part of the member states, which too often add administrative layers when transposing european texts. in my view, access to finance for smes and the development of online procedures should be given priority. this resolution was adopted by a large majority, which i welcome.
in writing. - i abstained on that resolution. it is true that it recognizes the need to simplify administrative procedures. but it advocates strengthening the union's relations with local authorities at the expense of the states.
in writing. ‒ the report proposes to simplify the rules on the european structural and investment funds (esi funds) on the assumption that they are still too complex for both the beneficiaries and the managing authorities. it is true that small and medium-sized enterprises, ngos and municipalities, which need eu funding, often lack the financial and human resources and the skills to successfully apply for and manage eu grants. the report therefore proposes 'simplifying the language' or establishing a single window for regional funding. the commission is also urged to encourage member states to 'significantly reduce the administrative burden and over-regulation' which affect, in particular, 'procurement procedures, the selection of project proposals and monitoring and control activities'. i believe, on the contrary, that strict controls are essential when public money is involved. i abstain on this report.

in writing. ‒ today, due to overly complicated procedures and over-regulation, and more particularly in the transposition of directives, many smes, ngos and micro-enterprises face inequalities in access to public procurement and subsidies. the joint lack of skills and financial resources in fact penalises them in certain administrative procedures such as public procurement or grant applications. the resolution proposal on the search for simplification and efficiency in cohesion policy for 2014-2020 aims to provide solutions to this complexity. that is why i voted in favour of this proposal, which is aimed in particular at reducing the administrative burden which is mainly and arbitrarily borne by the smaller structures. the text encourages the member states to simplify the regulation of public procurement by standardising procedures and to streamline and simplify control activities.
in writing. ‒ i supported this resolution which calls for a simplification and greater efficiency of cohesion policy for the period 2014-2020. procedures under the european structural and investment funds remain complex, both for the beneficiaries and for the managing authorities. this complexity, which particularly affects small beneficiaries such as smes or municipalities, must be reduced. to this end, in particular, administrative burden and over-regulation in procurement procedures, the selection of project proposals and monitoring and control activities should be eliminated. for example, we need stability of rules and standardization of procedures. in addition, the deadlines for the transition to e-cohesion must be respected, the sharing of good practice must be encouraged and the use of the multi-fund approach increased. cohesion policy is an essential instrument to support our territories and their people in their development and the exploitation of their wealth. we must therefore use all the levers we can to improve its operation.
in writing. ‒ the application, management, reporting and controls of the structural funds are still too complex despite the european union's desire for simplification. the procedures for beneficiaries, especially smes, who need european funding, present many obstacles. i therefore voted in favour of this text, which makes a clear statement and on which all the parties involved agree. it called on the commission to provide the member states and their regions with a roadmap to streamline and simplify control, monitoring and reporting activities, including for beneficiaries, in order to eliminate the difficulties currently encountered. it is urgent that everyone should be able to benefit from european funds, and that without hindrance.

i'm the reporter. madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, tomorrow 80% of europeans will be living in cities: that is why mobility should be a right for everyone. for those people who travel to work or to buy goods, for those people - and especially young people - who go to school, for those who go to the dentist or the doctor, and for those who go to the cinema or the stadium for entertainment: basically, mobility is our everyday life. however, much remains to be done to ensure that mobility benefits everyone, as it is still far from being chosen. most often, it is suffered, because of traffic jams, because of the loss of time, because of air pollution. the reason for this is the excessive use of the private car, which runs on traditional fuels. cities were built for cars: let's give cities back to the people, because there's a climate emergency. we're in the middle of cop 21. urban transport alone accounts for 25% of greenhouse gas emissions. it is up to us to reverse the trend if we want the european union to meet its 2030 emissions targets. there's also a public health emergency: in 2015, breathing kills. 400,000 premature deaths a year are caused by fine particulate matter emitted by diesel engines. should we, when we have pollution peaks, lock up pregnant women, children, the elderly to keep their lungs intact? there is no time to wait. pollution is the disease of the 21st century, as the un recognizes. there is also urgency with regard to our independence. the energy consumption required for our transportation makes us too dependent on oil dictatorships, now in the spotlight. there is also an urgency for the lives of road users. 38% of road deaths occur in urban areas. how can we reduce the number of deaths in cities if we do not reduce the use of cars? finally, there is a social emergency: 25 million european households are the new mobility precarious because they have little or no access to public transport, or because it is too expensive. so another form of mobility is not only possible, but essential. if we want to re-think how we move, we need to consider the social, environmental, economic and democratic impacts of transport. we must take into account the present and future generations. to achieve this, the european union must set itself ambitious targets. in the midst of cop 21, let us put energy efficiency at the heart of our urban mobility policies. this will happen, whether we like it or not, with the exit of diesel, with the disappearance of our urban centers from traditional gasoline cars by 2050. this will also be achieved by developing clean transport: tramways, cable cars, bicycles, car-sharing, which generate jobs. this will be achieved by shifting from road to river and from road to rail, but also by intermodality through the combination of walking, cycling and public transport. the obstacles are very, very many. there are all kinds of lobbyists here; the commission has already made a number of proposals, including the famous car lobby, the status quo lobby, which will do everything to prevent these proposals from being implemented. but we must not forget our responsibility. ambitious legislation is needed if we really want this commission - your commission, madam commissioner - to be the commission of last resort, as mr juncker says and reminds us. the europeans are waiting for us at the crossroads and are counting on us to move forward. so i say: let's not disappoint them, urban mobility must absolutely be a priority.
madam president, urban mobility is one of the major challenges of the 21st century because it is at the crossroads of the three pillars of sustainable development: ecology, economy and social. working towards sustainable urban mobility means making a concrete contribution to the fight against air pollution and global warming. with transport accounting for 25% of co2 emissions, with increasing urbanisation and hundreds of thousands of people dying every year from air pollution, we have a political responsibility to make sustainable mobility a key issue in european policies. i therefore call on all members to support amendment no 1, which raises the fundamental problem of diesel and calls for initiatives to move towards clean fuels and out of subsidies for diesel. working for sustainable urban mobility also means fighting social exclusion and ensuring territorial cohesion. this is a fundamental aspect of the mobility issue and i regret that during the debate in committee the right wing blocked amendments to strengthen the social dimension of the report.
member of the commission.– madam president, i wish to thank members for all their comments and for the questions they raised. allow me to comment a little bit more and give you more information about our next steps. we are all becoming more and more aware of the multidimensional challenges that urban mobility presents. with the 2011 transport white paper, the commission set the objective of a competitive and resource-efficient urban mobility. the urban mobility package of 2013 addressed in greater detail how to achieve these objectives, but this report gives new impetus to the implementation of that package. with parliament’s support, the commission will concentrate efforts in the area where eu action can bring added value but with full respect for the subsidiarity principle. in particular, we are planning to: pursue a more holistic approach to smart, sustainable and resilient cities; further support cities, industry and r&i by promoting a marketplace for trading solutions; offer cities and innovative projects promoters support for real—life testing under horizon 2020; help cities to use different eu funding opportunities, and to combine public and private investment, for instance from the european fund for strategic investment; and run platforms – as one of you also mentioned – for exchange of practices, since at eu level this can have a much bigger impact than many think. let me now directly respond to some of your questions and comments. as regards freight, by all means, you have full support for that from me. the 2011 white paper already talked about nearly—zero—emissions city logistics by 2030, so green urban logistics are in our programme and in our minds. the second question was on road safety, which is a very important element, especially for the most vulnerable in traffic. a lot of work has been done, but we are pushing member states on a daily basis to do even more. we especially work very closely with the countries that statistics have shown to be the worst, with the direct involvement of all stakeholders in the country to bring fatalities figures close to zero in the future. by the way, bikes, as mr cramer and some other colleagues have mentioned, are one of the important elements of the green freight solutions in cities so yes, this topic will not go away and we will continue to address it and look for options on how to support it even further. there were a couple of questions and comments regarding diesel. clearly we need to improve the overall system that allows cars to be placed on the market – the type-approval system. we need more european oversight, effective control mechanisms and better quality and greater independence of vehicle testing. we need to move – and i fully support this – from lab testing to real driving emission tests for co2 as soon as possible. at the same time, i do count on the electrification of transport being delivered, as we expect, in the near future. as regards awareness raising, the commission for example has been promoting multimodality with the ‘do the right mix’ campaign as part of european mobility week and has focused attention on walking and cycling in combination with an increased use of public and collective transport as a good way forward for all of us. allow me also quickly to go back to the comment regarding cycling. please, let us not underestimate the economic benefits that this brings, not only in health, but also the positive effects on congestion and co2 and, of course, the positive effect on the transport industry. i welcome the council’s declaration, and we will work within our mandate to support it. finally, allow me also just to say a couple more words regarding the overall subject. long-term engagement at all levels of governance is key to making european cities smart, well-connected and green, and the commission is ready to support the emergence of new ideas within our mandate. they are the stakeholders that can drive prosperity and offer quality jobs. within my portfolio, 2016 is the year for decarbonisation and i am sure that we will address urban mobility very comprehensively as part of that initiative. i am counting on members’ support and am really looking forward to making our planet look even better than it does today.

in writing. virunga national park is the most biodiverse park in africa. it has been on the unesco world heritage list since 1979 and is home to many iconic species (gorillas, okapis, elephants, etc.). oil exploration and exploitation, combined with a host of illegal activities, can cause irreversible damage to the park. it is threatened by this exploitation, but also by the exploitation of gas and minerals that feed all the greed, whether of multinational companies or of local armed groups or terrorists. at present, more than 140 people have already been killed in the drc in virunga national park. once again, economic interests take precedence over the environment, nature and the human race as a whole. against the principle of interference, i believe we must cooperate jointly with the drc, the united nations and all possible local actors to ensure the safety and preservation of this magnificent park and its species. we must also find a way of putting pressure on the european multinationals in the drc to respect the principles of human rights and the environment in the region.

in writing. ‒ the european union has put an end to banking secrecy by means of the council decision of 20 march 2014. there are now automatic exchanges of information between member states. austria and luxembourg were reluctant and demanded that switzerland and liechtenstein take similar measures because of their proximity to the eu countries, which in fact created unfair competition. as was the case for switzerland at the third plenary session in october, the european parliament was called upon to give its opinion on the protocol amending the agreement between the european community and the principality of liechtenstein. the agreement contains provisions which will limit the possibility for taxpayers to evade their reporting obligations to the tax authorities. tax transparency and the end of banking secrecy are necessary to limit capital flight. i therefore voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ this report concerns the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the protocol amending the agreement between the european community and the principality of liechtenstein providing for measures equivalent to those laid down in council directive 2003/48/ec on taxation of savings income in the form of interest payments. the amending protocol aims to implement the single global standard for the automatic exchange of financial account information between the member states of the union and liechtenstein. this standard was published by the oecd council in july 2014. this agreement is the follow-up to the eu-switzerland agreement signed last month, which marks the end of banking secrecy in liechtenstein, via the adoption of the oecd standard. in return, it should allow luxembourg and austria to abandon banking secrecy at union level. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ in order to convince the austrian and luxembourg authorities to ratify the agreement on the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts, which was signed in march 2014, the european union negotiated with liechtenstein the end of banking secrecy, which created unfair tax competition in europe. the agreement, which will take effect from 2017, provides for the automatic exchange of data between the member states of the union and liechtenstein on income, account balances and capital gains on the sale of financial assets. these measures will considerably reduce the ability of europeans to evade taxation in their home countries and will enable member states to recover tax revenue owed to them. we are in favour of this cooperation, which will limit tax evasion in europe. that is why i voted for this text.
in writing. ‒ this report proposes to strengthen the measures to combat tax fraud and evasion between the european union and liechtenstein. it aims in particular to make it more difficult for union citizens to conceal their assets from their national tax authorities. under the agreement, the union and liechtenstein will automatically exchange information on the financial accounts of residents of each other as of 2018. these will include income, interest, dividends, balances and proceeds from the sale of financial assets. i have supported this report because i believe that tax fraud and tax evasion are a penalty for citizens, because they drain the resources of the state and create a feeling of injustice.
in writing. the agreement on the automatic exchange of information relating to financial accounts signed between the european union and liechtenstein provides for the strengthening of cross-border tax cooperation. the measures provided for in the framework of this agreement are essential to strengthen the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion in europe. that is why i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ this report concerned the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the protocol amending the agreement between the european community and the principality of liechtenstein providing for measures equivalent to those laid down in council directive 2003/48/ec on taxation of savings income in the form of interest payments. thus, the application of this agreement in liechtenstein avoids distortion of competition. the rules must be respected by all parties to the agreement within the european economic area. i am also committed to financial transparency and have voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this report because it is in favour of greater financial transparency.
in writing. ‒ in march 2014, the automatic exchange of information at eu level sealed the fate of banking secrecy within the european union. this was not without the reluctance of austria and luxembourg. one of the conditions for the abandonment of banking secrecy by these countries was the acceptance by switzerland and liechtenstein of similar measures, in order not to create unfair competition. the loones report on the memorandum of understanding provides for an automatic exchange of information between the union and liechtenstein on the financial accounts of their respective residents as of 2017. liechtenstein will apply measures on automatic exchanges equivalent to those provided for in eu directive 2003/48. in addition, the agreement provides for a limitation of the possibilities for taxpayers to evade their reporting obligations by transferring their assets or by investing in financial products that do not fall within the scope of the agreement. the information to be exchanged concerns not only income but also account balances and proceeds from the sale of financial assets. it is important not to leave a country which practices financial opacity at the doorstep of the union, unless we see a continuation of capital flight. i voted yes.

in writing. ‒ this report aims to approve the taxation agreement concluded between the european union and liechtenstein in october 2015. the agreement will increase tax cooperation and compliance at international level through the establishment of an automatic exchange of information on financial accounts. the new agreement would thus contribute to the fight against tax fraud and evasion, but in view of the tax practices tolerated within the european union (massive tax evasion in luxembourg revealed by the luxleaks case), there are legitimate doubts about its effectiveness. the text excludes issues related to the taxation of pensions and insurance benefits, while life insurance represents the first investment vehicle. finally, it is possible to derogate from this agreement via the 'exemption from disclosure of information', which applies under conditions which are too broad and ill-defined. i'm not going to.

in writing. ‒ at a time when member states are putting more emphasis on external border control, it is all the more important to have the resources to consolidate the rights of migrants and asylum seekers. the socialists and democrats fully support the contents of this report and the recommendations of the european ombudsman. it is essential that frontex has an individual mechanism for handling complaints about fundamental rights. this mechanism should also apply to the working agreements signed by the agency with certain third countries, which allow, in particular, the organisation of joint return operations. these texts are not covered by international law. they therefore do not require both parties to respect the fundamental rights of migrants and asylum seekers. moreover, parliament does not know how they are implemented on a daily basis. the complaints mechanism will provide greater transparency in the face of possible violations of fundamental rights that would otherwise go undetected, unreported and unresolved. this will be a first step towards ensuring that the fundamental rights of migrants and asylum seekers are respected by frontex at the eu's borders and beyond.
in writing. ‒ in this report, which i voted for, we recall the importance of ensuring that frontex respects the fundamental rights and the rights of migrants, refugees and asylum seekers. the agency has already started efforts to this end. however, there are still areas of shadow. the effective handling of individual complaints should be encouraged when allegations of fundamental rights violations by border guards wearing the frontex badge are detected during the course of frontex operations. the office of the entitlement officer should play a leading role in this mechanism. for guest officers, for whom frontex cannot take disciplinary action, we recommend that the fundamental rights officer's office should forward complaints through a referral system to the national competent authority. the fundamental rights officer must also have the necessary resources to deal with complaints in the best possible way. finally, i would point out that our assembly relied on the recommendations of the european ombudsman in determining its position.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which supports the european ombudsman's recommendation that the european union's external border management agency, frontex, establish an individual complaint handling mechanism to deal with allegations of fundamental rights violations in the course of its operations. in view of the refugee crisis and the growing number of humanitarian and legal challenges facing frontex, it is necessary, as requested by the european ombudsman, for the european agency to put this mechanism in place. the report makes a number of proposals to make such a mechanism viable and possible. the european union must ensure control of its external borders and strengthen cooperation between member states.
in writing. ‒ a few days after the paris attacks on 23 november, the committee on civil liberties and the committee on petitions, meeting under an accelerated procedure, voted a resolution on frontex to facilitate complaints by migrants against border guards. this resolution provides that frontex, the european border management agency, facilitates complaints from migrants about possible violations of their rights, even though they are themselves present on our territory illegally. this procedure also allows third parties, such as heavily subsidised ngos, to lodge complaints on behalf of migrants. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. all of this, of course, has one goal: to reduce the number of evictions even further, which is already almost zero. it seems important to monitor the votes of the socialists and republicans who have recently shown their firmness on immigration and security. i am therefore logically opposed to the adoption of this text.
in writing. ‒ this report proposes to tackle pollution and noise in cities. no one is against it. however, it is surprising that this kind of problem can be tackled by the european institutions with large reinforcements of urban mobility observatories, commission action agendas or 'european mobility weeks', or concepts such as the 'sharable city'. and then there are the myriad expensive programs and "green growth" strategies! all this is wind and a lot of waste. the report is obviously intended to pave the way for a supranational governance to regulate the behaviour of individuals and to punish 'ecologically deviant behaviour'. the text thus promotes measures such as 'polluter pays' or the obligation to introduce speed limits of less than 30 km/h in urban areas. so i logically voted against it.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this text, where once again meps are using good pretexts to create bad policies to the detriment of the people and the member states. the delli report on sustainable urban mobility, for example, lays the foundations for an urban policy driven by the european commission, rather than a management by municipalities more in tune with the needs of their cities and their inhabitants. urban mobility plans will have to be subject to the timetables and objectives of the european commission. in addition to this disregard for the principle of subsidiarity, the objectives set by the report, if well-intentioned, will be achieved at the expense of the most modest households, which may not always be able to afford to invest in a vehicle with the latest standards or to buy a home close to their place of work. the 'polluter pays' principle is thus gradually gaining ground, ignoring social and economic realities. finally, all the new measures proposed represent an excessive cost which will not solve the real problems facing municipalities.
in writing. ‒ this report proposes to tackle air and noise pollution in city centres. on this principle, no one can object. the report does not, however, give us a clear indication of the means by which this objective can be achieved. unlike the rapporteur, we do not believe that the european institutions are best placed to reduce the level of pollution in the agglomerations. supranational ecological governance would be bureaucratic and therefore counterproductive. the commission uses such reports to give itself additional powers to impose outrageous measures on member states and local authorities, such as the requirement to drive at less than 30 km/h in urban areas or the principle of alternating traffic. we believe that this responsibility lies solely with the national authorities and local authorities, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity. that is why i voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report aims to promote a new mode of urban mobility by mobilising eu financial instruments to develop and maintain urban transport infrastructure. the main idea is to reserve part of the european funds such as the erdf, the cohesion fund, or horizon 2020 and its european fund for strategic investments (efsi), for sustainable urban mobility projects. in support of this objective, however, we have worked with my colleagues in the epp group to rebalance the approach of the rapporteur, whose initial proposals were considered unrealistic, particularly as regards the use of the car. i opposed several paragraphs in the vote on car-free sundays, on drastic reductions in conventional fuel vehicles in cities or on the use of part of the toll revenue to improve urban mobility. such decisions are the responsibility of the member states or local authorities, but should not be taken at european level, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity. nevertheless, considering that improving urban mobility through more varied and environmentally friendly modes of transport is a key challenge for our cities, i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. i supported this own-initiative report on sustainable urban mobility as part of the fight against global warming. a more sustainable and intelligent management of the mobility of people and goods in europe is essential to improving the quality of life of european citizens.
in writing. ‒ in a context of urban densification on the one hand and the need to connect all territories to each other on the other, i voted in favour of this resolution, which promotes smooth urban mobility based on the development of reliable, smart, greenhouse gas-saving and easily accessible public transport. as a former regional president, i have long advocated an integrated approach to mobility that limits the use of private transport solutions and reduces air pollution, noise, accidents, congestion, etc. intermodality must therefore be organised. urban planning must accompany and anticipate new shared uses. the prices should be incentive and take account of the different constraints of the day (courses, school pickup, etc.). as president of the intergroup on public services, i draw attention to the need to include all the populations in this dynamic, those on the periphery of the cities, but also those in the countryside, who often have no other choice but to take their own vehicle or, failing to have one, to be placed under house arrest and deprived of mobility, which is known to be one of the factors of involvement in the city.
in writing. ‒ the report aimed to promote the reduction of noise, pollution and congestion in cities. while the objective is certainly commendable, the methods proposed to remedy it are far from convincing. the report proposes, for example, 'european mobility weeks' or 'sharable cities'. apart from the utterly utopian and vague nature of these proposals, the report seeks above all to promote supranational ecological governance. while the peoples of europe are all yearning more and more for a return to sovereignty, europe is blatantly flouting the principle of subsidiarity. the re-emergence of pleasant, healthy and less congested city centres is due to the development of small local businesses and short-distance transport. the report proposes even more european union without stating that it is ineffective in the areas it deals with. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it is in favour of supranational ecological governance.
in writing. ‒ this text is well-intentioned (combating urban pollution). however, it is questionable whether the european institutions are best placed to address the problems raised. the principle of subsidiarity is at stake: anything that is not the exclusive competence of the union can only come to the union if its institutions are better placed to know about a matter. however, it is the municipalities that are best placed to tackle these problems. the unspoken aim of such a text is to pave the way for supranational ecological governance. the commission wants to increase its powers and impose inconsistent measures which will weigh heavily on the low-income households who cannot afford, for example, to buy a vehicle with the latest standards. in addition, municipalities will be required to introduce speed limits of 30 km/h in urban areas, as will alternating traffic. my colleagues from the national front in the committee called for the principle of subsidiarity to be fully respected and pointed out that improving the flow of traffic requires saving small shops in the city centre and returning to short circuits. i voted against the resolution.

president of the eurogroup.– mr president, in my final contribution, i would just like to pick up on a couple of points that the members have made. first of all, i think building the monetary union – and the same goes for the banking union – is about solidarity and organising it in our social economic system. therefore it is about reducing risks, becoming more resilient, becoming stronger and more flexible, and, at the same time, gradually sharing risks. that is the only way forward. that is the way we have built the banking union and must complete it, and that is the way we must strengthen the monetary union. ms de lange asked me whether it was not first about reducing risk and then sharing risks. i think that is too simple. we are at the moment in a phase of building up the banking union. as of 1 january 2016, new rules will apply. we are starting to build up the resolution fund, which will be complete in eight years’ time, and gradually we will share the risks inside the resolution framework. so it will go hand in hand. yes, we will start sharing risk in the banking union. we already do now, and in the coming eight years we will continue to do so until it is a fully common system. it is about the two approaches at the same time, and that is the only way to get it done – politically as well. ms ferreira was absolutely right when she said that you cannot leave economic policy up to the ecb. the ecb is already far beyond what can reasonably be expected from monetary policy with a very accommodative stance. so it is now up to politicians at national and european level. it is for both national and european levels to take their responsibilities, and that is also about applying what has been agreed. how can you build a common system and how can you build a union if you cannot apply the rules, and if you will not stick to the rules and the agreements that have been reached? ms ferreira also asked me about the fiscal stance for the eurozone. at the moment a neutral stance for the eurozone as a whole is a reasonable approach, but there are big differences between countries. some can do more, but there are limitations: there are few countries that actually have a fiscal surplus at the moment and could invest more. so there will be a different approach at national level in the fiscal stance and, overall, in the eurozone a neutral stance is, at this time, the right position to take. for the future we need to have that debate about the fiscal capacity. we have put it in the second phase of the five presidents’ report, but there is no reason why we should not debate it now, because there are many different ideas of what a fiscal capacity could mean. some see it as a common backstop for our monetary union, some see it as an investment instrument, and some see it as a social security funding system. these are very different approaches. let us debate that, because only if you have an agreement on the design of it do you know what size it has to have. then you have to find agreement on where the funding is to come from. these are big questions that will touch upon our labour market policy, on our social security system and possibly even our pension systems. it depends very much on how you design this fiscal capacity, and there is no agreement as yet on what their instrument should look like. so let us do the work on that and let us not wait until 2017. many of you have spoken about the responsibilities of member states and i fully agree. when you talk about structural reforms, part of it – a major part, i would say – is national responsibility and will probably be so for a very long time. the issues vary from one country to another, yet some are very much the same in all of our eurozone countries. the tax pressure on labour is much too high, forcing labour out of our economy. let us reverse that process. we are working on that in the eurozone, and many countries are taking measures there. we need further work on the pension system to make it sustainable, also in greece. pensions systems need to be sustainable if we want to insure our pensioners, also in the future. part of the structural reforms will also have to throughout europe. let us diversify that, become more resilient and strengthen economic recovery. i have to react to mr eickhout who always, when i meet him in brussels or here in strasbourg, addresses me as a dutch minister. his point is that i say different things in the national parliament than i do in the european parliament. i never do that. i always stress both the importance of this european dialogue and that of the national parliament. i strongly disagree with him that in national parliaments there is no serious debate about the european economy or european economic governance. he should come to the dutch parliament to participate in those debates. they are in depth, broad and serious, and i have to go to my parliament at least twice a month to discuss those issues. finally, mrs berès asked me about flexibility in the pact. over the course of the crisis, the pact has proven to be flexible. a number of countries have been given more time to deal with their fiscal deficits. fiscal targets have been adjusted over and over again. the real question is whether we can, in time, build fiscal buffers into our budgets again. that is my greatest concern: that we still have high sovereign debts, many countries still have high deficits, even though a lot of work has been done, and if a new economic setback were to occur, we do not have enough buffer capacity. on the flexibility that the commission has proposed: i strongly agree with that kind of flexibility, but it should be used well. the commission should take the requests for flexibility of the member states seriously and make sure that the credibility of the pact is not damaged. there is a balance between the flexibility in the pact and the credibility of the pact. finally, we have a lot of work to do in the short term. so let us have a debate about long-term monetary union governance, let us start that debate now, but let us also work on the very short—term measures we can take. i have already mentioned the banking union, competitiveness, structural reforms and the capital markets union, etc. there is work to be done.
mr president, the euro area is in danger. we must admit that its architecture is banking, since it has a monetary pillar based on the european central bank, which is essentially federal, but it is still without the indispensable budgetary and political pillar. the adjustments made since 2012 are progress, but the euro area still lacks an economic policy. it adds up national policies, framed by the stability and growth pact, a pact regularly violated by many countries and which is nothing more than a regulation on co-ownership of the euro. the euro area unlike the united states of america cannot practice the policy mix, i.e. support for growth and employment. it is urgent to equip it with the appropriate institutions so that it can finally be steered and governed: appointment of a full-time minister of finance whose function is incompatible with the office of minister in one of the euro area member states, availability and conflict of interest issues; the establishment of a treasury directorate-general to coordinate the management of government borrowing, strengthen the banking union, stabilise financial markets and guarantee deposits; the establishment of a euro area budget to neutralise systemic shocks and to encourage, by means of a bonus, structural reforms and investment; the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. and as a corollary, i think it is essential to place this new governance under the democratic control of a committee with representatives of the european parliament and representatives of the national chambers. any sharing of sovereignty requires democratic legitimacy. so, mr president, i urge you to be bold and courageous. i believe in the benefits of the euro, which means that we urgently need to remedy the fragility of the euro area.
mr president, i will speak anyway, but i am a little surprised that neither the president of the commission nor the president of the eurogroup responsible is here. so, who are we talking to, anyway? i would like to remind you that in 2012, before i was elected by that abominable mrs le pen, did we not propose a stimulus programme based on the central bank with the large public banks, using quantitative easing to invest in the real economy, in transport and energy infrastructure, in smes, in export development. this plan was blocked because of the german initiative. as long as there are no transfers to invest and balance the levels of the economy in a single area, the euro is doomed. yet you continue to do so. you are responsible for the failure of the euro, not us.
madam president, once again we are being offered little measures and wishes to improve the functioning of the euro area. but no further involvement of the european parliament will change that. no technocratic mechanism, camouflaged under increasingly light democratic umbrellas, can hide the reality: the euro is a total failure. it is a failure because it is based, from the beginning, on false principles. forcing monetary union between the countries of europe has not brought them together and will never bring them together. on the contrary, economies are becoming more and more divergent, european countries outside the euro are doing much better. the poor are getting poorer, the rich are getting richer, tensions are rising, people are rising against each other. they are being asked to make unsustainable sacrifices to save a currency, instead of putting the economy at their service. the greeks have been humiliated and are humiliated more and more every day. other peoples will soon be. many nobel prize winners and renowned economists have said it, and reality proves it in a relentless way: we must abandon this aberrant golden calf, we must stop sacrificing people to save the euro and instead sacrifice the euro to save people.
madam president, mr vice-president of the commission, the economic crisis of 2008 has shown two things: first, that our economic and monetary union, despite the displeasure of some, was an effective tool and shield for our national economies; the second is that we must, of course, go further in this union and the convergences it requires if we are to withstand the future shocks that are bound to come. our economic and monetary union is incomplete and certainly too fragile. focusing on the financial stability that is so necessary, it has neglected growth, which is also so necessary for economic recovery. i welcome the initiative of president juncker, who, in his state of the union address, has placed this issue at the heart of his priorities. i also welcome the fact that the democratic framework within which these reforms must take place has been taken into account, with the establishment of national competitiveness councils and a european budgetary committee. it is wise not to repeat the mistakes we have sometimes made in order to go faster, by not involving the europeans and their representatives enough in decision-making. these two bodies, like the european semester, will have to make economic competitiveness and growth a priority in order to create sustainable jobs and strengthen our economic and monetary area, that is to say, to strike the right economic and political balance between reducing member states' deficits and implementing recovery policies. in conclusion, i would like to address a short message to all those who are sceptical or opposed to such a strengthened union: what would be the weight of any european country with a population of no more than 80 million in relation to the other economic powers? how can we weigh and assert our positions without uniting on a continental scale? the idea of national isolation is dangerous not only for our economies but also for our democracies. political courage is about adapting to and anticipating a world which is constantly changing, not about denying it.

in writing. ‒ the gabriel report aimed to remove the visa requirement for the commonwealth of dominica, vanuatu, trinidad and tobago, samoa, grenada, east timor, saint lucia, saint vincent and the grenadines and the united arab emirates. these countries do not pose a risk of uncontrolled immigration or of disturbing public order. however, at a time when islamist terrorists are looking for the slightest loophole in our defence in order to attack us, i do not think it is appropriate to exempt certain countries from visas and to facilitate access to our territory in general from non-european countries. although i am in favour of closer economic ties with these countries, i cannot knowingly take the risk of allowing ill-intentioned people to take advantage of this to undermine european security. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this resolution because i am against visa-free travel for third countries.
in writing. ‒ if we take the particular case of vanuatu, i see no particular difficulty in lifting the short-stay visa requirement, i.e. three months over a period of 180 days, for nationals of this small island in oceania with a christian majority. the risk of migration is very low. however, beyond vanuatu, i question the strategic choice to grant short-stay visa exemptions in a hand-to-hand fashion when for some of these countries, particularly those in the western balkans, the migration and internal security risk to the member states of the european union is real. there is a regulation which lists a positive list of countries whose nationals are exempt from the short-stay visa requirement. these countries now number 42, including the united states and japan, and will soon be 61. shouldn't this list be revised in the light of international upheavals?
in writing. ‒ these agreements on the short-stay visa waiver are designed to intensify trade, increase investment and boost tourism. it is important to note that the visa refusal rate is low for these countries, which according to the report pose no threat either in terms of irregular migration or in terms of security and public order. nevertheless, the timing of such agreements, even as the porosity of europe's borders is a breeding ground for terrorism in europe, seems incongruous. i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, ms mariya gabriel, on the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the agreement between the european union and the republic of vanuatu. the european parliament was to take a decision on the conclusions of the agreement between the union and vanuatu which was negotiated by the commission. the purpose was to make it easier for people to obtain visas. citizens of both sets will be exempt from visa requirements for stays of up to 90 days for a period of 180 days. this exemption does not apply to persons travelling on business. this recommendation was adopted by a large majority, which i welcome.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the eu-vanuatu agreement on the short-stay visa waiver. according to ms gabriel's report, the country in question poses no threat either in terms of illegal migration or in terms of security and public order. as regards mobility, confidence in visa applicants is high, with a relatively low visa refusal rate. visa liberalisation simplifies the conditions for travel. however, we have a duty to ask ourselves whether it is appropriate to conclude visa waiver agreements at a time when the risk of terrorist attacks is real and when the european union has lost all control over mass immigration.
in writing. ‒ fn mps voted against this agreement because they are hostile to the short-stay visa exception, which it endorses. visas are required for national security purposes, except for those with our trusted partners, particularly european ones.
in writing. - i voted against this deal. as in the previous case, this is a series of agreements on the short-stay visa exemption with several countries. the agreement is expected to help boost tourism and strengthen trade and investment relations with these partners. the key to these agreements is trust: the visa refusal rate is very low because countries trust visa applicants. the rapporteur believes that the countries covered by these agreements do not represent a threat, either in terms of irregular migration or in terms of security. in view of the mass immigration we are experiencing and which the eu is no longer able to manage, in view of the risks and the recent attacks in france, one can only be surprised, or even worried, by this sudden willingness to open up. maybe the timing isn't right!
in writing. ‒ on the substance of the matter, i am in favour of short-stay visa exemptions to facilitate the mobility and travel of citizens of both parties, in this case the member states to the state of vanuatu and vice versa. i regret, however, that the french overseas departments are excluded. i'm officially denouncing this whole procedure. only the commission is empowered to negotiate these agreements on behalf of the states and citizens. it informs the european parliament of the state of the negotiations only at the very end of the process. above all, these agreements are implemented even before the european parliament gives its approval or not. the eu has a role to play in this process, and the eu is not a party to the treaty of amsterdam. in these circumstances, i vote against.
in writing. ‒ these agreements on the short-stay visa waiver are designed to intensify trade, increase investment and boost tourism. it is important to note that the visa refusal rate is low for these countries, which according to the report pose no threat either in terms of irregular migration or in terms of security and public order. as regards the united arab emirates, it should be noted that 150 000 eu nationals are established there and most of them work there. about 1.6 million europeans visit the uae each year, and some 230,000 emiratis have travelled to europe, mainly for business trips and luxury tourism. nevertheless, the timing of such agreements, even as the porosity of europe's borders is a breeding ground for terrorism in europe, seems incongruous. i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ these agreements provide for visa-free short-stay travel to the listed countries, in order to boost tourism and strengthen trade and investment relations. visa liberalisation will simplify travel conditions for entrepreneurs, facilitate investment and intensify economic links between businesses. as regards mobility, confidence in visa applicants from these countries is high, with a historically low visa refusal rate. the rapporteur believes that the countries in question do not represent a threat either in terms of illegal migration or in terms of security and public order. however, the question arises whether it is appropriate to conclude visa waiver agreements at a time when the risk of terrorist attacks is real and when the european union has lost all control over mass immigration. the answer is no, hence a vote against.
in writing. ‒ like the previous report, this one is about facilitating the issuance of visas, but this time for vanuatu. economic ties with the country are expected to intensify, resulting from a relationship of increased trust through the visa exemption. however, even if the rapporteur assures us that this country does not represent a threat to the security of the eu's territory or to its migration policy, the timing of these liberalizations does not seem appropriate. i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this agreement on the short-stay visa waiver between the european union and the republic of vanuatu. the aim was to allow visa-free travel for european and vanuatu nationals travelling to the territory of the other contracting party for a stay of up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by our colleague mariya gabriel on the agreement between the european union and vanuatu on the short-stay visa waiver. this agreement provides for a visa-free travel regime for nationals of the two parties concerned who are travelling to the territory of the other contracting party for a stay of up to 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa exemption covers all categories of persons (holders of ordinary, diplomatic, service/official or special passports) travelling for all purposes other than paid employment.
in writing. ‒ like the previous report, this one is about visa facilitation, but this time for vanuatu. economic ties with the country are expected to intensify, resulting from a relationship of increased trust through the visa exemption. however, even if the rapporteur assures us that this country does not represent a threat to the security of the eu's territory or to its migration policy, the timing of these liberalizations does not seem appropriate. i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ i supported the approval of the eu-vanuatu agreement to abolish the requirement for visas for short stays, i.e. for stays of less than 90 days for all categories of persons (ordinary, diplomatic). it is important that european citizens can travel to vanuatu without a visa and vice versa. this visa exemption should hopefully enable us to support this small pacific island, which was hit hard by the cyclone pam last march.
in writing. ‒ this agreement seals the visa exemption for very short stays and on the basis of reciprocity with vanuatu. a way to make it easier for our citizens to travel, whether it's for tourism or business.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text on the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the agreement between the european union and the republic of vanuatu on the short-stay visa waiver. the agreement provides for a visa-free travel regime for citizens of the union and of vanuatu when they travel to the territory of the other contracting party for a stay of up to 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa exemption applies to all categories of persons (holders of ordinary, diplomatic, service/official or special passports) travelling for any purpose other than gainful employment.
in writing. ‒ these agreements on visa-free short-stay visits are expected to boost tourism and strengthen trade and investment relations. visa liberalisation would simplify travel conditions for entrepreneurs, facilitate investment and intensify economic links between businesses. however, the question arises as to whether visa-free agreements are appropriate at a time when the risk of terrorist attacks is real and the european union has lost all control over mass immigration. this change in visa policy is contrary to common sense. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the agreement with the republic of trinidad and tobago on the short-stay visa waiver. while the report presents the liberalisation of visas for short stays as an opportunity to boost tourism, simplify travel conditions for entrepreneurs or encourage investment, i believe that at the moment it is not appropriate to conclude similar agreements. in the face of a growing terrorist threat and the european policy of mass immigration, these agreements seem inappropriate to me. indeed, even if the republic of trinidad and tobago is not directly a point of departure for immigration, i do not consider it advisable to proceed with such an agreement in the current context, regardless of the country concerned.
