in writing. ‒ as in previous reports on visa liberalisation, i voted against this visa exemption text for the samoan islands, as it is not appropriate to implement this policy at a time when the union is unable to know who is entering its territory.
in writing. ‒ i supported the approval of the agreement between the european union and samoa which aims to abolish the requirement for visas for short stays, i.e. for stays of less than 90 days for all categories of persons (ordinary, diplomatic, etc.). it is important that european citizens can return to samoa without a visa and vice versa. i hope that this visa exemption will help to support the tourism sector in this pacific island.
in writing. ‒ this agreement seals the exemption of visas for very short stays and on the basis of reciprocity with samoa, a way of facilitating the travel of our nationals, whether for tourism or business.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text on the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the agreement between the european union and the independent state of samoa on the short-stay visa waiver. the agreement provides for a visa-free travel regime for citizens of the union and for nationals of samoa when travelling to the territory of the other contracting party for a stay of up to 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa waiver is open to all categories of persons (holders of ordinary, diplomatic, service/official or special passports) travelling for any purpose other than gainful employment.
in writing. ‒ these agreements on visa-free short-stay visits are expected to boost tourism and strengthen trade and investment relations. visa liberalisation would simplify travel conditions for entrepreneurs, facilitate investment and intensify economic links between businesses. however, the question arises as to whether it is appropriate to conclude visa-free agreements at a time when the risk of terrorist attacks is real and when the european union has lost all control over mass immigration. this change in visa policy is contrary to common sense. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the agreement with grenada on the short-stay visa waiver. while the report presents the liberalisation of visas for short stays as an opportunity to boost tourism, simplify travel conditions for entrepreneurs and encourage investment, i believe that at the moment it is not appropriate to conclude similar agreements. in the face of a growing terrorist threat and the european policy of mass immigration, these agreements seem inappropriate to me. indeed, even if grenada is not directly a point of departure for immigration, i do not think it is wise to proceed with such an agreement in the current context, regardless of the country concerned.
in writing. ‒ this agreement calls for the short-stay visa exemption for persons coming from grenada. the aim is to intensify trade, increase investment and boost tourism. it is important to note that the visa refusal rate is low for these countries, which according to the report pose no threat either in terms of irregular migration or in terms of security and public order. however, it is not appropriate to conclude such agreements, even though the porosity of europe's borders is a breeding ground for terrorism in europe. we are also opposed, together with my colleagues in the national front, to this desire to create a world without frontiers. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this debate as the committee had recommended in the background.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this text which endorses the agreement with grenada on the short-stay visa waiver. since the european union refuses to control its external borders as it should and has abolished internal borders in the schengen area, it is urgent that france regain control of its national borders and apply its laws, particularly in the area of border control. i am therefore opposed to such agreements on principle.
in writing. ‒ these agreements on visa-free short-stay visits are expected to boost tourism and strengthen trade and investment relations. visa liberalisation will simplify travel conditions for entrepreneurs, facilitate investment and intensify economic links between businesses. the report also states that the country poses no threat in terms of illegal migration, security or public order. however, it is questionable whether it is worthwhile to conclude visa-free agreements at a time when the risk of terrorist attacks is real and the union has lost all control over mass immigration. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ according to the report, these agreements on the short-stay visa waiver should boost tourism and strengthen our trade relations with grenada. these new arrangements will facilitate the movement of entrepreneurs and investors, which will intensify economic links between companies. the commission has also proposed that the council adopt a decision on the conclusion of the agreement on the european economic area, which is to be signed by the european union and the republic of moldova on 1 january 2005. but at a time when western countries, and france in particular, are facing a very serious terrorist threat, it is absolutely not appropriate to conclude such agreements. that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ this report proposes that the european parliament give its consent to the conclusion of the agreement between the union and grenada, negotiated by the european commission, to facilitate the issuing of short-stay visas. it allows citizens of the european union and citizens of grenada to obtain a visa free of charge for the territory of all the contracting parties for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period. this visa is for all categories of persons (holders of ordinary, diplomatic, official and special passports) travelling for any purpose other than gainful employment. i voted in favour of the report, in support of these objectives.
in writing. this short-stay visa waiver measure will allow for a strengthening of political dialogue and economic relations between the eu member states and grenada. i voted for this measure to bring our territories closer together.
in writing. ‒ the gabriel report aimed to remove the visa requirement for the commonwealth of dominica, vanuatu, trinidad and tobago, samoa, grenada, east timor, saint lucia, saint vincent and the grenadines and the united arab emirates. these countries do not pose a risk of uncontrolled immigration or of disturbing public order. however, at a time when islamist terrorists are looking for the slightest loophole in our defence in order to attack us, i do not think it is appropriate to exempt certain countries from visas and to facilitate access to our territory in general from non-european countries. although i am in favour of closer economic ties with these countries, i cannot knowingly take the risk of allowing ill-intentioned people to take advantage of this to undermine european security. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this resolution because i am against visa-free travel for third countries.
in writing. ‒ if we take the particular case of grenada, i see no particular difficulty in lifting the short-stay visa requirement, i.e. three months over a period of 180 days, for the nationals of this small, sparsely populated island state located 200 km north of venezuela. the risk of migration is very low. however, beyond grenada, i question the strategic choice to grant short-stay visa exemptions in a hand-to-hand manner when, for some of these countries, particularly those in the western balkans, the migratory risk and the internal security of the member states of the european union is real. there is a regulation which lists a positive list of countries whose nationals are exempt from the short-stay visa requirement. today there are 42 of these countries, including the united states and japan, and soon there will be 61. should not this list be revised in the light of international developments?
in writing. ‒ these agreements on the short-stay visa waiver are designed to intensify trade, increase investment and boost tourism. it is important to note that the visa refusal rate is low for these countries, which according to the report pose no threat either in terms of irregular migration or in terms of security and public order. nevertheless, the timing of such agreements, even as the porosity of europe's borders is a breeding ground for terrorism in europe, seems incongruous. i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, mrs mariya gabriel, on the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the agreement between the european union and grenada. the european parliament was to take a decision on the conclusions of the agreement between the union and grenada, which was negotiated by the commission. the purpose was to make it easier for people to obtain visas. citizens of both sets will be exempt from visa requirements for stays of up to 90 days for a period of 180 days. this exemption does not apply to persons travelling on business. this recommendation was adopted by a large majority, which i welcome.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the eu-grenada agreement on the short-stay visa waiver. according to ms gabriel's report, the country in question poses no threat either in terms of illegal migration or in terms of security and public order. as regards mobility, confidence in visa applicants is high, with a relatively low visa refusal rate. visa liberalisation simplifies the conditions for travel. however, we have a duty to ask ourselves whether it is appropriate to conclude visa-free agreements at a time when the risk of terrorist attacks is real and when the european union has lost all control over mass immigration.
in writing. ‒ fn mps voted against this agreement because they are hostile to the short-stay visa exception, which it endorses. visas are required for national security purposes, except for those with our trusted partners, particularly european ones.
in writing. - i voted against this deal. as in the previous cases, this is a series of agreements on the short-stay visa exemption with several countries. the agreement is expected to help boost tourism and strengthen trade and investment relations with these partners. the key to these agreements is trust: the visa refusal rate is very low because countries trust visa applicants. the rapporteur believes that the countries covered by these agreements do not represent a threat, either in terms of irregular migration or in terms of security. in view of the mass immigration we are experiencing and which the union is no longer able to manage, in view of the risks and the recent attacks in france, one can only be surprised, even worried, by this sudden desire for openness. maybe this isn't the best time!
in writing. ‒ on the substance of the matter, i am in favour of short-stay visa exemptions to facilitate the mobility and travel of citizens of both parties, in this case of the member states to grenada and vice versa. i regret, however, that the french overseas departments are excluded. i'm officially denouncing this whole procedure. only the commission is empowered to negotiate these agreements on behalf of the states and citizens. it informs the european parliament of the state of the negotiations only at the very end of the process. above all, these agreements are implemented even before the european parliament gives its approval or not, an exemplary proof that democracy has no place in the union (note that the same procedure will be applied in the case of the transatlantic agreement). in these circumstances, i vote against.
in writing. ‒ these agreements on the short-stay visa waiver are designed to intensify trade, increase investment and boost tourism. it is important to note that the visa refusal rate is low for these countries, which according to the report pose no threat either in terms of irregular migration or in terms of security and public order. as regards the united arab emirates, it should be noted that 150 000 eu nationals are established there and most of them work there. around 1.6 million europeans visit the uae each year, and some 230,000 emiratis have travelled to europe, mainly for business and luxury tourism. nevertheless, the conclusion of such agreements, even at a time when the porosity of european borders is a breeding ground for terrorism in europe, seems incongruous. i voted against it.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament was presented with agreements on the short-stay visa waiver with nine third countries (dominica, vanuatu, trinidad and tobago, samoa, grenada, east timor, saint lucia, saint vincent and the grenadines, and the united arab emirates). the latter justified this exemption, which was surprising to say the least, by the development of economic relations and business travel and the fact that many european nationals are settled there. the european parliament was not regularly informed of the negotiations on these agreements; they were even implemented provisionally without waiting for the ep's decision. i am in favour of the liberalisation of short-stay visas. such agreements facilitate trade between peoples. but the eu's choices in this area are based on no other criteria than strategic and diplomatic issues. the one with the united arab emirates is a symbol of that. i therefore voted in favour of the first eight exemption agreements and abstained on the last one with the united arab emirates.

in writing. ‒ decision 2002/187/jha provides for the possibility for eurojust, which represents the premises of a future european public prosecutor's office, to conclude agreements or working arrangements with the agencies, institutions and bodies established by or on the basis of the treaties. such working arrangements or agreements shall allow for the exchange of information, including personal data, and for the secondment of liaison officers to eurojust. such agreements and arrangements may only be concluded after consultation by eurojust of the data protection supervisor and authorisation by the council. in order to broaden its scope of cooperation with the office for harmonization in the internal market (ohim) established by council regulation (ec) no 207/2009, eurojust has initiated a memorandum of understanding with ohim. the memorandum received a favourable opinion from eurojust's supervisory body and was finally approved by the eurojust college on 19 may. i voted against this report because it provides for the strengthening of eurojust's powers.

in writing. ‒ this report endorses the european commission's proposal to amend regulation no 609/2014 on own resources decisions laying down the rules for the provision of own resources and the measures relating to cash requirements. the text specifies the categories of own resources, the methods for calculating them and the arrangements for the payment of the member states' contributions. it also called for more automation of member states' contributions to the eu budget to avoid them becoming the subject of political negotiations. finally, the report recommends that the annual adjustments be rationalised to bring them into line with vat and gni-based own resources and to simplify and reduce the budgetary burden on the member states and the eu budget. it ensures the smooth management and operation of payments which are sometimes essential for certain economic sectors, and it also perpetuates the current system of eu own resources. i abstained because the proposal preserves the system of own resources.

in writing. ‒ this text calls for the approval of the european commission's proposal to amend regulation no 609/2014 on own resources decisions, which lays down the rules for making own resources available and the measures to meet cash requirements. it specifies in particular the categories of own resources, the methods of calculating them and the arrangements for the payment of the contributions of the member states. it was agreed to revise this procedure in order to reduce the risk of annual payment delays that the eu and member states have faced in recent years (resulting, for example, in an unprecedented volume of adjustments at the end of 2014). while the report recommends 'automating' member states' contributions to the eu budget to avoid them becoming the subject of political negotiations, the main aim is to streamline the annual adjustments to vat and gni-based own resources in order to simplify and reduce the budgetary burden on member states and to ensure the sound management and smooth functioning of payments. i didn't object to it.
in writing. ‒ this report approves the commission's proposal to amend regulation no 609/2014 on 'own resources decisions' which lays down the rules for making own resources available and the measures to meet cash requirements. following the many annual payment delays faced by the eu and member states in recent years, it was agreed in a commission proposal to revise this procedure. the report calls for more 'automation' of member states' contributions to the eu budget to avoid political conflicts over the timing of payments and to limit member states' discretion over the date of payment of their additional contribution arising from gni adjustments. while the system seeks to streamline the annual adjustments to own resources (vat and gni), this proposal preserves the eu's own resources situation. so i refrained.
in writing. ‒ this report calls for the approval of the commission's proposal to amend the regulation laying down the rules for making own resources available. the text specifically calls for the payment of member states' contributions to be automated so that they are not the subject of political negotiations. the aim of these proposals is to reduce the delay in payment of these contributions by limiting the discretion of the member states in setting the timetable. although these measures help to maintain the current system of the union's own resources, we cannot endorse the unprecedented budgetary burdens of member states' contributions. france loses more than 9 billion euros a year between what it receives and what it gives to the european union. i therefore abstained on that text.
in writing. ‒ this non-legislative report proposes the european parliament's opinion to the council on the revision of the regulation on the modalities and procedure for making available the traditional own resources, the vat-based own resource and the gni-based own resource and measures to meet cash requirements, which will enter into force at the beginning of 2016. the revision of this regulation is mainly technical for several reasons, starting with the need to apply the new procedure for the annual adjustment of vat and gni own resources, adopted at the end of 2014. the commission also proposes other minor revisions, such as the procedure for calculating interest on amounts made available late. the report calls for greater transparency by giving the european parliament access to information on the calculations. i think that this report is balanced and i have voted in favour of it.

in writing. ‒ the council adopted its position at first reading on the reform of the european trade mark system. the proposed reform includes a lower level of fees, the introduction of a compensation mechanism allowing member states to recover the costs of setting up services and procedures related to the application of the eu trade mark, the rationalisation of various technical provisions and the strengthening of cooperation between the office and national offices. the increase in the number of grounds for refusal of designations of origin and geographical indications thus allows for greater protection of the economic operators concerned. there was also an increase in the absolute grounds for refusal of designations of origin, geographical indications, traditional terms for wines, traditional specialities guaranteed and plant variety rights. this text streamlines the way the office operates. it allows lower fees and costs for economic operators and greater protection. i voted against the proposal to reject the council's position tabled by the efdd group.

in writing. ‒ in addition to the adaptation of terminology to the requirements of the lisbon treaty, the new system proposed includes a lower level of fees, the introduction of a compensation mechanism allowing member states to recover the costs of setting up services and procedures related to the application of the eu trade mark (5% of the office's annual revenue and the possibility of doubling the percentage in the event of a large budget surplus), as well as the rationalisation of various technical provisions and closer cooperation between the office and the national offices. it should be noted that the absolute grounds for refusal have been extended to cover designations of origin, geographical indications, traditional terms for wines, traditional specialities guaranteed and plant variety rights, and that the grounds for refusal have been extended to cover designations of origin and geographical indications, thus allowing for greater protection of the economic operators concerned. i therefore voted against the rejection amendment tabled by the efdd group.
in writing. ‒ the council adopted its position on the reform of the european trade mark system. the reform proposal renews the definition of a trade mark by removing the requirement of a graphic representation, this to allow the registration of trade marks of new forms, such as sound marks, movement marks, holograms without potentially excluding olfactory or taste marks. the trade mark sign shall be represented in a clear, precise, distinct and intelligible manner. the text shall also list the grounds for refusal or invalidity of the trade mark. the right for member states to decide to carry out checks on grounds of refusal of the right of use, the establishment of an administrative procedure before each national office to oppose the registration of a trade mark on the basis of the grounds of use and the establishment of an administrative procedure before each national office in respect of revocation or invalidity of a trade mark are also provided for. this text protects innovation and provides greater protection for economic operators, particularly as regards pgi. i voted against the motion for a resolution tabled by the efdd group.

in writing. i opposed the rejection amendment tabled by the efdd group on the recommendation of the juri committee to adopt the council's position on the reform of the european trade mark system. the recast directive will facilitate better protection for all trade marks in the union, in particular by proposing a new definition of a trade mark which removes the requirement of a graphic representation, which will allow the registration of trade marks of new forms such as sound trade marks; an adaptation to the current technological reality, especially as this is framed by the requirement of a sign represented in an intelligible and durable way. it is a framework that promotes transparency and access to brand understanding for all. the proposal for a directive also clearly sets out the grounds for refusal or invalidity of a trade mark, such as lack of distinctive character. finally, the member states are allowed to decide to carry out checks on grounds of their own motion, to institute an administrative procedure before each national office to oppose the registration of a trade mark on the basis of the grounds of its own motion, and to recognise national competence, which also encourages innovation.
in writing. ‒ the revision of the directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to trade marks aims to facilitate the registration, administration and uniform protection of trade marks in the union. this text promotes innovation (new definition of a trademark eliminating the requirement of a graphic representation thus allowing the creation of sound marks, movement marks, holograms, etc.) while allowing greater protection for economic operators, particularly french ones (strengthening cases of refusal of a trademark in the event of a conflict with earlier rights (appellations of origin, geographical indications, traditional terms)). i voted for this text in the committee on legal affairs. i therefore voted in favour of this text, voting against the amendment rejecting the text tabled by another group.

in writing. ‒ this legislative report aims to make trademark registration cheaper, faster and more reliable for businesses. it proposes a revision of the european directives for the harmonisation of national trade mark laws, in order to modernise the current provisions and to strengthen legal certainty while clarifying the rights conferred by trade marks. the text also seeks to improve cooperation between national offices and the office for harmonization in the internal market (ohim). an agreement was also reached on goods in transit, giving the holder of a registered trade mark the right to oppose the importation of goods from third countries into the territory of the european union when an unauthorised trade mark identical to the duly registered european trade mark is affixed to these products. this duty shall not apply if the final destination of the goods is not a member state of the union and if the proprietor of the trade mark is unable to prove that his trade mark is validly registered in the country of final destination. i have voted in favour of this report as an additional commercial tool for promoting and defending european products in the world.

in writing. ‒ the report presented aims to incorporate into community law the international regulations on the reporting and control of ships involved in transhipment operations. transhipment is a common practice whereby catches from one vessel that is still fishing are unloaded at sea onto another vessel that is about to land in a port. these operations create a disconnect between the fishing vessel and the landing party. they can be conducted in international waters and sometimes between two ships of different flags. this has the potential to make control and police operations more complex. they make systematic declarations at the port of landing compulsory for both vessels participating in a transhipment operation and for receiving vessels. the system thus restores the traceability of fish and thereby increases the efficiency of controls. i vote for it.

in writing. ‒ since 2000, the countries of the western balkans have benefited from autonomous trade measures (acms) from the european union. these mca constitute a unilateral preferential arrangement which allows them unlimited access to the union market. the text advocates extending these trade measures which are beneficial to these countries until 2020 in order to give them the time needed to align these preferences with those provided for in the saa (stabilisation and association agreement) which implies reciprocity between the two parties. the text, however, provides for the suspension of these preferential measures for bosnia, which has not yet agreed to adapt its trade agreements to take account of trade with croatia, which is now a member of the union. the european union is trying above all to preserve through this vote the possible accession of bosnia to the union, which we are firmly opposed to. i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. i supported this text which proposes several changes to the original regulation of the autonomous trade measures (acm) concluded between the union and bosnia and herzegovina. the text will thus benefit both parties as it proposes to extend the system of preferences granted to bosnia and herzegovina until 2020 while introducing a human rights safeguard clause.
in writing. ‒ relations between the european union and bosnia and herzegovina are governed by an interim agreement on trade pending the entry into force of the stabilisation and association agreement currently under ratification. as such, bosnia benefits from trade preferences coupled with 'autonomous trade measures', trade concessions granted unilaterally by the union, allowing almost all exports to enter the union without customs duties or quota restrictions. following croatia's accession to the european union in 2013, bosnia was obliged to adapt its international agreements. however, sarajevo has still not made this adjustment and is therefore not fulfilling its obligations towards the union. the european union has therefore decided to suspend its trade preferences. these will be restored when the eu-bosnia talks have resulted in an agreement taking into account the accession of croatia to the eu.
in writing. ‒ this report sought to extend exceptional trade measures in favour of countries in the process of joining the european union. this was bosnia. by thus extending aid to the balkans, and in particular to bosnia, the european union is thus keeping alive its idea of one day bringing that country into the union. i am firmly opposed to the enlargement of the union and its area of freedom of movement, and i voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this resolution because it is in line with the planned accession of bosnia and herzegovina.

in writing. ‒ i supported this report, whose content i believe reflects a good balance between the need to create a single energy market based on cleaner and cheaper energy and the need to let member states control and guide their nuclear policies. in view of the current energy fragmentation of the union, which is hampering its competitiveness and independence, i would like to stress two points in this report: the 10% target for european electricity interconnection and the categorical rejection of the nord stream 2 gas pipeline project, which, by creating a certain energy dependence on russia, would be in conflict with the european strategy for diversifying sources of supply. finally, the report proposes a reasonable compromise on shale gas, with the aim of establishing sufficient guarantees in terms of compliance with environmental standards in the production of this type of hydrocarbons. while diversification of sources of supply is a horizon to be achieved, strong environmental and public health safeguards should be maintained.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report sets out the european parliament's recommendations for building an efficient energy union, capable of providing citizens and businesses with sufficient energy at a competitive price. this report responds to the commission's communication on the energy union of february last. it stresses the importance of diversifying energy sources and supply routes. while recalling the competence of the member states in the field of energy packaging, parliament stressed the need to complete the internal energy market and the measures needed to achieve this. the introduction of a voluntary system of energy group purchases is one of the main proposals to reduce the energy bill of europeans. today, for example, we buy our gas at two or three times the price of our main economic partners, starting with the united states and china. i voted in favour of this report because it reflects the european parliament's ambition in the field of energy and because it provides practical solutions to strengthen european competitiveness.

in writing. - i voted against this bill. despite some positive points, such as the reminder of the national prerogative to choose the energy package or the maintenance of subsidies for fossil fuels, we are opposed to this text. we are not happy with his anti-russian and pro-american approach, in particular his demand that energy be included in the ptci and his denunciation of russia as an 'unreliable' partner. it calls for the end of regulated tariffs, the creation of an artificial market that will deprive us of long-term markets, and promotes the import of qatari and american shale gas. that is why we are firmly opposed to it.
in writing. ‒ the aim of the report is to create 'a more economically and physically integrated single energy market' which 'could lead to considerable efficiency gains'. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of consumers in the event of a dispute between the commission and the member states. and this is done by 'encouraging competition' to 'reduce prices'. with just a few days left until the end of cop 21, all environmental commitments have disappeared and the report encourages and supports "the exploitation of conventional indigenous oil and gas resources in the north sea, eastern mediterranean or black sea". the report also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the eu's energy policy is not undermined by the threat of nuclear proliferation. i am voting against this text, which does not take any account of the energy challenges facing europe.
in writing. ‒ the compromises adopted have resulted in a relative weakening of the report on its liberal component. as regards its ecological aspect, ambitions have been raised. the itre committee voted to strengthen the provisions on the ptci and the anti-russian component. a sentence denouncing the doubling of the russian-german nord stream gas pipeline has been added. however, a lively debate is not nearly over between the greens and the efdd on the one hand, and the epp and ecr on the other, on two issues. the main disagreement is over shale gas and nuclear energy. i voted against, because of the end of regulated tariffs, the creation of an artificial market which will deprive us of long-term contracts, indispensable industrial policy instruments, and redundant attacks on russia to promote the import of qatari and american lng.
in writing. ‒ this gróbarczyk report on the european energy union includes some laudable objectives such as the desire to retain the national prerogative of choosing the energy package, or the non-reception of the idea of the transformation committee of the agency for the cooperation of regulators, etc. however, this report is eminently anti-russian: it describes russia as an unreliable partner, it supports gas and oil pipeline projects designed to bypass russia, it wants to prohibit de facto gazprom from accessing the distribution market in the european union... it is therefore largely pro-american and in favour of the ptci. however, media reports have shown that the ptci negotiations were largely in favour of us energy exports and that the european negotiators were subject to the us energy lobby. this ideological relationship is therefore not in the interests of consumers, since it prefers to sacrifice cheap energy (at regulated prices) because of its origin and will favour the import of energy from countries that are not recommended (qatar, etc.). i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this particularly balanced text which calls for the implementation of a genuine energy union. the report stresses the competence of the member states in the composition of their energy mix, but also supports the development of renewable energies, conventional hydrocarbons and nuclear energy. it does not oppose in principle non-conventional energy sources, in particular shale gas. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competition' in the context of the directive. at institutional level, it insists that all matters relating to the energy union should be dealt with under the ordinary legislative procedure and therefore involve parliament fully. finally, and this is a very positive point, it asks the commission to report annually to parliament on the implementation of the energy union using detailed indicators. i voted for this text, but i was opposed to some of its provisions which presented russia as an 'unreliable partner'. these terms only add to the deterioration of relations between the eu and russia, as our producers and consumers continue to suffer from the fruitless escalation of reciprocal sanctions.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this report by the european parliament entitled 'towards a european energy union'. the eu's basic energy policy guidelines are in complete contradiction to the modest progress achieved at cop 21 in paris. following the commission's proposal for an energy union, this resolution follows the same lines: use of nuclear and fossil fuels, low ambition in promoting renewable energies, and capture and storage of co2. one of the few really positive points is the demand for a binding 40% energy efficiency target, which is necessary but not sufficient on its own. we are far from any climate ambition in which the energy question would be integrated; we remain in a mercantile approach that favors the big energy groups, ignoring any approach based on energy as a public good. energy poverty and moderation of energy consumption are hardly taken into account. we are therefore in a continuous process, far from any ambitious energy policy that can respond to the fight against global warming.

in writing. ‒ i fully share the objectives of this report to make a point and call for the acceleration of measures to improve the interconnection of electricity networks in europe. this interconnection is necessary in view of the very characteristics of electricity - a non-storable fluid - which must be consumed where the needs are located, which may, depending on the circumstances, be far from the place of production. this is a prerequisite for making renewable energy production installations 'profitable', whether they are industrial or come from consumers/producers. this is a necessity to ensure the energy security of the european continent. this is why financial incentives should be given priority to limit the risks of investment (juncker plan and efsi, dedicated taxation) in sustainable, 'smart' and connected technologies. in doing so, the competences of the national authorities must also be respected; the commission has also proposed that the member states should not destabilise existing networks by seeking to coexist two principles which are difficult to reconcile: energy independence and openness to competition. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the future of the european union. it must serve climate objectives but also public service values such as accessibility through connecting all territories and reducing the energy bill.

in writing. ‒ the european progress instrument aims to increase access to microfinance for people who have lost or are at risk of losing their jobs, who are in difficulty on the labour market or who are facing the threat of social exclusion. it is therefore a useful tool in the fight against poverty and unemployment. the figures show that 60% of people were unemployed or inactive when they applied for a microcredit through progress. it is therefore appropriate to support this instrument and to seek to improve its operation. the resolution makes a number of proposals to that end which i think are right, and that is why i have supported the text. these proposals concern improving access to the instrument, targeting target groups, complementarity of progress with other union instruments, among others. it is also necessary to increase the visibility of this instrument, to accompany it with training in entrepreneurship, and to extend its geographical scope of action. progress is to provide 46 000 microcredits by 2020, for a total of €500 million. we must ensure that this objective is achieved.
in writing. ‒ the schulze report aims to provide the union with a microfinance instrument for disadvantaged groups or microenterprises in difficulty. while we find this project interesting in that it supports freedom of enterprise and aims to create jobs in europe, it is clear from the text in question that more ideological objectives are also being pursued. the commission has also been active in the development of the european social fund, which is a key instrument for the european union's social dialogue. moreover, the financing of this project is not clearly defined. several funds and programmes are mentioned without clearly specifying their functions and contributions. this instrument could therefore be useful, in particular through social integration through work (unemployed, disabled people), access to credit for the most precarious entrepreneurs, the creation of sustainable jobs, especially in this period of austerity and banking prudence. however, the populations mentioned, the lack of budgeting and the low results highlighted oblige me to oppose this project. i therefore vote against.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the new common fisheries policy (cfp), which provides a structure for technical measures and multiannual plans. this report follows a consultation on technical measures launched in 2005, to which the fishermen interviewed responded by expressing several requests, such as adapting technical measures to fisheries, adapting technical measures to the landing obligation or introducing technical measures which are not contradictory. this text is therefore a step in the right direction, since it takes account of the demands of the fishermen and simplifies the technical measures of the cfp by adapting them to each type of fishery.

in writing. ‒ the new common fisheries policy will be accompanied by a new technical measures framework, which should be proposed by the commission in early 2016. the aim is to adapt the technical measures to the objectives of the new cfp. technical measures regulate fishing conditions, in particular the characteristics of fishing gear (e.g. mesh size), the minimum size of catches or fishing areas. the own-initiative report prepared by mr gabriel mato sets out parliament's vision for the future negotiations on this new technical measures framework. it stresses the following points:- simplification of technical measures to put an end to the successive stacking of contradictory regulations;- adaptation of technical measures to the regional specificities of fisheries; - adaptation of the regulatory framework to the new management logic imposed by the obligation to land all catches;- participation of fishermen in the process of drawing up technical measures;- adoption of multiannual management plans for the different areas and species. i agree with these objectives and have therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report is part of the implementation of the reform of the common fisheries policy (cfp) adopted in 2013. the new cfp is based on the objective of maximum sustainable yield (msy) and applies stock management at the level of biomass size, reproductive stock and fishing mortality. technical measures and multiannual plans are the main conservation tools to achieve these objectives. in view of the commission's proposal for early 2016 on a new framework for technical measures, this report sets out the european parliament's priorities in this area. the report stresses the importance of regional cooperation on conservation through multiannual plans to tackle the problem of juvenile catches and other by-catches. it also advocated closer involvement of fishermen in the decision-making process, including the development of technical measures. i voted in favour of the report, in support of these objectives.

in writing. ‒ the european union has had a new common fisheries policy for a year. this should lead to more sustainable fishing, ensuring the reproduction and conservation of species and protecting an important economic sector for many member states, including france. traditional fishing techniques are recognised and will be preserved. conserving fish stocks and ending discards - more than a quarter of catches are wasted every year - are crucial for the future of small-scale, artisanal and coastal fishing. for france, europe's leading maritime interface, this new common fisheries policy should be a real asset. however, the complexity and diversity of technical measures make their application difficult for fishermen. to ensure the implementation of the cfp objectives, future technical measures will need to be simplified, contained in a clearly structured legal framework and developed on the basis of sound scientific peer-reviewed advice.

in writing. ‒ the new common fisheries policy is based on three key ideas to ensure the sustainability of the fisheries sector through sustainable management of fisheries resources. the multiannual management of quotas aims to give clarity to fisheries companies, the objective of maximum sustainable yield aims at optimising catches in accordance with the state of stocks, and the participation of regional advisory councils brings management decisions closer to local operators, whether they are fishermen, scientists or members of ngos. the report submitted aims to simplify the measures and to harmonize the techniques relating to the landing obligation by large areas. i maintain that the objective remains to "sort through the deck". this report recommends that parliament should give a framework to the delegated acts adopted by the commission in the field of technical fisheries measures. it called for the selectivity of fishing gear to be improved and confirmed the involvement of the regional advisory councils in the formulation of concrete proposals to achieve the objective of reducing catches of fish below the required size. i vote for it.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the new common fisheries policy, which has been in force since january 2014. the policy is based on four main pillars: maintaining fish stocks above the maximum sustainable yield (msy), making all catches landed, management plans to manage fish stocks on a multiannual basis and regionalising technical measures. the purpose of this report is to make recommendations for the negotiations on the new technical measures framework adapted to the objectives of the new cfp, which the commission should propose in early 2016. technical measures regulate fishing conditions, in particular the characteristics of fishing gear, the minimum catch size or fishing areas. i am particularly in favour of the text which calls for the simplification of technical measures to put an end to the successive accumulation of contradictory regulations. i also supported the recommendation that fishermen should be involved in the process of developing these technical measures and that multiannual management plans should be adapted to the different areas and species.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by our colleague mr gabriel mato on the new common fisheries policy. the report stresses the following points: simplification of technical measures to put an end to the successive accumulation of contradictory regulations; adaptation of technical measures to the regional specificities of fisheries; adaptation of the regulatory framework to the new management logic imposed by the obligation to land all catches; the involvement of fishermen in the process of developing technical measures; the adoption of multiannual management plans for the different areas and species. since the 2013 cfp reform, all multiannual plans have to include a maximum sustainable yield objective with a timetable for achieving it, measures to implement the discard ban and the landing obligation, as well as back-up mechanisms for taking corrective action and review clauses.

in writing. ‒ the common fisheries policy was reformed in 2013, and it was time to review the technical measures resulting from it, some of which had not been changed since 1998. i therefore took part in the work of the committee on fisheries to formulate recommendations to the european commission on the future technical framework, which we adopted in the form of a resolution in strasbourg on tuesday 15 december. a broad consensus has been formed around the necessary simplification and regionalisation. because some measures, if applied indiscriminately to all, can have a detrimental effect on specific fisheries. i am also pleased to have had an amendment adopted in plenary which warns of the need for real regionalisation to allow for greater participation and support from the actors concerned. finally, the new fisheries policy must be selective. selectivity means avoiding juveniles and catching only target species, i.e. those for which quotas are held, using modernised gear and techniques. some existing technical measures will have to be abolished because they are now obstacles to selectivity.
in writing. ‒ simplifying technical measures is a step in the right direction. the report envisages regionalising them, but the commission will have the final say and will present its draft at the end of january 2016. the commission acknowledges, however, that rationalization and simplification are necessary. i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ the common fisheries policy (cfp) is supposed to guarantee the sustainability of fisheries while ensuring a fair standard of living for fishermen. it has recently been reformed, including the introduction of multiannual fishing plans (to avoid impairing the species' reproductive capacity) and a series of technical measures (ban on driftnets, prevention of accidental catches of porpoises, ban on the removal of shark fins from vessels). these provisions are spread over more than 30 different regulations and constitute a complex, heterogeneous and sometimes even contradictory system. the resolution therefore calls for a new framework that can be easily understood by fishermen and for the closer involvement of fishermen in the decision-making process. without prejudice to the content of the future cfp and relying solely on the measures recommended in this report, which seem to me to be in the right direction, i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ the european securities and markets authority (esma) is one of the three regulatory institutions created by the european union in the wake of the 2008 financial crisis. it is the sole authority responsible for the harmonisation of european technical standards and the financial stability of the eu for credit rating agencies registered in europe. but although it identified many flaws in the sovereign debt rating process, it issued only one monetary sanction: a symbolic fine of €30,000 against the canadian agency dbrs, for its "negligence". in short, esma is not playing its intended role. its chairman, steven maijoor, former dean of the school of business at maastricht university and former ceo of the afm, the dutch regulatory authority, has been in office since 2011. he recently said about the tobin tax on financial transactions: "we must make rules at 28 or not at all", a way of burying the project. it is also responsible for the postponement, to the greatest benefit of the financial sector, of the mifid ii directive, which is supposed to improve market surveillance. i vote against extending his mandate as head of esma.
in writing. ‒ for esma, the enf group voted against the re-appointment of steven maijoor, whose very favourable positions towards the financial industry have, for example, led esma to postpone the implementation of the emir directive by one year and to now delay the implementation of mifid ii. the commission prepared the text in 2010-2011, adopted it in co-decision in 2014 and it is expected to enter into force in 2018, but esma is dragging things out in level 2, to the greatest benefit of market operators in the uk in particular, who fear this regulatory overload. the nine-year delay in the entry into force of a central market regulation text illustrates the structural dysfunctions of market regulation as organised by the european institutions.
in writing. ‒ the extension of the mandate of the president of the european securities and markets authority, steven maijoor, does not seem appropriate. in his capacity as prime minister he has shown that he is more concerned with the interests of the city of london than with the interests of the peoples of europe. it was under his mandate that esma postponed the implementation of the emir directive by one year and delayed the implementation of mifid ii. while the commission prepared the text in 2010-2011, for adoption in co-decision in 2014, entry into force in 2018 shows that the esma is dragging its feet, to the greatest benefit of market operators in london who fear this regulatory overload. that is why i am voting against the extension of mr maijoor's mandate.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the extension of the mandate of the president of the european securities and markets authority (esma). steven maijoor, the first chairman of esma, was appointed in 2011 for a five-year term by the board of supervisors of esma following an open selection procedure. the council requested that this mandate be extended for a period of five years. after hearing the current president, the committee on economic and monetary affairs of the european parliament approved this request. i voted in accordance with the opinion of this committee. the term of office of the chairperson of the authority may be renewed only once, with the agreement of the european parliament.

in writing. ‒ as it is entitled to do, parliament votes today to oppose the adoption by the commission of an implementing regulation. in this case, it is the list of exotic species, i.e. alien, animal or plant species, considered to be invasive and potentially dangerous either for native species, the environment and biodiversity, or even for human health. their presence in lands not their own can also have a significant economic impact. the best-known example is the asian hornet, the enemy of our bees. it is estimated that these species represent the second largest cause of biodiversity loss in the world. it is therefore not an ancillary problem. the resolution of the european parliament is overwhelming: dubious methodology, no risk assessment or 'wet finger', disregard for the opinions of the competent national authorities or interested parties, etc. everything contributes to making the list presented by the brussels commission a 'political' list, sloppy, incomplete, useless. it is a pity that the treaties confer quasi-legislative powers on the commission and that the procedure for opposing them is so difficult to implement. but if it is a question of preventing brussels from doing harm, i can only support this text.

in writing. ‒ the objection relates to a list submitted by the commission concerning 'invasive alien species' (american lobster, pacific oyster, african black-spotted goby, etc.). it follows regulation (eu) no 1143/2014 as voted by the european parliament on 16 april 2014. the commission was required to submit a first list by 2 january 2016. some harmful species should really be included and are not (the assessments are not yet completed) while others are included before the assessment, which may affect the economic activities that exploit them. the commission therefore presented a list on a heterogeneous basis. this objection was raised by the socialist pavel poc, who was already rapporteur during the 2014 vote, and the elected members of the national front had supported his proposal at the time. we voted yes.

in writing. dominique martin supported this objection. the european commission has submitted a list of "invasive alien species", including the american lobster, the pacific oyster and the african black-spotted goby. however, this list is incomplete and arbitrary: some harmful species that should be included are not, while others are included automatically even though the evaluations are not yet complete. the inclusion on the list may adversely affect the economic activities that exploit them. the commission seems to have used, as it often does, arbitrary and heterogeneous criteria in drawing up its list. that is why we support this objection.
in writing. ‒ in april 2014, the european parliament endorsed the principle of monitoring invasive alien species to eradicate them when necessary. the commission has therefore established by means of implementing acts the list of species to be monitored. the resolution before us is critical of this list. indeed, it appears that 'the reasons for including a species in the draft union list are guided by political rather than scientific criteria'. as a result, "many of the most problematic invasive alien species are not on the list. for example, species of mammals and plant species that are widespread and rapidly spreading with significant and well-documented negative consequences for human health are not included in the list. the resolution also condemns the lack of information on the subject by parliament, since the documents were not sent in due time and in an appropriate manner. i vote in favour.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the dodds and niedermayer report, which follows up the analysis of the taxe commission (a special committee on tax records in the member states set up in february 2015 following the 'luxleaks' revelations) and makes concrete proposals on the taxation of multinational companies in europe. the text makes a major contribution to transparency through the country-by-country and sector-by-sector information that multinationals will be required to publish, the introduction of a new 'good taxpayer' label for companies that respect good tax practices and the mandatory disclosure of new tax measures by the european commission. i would like to make public the mechanism for declaring activity and taxing each country. finally, the report stresses the need for a european legal regime to protect whistleblowers.

in writing. ‒ the dodds-niedermayer resolution closes a year of fiscal wake-up in europe, initiated by the european parliament. the automatic and mandatory exchange of tax information, the audit and research work of the taxe special committee, its progressive report and the decision to renew the mandate of the committee, these advances are confirmed. the resolution, which was tabled by the committee on economic and monetary affairs and endorsed by two co-rapporteurs from opposing political families, however, elaborates on the european parliament's positions and sets out new recommendations. the text also provides a more detailed assessment of the optimisation practices and the state of corporate taxation in the european union. it also calls for a rigorous and objective method for drawing up a european list of tax havens, with very comprehensive sanctions for all those who use it. it also supports increased transparency by proposing that any new tax measure (rebates, credits, special rates) be communicated to the other member states and added to a centralised register. because it crowns, on these and many other essential aspects, the protection of whistleblowers, the harmonisation of the corporate tax base, i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ following the luxleaks case, i.e. the practice of favourable tax agreements between luxembourg and a number of multinationals, this report proposes 'better tax coordination' within the eu. while the report contains good proposals such as the obligation for multinationals to publish their turnover by sector and country or the legal protection of whistleblowers, it also proposes clearly anecdotal measures such as the creation of a 'taxpayer loyal' label for companies that pay their taxes. why not a medal? in fact, this is very revealing of the spirit of this text which purports to combat tax evasion without really wanting to tackle those who practice it. in this context i shall refrain from commenting in order not to discourage good intentions without at the same time endorsing the weakness of the proposed measures.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report paints a worrying picture of the aggressive tax optimisation practices of multinationals, estimating the damage to the public finances of the member states at between eur 60 and 170 billion per year. the recommendations made are largely commendable and in line with the oecd's general plan (country reporting, acis, transfer price controls, etc.). the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the european union and the member states. it would also have been better to take further action on sanctions against consultancies involved in aggressive optimisation schemes, including strict separation of consultancy activities from government and business. in the end, the report more directly obliges the commission to commit itself to these reforms, but the conclusions are largely redundant with those of the special committee taxe, which leads to abstention on the final vote.
in writing. ‒ the dodds niedermayer own-initiative report is largely duplicated by the taxe special committee report. it also follows the luxleaks scandal, but was launched in december 2014, three months before the special commission was set up, hence the redundancy. the theme is exactly the same: combating aggressive tax competition at union level and optimisation schemes. the damage at european level is estimated at between €50 and €70 billion per year for profit shifting alone, and €160 to €190 billion if special tax schemes and agreements and fraud are included. the conclusions are broadly similar, but the idea of abolishing bilateral conventions in favour of multilateral agreements under the aegis of the union, which would speak with one voice, is regrettable, since the states would thus lose control of these agreements. there are a few different proposals, such as the regulation of free ports, for more transparency. the proposal to strictly regulate conflicts of interest in consultancy firms was unfortunately rejected in committee. in view of these shortcomings, i abstain on this report.

in writing. ‒ i gave my full support to the report by edouard martin on the development of the conditions necessary for the maintenance and development of the base metal industry. it sets out a number of concrete solutions, including the introduction of a co2 adjustment at europe's borders to prevent unfair competition, the development of the circular economy or the introduction of new forms of corporate governance.
in writing. ‒ the report which was originally presented in the itre committee was in the right direction and edouard martin had timidly sketched out protectionist measures based on some very correct findings. the report, after the vote in committee, is nothing but a catalogue of good feelings, with a few good half measures alternating with some very bad ones. that's why i finally decided to abstain.
in writing. - this report is presented by the socialist member of parliament edouard martin, who was elected quietly after having betrayed his comrades in the "struggle" at arcelormittal, whom he made accept the plan to dismantle our lorraine steelworks. this document is in fact a progress report on the reflection of the reflection group on the development of the base metals sector. the text provides a good diagnosis of the state of the sector and reaffirms its strategic importance for industrial policy. the angle taken to safeguard and develop this industry is the ecological adjustment at the borders, by obliging importers to buy co2 emission allowances on the market for polluting rights when introducing products from the steel industry or primary aluminium. the report does not go beyond protectionism for such a strategic industry and it would have been easier to introduce an import levy rather than this complex system. the report also makes no mention of the flight of decision-making centres out of the european union and the weight of industries in emerging countries. i therefore abstained on this report which has become a catalogue of good feelings without proposals.
in writing. ‒ while the report's assessment of the state of the steel industry and aluminium production seems to us to be correct, particularly when it emphasises their strategic nature, the flight of decision-making centres out of europe and the impact of environmental constraints on the productivity of european companies, the same cannot be said for the proposed solutions, which are very complex and essentially consist of obliging importers to buy co2 emissions on the market for polluting rights. the introduction of an import levy based on an entry price mechanism and the reversal of the prohibition on long-term electricity supply contracts, which is a consequence of competition policy, would be sufficient to restore productivity in this sector. however, some amendments counterbalance the protections provided for in this report and lead me to abstain on this text.
in writing. ‒ this report sets out the lines of thinking to contribute to the development of the steel industry and aluminium production. the rapporteur makes a good assessment of the state of the sector and reaffirms that the development of this sector is strategic for the member states of the union, mainly in terms of jobs. he admits that the environmental standards imposed by the commission are the cause of the loss of competitiveness of this industry. the commission is proposing to oblige importers to buy emission allowances on the market for polluting rights in order to combat environmental dumping by emerging countries. even if this proposal is positive, it does not make it possible to stop our loss of competitiveness completely and will contribute to increasing the volatility of these emission allowances to the benefit of speculators. the report is generally in the right direction but remains unambitious. only intelligent protectionism can help to combat unfair international competition effectively. the amendments by the epp and the ecr group have also largely emptied the report of the main measures of interest, particularly in terms of provisions relating to border adjustment. i therefore abstained on that text.

in writing. ‒ for years we have witnessed a serious deterioration in the rule of law and fundamental rights in hungary. the government of viktor orbán is increasing its provocations and its attacks on democracy. refugees, stigmatised and treated as criminals, have a very limited access to international protection. the independence of the judiciary and the media is under threat. the specter of the death penalty is reappearing dangerously. racism, anti-semitism and xenophobia are on the rise. this worrying situation is a real test of the union's ability to react firmly when one of its member states acts in flagrant contradiction to its values. if we remain passive and inactive, similar phenomena could spread like wildfire to other european states. the aim of this resolution was to call on the european institutions to take strong action in the face of what is happening in hungary. i very much regret that, because of the european right, the text voted does not call for the activation of article 7 of the treaty, which could lead to the suspension of certain of the rights of a member state, and does not support the european citizens' initiative on the same demand.
in writing. ‒ since the accession to power of prime minister viktor orban, hungary has adopted authoritarian measures, as evidenced by the adoption of laws restricting fundamental rights and individual freedoms, especially in relation to minorities and foreigners. hungary has restricted freedom of religion and expression. these measures are contrary to the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, which has led to a letter of formal notice from the european commission. the european union is a community of law, and breaches of the treaties must be punished. that is why i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution which seeks to encourage the european commission and the european council to take full account of the recent deviations in that country. democracy and the rule of law must therefore be safeguarded by taking appropriate measures.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on the situation in hungary. the situation in that country is extremely worrying. the legislative measures adopted on refugees, migrants and asylum seekers are unfortunately only the latest step in a long series of measures taken by the hungarian government over the past few years. we have already warned about this in our resolution of 10 june. the commission, the council and the european council must assume their responsibilities. the council and the european council must hold a debate and adopt firm conclusions on the situation in hungary. the commission should activate the first phase of the eu framework for strengthening the rule of law and immediately launch a process of in-depth monitoring of democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. the commission shall assess the emergence of a systemic threat in hungary which could give rise to a clear risk of a serious breach within the meaning of article 7 of the eu treaty. the infringement procedure concerning the asylum acquis is not sufficient. a fire is not extinguished by a glass of water, especially when it threatens to spread.

on behalf of the enf group. mr president, the epo's decision to liberalize patents and the rights of seed breeders is a very bad thing. it's like giving a free pass to multinational corporations like syngenta, monsanto, etc., by allowing them to actually take control of our food. it's something very serious, in my opinion. this is a danger to our food sovereignty because this epo policy will encourage market concentration, increase farmers' dependence on a few multinationals - as you know - and will inevitably have consequences for consumers. and we'll have less control over manufacturing, which will be increasingly standardized. the project will enable industrial groups to organise the control of all seeds, including those that farmers collect directly from their harvest. in addition, this new constraint will restrict market access for local traditional and organic seeds. in france and europe, the seed sector is made up of many smes and cooperatives. at the global level, on the other hand, ten companies share 60% of the market. this concentration, together with the problems of intellectual property, will be detrimental to the maintenance of diversified agriculture. the seed industry must instead be controlled to avoid any monopoly and any questionable practices, which are being challenged, as in 2013 against a patent granted to syngenta guaranteeing it exclusive rights to all peppers with resistance to white flies. this patent prohibited farmers and breeders from using these plants without paying syngenta licensing fees. it was not an invention, but a discovery made by crossing species. another lawsuit was filed in late may 2014 against a european patent held by monsanto on fungus-resistant tomatoes. this was again a discovery that the multinational corporation had appropriated. this privatization of life is threatening small and medium-sized seed companies, which risk having their own varieties patented. this was the case, for example, of the french company gautier, which has been obliged since 2013 to pay the dutch seed company zwaan to market an aphid-resistant lettuce that it had selected itself a long time ago. it's still a little weird. the plant variety certificates were already controversial because they called into question the possibility for farmers to re-sow their own seeds free of charge. but despite this constraint, these plant breeding certificates still protected our seed-growers and farmers from patenting. this even more costly and much more restrictive practice is already in place in the united states. today, the epo's outrageous decision and the incomprehensible silence of the european commission seriously call into question what had been adopted, without enthusiasm, as an effective bulwark. more importantly, this decision raises once again the question of aligning european law with that of the united states, obviously with the aim of not hampering the trade negotiations under way. if, to achieve this, the european commission intends to trample on the text adopted in 2012, let it say so frankly!
mr president, commissioner, plant breeding is a particularly innovative sector. this is evidenced, on the one hand, by the high investment in research and development, which accounts for some 15% of the sector's turnover, and, on the other hand, by the genetic progress made by farmers all over the world. the operators need a clear and effective framework and protective tools, but we must also respect a number of ethical principles in relation to the living world. the sui generis right created by the upov convention and the certificate of plant variety origin, which embodies it, remain the most appropriate tools for the protection of plant varieties, and we must defend their exclusive use for this purpose, thus supporting the exclusion of plant varieties from patentability. the acceleration of innovation processes leads to a lag in the time between the pace of innovation and commercial obsolescence. we therefore expect the commission to secure this important sector for our economy.
mr president, commissioner, as we know, international law and the patent directive 98/44/ec explicitly prohibit the patentability of plant varieties, essentially biological processes, animal breeds and native traits, even when these are obtained by natural processes. in a surprising and controversial interpretation of patent law, the grand chamber of the european patent office took a dangerous step in march last year in favour of the patentability of plants obtained by essentially biological processes. the danger of not allowing any breeder to access existing varieties and use them to create new varieties, and any farmer to take his own seeds from his crops, is clear, but also the danger of allowing only a few powerful groups, capable of obtaining patents, to establish a monopoly on living things for a commercial and financial purpose, rather than working for innovation and shared progress. for these reasons, i call on the commission and the member states to clarify and enforce international law.

in writing. ‒ the volkswagen scandal, which exposed the german car manufacturer's cheating on its nitrogen oxide and co2 emission measurement systems, is a reminder of the need to be vigilant in the face of large industrial groups. from 2009 to 2015, software was installed on more than 11 million vehicles (sold worldwide) to deceive vehicle testing authorities. the subject is eminently european, with maximum emission levels set by the european union. this week the european parliament has issued a doubly ambitious response to this, first to the council and then to the states, which had let their guard down in the face of the interests of the car lobby, by taking the decision to raise the permitted levels of nitrogen oxide emissions. parliament's envi committee rejected this proposal, but, above all, by drafting a resolution which proposed the establishment of a committee of inquiry, thus having special powers, into this fraud and the attitude of the european commission during the period 2009-2015. i am aware of the difficulty of obtaining enough votes to enable parliament to have the means to investigate (it failed after the luxleaks scandal), and i voted without hesitation in favour of setting up the committee of inquiry into the volkswagen scandal.

in writing. ‒ the conclusion of this partnership and cooperation agreement will strengthen political and economic ties between the european union and vietnam. it will allow for more intensive cooperation on a wide range of issues of common interest, such as the fight against corruption, innovation, including new technologies, sustainable development, disarmament and the fight against terrorism. the vietnamese government has initiated many reforms to modernize its economic model and integrate it into the world economy. in less than 10 years, gdp per capita has doubled and many foreign companies have increased investment. however, some progress still needs to be made in the political field. social and labour standards remain too low, and certain freedoms, such as freedom of association and trade union rights, are not sufficiently guaranteed. the agreement should allow for improvements in these areas. this partnership, which coincides with the conclusion of the eu-vietnam free trade agreement, will allow the eu to increase its presence in asia and its influence in regional bodies such as asean.
