in writing. ‒ as a reminder, the dayton agreements were signed on 14 december 1995. they stopped the fighting in bosnia and herzegovina. one of the challenges today is to maintain the institutional balance of the dayton agreements in order to preserve civil peace and prevent the rights of the serb minority from being violated. that was the whole point of the alternative motion for a resolution which we tabled with the members of the group of the european liberal, democratic and reformist party. the joint motion for a resolution, on the other hand, repeatedly insisted on the forthcoming accession of bosnia, an accession which we oppose in principle, since we in the national front are resolutely opposed to the construction of a european union and a fortiori to its enlargement. that is why, since our alternative proposal was not adopted, i voted against the joint motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ i opposed this text which celebrates an agreement made behind the backs of the people by the american hegemony. the agreements put an end in 1995 to the bloody war that had torn the former yugoslavia since 1991. however, they only endorsed the partition of the country into two ethnic states - the federation of bosnia and herzegovina and the serb republic of bosnia, within an artificially unitary entity. the serbs and the bosnian croats were thus forced by an external gendarme to make common cause, without, 20 years later, the central institutions really functioning properly. can we really be happy when, from 1997, the international community imposed on bosnia and herzegovina a high civilian representative charged with taking "binding decisions" and "provisional measures": such as imposing common number plates, a single passport, a currency, a law on citizenship, a new flag, not to mention the dismissals of several local elected officials...? what about the right of peoples to self-determination, which has been strongly emphasized on many occasions in the european parliament, and again at this december part-session, in the preda report?
in writing. ‒ although the dayton agreements formally ended the deadly conflict between bosniaks, croats and serbs in december 1995, they are above all a sign of the inability of member state governments and european institutions to resolve this ethnic conflict. these agreements have left ethnic and religious divisions in the marble, creating many tensions between the different communities. under the auspices of the americans and without any democratic consultation, the ultimate authority of this state has been entrusted to a high representative of the international community. through the imf, austerity measures were imposed on them, which have only increased poverty, social inequality and youth unemployment. we also oppose, as this motion for a resolution calls for, the continuation of the process of bosnia's accession to the european union, because we consider that the enlargement of the union is a hindrance to the prosperity of the member states. we also object to the special attention that this proposal is trying to give to the roma, who would be the first victims of these community tensions. i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ the dayton peace accords marked the end of the war in bosnia and the creation of the federal state of bosnia and herzegovina in 1995. these agreements establish a system of governance in which the various federated entities are represented. the high representative for bosnia and herzegovina is responsible for ensuring that the dayton agreements are implemented. the complexity of the governance system makes political decision-making complicated, which endangers the stability of the country. although the country has enjoyed relative peace for twenty years, many obstacles still need to be overcome in order to establish an autonomous and functional state. as a candidate country for accession to the european union, bosnia and herzegovina is supported by the european union in implementing the reforms necessary for its proper functioning. there is still a great deal of work to be done before bosnia and herzegovina becomes a member of the union. i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ this resolution sets out the european parliament's position on the political situation in bosnia and herzegovina in the context of the 20th anniversary of the dayton peace agreement and the ongoing process of bosnia and herzegovina's accession to the union. the dayton peace accords were intended to end years of unrelenting political conflict and ethnic tension in the country, which had resulted in many deaths and millions of displaced persons. although the situation has improved markedly in the last 20 years, since bosnia and herzegovina has not experienced any major incidents, much remains to be done before it is integrated into the union. the association and stabilisation agreement signed in 2015 offers new prospects for cooperation, according to meps, but can be compromised by short-term political initiatives, such as the referendum organised by the republic of serbia (one of the two administrative entities making up bosnia and herzegovina) on the federal judiciary, which threatens the country's cohesion, sovereignty and integrity and progress towards eu membership. i have voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that internal political stability and respect for the fundamental principles of the union are key conditions for the integration of a country into the union.

in writing. ‒ this motion for a resolution concerns the export of arms. but beyond this, the report is moving in the direction of a europe of defence. several elements of the text assign to the european union the role of ensuring the foreign policy and security of its member states. the european union is thus entrusted with the task of deciding which countries should or should not benefit from arms exports in the name, of course, of the defence of human rights, for which parliament has been a champion. the report seeks to extend the eu's powers under the pretext of fighting arms trafficking. i think that we must be firm on these sensitive issues. the defence and arms industries must remain under the full control of the states, since they are essential to the maintenance of their sovereignty and the independence of the peoples. in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report presents the european parliament's annual evaluation of the implementation of the 2008 common position on arms exports. the report calls for stricter application of the criteria of the agreement through greater coordination at european level. the rapporteur calls on the member states to increase transparency on arms exports. the rapporteur also stresses the need to apply a more coherent embargo policy between the eu states and to increase cooperation between the member states, the european agencies (europol, eurojust) and third parties, in order to facilitate the prosecution of arms traffickers. with my colleagues from the epp group we have expressed a great deal of criticism of the unrealistic demands made on member states to provide information on contracts and the general arms trade. the rapporteur is encroaching on the competences of the member states and is ignoring the specific features of their arms export regimes. the french regime for arms export controls is, for example, stricter than the common position on all the criteria. for these reasons i voted against the report.

in writing. ‒ in 2008, the eu arms trade code was replaced by the legally binding eu common position (2008/944 / cfsp). it sets out eight criteria for the export of conventional arms. these completely hypocritical standards reveal the mirage of the union's common foreign and security policy. the member states are happy to derogate from this. criterion 2 mentions 'respect for human rights in the country of final destination' but the report does not say a word about arms exports to saudi arabia. criterion 3 states that "arms exports must not serve to aggravate or prolong tensions in the country of final destination" while the report "notes the decision of some member states to supply defensive arms to ukraine" without being unduly alarmed. the rapporteur, however, is 'very concerned about the consequences for the security and defence of the union of the transfer of sensitive knowledge and technology to third countries, such as russia'. i am in favour of democratic control of arms exports, which largely disqualifies the union for this. i am voting against this text.

in writing. ‒ the european patent office has agreed to patent plant characteristics. this is not the approach of the eu and france, which believe that plant characteristics and the 'material' used by breeders should remain accessible to all. to ensure that the work of breeders is protected to a minimum, france and the union have introduced a certificate of plant breeding. this mechanism allows farmers to harvest their crops with a contribution paid to breeding bodies. compared with us patent law, the european approach is the lesser evil. i think that this motion for a resolution expresses the need to separate from the us patent law which covers living things, and i therefore voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ the european patent office has agreed to patent plant characteristics, which is contrary to the approach of the eu and france, which believe that plant characteristics and the 'material' used by breeders must remain accessible to all. the solution adopted by the eu (2012) and france is the introduction of plant variety certificates (pvcs), which are a form of protection for the work of breeders without preventing their use for other work. for farmers, it is also a guarantee that they can reap whatever crops they have harvested, with a contribution. despite this last point, vocs are a lesser evil compared to us patent law, which covers living things and therefore benefits only a minority of multinationals such as monsanto, which does not hesitate to send its "seed militia" to check that farmers do not resent the varieties that "belong" to it... the resolution calls for the union not to align itself with us law, and once again in the context of the ttip negotiations. that is why i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution and the amendments tabled by the greens.

in writing. ‒ this resolution calls on the european commission to clarify the european patent rules in order to ensure unlimited use of organic material by seed breeders and thus to promote innovation while ensuring a level playing field for small breeders. the recent decision of the european patent office (epo) court to allow patents even on plant traits obtained by conventional breeding techniques, such as crosses, raises the question of the consequences in terms of hindering innovation and threatening global food security. based on a narrow interpretation of article 53 (b) of the european patent convention and article 4 of the biotechnology inventions directive, this decision calls for urgent clarification in order to avoid negative consequences for the competitiveness of the european union. i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ in 1998, the european commission published a directive excluding essentially biological processes (plant varieties, animal breeds) from the scope of patentability. however, on 25 march 2015, the european patent office (epo) issued two opinions allowing the grant of a patent for a plant resulting from an essentially biological process. the consequence of this principle would not only be to restrict the work of farmers but, above all, to restrict access to patents to those with sufficient means, while slowing down innovation in this sector. in voting in favour of this resolution, we ask the european commission to reject the opinions of the epo by taking a new stand against the patentability of essentially biological processes.
in writing. ‒ i call on the commission and the member states to clarify and enforce international law and the patent directive 98/44, which explicitly prohibits the patentability of plant varieties, 'essentially biological processes' of animal breeds and native traits, including when these are obtained by natural processes. the grand chamber of the european patent office took a dangerous step in march last year in favour of the patentability of plants obtained by 'essentially biological processes'. this is unacceptable. abuse of patents would undermine the legislation on plant varieties, which allows any breeder to access and use existing varieties to create new varieties, and also allows any farmer to extract his own seeds from his crops. it would also create another danger: that only a few powerful groups capable of obtaining patents would monopolize life for commercial and financial purposes rather than for innovation and shared progress. i therefore call for extreme vigilance when negotiating trade and partnership agreements with third countries.

in writing. ‒ burundi is a former german and belgian colony. it gained its independence in 1962. from 1972 to the early 2000s, however, civil war was virtually unabated. since 2000, ethnic conflicts have subsided under the peacemaking efforts of former tutsi president pierre buyoya, until old feuds were rekindled by the willingness of pierre nkurunziza, the current president, to seek a third presidential term. the situation has deteriorated sharply since last may. despite these tragic events, the complexity of the opposition would make any intervention by the european union unnecessary or even harmful. i therefore voted against this joint motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ the situation had calmed down in recent years in burundi, thanks to the efforts of former president pierre buyoya, a tutsi who made peace with the hutus through the arusha accords. but by announcing last april that he would seek a third presidential term, which was forbidden by the constitution, nkurunziza revived old opposition. in may, the constitutional court upheld his candidacy, which sparked very serious riots, with police opening fire on protesters in bujumbura. since april, several hundred people have been killed and more than 200,000 people have been "displaced". at present, the situation seems to be out of control and the whole region is threatened with fire. especially since the rwandan president, paul kagame, has vowed to overthrow the burundian president. all the more reason for the european institutions to remain cautious instead of playing the role of lecturers once again!

in writing. while i recognise that the current situation in burundi is dramatic and that there is a risk of a conflagration for the whole region, the european parliament is again proposing unrealistic positions, seeking to make the european commission the policeman of world problems. while the positions taken by rwandan president paul kagame are worrying, it seems more reasonable to let the african union play a mediating role, especially since this civil war is largely ethnically based. the european union, by its repeated interference, tends rather to inflame the situation, as was the case in the middle east or in ukraine, and it would be wiser to rely on the diplomacy of sovereign states to reach a solution. i therefore voted against this text.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on burundi. the situation was still confused at the time of the vote on the number of deaths in bujumbura. since then, nearly 100 deaths have been confirmed. there is real concern about the situation in the country following president pierre nkurunziza's decision to seek a third term and his re-election after the 21 july 2015 elections plunged the country into its worst political crisis since the end of the civil war.
in writing. ‒ this resolution follows developments in the dangerous situation that burundi is experiencing today but the terms of this resolution are yet another interference in the internal affairs of a sovereign state with entire passages that will be taken as neo-colonialism. i vote against it.
in writing. ‒ virunga national park, in the democratic republic of congo, has been a unesco world heritage site since 1979 and is a true 'ecological sanctuary'. today, the park is under serious threat from more than 20 armed groups (combat, deforestation, poaching) and from the prospecting of large oil companies, particularly soco international. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution which seeks to stop the activities of soco international in the park, to restore security in the area by disarming the rebels and to ask the commission to take action against companies which do not respect the laws and treaties in force.
in writing. ‒ virunga national park is the oldest nature park on the african continent. its area is 790,000 hectares. this park, a unesco world heritage site, is now threatened by the presence of armed groups who not only fight the congolese regular army but also use it for poaching. he is also threatened by the presence of the oil company soco international which has obtained the concession of 85% of the park by decision of the government of the drc. in the last ten years, nearly 140 guards have been killed and the prince of merode, who is related to the belgian royal family, has been seriously injured. the motion for a resolution in question calls for an end to prospecting in the park and for the disarmament of armed groups. both these requests are legitimate and i have therefore voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. ‒ located in the east of the drc, on the border of rwanda and uganda, it is the oldest nature park on the african continent. this "ecological sanctuary" of 790,000 hectares, which has been listed by unesco since 1979, is threatened by armed groups (more than twenty) who, in addition to fighting with the regular army, are engaged in poaching, deforestation and "other illegal and unsustainable forms of resource exploitation", but also and above all by the prospecting conducted by soco international, to which the drc government has granted oil concessions covering 85% of the park's area. total also explores in the area but has reportedly respected its commitment not to prospect inside the park. among the many endangered species that inhabit the park, the most iconic is the mountain gorilla. more than 140 guards have been killed on duty in the last decade and its director, prince emmanuel of merode, was himself seriously injured on 15 april 2014. for once, i think it is desirable for the european union and its member states to intervene and i voted in favour of this balanced text.
in writing. ‒ virunga national park in congo is the oldest nature park in africa. it is threatened by deforestation, poaching by armed groups and oil exploration by the soco company (over 85% of the park). many animal species are threatened. the resolution calls on soco to cease all oil exploration, on the drc government to disarm the rebels and respect freedom of the press, and on the drc government to defend human rights and take strong action against companies that circumvent national laws and international treaties. i therefore voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ in this resolution, the european parliament stresses the paramount importance of protecting the virunga national park in the democratic republic of congo from irreversible damage. listed as a world heritage site by unesco in 1979, virunga national park has been considered since 1994 as a world heritage site "in danger". the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. they called on the member states and the european commission to step up their efforts to help the country to tackle the root causes threatening the country's development, namely corruption and armed conflict. i voted in favour of this resolution in support of these objectives.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it is aimed at better protecting a remarkable natural area.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this resolution because it defends an ecological sanctuary against the threat of oil exploitation. for once, environmental protection may be able to outweigh the financial appetites of multinational corporations!
in writing. i voted for this resolution. it is designed to defend an ecological sanctuary that is a unesco world heritage site, which is now more than ever threatened by a london-based multinational oil company. we have to protect this park!
in writing. ‒ virunga national park, located in north kivu and eastern drc provinces, on the border of rwanda and uganda, is the oldest national park in africa. it is a unesco world heritage site and is world-renowned for its rich biodiversity, including the critically endangered mountain gorilla. yet, armed groups are engaged in poaching, deforestation, and other forms of illegal and unsustainable exploitation of the park's resources. in addition, in 2007 oil concessions in the park were granted to the french company total and the british company soco international. this was done in violation of the paris convention for the protection of the world cultural and natural heritage. the resolution considered it "necessary to prevent the virunga national park, . . . from suffering irreversible damage". the resolution 'urges the commission, the member states, the drc and the oil companies involved in extraction activities to preserve the current boundaries and territories bordering the virunga national park from fossil fuel exploitation'. there is no question of the greed of the european companies involved, nor is there any thought of retaliation. i am voting for this text.
in writing. ‒ virunga national park is an 'ecological sanctuary' of 790,000 hectares, listed by unesco since 1979, which is threatened both by armed groups (more than twenty) who, in addition to fighting with the regular army, engage in poaching, deforestation and 'other illegal and unsustainable forms of resource exploitation', but also and above all by prospecting by soco international, to which the drc government has granted oil concessions covering 85% of the park's area. total also explores in the area but has reportedly respected its commitment not to prospect inside the park. the motion for a resolution calls for appropriate measures: that soco international plc and its company registered in the drc permanently cease all exploration and exploitation in the virunga national park, that the drc government cancel oil exploration permits and that it fight against groups threatening this sanctuary. the park is home to many endangered species, including the mountain gorilla. we must act now. i therefore vote in favour of the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution for the protection of the virunga national park in the democratic republic of congo. the aim is to ensure the preservation of this world heritage-listed park, known in particular for its mountain gorillas, a critically endangered species listed in the cites convention since 1973. located in north kivu province and eastern province of the drc, on the border of rwanda and uganda, it is the oldest national park in africa.

in writing. ‒ i fully support this resolution on the virunga national park in the drc. this park, located in north kivu province and eastern province of the drc, on the border of rwanda and uganda, is africa's oldest national park, a world heritage site and world-renowned for its unique habitats and rich biodiversity, unmatched in africa; it is particularly known for its mountain gorillas. but it is endangered by conflict and the weakness of the state in some regions, which is no longer able to control what is happening there. so i support any initiative to protect this heritage of humanity.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the protection of the virunga national park in the democratic republic of congo. this park is the oldest national park in africa and is a unesco world heritage site. despite its protected status as a natural area, it is threatened by armed groups engaged in illegal resource extraction and large-scale poaching, resulting in irreversible damage. the oil company soco international has also been carrying out oil activities in and around the park, which is home to about ten iconic species, some of which are endangered, in violation of various conventions. we therefore call on the government of the democratic republic of congo to abandon oil exploration and exploitation in the park, to cancel oil exploration permits in the area, to reject changes to the park boundaries and to fight against any illegal activity. it is clear that in parallel, we will need to help the national government to define sustainable energy and economic solutions for the communities that are heavily dependent on the natural resources of the park.
in writing. ‒ this motion for a resolution calls on soco international and its drc registered company to permanently cease all exploration and exploitation in the virunga national park and to respect the current boundaries of the park; it also calls on the government of the drc to cancel the oil exploration licences. it calls on the drc government to disarm the rebels and restore security in the park area, but also to recognise and respect freedom of the press and media and to uphold the rule of law and human rights. it calls on the european union to help the government of the drc. it called on the commission and the member states to take legally binding measures to hold companies accountable for circumventing national laws and international treaties. i vote for the protection of this ecological sanctuary.
